q-1278.text: Are you obliged in this situation to signal parking of the damaged agricultural tractor?
q-1278.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle immobilised on the road because of damage must be marked so that other drivers notice it early enough — the hazard lights and a warning triangle serve that purpose. This applies to an agricultural tractor as well.

q-1292.text: In this situation, does the light displayed allow you to drive beyond the traffic light post if you do not cause impediments to traffic for oncoming vehicles?
q-1292.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible signal does not permit passing the traffic light, and the fact that no one is approaching from the opposite direction changes nothing. Traffic lights apply unconditionally — you may move off only when the permitting signal appears.

q-1319.text: Are you obliged in this situation to use the low beam lights or daytime running lights?
q-1319.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A moving vehicle must have its lights on around the clock: during the day dipped headlights or daytime running lights are enough. The point is for the vehicle to be visible to others, not to light the road.

q-1323.text: Are you allowed to drive with the daytime running lights on in decreased air clarity?
q-1323.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Daytime running lights may be used only when the air is clear. When fog, precipitation or haze appears, dipped headlights must be switched on, because the vehicle must then be lit at the rear as well.

q-1336.text: Are you obliged in this situation to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-1336.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At an intersection where priority is not set by signs or traffic lights, the right-hand rule applies: you let the vehicle approaching from the right pass. Approach at a speed that allows you to stop.

q-1337.text: You intend to go straight ahead. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-1337.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The intention to go straight ahead gives no advantage over the vehicle from the right — in the absence of signs and traffic lights, the order is decided by the right-hand rule. The direction that vehicle will take is irrelevant here.

q-1338.text: You are joining the traffic after picking up a passenger. Do you have priority over the oncoming vehicle turning left into the parking space?
q-1338.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When moving off after stopping, you are joining the traffic and must give way to all other road users, including the vehicle turning left into a parking space. Wait until your path is clear.

q-1339.text: You start driving. Are you obliged in this situation to yield the right of way to the vehicle visible in the mirror?
q-1339.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Moving off from a standstill is joining the traffic, and then all vehicles already travelling on the road have priority, including the one visible in the mirror. Before moving off, additionally check the blind spot.

q-1344.text: Are you obliged in this situation to yield the right of way to the vehicle visible in the mirror?
q-1344.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle already travelling on the road has priority over a driver who is only joining the traffic or changing their path. The manoeuvre may be started only when it will not force anyone to brake.

q-1366.text: Does the sign placed on the right roadway mean "no traffic" in both directions?
q-1366.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign prohibits the movement of all vehicles in both directions, but only on the roadway at which it is installed. On a road with two roadways the adjacent roadway remains outside the scope of this prohibition.

q-1368.text: Are you allowed to drive into the car wash through this road?
q-1368.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs close this road to your vehicle, and the destination of the journey creates no exception. Only those road users whom the sign or the plate under it expressly exempts from the prohibition may enter.

q-1369.text: Are you allowed to turn right in this situation?
q-1369.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material do not permit a right turn — a mandatory direction of travel or a prohibition applies here. The driver must comply with the signs, even if the road to the right seems passable.

q-1395.text: Are you allowed in this situation to continue overtaking?
q-1395.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A manoeuvre started in accordance with the rules may be completed if the section ahead of you is clear and you will return to your lane without forcing others to brake. Suddenly breaking off an overtaking is often more dangerous than calmly finishing it.

q-1399.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle?
q-1399.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle whose driver is signalling a turn and pulling towards the side of the carriageway may be overtaken on the opposite side, if enough room remains and visibility allows it. Keep a safe lateral distance while doing so.

q-1400.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle from the right?
q-1400.explanation: Correct answer: NO. As a rule, overtaking is done on the left. On the right it is allowed only exceptionally — when the vehicle being overtaken is signalling a left turn, and otherwise in lane traffic in a built-up area.

q-1401.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle?
q-1401.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place overtaking is prohibited, as follows from the signs visible in the material. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the road ahead seems clear and whether the vehicle in front is travelling slowly.

q-1403.text: Are you allowed in this situation, in the built-up area, to overtake the vehicle from the right?
q-1403.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area, on a roadway with several lanes in one direction, you may pass on the right a vehicle travelling in the adjacent lane. You must not, however, force others to brake or change lanes frequently.

q-1404.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle?
q-1404.explanation: Correct answer: YES. No ban on overtaking applies at this place, and the visibility and the length of the free section allow you to overtake and return to your lane. Before starting the manoeuvre, also make sure no one is overtaking you.

q-1410.text: Should you refrain from overtaking the vehicle in this situation?
q-1410.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You may overtake only when you are certain you will get back to your lane before the approaching vehicle. Here there is no such certainty, and with a long vehicle the manoeuvre takes noticeably longer — it should be abandoned.

q-1413.text: Are you allowed in this situation to continue overtaking?
q-1413.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A manoeuvre started in accordance with the rules may be completed if the section ahead of you is clear and you will return to your lane without forcing others to brake. Suddenly breaking off an overtaking is often more dangerous than calmly finishing it.

q-1416.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle?
q-1416.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place overtaking is prohibited, as follows from the signs visible in the material. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the road ahead seems clear and whether the vehicle in front is travelling slowly.

q-1421.text: Are you approaching a major road in the presented situation?
q-1421.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs announce that you are approaching an intersection with a road that has priority, so you will have to give way. Slow down in advance and watch both sides of the cross road.

q-1423.text: Are you obliged to stop at this sign in the presented situation?
q-1423.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign orders you to give way, but does not order an absolute stop. You need to stop only when the situation requires it — when a vehicle is approaching on the road with priority and must be allowed to pass.

q-1427.text: Are you allowed to turn left in this situation?
q-1427.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs at this place rule out a left turn — a prohibition or a mandatory different direction of travel applies. You must go in the permitted direction and turn or turn around only where it is possible.

q-1428.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn at this intersection?
q-1428.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs at this intersection leave no room for a U-turn: the no-left-turn prohibition also covers turning around, and a mandatory direction of travel gives no choice. Wanting to go back the other way does not exempt you from complying with the signs.

q-1430.text: Does this sign placed in the area of an intersection refer only to the roadway by which it has been placed?
q-1430.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A prohibition sign placed within an intersection applies only to the roadway at which it stands. The other approaches are governed by the signs installed there, so each direction must be assessed separately.

q-1431.text: Is it allowed in this situation to pull over?
q-1431.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The no-stopping prohibition in force here covers the whole road on the side where the sign is installed, and therefore also the shoulder. Pulling onto the shoulder is not a way of getting around the prohibition.

q-1433.text: Are you allowed to wait at the nearest junction for the possibility of making a U-turn within the lane dividing the roadways?
q-1433.explanation: Correct answer: YES. If the width of the strip separating the roadways allows, the driver may stop in the gap of that strip and wait for an opportunity to turn around. The vehicle must not protrude onto either roadway.

q-1435.text: Are you taking the proper lane in this situation?
q-1435.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The lane is chosen according to the arrows on the roadway and the signs above the lanes, and this is done early enough. The lane you are in does not lead in the intended direction, so changing it is necessary.

q-1439.text: Will you be able in this situation to turn left properly from the right lane you are taking?
q-1439.explanation: Correct answer: NO. To turn left, you must in good time take the lane closest to the centre of the roadway or the lane marked with a left arrow. Turning from the right lane would mean crossing the paths of other vehicles on the intersection.

q-1448.text: If you intend to turn right in this situation, should you continue further on the lane you are occupying and change it immediately before the junction?
q-1448.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Lanes are changed early enough so that you reach the intersection already in the correct lane. A change just before the intersection surprises other drivers and is often additionally prohibited by the road markings.

q-1451.text: If in this situation you intend to go to Gdańsk, should you change the lane to the left one?
q-1451.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The direction to Gdańsk is assigned to the lane you are already in, so changing to the left lane is not necessary. The assignment of directions to lanes is read from the boards above the roadway and from the arrows on the lanes.

q-1452.text: In this situation, can you go straight on to any lane if there are no other vehicles in the tunnel?
q-1452.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Which lane you may drive in is decided by the signs and road markings, and the absence of other vehicles suspends nothing. In a tunnel you must drive in the designated lane and not change it where this is prohibited.

q-1459.text: Is it allowable to stop the vehicle 11 metres beyond this road sign?
q-1459.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The indicated place still lies within the range of the prohibition arising from this sign, so the distance of 11 m changes nothing. You may stop only beyond the section covered by the prohibition.

q-1460.text: Is it allowed in this situation to stop the vehicle on the lane between the roadways?
q-1460.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The strip separating the roadways is not intended for stopping vehicles — it serves to separate the opposite directions of traffic. A vehicle standing there obscures visibility and itself becomes an obstacle.

q-1461.text: Are you allowed to park the vehicle in the presented lay-by?
q-1461.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The bay is intended for a purpose other than parking your vehicle, and this is decided by the signs at that place. Parking in it would make it impossible to use the bay for its intended purpose.

q-1462.text: Are you allowed in this situation to park the vehicle on the hard shoulder?
q-1462.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place a no-parking prohibition applies, and it covers the whole road on the side of the sign, so also the shoulder. You may park only where the prohibition ends.

q-1464.text: Are you allowed in this situation to stop your vehicle on the hard shoulder immediately behind this sign if it does not impede the movement of other vehicles?
q-1464.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition takes effect from the place where the sign is installed and also concerns the shoulder. Whether the stop obstructs anyone is irrelevant — the prohibition applies unconditionally.

q-1466.text: You intend to change into the left lane. Do you have the right of way over the vehicles driving in this lane?
q-1466.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver changing lanes gives way to vehicles already travelling in the lane they are entering. The manoeuvre may be started after signalling the intention and checking the mirrors and the blind spot.

q-1471.text: Are you allowed to turn left from the lane you are taking?
q-1471.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The directions of travel from individual lanes are set by the arrows on the roadway and the signs above the lanes, and a left turn is not permitted from the lane you are in. You must drive according to its designation.

q-1473.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn from the lane you are taking?
q-1473.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You may turn around only from a lane from which this manoeuvre is permitted — indicated by an arrow on the roadway or a sign above the lane. The lane you are in gives no such possibility, so you will turn around only at another permitted place.

q-1474.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn from the lane you are taking?
q-1474.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You may turn around only from a lane from which this manoeuvre is permitted — indicated by an arrow on the roadway or a sign above the lane. The lane you are in gives no such possibility, so you will turn around only at another permitted place.

q-1480.text: Are you allowed in this situation to continue overtaking from the right on the motorway?
q-1480.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A manoeuvre started in accordance with the rules should be completed smoothly, because suddenly breaking it off and braking on a motorway would surprise those behind. After finishing the overtaking, take the correct lane.

q-1482.text: Is overtaking forbidden in this situation?
q-1482.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On this section a ban on overtaking arising from the signs applies, regardless of whether the road ahead seems clear. You may overtake only after the prohibition ends.

q-1484.text: You are in the middle of overtaking. May you cause an accident in this situation?
q-1484.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Starting to overtake in such conditions risks a collision, because you have no certainty that the section ahead will remain clear until the end of the manoeuvre. You overtake only when the visibility and the room are beyond doubt.

q-1490.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn on the road marked in such a way?
q-1490.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs indicate a road on which turning around is prohibited — traffic here moves on each roadway in one direction, and a U-turn would mean driving against the flow. You change direction only at a designated junction or exit.

q-1491.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn on this section of the road?
q-1491.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On this section turning around is prohibited, which follows from the signs and from the nature of a road with separated roadways. You will perform the manoeuvre only where the traffic arrangement clearly allows it.

q-1492.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn on the bridge?
q-1492.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around is prohibited on a bridge, in a tunnel and under a viaduct, because these are narrow places with limited visibility. You must drive through the structure and turn around only at a permitted place.

q-1496.text: Are you allowed in this situation to change the traffic lane and turn right?
q-1496.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings at this place do not allow a lane change, and without it a right turn is impossible. The lane is chosen beforehand, not just before the place where you want to turn.

q-1497.text: You intend to drive into the left lane. Do you have the right of way over the vehicles driving in it?
q-1497.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When entering the adjacent lane, you give way to the vehicles already travelling in it — they have priority, not you. Signal your intention early enough and enter only into a safe gap.

q-1498.text: You intend to drive into the right lane of the roadway. Are you obliged to use an indicator?
q-1498.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every lane change must be signalled with the indicator early enough and clearly, and the signal switched off after the manoeuvre is completed. The signal itself, however, gives no priority.

q-1500.text: When driving by the right edge of the roadway in this situation should you signal the intention to change the lane?
q-1500.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to signal an intended lane change does not depend on which part of the roadway you are driving on. Other drivers must know early what you intend to do, also when you are travelling by the right edge.

q-1503.text: You intend to change the lane. Are you obliged to use an indicator?
q-1503.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Changing lanes is a manoeuvre of which others must be warned with the indicator before the vehicle begins to move sideways. The signal is switched on beforehand, not while moving into the adjacent lane.

q-1504.text: When entering the adjoining lane in this situation do you have the right of way?
q-1504.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority belongs to the vehicles travelling in the lane you intend to enter. You enter only when the gap is large enough that no one has to slow down or change their path.

q-1505.text: Are you still allowed to turn right in this situation?
q-1505.explanation: Correct answer: NO. From where you are, a right turn would require crossing markings that prohibit it, or turning from the wrong lane. You must drive on and change direction at the next permitted place.

q-1510.text: Are you allowed to change the lane in this place?
q-1510.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The road markings at this place separate the lanes in a way that prohibits changing them. Lanes are changed only where the line allows it, not whenever it seems convenient.

q-1512.text: There are no other vehicles behind you on the road. Are you allowed in this situation to resign from signalling your intention to turn right?
q-1512.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An intended change of direction is always signalled, regardless of whether you can see other road users. Your intentions are also read by pedestrians, cyclists and drivers you have not noticed.

q-1514.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn at this junction?
q-1514.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this intersection no sign prohibits turning around, so the manoeuvre is permitted. It is performed with particular caution, giving way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

q-1516.text: Are you allowed in this situation to turn right onto the closest roadway?
q-1516.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs rule out entering the nearest roadway from your direction — it may be a no-turn prohibition or a one-way road in the opposite direction. You may turn only where the signs allow it.

q-1517.text: Are you prohibited from making a U-turn from the sign to the closest intersection inclusive?
q-1517.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A sign prohibiting U-turns applies from the place where it is installed up to and including the nearest intersection, so also at the intersection itself. You may turn around only beyond it, provided there is no further such sign there.

q-1518.text: Are you allowed in this situation to turn left at the next intersection?
q-1518.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs in force here do not take away the possibility of a left turn — the no-U-turn and the no-left-turn prohibitions are two different signs. When turning, give way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians on the crossing.

q-1520.text: Are you allowed to start overtaking in the presented situation?
q-1520.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking may be started only when you are certain of a clear section and sufficient visibility, and here that condition is lacking. In case of doubt the manoeuvre is not started.

q-1523.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake a single-track motorcycle if you are driving a multi-track motorcycle?
q-1523.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The overtaking ban in force here refers to multi-track motor vehicles, so it does not cover a two-wheeled motorcycle. You overtake with a safe distance and only in sufficient visibility.

q-1524.text: You are driving a lorry of gross vehicle weight rating of 12 tones. Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the passenger car?
q-1524.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The overtaking ban in force here covers lorries, and a vehicle with a maximum permissible mass of 12 tonnes is one of them. Its driver must therefore stay behind the car and not begin the manoeuvre.

q-1526.text: You are driving a lorry of gross vehicle weight rating not exceeding 3.5 tonnes. Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the passenger car?
q-1526.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The overtaking restriction addressed to lorries concerns vehicles with a maximum authorised mass above 3.5 t, so it does not cover the driver of a lighter car. The manoeuvre may be performed if visibility and a clear section of road allow it.

q-1527.text: You are driving a bus. Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the passenger car?
q-1527.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The overtaking restriction shown in the material does not cover a bus, so its driver may overtake the car. The conditions remain sufficient visibility and the ability to complete the manoeuvre without obstructing others.

q-1531.text: Are you allowed to drive into the narrowed part of the road, if you do not force the oncoming vehicle to stop?
q-1531.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a narrowing, a driver may enter first only when they will not force the oncoming driver to stop. If both vehicles can pass each other smoothly, the manoeuvre is permitted; otherwise you must wait.

q-1533.text: Does the plate placed under the sign in this situation indicate the distance from the place where you are obliged to stop?
q-1533.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A plate with a stated distance informs how far from the sign the place the sign refers to is located — here the place of mandatory stopping. The stop is made only there, not at the sign itself.

q-1540.text: Do you have to abide by the prohibition expressed in this sign till the nearest intersection?
q-1540.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A prohibition sign applies from the place where it is installed up to the nearest intersection, unless it is cancelled earlier by an end-of-prohibition sign or defined differently by a plate. After the intersection the prohibition must be repeated with a new sign.

q-1541.text: Are you allowed to stop the vehicle for 1 minute beyond this sign?
q-1541.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A no-stopping prohibition covers every immobilisation of the vehicle, even a very short one — a minute is also a stop. Only an immobilisation forced by traffic conditions or the rules is permitted, for example standing in a jam.

q-1542.text: Are you only allowed to turn left at this intersection?
q-1542.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The mandatory sign visible in the material permits travel only in the indicated direction, i.e. to the left. The driver should take the correct lane in good time and not plan to go straight ahead or right.

q-1558.text: Can you drive your vehicle in such conditions with the fog lights switched on?
q-1558.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Fog lights may be used only when visibility is reduced by fog, rain or snow. In good visibility they dazzle other drivers and must be switched off.

q-1561.text: Are you allowed to continue driving in this situation, not paying attention to the behaviour of the pedestrian?
q-1561.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Near a pedestrian the driver must exercise particular caution and watch their behaviour, because the pedestrian may step onto the roadway. Driving without this observation risks failing to give way and hitting them.

q-1578.text: Are you allowed to park your vehicle for 5 minutes beyond this sign?
q-1578.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign visible in the material prohibits leaving the vehicle on this section, and the length of the stay is irrelevant — five minutes is also parking. The vehicle must be left at a place not covered by the prohibition.

q-1585.text: Are you allowed to stop your vehicle on this bridge, in order to drop off passengers?
q-1585.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping a vehicle on a bridge, a viaduct and in a tunnel is prohibited, and the purpose of the stop — including dropping off passengers — changes nothing. Passengers should get out before or beyond the structure, at a safe place.

q-1590.text: Are you allowed to stop the vehicle directly behind this pedestrian crossing?
q-1590.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping in the immediate vicinity of a pedestrian crossing, including just beyond it, is prohibited, because a standing vehicle hides pedestrians and restricts other drivers' visibility. You must look for a place further from the crossing.

q-1591.text: Are you allowed to park the vehicle beyond this sign if you leave enough space for pedestrians and vehicles?
q-1591.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition arising from the sign applies unconditionally and is not lifted by leaving free room for pedestrians and other vehicles. The vehicle must be parked outside the section covered by the prohibition.

q-1592.text: Are you allowed to park the vehicle on the pavement in front of these signs?
q-1592.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Parking on the pavement is permitted only where the rules or signs allow it, and at the indicated place a prohibition applies. You must find another place, outside the section covered by the prohibition.

q-1600.text: Are you obliged in this situation to take the left lane beyond this sign?
q-1600.explanation: Correct answer: NO. No duty to take the left lane arises here — the driver travels as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway and chooses the lane according to the direction of further travel. The left lane is for overtaking and turning left.

q-1603.text: Where all the lanes for driving straight ahead are free, are you obliged to take the left lane?
q-1603.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When all lanes for going straight ahead are clear, the driver uses the right lane, because the rule of driving as close as possible to the right edge applies. The left lane is taken for overtaking, turning left or passing an obstacle.

q-1614.text: Are you allowed in this situation to stay on the left lane, when there are no vehicles driving on the right lane?
q-1614.explanation: Correct answer: NO. After finishing overtaking or passing, the driver returns to the right lane if it is clear. Blocking the left lane obstructs others and forces them to overtake on the wrong side.

q-1616.text: Are you allowed to park your vehicle directly behind this sign?
q-1616.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition takes effect from the place where the sign is installed, so it also covers the section directly beyond it. The vehicle must be left before the sign or further on, where the prohibition no longer applies.

q-1621.text: Are you allowed to park on the bridge in this place?
q-1621.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a bridge a no-stopping prohibition applies, and thus also no parking, regardless of the chosen spot. A standing vehicle narrows the already limited roadway and hinders a possible evacuation.

q-1632.text: Should you change into the left lane in this situation, leaving the right lane for slower vehicles?
q-1632.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The right lane is the basic lane for everyone, not a lane reserved for slower vehicles. You move to the left lane to overtake, turn left or pass an obstacle, and then return to the right one.

q-1634.text: Was it proper to change lanes in this situation?
q-1634.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The lane change was correct, because it was preceded by checking the mirrors and the blind spot and by signalling the intention with the indicator early enough. Vehicles already travelling in the lane being entered kept their priority.

q-1647.text: Should you take into account that the cyclist may emerge from behind the tram in this situation?
q-1647.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The tram hides part of the road, so a cyclist may ride out from behind it whom the driver will notice only at the last moment. You must reduce speed and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-1651.text: Can you attempt to overtake a cyclist in this situation?
q-1651.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking a cyclist may be started only when there is room for a safe lateral distance and the manoeuvre can be completed without danger. In this situation the conditions do not allow it, so you must follow the cyclist.

q-1660.text: Was refraining from overtaking the cyclist proper in this situation?
q-1660.explanation: Correct answer: YES. If there is no room for a safe lateral distance or the manoeuvre cannot be completed without danger, abandoning the overtaking is correct. The driver then follows the cyclist at a safe distance and waits for favourable conditions.

q-1672.text: Should you slow down in this situation?
q-1672.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Speed must be adapted to the conditions on the road so as to remain in control of the vehicle and stop it before an obstacle whose appearance can be foreseen. A lower speed gives time to react and shortens the braking distance.

q-1674.text: Should you move away from the right edge of the roadway?
q-1674.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Driving as close as possible to the right edge does not mean driving right next to it — when there is an obstacle or a vulnerable road user by the edge, you must move to the left and keep a safe lateral distance.

q-1676.text: Are you obliged to have the left indicator permanently switched on when driving straight ahead due to passing of parked vehicles.
q-1676.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The indicator signals an intended change of direction or lane, and driving straight ahead along parked vehicles is not such a manoeuvre. A constantly switched-on indicator misleads others.

q-1678.text: You intend to change the lane. Are you obliged in this situation to signal it earlier?
q-1678.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intended lane change is signalled with the indicator early enough and clearly so that others have time to react. The signal itself gives no priority — you must still make sure the manoeuvre is safe.

q-1680.text: When slightly changing your path within the lane you are taking, are you obliged to signal it earlier with an indicator?
q-1680.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A slight correction of your line within the same lane is neither a change of direction nor a lane change, so it does not require an indicator. Only leaving the lane you are in is signalled.

q-1685.text: You intend to continue driving on the priority road. Should you use an indicator?
q-1685.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When the road with priority changes direction at the intersection, following it is a turn for the driver, and every change of direction is signalled with the indicator. Without a signal, others will assume you are going straight ahead.

q-1686.text: Are you allowed in this situation to resign from using an indicator?
q-1686.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A lane change is always preceded by a signal with the indicator, regardless of the volume of traffic and of whether the driver sees anyone behind. The signal is switched off immediately after the manoeuvre is completed.

q-1688.text: You are driving a vehicle which does not perform payable transport of passengers on regular lines. Are you allowed in this situation to change into the right lane?
q-1688.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A lane designated for vehicles carrying passengers for hire on regular routes is reserved exclusively for them and for the vehicles indicated in the signs. Another driver may not enter it.

q-1690.text: Are you obliged in this situation to use an indicator?
q-1690.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intended change of direction or lane must be shown in advance and unambiguously with the indicator, because only then can the other road users adapt their behaviour. After the manoeuvre the signal is switched off.

q-1691.text: Are you allowed in this situation to make a U-turn at this intersection?
q-1691.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this place nothing prohibits turning around — there is no prohibition sign and no markings restricting the directions of travel. The manoeuvre must be performed with particular caution, giving way to oncoming vehicles.

q-1695.text: Will you be allowed to make a U-turn at this intersection after the light turns green?
q-1695.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A green signal only permits passing the traffic light in the directions allowed at this place and does not lift a ban on U-turns arising from a sign or markings. You may turn around only where the ban does not apply.

q-1696.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn on this road?
q-1696.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On this road turning around is prohibited, which follows from the sign or from the nature of the road visible in the material. The direction of travel may be changed only at a place intended for it, for example at a junction or an intersection outside the prohibition.

q-1698.text: You intend to turn right. Are you obliged to use an indicator?
q-1698.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A right turn is a change of direction, which is signalled with the right indicator early enough, before the manoeuvre begins. After it is completed the signal must be switched off so as not to confuse others.

q-1699.text: Turning left at this junction, did you maintain the proper driving path?
q-1699.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The left turn was performed correctly: the vehicle did not enter the part of the roadway intended for the opposite direction and left the intersection in the correct lane of the cross road. Its path forced no one to change speed or direction.

q-1702.text: Turning left at this junction, did you maintain the proper driving path?
q-1702.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The path was correct — the driver turned so as to end up on the roadway of the cross road on its right side, without cutting the corner and without entering the path of oncoming vehicles.

q-1704.text: Intending to turn left at this junction, have you assumed the proper traffic lane?
q-1704.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before turning left, the driver moves as close as possible to the left edge of the part of the roadway intended for their direction and takes the lane intended for turning left. The lane should be taken early enough, before the intersection.

q-1705.text: Can you make a U-turn from the lane you are taking?
q-1705.explanation: Correct answer: NO. From the lane you are in you may travel only in the directions indicated by the signs, and turning around is not permitted among them. Changing to the opposite direction requires a lane from which such a manoeuvre is allowed.

q-1706.text: Are you allowed to only turn left from the lane you are taking?
q-1706.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs assign this lane exclusively the direction to the left, so going straight ahead or right from it is not permitted. If the driver wants to go a different way, they must change lanes beforehand.

q-1707.text: You intend to go straight across the intersection. Are you obliged to use the left indicator?
q-1707.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Going straight ahead is not a change of direction, so the indicator remains off. A left signal switched on would suggest a turn or a lane change and could provoke others into a wrong reaction.

q-1708.text: After performing a manoeuvre to the right at this intersection, are you obliged to switch off the indicator?
q-1708.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Signalling ends with the manoeuvre — after entering the cross road the indicator must be switched off. A signal left on would announce another turn and could prompt others to pull out in front of the vehicle.

q-1709.text: Are you allowed to continue going straight in the lane you are now taking?
q-1709.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The directions of travel from individual lanes are set by the signs, and this lane has not been assigned going straight ahead. You must drive in the indicated direction or, earlier and after making sure it is safe, change lanes.

q-1710.text: When turning left, was the path you chose proper?
q-1710.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The chosen path allowed you to leave the intersection on the correct side of the cross road and did not encroach on the path of oncoming vehicles. The turn was made without cutting the corner and without cutting in front of others.

q-1725.text: Are you allowed to stop directly beyond this level crossing to drop off a passenger?
q-1725.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping on a level crossing and in its immediate vicinity is prohibited, including just beyond it, because the vehicle would block the way off the tracks for the drivers behind. The passenger is dropped off further on, at a permitted place.

q-1728.text: Was the path of your car proper when you turned left at the intersection?
q-1728.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The turn was taken correctly — the vehicle passed through the intersection so as to enter the right side of the roadway of the cross road, without entering the path of oncoming vehicles or those travelling alongside.

q-1729.text: Was leaving the intersection in the right lane forbidden in the presented situation?
q-1729.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Leaving the intersection in the right lane is permitted, as long as the signs do not rule it out — the rule is to drive as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway. You must only not obstruct vehicles travelling alongside.

q-1732.text: Was it necessary before changing lanes at the intersection to make sure that it was safe?
q-1732.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before changing lanes, the driver is obliged to exercise particular caution and check the mirrors and the blind spot, and to give way to vehicles already travelling in that lane. A switched-on indicator does not release you from this duty.

q-1737.text: Is using an indicator necessary before turning right at the intersection?
q-1737.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every change of direction, including a right turn at an intersection, is signalled with the indicator early enough. Thanks to this, pedestrians, cyclists and drivers behind know what to expect.

q-1738.text: You are changing from the left lane to the middle lane. Did you have the right of way over the vehicle entering the lane from the right in this situation?
q-1738.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When two vehicles enter the same lane at the same time from adjacent lanes, the driver approaching from the right has priority. The driver changing lanes also gives way to everyone already travelling in that lane.

q-1770.text: Should you use the horn in the presented situation, in order to warn the cyclist of your intention to overtake?
q-1770.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn is used solely to warn of an immediate danger, and in a built-up area its misuse is prohibited. A sudden sound may startle a cyclist and upset their balance.

q-1793.text: Are you obliged in this situation in the built-up area to stop if the need be, in order to allow the bus to join the traffic?
q-1793.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area the driver must allow a bus to pull out from a marked stop — if necessary by slowing down or even stopping the vehicle. The bus driver, for their part, must exercise particular caution.

q-1824.text: You intend to go straight ahead, and the driver of the oncoming vehicle intends to turn left. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to him?
q-1824.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver turning left cuts across the path of vehicles coming from the opposite direction and going straight ahead, and it is they who give way to them. Even so, it is worth watching their behaviour and being ready to brake.

q-1829.text: You intend to go straight ahead. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-1829.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a junction of equal roads the vehicle approaching from the right has priority, so the driver on the left gives way. You must, however, make sure they really do intend to slow down and stop.

q-1830.text: You intend to turn left and the driver of the oncoming vehicle intends to go straight ahead. Have you got priority before him?
q-1830.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The left-turning driver's priority at this place follows from the signs or signals shown in the material, which regulate traffic in this direction separately. The manoeuvre is still carried out after making sure the oncoming vehicle is slowing down.

q-1831.text: You intend to go straight ahead, and the driver of the oncoming vehicle intends to turn left. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to him?
q-1831.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this place the left-turning driver's priority follows from the signs or signals shown in the material, which regulate this direction of traffic separately. The driver going straight ahead must then slow down and let the turning vehicle through.

q-1864.text: What category driving license should you have when driving a four-wheeled vehicle other than a light one?
q-1864.explanation: Correct answer: A. A quadricycle other than a light one may be driven on a category B1 driving licence. Category AM covers a moped and a light quadricycle, and category A concerns motorcycles.

q-1866.text: What obligation do you have as the owner of a passenger car?

options.A: Submitting the vehicle to regular technical inspections.

q-1866.explanation: Correct answer: A. The owner of a vehicle must have it undergo periodic technical inspections, because only a vehicle with a valid inspection may be used on the road. Personal accident insurance and comprehensive cover are voluntary.

q-1876.text: When should you check the pressure in tires of a passenger car?

options.A: Before the beginning of a journey.
options.C: At least 24 hours before the planned journey.

q-1876.explanation: Correct answer: A. Pressure is checked immediately before driving, while the tyres are still cold, because only then does the measurement correspond to the manufacturer's values. After driving the tyres are warm and the reading is too high.

q-1877.text: How can you carry a load on a trailer pulled by a passenger car?

options.A: The load may cover some lights of the trailer.
options.B: The load must not disturb the steerability of the vehicle.
options.C: The load does not have to be secured against the change of position.

q-1877.explanation: Correct answer: B. The load must be arranged so as not to impair the stability of the combination — a badly placed load makes the trailer sway and causes loss of control of the vehicle. It must not cover the lights or be left unsecured either.

q-1878.text: How will you carry a load on a trailer pulled by a passenger car?

options.A: I will secure it against moving around.
options.B: I will place the load loosely on a trailer.
options.C: I will not secure the load against moving around if I drive slowly.

q-1878.explanation: Correct answer: A. The load must be secured against shifting, because under braking or on a bend it moves and changes the distribution of mass. Low speed changes nothing — the duty to secure it is unconditional.

q-1879.text: How will you carry a loose load on a trailer pulled by a passenger car?

options.A: Not covered - placed below the height of the side boards.
options.B: Not exceeding the speed of 30 km/h.
options.C: Covered in a tight load-carrying platform.

q-1879.explanation: Correct answer: C. A loose load is carried in a sealed load compartment and covered, so that it neither spills nor blows onto the road. Material falling from under the wheels endangers motorcyclists and cyclists in particular.

q-1880.text: How should the device used for fixing the load on a trailer pulled by a passenger car be secured?

options.A: It should be secured against loosening.
options.C: It does not have to be secured against falling down during driving.

q-1880.explanation: Correct answer: A. Straps and other fastening devices are secured so that they neither loosen nor fall off while driving. A loosely hanging item may catch on the road, strike another road user or release the load.

q-1881.text: How should a load be placed on a passenger car?

options.A: It may slightly cover the registration plates.
options.B: It may cover the rear fog light.
options.C: It must not limit the visibility of the road.

q-1881.explanation: Correct answer: C. The load must not restrict the driver's view of the road — that is a condition of controlling the vehicle. It must not cover the lights or number plates either, or hinder the use of the mirrors.

q-1882.text: How will you place luggage in a passenger car?

options.A: I will place the heaviest luggage deepest and lowest, in the central part of the boot.
options.C: I will place the heaviest luggage in the upper part of the boot, over the lighter one.

q-1882.explanation: Correct answer: A. The heaviest luggage is placed low and deep, in the middle part of the boot, because this lowers the centre of gravity and improves the car's stability. A heavy object placed high can be thrown into the cabin under braking.

q-1883.text: How will you place a load on a trailer of a passenger car?

options.A: So that it does not cover the lights of the trailer.
options.B: I will put it only on one side of the trailer.
options.C: I will always place it at the rear of the trailer.

q-1883.explanation: Correct answer: A. The load is arranged so that it does not cover the trailer's lights or reflectors — otherwise the driver behind will not read braking or a change of direction. The mass is also distributed evenly, not on one side.

q-1888.text: What must not you do when driving a passenger car?

options.A: Pull a person on sleights behind the car.
options.C: Carry a child in a child safety seat placed in the front seat.

q-1888.explanation: Correct answer: A. Towing a person on a sledge, skis or roller skates behind a vehicle is prohibited, because such a person has no protection and can fall under the wheels at any moment. A CB radio and a child seat in the front seat are allowed.

q-1891.text: Does the board under the prohibitory sign indicate the length of the road on which the prohibition is binding?
q-1891.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A plate under a prohibition sign giving a length informs over what section of road the prohibition applies, counting from the place where the sign is installed. After covering that section the prohibition ceases.

q-1898.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicles coming from the opposite direction?
q-1898.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When turning left, you cross the path of oncoming vehicles, so you must give way to them. The manoeuvre begins only when it can be completed without forcing them to brake.

q-1905.text: Which of the listed ways of carrying the extinguisher in a passenger car is proper?

options.A: The extinguisher is placed on the rear shelf.
options.B: The extinguisher is placed loosely between the seats.
options.C: The extinguisher is mounted under the passenger seat.

q-1905.explanation: Correct answer: C. The fire extinguisher is mounted low and within reach, for example under the passenger seat, so that it is available at once and does not turn into a projectile under harsh braking. A loose extinguisher is dangerous for the people in the car.

q-2025.text: What is the purpose of using the ASR system in a passenger car?

options.B: Preventing blocking of the braked wheels.

q-2025.explanation: Correct answer: C. The ASR system limits spin of the driven wheels when moving off and accelerating, by reducing drive torque or lightly braking the spinning wheel. Preventing the wheels from locking under braking is the job of the ABS system.

q-2026.text: What is the purpose of using the ESP system in a passenger car?

options.A: Preventing skidding of the wheels while engine braking.
options.B: Preventing blocking of the braked wheels.
options.C: Stabilizing the movement of the vehicle when driving along the curve.

q-2026.explanation: Correct answer: C. The ESP system stabilises the vehicle's path on a curve: it detects the onset of a skid and brakes selected wheels, bringing the vehicle back onto the intended line. It does not, however, replace a sensible choice of speed for the bend.

q-2127.text: You are going straight through the junction. Do you have the right of way over the oncoming vehicle turning left?
q-2127.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver going straight ahead has priority over an oncoming vehicle turning left, because it is the turning driver who crosses their path. Despite having priority, you must watch that vehicle and be ready to reduce speed.

q-2128.text: You intend to turn left at the intersection. Are you obliged in this situation to give way to the oncoming vehicle going straight ahead?
q-2128.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning left crosses the path of oncoming vehicles going straight ahead, so they must give way to them. The manoeuvre may be started only when it will not force the approaching driver to brake or change direction.

q-2129.text: You intend to turn left at the junction. Do you have to yield the right of way to the oncoming bus going straight?
q-2129.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A bus has no additional rights at an intersection, but as a vehicle coming straight from the opposite direction it has priority over the driver turning left. You must let it pass, remembering that a long vehicle clears the intersection more slowly.

q-2143.text: How often should you turn a non-traumatic victim to the other side after laying him in the recovery position?
q-2143.explanation: Correct answer: B. A non-trauma casualty placed in the recovery position is turned onto the other side every 30 minutes so that the arm is not compressed and circulation in the limb is not disturbed. Their breathing is monitored the whole time.

q-2145.text: You notice shortness of breath in a child. There is no one around to help. Which of the following actions should be taken?

options.A: Call for help, and then perform artificial breathing and chest compressions.
options.B: Perform artificial breathing and chest compressions for 1 minute and then call for help.
options.C: Perform artificial breathing and chest compressions for 15 minutes and then call for help.

q-2145.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a child, breathing usually stops before the circulation does, so a rescuer acting alone first performs rescue breaths and chest compressions for 1 minute and only then calls for help. They then continue resuscitation.

q-2161.text: In case of a wound hemorrhage and lack of sterile dressing you should:

options.B: use the clothing of an injured person as dressing.
options.C: wait until somebody lends you the first aid kit.

q-2161.explanation: Correct answer: B. Stemming a haemorrhage matters more than the sterility of the dressing, so without a first-aid kit you use the casualty's clean clothing and press on the wound. Delaying help or waiting for someone else's kit risks a large loss of blood.

q-2163.text: What should you do in the case of nose bleeding?

options.A: Squeeze the wings of the nose and lean your head forward.
options.B: Do not stem and wait until the blood stops flowing.
options.C: Squeeze the wings of the nose and lean your head back.

q-2163.explanation: Correct answer: A. With a nosebleed the sides of the nose are pinched and the head tilted forward, so that the blood flows out rather than down the throat. Tilting the head back risks choking and vomiting.

q-2164.text: Compression dressing should be applied in the case of:
q-2164.explanation: Correct answer: C. A pressure dressing is applied to stem a haemorrhage — the compressing layer presses on the wound and slows the flow of blood. With a crushed limb or fluid leaking from the ear, pressure is not advisable.

q-2165.text: How long should you continue to give chest compressions and artificial respiration in a person with a cardiac arrest?

options.A: Until the medical rescue team arrives.
options.C: Until the body of the injured person maintains proper temperature.

q-2165.explanation: Correct answer: A. Resuscitation is continued without interruption until the emergency medical team arrives and takes over, or until the casualty shows signs of life. Stopping it after a predetermined time is not acceptable.

q-2177.text: What should be preceded by chest compressions in an infant that has been placed on a table or the floor?

options.A: Place diapers or a towel under the child's back, so that the forehead, chin and chest are in one line.
options.B: Raise the child's leg up so that blood is rushed to the heart.
options.C: Place a pillow under the child's head.

q-2177.explanation: Correct answer: A. In an infant the large head bends the neck forward, so a nappy or a small towel is placed under the back so that the forehead, chin and chest are in one line and the airway stays open. A pillow under the head is a mistake.

q-2180.text: Which of these symptoms indicate rib fracture in a conscious victim?

options.A: The victim complains of pain that intensifies with deep breathing and movement.
options.B: The victim limps on his left leg.
options.C: The victim complains of stomach pain.

q-2180.explanation: Correct answer: A. A typical symptom of broken ribs in a conscious casualty is chest pain that gets worse with a deep breath, coughing and movement, so they breathe shallowly. Limping or abdominal pain point to other injuries.

q-2183.text: How long should you stabilize the head of a trauma patient manually?

options.B: Until it is taken over by a member of medical rescue team.
options.C: Until you ascertain the motility of their legs.

q-2183.explanation: Correct answer: B. The head of a casualty with a suspected cervical spine injury is stabilised with the hands continuously, until a member of the emergency medical team takes over. Letting go earlier risks displacing the vertebrae and damaging the spinal cord.

q-2188.text: A victim has a closed fracture of the lower limb and complains of severe pain. He is waiting for the arrival of the medical rescue team. What actions should be taken by a witness to the incident?

options.A: Encourage the victim not to move.
options.C: Try to position the limb higher than the heart.

q-2188.explanation: Correct answer: A. With a closed fracture the most important thing is immobilisation — the casualty is encouraged not to move, because movement increases the pain and damages the tissue around the fracture. A bystander gives no medicines and does not raise the broken limb.

q-2190.text: What should you do if you suspect a cervical spine injury and lack of breath in the victim of a road accident?

options.A: Bend the victim's head to his chest.
options.B: Place something soft under the victim's head, e.g. a rolled up jacket.

q-2190.explanation: Correct answer: C. Absence of breathing means an immediate threat to life, so despite a suspected cervical spine injury cardiopulmonary resuscitation is started at once. The head is moved as little as possible, but restoring breathing and circulation comes first.

q-2199.text: In which situation, do you not use an automatic external defibrillator (AED) on a victim?

options.A: When there is a cardiac arrest.
options.B: When there is a cardiac arrest and AED recommends discharge.
options.C: Where the victim has wet clothes or is lying in a puddle.

q-2199.explanation: Correct answer: C. An AED is used in cardiac arrest, but it must not be used when the casualty is wet or lying in water — moisture disperses the shock and endangers the rescuer. First the chest is dried and the casualty moved to a dry place.

q-2212.text: Are you allowed in this situation to use a warning sound signal?
q-2212.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A warning sound signal may be used when it is needed to warn other road users of danger. In a built-up area it is allowed only to avoid an accident, and the signal itself does not replace slowing down.

q-2215.text: Should you begin braking in the presented situation?
q-2215.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material indicates a danger, and the effective response is to reduce speed early. Braking started early enough shortens the stopping distance and gives time to assess how events develop.

q-2219.text: Are you allowed to continue driving without any reaction to the behaviour of the pedestrian?
q-2219.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The pedestrian's behaviour visible in the material signals a danger, so the driver must react — slow down and, if necessary, stop the vehicle. Driving on without any reaction, hoping the pedestrian will give way by themselves, is not permitted.

q-2239.text: Are you allowed to turn left in this situation?
q-2239.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A left turn is not prohibited at this place by signs or by the traffic arrangement visible in the material. Before the manoeuvre you must take the correct position on the roadway, signal your intention and give way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

q-2241.text: Are you allowed to turn right in this situation?
q-2241.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Turning right is not prohibited at this place. The manoeuvre is performed by the right edge of the roadway, after signalling the intention beforehand and giving way to pedestrians and cyclists travelling on the road you are entering.

q-2243.text: Are you allowed to turn right in this situation?
q-2243.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material do not permit a right turn — a mandatory direction of travel or a prohibition applies here. The driver must comply with the signs, even if the road to the right seems passable.

q-2246.text: Can you pass the stationary obstacle by using the part of the road intended only for the oncoming vehicles?
q-2246.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing an obstacle using part of the roadway for the opposite direction is permitted if there is no prohibition and visibility allows a safe return to your lane. The vehicle coming the other way in its own lane then has priority.

q-2254.text: Is slowing down justifiable in this this situation?
q-2254.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In the situation shown there are circumstances that limit visibility or increase the risk, and speed is always chosen according to the conditions, not only the permitted limit. A lower speed gives more time to react and shortens the braking distance.

q-2255.text: Are you properly preparing to drive past in this situation?
q-2255.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before passing an oncoming vehicle, the driver moves closer to the right edge of the roadway, reduces speed and keeps a safe lateral distance from the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction. On a narrow road you must allow for the need to stop the vehicle.

q-2258.text: Should you stop your vehicle when the oncoming vehicle is passing?
q-2258.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The width of the roadway or an obstacle on your side does not allow you to pass each other safely, so the oncoming vehicle has priority and you must stop and let it pass. Forcing your way through risks a head-on collision.

q-2260.text: Are you obliged to assess the situation behind the vehicle on the remaining lanes before passing this stationary obstacle?
q-2260.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing involves changing your path, so before the manoeuvre you must check in the mirrors and the blind spot what is happening behind and in the adjacent lanes. Only then do you signal the intention and change the vehicle's position.

q-2268.text: You are driving outside a built-up area on a one-way road. Can you overtake the vehicle on the right?
q-2268.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On a one-way roadway there is no oncoming traffic, so overtaking on the right is permitted, provided the width of the roadway and the situation around the vehicle allow it. The manoeuvre requires particular caution and a blind-spot check.

q-2270.text: Are you allowed to overtake a vehicle on the right in this section of the one-way road?
q-2270.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On a one-way roadway there are no oncoming vehicles, so overtaking on the right is permitted. Before the manoeuvre you must make sure the vehicle being overtaken is not changing lanes, and check the blind spot.

q-2281.text: When joining the traffic in this situation are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2281.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Joining the traffic always requires particular caution and giving way to all other road users. The driver must make sure they will not force anyone to brake or change their path.

q-2286.text: Are you obliged in this situation to exercise particular caution when driving from the road into the property?
q-2286.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Turning off the road into a property involves crossing the path of other vehicles and the way of pedestrians and cyclists, so it requires particular caution. The intention must be signalled beforehand and way given.

q-2287.text: When emerging from the property onto the road, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2287.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving a property onto the road is joining the traffic, so it requires particular caution and giving way to vehicles on the road and to pedestrians on the pavement. With limited visibility you pull out very slowly.

q-2292.text: When emerging from the dirt road onto the hard surface road, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2292.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Entering a paved road from an unpaved road is joining the traffic — the driver exercises particular caution and gives way to vehicles travelling on the paved road. In addition, wheels fouled with mud lengthen the braking distance.

q-2305.text: When entering the roadway in the presented situation should you exercise particular caution?
q-2305.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Entering the roadway from a place that is not a road is joining the traffic — particular caution applies and way must be given to vehicles and pedestrians. The manoeuvre begins only after making sure you will obstruct no one.

q-2308.text: When exiting the lay-by, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2308.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving a bay onto the roadway is joining the traffic, so you must exercise particular caution and give way to vehicles travelling on the roadway. The intention is signalled with the indicator after checking the mirrors and the blind spot.

q-2319.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution when turning right in this situation?
q-2319.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-2325.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution in this situation?
q-2325.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-2326.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution in this situation?
q-2326.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-2327.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution in this situation?
q-2327.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-2328.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution in this situation?
q-2328.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-2332.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution in the presented situation?
q-2332.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty of particular caution arises wherever the road conditions or the behaviour of other road users signal a danger. The driver then raises their attention, reduces speed and is ready to react at once.

q-2333.text: Are you exempt from the duty to exercise particular caution in the presented situation?
q-2333.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Nothing releases you from the duty of particular caution — neither priority, nor a green signal, nor the absence of other vehicles in sight. In the conditions shown, the driver must raise their attention and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-2335.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution when driving in the fog?
q-2335.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Fog greatly shortens visibility and distorts the judgement of distance and speed, so it requires particular caution. Speed is chosen so that the vehicle can be stopped before an obstacle seen within the range of visibility, and the proper lights are switched on.

q-2339.text: When passing the presented vehicle are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2339.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking always requires particular caution — the driver judges distance, speed and visibility, and when returning to their lane must not cut in front of the vehicle overtaken. With two-wheelers and slow vehicles an appropriate lateral distance must be kept.

q-2340.text: When driving behind the vehicle marked in such a way are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2340.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The marking visible in the material shows that the vehicle is of a special kind and may behave differently from the others — pull away more slowly, brake suddenly or stop. So when following it, you increase the distance and your attention.

q-2342.text: Do you have to exercise particular caution when approaching the stopping place of a vehicle marked in such a way?
q-2342.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material warn that people getting on or off, including children or persons with limited mobility, may appear by the vehicle. When approaching, you must slow down and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-2345.text: Are you obliged to stop the vehicle in this situation?
q-2345.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop the vehicle follows from the sign, signal or instruction shown in the material — the driver must comply with it regardless of whether the road appears clear. The stop is made before the line or the place it refers to.

q-2346.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution when passing a vehicle marked in such a way?
q-2346.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing a vehicle marked in this way, you must allow for people who may step onto the roadway from behind it. The driver then drives slowly, with a greater lateral distance, and is ready to stop before an obstacle.

q-2347.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution in this situation and stop the vehicle if the need be?
q-2347.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution includes being ready to stop the vehicle when the safety of other road users requires it. In the situation shown, merely slowing down may not be enough, so you must anticipate the need to come to a complete stop.

q-2357.text: Should you anticipate the pedestrian bursting onto the road?
q-2357.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In the conditions shown in the material a pedestrian may suddenly step onto the roadway, so the driver assumes this possibility and reduces speed. The principle of limited trust requires anticipating wrong behaviour by other road users.

q-2361.text: Should you refrain from overtaking this vehicle in the presented situation?
q-2361.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking must not be performed when visibility, the width of the roadway or the behaviour of other road users give no certainty of completing the manoeuvre safely. The only correct solution is then to stay behind the vehicle in front.

q-2374.text: You intend to drive into the gate. Are you obliged to give the right of way to these pedestrians?
q-2374.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The pedestrians visible in the material have priority, so the driver must give way to them — they may not enter their path or force them to hurry or stop. If necessary, they stop the vehicle.

q-2375.text: You intend to drive into the gate. Are you obliged to give the right of way to these pedestrians?
q-2375.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When entering a gateway, the driver crosses the pavement or a footpath, and the pedestrian has priority there. You must stop before their path and enter only when they have passed.

q-2381.text: Do you have the right of way over pedestrians in this situation?
q-2381.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the circumstances shown priority belongs to the pedestrians, and the driver must give way to them. Entering their path or forcing them to quicken their pace is not permitted, even when the vehicle is moving very slowly.

q-2384.text: When continuing driving in the place shown, are you obliged to drive slowly?
q-2384.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to drive slowly follows from the conditions and the signs visible in the material — at such a place speed must allow you to stop before any obstacle. Slow driving also gives time to watch pedestrians and other road users.

q-2387.text: Are you obliged to stop the vehicle in this situation?
q-2387.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop the vehicle follows from the sign, signal or instruction shown in the material — the driver must comply with it regardless of whether the road appears clear. The stop is made before the line or the place it refers to.

q-2391.text: Are you obliged to allow the pedestrian to cross the road?
q-2391.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The pedestrian in the situation shown enjoys priority, so the driver slows down and, if necessary, stops the vehicle to allow them to cross. You may move off only when the pedestrian is safely out of your path.

q-2392.text: Are you obliged to stop in this situation to enable the disabled person to cross the road?
q-2392.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A person with a disability moving on the roadway has special protection — the driver exercises particular caution and, if necessary, stops the vehicle to allow them to move safely. You move off only after they have passed.

q-2395.text: Are you allowed to slowly continue driving in this situation, watching out for pedestrians?
q-2395.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Driving slowly does not replace giving way — pedestrians must be allowed to cross freely, and so the vehicle must be stopped. Driving between pedestrians forces them to change pace and is not permitted.

q-2397.text: In the presented situation the tram has stopped at the tram stop. Are you allowed to continue driving?
q-2397.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The situation shown in the material requires you to stop and let through the people or vehicles that have priority, so continuing is prohibited. You may move off only when the obstacle is gone and the way is clear.

q-2402.text: Are you allowed to get out of the vehicle without making sure that you will not cause danger to traffic?
q-2402.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Getting out of the vehicle may begin only after making sure it will not cause a hazard. Look in the mirrors and over your shoulder, especially for cyclists and motorcyclists riding alongside the vehicle.

q-2403.text: Are you allowed to open the door of the vehicle without making sure that you will not cause danger to traffic?
q-2403.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A door may be opened only after making sure it will not endanger other road users. A suddenly opened door is a frequent cause of accidents with cyclists, so it is opened slowly, after looking in the mirror and behind.

q-2409.text: May a vehicle left as such, in this situation impede traffic or parking for other drivers?
q-2409.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle left carelessly takes up more room than necessary and narrows the passage, thereby obstructing traffic and preventing others from parking properly. When parking, the vehicle is positioned straight and within the marked space.

q-2420.text: Are you allowed to leave the scene of the accident because you believe that the perpetrator of the accident will give first aid to the injured person?
q-2420.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A witness to an accident must stop, give help as far as possible and call the services, and assuming that someone else will do it does not release them from this. Driving away from the scene is abandoning the casualty.

q-2429.text: Are you obliged in this situation to make sure that there is no train coming from either side?
q-2429.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before entering a railway crossing, the driver must make sure no train is approaching from either side, and only then cross. This duty exists regardless of whether the barriers are raised and the signals are silent.

q-2430.text: You know that the emergency services will arrive to the scene of the accident soon. Should you persuade the perpetrator to take the injured person to the hospital?
q-2430.explanation: Correct answer: NO. If medical help is on its way, the casualty is not transported in a random vehicle — moving them may worsen the injuries, especially to the spine. Until the services arrive, the scene is secured and first aid is given.

q-2432.text: When calling the emergency number in this situation should you first of all state the place of the incident?
q-2432.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The dispatcher first needs the location of the incident, so that the nearest teams can be sent even if the call is cut off. Only then do you give the type of incident, the number and condition of the casualties and your own details.

q-2434.text: When approaching this level crossing, do you have to make sure that there will be no train coming when you are driving through it?
q-2434.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Entering the crossing is permitted only when the driver is certain they will manage to leave it before a train arrives. You must therefore assess the visibility of the tracks and make sure there is room beyond the crossing to drive off.

q-2436.text: When the barriers are lifted, are you obliged to make sure that there is no train approaching?
q-2436.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Raised barriers do not release you from watching the tracks yourself — the equipment may malfunction. The driver approaches the crossing at a limited speed and checks for themselves that no train is approaching from either side.

q-2438.text: Seeing people in a burning car, are you obliged to administer first aid to them and inform the fire brigade?
q-2438.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Anyone who sees a human life in danger must call the appropriate services and give help to the extent their own safety allows. You must not endanger yourself, but neither may you drive away with indifference.

q-2440.text: Are you allowed in this situation to stop your vehicle before the level crossing?
q-2440.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal or signs visible in the material order the vehicle to stop before the railway crossing. You must stop before the stop line, and where there is none — before the barrier or at such a place as not to enter the tracks.

q-2442.text: Can you drive through the level crossing without stopping after the vehicle in front of you has started off?
q-2442.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to stop before the crossing applies to each vehicle separately, so you must stop again at the proper place and check the tracks yourself. The vehicle in front moving off is not permission to cross.

q-2445.text: In this situation, should you evacuate the injured person from the fuming car, bearing in mind your own safety?
q-2445.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A casualty is moved exceptionally, when staying in the vehicle threatens their life, and a smoking car threatens fire. The evacuation is carried out quickly, protecting the head and spine, and only when the rescuer is not in danger themselves.

q-2448.text: When intending to drive left beyond the level crossing in this situation, can you continue driving?
q-2448.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You may enter the crossing only when there is room beyond it allowing you to leave it immediately. Since you intend to turn left and could be stopped on the tracks, you must wait before the crossing.

q-2455.text: Can you drive away and leave the lying person without any intervention in this situation?
q-2455.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Seeing a person lying on the ground, the driver must stop, assess their condition, call for help and secure the scene. Driving off without any reaction is leaving a person in a life-threatening situation.

q-2457.text: Are you obliged to stop and inform the emergency services in this situation?
q-2457.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A road user who comes upon an incident with an injured person must stop, give help as far as they are able and notify the emergency services. The scene must also be secured so that another accident does not happen.
