q-2458.text: Are you allowed in this situation to enter the level crossing, if the red light has already gone out, but halfbarriers are yet the be fully raised?
q-2458.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Entering the crossing is permitted only after the barriers or half-barriers have been fully raised. As long as the arm remains even partly lowered, the crossing is closed and a train may still be approaching.

q-2461.text: Other vehicles are driving behind you. Are you allowed to move away, carefully passing the lying person in this situation?
q-2461.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A person lying on the roadway is in immediate danger, and vehicles coming from behind may not notice them. You must stop, secure the scene, call for help and give first aid.

q-2465.text: Are you allowed to enter this level crossing directly after the passage of a train, regardless of the signal displayed?
q-2465.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The red signal shown also applies after a train has passed, because another train may be approaching from the opposite direction. Entry is permitted only after the signal goes out and the barriers are fully raised.

q-2467.text: Are you allowed to drive onto this level crossing right after the barriers have been lifted without making sure that there is no train approaching?
q-2467.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The raising of the barriers does not replace watching the tracks yourself, because the safety equipment may operate incorrectly. Before entering, you must look in both directions and make sure no train is approaching.

q-2471.text: In the presented situation, are you obliged to stop and take an interest in this person?
q-2471.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A person whose condition may indicate a threat to health or life needs checking — the driver stops, tries to make contact and, if necessary, calls for help. Passing such a person by with indifference is not acceptable.

q-2472.text: Are you allowed to drive onto the level crossing when the barriers are not fully lifted?
q-2472.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The crossing may be crossed only after the barriers have been fully raised. A partly lowered arm means the crossing is still closed, and the equipment may lower it again at any moment.

q-2475.text: In the presented situation the engine will not start and you have no possibility of removing the vehicle from the track-way. Are you obliged to warn the driver of the rail vehicle of danger?
q-2475.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver whose immobilised vehicle is standing on the tracks must immediately warn the driver of the rail vehicle of the danger — with an available signal and, as far as possible, from a safe distance. The appropriate services must also be notified.

q-2476.text: In the presented situation, seeing the injured person with his head submerged in the water, should you leave him unmoved for fear of injuring his spine?
q-2476.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The danger of drowning is immediate, so the casualty's face must be lifted out of the water at once and the airway opened. The risk of spinal injury is reduced by turning them carefully as a whole, supporting the head.

q-2478.text: In the presented situation the engine will not start. Are you obliged to try to remove the vehicle from the track-way?
q-2478.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver whose vehicle has become immobilised on the tracks is obliged to immediately attempt to remove it from the tracks, and when that is impossible — to warn others, including the tram driver, of the obstacle. A tram cannot steer around a vehicle standing on the tracks.

q-2480.text: Do you have to be prepared to stop your vehicle when approaching the tram crossing?
q-2480.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Approaching a tram crossing requires particular caution: you must reduce speed and be ready to stop, because the tram has priority and its braking distance is long. This readiness also applies when the tracks seem empty.

q-2482.text: Are you obliged in this situation to make sure that there is no tram approaching?
q-2482.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before entering the tram tracks, the driver must make sure no tram is approaching, because a rail vehicle has priority and cannot leave the tracks. Visibility along the tracks must be checked in both directions.

q-2486.text: Are you obliged in this situation to make sure that there is no tram approaching?
q-2486.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver must make sure no tram is approaching before occupying the tracks. A rail vehicle cannot change its course or brake quickly, so it is the driver of the road vehicle who must assess the situation before entering.

q-2490.text: Can you pass the stationary vehicle in this situation?
q-2490.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Passing a stationary vehicle is prohibited where it has stopped to give way to a pedestrian, and when it obscures the view of the section the driver is entering. In such a place you should stop behind it and wait.

q-2491.text: Should you stop behind the stationary vehicle in this situation?
q-2491.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A standing vehicle blocks the view, and its driver may have stopped to give way to a pedestrian. The only safe solution is to stop behind it and move off only when the reason for the stop is gone.

q-2492.text: Are you obliged to stop the vehicle in the presented situation?
q-2492.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop the vehicle follows from the sign, signal or instruction shown in the material — the driver must comply with it regardless of whether the road appears clear. The stop is made before the line or the place it refers to.

q-2493.text: Are you obliged to stop the vehicle in the presented situation?
q-2493.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop the vehicle follows from the sign, signal or instruction shown in the material — the driver must comply with it regardless of whether the road appears clear. The stop is made before the line or the place it refers to.

q-2495.text: When leaving the slow traffic lane, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2495.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving a lane is a lane change, and thus a manoeuvre requiring particular caution: you must check the mirrors and the blind spot, signal the intention and give way to vehicles travelling in the lane you are entering.

q-2501.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution when reversing?
q-2501.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Reversing requires particular caution, and the driver must give way to all other road users and make sure the manoeuvre endangers no one. If visibility behind the vehicle is insufficient, the help of another person should be used.

q-2509.text: Are you allowed to enter the junction in this situation?
q-2509.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Entry is prohibited by the signal visible in the material — the driver must stop before the traffic light or the stop line. You must also not enter the intersection when there is no room beyond it to leave it.

q-2511.text: Will a signal be displayed in a moment prohibiting entry?
q-2511.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown in the material announces that a signal prohibiting entry beyond the signal head is about to appear. The driver should slow down and prepare to stop before the stop line, not speed up to make it before the change.

q-2513.text: Do warning signs oblige the tram driver to exercise particular caution?
q-2513.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Warning signs give notice of a dangerous place and require every driver, a tram driver included, to pay more attention and adapt speed to the expected hazard. This duty does not depend on whether the hazard is already visible.

q-2514.text: Is the tram driver obliged to adhere to the warning signs?
q-2514.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Road signs apply to all road users travelling on a given road, and a tram driver is the driver of a vehicle. A tram enjoys priority only where the rules or signing provide for it, but it is not exempt from obeying signs.

q-2519.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn left?
q-2519.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material does not prohibit a left turn, so the manoeuvre is permitted. Before carrying it out, signal your intention, take special care and give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction and to pedestrians crossing the carriageway.

q-2524.text: In this situation, do you have an obligation to yield the right of way to vehicles moving on the transverse road?
q-2524.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material gives priority to the tram driver, so it is the vehicles from the side road that must give way. Priority must not be forced, though — you must watch whether the others actually comply.

q-2526.text: Are you joining the traffic in this situation?
q-2526.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Joining the traffic is leaving a depot, premises or a road that is not a public road, or entering the carriageway from the verge or the pavement. Moving off after a stop forced by traffic conditions is continuing along the same road.

q-2527.text: In this situation, is the tram driver obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2527.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The place shown in the material is one where a collision with another road user is easy, so the tram driver must pay more attention, slow down and be ready to stop. A tram takes a long distance to brake and cannot steer round an obstacle.

q-2530.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop the vehicle and yield priority to the driver of the car travelling on the transverse road?
q-2530.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material grants priority to the tram driver, so there is no duty to stop or to give way to vehicles from the side road. Even so, take care and watch whether the other drivers respect the priority.

q-2535.text: You are driving a vehicle in the rain. Which of the following actions should you first of all take in order to drive more safely?

options.A: Turn off the traction control system.

q-2535.explanation: Correct answer: C. A wet surface reduces grip and lengthens the braking distance, and water between the tyre and the road threatens loss of contact with it. Reducing speed is the basic measure; switching off traction control and driving in ruts increase the risk.

q-2536.text: You are driving a passenger car during a heavy rain. Which of the following actions should you take after driving into a rut filled with water?
q-2536.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a rut filled with water the tyre loses contact with the surface, so any sudden action ends in a skid. Ease off the accelerator smoothly, hold the steering wheel straight and wait until the wheels regain grip.

q-2538.text: Which of the following actions may contribute to an increase in safety level while driving on the road covered with snow?

options.A: Braking only with a hand brake.

q-2538.explanation: Correct answer: B. Winter tyres have a soft compound and deeper tread grooves, so they clear snow better and shorten the braking distance. Braking with the handbrake locks the wheels and causes a skid, and sharp acceleration causes loss of grip.

q-2558.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield priority to vehicles travelling on the transverse road?
q-2558.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material indicates that it is the tram driver who has priority, so they do not give way to vehicles approaching along the side road. Priority does not, however, release you from the duty of care when crossing the junction.

q-2561.text: When turning right at the intersection, are you required to exercise particular caution?
q-2561.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Changing direction at a junction is a manoeuvre requiring special care: watch pedestrians and cyclists on the side you are turning towards and make sure the vehicle does not take the neighbouring lane or endanger others as it comes out of the curve.

q-2564.text: In this situation, are you obliged to signal the intention to change your direction of driving?
q-2564.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intention to change direction is signalled early and clearly, so that the other road users can adjust their behaviour. The signal is switched on before the manoeuvre begins and switched off immediately after it ends.

q-2567.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2567.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material is one where the rules require special care: pay more attention, adapt speed to the conditions and be ready to react immediately to a change in the situation on the road.

q-2568.text: After performing a turn manoeuvre, are you obliged to immediately turn off the indicator?
q-2568.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The indicator is switched off immediately after the manoeuvre is completed, because a signal left on misleads others and may prompt them to pull out in front of the vehicle. Signalling must correspond to what the driver actually intends to do.

q-2571.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution, in this situation?
q-2571.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-2572.text: In this situation, given the position of the tracks can the tram be overtaken from the left side?
q-2572.explanation: Correct answer: YES. As a rule a tram is overtaken on the right, but when the position of the tracks makes that impossible — for example when they run along the right edge of the carriageway — overtaking on the left is permitted. The manoeuvre requires special care and a clear lane.

q-2595.text: When reversing, does a tram driver have priority over other vehicles and road users?
q-2595.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver reversing a vehicle gives way to all other road users — this applies to a tram driver too. The manoeuvre requires special care and, when visibility behind the vehicle is insufficient, the help of another person.

q-2611.text: In this situation, is the tram driver obliged to reduce the speed and if necessary stop?
q-2611.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Approaching a place where another road user may appear requires special care: the tram driver slows down and is ready to stop. A tram cannot steer round an obstacle, and its braking distance is long.

q-2612.text: Does the tram, as a rail vehicle have priority over pedestrians passing through the pedestrian crossing?
q-2612.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver approaching a pedestrian crossing must take special care and give way to a pedestrian on the crossing. The tram's status as a rail vehicle changes nothing here — a rail vehicle's priority concerns its relationship with other vehicles.

q-2613.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2613.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material is one where the rules require special care: pay more attention, adapt speed to the conditions and be ready to react immediately to a change in the situation on the road.

q-2616.text: Does this sign indicate that children are accompanied at this point through the road by an authorized person?
q-2616.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The warning sign only gives notice of a place where children are often present, for example near a school. It does not announce the presence of a person escorting children across the carriageway, so the driver must expect them to step onto the road on their own and suddenly.

q-2617.text: In this situation, should you anticipate that children often use this crossing?
q-2617.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material indicates a crossing often used by children. Slow down and be ready to stop, because children step onto the carriageway suddenly and misjudge a vehicle's distance and speed.

q-2619.text: Is it advisable to use a powder extinguisher to stifle burning fuel e.g. after a collision with a car?
q-2619.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A powder extinguisher is suitable for putting out burning liquids, because the powder cuts off the oxygen supply and interrupts combustion. Water must not be used on fuel — it spreads across the surface and the fire spreads.

q-2620.text: When you drive a tram, can you leave the scene of a road accident, in which there is an injured person so as not to obstruct traffic?
q-2620.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A participant in an accident with injured people must stop the vehicle, give help, call the services, secure the scene and stay there until they arrive. Traffic disruption does not justify leaving or moving the vehicles.

q-2621.text: As a participant in a road accident are you obliged to take measures to ensure safety at the scene of the incident?
q-2621.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident must secure the scene: warn other drivers, use the hazard lights and the warning triangle, and then help the injured and call the emergency services. The point is to prevent further collisions.

q-2635.text: How many fire extinguishers must a two-car tram be equipped with?

options.A: One fire extinguisher in each car.
options.B: One fire extinguisher for the entire carriage.
options.C: At least two fire extinguishers in each car.

q-2635.explanation: Correct answer: A. Every car of the set must have its own fire extinguisher in an easily accessible place, because a fire can start in any car and passing between them is sometimes impossible. One extinguisher for the whole set does not meet this requirement.

q-2649.text: Which of these atmospheric factors reduces the possibility of skidding?
q-2649.explanation: Correct answer: A. Of the phenomena listed, the most dangerous for the grip of wheel on rail are drizzle, which forms a slippery layer with dust, and hail rolling on the rail head. A thin layer of ice is cut through by the wheel's pressure, so it is less of a threat.

q-2660.text: Does this sign warn you of approaching a place particularly frequented by children?
q-2660.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This warning sign announces a place frequented by children, for example near a school or a playground. Slow down, watch the verge and the pavement closely and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-2669.text: Upon seeing this warning sign, should the tram driver expect vehicles entering on to the track?
q-2669.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign announces a place where other vehicles may find themselves on the tracks, for example crossing them or joining the traffic there. The tram driver should slow down and be ready to brake.

q-2672.text: The prohibition expressed in this visible sign, will it be cancelled at the next crossroad?
q-2672.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A prohibition addressed to a tram driver applies until the nearest crossing or fork of the tracks, not until the nearest road junction. Merely passing a road junction does not release the tram driver from obeying this sign.

q-2686.text: How is authorized to inspect the documents of a tram driver?

options.A: A police officer or the municipal police.
options.B: An officer of any of the enforcement services, but only in the presence of a representative of the traffic control.

q-2686.explanation: Correct answer: A. Roadside checks, including checking the driver's documents, are carried out by a police officer, and within their powers also by a municipal guard. A tram driver is the driver of a vehicle, so they are subject to such checks under the general rules.

q-2688.text: The prohibition expressed by this sign, will it be cancelled at the next rail junction or its fork?
q-2688.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A sign addressed to a tram driver applies until the nearest crossing or fork of the tracks — there its effect ends. If the prohibition is to continue further, it must be repeated with another sign.

q-2697.text: In this situation, is the tram driver obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2697.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The place shown requires increased attention and an adapted speed, because a pedestrian or another vehicle may appear there at any moment. The tram driver must be ready to brake — a tram has no way of steering round an obstacle.

q-2699.text: Seeing this signal, must the tram driver regardless of the circumstances stop the vehicle?
q-2699.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A signal announcing a ban on entry requires stopping before the signal head, but if the vehicle is already so close that stopping would require harsh braking, the driver may continue. For a tram with passengers, harsh braking is in itself dangerous.

q-2702.text: Do light signal have priority over road signs governing the right of way?
q-2702.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When the traffic lights are working, drivers follow the signals, and priority signs recede into the background. Those signs apply when the lights are switched off or show a flashing amber; the instructions of a person directing traffic override both.

q-2703.text: Does this signal indicate that in a moment the signal in the shape of a horizontal line will light up?
q-2703.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown in the material serves as a warning and announces the signal in the shape of a horizontal bar, which prohibits passing the signal head. The tram driver should slow down and prepare to stop.

q-2704.text: In this situation, must the tram driver wait until the green light comes on?
q-2704.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A tram driver follows above all the signals intended for rail vehicles, given in the form of white bars, not the general green signal. Permission to proceed is given by the appropriate signal of their own signal head.

q-2705.text: With this light arrangement, does the tram driver have the right to enter the intersection?
q-2705.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The arrangement of lights shown in the material does not permit the tram driver to enter, so you must stop before the signal head or the stop line. You may move off only once the signal permitting travel appears.

q-2712.text: Does this horizontal marking indicate that the tram driver should expect vehicles that may enter the dedicated track on the right?
q-2712.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible road marking defines the course of a separated tramway and the boundary that other drivers may not cross, not a place where vehicles enter from the right. Places where vehicles may find themselves on the tracks are indicated by other signing.

q-2716.text: Should you in this place, anticipate cars entering on to the dedicated track?
q-2716.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material indicates a place where other vehicles may enter or cross the separated tramway. The tram driver should slow down there, watch the sides and be ready to stop the tram.

q-2718.text: If you are driving a tram merging into the traffic, are you obliged to observe the track, which you intend to enter?
q-2718.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Joining the traffic requires special care and giving way to all other road users. The tram driver must therefore watch the track being entered and make sure it is clear and properly set for the passage.

q-2719.text: If you continue driving after being forced to stop by a pedestrian who crossed the road at unauthorized location, are you in such a situation merging into traffic?
q-2719.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Moving off after a stop forced by traffic conditions is continuing along the same road, not joining the traffic. Joining the traffic is only leaving a depot, premises or a road that is not a public road.

q-2720.text: In this situation, when merging into traffic, are you obliged to yield the right of way to another tram in motion?
q-2720.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver joining the traffic gives way to all other road users, including a tram already moving. The manoeuvre requires special care and starting only when it will not force anyone to brake.

q-2722.text: In this situation, are you obliged to adhere to the "give way" sign?
q-2722.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A sign binds only those drivers it faces and who are travelling along the road it is placed beside. At the place shown it does not concern the tram driver, so no duty to give way arises from that sign.

q-2723.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop the tram before the conditional stop line?
q-2723.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A conditional stop line marks the place where the driver stops when required by the duty to give way or by a signal. In the situation shown, stopping is necessary, so that line may not be crossed.

q-2728.text: In this situation, are you obliged to signal the intention to change your direction of driving?
q-2728.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intention to change direction must be signalled early and clearly, so that the other road users can adjust their behaviour. The signal is switched off immediately after the manoeuvre is completed, because otherwise it misleads others.

q-2737.text: Does this sign oblige you to exercise particular caution and adjust the speed to be able to properly and quickly respond to a dangerous situation?
q-2737.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A warning sign gives notice of a danger and imposes a duty to pay more attention and choose a speed that allows you to react to what may happen. The point is being able to stop the vehicle before an obstacle.

q-2738.text: Does this sign oblige you to exercise particular caution?
q-2738.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A warning sign informs of a dangerous stretch or place and obliges the driver to pay more attention and adapt speed to the expected hazard. The duty lasts until the place the sign refers to has been passed.

q-2739.text: When joining traffic at the exit of a depot, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-2739.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving the depot is joining the traffic, and that requires special care and giving way to all other road users. Make sure the road and the track are clear, and move off only when it will obstruct nobody.

q-2740.text: In such a situation, are you allowed to move on without waiting for the pedestrian to leave the pedestrian crossing?
q-2740.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A pedestrian on the crossing must be given way, and you may move off only once they have left the crossing and are not endangered. Starting earlier forces the pedestrian to speed up or step back.

q-2756.text: Are tram drivers subject to the same permissible blood alcohol content level as other drivers?
q-2756.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A tram driver is the driver of a vehicle, so the same permitted blood alcohol level applies to them as to other drivers. Alcohol lengthens reaction time and impairs the judgement of distance, and a tram with passengers takes an exceptionally long distance to brake.

q-2757.text: Can a tram driver prior to commencing work take a medicine, in which the leaflet contains the following entry "during the treatment period, do not drive"?
q-2757.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Such wording means the medicine lowers psychophysical fitness — it may cause drowsiness, slow reactions or blur vision. Driving after taking it is not permitted; another form of treatment must be discussed with a doctor.

q-2758.text: Should the tram driver prior to commencing work, make sure that the medicine he is taking has no contraindications to driving vehicles?
q-2758.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver is responsible for their own psychophysical state, so before starting work they should check the leaflet or ask a doctor or pharmacist whether the medicine they are taking rules out driving. Many common medicines weaken concentration and lengthen reaction time.

q-2759.text: Is driving a tram under the influence of substances with a similar effect as alcohol prohibited?
q-2759.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban covers not only alcohol but also drugs and medicines and other substances that act similarly, because they weaken attention, lengthen reaction time and impair the assessment of situations. A driver in such a state may not drive any vehicle.

q-2782.text: When leaving the tram during a stop at the tram terminus, should you protect it from being started by an unauthorized persons?
q-2782.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver leaving the vehicle must secure it against moving off and against being started by unauthorised persons: immobilise it with the brake and prevent access to the driving position. A tram left unsecured is a direct hazard to its surroundings.

q-2797.text: Will the rail brakes work after the failure of the converter?

options.B: Yes, provided the power supply from the second carriage is working.

q-2797.explanation: Correct answer: A. Track brakes serve as the emergency brake and are powered from the battery, independently of the converter. That way they work even when the converter fails and the auxiliary circuits lose their supply.

q-2801.text: When driving a tram, should you anticipate that the children playing nearby the tracks may behave unpredictably and it will be necessary to reduce the speed or stop the vehicle?
q-2801.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Children absorbed in play do not watch their surroundings and may suddenly run onto the tracks, and they misjudge a vehicle's distance and speed. The tram driver should slow down early, use the warning signal and be ready to stop the tram.

q-2802.text: Can you allow passengers leave the tram during a prolonged breakdown, even if this might impede traffic and expose them to danger?
q-2802.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver is responsible for the passengers' safety, so getting off may take place only in a safe place and manner, after the road has been secured. Letting people out straight onto the carriageway between moving vehicles is not acceptable.

q-2805.text: As a tram driver, are you obliged to provide your personal details to a passenger involved in the accident?
q-2805.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an incident must give their personal details at the request of another participant. They are needed to report the damage and pursue claims, and refusing makes it harder to establish the circumstances of the accident.

q-2806.text: Are you obliged to provide details of the company you work for and details of the insurance company to a passenger who is involved in the accident?
q-2806.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The injured party must know to whom to direct a claim, so a participant in an incident gives, on request, the details of the vehicle's owner or user and its insurer. Without this information, reporting the damage to the insurer is practically impossible.

q-2807.text: As a tram driver, regardless of whether you have been trained or not, are you obliged to provide necessary assistance to the victims of the accident?
q-2807.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to give help rests on every participant in an incident within the limits of their abilities: call the emergency services, secure the scene and do what you can. Lack of training does not release you from this duty.

q-2812.text: Can fatigue induce effects similar to those of alcohol, such as impaired concentration and prolonged reaction time?
q-2812.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Tiredness weakens concentration, lengthens reaction time and impairs the assessment of situations, so it acts much like alcohol. The only effective remedy is rest and sleep; coffee or an open window bring only momentary improvement.

q-2824.text: You are driving a passenger car. Are you allowed in this situation to drive onto the bridge?
q-2824.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition sign installed before the bridge covers passenger cars, so the driver of such a vehicle may not enter there and must use the diversion. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the road beyond the sign seems passable.

q-2825.text: You are driving a single-track motorcycle. Are you allowed in this situation to drive onto the bridge?
q-2825.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The prohibition expressed by the sign before the bridge does not cover two-wheeled motorcycles — they are excluded from it, so entry is allowed. You must, however, expect that speed limits or other prohibitions may apply further on.

q-2832.text: You are driving a lorry of gross vehicle weight rating of 12 tones. Are you allowed in this situation to drive onto the motorway through this gate?
q-2832.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing visible above the gate permits vehicles of this category to pass, so a lorry with a maximum permissible mass of 12 tonnes may use it. Before entering, make sure the height and width of the passage are sufficient.

q-2833.text: You are driving an agricultural tractor. Are you allowed to drive onto the road beyond these prohibitory signs?
q-2833.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible prohibition signs cover agricultural tractors, so entering this road is not allowed and another route must be chosen. The prohibition applies from where the sign stands, regardless of traffic density and the time of day.

q-2835.text: You are driving a vehicle whose height is 2.8 metres, loaded up to the height of 3.8 metres. Are you allowed to drive onto the road beyond this sign?
q-2835.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Whether you can pass is decided by the height of the vehicle together with its load, that is, 3.8 metres, not the height of the vehicle alone. The sign limits the permitted height on this road, so you must turn round or choose a detour.

q-2837.text: You are driving a combination of vehicles whose total length is 11 metres. Are you allowed to drive into the petrol station beyond this sign?
q-2837.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The length limit applies to the whole vehicle combination together with the trailer, not to the towing vehicle alone. A combination 11 m long exceeds the value given on the sign, so entering this place is prohibited.

q-2840.text: You are driving a vehicle whose gross vehicle weight rating is 16 tones, and whose gross vehicle weight is 14 tones. Are you allowed to drive onto this bridge?
q-2840.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The mass limit before the bridge refers to the vehicle's actual total mass, not its permissible mass. What counts is therefore 14 tonnes, which does not exceed the value on the sign, so entry is allowed.

q-2841.text: Does this sign prohibit you from overtaking single-track motorcycles?
q-2841.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The overtaking ban expressed by this sign concerns multi-track motor vehicles. A two-wheeled motorcycle is not covered by it, so overtaking one remains permitted, provided the road conditions and the other regulations allow it.

q-2842.text: Is the prohibition expressed on this sign obligatory from the place of its mounting?
q-2842.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The plate under the sign shifts the start of the prohibition: it takes effect only at the distance stated on the plate, not at the place where the sign is installed. On the section before that place the prohibition is not yet in force.

q-2843.text: Does the board placed under this prohibitory sign indicate the distance from the place where this sign is obligatory?
q-2843.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate placed under a prohibition sign informs at what distance from it the place lies from which the prohibition takes effect. Up to that place you may drive without the restriction imposed by this sign.

q-2845.text: Does this sign indicate the end of the built-up area?
q-2845.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This sign marks the end of a built-up area. From the place where it stands, the rules specific to a built-up area cease to apply, including the lower speed limit, and the rules for a road outside a built-up area take effect.

q-2851.text: Are you obliged in this situation to slow down when there are no pedestrians on the road?
q-2851.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The warning requires heightened observation and readiness to react, but the duty to reduce speed itself arises when pedestrians appear on or by the road. When no one is there, speed need not be reduced.

q-2856.text: You are driving a lorry of gross vehicle weight rating of 12 tones. Are you allowed in this situation to turn left at the nearest junction?
q-2856.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition shown in the material covers a vehicle of that maximum permissible mass, so a left turn at the nearest junction is not allowed for you. That direction remains available only to vehicles not covered by the prohibition.

q-2860.text: Does the express road begin in 1000 metres from this sign?
q-2860.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign with a stated distance warns that the expressway will begin only in 1000 metres. The rules applying on an expressway, including different speed limits and restrictions for slow vehicles, will take effect from its start.

q-2864.text: Beyond this sign, are you allowed to stop in any place by the right edge of the roadway to drop off a passenger?
q-2864.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign prohibits stopping the vehicle, and the prohibition also covers a brief halt to drop off a passenger. You may stop only when traffic conditions or the rules force you to, for example a jam or a signal ordering a stop.

q-2866.text: Does this sign indicate the beginning of a built-up area?
q-2866.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This sign marks the beginning of a built-up area. From the place where it stands, the rules specific to a built-up area apply, above all the lower speed limit and greater readiness for pedestrians and cross traffic.

q-2875.text: You are driving an articulated vehicle of gross vehicle weight rating of 24 tones. Is parking your vehicle on the road beyond this sign only allowed in specially designated parking lots?
q-2875.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On the road beyond this sign, parking such a vehicle is allowed only in places designated for it, that is, in car parks. Elsewhere you may stop only when traffic conditions or the rules require it.

q-2877.text: Are you on a two-way road in the presented situation?
q-2877.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material indicates that traffic on this carriageway runs in both directions. On a two-way carriageway you must expect oncoming vehicles, so overtaking requires a clear stretch and good visibility.

q-2879.text: Is the right lane in this situation devoted to any vehicle?
q-2879.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The right lane is intended for a selected group of vehicles, as follows from the signs visible in the material. Other drivers may not drive in it and should use the lane next to it, entering the reserved lane only where it is permitted.

q-2880.text: Are you changing the lane if you cross the white dashed line in this situation?
q-2880.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Not every broken white line separates lanes — it may also be an edge line or separate the roadway from another part of the road. Crossing it in this situation is therefore not a lane change.

q-2882.text: Does this horizontal sign prohibit changing lanes?
q-2882.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A solid line separating lanes means that crossing it is prohibited, and a lane cannot be changed without crossing it. The manoeuvre becomes permitted only where the line turns into a broken one.

q-2883.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drive a passenger car straight ahead on the lane you are taking?
q-2883.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The permitted directions of travel from individual lanes are set by the signs, and going straight ahead is not permitted from the lane you are in. You must move to the lane appropriate for the chosen direction early enough, before the intersection.

q-2885.text: Are you allowed in this situation to use all lanes along the entire width of the roadway?
q-2885.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs and markings visible in the material divide the roadway and do not leave all the lanes at your disposal — part of the width of the roadway is intended for another direction or for another group of vehicles. You may drive only in the lane intended for you.

q-2889.text: Are you allowed to turn right at this intersection from the lane you are occupying?
q-2889.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A right turn is permitted from the lane you are in, as follows from the signs visible in the material. Before the manoeuvre you must signal your intention with the indicator and move towards the right edge of the roadway, giving way to pedestrians stepping onto the cross roadway.

q-2892.text: Are you allowed in this situation to change the lane you are occupying?
q-2892.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The markings at this place do not prohibit changing lanes, so the manoeuvre is permitted. Before performing it, you must check the mirrors and glance at the blind spot, signal your intention and give way to those travelling in the lane you are entering.

q-2895.text: Are you allowed to turn left at the intersection from the lane you are taking?
q-2895.explanation: Correct answer: NO. From the right lane the signs do not permit a left turn, so you must go in the direction assigned to that lane. You should have moved to the lane allowing a left turn earlier, before reaching the intersection.

q-2898.text: Is stopover of the vehicle allowed on this hard shoulder?
q-2898.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition in force at this place also covers the shoulder, so leaving the vehicle parked there is not permitted. The vehicle must be parked further on, beyond the range of the prohibition, or at a place designated for it.

q-2899.text: Are you allowed to stop your vehicle on this hard shoulder?
q-2899.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition in force at this place covers the shoulder and also concerns a short stop at the driver's will. You may stop only when forced to by traffic conditions or the rules, for example a jam or a signal ordering a stop.

q-2901.text: Are you allowed in this situation to change lanes in order to go straight?
q-2901.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings at this place do not allow a lane change, so you cannot get this way to the lane allowing you to go straight ahead. You must go in the direction permitted from the lane you are in; the lane change should have been made earlier.

q-2902.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn at this junction in this situation?
q-2902.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this place nothing prohibits turning around — there is no prohibition sign and no markings restricting the directions of travel. The manoeuvre must be performed with particular caution, giving way to oncoming vehicles.

q-2904.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn at this intersection from the lane you are taking?
q-2904.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings of this lane do not permit turning around at the nearest intersection — from the lane you may travel only in the direction assigned to it. You may turn around only where the signs and the rules allow it.

q-2906.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drive onto the lane by the edge of the roadway?
q-2906.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The lane by the right edge of the roadway is separated by markings that do not allow entry at this place, or it is intended for another group of vehicles. A lane change here would be a breach of the prohibition in force.

q-2908.text: Is stopping the vehicle in this place, in order to give the right of way to other drivers, proper in this situation?
q-2908.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Giving way is done by reducing speed early enough and stopping at the proper place, not where the vehicle blocks the traffic of others or where stopping is prohibited. Such a stop is a mistake.

q-2909.text: Are you allowed to stop the vehicle on the hard shoulder in this situation?
q-2909.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this place no prohibition covers the right shoulder, so stopping on it is permitted. The vehicle must be positioned so that it does not obstruct others and is clearly visible to those approaching from behind.

q-2911.text: Is driving on this lane allowed only in the direction indicated by the arrow?
q-2911.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An arrow on a lane bindingly sets the direction in which you may travel from that lane; travelling in another direction is not permitted. You must move to the lane corresponding to your intended direction early enough.

q-2913.text: You are driving a bus carrying passengers free of charge. Are you allowed in this situation to drive onto the lane marked with the "BUS" sign?
q-2913.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A lane marked BUS is intended for buses carrying passengers for payment on regular routes and for the vehicles indicated in the signing. A bus carrying passengers free of charge does not belong to that group.

q-2914.text: You are driving a motor vehicle. Are you allowed to go straight across the intersection from the lane you are occupying?
q-2914.explanation: Correct answer: NO. From the lane you are in the signs do not permit going straight through the intersection — the lane leads in another direction or is intended for other road users. You must move to the correct lane before reaching the intersection.

q-2915.text: Are you allowed to change the lane in the place marked in such a way?
q-2915.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings at this place prohibit crossing the line separating the lanes, and without that a lane change is impossible. The manoeuvre will be permitted only beyond the section covered by the prohibition.

q-2916.text: Are you allowed to stop your vehicle at this bus stop in order to drop off a passenger?
q-2916.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The place at the stop is reserved for public transport vehicles, so other drivers must not stop there, even briefly to drop off a passenger. You may stop only outside the area of the stop.

q-2919.text: You intend to continue going straight ahead. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-2919.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this intersection priority belongs to you, and the driver approaching from the left is obliged to let you pass. Even so, you must watch their behaviour and be ready to brake if they do not give way.

q-2920.text: You intend to continue going straight ahead. Are you obliged in this situation to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-2920.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this intersection the driver approaching from the right has priority, so you must slow down and, if necessary, stop the vehicle and let them pass. The intention to go straight ahead gives no privilege.

q-2921.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have priority over the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-2921.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority belongs to you, and the vehicle approaching from the left is obliged to give way. When turning left, however, you must let pass vehicles coming straight from the opposite direction and pedestrians stepping onto the cross roadway.

q-2922.text: You intend to go straight ahead. Do you have priority over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-2922.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The vehicle approaching from the right has priority, so it is you who must give way, even though you are going straight ahead. You should approach the intersection at a speed that allows you to stop before it.

q-2923.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have priority over the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-2923.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority belongs to you, and the vehicle approaching from the left is obliged to give way. When turning left, however, you must let pass vehicles coming straight from the opposite direction and pedestrians stepping onto the cross roadway.

q-2925.text: You intend to continue going straight ahead. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle coming from the opposite direction that intends to turn left?
q-2925.explanation: Correct answer: NO. It is the driver turning left who is obliged to give way to vehicles coming straight from the opposite direction. Going straight, you keep priority, but you must watch whether that driver really waits.

q-2926.text: You intend to turn right. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the oncoming vehicle that is turning left?
q-2926.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning right, you stay on your side of the roadway, and the duty to give way rests on the driver turning left from the opposite direction. The paths of the two vehicles do not cross, so you do not give way to them.

q-2927.text: You intend to turn left. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-2927.explanation: Correct answer: YES. From the rules of priority in force at this intersection it follows that the vehicle approaching from the left goes first. The left turn may be started only after letting it pass and after checking for oncoming vehicles.

q-2929.text: You are turning right and the motorcyclist approaching from the left intends to continue going straight. Do you have priority over it?
q-2929.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The motorcyclist is approaching from your left, so it is they who must give way. The speed of a two-wheeler is easy to underestimate, so before turning right you must make sure its rider really is slowing down.

q-2931.text: You are going straight ahead. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the motorcyclist?
q-2931.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority belongs to the motorcyclist, so you may continue straight ahead only after they have passed. A motorcycle is narrower and less visible, which makes it easy to misjudge its speed and distance.

q-2932.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have priority over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-2932.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The vehicle approaching from the right has priority, so you must let it pass. The left turn may be made only when it will not force any driver to brake harshly or change direction.

q-2933.text: You are going straight ahead. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-2933.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver approaching from the right has priority and goes first, regardless of the fact that you are going straight ahead. You must approach the intersection at a speed that allows the vehicle to be stopped.

q-2934.text: You intend to turn left. Have you got priority over the motorcycle?
q-2934.explanation: Correct answer: YES. It is the motorcyclist who is obliged to give way to you, so the left turn is permitted. The manoeuvre must, however, be started only after making sure the two-wheeler is slowing down and actually giving way.

q-2936.text: Are you allowed in this situation to resume driving, regardless of the movement of pedestrians on the roadway?
q-2936.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The conditions shown in the material require you to give way to road users who are already on the carriageway, above all pedestrians. You may move only once they have cleared the way and would not have to be forced to stop.

q-2940.text: Should you resign from overtaking in the presented situation?
q-2940.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The conditions visible in the material do not give a section that is clear and visible along the whole length needed to overtake, so the manoeuvre must be abandoned. Overtaking may be started only when there is certainty of a safe return to your lane.

q-2942.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle?
q-2942.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs and conditions visible in the material do not stand in the way of overtaking, and the section ahead of the vehicle is clear and clearly visible. Before the manoeuvre you must signal your intention, check that no one is overtaking from behind, and keep a safe distance.

q-2943.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle?
q-2943.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs and conditions visible in the material do not stand in the way of overtaking, and the section ahead of the vehicle is clear and clearly visible. Before the manoeuvre you must signal your intention, check that no one is overtaking from behind, and keep a safe distance.

q-2945.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle?
q-2945.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The conditions or signs visible in the material rule out overtaking — there is no clear and clearly visible section, or the manoeuvre is prohibited at this place. You must stay behind the vehicle in front and keep a safe distance.

q-2947.text: Are you allowed to overtake the cyclist in this situation?
q-2947.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking a cyclist requires a safe distance of not less than 1 m, and the conditions visible in the material do not allow it to be kept or the manoeuvre to be performed without danger. You must follow the cyclist until the situation changes.

q-2948.text: Should you refrain from overtaking in this situation?
q-2948.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The conditions visible in the material do not provide a section that is clear and visible along the whole length needed to overtake, so the manoeuvre must be abandoned. Overtaking is started only when it will not force anyone to brake or change their path.

q-2953.text: You are driving a vehicle in a built-up area. Are you allowed to overtake the directly preceding vehicle from the right in this situation?
q-2953.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area, on a roadway with at least two marked lanes in the same direction, overtaking on the right is permitted. You must remain cautious and not obstruct other drivers.

q-2990.text: Are yo obliged to stay at the scene of the accident in this situation?
q-2990.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident must remain at the scene until the services arrive, and may leave only if they have to fetch help. Driving away from the scene of an accident is a serious breach of a driver's duties.

q-2994.text: Are you obliged to give necessary aid to the victim of the accident in this situation?
q-2994.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident must give the injured person the necessary help within their abilities and call an ambulance. Help is given in a way that does not worsen the injured person's condition and does not endanger the rescuer.

q-3007.text: In this situation, are you obliged to ensure traffic safety at the scene of the accident?
q-3007.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident must secure the scene: switch on the hazard lights, set up the warning triangle and warn approaching traffic. The point is to prevent another collision and to let the rescuers reach the scene safely.

q-3040.text: Does this sign indicate the end of a built-up area?
q-3040.explanation: Correct answer: NO. This sign has a different meaning and does not mark the end of a built-up area. The end of a built-up area is indicated by a separate sign, and only from it do the rules specific to a built-up area, including the lower speed limit, cease to apply.

q-3060.text: Are you obliged in this situation to change the lane if you continue driving?
q-3060.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The lane you are in does not allow you to continue in the chosen direction — it ends or leads elsewhere, so you must move to the adjacent one. The lane change should be made early enough, signalling the intention and giving way to those travelling in that lane.

q-3061.text: Are you allowed to turn left into the parking space situated by the road?
q-3061.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings in this place do not allow crossing to the opposite side of the roadway, so a left turn into the car park is prohibited. You must reach the car park by another route, turning around where it is permitted.

q-3062.text: Are you allowed to drive into the parking space visible on the left side of the road marked in this way?
q-3062.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The markings in this place allow crossing to the left side of the roadway, so turning into the car park is permitted. Before the manoeuvre you must signal your intention and give way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians.

q-3063.text: Are yo obliged to follow the yellow horizontal signs in this situation?
q-3063.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Yellow road markings are temporary and take precedence over the white markings in the same place. As long as they are visible, the driver follows them, and the white lines are of no significance.

q-3064.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drive straight on from the lane you are using?
q-3064.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs set for the lane you are in a direction other than straight ahead, and you may not depart from that indication. You should have moved to the lane allowing you to go straight ahead earlier, before reaching this place.

q-3066.text: Are you allowed in this situation to change to the left lane if you intend to turn right?
q-3066.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings at this place prohibit crossing the line separating the lanes, and the intention to turn left does not exempt you from this prohibition. You should have moved to the correct lane earlier, before the line became solid.

q-3067.text: Do these horizontal signs allow you to turn left before the pedestrian crossing?
q-3067.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings at this place do not allow crossing to the left side of the roadway before the pedestrian crossing, so such a turn is prohibited. You must continue and turn only where the manoeuvre is permitted.

q-3068.text: Are you allowed in this place to change the lane if you intend to drive straight on?
q-3068.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The markings at this place do not prohibit crossing the line separating the lanes, so a lane change is permitted. Before the manoeuvre you must check the mirrors and the blind spot, signal your intention and give way to those travelling in the lane you are entering.

q-3069.text: Are you obliged to stop the vehicle before the presented solid line?
q-3069.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign or signal visible in the material orders an absolute stop of the vehicle, and the solid line marks the place before which this must be done. The stop must be complete, and only then is the situation assessed and way given.

q-3070.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drive into the intersection without stopping the vehicle before the presented solid line?
q-3070.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to stop follows from the sign or signal visible in the material, and the solid line indicates the stopping place. Entering the intersection without a complete stop is a violation of the rules, even when the road seems clear.

q-3071.text: Does the horizontal dotted line visible in this intersection indicate continuation of the traffic lane occupied?
q-3071.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A broken line drawn through the intersection indicates the course of the lane and shows how to continue on the other side. Following this guidance keeps traffic orderly and prevents you from driving into another vehicle's path.

q-3072.text: Does this triangular horizontal sign warn you of a place on the road where there is or might be a danger?
q-3072.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A triangular road marking serves as a warning and announces a place where a danger exists or may exist. Once you notice it, you must raise your attention, slow down and be ready to react.

q-3073.text: Does the line on the road composed of triangles indicate a place of conditional stop in order to yield the right of way?
q-3073.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A line made up of triangles marks the place of a conditional stop: the driver stops before it only when giving way requires it. When the road is clear, you may pass without stopping, exercising particular caution.

q-3074.text: Are you allowed to overtake on the left of the vehicle moving on your lane in a place marked in such a way?
q-3074.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings at this place do not allow moving to the left side, and without that, overtaking a vehicle travelling in the same lane is impossible. You must stay behind it and keep a safe distance until the end of the section covered by the ban.

q-3076.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drive into the petrol station through the entry on the left?
q-3076.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Entering the station would require crossing to the left side of the roadway, and the markings at this place do not allow it. You must drive on and use another entrance or turn around where the manoeuvre is permitted.

q-3081.text: Does this sign warn you of recently introduced change in priority rules at the nearest intersection?
q-3081.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This sign warns that priority at the nearest intersection has recently been changed, so habits from previous journeys may mislead you. You must read the signs at the intersection itself carefully and adapt to the new rules.

q-3083.text: If you go straight on will you be driving on a major road?
q-3083.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material indicate that the road with priority runs straight ahead, so by going straight you remain on it. Priority does not, however, release you from watching the intersection and being ready for drivers who fail to give way.

q-3085.text: Are you informed in this situation of the end of the priority road?
q-3085.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material inform of the end of the road with priority. From this point, at the following intersections the general rules apply or priority follows from other signs, so they must be read carefully.

q-3093.text: May any vehicle stop in a lay-by marked in this way in order to drop off a passenger?
q-3093.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A bay marked in this way is intended for public transport vehicles, and only they may stop in it. Other drivers have no right to occupy it, even for the brief moment needed to drop off a passenger.

q-3097.text: You are turning left. Are you allowed in this situation to go before the tram?
q-3097.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority here follows from the signals or signs visible in the material, which open your direction of travel ahead of the rail vehicle. Even so, before entering you must make sure the tram really is stopping or giving way.

q-3098.text: When passing next to a tram at a tram stop not situated at the sidewalk, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-3098.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At such a stop passengers get on and off directly onto the carriageway, so a driver passing must take special care and, if necessary, stop the vehicle. Pedestrians walking to and from the tram have priority.

q-3105.text: Are you prohibited in this situation to drive past the traffic light post with this light displayed?
q-3105.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown prohibits passing the traffic light, so the driver must stop the vehicle before the stop line, and in its absence before the traffic light itself. The absence of other vehicles does not release you from this duty.

q-3109.text: If are involved in an accident in which persons were killed or injured, are you obliged to leave the scene of the accident, upon arrival of the traffic control services?
q-3109.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A participant in an accident with people killed or injured must remain at the scene until the services that arrive have completed their work. Their mere arrival changes nothing; you may leave only to call for help, and must return immediately.

q-3110.text: If you are involved in an accident, in which people are killed or injured, are you allowed to start removing its effects - clean, prepare the tram for towing etc.?
q-3110.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In an accident with people killed or injured, the position of the vehicles may not be changed and traces may not be disturbed until the authorised services arrive and complete their work. The exception is action necessary to save the life and health of the injured.

q-3115.text: Are you prohibited from entering the junction in this situation?
q-3115.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal and the signs visible in the material open your direction, so entering the intersection is permitted. You may enter, however, only when there is room beyond the intersection to leave it without blocking others.

q-3116.text: Does the light displayed over your lane oblige you to stop before the traffic light post?
q-3116.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown above your lane permits travel, so there is no duty to stop before the traffic light. When passing through, however, you must watch the other road users and be ready to react.

q-3118.text: Is the next signal going to prohibit you from entering the junction?
q-3118.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The order of signals in a traffic light is fixed, and after the signal visible in the material comes the signal permitting entry to the intersection. You should therefore prepare to move off, not to stop, while watching the situation ahead.

q-3120.text: Can you expect in this situation that the next light will be red?
q-3120.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signals in a traffic light change in a fixed order, and the signal visible in the material is not followed by red. You should therefore not assume the direction is being closed and brake unnecessarily before the traffic light.

q-3121.text: Does the light displayed over your lane allow you to turn left?
q-3121.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown above the lane determines in which direction you may travel from it, and in this case it permits a left turn. The permission does not, however, release you from the duty to give way where it is required.

q-3122.text: You have just stopped your vehicle. Did you do it in the correct place in consideration of the light signal given?
q-3122.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a signal prohibiting travel, the vehicle stops before the stop line, and where there is none — before the traffic light, so that it can be seen. Stopping further on means occupying space intended for other road users.

q-3123.text: Are you obliged in this situation to obey the signal displayed by the presented person?
q-3123.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The instructions and signals of a person authorised to direct traffic must be obeyed absolutely, even if they contradict the signs or the traffic lights. Such a person ranks above all other means of controlling traffic.

q-3124.text: Can you continue driving straight on, in this situation?
q-3124.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal or sign shown in the material closes your direction of travel, so the vehicle must be stopped and you wait for permission. Driving on would mean entering an area that other road users now have the right to use.

q-3125.text: Are you obliged to stop the vehicle in this situation?
q-3125.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop the vehicle follows from the sign, signal or instruction shown in the material — the driver must comply with it regardless of whether the road appears clear. The stop is made before the line or the place it refers to.

q-3126.text: Is it prohibited to turn right in this situation even when it does not impede movement of other road users?
q-3126.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A prohibition arising from a sign or signal applies unconditionally and does not depend on whether the manoeuvre would obstruct anyone. An empty road is no grounds for turning; you continue in the permitted direction.

q-3127.text: Does the signal displayed by the authorised person indicate that in a moment you will be allowed to enter the junction?
q-3127.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal of the person directing traffic visible in the material announces a change and will shortly open your direction of travel. Until then you should remain before the intersection and move off only after an unambiguous permission.

q-3129.text: Does the signal displayed by the police officer allow you to enter the junction?
q-3129.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The posture and signal of the police officer directing traffic open your direction of travel in this situation, so entering the intersection is permitted. Such a person's instructions take precedence over signs and traffic lights.

q-3130.text: Are you obliged to stop in this situation?
q-3130.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop follows from the sign or signal shown in the material and does not depend on whether the road appears clear. The vehicle stops before the designated place, and driving resumes once the obstacle or the prohibition is gone.

q-3131.text: Are you allowed in this situation to turn right if you do not impede other drivers' movement?
q-3131.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs or signal visible in the material do not permit a right turn from where you are, and the lack of obstruction to others changes nothing. A prohibition must not be circumvented by your own assessment of the situation on the road.

q-3134.text: Are you allowed to go straight across the junction in the presented situation?
q-3134.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal or signs visible in the material do not permit going straight ahead from the lane you are in. You must stop before the intersection or go in the direction that is permitted for that lane.

q-3135.text: Are you obliged in this situation to abide by the signal of the person directing the traffic?
q-3135.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signals of a person directing traffic are binding on the driver and stand above road signs and traffic lights. They must therefore be followed even when they differ from what the traffic light shows.

q-3139.text: Do you have to comply with the light signal in this situation?
q-3139.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to obey the traffic light falls away when traffic is directed by an authorised person, whose instructions take precedence, or when the signal does not concern your lane and direction. You must then drive as that person indicates.

q-3144.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution beyond this sign when changing from the right to the left lane?
q-3144.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A lane change requires particular caution: you must check the mirrors and the blind spot, signal the manoeuvre with the indicator and give way to vehicles travelling in the lane you are entering. Only then may you change your path.

q-3154.text: Do you have to keep a safe distance from the vehicle you are passing?
q-3154.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing an oncoming vehicle, the driver must keep a safe lateral distance and, if necessary, move closer to the right edge of the roadway and reduce speed. The distance is chosen according to speed, the width of the roadway and the type of vehicle being passed.

q-3155.text: When passing a stationary vehicle are you obliged to keep a safe distance from the vehicle?
q-3155.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing a vehicle standing on the road, you must keep a safe lateral distance and exercise particular caution, because a pedestrian may step out from behind such a vehicle or its door may open. If necessary, you should reduce speed.

q-3157.text: When passing a stationary obstacle are you obliged to keep a safe distance from the obstacle?
q-3157.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing an obstacle on the road, the driver must keep a safe lateral distance and particular caution, because a pedestrian or another vehicle may appear from behind the obstacle. The size of the distance is chosen according to speed and the width of the roadway.

q-3158.text: Are you obliged to keep at least 1 metre distance from the stationary object you are passing?
q-3158.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When passing, the rules require a safe distance, whose size depends on speed, the width of the roadway and the type of object. The fixed minimum of 1 m applies to overtaking a cyclist, a moped rider, an electric scooter or a pedestrian, not to every object being passed.

q-3159.text: Are you allowed in this situation to keep whichever distance from the oncoming lorry you are passing?
q-3159.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When passing an oncoming vehicle you must keep a safe lateral distance, and with a large vehicle it should be greater: a lorry creates a gust of air and may have protruding parts of its load. If necessary, reduce speed and move closer to the right edge of the roadway.

q-3170.text: When passing the stationary object on the left, are you obliged to keep a safe distance?
q-3170.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every passing manoeuvre requires keeping a safe distance from the object being passed and particular caution, regardless of which side the object is on. The distance must take into account the driving speed and the possibility of someone suddenly appearing from behind the object.

q-3176.text: Are you warned in this situation of three dangerous bends, the first one to the left?
q-3176.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign together with the plate informs of a series of dangerous bends, and the shape of the symbol indicates the direction of the first one. Before such a stretch you must slow down, because visibility in the bends is limited and overtaking is difficult.

q-3177.text: Does the sign placed on the right roadway mean that it is closed to the traffic?
q-3177.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A prohibition sign installed on a roadway closes it to traffic, so you must not enter it. Traffic then uses the other roadway, in accordance with the designated traffic arrangement, and driving past the sign is a violation of the prohibition.

q-3179.text: Does the horizontal sign indicate the place to stop in order to yield the right of way?
q-3179.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This road marking indicates the place where the driver is to stop if giving way requires it. By itself it does not always require stopping — you must, however, approach so as to have a good view of the road with priority.

q-3184.text: Are you obliged in this situation, after going beyond the traffic lights, to stop in the place indicated by the "stop" sign?
q-3184.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When the traffic lights are working and have permitted entry, they decide the passage, and the stop sign applies when the lights are switched off or show a flashing yellow. After passing the traffic light you should clear the intersection promptly, not stop again.

q-3187.text: Does the vehicle driver have a better ability to asses the risk on the road after using a small amount of drugs?
q-3187.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Even a small dose of a narcotic impairs judgement, lengthens reaction time and weakens concentration, and often gives a false sense of confidence. Driving after taking such a substance is prohibited and carries serious consequences.

q-3194.text: In this situation, does the tram driver have the right of passage over vehicles driving in the transverse road?
q-3194.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material gives the tram's direction of travel priority over the side road, so the tram driver may cross first. Even so, they must watch the side road and be ready to brake should someone fail to give way.

q-3195.text: In this situation, does the tram driver have the right of passage over vehicles driving on the nearest transverse road?
q-3195.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material does not give the tramway priority over the nearest cross carriageway, so the tram driver must give way. Being a rail vehicle gives the tram an advantage only at a junction of equal roads, not where signs decide.

q-3199.text: In this situation, does the tram driver have the right of passage over the tram driving on the transverse track?
q-3199.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Between two rail vehicles priority is decided by the general rules and the signing, and here the tram on the cross track has the advantage. The tram driver must therefore stop before the crossing of the tracks and let the approaching tram through.

q-3210.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have the right of way over the vehicle coming straight from the opposite direction?
q-3210.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning left, you must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction that are going straight ahead or turning right. The manoeuvre is performed only when you are sure it will not force anyone to brake or change direction.

q-3212.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have to yield the right of way to the rail vehicle?
q-3212.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When turning left, you must give way to a rail vehicle regardless of the side from which it approaches. A tram has a long braking distance and cannot steer around an obstacle, so you must not enter the tracks in front of it.

q-3230.text: You intend to turn left at the junction. Should you speed up in this situation, in order to pass before the oncoming vehicles?
q-3230.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver turning left gives way to oncoming vehicles, and accelerating in order to force your way through is dangerous and not permitted. You must wait for a gap that allows the manoeuvre without disturbing traffic.

q-3232.text: Does the vehicle driver have difficulties in simultaneous performance of two or more activities at the same time after alcohol consumption?
q-3232.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Alcohol narrows the field of attention and makes it harder to divide it between several tasks, for example watching the road, controlling speed and changing gear. Reaction time also grows, which makes ordinary situations on the road dangerous.

q-3233.text: Do you have to abide by the vertical warning sign "give way" in this situation?
q-3233.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty arising from the sign ceases when traffic at the intersection is directed by an authorised person or when working traffic lights give your direction a permitting signal. These indications take precedence over the vertical sign.

q-3235.text: You intend to go straight ahead. Are you obliged to give way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-3235.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this situation your direction of travel has priority, as follows from the signs visible in the material, so the right-hand rule does not apply. Even so, when approaching the intersection, stay cautious and watch the vehicle on the right.

q-3340.text: Which of the following actions should you perform to move off smoothly?

options.C: First increase the engine revolutions significantly and then quickly disengage the clutch pedal.

q-3340.explanation: Correct answer: A. A smooth start means gradually releasing the clutch pedal while gently adding throttle at the same time. Dropping the clutch suddenly or raising the revs hard beforehand ends in a jolt, a stalled engine or wheelspin.
