q-3346.text: In case of the vehicle being stopped by traffic congestion, are you obliged beyond this sign to keep a distance of not less than 5 metres from the vehicle in front?
q-3346.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On a section marked with this sign, when the vehicle stops because of a jam, you must keep a distance of not less than 5 m from the vehicle in front. The free space makes it easier to evacuate people and for the emergency services to get through.

q-3353.text: What is forbidden when driving a passenger car?

options.B: Using a phone which requires holding a mouthpiece in a hand.
options.C: Using cruise control in a built-up area.

q-3353.explanation: Correct answer: B. While driving you may not use a phone that requires holding the handset or microphone in the hand, because it occupies the driver's hand and attention. Carrying an intoxicated person and using cruise control in a built-up area are not prohibited.

q-3359.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drop off a passenger in this lay-by?
q-3359.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible bay is intended for public transport vehicles, so other drivers may not stop in it even for a moment. Stopping there blocks the bus or tram and forces passengers to get off onto the carriageway.

q-3362.text: Can you overtake the vehicle in front of you in this situation?
q-3362.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The conditions or signs visible in the material rule out overtaking — there is no clear and clearly visible section, or the manoeuvre is prohibited at this place. You must stay behind the vehicle in front and keep a safe distance.

q-3363.text: Is it reasonable to use the horn repeatedly instead of stopping the vehicle?
q-3363.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn does not replace the duty to stop or give way and gives no right to force your way through. In this situation you must slow down and stop the vehicle; hurrying others along with the horn only increases the risk.

q-3364.text: You intend to make a U-turn. Is there going to be a collision with the tram?
q-3364.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The manoeuvre can be performed without entering the tram's path, so no collision will occur. Turning around does, however, require judging the distance and speed of the rail vehicle and giving way to it wherever the tracks must be crossed.

q-3366.text: Is it allowed to use a sound signal in this situation?
q-3366.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In a built-up area the horn may be used only when necessary to warn of an immediate danger, and no such need exists here. Instead of sounding the horn, you should slow down and watch the situation.

q-3367.text: Should you increase the distance from the drunk cyclist when passing him?
q-3367.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A drunk cyclist loses balance and may suddenly swerve sideways, so the distance must be increased beyond the usual minimum and speed clearly reduced. The manoeuvre is performed only when the width of the roadway allows a safe path.

q-3370.text: Are you allowed in this situation to go before the rail vehicle on the left of the road?
q-3370.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In this situation priority follows from the signing and signals shown in the material, which open your direction of travel ahead of the rail vehicle. Before entering the tracks, however, you must make sure the tram really is slowing down or standing.

q-3372.text: You intend to go straight ahead. Are you obliged to give way to the oncoming vehicle which is turning left?
q-3372.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Going straight ahead has priority over an oncoming vehicle that is turning left and crossing your path — it is that vehicle that must give way. Despite having priority, you should watch it and be ready to react.

q-3373.text: You intend to go straight ahead. Have you got priority over the vehicles at the intersection?
q-3373.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material give your direction priority over the vehicles on the intersection, so you may pass first. Priority does not, however, release you from watching and being ready to brake if someone fails to give way.

q-3374.text: You intend to go straight ahead. Are you obliged to give way to the tram which is turning left?
q-3374.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A tram turning left crosses the straight-ahead direction, and in this situation it is the tram that gives way. It is still worth watching the rail vehicle and being ready to slow down, because its braking distance is long and it cannot break off the manoeuvre at any point.

q-3378.text: You intend to turn left. Have you got priority over the oncoming vehicle going straight?
q-3378.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning left, you cross the path of oncoming vehicles and must give way to them. The manoeuvre is performed only after judging their distance and speed, without forcing anyone to brake harshly.

q-3384.text: Are you obliged in this situation to give way to the tram?
q-3384.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In this situation the rail vehicle has priority, so you must let it pass and not enter its path. A tram takes much longer to brake than a car and cannot leave the tracks, so forcing your way in front of it is particularly dangerous.

q-3390.text: Have you got priority in this situation over the vehicle coming from the opposite direction, turning left?
q-3390.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle turning left crosses the path of oncoming vehicles, so it is that vehicle that gives way, and you go first. You should not, however, assume the driver will certainly wait — it is worth staying ready to brake.

q-3399.text: Are you allowed in this situation to go before the oncoming vehicle?
q-3399.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver turning left gives way to oncoming vehicles, so you must let them pass and only then perform the manoeuvre. Driving in front of the approaching vehicle would force it to brake and risk a front-side collision.

q-3402.text: Does the arrow signal displayed indicate that the traffic may turn left without conflict with other road users?
q-3402.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This signal permits driving in the direction indicated and at the same time means that the conflicting directions are closed at that time. Even so, you must watch the junction, because someone may enter it against the signals.

q-3414.text: Are you informed in this situation of the beginning of a major road?
q-3414.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign visible in the material has a different meaning and does not inform of the beginning of a road with priority. The beginning of such a road is marked by a separate sign in the shape of a yellow diamond, and priority at the nearest intersection is decided by the signs on the spot.

q-3415.text: Are you allowed to enter the intersection in this situation?
q-3415.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal or sign visible in the material closes the entry to the intersection, so you must stop before it and wait for permission. Entering would block the way of those who currently have the right to pass.

q-3417.text: Are you allowed to stop the vehicle on the roadway directly behind this junction?
q-3417.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping a vehicle directly beyond an intersection is prohibited, because it blocks the exit and forces others to stop on the intersection itself. For parking you must find a place further on, where the vehicle does not obstruct traffic or restrict visibility.

q-3418.text: In the presented situation are you obliged to stop in all cases?
q-3418.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop arising from the visible signing is unconditional: the vehicle must be stopped at the designated place even when nobody is approaching. Only after stopping and assessing the situation may you continue.

q-3419.text: If you want to continue driving left beyond the level crossing, should you stop before the half-barrier?
q-3419.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before a lowered half-barrier you must stop, and going around it by entering the part of the roadway intended for the opposite direction is prohibited. The intention to turn left beyond the crossing changes nothing — you drive on after the crossing opens.

q-3420.text: Should you take into account the possibility of a cyclist entering the road in this situation?
q-3420.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A cyclist near the roadway may suddenly ride onto it, especially when it is a child or when the cycle path ends. You must therefore reduce speed, increase the distance and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-3421.text: Is overtaking a cyclist forbidden in this situation?
q-3421.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place no overtaking ban applies, so the manoeuvre is permitted if the conditions allow it. When overtaking a cyclist, you must keep a distance of not less than 1 m and first make sure the road ahead of the vehicle is clear.

q-3426.text: May the vehicle left on the road beyond this sign be removed at the cost of the owner?
q-3426.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle left in breach of the prohibition arising from the sign may be towed away, and the costs of removal and storage are charged to the owner. That is why, before leaving the vehicle, you must check the signs in force on the section concerned.

q-3429.text: Which of the following actions should you perform when driving a passenger car at night in a fog?

options.B: Turn on the high-beam lights in order to improve visibility.
options.C: Drive very close to the car in front in order to see its sidelights.

q-3429.explanation: Correct answer: A. In fog visibility is severely limited, so speed must be reduced so that you can stop the vehicle within the distance you can see. Main-beam headlights reflect off the droplets and worsen visibility, and driving close behind the vehicle ahead removes the reserve for braking.

q-3431.text: In the presented situation, does the illuminated light allow you to go beyond the traffic lights?
q-3431.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signals shown close your direction of travel, so the vehicle must be stopped before the stop line, and in its absence before the traffic light. You may move off only after the signal permitting travel appears.

q-3432.text: In the presented situation, does the illuminated light prohibit you from going beyond the traffic lights?
q-3432.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signals shown prohibit passing the traffic light, so the driver must stop the vehicle before the stop line, and where there is none — before the traffic light itself. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the intersection seems empty.

q-3433.text: In the presented situation, does the illuminated light prohibit drivers going straight from driving beyond the traffic lights?
q-3433.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown for going straight ahead closes that direction, so those going straight must stop before the traffic light. A signal permitting another direction does not entitle you to go straight — what counts is the indication for your own path.

q-3434.text: In the presented situation, can you resume driving only after the tram has moved off?
q-3434.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You do not have to wait until the tram moves off — you may continue when passengers have finished getting on and off and the way is clear. Until then particular caution applies and pedestrians walking to and from the tram have priority.

q-3439.text: Does the plate under this sign indicate the end of the road with dangerous bends?
q-3439.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate placed under the sign defines its scope, and in this case indicates the end of the section with dangerous bends. From that point the warning no longer applies, but speed is still chosen to suit the road conditions.

q-3443.text: Are you allowed in this situation to comply with indications of the white arrows?
q-3443.explanation: Correct answer: NO. White arrows are permanent markings, and temporary yellow markings and the instructions of a person directing traffic take precedence over them. You must therefore follow the current, overriding traffic arrangement, not the white arrows.

q-3444.text: You intend to turn right. Do you have the right of way over the motorcyclist turning left?
q-3444.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this situation the motorcyclist has priority, so before turning right you must let them pass. A two-wheeler is narrow and its speed and distance are easy to underestimate, so before the manoeuvre you must watch the road carefully.

q-3445.text: You intend to make a U-turn. Do you have to yield the right of way to the rail vehicle?
q-3445.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning around gives way to a rail vehicle and to the other road users — the manoeuvre may be started only when it will not obstruct anyone. A tram runs on a fixed track and cannot leave the road.

q-3454.text: You intend to continue going straight ahead. Do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-3454.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Going straight ahead, you have priority over the vehicle approaching from the left — it has your vehicle on its right and must give way. Even so, enter the intersection only after making sure the driver on the left really is slowing down.

q-3456.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-3456.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The vehicle approaching from the right has priority here, so the driver turning left must wait until it has passed. You begin the turn only when it will not force anyone to change speed or direction.

q-3458.text: Can you continue overtaking in this situation?
q-3458.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In this situation no ban on overtaking applies and there is no obstacle preventing a safe completion of the manoeuvre, so you may continue it. Overtaking ends with a smooth return to your lane without forcing the vehicle overtaken to brake.

q-3459.text: Are you obliged to observe the behaviour of the pedestrians in this situation?
q-3459.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver is obliged to watch pedestrians on and beside the road and to anticipate that they may step onto the roadway. The principle of limited trust requires allowing for their mistake, reducing speed and being ready to stop.

q-3460.text: Does the speed limit under this warning sign apply only to the area of road works and ceases to apply upon leaving this area?
q-3460.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A speed limit placed beneath a warning sign applies until the place where it is cancelled by the appropriate sign or by a sign giving a different value. Merely passing the roadworks does not lift it, so accelerating right after the last machine is a mistake.

q-3463.text: When passing this obstacle are you obliged to keep a safe distance from it?
q-3463.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing is performed with a safe distance from the object being passed, chosen according to speed and the width of the roadway. The distance must also suffice if a pedestrian steps out from behind the obstacle or the door of a stationary vehicle opens.

q-3465.text: You intend to make a U-turn at the junction while the vehicle is entering the junction. Are you obliged to yield the right of way?
q-3465.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Turning around at an intersection requires giving way to vehicles entering it in accordance with the priority in force. The manoeuvre may be performed only when it will obstruct no one; merely occupying the intersection gives no rights.

q-3466.text: You intend to go straight ahead. Have you got priority over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-3466.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The vehicle approaching from the right has priority, so it is you who must give way, even though you are going straight ahead. You should approach the intersection at a speed that allows you to stop before it.

q-3467.text: You intend to turn left. Have you got priority over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-3467.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The order of passage here is decided by the priority arising from the signs or signals visible in the material, not by the right-hand rule alone — it is the vehicle approaching from the right that must give way to you. When turning left, however, watch whether it really is slowing down.

q-3468.text: Are you allowed in this situation to turn to the parking space situated on the left-hand side of the road?
q-3468.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A left turn is not permitted here, because the markings visible in the material prohibit crossing to the opposite side of the roadway. The entrance to such a car park must be sought at a place where the manoeuvre is permitted, or reached by another route.

q-3469.text: In this situation, is the tram driver obliged to stop just before the line outlined by triangles?
q-3469.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A line made up of rectangles marks a conditional stopping place — the vehicle stops there when there is a duty to give way. It may be crossed only when driving on does not endanger other road users.

q-3477.text: In this situation, does the tram driver have the right of passage over trams that may approach from the left side?
q-3477.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The tram driver has no priority here over trams that may approach from the left — the order is decided by the signals and signing shown in the material, not by the layout of the tracks itself. Before entering, make sure nothing is approaching from the left.

q-3484.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive straight ahead?
q-3484.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Going straight ahead is permitted by the signal or signing shown in the material, so that direction is allowed. You may move off, however, only after making sure the road beyond the junction is clear and the vehicle will not block it.

q-3485.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn left?
q-3485.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material does not prohibit a left turn, so the manoeuvre is permitted. Before carrying it out, signal your intention, take special care and give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction and to pedestrians crossing the carriageway.

q-3486.text: In this situation, should you be prepared to enter the intersection?
q-3486.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown in the material announces that permission to proceed is imminent, so prepare to move off and watch your surroundings. Entry, however, takes place only once the permitting signal appears and you have made sure the junction can be left.

q-3492.text: Are you allowed to stop signalling the intention to change the direction of travel immediately after you start the manoeuvre?
q-3492.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The indicator must work for the whole duration of the manoeuvre — from the signal given in advance until its completion. Switching the indicator off right after starting to change direction deprives others of information about your intention and misleads them.

q-3493.text: In this situation, are you required to use an indicator when changing the driving trajectory?
q-3493.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every change of course is signalled in advance with the indicator, so that the other road users know which way you intend to move. The signal does not, however, release you from making sure the manoeuvre will cut in on nobody.

q-3494.text: In this situation, are you obliged to apply the principle of limited trust?
q-3494.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The principle of limited trust applies whenever the behaviour of another road user indicates that they may act incorrectly. You must then slow down, watch that road user closely and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-3496.text: In this situation, are you obliged to allow the driver to leave the intersection?
q-3496.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle that is already on the junction must be allowed to leave it, even if you yourself have priority or a permitting signal. Forcing your way in ends with the junction blocked and all directions brought to a standstill.

q-3499.text: In this situation, should you anticipate that the driver may enter the track, thus blocking the crossing?
q-3499.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You must anticipate that the car driver will enter the tramway and stop on it, blocking the passage. That is why, approaching, you reduce speed and stay ready to brake instead of assuming the track will remain clear.

q-3502.text: In this situation, should the tram driver wait until the pedestrian leaves the crossing?
q-3502.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A pedestrian already on the crossing has priority, so the tram driver waits until they step off the tramway and leave the crossing. Moving towards them in the hope that they will quicken their step is not acceptable — a tram has a long braking distance.

q-3507.text: Is it permissible to overtake on crossings for cyclists, on which traffic is directed?
q-3507.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban on overtaking at a cycle crossing and directly before it does not apply where traffic is directed by light signals or by a person authorised to do so. The manoeuvre is still carried out with special care towards cyclists.

q-3523.text: You are driving a passenger car. How should you behave while driving through a wide puddle?
q-3523.explanation: Correct answer: C. A large puddle is driven through after smoothly reducing speed: at high speed the tyres lose contact with the surface and aquaplaning occurs, and harsh braking on water risks a skid. After leaving it, it is worth gently drying the brakes.

q-3526.text: You intend to turn diagonally left. Do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-3526.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning left diagonally, you give way to the vehicle approaching from the right — it goes first. The manoeuvre may be performed only when it will not force another driver to brake or change direction.

q-3527.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-3527.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The vehicle approaching from the right has priority here, so the driver turning left must wait until it has passed. You begin the turn only when it will not force anyone to change speed or direction.

q-3528.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-3528.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority belongs to you, and the vehicle approaching from the left is obliged to give way. When turning left, however, you must let pass vehicles coming straight from the opposite direction and pedestrians stepping onto the cross roadway.

q-3530.text: You intend to continue going straight. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the approaching vehicle?
q-3530.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Despite going straight ahead, you must give way to the approaching vehicle — this follows from the priority arrangement set by the signs or signals visible in the material. You may enter its path only after it has passed.

q-3531.text: Are you obliged to stop the vehicle in this situation?
q-3531.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Nothing here imposes a duty to stop the vehicle — there is no sign, no signal and no obstacle that would require it. It is enough to take care, adjust your speed and stay ready to stop should the situation change.

q-3532.text: Are you obliged to keep a safe distance when passing a stationary vehicle?
q-3532.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing is performed keeping a safe distance from the vehicle or obstacle being passed, chosen according to speed and the road conditions. The distance is to protect against a door opening, the passed vehicle moving off and a pedestrian stepping out from behind the obstacle.

q-3534.text: Is it obligatory in this situation to decrease the speed of the vehicle in order to execute the passing manoeuvre safely?
q-3534.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Speed is chosen according to the conditions, and passing requires ensuring a safe distance and the ability to stop before a sudden obstacle. Reducing speed gives time to react if someone appears from behind the object being passed.

q-3535.text: Will you be acting accordingly if you go past the vehicle in front from the right side?
q-3535.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle that has stopped or is signalling an intention to turn left is passed on its right side, provided there is enough room. The manoeuvre is performed slowly, watching whether anyone is stepping or driving out from behind the vehicle being passed.

q-3540.text: Are you obliged to stop your vehicle before the last car of a tram?
q-3540.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to stop behind a tram applies at a stop without an island when passengers are getting on or off. Here those conditions are not met, so it is enough to drive carefully, slowly and without obstructing pedestrians.

q-3541.text: Are you allowed to drive onto the solid line dividing the traffic lanes?
q-3541.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A solid line separating lanes must not be crossed or driven on — the vehicle must remain on its own side of that line. A lane change is planned where the line is broken.

q-3542.text: Should you in this situation, increase attention and be prepared for the possibility of a pedestrian emerging from the left side of the roadway?
q-3542.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A pedestrian may step onto the roadway also from the left side, so the driver watches the full width of the road and its surroundings, not only the right shoulder. Heightened attention and readiness to brake let you stop the vehicle before the pedestrian.

q-3544.text: Are you obliged to use the low-beam lights in this situation?
q-3544.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A moving vehicle must be lit around the clock, all year round. After dusk, in a tunnel and when the clarity of the air is reduced, dipped headlights are compulsory, not daytime running lights alone.

q-3545.text: Does this horizontal sign indicate the place to stop only in the situation when there is a vehicle approaching on the transverse road?
q-3545.explanation: Correct answer: NO. This line marks the stopping place whenever a stop is required, not only for a vehicle approaching on the cross road. You must also stop to give way to pedestrians or cyclists, and where stopping is mandatory — even when the road is empty.

q-3546.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake a railway vehicle?
q-3546.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place overtaking the rail vehicle is not permitted — the conditions and the rules in force here do not allow the manoeuvre to be safely started or completed. Besides, a tram running along the middle of the roadway is overtaken on the right, not on the left.

q-3547.text: You intend to continue driving straight ahead. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-3547.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At an intersection where priority is not determined by signs or signals, the right-hand rule applies. A driver going straight ahead also gives way to a vehicle approaching from the right and enters only when they will not obstruct it.

q-3548.text: Is it allowed to stopover at the entry to the gate?
q-3548.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Parking in a place that obstructs entry or exit, in particular at a gateway, is prohibited, because it blocks access to the property. A short stop is permitted only when it obstructs no one's passage.

q-3549.text: You intend to drive straight on. Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-3549.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At an intersection where priority is not determined by signs or signals, the right-hand rule applies. A driver going straight ahead also gives way to a vehicle approaching from the right and enters only when they will not obstruct it.

q-3550.text: Do you have to yield the right of way to the motorcyclist when turning left in this situation?
q-3550.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning left, you give way to oncoming vehicles that are going straight ahead or turning right. The motorcyclist is not moving in that way here, so the duty to give way does not arise — even so, signal the manoeuvre in advance and watch them.

q-3551.text: You are turning left and the car driver intends to drive straight on. Do you have the right of way over him?
q-3551.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The order is decided by the priority arrangement arising from the signs or signals visible in the material, not by the direction of travel alone — the car driver going straight ahead must give way to you. Turn, however, only after making sure they really are slowing down.

q-3553.text: You intend to turn right. Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-3553.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning right, you do not give way to the vehicle approaching from the left — for that driver you are on the right, and it is they who must give way. Perform the manoeuvre by the right edge of the roadway, signalling it in advance.

q-3554.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have to yield the right of way to the motorcyclist?
q-3554.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When turning left, you give way to oncoming vehicles, and a motorcycle is no exception here. A motorcycle's narrow silhouette makes it easy to judge it as further away and slower, so it is better to wait until it has passed.

q-3556.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have the right of way over the vehicle coming from the opposite direction?
q-3556.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority here follows from the signs and signals visible in the material, not from the direction of travel alone — it is the oncoming vehicle that must give way. Still make the turn carefully, checking the other driver's intention.

q-3557.text: You intend to turn left and the driver of the oncoming vehicle intends to turn right. Do you have to yield the right of way to him?
q-3557.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When one driver turns left and the oncoming one turns right, their paths do not cross — each enters the same road on their own right-hand side. You must, however, make sure the other driver really is turning.

q-3561.text: You are going straight and the driver on the motorcycle intends to turn left. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the motorcyclist?
q-3561.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A vehicle going straight ahead has priority over an oncoming vehicle turning left — it is the motorcyclist who must wait. Watch them, however, because a driver turning left often underestimates the speed of the approaching vehicle.

q-3562.text: You intend to go straight on. Are you obliged to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle turning left?
q-3562.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Going straight ahead, you do not give way to the motorcyclist turning left from the opposite direction — it is they who must wait until you have passed. Stay cautious, however, and be ready to brake if they move off in front of your vehicle.

q-3563.text: The vehicle moving next you is overtaking you. Are you allowed to accelerate in this situation?
q-3563.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver who is being overtaken must not increase speed — they are to drive by the right edge of their lane and, if necessary, make the manoeuvre easier. Accelerating prolongs the overtaking and keeps the overtaking driver on the opposite lane.

q-3566.text: When driving at the speed of 50 km/h should you slow down while approaching the closest junction when the situation on the right hand side of the road is not adequately visible?
q-3566.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When approaching an intersection with limited visibility, you must exercise particular caution and reduce speed enough to be able to stop before a vehicle approaching from the right. The permitted 50 km/h is an upper limit, not a recommended speed.

q-3567.text: Can you stop your vehicle in any place if there is a need to yield the right of way to the vehicle?
q-3567.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When giving way, you stop the vehicle at the place designated by signs and lines: before the stop line, and where there is none — before the intersection, so as to see the road with priority. You must not stop on a pedestrian crossing or on the tram tracks.

q-3568.text: Are you posing a threat to safety on the road in this situation?
q-3568.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Such a way of driving breaches the safety rules and may force other road users to brake sharply or change course. The driver must drive so as not to cause danger or obstruction to anyone.

q-3573.text: You witness a pedestrian being run down. How should you behave?

options.A: Not to take any action because the first aid must be given by the person who caused the accident.
options.C: Stop and give the first aid to the injured person.

q-3573.explanation: Correct answer: C. A witness to an accident must stop, call medical help and give the casualty first aid as far as they are able. Waiting for the person at fault to act, or calling roadside assistance, does not save the life of a pedestrian who has been hit.

q-3583.text: Can you overtake the vehicle in this situation?
q-3583.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The conditions or signs visible in the material rule out overtaking — there is no clear and clearly visible section, or the manoeuvre is prohibited at this place. You must stay behind the vehicle in front and keep a safe distance.

q-3585.text: You are turning right and the driver of the oncoming car intends to turn left. Do you have the right of way over him?
q-3585.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning left gives way to oncoming vehicles, including those turning right. Your path is shorter and runs by the right edge, so it is that driver who must wait.

q-3615.text: At what speed are you allowed to drive a passenger car with a trailer on the road beyond this sign?
q-3615.explanation: Correct answer: B. A combination of a car and a trailer may travel at no more than 80 km/h on the road beyond this sign — the high limits that apply on it concern only vehicles without a trailer. A trailer lengthens the braking distance and worsens the stability of the combination.

q-3617.text: At what maximum speed are you allowed to drive a passenger car on the road beyond this sign?
q-3617.explanation: Correct answer: C. Beyond this sign a car may travel at no more than 140 km/h — the highest permitted speed for this category of road. Speed must always be adapted to the traffic, visibility and the state of the surface, though.

q-3618.text: At what speed are you allowed to drive a passenger car on the road beyond this sign?
q-3618.explanation: Correct answer: C. Beyond this sign a car may travel at no more than 90 km/h — that is the permitted speed on a road of this category outside a built-up area. Higher values are reserved for roads with separate carriageways for each direction.

q-3620.text: At what speed are you allowed to drive a passenger car on the road beyond this sign?
q-3620.explanation: Correct answer: A. This sign introduces a residential zone, in which the permitted speed is 20 km/h. The pedestrian there uses the whole width of the road and has priority over vehicles, and parking is allowed only in designated places.

q-3623.text: At what speed are you allowed to drive a passenger car on the road beyond this sign?
q-3623.explanation: Correct answer: B. Beyond this sign a car may travel at no more than 120 km/h — that limit applies on a road of this category with separate carriageways for the two directions. The value of 140 km/h is reserved for another category of road.

q-3625.text: What distance should you keep while passing another vehicle in a passenger car?

options.A: Safe, but not shorter than 1.5 metres.
options.B: Safe, dependent on the width of the road and traffic conditions.
options.C: Safe, that is always the same.

q-3625.explanation: Correct answer: B. When passing an oncoming vehicle, the rules give no fixed number of metres — the distance is to be safe, that is, suited to the width of the carriageway, the speed and the traffic conditions. On a narrow, wet or poorly visible road you must increase it and slow down.

q-3626.text: During which of the following manoeuvres are you obliged to keep a distance not less than 1 metres from the vehicle?
q-3626.explanation: Correct answer: B. When overtaking a cyclist, the driver must keep a distance of no less than 1 m. The same requirement applies to overtaking a moped, a motorcycle and a column of pedestrians; when passing oncoming traffic or an obstacle, the distance is defined as safe, with no figure given.

q-3627.text: What distance should you keep when passing a stationary obstacle on the road in a passenger car?

options.A: Safe, but not less than 0.8 metres.
options.C: Safe, depending on the width of the road and traffic conditions.

q-3627.explanation: Correct answer: C. For passing an obstacle, the rules specify no particular number of metres — the distance is to be safe, suited to the width of the carriageway, the speed and the traffic conditions. It must also be enough should a pedestrian suddenly step out from behind the obstacle.

q-3628.text: What distance should you keep when overtaking a passenger car?

options.A: Safe, dependent on the width of the road and traffic conditions.

q-3628.explanation: Correct answer: A. When overtaking a car, the rules give no number of metres — the distance is to be safe, suited to the width of the carriageway, the speed and the traffic conditions. The minimum of 1 m applies when overtaking a bicycle, a moped, a motorcycle and a column of pedestrians.

q-3629.text: What distance should you keep when overtaking a motorcycle?

options.A: Safe but not longer than 0.5 metres.
options.B: Safe but not longer than 1 metre.
options.C: Safe but not shorter than 1 metre.

q-3629.explanation: Correct answer: C. When overtaking a motorcycle, the driver must keep a distance that is safe and no less than 1 m. The value given is a minimum: at higher speed or in gusts of wind the distance must be increased, because a two-wheeler is easily knocked off its line.

q-3630.text: What distance should you keep while overtaking a group of pedestrians?

options.A: Safe but not shorter than 0.6 metres.
options.B: Safe but not shorter than 0.8 metres.
options.C: Safe but not shorter than 1 metre.

q-3630.explanation: Correct answer: C. When overtaking a column of pedestrians, the driver keeps a distance that is safe and no less than 1 m. The same requirement applies to a bicycle, a moped and a motorcycle; with a column of pedestrians you must additionally expect it to sway suddenly.

q-3634.text: In what way does doubling of the speed of a passenger car influence the braking distance?

options.C: It has no influence on the braking distance.

q-3634.explanation: Correct answer: B. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed, so doubling the speed makes that distance four times longer. That is why even a small increase in speed greatly reduces the chance of stopping before an obstacle.

q-3635.text: The driver of the oncoming car intends to turn left. Do you have to yield the right of way to him?
q-3635.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The order here is decided by the priority arising from the signs or signals visible in the material, not by the direction of travel alone — the oncoming vehicle goes first. Wait until it clears the intersection and only then move off.

q-3642.text: You are driving a motor vehicle. Does this sign prohibit you from overtaking multi-track motor vehicles?
q-3642.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This sign prohibits the driver of a motor vehicle from overtaking other multi-track motor vehicles. The ban does not cover two-wheeled or non-motor vehicles and applies up to the nearest intersection or to the sign that cancels it.

q-3643.text: You are driving a motor vehicle. Does this sign prohibit you from overtaking single-track motor vehicles?
q-3643.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The ban arising from this sign concerns only multi-track motor vehicles, so a motorcycle or moped may be overtaken. The manoeuvre must, however, be performed with a distance of not less than 1 m and only when it is safe.

q-3645.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle and then change lanes, if you want to leave the highway at the nearest exit?
q-3645.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On a motorway you overtake on the left, and nothing prohibits completing such a manoeuvre before the exit. After overtaking, however, you must signal the lane change in good time and move into the exit lane without cutting in front of anyone.

q-3650.text: What distance from the preceding vehicle should you keep when driving a passenger car outside the built-up area in a tunnel 600 metres long?
q-3650.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a tunnel longer than 500 m outside a built-up area, the driver of a car keeps a distance of no less than 50 m from the vehicle ahead. This distance makes evacuation and access for the rescue services easier in the event of a fire or collision.

q-3651.text: Which of the following factors has direct influence on the stopping distance of the passenger car?
q-3651.explanation: Correct answer: A. The stopping distance is the sum of the distance covered during the driver's reaction time and the braking distance, so reaction time affects it directly. Tiredness, conversation or alcohol lengthen that time, and with it the whole stopping distance.

q-3652.text: Which of the following factors has direct influence on the stopping distance of the passenger car?

options.B: The speed and the condition of the road surface.

q-3652.explanation: Correct answer: B. The stopping distance is directly affected by speed, because the braking distance grows with its square, and by the state of the surface, on which tyre grip depends. The mass of a passenger or of the vehicle is not a direct factor here.

q-3653.text: Can you use the horn if the presented vehicle starts to change the lane while you are overtaking?
q-3653.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The horn may be used when it is necessary to warn of a danger, and another vehicle moving into your lane during overtaking is precisely such a case. Apart from warning of a danger, the horn must not be used in a built-up area.

q-3655.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drive with the front fog lights on?
q-3655.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Front fog lights may be switched on only in fog, precipitation or another severe reduction in the clarity of the air. In good visibility they needlessly dazzle other drivers, so their use is not allowed.

q-3657.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the preceding vehicle?
q-3657.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is prohibited at this place — this follows from the signs visible in the material and from the lack of conditions for completing the manoeuvre safely. You may overtake only where the prohibition ceases to apply and visibility is sufficient.

q-3658.text: You are involved in a road accident. Are you obliged to give first aid to the injured persons if you do not have medical qualifications?
q-3658.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident must help the casualties as far as they are able: call the emergency services, secure the scene and carry out simple life-saving actions. A lack of medical training does not release them from this duty.

q-3661.text: Are you obliged to always stop the vehicle before the level crossing?
q-3661.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An unconditional stop before a railway crossing is required only where a sign or signal orders it, or when the barriers are closed or beginning to close. In other cases particular caution and making sure the tracks are clear are enough.

q-3662.text: Are you obliged to stop in the designated place even when you have made sure that there is no rail vehicle approaching?
q-3662.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The designated place shows where to stop the vehicle if the need arises, but in itself it does not order a stop. When, having made sure, nothing is approaching, you may drive through without stopping, taking special care.

q-3664.text: Before driving into the track-way directly before the vehicle in front, are you obliged to make sure that there is no rail vehicle approaching?
q-3664.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before entering the tracks you must make sure no rail vehicle is approaching and that there is room beyond the tracks to stop the whole vehicle. Following right behind the vehicle in front does not release you from assessing the situation yourself.

q-3667.text: When approaching the tram track, are you obliged to make sure that there is no rail vehicle approaching?
q-3667.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When approaching a tram crossing, the driver exercises particular caution and makes sure no rail vehicle is approaching. A tram has a long braking distance and cannot steer around an obstacle, so entering the tracks must be entirely certain.

q-3669.text: As the driver of a vehicle involved in a road accident, are you obliged to give first aid to casualties?
q-3669.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver involved in an accident must give the victims the necessary help and call the rescue services. Help is given to the extent possible for the person concerned, while also looking after their own safety and marking the scene.

q-3670.text: When driving a vehicle involved in a road accident in which people are injured, are you obliged to remove the vehicle from the scene of the accident not to obstruct the traffic?
q-3670.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When people have been injured or killed in an accident, the vehicles may not be moved until the Police arrive, because the position of the vehicles and the traces serve to establish what happened. The scene is to be marked and secured, not cleared.

q-3672.text: You have participated in a road accident in which people got injured. Are you obliged to remain at the scene of the accident?
q-3672.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident with injured people stays at the scene until the Police arrive, gives help, calls the services and secures the scene. They may leave only when saving a life requires it — and must then return immediately.

q-3673.text: You have been involved in a road accident as the driver of the vehicle. After administering first aid to the injured persons, are you allowed to leave the scene of the accident before the arrival of the police?
q-3673.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Helping the injured does not end the driver's duties: they must stay at the scene until the Police arrive, give their details and make it possible to establish what happened. Leaving before the services arrive is treated as fleeing the scene of an accident.

q-3675.text: As a vehicle driver involved in a road accident, in which a person got killed, are you obliged to remain at the scene of the accident?
q-3675.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When someone has been killed in an accident, the driver remains at the scene until the Police arrive, calls the services, secures and marks the scene, and does not change the position of the vehicles or the traces. Leaving the scene of the accident is a crime.

q-3678.text: Does this line composed of white reflective road studs mark the left edge of the roadway?
q-3678.explanation: Correct answer: YES. White reflective road studs mark the left edge of the carriageway, and red ones the right edge. The colour of the studs lets you quickly judge the course of the road and your own position on the carriageway at night.

q-3679.text: Are you allowed in this situation to go straight across the intersection?
q-3679.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Going straight ahead is ruled out here by the traffic arrangement visible in the material — a sign, signal or road marking indicates other permitted directions. The driver must take in good time the lane consistent with the permitted direction of travel.

q-3685.text: In the presented situation, are you obliged to stop before the major road?
q-3685.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material order a stop before the road with priority — merely slowing down is not enough. The vehicle stops before the line, and where there is none, at a place that provides visibility, and only then gives way.

q-3686.text: You intend to continue driving through the presented road. Do you have to yield the right of way to drivers on this road?
q-3686.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver joining the traffic on another road gives way to all its users. The manoeuvre is performed with particular caution and only when it will not force anyone to brake or change direction.

q-3687.text: Do you have to comply with the yellow horizontal road signs in this situation?
q-3687.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Yellow road markings are temporary and take precedence over the white markings that remain on the roadway. The driver follows the yellow lines, even if they run differently from the permanent lines.

q-3688.text: Do you have to comply with the "STOP" sign in the presented situation?
q-3688.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign applies only to a driver travelling on the road and in the direction for which it was installed. In the situation shown in the material the sign does not concern your approach, so it does not oblige you to stop.

q-3690.text: You are changing the lane from the right to the left. Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicles driving on the left lane?
q-3690.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When changing lanes, the driver gives way to vehicles travelling in the lane they are entering. The manoeuvre requires signalling in advance with the indicator, checking the mirrors and the blind spot, and particular caution.

q-3695.text: Do these horizontal warning signs warn you of a place where there is or there might be a danger?
q-3695.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Warning road markings give advance notice of a place where a danger exists or may exist, and usually announce a change in traffic conditions. Once you notice them, you should raise your attention and adjust your speed to the situation.

q-3715.text: Are you obliged in this situation to signal the stop of the damaged combination vehicle?
q-3715.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A combination of vehicles immobilised because of damage must be marked so that other drivers notice it early enough. The hazard lights serve that purpose, and where they are missing or not working — a warning triangle placed according to the type of road.

q-3722.text: In which picture is the headrest properly mounted?
q-3722.explanation: Correct answer: A. The head restraint is set correctly when its upper edge reaches the height of the top of the head and the gap from the back of the head is small. Set this way, it limits the head being thrown back and protects the neck in a rear-end collision.

q-3723.text: Which of the following elements must any passenger car be fitted with?
q-3723.explanation: Correct answer: A. Every car must be equipped with a warning triangle for marking a vehicle immobilised on the road. A first-aid kit and a spare wheel are useful, but the rules impose no duty to carry them.

q-3724.text: Which of the following elements should each passenger car be equipped with?
q-3724.explanation: Correct answer: B. A fire extinguisher is compulsory equipment for a car, placed so that it can be reached quickly. A first-aid kit and a spare wheel remain recommended but not compulsory equipment.

q-3729.text: Are you obliged in this situation, when parking the motorcycle on the roadway, to switch on the position lights or parking lights?
q-3729.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In conditions of reduced clarity of the air, a vehicle left on the carriageway must be marked with position or parking lights. A motorcycle is narrow and dark, so without lights other drivers would notice it too late.

q-3730.text: When parking a bus on the roadway in this situation, are you obliged to switch on the position lights or parking lights?
q-3730.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In conditions of reduced clarity of the air, a vehicle left on the carriageway must be marked with position or parking lights. A bus's large body takes up a considerable part of the carriageway, and unlit it is a serious obstacle for approaching traffic.

q-3731.text: When parking on the road in this situation, are you obliged to switch on the position lights or parking lights?
q-3731.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In conditions of reduced air transparency a vehicle left on the road must be marked with position or parking lights so that other drivers notice it from an adequate distance. Switching off all the lights turns the vehicle into an invisible obstacle.

q-3732.text: When parking a lorry on the road in this situation, are you obliged to switch on the position lights or parking lights?
q-3732.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In conditions of reduced clarity of the air, a vehicle left on the road must be marked with position or parking lights. A lorry is long and wide, so its outline must be shown to other drivers early enough.

q-3742.text: Are only authorised vehicles allowed to stop in the place marked with this stop line?
q-3742.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A stop line marks the place where public transport vehicles stop, and only they have the right to stop there. Placing another vehicle in that spot forces a bus or tram to stop on the roadway, away from the kerb.

q-3756.text: You iare driving straight on and the motorcycle driver intends to turn left. Do you have to yield the right of way to him?
q-3756.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority here is decided by the traffic arrangement visible in the material, not by the direction of travel alone — going straight ahead gives no advantage over the motorcyclist, who has priority. You must let the one turning left pass and not force them to brake.

q-3759.text: Which of the following lights are you allowed to use when you are driving a passenger car during a fog?
q-3759.explanation: Correct answer: B. In fog you may use front fog lights, which light the carriageway low and wide and reflect less off the water droplets. Main-beam headlights are prohibited in such conditions, and daytime running lights are not enough.

q-3761.text: Which of the following actions should be performed while driving a passenger car and overtaking in a fog outside the built-up area?

options.C: Turn on the rear fog lights, regardless of how limited the visibility is.

q-3761.explanation: Correct answer: B. When overtaking in fog outside a built-up area, the driver must give short sound signals, because a light signal may be invisible in fog. Rear fog lights are switched on only when visibility is severely limited.

q-3765.text: Does this sign warn you of a place where two-way traffic begins?
q-3765.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material warn of the start of a section with two-way traffic, where oncoming vehicles will appear. You must then drive closer to the right edge of the roadway, reduce speed and refrain from overtaking.

q-3775.text: Are you allowed in this situation to use the lane by the right edge of the road on Sundays?
q-3775.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The restriction on using this lane applies only on the days and at the times indicated in the signs visible in the material. Outside those times the lane is available to all drivers on general terms.

q-3776.text: Do the white reflective elements mark the left edge of the road in this situation?
q-3776.explanation: Correct answer: YES. White reflective road studs mark the left edge of the carriageway, and red ones the right. Their colour helps at night to recognise the course of the road and judge whether the vehicle is keeping to the correct side.

q-3778.text: How should you behave while passing an oncoming vehicle at night in a passenger car?

options.A: Look straight into the lights of the oncoming vehicle.
options.B: Change the low beam lights into high beam lights.
options.C: Look right to the source of light of the oncoming vehicle and look for possible obstacles there.

q-3778.explanation: Correct answer: C. You look to the right of the lights of the oncoming vehicle, at the right edge of the carriageway, because that is where a pedestrian or a cyclist may be. Looking straight into the headlights dazzles you, and switching on main beam would dazzle the other driver.

q-3781.text: Are you allowed to replace a halogen bulb in any headlight with a xenon lamp?

options.B: No, because it may lead to dazzling other drivers.
options.C: Yes, if the cap of the light fits in the lampholder in the headlight.

q-3781.explanation: Correct answer: B. A headlamp is designed for a specific light source; fitting a xenon lamp in place of a halogen bulb scatters the beam and dazzles other drivers. A matching base does not mean that such a light source is approved.

q-3783.text: Which of the following actions is allowed when driving a passenger car?

options.C: Using a phone which requires holding it in hand.

q-3783.explanation: Correct answer: A. Using navigation is allowed provided the device is mounted and does not need to be held in the hand. Unfastening the seat belt while driving and a phone held in the hand are prohibited, because they deprive the driver of protection and control over the vehicle.

q-3784.text: What is the allowable minimum depth of the thread in a tire not fitted with a tire indicator bar.
q-3784.explanation: Correct answer: A. The minimum permitted tread depth is 1.6 millimetres, measured around the whole circumference of the tyre. Shallower tread does not clear water from under the wheel, which increases the risk of skidding and lengthens the braking distance.

q-3785.text: Which of the following faults precludes the car from being safely used on the road?

options.C: Burnt out light bulb of the left rear indicator.

q-3785.explanation: Correct answer: C. A non-working indicator makes it impossible to signal an intention to change direction or lane, so other road users cannot read the manoeuvre. A dirty air filter and overheating spark plugs worsen the engine's running but do not mislead others.

q-3803.text: Are you allowed to turn left at the junction when driving on the right lane?
q-3803.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The direction of travel from individual lanes is set by the signs visible in the material, and a left turn is not permitted from the right lane. You must move into the correct lane in good time, before the intersection, not within it.

q-3809.text: Are you allowed to drive across this intersection without stopping in the place marked with the solid line?
q-3809.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The line indicates the place where the vehicle must be stopped unconditionally before entering the junction; merely slowing down does not fulfil that duty. After stopping, make sure the way is clear, and only then move off.

q-3813.text: Does the line in front of you, composed of rectangles, indicate the place to stop the vehicle in front of the pedestrian crossing?
q-3813.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A line made up of rectangles marks the place where the vehicle is to stop if the need arises — for example before a pedestrian crossing. You must not cross that line as long as the crossing is not clear.

q-3815.text: Are you allowed to turn left from the lane you are taking at the nearest intersection?
q-3815.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material permit a left turn from this lane, so the manoeuvre is allowed. It must be signalled with the indicator early enough, and way given to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians on the crossing.

q-3828.text: You intend to drive straight on. Do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-3828.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The vehicle approaching from the right has priority, so it is you who must give way, even though you are going straight ahead. You should approach the intersection at a speed that allows you to stop before it.

q-3838.text: Are you obliged in this situation to give way to the tram whose driver signals the intention to turn left?
q-3838.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A switched-on indicator by itself does not create priority — the order of passage is decided by the traffic rules and the signs visible in the material, and these give priority to you. The tram changing direction must let you pass.

q-3856.text: What might be the result of too weak pressure on the brake pedal of a passenger car?
q-3856.explanation: Correct answer: A. Too little pressure on the pedal does not use the full grip of the tyres, so the vehicle slows more slowly and the braking distance grows. Locked wheels and loss of steering are the result of pressing too hard in a vehicle without ABS.

q-3857.text: What might be the result of too strong braking of a passenger car not fitted with the ABS?

options.A: Shortening of the braking distance by at least half.

q-3857.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a vehicle without ABS, braking too hard locks the wheels; locked wheels do not steer the vehicle, so the steering stops working and the car slides on in its current direction. You must then release the pedal for a moment and brake again.

q-3858.text: Which of the following ways of braking in a passenger car fitted with the ABS is the most effective?

options.A: Pulse pressing of the brake pedal.
options.B: Fast and strong pressing of the brake pedal.
options.C: Pressing the clutch pedal and then the brake pedal.

q-3858.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a vehicle with ABS the brake pedal is pressed quickly and hard, and the system itself pulses the braking force so that the wheels do not lock. Braking interrupted by the driver only lengthens the stopping distance.

q-3859.text: Which of the following action should be taken when the operating ABS pushes out the brake pedal while braking?

options.A: Sustain the pressure on the brake pedal.
options.B: Decrease the pressure on the brake pedal.

q-3859.explanation: Correct answer: A. Pulsing of the pedal is a normal sign that ABS is working, not a fault, so the pressure must be kept up until the vehicle stops or the danger passes. Easing off or releasing the pedal interrupts the braking and lengthens the stopping distance.

q-3860.text: In which of the following situations can the ABS help a driver in sustaining steerability?

options.A: While braking, when the vehicle started laterally skidding.
options.B: Only while braking on the straight part of the road.
options.C: Only while braking on the bend.

q-3860.explanation: Correct answer: A. ABS does not let the wheels lock, so even while braking in a sideways skid the wheels still respond to the steering and the vehicle can be steered. It works the same on a straight and in a bend, but it is no substitute for careful driving.

q-3861.text: Which of the following results may you cause when moving off uphill you release the emergency brake lever too early in relation to releasing the clutch pedal?
q-3861.explanation: Correct answer: B. Until the clutch begins to transmit drive, only the brake holds the vehicle on the hill; released too early, it lets the car roll back, straight into the vehicle standing behind. The lever is released only once you feel the car pushing forward.

q-3863.text: In the presented situation, is the distance between the warning sign and the dangerous spot up to 100 metres?
q-3863.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area a warning sign is placed up to 100 metres before the dangerous place; outside a built-up area this distance is greater. A plate under the sign may indicate a different, specific distance.

q-3882.text: Which of the following actions must be taken when the warning light of the brake system turns red during driving?

options.A: Decrease the speed and wait for the lamp to turn off.
options.B: Stop the vehicle and check the level of brake fluid and the operation of the brakes.
options.C: Continue driving and report this event during the next technical inspection of the vehicle.

q-3882.explanation: Correct answer: B. A red brake-system warning light signals a fault that threatens braking performance, so you must stop the vehicle in a safe place and check the brake fluid level. Driving on with faulty brakes is not permitted.

q-3885.text: What does the cooling system warning light flashing red on the move in a passenger car warn of?

options.A: Of too high temperature of the cooling liquid.
options.B: Of too low temperature of the cooling liquid.
options.C: Of too low level of the windscreen washer solvent.

q-3885.explanation: Correct answer: A. A red cooling-system warning light warns that the coolant temperature is too high. Driving on risks serious engine damage, so stop the vehicle in a safe place and let the engine cool down.

q-3889.text: Which of the following circumstances may indicate bad technical condition of a passenger car?

options.B: Traces of leakages of operating fluids in the place of parking.
options.C: The battery charging light turning red before starting the engine.

q-3889.explanation: Correct answer: B. Stains under a parked car indicate a leak of oil, brake fluid or coolant, and thus a leaking system. Colourless exhaust is a normal symptom, and the charging warning light glowing before the engine is started is normal.

q-3890.text: Which of the following circumstances may indicate bad technical condition of a passenger car?

options.A: Emission of black, blue or white thick fumes.
options.C: The engine oil pressure light turning red before starting the engine.

q-3890.explanation: Correct answer: A. Thick black or blue exhaust means incomplete combustion of fuel or the burning of oil, that is, an engine fault and excessive emissions. Colourless exhaust is the norm, and the oil pressure light glowing before the engine is started is normal.

q-3891.text: In which of the following cases using a passenger car does not threaten the road safety?

options.A: Excessively worn out brake pads or brake plates.
options.C: Short-lived use of the temporary use spare wheel when one tire is damaged.

q-3891.explanation: Correct answer: C. A space-saver spare is intended precisely for a damaged tyre and may be used briefly, at the speed marked on the wheel. Worn brakes and damaged shock absorbers directly impair braking and stability, so they rule out driving.

q-3903.text: Does this sign warn of a road section where you must exercise particular caution due to ruts on the surface of the road?
q-3903.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a section with ruts — permanent deformation of the surface that pulls at the wheels and makes lane changes harder. You must reduce speed, hold the steering wheel more firmly and allow for water collecting in the ruts.

q-3904.text: Does this sign warn of a crossroad in which priority is not determined by the road signs?
q-3904.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces an intersection where no approach is singled out by signs, so the right-hand rule applies. When approaching it you must exercise particular caution and let vehicles coming from the right pass.

q-3905.text: Is the distance between the warning sign and the dangerous spot in the presented situation between 150 and 300 metres?
q-3905.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The distance of 150 to 300 metres applies to roads outside built-up areas; in a built-up area a warning sign is placed up to 100 metres before the dangerous place. A plate under the sign may indicate a different, specific distance.

q-3906.text: Are you allowed, in the presented situation, to enter the narrowed part of the road if it does not force the oncoming vehicle to stop?
q-3906.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a narrowing where the oncoming driver has priority, you may enter only when you will not force them to stop or brake harshly. In case of doubt, you must wait before the narrowing.

q-3907.text: In the presented situation, are you obliged only to turn right?
q-3907.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material do not restrict travel exclusively to a right turn — other directions are also permitted. An order to go only right would follow from a mandatory sign or from direction arrows on the lane.

q-3908.text: Does this sign indicate that the road you are taking is a minor road?
q-3908.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material do not impose the duty to give way, so the road you are on is not subordinate. Subordination would be indicated by a sign ordering you to give way or to stop before the intersection.

q-3910.text: In this situation, will you have priority over the cyclist when he is on the crossing?
q-3910.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Approaching a cycle crossing, the driver gives way to a cyclist on the crossing. The tram's priority does not apply at this place, so you must slow down and be ready to stop.

q-3912.text: When turning right in this situation, can you assume that there will be no collision with other directions of traffic?
q-3912.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The traffic arrangement shown in the material separates the conflicting directions, so the right turn is made without crossing the path of other vehicles. Even so, watch the pedestrian crossing and the cycle crossing and take care.

q-3913.text: In this situation, is the tram driver obliged to yield the right of way and exercise particular caution?
q-3913.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A tram's priority is not unconditional — in the situation arising from the signing shown in the material it is the tram driver who gives way. A tram's long braking distance requires slowing down early and watching the surroundings closely.

q-3914.text: Does the car approaching from the right side have the right of way, in this situation?
q-3914.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The right-hand rule applies only when priority is not defined by signs, signals or special rules. In this situation the order of passage is decided by the traffic arrangement shown in the material, and it gives priority to you.

q-3917.text: Does the warning sign "frosty road" oblige the tram driver to exercise particular caution?
q-3917.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Warning signs apply to all drivers, a tram driver included, and a frosted surface means less grip on the rails as well. Slow down, brake gently and increase the distance from the vehicle ahead.

q-3923.text: In this situation, are obliged to signal the intention to turn left?
q-3923.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intention to change direction is signalled in advance with the indicator, so that the other road users can anticipate the manoeuvre. This duty also applies to a tram driver, and signalling ends once the manoeuvre has been carried out.

q-3941.text: In the presented situation, does the illuminated light allow you to go beyond the traffic lights?
q-3941.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal visible in the material prohibits passing the traffic light. The vehicle must be stopped before the traffic light, or before the stop line if one is marked, and wait for the signal permitting travel.

q-3943.text: If a tram, equipped with a shoe brake rolls on despite the brake being pressed and parking brake lights flashing, it may indicate:

options.A: an excessive number of passengers in the tram.
options.B: too low voltage of battery charging.

q-3943.explanation: Correct answer: C. A shoe brake works through friction of the linings on the drum; when the linings are worn, the clamping force is not enough and the vehicle rolls on despite the brake being applied. Such a tram must be withdrawn from service and the fault reported.

q-3976.text: How should a tram driver brake?

options.A: Each time using the track brakes.
options.B: In such a way as not to pose danger to traffic.

q-3976.explanation: Correct answer: B. Braking should be smooth and suited to the situation, so that it endangers neither other road users nor standing passengers. Track brakes and the sander are emergency measures, used when needed, not at every stop.

q-3983.text: You are driving a tram. How should you react when weather conditions deteriorate, e.g. snowfall or leaves falling.

options.A: I should reduce the speed, adjusting it to the prevailing conditions.
options.B: I should drive at a speed close to the maximum so that the travel time is consistent with the time specified in the timetable.
options.C: I should not pay attention to it, because weather conditions do not affect the tram drive.

q-3983.explanation: Correct answer: A. Wet rails and a layer of leaves drastically reduce wheel grip, so the tram's braking distance grows. Speed must be adapted to conditions, and the timetable does not justify driving that endangers safety.

q-3991.text: Is a tram diver allowed to use a hand-held mobile phone, when driving?
q-3991.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Using a hand-held phone while driving is prohibited, because it occupies a hand and draws attention away from the road. The tram driver is responsible for the passengers' safety, so the call must wait until a stop.

q-3992.text: When driving, is a tram driver allowed to use a mobile phone if it does not require holding the phone in his hand?
q-3992.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban concerns a phone that requires holding the handset in the hand, so a hands-free kit is permitted. Even then the conversation must not draw attention away from the road and from operating the vehicle.

q-3993.text: If you participate in a road accident in which people are injured, are you obliged to immediately stop the tram, without posing any threats?
q-3993.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident with injured people stops the vehicle immediately, but in a way that does not cause additional danger to others. They then secure the scene, give help and call the rescue services.

q-3994.text: If possible, are you obliged to remove the tram from an accident scene, in which there are no casualties or injured persons?
q-3994.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When nobody is injured or killed, the participants remove the vehicles from the scene of the collision so as not to obstruct traffic. With a tram, a blocked tramway stops the whole line, so clearing the scene is particularly important.

q-3995.text: If you are involved in an accident, are you obliged to provide your personal details at the request of a passenger, who is also involved in the incident
q-3995.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an incident gives their own details and those of the vehicle's owner or keeper at the request of another person involved in the incident, a passenger included. These details are needed to pursue claims and establish what happened.

q-3996.text: If you are involved in a road accident, are you obliged to notify the police if there are no casualties or injured persons?
q-3996.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When nobody has been hurt, it is enough to remove the vehicles from the scene and exchange details with the other participant. The Police are called when there are injured or killed, or when the circumstances are disputed, for example on suspicion of intoxication.

q-3997.text: If you are involved in a road accident, are you obliged to notify the police and call the paramedics if there are casualties and injured persons?
q-3997.explanation: Correct answer: YES. With injured or killed, an ambulance and the Police must be called, and until they arrive you stay at the scene, give help and do not change the position of the vehicles or the traces. The report should include the location, the number of casualties and the type of injuries.

q-3998.text: Are you obliged in this situation, to yield the right of way to the oncoming vehicle before overtaking?
q-3998.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing the obstacle requires moving onto the part of the roadway intended for the opposite direction, so the oncoming vehicle has priority. The manoeuvre begins only when the lane is clear for the whole necessary length.

q-3999.text: In the presented situation will the next light be red?
q-3999.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The order of signals is fixed: after green comes yellow, then red, and only then red with yellow. The signal visible in the material precedes red, so you must prepare to stop before the line.

q-4000.text: In the presented situation will the next light be green?
q-4000.explanation: Correct answer: NO. After the signal visible in the material, red will come on, and green appears only after red and after the red-with-yellow signal. Counting on a quick change to green leads to crossing the line on a red light.

q-4001.text: When U-turning in this situation, will there be conflict with other road users?
q-4001.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this situation turning around can be done without entering the path of other road users, and the manoeuvre is not prohibited at this place. Before starting it, however, you must make sure the way is clear and give way.

q-4002.text: Does this solid line visible on the right permit other vehicles to enter the track?
q-4002.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A solid line separating the tramway from the lane is a line that may not be crossed, so other vehicles may not enter the tramway at this place. Entering the tramway is permitted only where there is a broken line or appropriate signing.

q-4003.text: When passing a vehicle for driving lessons, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-4003.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing a vehicle marked as a learner vehicle requires special care, because its driver is learning and may react unpredictably. Increase the distance, slow down and be ready for that vehicle to stop suddenly.

q-4004.text: When entering such a marked intersection, are you obliged to yield priority to vehicles driving on it?
q-4004.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to give way follows from the signing shown in the material — the vehicle entering must let through the vehicles already moving on the junction. Entry is allowed only when it will not force those vehicles to brake or change direction.

q-4006.text: When driving a tram, are you allowed to talk on a mobile phone requiring you to hold the receiver or microphone in your hand?
q-4006.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver of a vehicle, a tram included, is prohibited from using a phone that requires holding the handset or microphone in the hand. A hand occupied by the phone and divided attention lengthen reaction, so only a hands-free kit is permitted.

q-4007.text: In this situation, when passing next to the tram stop, are you obliged to exercise particular?
q-4007.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Around a stop, passengers get on and off, often stepping onto the carriageway or the tracks, so passing it requires special care. Speed must be chosen so that you can stop the vehicle before a pedestrian who suddenly appears.

q-4008.text: Does the raised hand of the police officer indicate that a change in the signal transmitted is about to occur?
