q-4008.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The raised hand of a person directing traffic gives notice of a change in the signal being given and has the meaning of an amber signal. Whoever has not yet entered the junction must stop before it; whoever is already on it should leave it.

q-4009.text: How do you behave when entering an equivalent intersection?

options.B: I observe the whole intersection and its surroundings.
options.C: I only look to the right.

q-4009.explanation: Correct answer: B. At a junction of equal roads the vehicle from the right has priority, but danger can appear from any side — from pedestrians, cyclists and turning vehicles. Looking in one direction only misses part of the situation on the road.

q-4010.text: In a place marked as such, are you obliged to anticipate that a cyclist may appear on the crossing?
q-4010.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material indicates a place intended for cycling across the road, so the driver must expect a bicycle to appear. Approach at a speed that allows the vehicle to be stopped, and do not obstruct the passage.

q-4011.text: You are entering such a marked intersection. Do you have the right of passage over other vehicles?
q-4011.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material imposes on the vehicle entering a duty to give way, rather than granting it priority. Entry is possible only after making sure that other vehicles will not be forced to change speed or direction.

q-4012.text: Does this warning sign indicate the right of way for trams?
q-4012.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Warning signs only give notice of a danger and require care; they do not settle priority. Who has priority is decided by priority signs, signals or the general rules of the road.

q-4013.text: For what reason should the tram driver slow down when driving through a place with lowered overhead line e.g. under a viaduct?

options.A: Because quick passage through such a place causes an echo that may disturb the residents of nearby houses.
options.B: Because quick passage through such a place may damage the current collector and traction.
options.C: Because it will be difficult to brake the vehicle.

q-4013.explanation: Correct answer: B. Where the overhead line is lowered, the current collector works at its extreme position, and a fast pass causes blows and bounces that can damage both the collector and the wire. Reducing speed limits those loads.

q-4014.text: Does this warning sign apply to the tram driver?
q-4014.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Road signs apply to all drivers travelling on the road, and therefore to a tram driver as well. The exception is signs whose content or plate expressly limits their application to a specific group of vehicles.

q-4015.text: Do these signs always oblige the tram driver to stop, in order to yield the right way?
q-4015.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to give way does not always mean stopping the vehicle — an unconditional stop follows only from a sign that expressly requires it. If the road with priority is clear, you may continue without stopping.

q-4016.text: Does this warning sign inform you that in a distance no longer than 100m you will encounter the beginning of road works?
q-4016.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign gives notice of works being carried out on the road, and in a built-up area it is placed no more than 100 m before the start of such a stretch. Slow down and expect a narrowed carriageway and a changed traffic arrangement.

q-4018.text: Does the speed limit defined by this sign apply only to the nearest junction or rail intersection provided other signs do not instruct otherwise?
q-4018.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The speed limit applies from where the sign stands to the nearest junction or crossing of the tracks, unless it is cancelled or repeated by another sign before then. After that point the speed under the general rules applies again.

q-4019.text: Does this information sign indicate the start of a multi-track section?
q-4019.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material has a meaning other than indicating the start of a multi-track section and informs of a different element of the traffic arrangement. A sign's meaning follows from its content, not from the situation in which it appears.

q-4021.text: You intend to turn right. Are you obliged to give way to vehicles approaching from the same direction, continuing straight-ahead?
q-4021.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning right, you do not cut across the path of vehicles going straight ahead from the same direction, so you have no duty to give way to them. You must, however, give way to pedestrians and cyclists crossing the road you are turning into.

q-4022.text: Does the sign on the overhead wire indicate that you are approaching a junction with a change induced signalling device?
q-4022.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign placed on the overhead line warns the tram driver that the signals at the next junction are switched on demand, that is, triggered by the approaching tram. Speed must be chosen so that you can react in time to a signal that appears only once triggered.

q-4023.text: Should the tram driver "park" the tram prior to manual positioning of the rail switch?
q-4023.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The tram driver then leaves the driving position and stops controlling the vehicle, so the tram must first be immobilised and secured against moving off on its own. Only a secured vehicle allows the switch to be changed safely.

q-4024.text: During a stop at the terminus, are you allowed to leave the tram without securing it?
q-4024.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver who leaves the vehicle must first secure it against moving off on its own and against use by an unauthorised person. This duty also applies to a stop at the terminus loop, even when the break is short.

q-4025.text: Is a tram driver allowed to drive after consuming alcohol (e.g. after drinking one beer), if he feels good?
q-4025.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Driving in the state after alcohol consumption is prohibited regardless of how the driver feels. Alcohol lengthens reaction time and impairs the judgement of distance and speed, and a subjective sense of sobriety does not change its concentration in the body.

q-4026.text: Can a tram driver, taking into account all forms of employment, rest less than 11 hours per day?
q-4026.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A tram driver is entitled in every 24-hour period to an uninterrupted rest of at least 11 hours, counted jointly for all forms of employment. Shortening it leads to mounting tiredness, which clearly impairs attention and speed of reaction.

q-4027.text: When driving a tram, are you allowed to talk on the mobile phone, if you are not holding the receiver or microphone in your hand?
q-4027.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban covers only a phone that requires holding the handset or microphone in the hand, so a conversation via a hands-free kit is permitted. You must still keep control of the vehicle, and the conversation must not draw attention away from the situation on the road.

q-4029.text: In this situation, are you allowed to enter beyond the traffic signal if you assess that you will not be able to leave the intersection before the end of the transmitted signal?
q-4029.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A permitting signal does not entitle you to enter the junction if there is no room beyond it to leave before the signal changes. A vehicle stuck on the junction blocks the road users from the other directions.

q-4030.text: You intend to turn left at this intersection. Are you allowed to go across without exercising particular caution?
q-4030.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning left, you cut across the path of vehicles coming from the opposite direction and the way of pedestrians and cyclists on the road you are entering. Such a manoeuvre always requires special care and making sure it will not cause danger.

q-4031.text: In this situation, are you obliged to signal the change of driving direction?
q-4031.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every change of direction must be signalled in advance and clearly, so that the other road users can anticipate the driver's intention. Signalling ends immediately after the manoeuvre is carried out, so as not to mislead others.

q-4032.text: Is a tram driver performing passenger transport, entitled to at least 35 hours of uninterrupted rest per week?
q-4032.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A tram driver carrying passengers is entitled in every week to an uninterrupted rest of at least 35 hours. The longer break restores the psychophysical fitness on which attention and speed of reaction on duty depend.

q-4033.text: In this situation, should you anticipate vehicles that may want to enter the track from the left side?
q-4033.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The traffic arrangement at this place allows other vehicles to find themselves on the tramway, for example when changing direction or crossing the tracks. The tram driver should watch the left side and drive so as to be able to brake in time.

q-4034.text: Do you have the right to drive up to the signalling device when driving through the line marked by rectangles, in the presented situation?
q-4034.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The line made up of rectangles marks the place where the vehicle must stop when the signal being given requires it. It may not be crossed in order to get closer to the signal head, even if that improves its visibility.

q-4035.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop the tram just before the line constituting of triangles?
q-4035.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A line made up of triangles means a conditional stop — you must stop only when the duty to give way requires it. If nobody with priority is approaching, you may drive through without stopping, taking care.

q-4036.text: Do you have an obligation to stop the tram on the line marked by triangles, if another vehicle was to approach the transverse road?
q-4036.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A conditional stop line becomes the stopping place when you have to give way to an approaching vehicle. You may move off only when your passage will not force that vehicle to brake or change direction.

q-4038.text: Which of the following reasons may cause an interruption in the flow of high voltage current directly to the wagon?

options.B: Damage to the external sound signal.
options.C: The graphite insert of the pantograph is chipped.

q-4038.explanation: Correct answer: C. It is the graphite insert that slides along the contact wire and carries current to the car, so a chipped insert causes the contact to break and the supply to drop out. The battery and the bell have nothing to do with the high-voltage circuit.

q-4039.text: What effect can a chipping of the pantograph's graphite inserts induce?

options.A: Increase in current consumption from the overhead line.
options.B: Excessive rocking, or even break of the overhead line.

q-4039.explanation: Correct answer: B. A damaged insert does not slide evenly along the wire but catches on it and sets the line vibrating, which at higher speed can lead to it breaking. That is why a fault noticed must be reported immediately.

q-4040.text: When do you use the mechanical brake (also called parking brake)?

options.B: Only in the final stage of braking and during a stop.

q-4040.explanation: Correct answer: B. As speed falls, the electrodynamic brake loses effectiveness, so the final braking to a stop is taken over by the mechanical brake. The same brake then holds the vehicle stationary while stopped.

q-4041.text: Which of the mentioned factors induces the operation of the parking brake?
q-4041.explanation: Correct answer: B. The parking brake is applied by the force of a tensioned spring and released only by the release device. As a result, a loss of power or pressure causes the vehicle to brake automatically, not to release its brakes.

q-4042.text: What determines the electrodynamic braking efficiency?

options.C: The electrodynamic brakes are independent of the tram system.

q-4042.explanation: Correct answer: A. Electrodynamic braking relies on the traction motors working as generators, so its effectiveness depends directly on their condition. Damage to the motors removes this kind of braking and forces the use of the mechanical brake.

q-4043.text: What should you do to release (loosen) the parking brakes for towing a damaged tram?

options.A: Disconnect the wagon, Upon disconnecting the brakes are automatically loosened.
options.B: Mechanically or electrically unfasten the brake release.
options.C: Set the reversing switch to the neutral position.

q-4043.explanation: Correct answer: B. The parking brake holds the wheels by spring force, so neither switching off the car nor setting the reverser will release it. For towing, the release devices are unhooked mechanically or electrically, and the car must first be secured against rolling away.

q-4044.text: At this intersection, is the tram driver obliged to give way to vehicles driving on the transverse road?
q-4044.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The order of passage here is decided by the signing shown in the material, from which a duty to give way to those travelling on the side road follows. A tram does not always have priority — on a minor road it gives way like any other vehicle.

q-4045.text: Are you obliged to also yield the right of way beyond the visible sign to vehicles that may approach the road from the right side?
q-4045.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to give way arising from this sign concerns all vehicles travelling on the road being entered, regardless of the side they approach from. Entry is possible only after making sure nobody will be obstructed.

q-4046.text: In this situation, do you have the right of passage over vehicles driving next to you and that intends to keep going straight ahead?
q-4046.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Where a tram's path crosses the path of other vehicles and signing does not decide the matter, the tram has priority. The tram driver should, however, make sure the drivers alongside really are giving way, and be ready to brake.

q-4047.text: At this place of intersection of the tracks, do you have priority over a tram that may approach from the left side?
q-4047.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The order of passage at this place is decided by the signing and signals shown in the material, and from them follows a duty to give way to the tram approaching from the left. The crossing of the tracks may be driven over only after making sure it is clear.

q-4048.text: Can a tram driver increase the speed when the tram he is driving is being overtaken?
q-4048.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver of the vehicle being overtaken may not increase speed, because that would prolong the manoeuvre and force the overtaking driver to stay alongside for longer. Drive steadily and, if necessary, make it easier to complete the overtaking.

q-4049.text: Are you required to reduce the speed to maintain a safe distance from the slower moving vehicle next to you?
q-4049.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Speed is chosen according to traffic conditions, and those include the width of the free space beside a slower-moving vehicle. If the lateral distance becomes too small, slow down and wait until the situation allows you to pass that vehicle safely.

q-4050.text: Are you obliged to maintain a safe distance each time when driving past vehicles?
q-4050.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing an obstacle always requires special care and a safe distance from the vehicle, road user or obstacle being passed. The size of that distance depends on speed, the width of the road and conditions, but it may never be omitted.

q-4051.text: In this situation, is the tram driver performing a passing manoeuvre?
q-4051.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing an oncoming vehicle means driving past a vehicle moving in the opposite direction, and that is exactly what happens in this situation. The manoeuvre requires a safe distance and, if necessary, reducing speed.

q-4053.text: In this situation, are you performing a passing manoeuvre?
q-4053.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Passing an obstacle concerns a vehicle, road user or obstacle that is not moving, whereas in this situation the object being passed is in motion. The manoeuvre being carried out is therefore of a different kind, though it too requires a safe distance.

q-4054.text: In every situation, are you obliged to maintain a safe distance of at least 1 metre from the vehicle being passed, traffic user or obstacles?
q-4054.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A distance of no less than 1 m applies when passing vulnerable road users, such as a pedestrian, a cyclist, a moped rider or a person on a personal transporter. In other cases the distance must be safe, suited to speed and conditions.

q-4055.text: Can a tram driver who has no possibility of observing the road behind the tram reverse without the help of another person?
q-4055.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You may reverse only when the driver can see the space behind the vehicle; if visibility is insufficient, they must get the help of another person. The manoeuvre also requires giving way to all other road users.

q-4056.text: A tram driver has wrongly positioned the rail switch, and noticed this about 1 m behind it. Can he reverse the tram without making sure it poses no danger?
q-4056.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Even a short reverse is a manoeuvre before which you must make sure it will not endanger other road users, especially pedestrians and vehicles behind the tram. Where there is no visibility, the help of another person is necessary.

q-4057.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution when passing a vehicle transporting an organized group of children up to 18 years, who are getting off the vehicle?
q-4057.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing a marked vehicle from which children are getting off requires special care and, if necessary, stopping as well. Children may suddenly step onto the carriageway from behind the vehicle and do not judge distance or speed correctly.

q-4059.text: What kind of brake is the parking brake?

options.A: Active - operates only after switching on the tram and pressing brake pedal.
options.B: Passive - operates even after switching off the tram.
options.C: Passive - operates only after lowering the pantograph on the wagon.

q-4059.explanation: Correct answer: B. The parking brake is applied by spring force, so it needs no power supply to hold the vehicle and works even after the tram is switched off. This design prevents the car rolling away when the power fails.

q-4063.text: What effect will stopping the wagon at the point of contact between the pantograph and an insulator trigger?

options.A: Loss of wagon start-up and operation of the inverter.
options.C: Damage to the graphite inserts of the pantograph.

q-4063.explanation: Correct answer: A. An insulator does not conduct current, so a collector standing at that point draws no supply and the car has nothing to move off with or to feed the converter. That is why stopping at such a point is a mistake.

q-4064.text: When you see a pedestrian behaving in such a manner, should you apply the principle of limited trust?
q-4064.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The principle of limited trust lets you count on others obeying the rules only as long as their behaviour does not indicate otherwise. Towards pedestrians whose behaviour raises doubts, slow down and be ready to stop.

q-4065.text: In what situations, can a tram driver let a passenger in a hurry in or out of the tram?

options.A: While waiting for the lights to change.
options.B: Only if the passenger is standing at the tram stop.
options.C: Beyond the tram stop, at the express request of the passenger.

q-4065.explanation: Correct answer: B. Getting on and off takes place only at stops, prepared for passengers' safe access. Away from a stop a passenger steps straight onto the carriageway between moving vehicles, and their haste changes nothing here.

q-4066.text: Which of these signs on the tram, in addition to the tram's route markings is required?

options.C: rolling stock number, logo and name of city in which the tram runs.

q-4066.explanation: Correct answer: A. A tram is not registered like a car and carries no number plate, but it must have a visible fleet number identifying the car. A logo or the city's name is not required, though operators often display them.

q-4067.text: In which places can a tram driver let passengers in or out of the tram?

options.A: At any location, including tram stops.

q-4067.explanation: Correct answer: B. The exchange of passengers takes place at stops, because only there is access to the vehicle prepared and other drivers expect pedestrians. Stopping elsewhere exposes those getting off to contact with vehicle traffic.

q-4068.text: Should you expect bicycle traffic beyond the warning sign visible in the foreground?
q-4068.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign shown in the material gives notice of a place where cyclists join or cross the road. Slow down, watch the sides of the road and be ready to give way where cyclists are entitled to priority.

q-4069.text: When driving a tram, are you obliged to carry on you a driving permit for the vehicle?

options.B: No, because it is not required for city transport.
options.C: No, provided I have a relevant document issued by the employer

q-4069.explanation: Correct answer: A. Driving a tram requires a separate permit, which must be carried throughout the journey and shown during a check. A document issued by the employer does not replace that entitlement.

q-4071.text: How should you proceed to replace a blown high voltage fuse?
q-4071.explanation: Correct answer: B. Before reaching into a high-voltage circuit, the supply must be cut off, and that is done by lowering the pantograph. Switching off the converter alone or putting on gloves does not remove the voltage from the circuit.

q-4072.text: What should a tram driver do before driving, immediately after closing the door?

options.A: Carefully observe the surroundings and give a signal departure using the bell.
options.B: It's enough to give a signal of departure using the bell.
options.C: Only check the closed door signals.

q-4072.explanation: Correct answer: A. Pulling away from a stop requires checking the whole surroundings, because pedestrians may still be at the doors and in front of the car. Only observation combined with the bell signal warns them and allows a safe departure.

q-4073.text: Which position of the tram driver is correct when manually adjusting the rail switch?

options.A: The position of the tram driver is irrelevant.
options.B: With his back to the tram.

q-4073.explanation: Correct answer: C. Standing facing the tram, the driver sees their vehicle and will notice if it moves, while at the same time watching what is happening on the track. With their back turned they lose that view and react late.

q-4075.text: In which place can the tram driver let passengers off due to lengthy traffic impediments?

options.A: At any place of his choice.
options.B: Only at the tam stop, regardless of the circumstances.
options.C: In a place where there is no risk to passengers and road traffic.

q-4075.explanation: Correct answer: C. When the vehicle is immobilised for a long time, letting the passengers out is permitted, but only where they can get off safely and it will not endanger traffic on the road. The choice of place is decided by safety, not by convenience or passengers' requests.

q-4076.text: What should a tram driver do to safely perform the electrical connection of the carriages?

options.A: It's enough to lower the pantographs.
options.B: It's enough to disconnect the batteries
options.C: Lower the pantograph and disconnect the batteries.

q-4076.explanation: Correct answer: C. A car has two power sources: the overhead line and the batteries, so cutting off only one of them leaves the circuits live. Safe coupling requires the pantographs to be lowered and the battery disconnected.

q-4077.text: How should the tram driver behave before leaving the cabin onto the road, beyond the tram stop, to manually set the rail switch?

options.B: Park the tram and make sure that he can safely leave the cabin.
options.C: Turn off all lights on the tram and set the reversing switch to the neutral position.

q-4077.explanation: Correct answer: B. Before the tram driver steps onto the carriageway, the car must be immobilised and secured, and leaving the cab is preceded by checking that nothing is approaching. Switching off the converter or the lights does not make this manoeuvre safe.

q-4078.text: What could be the cause of interrupting the drive during start-up if the internal bell rings and there is no indication of closed doors?

options.A: Opening of the windows if the interior is air-conditioned.
options.B: Emergency opening of the door by a passenger.

q-4078.explanation: Correct answer: B. Open doors block starting, and the absence of the door-closed indication together with the internal bell points precisely to an emergency opening by a passenger. The cause must then be established and the doors closed before moving off again.

q-4079.text: How should you behave when driving a tram during lightning storms and you are concerned about lightning strikes?

options.A: Stop the tram, lower the pantograph and let the passengers out.
options.B: Continue driving, the inside of the tram is safe.
options.C: Stop the tram, lower the pantograph and do not let the passengers out.

q-4079.explanation: Correct answer: B. The car's metal body conducts the charge along its shell, so the interior remains safe and the journey can continue. Stopping the set and letting people out into the open would increase the danger.

q-4080.text: How should a tram driver behave when driving through places with lowered overhead lines e.g. under a viaduct?

options.A: Reduce speed over the entire section of the lowered overhead lines.
options.B: Increase speed over the entire section of the lowered overhead lines.

q-4080.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a section where the wire is lowered, the collector works at its extreme position and at higher speed strikes the wire, which risks damaging the pantograph and the overhead line. Speed must be reduced along the whole length of that section, not only at its start.

q-4081.text: How should the tram driver drive when approaching an intersection?
q-4081.explanation: Correct answer: A. You approach a junction so as to be able to stop the vehicle before it, and coasting or braking allows that. Accelerating lengthens the stopping distance and takes away time to assess the situation.

q-4082.text: In what situation can the tram driver safely drive through the rail switch?

options.A: When the rail switch signaling unit indicates that it has been reset.
options.B: Without paying attention to the signalling unit, if there is delay relative to the timetable.
options.C: When the switch points properly cling.

q-4082.explanation: Correct answer: C. The safety of the passage is decided by the switch blades actually fitting fully against the rail, not by the indicator alone, which may be ahead of the state of the equipment. A switch not fully closed risks derailment, so it must be checked by eye and speed reduced.

q-4083.text: What behavior is required of a tram driver driving through the rail switches and frogs?
q-4083.explanation: Correct answer: B. At these places the track has gaps and changes in wheel guidance, so the passage involves blows that load the bogies and the track. Reducing speed limits the risk of derailment and damage and improves passenger comfort.

q-4084.text: Which rule of the driving technique should be adhered to by the tram driver when entering a sharp bend of the track?
q-4084.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a sharp curve the centrifugal force grows, pressing on the outer rail and increasing the risk of derailment and the wear of wheels and track. Speed must be reduced before the curve, also because standing passengers may lose their balance.

q-4085.text: What impact has the position of the tram driver's seat on the operation of the control devices?
q-4085.explanation: Correct answer: C. The seat position determines free reach of the hands and feet to all the controls and the view of the track and surroundings. A badly chosen position delays reactions and tires faster, so the seat is adjusted before the journey begins.

q-4086.text: If a wheel slip occurs in a tram during start-up, you must stop, and then:
q-4086.explanation: Correct answer: A. Wheel slip means that the tractive force has exceeded the grip of wheel on rail, so the next start must be gentler. Harder acceleration deepens the slip and leads to wear of the wheels and rails.

q-4087.text: What should a tram driver do upon sudden appearance of a vehicle on the tracks directly in front of the tram?

options.A: Gently brake not to cause danger to passengers.
options.B: Decisively brake trying hard to avoid a collision.

q-4087.explanation: Correct answer: B. A tram cannot steer round an obstacle, so the only way to avoid a collision is immediate, decisive braking using all available brakes. The consequences of a collision would be more dangerous for the passengers than the harsh braking itself.

q-4088.text: How should you start-up a tram.

options.A: In a manner that prevents the wheels from skidding.
options.B: In a manner that causes a significant acceleration.
options.C: In a manner that prevents overloading the batteries.

q-4088.explanation: Correct answer: A. Starting is carried out smoothly, so that the wheels do not lose grip on the rails. Wheel slip lengthens the starting distance, damages the surface of the wheels and rails and worsens passenger comfort. On slippery rails using the sander beforehand helps.

q-4089.text: Which brakes are used to soft stop the tram at the tram stop?

options.B: The electrodynamic brake and in the final phase the parking brake.

q-4089.explanation: Correct answer: B. The electrodynamic brake can be metered smoothly, so it serves for shedding speed. At very low speed its effectiveness fades, so stopping and holding the car is taken over by the parking brake. The track brake is an emergency brake and stops abruptly.

q-4090.text: What effect could be caused by an electrical arc formed when passing through the isolator with an enabled drive?

options.A: A drop in the battery voltage.

q-4090.explanation: Correct answer: B. With traction engaged, the circuit is broken under load and a high-temperature electric arc forms. It burns the contact strip and the pantograph structure and destroys the contact wire. An insulator is passed without drawing current.

q-4091.text: When is a tram driver required to adapt the speed to the prevailing conditions of the road?

options.C: Only in the areas of pedestrian crossings.

q-4091.explanation: Correct answer: A. The duty to drive at a speed that ensures control of the vehicle applies at all times, regardless of place and time. A sign or rule sets only the upper limit, and the state of the track, the weather and visibility often require slower driving.

q-4092.text: What should a tram driver do, if the passengers upon entering the tram, do not want to close the doors and their professional repair is necessary.

options.A: Ask all the passengers to leave the tram and drive the empty tram back to the depot.
options.B: Start driving with the doors open, warning the passengers of a possible inconvenience.
options.C: Turn on the drive lock and continue driving with the passengers.

q-4092.explanation: Correct answer: A. Carrying passengers in a car with faulty doors is not permitted, because open doors risk a person falling out onto the track. Once everyone has been asked to leave, the car returns to the depot as an empty run. Switching off the traction interlock is prohibited.

q-4093.text: What should a tram driver do when approaching a dirty rail switch?

options.A: Continue driving without paying attention to the dirty state of rail switch.
options.B: Stop and clean up the rail switch before driving on it.

q-4093.explanation: Correct answer: B. Dirt prevents the blade from fitting exactly against the stock rail, so the car may go the wrong way or derail. That is why you must stop before running onto it and clean the switch.

q-4094.text: What should a tram driver do after setting the tram in motion?

options.A: Repeatedly switch on the drive, until reaching the desired speed.
options.B: Speed up the tram to the desired speed, and drive as long as possible on the freewheel.

q-4094.explanation: Correct answer: B. Once the intended speed is reached, traction is switched off and the tram coasts, which saves energy and reduces wear of the drive. Switching the start-up on repeatedly causes jolts and unnecessary current draw.

q-4096.text: How should a tram driver pass through the section isolator placed on the overhead line?

options.A: Always in start-up, otherwise the tram will stop under the isolator due to lack of electricity.
options.C: Always on braking, because then the tram via the isolator gives power to the overhead line.

q-4096.explanation: Correct answer: B. A section insulator separates sections of the overhead line, so with traction engaged the circuit breaks under load and an arc forms that destroys the pantograph and the wire. Such a place is passed without drawing current, that is, coasting or braking.

q-4097.text: What does pressing the dead man's switch during a tram stop result in?

options.B: It enables start-up of the tram.
options.C: It turns on the tram's lights.

q-4097.explanation: Correct answer: B. The dead man's switch confirms the driver's presence and fitness; until it is pressed, the traction circuit stays locked. Pressing it removes the lock and allows starting. Releasing it while driving triggers emergency braking.

q-4098.text: What is the maximum permissible speed of the tram in a built-up area in the hours 5:00 - 23:00 (if the road signs do not indicate otherwise)?
q-4098.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a built-up area during the hours indicated the general limit of 50 km/h applies, and it covers a tram as well. A sign may set a lower value, and traffic conditions often require even slower driving.

q-4099.text: What should the tram driver take into account when towing a damaged tram?

options.A: An increased likelihood of the tram derailing at a sharp bend.

q-4099.explanation: Correct answer: B. A towed car increases the mass of the set, and its own brakes usually do not work to their full extent, so the braking distance grows clearly. Drive slower, avoid sudden manoeuvres and keep a greater distance.

q-4101.text: Is it necessary to reduce the speed of the tram when passing the rail switch?

options.A: Yes, it is only necessary on rail switches operated unilaterally, marked with the sign BT-4 "Z-Stop".
options.C: No, it is not mandatory as it could cause a delay in exit from the intersection.

q-4101.explanation: Correct answer: B. A switch is always passed slowly, because at higher speed the risk of derailment and of the blade moving under the car grows. This duty does not depend on the type of switch or on whether it lengthens the time taken to cross the junction.

q-4104.text: On which section does the speed limit apply to, subject to this sign?

options.C: To the nearest intersection (fork) of tracks.

q-4104.explanation: Correct answer: C. The restriction introduced by the sign shown in the material applies until the nearest crossing or fork of the tracks — there the section ends. A stop or a traction pole does not end such a restriction.

q-4105.text: On which section does the speed limit apply to subject to this sign?

options.A: To the nearest road intersection without tracks.
options.B: To the location of the sign indicating the end of the sign.

q-4105.explanation: Correct answer: B. The restriction arising from the sign shown in the material lasts until the place where the cancelling sign is set up. Up to that point the speed may not exceed the value given; a stop or a junction alone does not end it.

q-4106.text: How should a tram driver behave on the section beyond the visible prohibition sign?

options.A: He can drive at a speed 10 km/h greater than the value indicated on the sign.
options.B: He should drive at a speed no greater than than the value indicated on the sign.
options.C: He can drive at any speed, if there are no obstacles on the track.

q-4106.explanation: Correct answer: B. A prohibition sign limiting speed sets a value that may not be exceeded even by a small margin. The absence of obstacles on the track does not lift the prohibition, and in worse conditions you should drive even slower.

q-4107.text: What effect will the use of sandboxes during start-up on slippery rails trigger?
q-4107.explanation: Correct answer: A. Sand applied to the rail head increases wheel grip, so the driving torque is transmitted without wheel spin. The sander is operated in advance, before the wheels begin to slip.

q-4108.text: What type of fire extinguisher should a tram be equipped with?
q-4108.explanation: Correct answer: C. A tram is an electric vehicle in which the installation remains live, so it is extinguished with an agent that does not conduct electricity: carbon dioxide or powder. Water and foam conduct electricity and risk electric shock and destruction of the equipment.

q-4109.text: Is driving a tram without covers on the couplings between the carriages from the side of the passenger doors permitted?

options.B: It is permitted in every case.
options.C: It is permitted provided there are markings on the couplers indicating prohibition of entry between the carriages.

q-4109.explanation: Correct answer: C. The space between the cars is dangerous for passengers, so the absence of a guard is permitted only when the coupling bears a marking prohibiting stepping between the cars. Without such a marking, driving is not allowed.

q-4110.text: In what situation can you use the emergency lights if the tram is equipped with one?

options.A: To thank another vehicle driver for yielding the right of way.
options.B: During each stop at a tram stop situated on the roadway (not separated)
options.C: To signal the presence of a tram immobilised due to a breakdown.

q-4110.explanation: Correct answer: C. Hazard lights warn other road users that the vehicle is standing in a place where it creates a hazard, for example after a breakdown. They are not for saying thank you or for signalling an ordinary stop at a tram stop.

q-4111.text: In which situation, are you allowed to leave the tram depot with a damaged external warning bell?

options.A: If you will only drive during the day.
options.C: If the fault has been noted down in the tram's document and certified by technical service.

q-4111.explanation: Correct answer: B. The sound signal is compulsory equipment — without it the tram driver cannot warn a pedestrian or a driver of the approaching car. A tram with a faulty bell may not be taken out on the route, and an entry in the documents does not change that.

q-4112.text: Which brakes perform an emrgency function in a tram?
q-4112.explanation: Correct answer: C. Track brakes are pulled by an electromagnet straight onto the rail, so they work regardless of wheel grip and give the greatest deceleration. For that reason they serve as an emergency brake and are used in a situation of danger.

q-4113.text: What is the purpose of the drive lock circuit ("green line")?

options.A: It prevents the tram from entering a track occupied by a tram driving from the opposite direction.
options.B: It prevents the tram driving with open (half-open) doors.
options.C: It allows passengers to open the door before the tram stops.

q-4113.explanation: Correct answer: B. The interlock circuit closes only when all the doors are shut; as long as even one remains open, engaging traction is impossible. This protects passengers from falling out of the car while it is moving.

q-4114.text: What effect will the use of sandboxes when braking on slippery rails trigger?

options.A: It will prolong the braking distance.
options.B: It will reduce the braking distance - reduce wheel slip.
options.C: It will not affect the braking distance.

q-4114.explanation: Correct answer: B. Sand increases the grip of wheel on rail, so the wheels do not go into a slide and the braking distance shortens. The sander should be operated at the start of braking, not only once the car is already sliding.

q-4115.text: How can a tram driver adjust the braking force of the rail brakes?

options.C: It has no effect on regulating the braking force of the brakes.

q-4115.explanation: Correct answer: C. A track brake works on an on-or-off basis — the electromagnet presses the shoe onto the rail with a constant force. The driver can only apply or release it; there is no way of metering the deceleration.

q-4117.text: What should be the distance from a preceding tram while driving?

options.B: Enough to allow a collision-free stop of the vehicle.
options.C: It is regulated by internal rules of the company.

q-4117.explanation: Correct answer: B. The distance is chosen according to conditions so that, after the car ahead brakes, you can stop without a collision. On slippery rails, on a descent and with a heavier set the distance must be increased; no fixed number of metres applies here.

q-4118.text: Which of the following brakes will be activated if you release the dead man's switch while driving?

options.C: Emergency braking ( rail, shoe and at the minimum the electrodynamic brakes).

q-4118.explanation: Correct answer: C. Releasing the dead man's switch is treated by the system as the driver losing control, so it triggers emergency braking with all brakes by itself. The car stops as quickly as possible, and the switch must be held throughout the journey.

q-4119.text: How should you behave when entering the tram stop?

options.C: Brake, simultaneously using all 3 types of brakes.

q-4119.explanation: Correct answer: B. Smooth but decisive braking lets the car be stopped precisely at the platform without knocking standing passengers over. Harsh braking and simultaneous use of all the brakes are kept for emergencies.

q-4120.text: How do you brake after getting the tram out of a skid?

options.A: With less force so as to prevent further locking of the wheels.
options.B: By releasing the dead man's switch.
options.C: By using the countercurrent, after resetting the reverser to the backward drive.

q-4120.explanation: Correct answer: A. Locked wheels do not brake but slide along the rail, so once they are turning again the braking force is reduced and metered so that the slide does not recur. Applying sand at the same time helps.

q-4121.text: What should you assume when determining the distance from a preceding tram?

options.A: that the driver may suddenly brake
options.B: that the driver will not brake suddenly because he is carrying passengers.
options.C: that the driver will not brake suddenly because he sees in the mirror that there is a tram driving behind him.

q-4121.explanation: Correct answer: A. The car ahead may stop suddenly — because of a pedestrian, a car or a fault. The distance is chosen precisely for such a case, not on the assumption that the other driver will behave conveniently for the one behind.

q-4122.text: What may determine the safe distance from a preceding tram?

options.A: The travel time set out in the timetable.
options.C: The number of tram stops on a given route.

q-4122.explanation: Correct answer: B. Rain, wet leaves, snow and frost worsen the grip of wheel on rail and lengthen the braking distance, so the distance must be increased. The timetable and the number of stops have no bearing on the safe distance.

q-4123.text: If the speed of the tram determines the ability to stop safely, on what in particular should the tram's speed be adjusted to?

options.A: The condition of the track and visibility of the road.
options.B: The power and number of engines on the tram.

q-4123.explanation: Correct answer: A. The braking distance depends on the grip of the wheels on the rails, and an obstacle can be avoided or stopped before only when it is seen early enough. That is why speed is adapted to the state of the track and to visibility.

q-4124.text: You are driving a tram. What should you do when approaching a puddle located on the trackway?

options.A: Drive through with the greatest possible speed.
options.B: Drive through with the least possible speed.
options.C: Stop the tram before each puddle.

q-4124.explanation: Correct answer: B. Water covers the rail head and whatever lies beneath it, and grip drops markedly. Passing at the lowest possible speed reduces the risk of a slide, allows stopping if necessary and does not splash people beside the track.

q-4125.text: What effect does residual material on the tracks originating from wet leaves induce?

options.A: It reduces the possibility of skidding.
options.B: It has no effect on the possibility skidding?
options.C: It increases the possibility of skidding.

q-4125.explanation: Correct answer: C. Crushed damp leaves form a slippery, greasy layer on the rail head that drastically lowers grip. The risk of wheel spin when starting and of sliding when braking grows, so you must drive slower and use the sander.

q-4126.text: How does the presence of leaves in the trackway affect the behaviour of the tram.

options.A: It has no effect on grip.

q-4126.explanation: Correct answer: B. Leaves crushed by the wheels leave a smooth film on the rail, so grip falls. The result is wheel spin on starting and a longer braking distance, so speed is reduced in advance.

q-4127.text: What effect does the initial phase of the rainfall have on the condition of the trackway?

options.A: It results in an improved grip between the wheels and rails.
options.B: It poses a threat to skidding during start-up and braking.
options.C: It has no impact on the tram's drive.

q-4127.explanation: Correct answer: B. The first drops mix with dust, grease and metal particles on the rail and form a slippery emulsion. Grip is then at its lowest, so starting and braking are carried out particularly gently.

q-4128.text: When does rainfall have the greatest impact on the start-up and braking of the tram?

options.B: When a prolonged rainfall turns into a drizzle.

q-4128.explanation: Correct answer: A. The most dangerous are the first minutes of rain: water lifts dust and greasy deposits off the rail, forming a slippery layer. Later, heavy rain washes the dirt away and grip partly returns.

q-4129.text: What increases the risk of a tram skidding?

options.A: Heating up of the rails by the sun.
options.B: The effect of sand and dust covering the rails.

q-4129.explanation: Correct answer: C. Wet leaves crushed by the wheels turn into a slippery mass on the rail head and deprive the wheel of grip. Sand does the opposite — it increases grip, and warm rails do not affect sliding in that way.

q-4130.text: In which season of the year are the conditions most difficult to drive a tram?
q-4130.explanation: Correct answer: C. In autumn wet leaves, frequent rain, fog, early dusk and morning frost coincide on the rails. Grip then drops the most and visibility is limited, so this season is regarded as the most difficult.

q-4131.text: How should a tram driver behave, if the railheads are flooded with water on a considerable section?
q-4131.explanation: Correct answer: A. Under water the state of the track and any obstacles cannot be seen, grip practically vanishes, and water may flood the motors and electrical equipment. That is why driving is stopped and the situation reported to traffic control.

q-4132.text: How should the tram driver behave, if he notices stones in the grooves of the rails?

options.A: Drive at maximum speed so that the stones are thrown to the sides.
options.B: Drive slowly, because a low speed ensures the tram does not derail.
options.C: Remove the stones before driving through such section of the track.

q-4132.explanation: Correct answer: C. A stone in the rail groove lifts the wheel flange above the rail head and may lead to derailment, and thrown aside it injures people beside the track. That is why the car is stopped and the obstacle removed before passing.

q-4136.text: How should the internal mirrors on a tram be positioned?

options.A: To see only the tram driver's cabin space.
options.B: To see the area of the wagon close to the door.
options.C: To see the outline of the vehicle.

q-4136.explanation: Correct answer: B. The interior mirror serves to watch the door zone: the driver must see whether the exchange of passengers is complete and whether anyone has been caught in the doors. The car's outline is watched with the exterior mirrors.

q-4138.text: In what situation can a tram drive start driving, if the passengers have not moved away from the edge of the tram stop.

options.A: If there is a delay relative to the timetable.
options.B: On condition that he exercises particular caution.
options.C: Only when passengers move away to a safe distance.

q-4138.explanation: Correct answer: B. The tram driver may move off, but only with special care: they constantly watch the people at the edge of the platform and are ready to stop the car immediately. Running late against the timetable does not justify the risk.

q-4141.text: When can a tram driver increase the speed negotiating a curve of the road?

options.A: At the entrance of the curve.
options.B: When the last carriage leaves the curve.
options.C: When the first carriage exits the curve.

q-4141.explanation: Correct answer: B. As long as even one car remains in the curve, increasing speed raises the lateral forces, risks derailment and throws the passengers about. You may accelerate only once the last car has left the curve.

q-4142.text: What should a tram driver do in this situation, immediately after stopping the tram at the tram stop?

options.A: Make sure, using the right exterior mirror that vehicles did not stop on the roadway.
options.B: Turn on the right turn signal to indicate a stop.
options.C: Immediately open the door to observe the movement of passengers.

q-4142.explanation: Correct answer: A. Before the doors are opened, the tram driver checks in the right exterior mirror whether the vehicles on the carriageway have stopped — those getting off may end up in their path. The doors are opened only once the exit is safe.

q-4143.text: In what situations while driving, is the tram driver allowed to disable the driving lock?

options.A: At the request of a passenger.
options.B: Where the wagon is crammed full with passengers.
options.C: It is forbidden in every situation.

q-4143.explanation: Correct answer: C. The interlock does not allow driving with doors not fully closed and protects passengers from falling out. Switching it off while driving is prohibited regardless of how full the car is and of anyone's requests.

q-4144.text: Which of the mentioned braking systems should a cable car be equipped with?
q-4144.explanation: Correct answer: B. The service brake serves for everyday reduction of speed and stopping of the car, so every tram going out on the line must have one. The emergency and parking brakes perform other tasks and do not replace it.

q-4145.text: What should you check first if the tram fails to move after switching on?

options.B: The setting of the direction reverser.

q-4145.explanation: Correct answer: C. The most common cause is a door leaf not fully closed: until the indication confirms the doors are closed, the interlock will not allow traction to be engaged. That is why it is checked first, and only then are other faults looked for.

q-4146.text: What voltage should the voltmeter indicate when you turn on the battery?

options.B: Less than the value specified for the given type of tram.
options.C: Greater than the value specified for the given type of tram.

q-4146.explanation: Correct answer: C. For each type of car a minimum battery voltage is specified, and the voltmeter reading must be above it. A lower value means a discharged battery — the control circuits and brakes may fail, so the car may not be taken out onto the line.

q-4147.text: What Should a tram driver do, if upon switching on drive the shoe brakes fail to disinhibit?

options.A: Continue driving without undertaking any actions.
options.C: Call traffic control, because it is not possible without special tools.

q-4147.explanation: Correct answer: B. Driving with brake shoes not released overheats and destroys the brake, so the driver unhooks the release devices and frees the shoes themselves. This is an action provided for in the car's operation and needs no special tools.

q-4148.text: What effect does pressing of the pedal or tilting of the electrodynamic brake's lever "beyond the limiter" induce?

options.B: Increased efficiency of the electrodynamic braking effect.

q-4148.explanation: Correct answer: A. Beyond the stop is the emergency braking position, in which the track brakes, giving the greatest deceleration, are additionally engaged. It is used only in a situation of danger, because the stop is very abrupt.

q-4149.text: What most often cause loss of start-up?

options.A: Tram power failure (e.g. loss of overhead connection or a tram stop "on the insulator").
options.B: Damage to the internal lighting of the wagon.

q-4149.explanation: Correct answer: A. Without voltage from the overhead line the motors will not move the car. Most often this is a power failure on the section, or the tram has stopped with the pantograph on an insulator — then the car must be moved away from that spot.

q-4155.text: Should you start changing lanes in this situation, if you intend to leave the highway?
q-4155.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving the motorway is prepared in advance: you take the correct lane early enough, signal the manoeuvre with the indicator and give way to vehicles travelling in that lane. A late lane change or braking in the traffic lane is very dangerous.

q-4156.text: Is it forbidden to stop vehicles in this place?
q-4156.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The prohibition follows from the sign or markings visible in the material and covers every immobilisation of the vehicle, even a short one — the exceptions are situations forced by traffic conditions. Stopping at such a place obstructs traffic and restricts visibility.

q-4158.text: You intend to go straight ahead. Are you allowed to drive directly by the right edge of the roadway on the presented section of the road?
q-4158.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material reserve the outer right part of the roadway for other users, so when going straight ahead you must keep to your lane. Entering there obstructs those for whom that space was set aside and creates a danger.

q-4159.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drive into the narrowed part of the road without stopping before the traffic light post?
q-4159.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal visible in the material permits travel, so stopping is not required. Vehicles pass through the narrowed section in one lane alternately, so you enter only when the signal permits and the section is clear.

q-4160.text: You are driving a passenger car in a fog which limits the visibility to 40 metres. Which of these actions may improve safety of driving?

options.A: Switching on the high beam lights.
options.B: Decreasing the distance between the preceding vehicle.
options.C: Switching on the rear fog lights.

q-4160.explanation: Correct answer: C. Rear fog lights shine much more strongly than position lights, so a driver behind sees the vehicle earlier. Main-beam headlights reflect in fog and dazzle the driver themselves, and reducing the distance in such visibility is dangerous.

q-4167.text: What will you do to reduce the effect of internal fogging on the windshield when driving in the rain?

options.A: I will turn on the windshield wiper.
options.B: I will turn on air conditioning and direct airflow to the windshield.
options.C: I will direct airflow to the feet.

q-4167.explanation: Correct answer: B. The window mists up when humid air from inside meets the cold glass. Air conditioning dries the air, and a blower directed at the window removes the condensation fastest. The wipers work on the outside and will not clear internal misting.

q-4169.text: How should the tram driver position the right external mirror?

options.A: To see the entire platform and passengers.
options.B: To see the side of the tram and the space behind the vehicle.
options.C: It can be folded, because it is not useful while driving.

q-4169.explanation: Correct answer: B. The exterior mirror should show the side of the car and the space behind it — only then does the driver see the door zone and vehicles approaching along the carriageway. Folding the mirror deprives them of that view and is not permitted.

q-4170.text: At what permissible speed can you drive in a residential area?
q-4170.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a residential zone a speed of no more than 20 km/h applies, because pedestrians, children included, use the whole width of the road and have priority. The driver must be ready to stop the vehicle at any moment.

q-4172.text: Should you at the next rail intersection yield the right of way to a tram that could have come from the right?
q-4172.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a crossing of tracks where priority is not defined by signs or signals, the general right-hand rule applies — the one approaching from the right has priority. Such a tram must therefore be given way.

q-4173.text: Taking into account the order to secure vehicles during stops, should all the doors remain closed when the tram driver is in the cabin?
q-4173.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The requirement to secure the vehicle is meant to prevent it moving off on its own, and the tram driver's presence in the cab meets that condition. The doors may then stay open, for example while passengers get on and off.

q-4201.text: Are you obliged to slow down in this situation?
q-4201.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to reduce speed follows from the sign and the situation visible in the material — when approaching a place of increased risk, the driver must drive so as to retain the ability to stop. The formal limit does not release you from this obligation.

q-4203.text: Can you continue driving not taking into account the behaviour of the pedestrian?
q-4203.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A pedestrian beside the road may behave unpredictably, so the driver must watch them, reduce speed and be ready to stop. Children, elderly people and people with impaired coordination require particular attention.

q-4205.text: Can you make a U-turn from the lane marked in this way?
q-4205.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this place neither signs nor road markings prohibit turning around, so the manoeuvre is permitted. It may be performed only with sufficient visibility, after giving way to approaching vehicles and without obstructing traffic.

q-4208.text: Are you warned in this situation of a level crossing fitted with full barriers or half-barriers?
q-4208.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material warns precisely of a railway crossing with barriers or half-barriers. You must reduce speed and be ready to stop before a closing barrier; going around a lowered barrier is prohibited.

q-4211.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn in this place?
q-4211.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around at this place is prohibited, as follows from the sign or the markings visible in the material. The manoeuvre is performed where it is not prohibited and where visibility allows a safe assessment of traffic from both directions.

q-4228.text: Does this "stop" sign on the roadway warn you of approaching a priority road?
q-4228.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The word "stop" on the roadway gives advance notice that further on there is an intersection with a road that has priority and that you must stop there. The stop itself is made before the conditional stop line or before the edge of the roadway of the cross road.

q-4233.text: How should you behave to drive at a safe speed?

options.A: Maintain the speed to avoid collision with the preceding vehicle.
options.B: Adhere to the road signs restricting speed?
options.C: Adhere to the rules applicable in the built-up area?

q-4233.explanation: Correct answer: A. A safe speed is one at which the driver can stop before an obstacle, including a braking vehicle ahead. Signs and general limits set only the upper bound and do not in themselves guarantee safety.

q-4242.text: After passing the vehicle in this situation, are you allowed to change the low beam lights into high beam lights?
q-4242.explanation: Correct answer: YES. High beam is switched off so as not to dazzle the driver of an oncoming vehicle; when the vehicles have passed each other and there is no one ahead, it may be switched on again. If another vehicle is travelling ahead, high beam is not switched on.

q-4243.text: When driving a motor vehicle in these conditions, are you allowed to use position lights only?
q-4243.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Position lights only mark the vehicle and do not light the road. While driving, a motor vehicle must have dipped headlights or daytime running lights on, and in conditions of reduced clarity of the air — dipped headlights.

q-4256.text: In the presented situation, are you warned of an intersection in which the traffic flows around a traffic island or a square in the direction indicated on the sign?
q-4256.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material warns that you are approaching a roundabout, where vehicles travel around an island in the direction indicated. You should reduce speed and take the lane appropriate for your intended direction in good time.

q-4257.text: Are you warned in this situation of a considerable road elevation?
q-4257.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign shown in the material warns of a considerable ascent. On a climb heavy vehicles lose speed, so you must select the right gear in time, increase the distance and not begin overtaking without a margin of visibility.

q-4258.text: In the presented situation, are you allowed to drive through the railway crossing without stopping?
q-4258.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign in force at this place orders an unconditional stop of the vehicle regardless of whether a train is visible. Only after stopping and making sure once again that the tracks are clear may you enter the crossing.

q-4260.text: You are driving a vehicle in the built-up area. In the presented situation, are you obliged to allow the bus driver to join the traffic?
q-4260.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area the driver is obliged to allow a bus moving off from a marked stop to join the traffic — if necessary they reduce speed or stop the vehicle. The bus driver must not create a danger while doing so.

q-4343.text: Are you warned in this situation of approaching an intersection at which the right of way is not established by signs?
q-4343.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material warns of an intersection of equal roads, where priority is not set by signs. The right-hand rule applies there, so you must reduce speed and be ready to give way to a vehicle approaching from the right.

q-4344.text: In the presented situation, before driving onto the rails, are you obliged to make sure that no rail vehicle is approaching?
q-4344.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before entering the tracks, the driver is obliged to exercise particular caution and make sure no rail vehicle, which has priority, is approaching. You enter the tracks only when there is room beyond them to clear them completely.

q-4345.text: You intend to go straight on, while the motorcyclist intends to turn left. Do you have to yield the right of way to the motorcyclist?
q-4345.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Going straight ahead by itself gives no priority — it is decided by the shape of the intersection and the signs or signals in force at that place. In this situation priority belongs to the motorcyclist, so you must give way to them.

q-4347.text: Are you allowed to begin overtaking in this situation?
q-4347.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking may be started only with sufficient visibility, a clear section of road and no prohibition arising from signs or road markings. In these conditions the manoeuvre cannot be performed safely, so it must be abandoned.

q-4348.text: You plan to turn right and the bus driver intends to turn left. Have you got priority over him?
q-4348.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority is decided not by the direction of the turn but by the hierarchy of the roads and the signs in force at this intersection. In this situation the bus driver has priority, so you must give way and let them complete the manoeuvre.

q-4349.text: Are you allowed to pass the preceding stationary vehicle on the left?
q-4349.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Passing on the left is not permitted when it would require entering the part of the roadway intended for the opposite direction contrary to the markings. A vehicle that is signalling a left turn and has moved towards the centre of the roadway is passed on its right side.

q-4350.text: You intend to turn right. Do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-4350.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The intention to turn right alone gives no priority. It is decided by the signs and the hierarchy of roads at the intersection, and in this situation the vehicle approaching from the left has priority — you must let it pass before starting the manoeuvre.

q-4351.text: You are driving on the major road. Do you have the right of way over the cyclist in this situation?
q-4351.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The priority arising from travelling on a road with priority concerns vehicles entering from subordinate roads. It does not release you from the duty to give way to a cyclist on a cycle crossing or to one going straight ahead when you change direction.

q-4352.text: Do you have the right of way over the cyclist in this situation?
q-4352.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this situation priority belongs to the cyclist, so the driver must slow down and let them ride through. When approaching a cycle crossing or crossing a bicycle's path, particular caution is exercised.

q-4353.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drive onto the pavement to avoid this vehicle?
q-4353.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The pavement is intended for pedestrians and the driver may not drive onto it to get around an obstacle. If there is no room on the roadway to pass safely, you should stop and wait until passage becomes possible.

q-4354.text: Are you allowed in this situation to drive a vehicle with high-beam lights switched on?
q-4354.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle the driver of an oncoming vehicle, a vehicle ahead or another road user. In such conditions dipped headlights apply, and they must be switched to early enough.

q-4355.text: After turning left, do the signs on the crosswise roadway prohibit you from going to the right uttermost lane?
q-4355.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible road markings do not introduce a ban on changing lanes — such a ban would follow from a solid line. After the turn you may therefore take the outer right lane, signalling the manoeuvre and giving way to vehicles already in that lane.

q-4356.text: Did you chose the place for stopping correctly in this situation?
q-4356.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping is permitted only where it does not endanger safety or obstruct other road users, and in many places it is expressly prohibited. The chosen place does not meet these conditions, so it must be changed.

q-4357.text: Are you passing the preceding vehicle correctly?
q-4357.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The manoeuvre is performed with particular caution and a safe distance from the vehicle being passed, without breaching prohibitions arising from the signs. The driver at the same time remains ready for a pedestrian appearing from behind the vehicle being passed.

q-4358.text: Have you got priority over the vehicle approaching from the left in this situation?
q-4358.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority at an intersection is decided by signs, signals and the hierarchy of roads, not by the side from which another vehicle approaches. In this situation the vehicle on the left has priority, so you must stop and let it pass.

q-4359.text: Are you obliged to observe the road in the exterior mirror in this situation before you join the traffic?
q-4359.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Joining the traffic requires particular caution and giving way to all other road users. Observation in the exterior mirror, supplemented by a glance over the shoulder at the blind spot, is a condition of safely starting to drive.

q-4362.text: While driving a car in the rain the risk of skidding is:

options.A: the highest in the initial stage of the rain.
options.B: the lowest in the initial stage of the rain.
options.C: the highest in the final stage of the rain.

q-4362.explanation: Correct answer: A. At the start of rain, water mixes with the dust, oil and rubber particles lying on the surface and forms a slippery layer that clearly reduces grip. Longer rain washes this dirt away, so the first minutes call for reduced speed.

q-4364.text: What is the influence of the speed of driving on the field of view of a passenger car driver?

options.A: When the speed increases the field of view narrows down.
options.B: When the speed increases the field of view expands.

q-4364.explanation: Correct answer: A. The faster the vehicle travels, the more the eyes concentrate on a distant point ahead of the vehicle, and the picture at the sides stops being registered. The narrowed field of vision means a pedestrian or cyclist at the side is noticed much later.

q-4367.text: Which of the following factors may restrict the field of view of a passenger car's driver?

options.A: Using air conditioning during the rain.
options.C: Blinding lights of other oncoming vehicles.

q-4367.explanation: Correct answer: C. Being dazzled by the lights of oncoming vehicles deprives the eye of the ability to distinguish detail for several seconds and genuinely limits the field of vision. You should then slow down and direct your gaze at the right edge of the carriageway.

q-4368.text: Which of the following factors may restrict the field of view of a passenger car's driver at night?
q-4368.explanation: Correct answer: C. Wrongly adjusted lights illuminate too short a stretch of road or aim the beam too high, so the driver sees less while dazzling others at the same time. The headlight adjustment should be checked especially when the vehicle is loaded.

q-4369.text: Which of the following factors may restrict the field of view of a passenger car's driver?

options.A: Blinking his eyes during a brake in driving.
options.B: 15 minutes of rest after two hours of driving.

q-4369.explanation: Correct answer: C. Alcohol disturbs the cooperation of the eyes and the brain: it lengthens reaction time, weakens the judgement of distance and narrows the field of vision to a thin slice ahead of the vehicle. A short rest or blinking does not have such an effect.

q-4370.text: Which of the following factors may restrict the field of view of a passenger car's driver?

options.A: The driver's seat mounted too low.
options.B: 15 minutes of rest after two hours of driving.
options.C: Sunglasses used on a sunny day.

q-4370.explanation: Correct answer: A. A seat set too low hides the road behind the edge of the bonnet and the dashboard, and one set too high limits the view with the top edge of the windscreen. Correct seat adjustment is a condition of a full field of vision and easy operation of the vehicle.

q-4371.text: What is the influence of the speed of driving on the angle of view of a passenger car's driver?

options.A: The higher the speed the larger the angle of view.
options.B: The higher the speed the smaller the angle of view.

q-4371.explanation: Correct answer: B. As speed increases, the eyes concentrate on an ever more distant point and the angle of vision becomes smaller. The driver notices what is happening at the side of the road later, so at high speed you must consciously check your surroundings.

q-4372.text: You are driving at the speed of 80 km/h. What starting position will ensure optimal trajectory on the bend?

options.A: In the middle of the road, partially crossing the line shown.
options.B: By the line dividing the lanes - on the right side of the roadway.
options.C: By the right edge of the road.

q-4372.explanation: Correct answer: B. The optimal line through a bend starts from its outer side, without leaving your own lane. The outer position here is next to the line dividing the lanes, on the right half of the carriageway; that line must not be crossed.

q-4373.text: You are driving at the speed of 90 km/h. What starting position will ensure optimal trajectory on the bend?

options.A: In the middle of the road, partially crossing the line shown.
options.B: By the line dividing the lanes - on the right side of the roadway.
options.C: By the right edge of the road.

q-4373.explanation: Correct answer: C. The optimal line through a bend starts from its outer side, while staying in your own lane. The outer position here is the right edge of the carriageway, which eases the turning radius and leaves a reserve of grip.

q-4374.text: How should you behave in order to accelerate the passenger car properly on a flat part of the road?

options.A: Use the engine revolutions maximally in every gear.
options.B: Accelerate to such speed in lower gear that after switching to the next gear the vehicle does not jerk and does not choke.
options.C: In every case increase the gear by two.

q-4374.explanation: Correct answer: B. You change up only after the vehicle has gained, in the lower gear, a speed at which the higher gear will keep the engine in its flexible range. Acceleration is then smooth and economical, and the drivetrain is not overloaded.

q-4375.text: In what way are you allowed to carry bicycles on a passenger car?

options.A: Placed in holders at the rear of the car and limiting the legibility of the registration plate.
options.B: Placed in holders at the rear of the car and covering one side light of the car.
options.C: Placed in holders fixed on the roof rack.

q-4375.explanation: Correct answer: C. A carried load must not cover the lights, reflectors or the number plate, and must not restrict the driver's view. Roof-rack carriers meet these conditions, and the bicycles must be firmly fastened.

q-4376.text: Is traffic allowed only for authorised vehicles on the right lane of the road beyond this sign?
q-4376.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The information sign reserves the right lane exclusively for a specific group of authorised vehicles. Other drivers may not use it and must use the adjacent lane; entering such a lane is permitted only to the extent the signs allow.

q-4378.text: Should you limit your trust to this traffic user in this situation and start braking?
q-4378.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The principle of limited trust requires you to allow for improper behaviour by another road user when the way they are moving or the situation indicates it. Starting to brake earlier shortens the stopping distance and lets you avoid a collision.

q-4379.text: Does the word "STOP" on the roadway confirm the marking of the entry to the junction with a vertical "stop" sign?
q-4379.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The word "STOP" on the roadway appears together with the vertical sign of the same meaning and confirms that it is in force. The driver must stop before the absolute stop line, and where there is none — before the intersection itself.

q-4381.text: Are you allowed to turn left in this situation?
q-4381.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force at this place rule out a left turn, and the driver must go in the direction that is permitted. Changing direction contrary to the signs or the arrows on the roadway is an offence and surprises the other road users.

q-4384.text: Are you allowed to turn right in this situation?
q-4384.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force at this place prohibit a right turn, so you must continue in the permitted direction. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the cross road seems clear.

q-4385.text: In this situation can you turn right from the traffic lane you are occupying?
q-4385.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The permitted directions of travel from a given lane are decided by the signs and direction arrows, and in this situation the lane you are in allows a right turn. The manoeuvre is signalled beforehand and way is given to pedestrians and cyclists crossing the roadway.

q-4386.text: Should you exercise particular caution when emerging from the field onto a hardened road?
q-4386.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Entering a paved road from a field is joining the traffic, which requires particular caution and giving way to all other road users. You must also remember the soil carried onto the roadway by the wheels, because it reduces grip.

q-4388.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution in this situation?
q-4388.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-4391.text: Should you be prepared to stop your vehicle in this situation?
q-4391.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The conditions at this place require readiness to stop, because priority may belong to another road user or the road may turn out to be blocked. Speed is chosen so that the vehicle can be stopped within the visible section of road.

q-4394.text: Is it justifiable to decrease the speed when passing in this situation?
q-4394.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing narrows the free space and hides what is behind the object being passed, so reducing speed is justified here. A lower speed allows you to keep a safe distance and stop when a pedestrian suddenly appears.

q-4395.text: Can you drive with high-beam lights switched on in this situation?
q-4395.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle the driver of an oncoming vehicle, a vehicle ahead or another road user. In such conditions dipped headlights apply, and they must be switched to early enough.

q-4396.text: Are you allowed in this situation to use daytime running lights instead of low beam lights?
q-4396.explanation: Correct answer: YES. During the day, when the air is normally clear, daytime running lights may be used instead of dipped headlights. From dusk to dawn and in conditions of reduced clarity, dipped headlights are compulsory.

q-4397.text: Should you use the horn in this situation?
