q-4397.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn is used solely when necessary to warn of an immediate danger, and in a built-up area its use is prohibited otherwise. Here the right course is to slow down and take special care.

q-4409.text: Are you allowed to drive a bus with a single axle load of 10 tons on a road marked in such a way?
q-4409.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing indicates a road with a permitted single-axle load no lower than the axle load of this bus. A load of 10 tonnes is within the permitted range, so driving along this road is allowed.

q-4410.text: You are driving a bus which performs paid transport on regular lines. Are you allowed to use the right lane at any time in this situation?
q-4410.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A lane designated by signing for buses is intended precisely for vehicles carrying passengers for payment on regular routes. The driver of such a bus may use it without time restrictions, taking care towards other road users.

q-4411.text: Do these white reflective road studs placed on the right side on the dashed line divide the lanes in this situation?
q-4411.explanation: Correct answer: YES. White reflective road studs are placed together with the lines separating lanes so that their course is visible at night and in bad weather. They do not change the meaning of the line — it is the line that decides whether a lane change is permitted.

q-4413.text: You intend to turn left and the vehicle approaching from the right plans to go straight. Have you got the right of way over this vehicle?
q-4413.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At an intersection of equal roads the vehicle approaching from the right has priority, and additionally a driver turning left gives way to those going straight ahead. The manoeuvre may be started only after letting that vehicle pass.

q-4415.text: Is it allowed to drive a lorry of a single axle load of 10 tons on the road marked in such a way?
q-4415.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing indicates a road with a permitted single-axle load no lower than the axle load of this lorry. The value of 10 tonnes does not exceed the permitted load, so the passage is allowed.

q-4444.text: Is the tractor left unattended in the parking lot properly protected against being started by unauthorized person?
q-4444.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver who leaves the vehicle must secure it against being started by an unauthorised person and against moving on its own. Switch off the engine, take the key and apply the parking brake.

q-4446.text: Are you allowed to move away from the parked tractor, if the engine is running?
q-4446.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A vehicle left unattended may not be left with the engine running, because it could be started or move without a driver. Before walking away, switch off the engine and secure the vehicle against moving off.

q-4447.text: Is the motorcycle left unattended in the parking lot properly protected against being started by unauthorized person?
q-4447.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When leaving a motorcycle, the rider must prevent it being started by an unauthorised person: switch off the engine, remove the key and lock the steering. In the state shown, those conditions are not met.

q-4448.text: Are you allowed to move away from the parked motorcycle, if the engine is running?
q-4448.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A vehicle left unattended must have its engine switched off, otherwise it is easy to start or move. Only after switching off the engine and securing the motorcycle may the rider walk away from it.

q-4449.text: Is the bus left unattended in the parking lot properly protected against being started by unauthorized person?
q-4449.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A bus left unattended must be secured against being started by an unauthorised person and against rolling away. Switching off the engine, taking the key and applying the parking brake are necessary.

q-4450.text: Is the vehicle left unattended in the parking lot properly protected against being started by unauthorized person?
q-4450.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When leaving the vehicle, the driver must secure it against being started by an unauthorised person and against moving on its own. In the state shown that condition is not met, because the vehicle remains ready to drive.

q-4451.text: Are you allowed to move away from the parked vehicle, if the engine is running?
q-4451.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver may not walk away from a vehicle left with the engine running, because such a vehicle is easy to start or set in motion. First switch off the engine and secure the vehicle against moving.

q-4452.text: Are you allowed to move away from the parked bus if the engine is running?
q-4452.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A bus left unattended may not be left with the engine running, because it risks being started by an unauthorised person or rolling away. The driver first switches off the engine and secures the vehicle, and only then may walk away.

q-4454.text: Is the vehicle left unattended in the parking lot properly protected against being started by unauthorized person?
q-4454.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When leaving the vehicle, the driver must secure it against being started by an unauthorised person and against moving off by itself. In the state shown this condition is not met, because the vehicle remains ready to drive.

q-4458.text: You intend to turn right. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-4458.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The direction of travel does not change the rules of priority — a right turn does not release you from the duty to let pass a vehicle to which the signs or signals in the material grant priority. The vehicle approaching from the left goes first.

q-4472.text: In which of the listed cases regular technical inspections of a vehicle has influence on its safe use in road traffic?

options.A: Only after the warranty period expiry.

q-4472.explanation: Correct answer: C. The technical condition deteriorates throughout the vehicle's life, regardless of whether it is still under warranty. Regular technical inspections detect wear of the brakes, suspension or lights before it leads to an accident.

q-4474.text: You intend to follow the road ahead. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-4474.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At an intersection of equal roads the vehicle approaching from the right has priority, so the driver on the left gives way. You must, however, make sure they really intend to slow down and stop.

q-4475.text: You are turning right and the driver of the oncoming vehicle intends to turn left. Have you got priority over him?
q-4475.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning left is obliged to give way to oncoming vehicles, including those turning right. Even so, it is worth making sure the motorcyclist really is stopping before performing the manoeuvre.

q-4479.text: What does the warning light with the battery symbol turned red when on the move warn of?

options.A: Of the damage to the battery.
options.B: Of a total discharge of the battery.
options.C: Of faulty operation of battery charging.

q-4479.explanation: Correct answer: C. The light with the battery symbol signals that the charging system is not supplying current, so the vehicle is running solely on the energy stored in the battery. Shorten the journey to the nearest workshop and switch off unnecessary electrical consumers.

q-4481.text: Which of the following results may be caused by continuing driving when the engine oil pressure warning light is flashing red?

options.C: Damage to the drive transferring mechanisms.

q-4481.explanation: Correct answer: A. A lit oil-pressure light means that oil is not reaching the engine's moving parts at the correct pressure. Driving on leads to overheating and seizure, so stop the vehicle safely and switch off the engine.

q-4483.text: Which of the following persons are obliged to use seat belts?

options.A: A person carried on a wheelchair.

q-4483.explanation: Correct answer: B. The driver of a vehicle fitted with seat belts must use them for the whole journey. Exempt from the duty are, among others, women who are visibly pregnant and people carried in a wheelchair.

q-4484.text: What is the role of a properly placed headrest in case of a road accident?

options.A: It protects the top of the head.

q-4484.explanation: Correct answer: B. In an impact, especially from behind, the head is thrown back violently, and the head restraint limits this movement and protects the cervical vertebrae. It is effective only when it reaches the upper part of the head and sits close to it.

q-4485.text: In head-on crashes the use of seat belts:

options.A: reduces the risk of serious or deadly injuries.
options.B: increases the risk of light injuries.
options.C: does not have influence on the risk of injuries regardless of their kind.

q-4485.explanation: Correct answer: A. The belt holds the body against the seat, spreads the force of the impact over strong parts of the skeleton and prevents striking the interior or being thrown out of the vehicle. As a result the risk of serious and fatal injuries falls clearly.

q-4486.text: In which situation will a fastened safety belt not function properly:

options.B: When its upper part is located below the neck.

q-4486.explanation: Correct answer: A. A twisted belt rests against the body as a narrow strip, so instead of spreading the force of the impact it concentrates it on a small area and can itself cause injuries. The belt must lie flat, fit the body and be taut.

q-4488.text: Were you obliged to use an indicator in the situation shown?
q-4488.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intended change of direction or lane must be signalled clearly and early enough with the indicator, and after the manoeuvre the signal switched off. Signalling informs others and lets them adapt their driving.

q-4495.text: What is the purpose of using the ABS system in a passenger car?

options.A: Preventing losing stability and ensuring steerability of the vehicle while braking.
options.B: Preventing skidding - regardless of its speed and road conditions.

q-4495.explanation: Correct answer: A. ABS does not let the wheels lock under braking, so the vehicle stays stable and steerable and the driver can steer round an obstacle. The system does not change the laws of physics, though, and does not protect against the effects of excessive speed.

q-4534.text: Which of the following actions should you take while driving a passenger car on the road covered with snow?

options.A: Avoid sudden movements of the driving wheel.

q-4534.explanation: Correct answer: A. Grip on snow is low, so any sudden steering movement risks losing control of the vehicle. Steering, braking and accelerating should be smooth, and speed adapted to the state of the surface.

q-4538.text: Does this sign placed under the signalling device indicate that it is prohibited to enter the railroad switch and an obligation to stop and check whether the switch rails are properly positioned?
q-4538.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Such signing prohibits entering the switch without stopping and requires the tram driver to check that the switch blades are set for the intended direction of travel. Only after that check may the journey continue.

q-4540.text: Does the visible broken line on the roadway indicate a stop for trams, buses or trolley buses?
q-4540.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The zigzag line marks on the carriageway the stop for public transport vehicles. Within that marking, stopping and parking of other vehicles is prohibited so that a bus or tram can pull up to the kerb freely.

q-4542.text: When turning left in this situation, are you obliged to give way to the tram from the opposite direction?
q-4542.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning left gives way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction, and in addition a tram enjoys the priority that comes from running on rails. The manoeuvre begins only after the tram has passed.

q-4543.text: Does the visible broken line on the road indicate a parking place for the disabled?
q-4543.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The zigzag line marks a stop for public transport vehicles, not a parking space. A space for a person with a disability is marked with a separate sign and symbol, usually in blue.

q-4545.text: In this situation, are you performing an overtaking manoeuvre?
q-4545.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking is driving past a vehicle moving in the same direction. Since the vehicle being passed is in motion, the manoeuvre being carried out is overtaking, not passing an obstacle, and all the rules connected with it apply.

q-4546.text: In such a situation, do you have the right of way over the pedestrian?
q-4546.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A pedestrian on the crossing has priority over every vehicle, a tram included. The driver must reduce speed and let them cross safely to the other side.

q-4547.text: How should the tram driver behave in increasing traffic intensity?

options.A: Reach maximum speed to make up for possible delays.
options.B: Use the sound signal to speed up passage.
options.C: Slow down and increase the distance from the preceding tram to lower the level of risk.

q-4547.explanation: Correct answer: C. A tram is heavy and brakes over a long distance, and in dense traffic the number of sudden situations grows. Reducing speed and increasing the distance from the tram ahead gives time to react and lowers the risk of a collision.

options.A: wetting of the rails by rainfall.
options.B: moisture settling on cooled rails, mainly in the autumn.
options.C: evaporation of moisture after a rainfall.

q-4548.explanation: Correct answer: B. On chilled rails, especially in autumn, moisture from the air settles and forms a thin, very slippery layer. Wheel grip drops sharply, so starting and braking must be carried out exceptionally gently.

q-4549.text: How should the tram driver behave when it starts raining?

options.C: Do not change method of start-up.

q-4549.explanation: Correct answer: A. The first drops of rain form a slippery layer on the rails, so the wheels easily slip when starting. A gentler start keeps grip and at the same time protects standing passengers from falling.

q-4551.text: What should the tram driver do before driving onto the rail switch?

options.A: Only look at the signalling device indicating the direction of the rail switch.
options.B: Look at the switch point and signalling device indicating the direction of the rail switch.
options.C: Only look in the direction of travel.

q-4551.explanation: Correct answer: B. The indicator reports the commanded position of the switch, but the actual setting is confirmed only by a visual check of the blades. Checking both of these protects against derailment and against going the wrong way.

q-4552.text: What should the tram driver do, seeing the signalling device indicating a change in the position of the rail switch to the right?

options.A: Take a look at the switch points to make sure it is positioned in the right direction.
options.B: Exclusively follow the indication of the signalling device.
options.C: In any case, stop the tram and go out to the rail switch.

q-4552.explanation: Correct answer: A. The indicator's reading is only information about the commanded setting, and the actual position is decided by the blades. The driver confirms it by eye, and stopping the tram and getting out is necessary only when the switch is not set correctly.

q-4553.text: What does the proper technique of driving a tram consist of?

options.A: Starting-up as long as possible, coasting as short as possible and gentle braking.
options.B: A gentle start-up, coasting as long as possible and sudden braking.
options.C: A gentle start-up, coasting as long as possible and gentle braking.

q-4553.explanation: Correct answer: C. A gentle start and gentle braking protect standing passengers from falling and reduce wear of the drive and the brakes. Long coasting makes use of the tram's momentum and clearly saves energy.

q-4562.text: In the case of not giving first aid to the road accident casualty who is in life endangerment situation the criminal responsibility is on:

options.A: any person who could have given them first aid without endangering their own or others' safety.
options.C: only on a road accident participant.

q-4562.explanation: Correct answer: A. The duty to help a person in immediate danger to life or health rests on everyone who can do so without endangering themselves or another person. Failing to give such help carries criminal liability.

q-4563.text: The car accident casualty who is in the vehicle should be:

options.A: evacuated from the vehicle - in all cases.
options.B: evacuated from the vehicle - in case of stating a cardiac arrest in them.
options.C: always left in the vehicle - till the coming of a doctor.

q-4563.explanation: Correct answer: B. Moving a casualty risks worsening spinal injuries, so they are taken out of the vehicle only when saving their life requires it. Cardiac arrest is such a case, because resuscitation is carried out on a hard, flat surface.

q-4568.text: Does the speed limit defined by this sign apply to the tram driver exclusively to the nearest junction or rail intersection, provided the signs do not instruct otherwise?
q-4568.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A speed limit introduced by a sign binds the tram driver until the nearest junction or crossing of the tracks, unless other signs provide otherwise. After passing such a place, the speed under the general rules applies.

q-4569.text: In this situation, are you allowed to enter beyond the signalling device?
q-4569.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal head is showing a signal prohibiting further travel, so you may not pass it. Stop before the stop line or, where there is none, before the signal head, and wait for the permitting signal.

q-4578.text: You are a car accident participant. Which of the listed pieces of information should you give when calling the emergency number?

options.A: The place of the accident, the number and the condition of casualties.
options.B: Only the number of vehicles taking part in the accident.

q-4578.explanation: Correct answer: A. The person taking the call must above all be told the location of the incident and the number and condition of the casualties, because that decides how many rescue teams of what kind will be sent. The call is ended only when they say so.

q-4579.text: You are a car accident participant. How should you behave when there is clothing burning on a person?

options.A: Push the person to the ground and put out the fire by covering them with a jacket, blanket or a coat.
options.B: Wait for the coming of the fire brigade.
options.C: Put out the fire using an extinguisher.

q-4579.explanation: Correct answer: A. Burning clothing is put out by laying the casualty on the ground and smothering the flames with a jacket, blanket or coat — lying down limits the supply of air and protects the airway. Waiting for the fire brigade would mean extensive burns.

q-4592.text: Which of the listed emergencies makes it impossible to use a passenger car in road traffic?
q-4592.explanation: Correct answer: C. Brake lights tell drivers behind that you are slowing down, so their failure is a fault in a safety system that excludes the vehicle from use on the road. Non-working air conditioning or parking sensors do not affect whether the car may be used.

q-4593.text: Which of the listed actions should be taken in the first place when the red engine oil pressure control light goes on while driving?

options.C: Stop the vehicle and turn off the engine.

q-4593.explanation: Correct answer: C. A red oil-pressure light means there is no proper lubrication, and keeping the engine running risks seizing it in a very short time. Pull over safely, stop the vehicle and switch off the engine immediately, and only then check the oil level.

q-4595.text: Are you taking the proper lane if you want to turn left at the nearest junction?
q-4595.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Before turning left you must move in good time to the outer left lane intended for that direction. The lane you are in does not allow a left turn, so you must change it before the intersection or drive according to its designation.

q-4596.text: Is the presented U-turn manoeuvre prohibited in these road conditions?
q-4596.explanation: Correct answer: NO. No ban on turning around applies at this place, and the road conditions allow the manoeuvre without forcing others to brake harshly. The driver turning around must, however, give way to the other vehicles and make sure of the visibility.

q-4598.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the vehicle from the right if there is such a possibility?
q-4598.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking on the right is permitted in the exceptions provided for by the rules — among others, for a vehicle signalling an intention to turn left and on a roadway with marked lanes in a built-up area. The situation in the material corresponds to such an exception.

q-4600.text: Is the number 112 an all-Poland emergency number for all emergency services?
q-4600.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The number 112 works throughout the country and connects you to an operator who takes the report and passes it to the ambulance service, the police or the fire brigade. The call is free and can be made from a landline or a mobile phone.

q-4601.text: What should you do if as a result of a traffic accident, fuel leaking from the damaged vehicles gather around the tram?

options.A: Disconnect the pantograph from the grid and evacuate the passengers to a safe place.
options.B: Immediately move away from the tram, leaving the decision to evacuate to the passengers.
options.C: Wait in the tram until arrival of the fire brigade.

q-4601.explanation: Correct answer: A. Spilt fuel near a tram risks ignition from sparking at the current collector, so first the pantograph is disconnected from the line, and then the passengers are evacuated to a safe place. Staying in the car or waiting passively exposes everyone to fire.

q-4602.text: You drive a rail vehicle. How will you behave when you notice a fire in the electrical installation?

options.A: I will stop the vehicle, open the door to evacuate the passengers, disconnect the pantograph from the rail grid and proceed to extinguish the fire.
options.B: I will drive to the nearest stop and then call the Fire Brigade.
options.C: Leave the tram as fast as possible.

q-4602.explanation: Correct answer: A. With an electrical fire, stop the vehicle, open the doors and get the passengers out, disconnect the pantograph from the overhead line, and only with the power cut off put out the fire. Driving on to the stop or fleeing the car would leave the passengers without help.

q-4612.text: In this situation, can you enter the intersection in order to go straight?
q-4612.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal or sign in force at this place permits entering the intersection, and going straight ahead does not conflict with vehicles that have priority. You may enter, however, only when there is room beyond the intersection to leave it.

q-4613.text: What speed must you drive on a motorway?

options.C: A speed which does not cause an obstacle for other drivers, but not exceeding the maximum speed limit.

q-4613.explanation: Correct answer: C. On a motorway there is no fixed minimum speed expressed as a number — you should drive safely, without obstructing others, but without exceeding the permitted speed. Unjustifiably slow driving is as dangerous there as excessive speed.

q-4614.text: When you ride a moped, do you have to wear a helmet?

options.B: No, if I drive at a low speed.
options.C: Not if I travel as a passenger.

q-4614.explanation: Correct answer: A. A moped rider must always wear a protective helmet, regardless of speed and the length of the route; the duty also covers a passenger being carried. The helmet must be fastened correctly, otherwise it does not do its job.

q-4619.text: Do you always have to stop before you enter a railway crossing marked with this sign?
q-4619.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign warns of a railway crossing and requires particular caution, but does not in itself oblige you to stop the vehicle. You must stop when required by a STOP sign, a red signal, lowering barriers or an approaching train.

q-6010.text: Do the signs you see here warn you that you are approaching a pedestrian crossing?
q-6010.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible announce a different danger than a pedestrian crossing. The approach to a crossing is warned of by a separate sign with a pedestrian silhouette on stripes, and the crossing itself is marked with an information sign and stripes on the roadway.

q-6011.text: Once you go past these signs, should you expect the road to narrow on both sides?
q-6011.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces a narrowing of the roadway on both sides, so the width of the road decreases symmetrically and the lanes become narrower. You must reduce speed, increase the lateral distance and pass oncoming vehicles carefully.

q-6012.text: Does this sign warn you of an area that experiences intense precipitation?
q-6012.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Warning signs do not inform about weather phenomena such as heavy precipitation — this sign announces a different danger related to the road. The driver learns about weather conditions from variable message boards and announcements.

q-6014.text: Does this sign warn you of the possibility of black ice on the road?
q-6014.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces a section where black ice or icing may occur on the roadway, especially on bridges, in dips and in shaded places. You should reduce speed, lengthen the distance and avoid sudden braking and steering.

q-6015.text: Can you expect an oncoming vehicle after passing this warning sign?
q-6015.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces a section of road with traffic in both directions, so you must allow for oncoming vehicles. You should keep to the right side of the roadway, reduce speed and not occupy the left part of the road.

q-6016.text: Can you enter the road past this sign for the purpose of making a U-turn?
q-6016.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign prohibits entering this road, and the prohibition applies regardless of the purpose of the manoeuvre — also when the driver only wants to turn around. You should turn around at another, permitted place, without passing the sign.

q-6017.text: Can you drive past this sign with a vehicle (without a trailer) having a gross vehicle mass of 3 t?
q-6017.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The prohibition expressed by this sign concerns vehicles whose actual total mass exceeds the value given on the sign. A car with a mass of 3 t travelling without a trailer does not exceed that value, so it may pass the sign.

q-6018.text: In this situation, do you have to stop immediately in front of the stopping line and not in front of the sign?
q-6018.explanation: Correct answer: YES. If a stop line is marked on the roadway, the driver stops the vehicle directly before it, not level with the sign or the traffic light. The line marks a boundary that must not be crossed and leaves room for other road users.

q-6019.text: Can you make a U-turn at the nearest intersection?
q-6019.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this intersection turning around is ruled out — this follows from the prohibition in force there or from the traffic arrangement indicated by the signs. The manoeuvre must be performed at another place, where it is permitted and will not force others to brake.

q-6021.text: In this situation, can you turn left once you go past this sign?
q-6021.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign in force at this place rules out a left turn — the permitted directions of travel are different. The prohibition concerns the nearest intersection, so the intended direction must be reached by another route.

q-6022.text: Does the speed limit you see here apply only to the nearest intersection?
q-6022.explanation: Correct answer: NO. This limit does not end at the nearest intersection — it applies throughout the whole area for which it was introduced. Only a sign cancelling it or the end of that area restores the speed that follows from the general rules.

q-6023.text: Can you make a U-turn at this intersection?
q-6023.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this intersection turning around is not permitted because of the prohibition in force there or the traffic arrangement set by the signs. The manoeuvre must be postponed to a place where it is permitted and safe.

q-6024.text: In this situation, can you turn right at the nearest intersection?
q-6024.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force at this place rule out a right turn at the nearest intersection. The driver must go in the direction that is permitted, and carry out the intended change of route further on.

q-6026.text: Does this sign indicate that you are obliged to drive straight ahead at the nearest intersection?
q-6026.explanation: Correct answer: NO. This sign has a different meaning and does not impose the duty to drive straight ahead through the nearest intersection. The straight-ahead order is expressed by a mandatory sign with a vertical arrow pointing upwards.

q-6027.text: When you approach a place marked with this sign, are you obliged to exercise special caution?
q-6027.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a danger, so the driver is obliged to exercise particular caution: raise their attention, observe the surroundings and be ready to react, including stopping the vehicle.

q-6028.text: On a road marked in this way, can you drive a passenger car at a speed of 100 km/h?
q-6028.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The permitted speed for a passenger car on a road marked in this way is not lower than 100 km/h, so such driving complies with the rules. Speed must, however, always be adapted to the traffic conditions and visibility.

q-6029.text: Beyond this sign, is 120 km/h the maximum speed at which you may drive a passenger car?
q-6029.explanation: Correct answer: NO. For a passenger car on the road indicated by this sign a different permitted speed applies from the one given in the question. The limit is decided by the type of road, not by the driver's habit.

q-6030.text: On a road, once you go past this sign, can you drive at a speed of 30 km/h?
q-6030.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Beyond this sign a requirement applies to drive at a speed not lower than indicated, and 30 km/h is below it. You may drive more slowly only when forced to by traffic conditions, the state of the road or safety.

q-6032.text: In this situation, are you obliged to give right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right side?
q-6032.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At an intersection of equal roads, where priority is not determined by signs or signals, the vehicle approaching from the right has priority. When approaching such a place, you must reduce speed and be ready to stop.

q-6033.text: On a road, past this sign, can you make a U-turn?
q-6033.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign indicates a road on which U-turns are ruled out because of its character and the way traffic is organised. The manoeuvre would be very dangerous there; you may turn around only beyond the section covered by this sign.

q-6034.text: On a road, once you go past this sign, can you make a U-turn?
q-6034.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign does not introduce a ban on turning around, so the manoeuvre is permitted. When performing it, you must give way to other road users, have sufficient visibility and not force anyone to brake harshly.

q-6035.text: Does the first sign you see here tell you to drive with a speed of up to 50 km/h?
q-6035.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The nearest visible sign does not set such a limit — its meaning is different. A limit to a specific value is introduced by a prohibition sign with a number in a red border, and it applies from the place where it is installed.

q-6036.text: Does this sign inform you of approaching an exit from the motorway?
q-6036.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces that you are approaching a motorway exit and lets you take the correct lane in good time. You should slow down only in the deceleration lane, not in the lane used by the other vehicles.

q-6039.text: In this situation, when you're changing lanes, are you obliged to use your turn signal?
q-6039.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every lane change must be signalled with the appropriate indicator, in advance and clearly, so that others have time to react. After the manoeuvre is completed the signal is switched off immediately.

q-6041.text: On a road, once you go past this sign, can you drive at a speed of 20 km/h?
q-6041.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The value of 20 km/h does not exceed the permitted speed in force beyond this sign, so such driving complies with the rules. You must not, however, obstruct other drivers without a justified reason.

q-6042.text: On a road, once you go past this sign, do you have the right of way over pedestrians?
q-6042.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Beyond this sign pedestrians have priority and may use the full width of the road. The driver moves there very slowly, gives way to pedestrians and, if necessary, stops the vehicle.

q-6043.text: On a road, once you go past this sign, are you obliged to give the right of way to pedestrians ?
q-6043.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Pedestrians there have priority over vehicles and may move across the full width of the road, including children playing by the roadway. The driver must drive very slowly and be ready to stop.

q-6046.text: On a road marked this way, can you drive a light four wheeled vehicle (microcar, quad)?
q-6046.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Only vehicles capable of reaching the speed required there may enter this road, and a light quadricycle does not meet that condition. Slow vehicles must use roads of a lower category.

q-6047.text: On a road marked this way, can you drive a light four wheeled vehicle (microcar, quad)?
q-6047.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Only vehicles capable of reaching the speed required there may enter this road, and a light quadricycle does not meet that condition. Slow vehicles must use roads of a lower category.

q-6049.text: In this situation, when you're changing lanes, are you obliged to indicate your intention of making such a manoeuvre?
q-6049.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intention to change lane is signalled with the indicator in advance and clearly, regardless of the traffic density and whether anyone is driving alongside. After the manoeuvre the signal must be switched off.

q-6050.text: When riding a moped vehicle, can you turn right onto the road marked this way?
q-6050.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing of this road does not exclude mopeds from traffic, so a right turn is allowed. Before the manoeuvre, signal your intention, move to the right edge of the carriageway and give way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway.

q-6051.text: When riding a moped vehicle, can you turn right once you go past this sign?
q-6051.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign does not prohibit a right turn at the nearest junction, so the manoeuvre is also permitted for a moped. Take up position at the right edge of the carriageway beforehand and clearly signal your intention to turn.

q-6052.text: Do these road markings tell you to change lanes by going to the next lane indicated by an arrow?
q-6052.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Guiding arrows inform that the lane you are in is ending or being closed to traffic, so you must move to the adjacent lane indicated by the arrow. The lane change is made in advance, signalled with the indicator.

q-6053.text: Does this road marking allow you to go straight through the intersection using this lane?
q-6053.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The lane you are in is not intended for going straight ahead — the permitted directions are indicated by the arrows on the roadway and you must drive according to them. The lane change should have been made before the intersection.

q-6054.text: Does this road marking allow you to make a U-turn?
q-6054.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This road marking may be crossed, so by itself it does not rule out turning around. The manoeuvre may be performed if no vertical sign prohibits it and visibility and traffic allow it to be done without danger.

q-6055.text: Does this road marking allow you to go straight in this lane?
q-6055.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The arrow painted on this lane indicates other permitted directions of travel, so going straight ahead from this lane is not permitted. You must move to the lane intended for going straight before the intersection.

q-6058.text: Can you stop a passenger car in a spot designated as a stop area (a zigzag line)?
q-6058.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The area marked with a stop line is reserved for public transport vehicles, so stopping another vehicle there is prohibited, even for a brief moment. You can ask for directions after stopping in a permitted place.

q-6060.text: Does this road marking designate a parking lane?
q-6060.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This road marking separates from the road a strip intended for parking vehicles. The vehicle should be placed within the marked area so that it does not protrude into the traffic lane and does not obstruct others.

q-6063.text: On a line marked by triangular road markings, are you unconditionally obliged to stop the vehicle?
q-6063.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A line made up of triangles means a duty to give way, not an absolute stop. You need to stop only when the situation requires it; an unconditional stop is ordered by a STOP sign together with a solid line.

q-6064.text: Does a broken line in front of a pedestrian crossing indicate a conditional stopping area?
q-6064.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The broken line before the crossing marks the place of a conditional stop — the driver stops before it when the need arises, for example to give way to pedestrians. If nothing requires a stop, it may be crossed.

q-6065.text: Does this road marking allow you to continue riding a moped vehicle in this lane?
q-6065.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The road marking indicates that you cannot continue in this lane — the lane ends or is intended for another direction or other vehicles. Move into the neighbouring lane in good time, signalling the manoeuvre.

q-6066.text: Can you stop in the spot designated as a stop area (a zigzag line)?
q-6066.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The stop area is intended solely for public transport vehicles, so other vehicles may not stop there even for a moment. To answer a phone call, choose a place where stopping is allowed.

q-6067.text: Do the visible road markings in the right lane indicate the start of an exit from the motorway?
q-6067.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible road markings have a different meaning than the beginning of a deceleration lane. A motorway exit is announced by separate vertical signs, and its beginning is marked by the line separating the deceleration lane from the main carriageway.

q-6068.text: Does this signal mean a collision-free left turn?
q-6068.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A green arrow shown in a separate phase means that the other directions are held at that time, so the left turn is made without conflict with other vehicles. Even so, you must watch the road and remain cautious.

q-6070.text: Can you drive through the pedestrian crossing in this situation?
q-6070.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The situation at the crossing does not allow passage — the pedestrians have priority, and the driver must give way to them and, if necessary, stop the vehicle before the crossing. You may move off only when the crossing is clear.

q-6071.text: Does this signal mean that you can enter a pedestrian crossing and a crossing for cyclists?
q-6071.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown does not permit entering the pedestrian crossing or the cycle crossing — the vehicle must be stopped before them. Entering without authorisation would block the crossing and create an immediate danger.

q-6072.text: In this situation, can you enter the railway crossing?
q-6072.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal, the barriers or the situation at the crossing prohibit entry, so the vehicle must be stopped before the crossing and you must wait. Entering a closing crossing or at a red signal is exceptionally dangerous.

q-6073.text: In this situation, do you have the right of way over a tram?
q-6073.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A tram's priority is not absolute — the order is decided by signs, signals and the general traffic rules. In this situation priority belongs to the driver of the vehicle, but you must make sure the tram driver really is giving way.

q-6074.text: In this situation, after the light turns green and the pedestrians leave the crossing, can you enter the intersection?
q-6074.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal in force permits entering the intersection, and the priority of the other road users has already been respected. You may move off, however, only when there is room beyond the intersection to leave it.

q-6075.text: In this situation, can you enter the intersection?
q-6075.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal in force permits entering the intersection, and the priority of the other road users has already been respected. You may move off, however, only when there is room beyond the intersection to leave it.

q-6077.text: In this situation, can you make a U-turn?
q-6077.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this place neither signs nor road markings prohibit turning around, so the manoeuvre is permitted. It may be performed only with sufficient visibility, after giving way to approaching vehicles and without obstructing traffic.

q-6078.text: In the situation that you see here, can you enter the railway crossing?
q-6078.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal, the barriers or the situation at the crossing prohibit entry, so the vehicle must be stopped before the crossing and you must wait. Entering a closing crossing or at a red signal is exceptionally dangerous.

q-6079.text: In this situation, are the traffic lights more important than the road signs?
q-6079.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When the traffic lights are working, the driver follows their indications above all, and the signs determining priority remain inactive at that time. The signs take effect only when the lights are switched off or show a flashing signal.

q-6080.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop before you enter the intersection?
q-6080.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Nothing here orders an absolute stop — only caution and, where necessary, giving way apply. Stopping becomes necessary only when required by a STOP sign, a signal or the situation on the road.

q-6081.text: In this situation, can you enter the intersection?
q-6081.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal in force or the situation at the intersection rules out entering, so you must stop before the stop line, and where there is none — before the intersection. Entering an occupied intersection would block the cross traffic.

q-6082.text: In this situation, can you enter the intersection?
q-6082.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal in force permits entry, and the intended passage does not conflict with vehicles that have priority. You may enter on condition that the intersection can be left without stopping on it.

q-6083.text: In this situation, can you make a U-turn at the intersection?
q-6083.explanation: Correct answer: YES. No ban on turning around applies at this intersection, and the signal in force permits travel, so the manoeuvre is allowed. The driver turning around gives way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians on the crossing.

q-6084.text: Do you merge with traffic when you leave the residential area?
q-6084.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving a residential zone onto a road is joining the traffic, so the driver is obliged to give way to all road users on that road. The manoeuvre is performed with particular caution.

q-6086.text: Do you have the right of way over all vehicles at an intersection marked in such a way?
q-6086.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Travelling on a road with priority does not give an advantage over everyone — you must give way, among others, to emergency vehicles, and when turning, also to oncoming vehicles. Pedestrians on a crossing also have priority.

q-6087.text: If you turn right at this intersection, do you have the right of way over the approaching vehicle?
q-6087.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The path of a right turn does not cross the way of the approaching vehicle, so priority belongs to the driver performing this manoeuvre. You must, however, watch cyclists and pedestrians on the right.

q-6088.text: If you turn left at this intersection, do you have the right of way over the approaching vehicle?
q-6088.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning left, the driver crosses the path of the approaching vehicle and must therefore give way to it. The manoeuvre may be started only when it will not force anyone to change speed or direction.

q-6089.text: If you turn left at this intersection, do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction?
q-6089.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A vehicle coming straight from the opposite direction has priority over one turning left, even when both are travelling on a road with priority. The turning driver waits until the way is clear, positioning the vehicle so as not to block the intersection.

q-6090.text: If you enter the road from a sidewalk, does this mean that you are merging with traffic?
q-6090.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Entering the roadway from the pavement is joining the traffic, so you must give way to all vehicles and pedestrians and exercise particular caution. The manoeuvre begins only when it will not obstruct anyone.

q-6091.text: If you go straight ahead at this intersection, do you have the right of way over a cyclist?
q-6091.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this situation it is the cyclist who has priority, and the driver of the vehicle must give way to them — this follows from the signs and the road layout visible in the material. Before a cycle crossing, particular caution and readiness to stop apply.

q-6094.text: If you merge with traffic, should you give the right of way to a pedestrian who is not on a pedestrian crossing?
q-6094.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When joining the traffic, the driver is obliged to give way to all other road users, including pedestrians — also when the pedestrian is not on a pedestrian crossing. The manoeuvre may be started only when it will obstruct no one.

q-6095.text: If you enter a road from a car park, should you give the right of way to vehicles travelling on the road?
q-6095.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving a car park is joining the traffic, so the driver gives way to vehicles travelling on the roadway, and also to pedestrians and cyclists in their way. You may move off only when no one will have to brake or change direction.

q-6096.text: In this situation, are you obliged to give the right of way to a tractor?
q-6096.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority is decided by the signs and the layout of the intersection, not by the type of vehicle — an agricultural tractor has no special rights on that account. In this situation it is you who has priority, although a slower vehicle requires increased caution.

q-6097.text: If you turn left at this intersection, do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-6097.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority follows from the signs at the intersection visible in the material — you are on the road with priority, so the vehicle approaching from the left must give way to you. Even so, the left turn is made after making sure that driver really is waiting.

q-6098.text: If you go straight, are you obliged to give the right of way to the cyclist?
q-6098.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The cyclist enjoys priority at this place, so the driver of the vehicle must give way to them, even when going straight ahead. When approaching a cycle crossing, you must exercise particular caution and not enter it in front of the cyclist.

q-6099.text: If you turn left at this intersection, do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction?
q-6099.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning left, the driver gives way to oncoming vehicles that are going straight ahead or turning right, because they cross their path. The manoeuvre is completed only after they have passed.

q-6100.text: In this situation, if you turn right, do you have the right of way over a vehicle approaching from the left?
q-6100.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority follows from the signs and the layout of the intersection in the material — the vehicle approaching from the left is obliged to give way to you. Make the right turn close to the right edge of the roadway, watching cyclists and pedestrians.

q-6101.text: If you go straight, should you give the right of way to a vehicle approaching from the left?
q-6101.explanation: Correct answer: NO. According to the signs visible in the material it is you who has priority, so the vehicle approaching from the left must wait. Vehicles from the right have priority only at an intersection of equal roads, where there are no signs determining priority.

q-6102.text: You intend to turn left at this intersection. Are you obliged to give the right of way to a vehicle approaching from the left?
q-6102.explanation: Correct answer: NO. From the signs at the intersection in the material it follows that you are on the road with priority, so the vehicle approaching from the left must give way to you. When turning left, you nevertheless give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

q-6103.text: Are you merging with traffic in this situation?
q-6103.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Joining the traffic includes, among others, moving off from a parked position, leaving a car park, a property or a residential zone, and also entering the roadway from the shoulder or the pavement. The driver must then give way to all other road users.

q-6104.text: If you go straight at this intersection, should you give the right of way to a vehicle approaching from the left?
q-6104.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs at this intersection, visible in the material, give priority to your direction of travel, so the driver approaching from the left must wait. Despite having priority, you should watch whether they really are slowing down and giving way.

q-6105.text: In this situation, should you allow the emergency vehicle to pass?
q-6105.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle emitting blue flashing lights together with a siren of variable tone is an emergency vehicle, which must be allowed to pass, if necessary by pulling over or stopping. You should brake calmly, without cutting in front of others.

q-6106.text: At this intersection, do you have the right of way over a vehicle approaching from the left?
q-6106.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs at this intersection order you to give way, so the vehicle approaching from the left goes first. You must approach at a speed that allows you to stop before the intersection and assess the traffic from both sides.

q-6108.text: In this situation, do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-6108.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material designate your road as the road with priority, and the right-hand rule then yields to the signs. The vehicle approaching from the right is obliged to let you pass, which does not release you from watching its behaviour.

q-6109.text: If you go straight at this intersection, do you have the right of way over a vehicle approaching from the left?
q-6109.explanation: Correct answer: YES. From the signs at the intersection in the material it follows that you are on the road with priority, so the driver approaching from the left must give way to you. Priority must, however, be confirmed by observation — do not enter if you see that they are not braking.

q-6110.text: If you turn right, do you have the right of way over a vehicle approaching from the opposite direction?
q-6110.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this situation the oncoming vehicle has priority, and you, as the one turning, must give way to it — this follows from the signs and the road layout visible in the material. The turn is made only after it has passed.

q-6111.text: In this situation, if you turn left, do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-6111.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs at the intersection visible in the material give priority to your road, so the vehicle approaching from the right must give way to you despite the right-hand rule. When turning left, however, remember the oncoming vehicles.

q-6112.text: In this situation, if you go straight, do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-6112.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Your road is the road with priority at this place, as follows from the signs visible in the material, so the driver on the right is obliged to give way. The right-hand rule applies only where there are no signs determining priority.

q-6113.text: In this situation, if you go straight, do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-6113.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Your road is the road with priority at this place, as follows from the signs visible in the material, so the driver on the right is obliged to give way. The right-hand rule applies only where there are no signs determining priority.

q-6114.text: If you go straight, do you have the right of way over a vehicle approaching from the left?
q-6114.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The vehicle approaching from the left is obliged to give way to your direction of travel, as follows from the signs visible in the material. Priority does not, however, mean a right to force your way in — you must make sure the other driver is slowing down.

q-6115.text: If you turn left, do you have the right of way over a vehicle approaching from the opposite direction?
q-6115.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver turning left crosses the path of oncoming vehicles, so it is they who give way to them. This rule applies regardless of whether you are on a road with priority or a subordinate one.

q-6117.text: If you go straight, do you have the right of way over a vehicle approaching from the opposite direction and turning left?
q-6117.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Going straight ahead has priority over turning left, because it is the turning driver who crosses the path of the oncoming vehicle. Even so, it is worth watching the other driver, because misjudging the distance is a frequent cause of collisions here.

q-6118.text: If you turn right, do you have the right of way over a vehicle approaching from the opposite direction?
q-6118.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The vehicle approaching from the opposite direction has priority here, so the driver turning right must wait until it has passed. This follows from the road layout and the signs visible in the material, not from the direction of the turn itself.

q-6119.text: In this situation, are you obliged to give the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction?
q-6119.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In this situation priority belongs to the oncoming vehicle, and you must give way to it — this follows from the signs or the road layout visible in the material. You should stop at a place that does not block the roadway for the other driver.

q-6120.text: In this situation, can you drive past the traffic lights, if stopping in front of the lights would require rapid braking?
q-6120.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The yellow signal prohibits passing the traffic light, but a driver who is so close that stopping would require harsh braking may continue. You must then clear the intersection promptly and not accelerate to make it.

q-6121.text: Turning right in this situation, must you give right of way to the pedestrian?
q-6121.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning into a cross road is obliged to give way to a pedestrian crossing the roadway they are entering. The turn must be made slowly, also looking in the mirrors and the blind spot on the side of the turn.

q-6123.text: In this situation, can you unconditionally turn right at the intersection?
q-6123.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The green arrow signal permits a right turn only after first stopping before the traffic light. Then you may turn, giving way to vehicles and pedestrians for whom the green signal is showing.

q-6128.text: In this situation, if you intend to turn left, can you go past the traffic lights?
q-6128.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal displayed on the traffic light currently prohibits passing it, so you must stop before the designated place. The intention to turn left gives no additional right to enter the intersection.

q-6129.text: In this situation, after the light turns green, can you make a U-turn at the intersection?
q-6129.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A green signal permits passing the traffic light, and turning around at an intersection is allowed if neither a sign nor road markings prohibit it. The manoeuvre is performed from the lane for those turning left, giving way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

q-6130.text: In this situation, do you have the right of way over the pedestrian?
q-6130.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this situation the pedestrian has priority, and the driver must give way to them and, if necessary, stop the vehicle. When approaching a pedestrian crossing, particular caution applies and a speed that allows you to stop before it.

q-6133.text: Can you go straight from this lane?
q-6133.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The permitted directions of travel from a given lane are set by the arrows on the roadway and the signs above the lanes; at this place they permit going straight ahead. The correct lane should be taken early enough before the intersection.

q-6134.text: In this situation, can you make a U-turn from this lane?
q-6134.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around is permitted only from the lane from which the direction arrows or signs allow it; from the lane you are in such a manoeuvre is not permitted. Turning around contrary to the signs surprises other drivers and risks a collision.

q-6135.text: In this situation, can you enter the intersection without stopping?
q-6135.explanation: Correct answer: YES. There is no duty to stop, because the signal and the signs visible in the material permit passage, and the road beyond the intersection is clear. You may enter only when you will not have to stop on the intersection itself.

q-6136.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop, even if this would mean rapid braking?
q-6136.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver who is so close that stopping would require harsh braking may continue and leave the intersection. This rule protects against a rear-end collision, but does not justify accelerating before the signal changes.

q-6138.text: Does the posture of the policeman at the intersection indicate that you may turn right?
q-6138.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A person directing traffic standing sideways to approaching vehicles corresponds to a green signal, so you may enter the intersection, including turning right. The instructions of the person directing traffic take precedence over traffic lights and signs.

q-6140.text: Intending to turn right in this situation, do you have the right of way over the pedestrian?
q-6140.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In this situation the pedestrian does not have priority — they have not stepped onto the crossing or a red signal applies to them, so you may turn right. Even so, you must drive slowly and be ready to give way should the pedestrian step onto the roadway after all.

q-6142.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop in front of the intersection?
q-6142.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An absolute duty to stop follows from a STOP sign, a red signal or an instruction from a person directing traffic, and none of these is present in this situation. It is enough to approach carefully and, if necessary, give way without stopping.

q-6143.text: In this situation, if you intend to turn right, can you enter the intersection?
q-6143.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal or sign visible in the material currently prohibits entering the intersection, and the intention to turn right does not change that. You must stop before the stop line or before the traffic light.

q-6148.text: In this situation, can you start driving?
q-6148.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal or instruction shown in the material still prohibits moving off, so you must stay put until permission to proceed is given. Setting off before the right moment blocks others and creates a real hazard.

q-6149.text: In this situation, if you want to continue driving, are you obliged to first wait for the tram to start moving?
q-6149.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver does not have to wait until the tram moves off; you may continue after allowing passengers to reach the island or the pavement safely. If no one is left on the roadway, you may carefully pass the stationary tram.

q-6151.text: In this situation, can you bypass the tram?
q-6151.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The tram is standing at a stop without an island, and passengers are getting on or off, so the driver is obliged to stop behind it and wait. Passing may be done only when no one is left on the roadway.

q-6154.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop the car at the indicated place?
q-6154.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop follows from the sign, signal or instruction visible in the material, and the stop must take place exactly at the indicated place. You must not drive further, because that obscures visibility and misleads other drivers.

q-6155.text: Does the signal of the policeman mean that you are obliged to turn right at the nearest intersection?
q-6155.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal given by the person directing traffic regulates passage — it permits or prohibits travel — and does not impose a direction at the nearest intersection. An order to turn right would follow from a mandatory sign or from an explicit instruction indicating the direction.

q-6159.text: In this situation, if you turn left, are you obliged to stop before the intersection?
q-6159.explanation: Correct answer: YES. For the left direction, a signal or sign ordering a stop currently applies, so you must halt before the intersection. You may move off only after permission to go and after giving way to those who have priority.

q-6160.text: In this situation, can you stop a car on the sidewalk just in front of a public transport stop?
q-6160.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping a vehicle within a public transport stop is prohibited, even when standing on the pavement just before it. This place must remain free for public transport vehicles and for passengers waiting at the stop.

q-6161.text: In this situation, can you continue driving in the left lane?
q-6161.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material exclude the left lane from further travel in your direction, so you must move to the right lane. The lane change is made early, with the indicator and after checking the mirrors and the blind spot.

q-6162.text: In this situation, are you obliged to continue driving in the right lane?
q-6162.explanation: Correct answer: YES. From the signs visible in the material it follows that only the right lane allows further travel in your direction, so you should take it. The manoeuvre must be performed early enough, signalling the intention and without cutting in front of those travelling in that lane.

q-6165.text: Is it permitted to stop the car in a tunnel?
q-6165.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping a vehicle in a tunnel is prohibited, because visibility there is limited and a stationary vehicle is very hard to notice from an adequate distance. The exception remains a stop forced by traffic conditions or the rules, for example a jam.

q-6166.text: If you stop a car on a sidewalk, do you have to allow a 1.5 m wide passage for pedestrians?
q-6166.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When stopping a vehicle on the pavement, you must leave pedestrians a passage at least 1.5 m wide, along the whole length of the vehicle. The width is measured from the vehicle to the edge of the pavement, and the passage must not be blocked by other obstacles.

q-6168.text: If you intend to go straight, can you enter this intersection from any lane?
q-6168.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The directions of travel from individual lanes are set by direction arrows and signs above the roadway, so you may go straight ahead only from the lanes that permit it. The correct lane should be taken early enough before the intersection.

q-6170.text: Can you park the car at a distance of 5 m from a pedestrian crossing?
q-6170.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Parking before a pedestrian crossing is permitted only at a distance of at least 10 m, so 5 m is too little. A vehicle standing closer hides the pedestrian and deprives drivers of the chance to notice them in time.

q-6171.text: On this road, once you go past this sign, can you park the car at any place on the road, provided that this does not constitute an obstacle to traffic?
q-6171.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In a residential zone parking is permitted only in places designated for it, even if the vehicle would obstruct no one. The whole zone serves above all pedestrians, who may use the full width of the road.

q-6172.text: If you stop a car on a sidewalk, do you have to ensure that pedestrians have a passage of at least 2.5 m wide?
q-6172.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The required width of the passage left for pedestrians on the pavement is at least 1.5 m, not 2.5 m. This strip must be free along the whole length of the vehicle and must not be blocked by anything.

q-6173.text: Can you stop a car on a sidewalk, leaving a passage of 2 m, if this causes an obstacle to pedestrian traffic?
q-6173.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Leaving a 2 m passage is not enough if the parking still obstructs pedestrians — the condition for stopping on the pavement is the absence of such obstruction. You must then find another place, also out of consideration for prams and persons with disabilities.

q-6174.text: In this situation, should you change lanes to the right?
q-6174.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material indicate that further travel in your direction is possible from the right lane, so you should move over to it. The manoeuvre is made in advance, with the indicator, after checking the mirrors and the blind spot.

q-6175.text: Can you turn left at the intersection from this lane?
q-6175.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The direction arrows on the roadway and the signs above the lanes do not permit a left turn from this lane, so from it you may travel only in the permitted direction. The lane corresponding to your intended direction must be taken earlier.

q-6176.text: After the light turns green, can you turn left from this lane?
q-6176.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The markings permit a left turn from this lane, and the green signal permits entry to the intersection. When turning, you must give way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians crossing the roadway you are entering.

q-6177.text: In this situation, can you change lanes immediately before the intersection?
q-6177.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Directly before the intersection the lanes are separated by a solid line, which must not be crossed, so a lane change is prohibited there. The correct lane should be taken earlier, before the broken line turns into a solid one.

q-6178.text: At this place, can you change from the currently occupied traffic lane to the left lane?
q-6178.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this place the lanes are separated by a broken line and no sign prohibits a lane change, so the manoeuvre is permitted. It must be signalled with the indicator, and way given to vehicles travelling in the lane you are entering.

q-6179.text: At this intersection, can you go straight from the left lane?
q-6179.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs at this intersection permit going straight ahead from the left lane, so a lane change is not necessary. After passing the intersection the rule of driving as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway applies.

q-6180.text: In this situation, if you intend to turn left, should you change the lane?
q-6180.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A left turn is not permitted from the lane you are in, so you must move to the lane intended for that direction. The lane change is made early enough, before the separating line becomes solid.

q-6181.text: Can you make a U-turn on the bridge?
q-6181.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around on a bridge is prohibited, just as in a tunnel, on a viaduct and under one. The roadway is narrow there, there is no room for the manoeuvre, and a vehicle turning around completely blocks the passage.

q-6182.text: At this intersection, can you turn right from the left lane?
q-6182.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The direction arrows marked on the lane you are in do not include a right turn, so such a manoeuvre from it is prohibited. The lane consistent with the intended direction must be taken well before the intersection.

q-6183.text: In this situation, if you intend to go straight, should you change the lane you are occupying?
q-6183.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs permit going straight ahead from the lane you are in, so a lane change is not needed. Unnecessary moving between lanes before an intersection only obstructs traffic and increases the risk of a collision.

q-6184.text: Can you go straight from this lane?
q-6184.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The direction arrows on the lane you are in include going straight ahead, so you may continue without changing lanes. Before the intersection you only need to make sure there is room beyond it to enter.

q-6185.text: In this situation, can you make a U-turn immediately after this sign?
q-6185.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign visible in the material prohibits turning around, and the prohibition applies from the place where it is installed, so directly beyond it the manoeuvre is not permitted. You may turn around only where the prohibition ceases to apply.

q-6186.text: In this situation, can you stop the car immediately after this sign?
q-6186.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign visible in the material prohibits stopping, and the prohibition takes effect from the place where it is installed. You may stop the vehicle only beyond the section covered by the prohibition, unless traffic conditions force you to.

q-6189.text: In this situation, can you start overtaking on the right?
q-6189.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking on the right is permitted when the vehicle being overtaken is signalling an intention to turn left, and also on a roadway with marked lanes where traffic moves in columns. You must always make sure, however, that there is enough room on the right.

q-6190.text: On this road, once you go past this sign, can you overtake the vehicle you see on the left?
q-6190.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking is, as a rule, done on the left, and at this place neither a sign nor the road markings prohibit it. Before the manoeuvre you must make sure the section is clearly visible and free of oncoming vehicles.

q-6193.text: In this situation, can you overtake the car travelling in front of you?
q-6193.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs and conditions visible in the material do not stand in the way of overtaking, and the section ahead of the vehicle is clear and clearly visible. Before the manoeuvre you must signal your intention, check that no one is overtaking from behind, and keep a safe distance.

q-6194.text: In this situation, have you just completed a passing manoeuvre?
q-6194.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Passing is driving past a stationary vehicle, road user or obstacle, and in this situation you performed a different manoeuvre. If the vehicle you went past was moving, it was overtaking or passing an oncoming vehicle.

q-6196.text: In this situation, while exercising special caution, can you bypass the tram?
q-6196.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A tram standing at a stop without an island must not be passed while passengers are getting on or off; particular caution alone does not lift this prohibition. The driver is obliged to stop behind the tram and wait.

q-6198.text: In this situation, should you slow down?
q-6198.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Speed must be adapted to the conditions on the road so as to remain in control of the vehicle and stop it before an obstacle whose appearance can be foreseen. A lower speed gives time to react and shortens the braking distance.

q-6199.text: Is it forbidden to perform a reverse manoeuvre on a one-way road?
q-6199.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Reversing on a one-way road is not prohibited in itself; the driver need only exercise particular caution and give way to other road users. The prohibition concerns places such as a tunnel, a bridge, a motorway or an expressway.

q-6200.text: Can you perform a reverse manoeuvre on a one-way road?
q-6200.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Reversing on a one-way road is permitted, provided the driver exercises particular caution and gives way to other road users. The manoeuvre should be short, and with limited visibility the help of another person must be used.

q-6201.text: Is it permitted to perform a reverse manoeuvre on a bridge, if you exercise special caution?
q-6201.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Reversing on a bridge is prohibited, and particular caution does not lift this prohibition; the same prohibition applies in a tunnel, on a viaduct and under one. The narrow roadway and lack of a shoulder mean that a reversing vehicle blocks traffic.

q-6202.text: Is it forbidden to perform a reverse manoeuvre on a single lane expressway?
q-6202.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Reversing is prohibited on a motorway and on an expressway, even when it has only one roadway. The high speeds of the other vehicles mean that a reversing vehicle is noticed far too late.

q-6203.text: Can you perform a reverse manoeuvre on a motorway if you turn on the vehicle's hazard lights?
q-6203.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a motorway and on an expressway reversing is prohibited without exception, and switching on the hazard lights changes nothing. Having missed the exit, you must continue to the next junction and turn back there.

q-6204.text: Can you reverse the car on the road once you go past this sign?
q-6204.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material does not introduce a ban on reversing, so the manoeuvre is permitted. It must, however, be performed with particular caution, making sure there is no one behind the vehicle and giving way to other road users.

q-6205.text: In this situation, have you performed an overtaking manoeuvre?
q-6205.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is driving past a vehicle moving in the same direction. If the vehicle you went past was standing or coming from the opposite direction, it was passing an obstacle or an oncoming vehicle, not overtaking — despite the similar path.

q-6206.text: Is it forbidden to perform a reverse manoeuvre on a bridge?
q-6206.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Reversing is prohibited in tunnels, on bridges and viaducts, because there is no room there to get around the vehicle and no possibility of escaping onto the shoulder. The change of direction must be made only after leaving the structure.

q-6207.text: Is it permitted to perform a reverse manoeuvre on an express road?
q-6207.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On an expressway, just as on a motorway, reversing is prohibited because of the high speeds and the impossibility for other drivers to anticipate such a manoeuvre. The only solution is to drive on to the nearest exit.

q-6208.text: Is it forbidden to perform a reverse manoeuvre on an express road?
q-6208.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban on reversing applies along the whole length of an expressway and a motorway, including on the hard shoulder and at the entry. A driver who has missed an exit must continue to the next junction.

q-6209.text: In this situation, can you bypass the car visible on the right?
q-6209.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Driving past a stationary vehicle or an obstacle is passing, which may also be done on the right if the width of the roadway allows. The manoeuvre requires caution and not endangering pedestrians and cyclists.

q-6210.text: In this situation, can you bypass the car in front of you?
q-6210.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Passing is prohibited when the vehicle in front has stopped to give way to a pedestrian, and also when there is no room on the roadway to perform the manoeuvre safely. In such a situation you should wait behind that vehicle.

q-6211.text: Can you use daytime lights while driving after dusk on a well-lit road?
q-6211.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Daytime running lights may be used only during the day and when the air is normally clear. From dusk to dawn dipped headlights are compulsory, however well lit the road is — especially since the vehicle would otherwise remain unlit at the rear.

q-6213.text: In this situation, can you use high-beam lights?
q-6213.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used where they would dazzle others: with an oncoming vehicle, when following another vehicle, and in fog or precipitation, when the light reflects off water droplets. You then drive on dipped headlights.

q-6214.text: In this situation, can you turn off the external lights of the car?
q-6214.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A moving vehicle must have its lights on around the clock — dipped headlights or, during the day in clear air, daytime running lights. Switching off the exterior lighting makes the vehicle invisible to others and is not permitted.

q-6216.text: If you are driving with your low-beam lights turned on in heavy rain limiting visibility, can you also use the front anti-fog lights?
q-6216.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Front fog lights may be switched on in fog, heavy rain or snow, that is, when the clarity of the air is reduced. They are used together with dipped headlights and switched off as soon as visibility improves.

q-6217.text: Can you sound the horn to warn others against imminent danger?
