q-6217.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The horn may be used when it is necessary to warn of an immediate danger. In a built-up area this is the only permitted reason for using it; beyond that, the horn is not for hurrying other drivers along.

q-6218.text: If you park your car at night on an unlit road, are you obliged to use position or parking lights?
q-6218.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle standing at night on an unlit roadway must be marked with position or parking lights so that it is visible to those approaching. The duty does not apply to parking in a place lit well enough to make the vehicle visible or in a designated car park.

q-6222.text: In this situation, can you use high-beam lights?
q-6222.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used where they would dazzle others: with an oncoming vehicle, when following another vehicle, and in fog or precipitation, when the light reflects off water droplets. You then drive on dipped headlights.

q-6223.text: In this situation, should you change high-beam lights to low-beam lights?
q-6223.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Main beam must be switched to dipped whenever it could dazzle another road user — the driver of an oncoming vehicle or one travelling ahead of you. The switch is made early enough, not only at the moment of passing.

q-6224.text: In this situation, can you use daylights?
q-6224.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Daytime running lights replace dipped headlights only during the day and when the air is normally clear. At night, at dusk and in fog, rain or snow, dipped headlights must be switched on, because daytime lights do not light the road and do nothing at the rear of the vehicle.

q-6225.text: In this situation, are you obliged to change high-beam lights to low-beam lights?
q-6225.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Main beam must be switched to dipped whenever it could dazzle another road user — the driver of an oncoming vehicle or one travelling ahead of you. The switch is made early enough, not only at the moment of passing.

q-6226.text: Does the obligation to use low-beam lights in the car apply only to the winter period?
q-6226.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to drive with lights on applies all year round and around the clock. During the day, in clear air, daytime running lights may be used instead of dipped headlights, but driving without lights is never allowed.

q-6228.text: Are you always obliged to exercise special caution, while driving?
q-6228.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Ordinary caution applies at all times. Particular caution — heightened attention and readiness to react quickly — is required only in the situations specified by the regulations: at an intersection, at a pedestrian crossing, when overtaking, reversing or changing lanes.

q-6229.text: While driving in thick fog, are you always obliged to exercise special caution?
q-6229.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Fog reduces the transparency of the air, so the regulations then require particular caution. This means reducing speed, increasing the distance to the vehicle ahead and being constantly ready to stop before an obstacle that appears suddenly.

q-6230.text: Are you always obliged to exercise caution, while driving?
q-6230.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Ordinary caution applies throughout the whole journey: the driver watches the road, adapts their behaviour to the conditions and avoids actions that could create a danger. In selected situations this requirement is raised to particular caution.

q-6233.text: Are you obliged to always exercise special caution while driving from dusk to dawn?
q-6233.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Night-time alone does not create a duty of constant special care — ordinary care, adapted to conditions, applies at all times. Special care is required in the situations specified in the rules, regardless of the time of day.

q-6234.text: While overtaking this car, are you obliged to exercise special caution?
q-6234.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking belongs to the manoeuvres for which the rules always require particular caution. Before starting it, you must make sure no one is overtaking you, that there is enough room and visibility, signal the intention and keep a safe lateral distance.

q-6235.text: In this situation, before you overtake the cyclist, are you obliged to sound the horn?
q-6235.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A horn signal is not a condition of overtaking, and in a built-up area it may be used only to prevent an immediate danger. The horn may startle the cyclist; what matters more is overtaking them with a distance of not less than 1 m.

q-6237.text: In this situation, when entering the property, are you obliged to give the right of way to the pedestrian?
q-6237.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver who turns off the road into a property crosses the path of pedestrians and must give way to them, even when there is no marked crossing there. The manoeuvre is performed slowly, with particular caution.

q-6238.text: Are you obliged to give the right of way to pedestrians on a yard with no designated pavements and road?
q-6238.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Where no roadway or pavement has been marked out, a pedestrian may use the full width of the road and has priority over vehicles. The driver must give way to them, drive slowly and be ready to stop immediately.

q-6240.text: On this road, once you go past this sign, are you obliged to give the right of way to pedestrians in all circumstances?
q-6240.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material designates an area in which a pedestrian may use the full width of the road and has priority over vehicles. The driver moves there very slowly, gives way to pedestrians regardless of where they cross, and must be ready to stop.

q-6242.text: Driving past a school bus, are you always obliged to exercise special caution?
q-6242.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing a vehicle carrying children always requires particular caution, because a child getting off or on may run onto the road at any moment. You must reduce speed and be ready to stop immediately.

q-6243.text: On a road marked this way, are you obliged to give the right of way to the pedestrian in all circumstances?
q-6243.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material do not give the pedestrian unconditional priority along the whole road. The driver gives way to the pedestrian in the situations indicated by the rules, above all on the crossing and before stepping onto it, and the pedestrian may not step directly in front of an approaching vehicle.

q-6244.text: In this situation, should you exercise special caution?
q-6244.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material is one in which the regulations require particular caution — attention must increase and the driver must be ready to react immediately. In practice this means easing off the accelerator and watching the surroundings closely.

q-6246.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise special caution?
q-6246.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-6247.text: On this road, once you go past this sign, are you obliged to give the right of way to the pedestrian walking in the middle of the road?
q-6247.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material introduces an area in which a pedestrian may walk across the full width of the road, including its middle, and has priority over vehicles. The driver adapts their speed to the pedestrian traffic and, if necessary, stops the vehicle.

q-6248.text: In this situation, are you obliged to apply the rule of limited trust?
q-6248.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The principle of limited trust applies whenever the behaviour of another road user indicates that they may act improperly. You must then reduce speed, watch that road user closely and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-6250.text: In this situation, should you carefully observe the behaviour of the pedestrian?
q-6250.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A pedestrian near the roadway may change their mind at any moment and step onto the road, so the driver constantly watches their posture, the direction of their gaze and their pace. Such observation is part of the principle of limited trust.

q-6251.text: In this situation, if you exercise special caution, can you enter the pedestrian crossing?
q-6251.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Particular caution alone does not entitle you to enter the crossing. This is prohibited when a pedestrian is on the crossing or stepping onto it, and also when there is no room beyond the crossing to continue and the vehicle would stop on it.

q-6254.text: If you drive through a puddle, should you slow down to avoid splashing pedestrians?
q-6254.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver is obliged to drive so as not to expose others to harm or inconvenience; splashing a pedestrian with water from a puddle is precisely such behaviour. Before a puddle you must slow down and, if possible, go around it with a safe distance from the pavement.

q-6255.text: In this situation, are you obliged to apply the rule of limited trust?
q-6255.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The principle of limited trust applies whenever the behaviour of another road user indicates that they may act improperly. You must then reduce speed, watch that road user closely and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-6257.text: In this situation, can you use the horn?
q-6257.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In a built-up area the horn may be used solely to prevent an immediate danger. In the situation shown there is no such threat, so the horn would be unnecessary and could frighten other road users.

q-6258.text: In this situation, should you apply the rule of limited trust?
q-6258.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The principle of limited trust requires you to allow for a mistake by another road user, especially when their behaviour suggests they may not comply with the rules. The driver then reduces speed and prepares for an unexpected manoeuvre.

q-6259.text: In this situation, should you expect a pedestrian suddenly barging onto the road?
q-6259.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver must anticipate the behaviour of others, and the presence of pedestrians beside the roadway means a real risk of a sudden step onto the road. Speed must therefore be chosen so that the vehicle can be stopped before a pedestrian who appears unexpectedly.

q-6260.text: In this situation, are you obliged to allow the pedestrian to cross the road?
q-6260.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The pedestrian in the situation shown enjoys priority, so the driver slows down and, if necessary, stops the vehicle to allow them to cross. You may move off only when the pedestrian is safely out of your path.

q-6261.text: In this situation, can you drive through the pedestrian crossing without reducing speed?
q-6261.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When approaching a pedestrian crossing, the driver must exercise particular caution and reduce speed so as not to endanger the pedestrian and to be able to stop. Driving without slowing down makes it impossible to react to a pedestrian stepping onto the crossing.

q-6263.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise special caution?
q-6263.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-6264.text: In this situation, if you turn left, are you obliged to give the right of way to the cyclist going straight?
q-6264.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When turning left, you cross the path of a cyclist continuing straight ahead, so you must give way to them. A bicycle is a fully-fledged road user, and its speed is easy to underestimate — which is why the manoeuvre requires particular caution.

q-6265.text: In this situation, if you turn left, do you have the right of way over the cyclist going straight?
q-6265.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The vehicle going straight ahead has priority, and the one turning left must give way to it — this also applies to a bicycle. Before starting the turn, you must make sure the cyclist has already passed or that there is enough room and time.

q-6266.text: In this situation, while overtaking, can you drive into the space between the bicycles riding in a column formation?
q-6266.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A column of bicycles riding one behind another is treated as a whole, and moving in between the individual bicycles is prohibited. You may overtake only the whole group at once, when there is enough room and visibility, with a distance of not less than 1 m.

q-6267.text: In this situation, is it forbidden to overtake the cyclist?
q-6267.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the conditions shown no prohibition rules out overtaking the cyclist, so the manoeuvre is permitted. It must be performed with particular caution, in good visibility and with a lateral distance of not less than 1 m.

q-6269.text: Can the person riding the bicycle overtake the slowly-moving vehicles on their right?
q-6269.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A cyclist may overtake slowly moving vehicles on the right — this is an exception to the rule of overtaking on the left. The manoeuvre requires caution, because the driver being overtaken may suddenly turn right or open a door.

q-6270.text: In this situation, can you overtake the cyclist if you keep to the distance of 0.5 m?
q-6270.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When overtaking a cyclist, a safe distance of not less than 1 m applies, so 0.5 m is too little. If such a distance cannot be kept, you must wait with the manoeuvre until there is enough room for it.

q-6271.text: In this situation, is it forbidden to overtake the cyclist if you keep to a distance of approx. 0.5 m?
q-6271.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The required lateral distance when overtaking a cyclist is at least 1 m, so about 0.5 m means a prohibited manoeuvre. Passing too close forces the cyclist into a sudden reaction and risks them falling.

q-6272.text: In this situation, do you have to apply the rule of limited trust?
q-6272.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver may assume that others obey the rules, but only as long as their behaviour or the circumstances do not indicate otherwise. In the situation shown such signals are present, so you must slow down and prepare for another road user's mistake.

q-6273.text: In this situation, seeing the behaviour of the cyclists, are you obliged to stop?
q-6273.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The cyclists' behaviour does not create a situation in which the rules would require stopping the vehicle. It is enough to exercise particular caution, reduce speed and keep a safe distance, remaining ready to brake should anything change.

q-6275.text: In this situation, going past a cyclist, do you have to exercise special caution?
q-6275.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A cyclist is a vulnerable road user, easily loses balance and may swerve sideways to avoid a hole or an obstacle. When passing them, you must slow down, exercise particular caution and keep a clear lateral distance.

q-6278.text: In this situation, can you enter the crossing if you exercise special caution?
q-6278.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Particular caution does not lift the prohibition on entering the crossing. Entry is prohibited when the barriers or half-barriers are closed or beginning to close, when a red signal is shown, and also when there is no room on the other side to drive off the crossing.

q-6279.text: In this situation, can you drive through the railway crossing without stopping?
q-6279.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An absolute stop before a crossing is required only when a sign or signal orders it. If nothing of the kind is present, the crossing is clear and there is room beyond it to drive off, you may cross, exercising particular caution.

q-6280.text: In this situation, can you enter the railway crossing?
q-6280.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Entering a railway crossing is prohibited when the safety equipment or signals prohibit it or when the vehicle would not be able to leave it without stopping. You should stop before the crossing and wait until it is clear.

q-6281.text: Is it forbidden to park the car immediately after the countdown post you see here?
q-6281.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Marker posts announce a railway crossing, and in its vicinity a prohibition on stopping and parking applies. A vehicle standing at this place would obscure the view of the tracks and hinder evacuation from the crossing.

q-6282.text: In this situation, can you park the car on the right side, on the sidewalk immediately in front of the railway crossing?
q-6282.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the immediate vicinity of a railway crossing stopping and parking are prohibited, also on the pavement. A standing vehicle would restrict the view of the tracks for drivers approaching the crossing and force pedestrians onto the roadway.

q-6283.text: In this situation, can you bypass the barrier and enter the railway crossing after making sure that the train is not coming?
q-6283.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Going around a lowered barrier or half-barrier is absolutely prohibited, regardless of whether a train is visible. The barrier is also closed when a train is approaching from the other side or when another train will occupy the tracks.

q-6286.text: In this situation, can you enter the railway crossing?
q-6286.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal, the barriers or the situation at the crossing prohibit entry, so the vehicle must be stopped before the crossing and you must wait. Entering a closing crossing or at a red signal is exceptionally dangerous.

q-6287.text: Can you, as a driver, move away from a car which engine is running?
q-6287.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver may leave the vehicle only after securing it against moving off and switching off the engine. An engine left running risks the vehicle setting off on its own and also makes it easier to steal.

q-6290.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop in front of the railway crossing?
q-6290.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop follows from the sign or signal visible in the material, which the driver must obey regardless of whether they see an approaching train. The stop is made before the line or before the crossing itself, and you may move off only after making sure the tracks are clear.

q-6292.text: If you're involved in a car accident in which there are injured persons, can you leave the scene of the accident once the ambulance service has been called?
q-6292.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A participant in an accident with injured people must stay at the scene until the Police arrive; calling the services alone does not release them from this duty. They may leave only to fetch help themselves or take an injured person to hospital, and must then return immediately.

q-6293.text: If you're involved in a car accident in which there are fatalities, are you obliged to remain on the scene of the accident after the ambulance service had been called?
q-6293.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In an accident with fatalities, a participant remains at the scene until the Police arrive, secures the scene and does not change the position of the vehicles or the traces. Their presence is needed to establish what happened.

q-6294.text: If you're involved in a car accident in which there are injured parties, can you remove your car from the scene of the accident so that it does not create an obstacle to traffic?
q-6294.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When people have been injured in an accident, the vehicles may not be moved — their position and the traces on the road serve to establish what happened. The scene must be marked and secured, and the Police, once there, will direct traffic.

q-6295.text: If you're involved in a car accident in which there are injured persons, are you obliged to leave your car at the scene of the accident?
q-6295.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In an accident with injured people the vehicle stays where it stopped, because its position is evidence in the case. The driver marks the scene and waits for the Police; moving the vehicle is permitted only when saving a life requires it.

q-6296.text: If you're involved in a car accident in which there are no injuries or fatalities, are you obliged to call the Police?
q-6296.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In an incident with nobody killed or injured, calling the Police is not compulsory — it is enough to write a statement and exchange details. The Police are worth calling when the participants disagree about what happened or a crime is suspected.

q-6297.text: If you're involved in a car accident in which there are no injuries or fatalities, are you obliged to immediately remove your car from the scene of the accident?
q-6297.explanation: Correct answer: YES. If nobody has been hurt, the participants must immediately remove the vehicles from the scene so as not to cause danger or obstruct traffic. Details and circumstances are written down afterwards, in a safe place off the carriageway.

q-6298.text: If you're involved in a car accident in which there are injured parties, are you obliged to call the emergency service and provide the necessary assistance to the victims?
q-6298.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident must call an ambulance and the Police and help the casualties to the extent their skills and the conditions allow. First, however, they secure the scene, so as not to endanger themselves while rescuing others.

q-6299.text: If you're involved in a car accident, are you obliged to provide your personal details at the request of the second party involved in the same accident?
q-6299.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At the request of another participant in the incident, you must give your personal details, as well as the details of the vehicle's owner and its insurance. Without this information the injured party could not claim compensation.

q-6300.text: If you have stopped your vehicle on an expressway due to a breakdown, must you switch on your emergency lights, and if the vehicle is not so equipped, your position lights?
q-6300.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An immobilised vehicle must be marked with the hazard lights or, if it is not equipped with them, with the position lights. On an expressway a reflective warning triangle is additionally set up, because approaching vehicles travel at very high speed there.

q-6301.text: Is it correct to place a warning triangle at a distance of 30-50 m behind the car, if the car breaks down on an express road?
q-6301.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a motorway and an expressway the triangle is placed 100 m behind the vehicle, because only such a distance gives those approaching time to react. The distance of 30–50 m applies to roads outside built-up areas, but not to those with the highest speeds.

q-6302.text: If you're involved in an accident on a motorway, do you have to signal the fact that your car is immobilized by turning on the emergency lights?
q-6302.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle immobilised on a motorway must be marked with the hazard lights switched on and additionally with a warning triangle placed 100 m behind it. Thanks to this, those approaching at high speed have time to change lanes and slow down.

q-6303.text: In the situation that you see here, while you park a broken-down car on the road outside a built-up area, are you obliged to place a warning triangle behind it at a distance of 150 m?
q-6303.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Outside a built-up area the warning triangle is placed at a distance of 30–50 m behind the vehicle, not 150 m. The distance of 100 m applies only on a motorway and an expressway.

q-6304.text: If you park a broken-down car outside a built-up area, are you obliged to place a warning triangle immediately behind the car or on it?
q-6304.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Placing the triangle directly behind the vehicle or on it concerns stopping in a built-up area. Outside a built-up area the triangle is placed 30–50 m behind the vehicle so that the warning reaches drivers early enough.

q-6305.text: While parking a broken-down car on a paved road outside a built-up area, do you have to leave the low-beam lights on?
q-6305.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An immobilised vehicle is signalled with the hazard lights, and when there are none — with the position lights, and with a warning triangle placed behind the vehicle. Leaving the dipped headlights on is not required and would only drain the battery, and at night could dazzle.

q-6306.text: In the presented situation, are you obliged to signal the fact that you have parked a broken-down car on a road which is not an express road, if the car may be seen from a sufficient distance?
q-6306.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a road other than a motorway or an expressway, the stopping of a broken-down vehicle need not be additionally signalled if the vehicle is visible from an adequate distance. When visibility is limited, the duty to mark it returns.

q-6307.text: Should you signal the fact of parking a broken-down car on an area excluded from driving?
q-6307.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An area closed to traffic is a place where stopping is prohibited, so a vehicle standing there is a surprise to others and must be marked. The hazard lights and a reflective warning triangle are used.

q-6308.text: In cases of breakdown, must you immediately remove the vehicle from the crossing and if this is not possible, should you warn the engine driver of the rail vehicle?
q-6308.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle immobilised on a crossing must be removed from it immediately, and when that is not possible — the train driver must be warned and help called, using the emergency number given at the crossing. The passengers should meanwhile leave the vehicle and move to a safe place.

q-6309.text: In the event of immobilization of the car due to a technical problem on a railway crossing, do you have to immediately move the car from the railway crossing?
q-6309.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle standing on the tracks blocks the way for a tram, which cannot steer aside or brake quickly, so it must be removed immediately. If it cannot be done by your own efforts, you should warn the tram driver and call for help.

q-6310.text: If you're involved in a car accident, are you obliged to provide the details of the car owner at the request of another person involved in such accident?
q-6310.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At the request of another participant in the incident, you give not only your own details but also those of the vehicle's owner or keeper. They are needed because claims are directed to the owner and their insurer, not only to the driver.

q-6311.text: If you're involved in a car accident, are you obliged to provide the details concerning motor third-party liability insurance at the request of another person involved in the accident?
q-6311.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an incident must give the details of the third-party liability insurance policy: the name of the insurer, the policy number and its period of validity. Without this the injured party could not report the damage to the right insurer.

q-6312.text: If you're involved in an accident on a motorway, are you obliged to signal the fact that your car is immobilized by placement of a warning triangle 100 m behind the car?
q-6312.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle immobilised on a motorway or expressway is marked with a reflective warning triangle placed 100 m behind the vehicle and with the hazard lights switched on. Such a large distance follows from the high speeds: drivers approaching from behind must receive the warning early enough.

q-6314.text: Can you use emergency lights while towing a vehicle?
q-6314.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Hazard lights serve to warn of an immobilised vehicle or one creating a danger, not for driving in a towed combination. The towing and towed vehicles are marked with the prescribed lights, and constant flashing would make it impossible to signal manoeuvres clearly with the indicators.

q-6315.text: Once you reach an accident spot, can you secure such a spot by appropriately positioning your car and turning on your emergency lights?
q-6315.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver who reaches the scene of an accident has the right and the duty to secure it. They may position their own vehicle to shield the scene, switch on the hazard lights and set up a warning triangle. This protects the injured and the rescuers from being run into.

q-6316.text: Can the consumption of amphetamines increase the driver's tendency of risky and aggressive behaviour?
q-6316.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Amphetamine stimulates, gives a false sense of strength and ability, lowers self-criticism and increases readiness for risk and aggression behind the wheel. The period of stimulation is followed by a sharp drop in ability and drowsiness, equally dangerous for a driver.

q-6317.text: Can the use of tranquilisers and sleeping pills affect the driver's control of the trajectory of the car?
q-6317.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Sedatives and sleeping pills slow reactions, weaken alertness and impair precision of movement, so the vehicle begins to drift within its lane. Before driving, check the leaflet and ask a doctor or pharmacist about the medicine's effect on driving.

q-6318.text: Can consuming alcohol affect a driver's field of vision?
q-6318.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Alcohol narrows the field of vision, causing so-called tunnel vision, weakens peripheral perception and slows the eye's accommodation and adaptation to changes in light. The driver notices pedestrians and vehicles approaching from the side later.

q-6320.text: Do psychoactive substances (such as "speed") affect the ability of safe driving in even the most experienced drivers?
q-6320.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Psychoactive substances, including so-called legal highs, disturb perception, the judgement of distance and reaction time, and their composition and strength are unpredictable. Experience is no protection, because no amount of practice compensates for a disturbed brain.

q-6321.text: Can you drive a vehicle after taking medication prescribed by a doctor in every situation?
q-6321.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Not every medicine prescribed by a doctor is harmless for driving, because many of them cause drowsiness, dizziness, visual disturbances or a longer reaction time. Read the leaflet and ask a doctor or pharmacist; if the medicine impairs your fitness, you may not drive.

q-6322.text: If you intend to drive a vehicle after taking medications, should you make sure that they do not adversely affect your psychophysical condition?
q-6322.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver is responsible for their own psychophysical state, so before driving after taking a medicine they must check that it does not weaken alertness, vision and reaction time. Look for the information in the leaflet, from a doctor or pharmacist, and in case of doubt do not drive.

q-6323.text: If you start feeling tired and drowsy during a long trip, should you continue driving?
q-6323.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Tiredness and drowsiness lengthen reaction time and threaten microsleep, which the driver does not even notice. They cannot be overcome by willpower, coffee or an open window, so you must stop in a safe place and rest or sleep.

q-6324.text: What's the maximum speed at which you can drive a passenger car on a road marked with this sign?
q-6324.explanation: Correct answer: A. Beyond the sign shown in the material a car may travel at no more than 90 km/h, because that is the general limit outside a built-up area on a road with a single two-way carriageway. Higher values apply to dual carriageways, expressways and motorways.

q-6333.text: At what maximum speed limit can you drive, on the road past this sign?
q-6333.explanation: Correct answer: C. Beyond this sign a speed limit of 20 km/h applies, because that is how a residential zone is marked. A pedestrian may use the whole width of the road there and has priority over vehicles, and parking is allowed only in designated places.

q-6336.text: How should the headrest be positioned?

options.A: In such a way that its upper part is at the level of the top of the head.
options.B: In such a way that its upper part is above the level of the top of the head.
options.C: In such a way that its upper part is at the level of the neck.

q-6336.explanation: Correct answer: A. The head restraint protects the cervical spine in a rear-end collision. It is set so that its upper edge is level with the top of the head and the gap from the back of the head is as small as possible. A restraint set too low increases the risk of injury.

q-6337.text: What is the function of the anti-lock braking system (ABS)?

options.A: It shortens braking distance in all conditions.
options.B: It prevents the loss of tyre grip while accelerating.
options.C: It facilitates bypassing obstacles while braking.

q-6337.explanation: Correct answer: C. ABS does not let the wheels lock under braking, so the vehicle stays steerable and the driver can steer round an obstacle without easing off the brake. It does not shorten the braking distance in all conditions: on gravel or fresh snow it can even be longer.

q-6338.text: How can the shortest braking distance of a car equipped with the anti-lock braking system (ABS) be achieved?

options.A: By braking in a pulsating manner.
options.B: By gently pressing the braking pedal.
options.C: By pressing the braking pedal to the maximum.

q-6338.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a vehicle with ABS you brake by pressing the pedal fully and keeping up the pressure, because the system itself modulates the braking force wheel by wheel. Pumping the pedal or pressing gently only lengthens the braking distance.

q-6339.text: What is the function of the anti-lock braking system (ABS) applied in cars?

options.A: It helps to change the course of driving while braking.
options.B: In shortens braking distance in all conditions.
options.C: It prevents the loss of the drive wheel grip while accelerating.

q-6339.explanation: Correct answer: A. ABS keeps the wheels turning during braking, so the steering stays effective and you can change course. It does not shorten the braking distance in all conditions, and grip of the driven wheels under acceleration is the job of traction control.

q-6340.text: What is the function of airbags?

options.A: They reduce damages to the car as a result of a crash.
options.B: They provide full protection of the driver and passengers in case of a crash.
options.C: They reduce bodily injuries which may be suffered by the driver and passengers as a result of a crash.

q-6340.explanation: Correct answer: C. An airbag is a supplement to the seat belt: it cushions the body's impact and reduces injuries to the driver and passengers. It gives no complete protection and does not protect the bodywork, and with the belt unfastened it can itself cause injury.

q-6344.text: Should you wear your seatbelts while driving in these road conditions?

options.A: No, if I am travelling at a low speed.
options.C: Yes, but only while travelling faster than 50 km/h.

q-6344.explanation: Correct answer: B. The duty to use seat belts always applies when driving on a road, regardless of speed, length of journey and conditions. Even at low speed the forces in a collision exceed what human muscles can hold many times over.

q-6346.text: Approximately, by how much does the braking distance increase if speed is doubled?
q-6346.explanation: Correct answer: A. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed, so doubling the speed makes that distance roughly four times longer. On top of that comes the stretch covered during the reaction time, which grows in direct proportion to speed.

q-6347.text: What minimum distance should you keep from the car in front of you when stuck in a traffic jam in a tunel?
q-6347.explanation: Correct answer: B. When standing in a traffic jam in a tunnel, keep a distance of at least 5 m from the vehicle ahead. The free space lets you pull out of the column and makes access easier for the rescue services in the event of a fire or accident.

q-6349.text: What should you pay most attention to while you're passing another vehicle?

options.A: To proper positioning of your hands on the steering wheel.

q-6349.explanation: Correct answer: C. When passing an oncoming vehicle, what matters most is an adequate lateral distance from it, because a slight deviation from your line ends in a side collision. The distance must be increased with large vehicles, cyclists and a crosswind, reducing speed if necessary.

q-6351.text: What does a safe distance you should keep while driving behind another car depend on?

options.A: On the speed with which you're driving.
options.B: On the power of your engine.
options.C: On the width of the road.

q-6351.explanation: Correct answer: A. A safe distance depends above all on speed: the faster you drive, the longer the stretch covered during the reaction time and the longer the braking distance. On a wet or slippery surface and in poorer visibility the distance must be increased further.

q-6352.text: What can you expect while braking forcefully in these road conditions?

options.A: Increased traction of the wheels to the road.
options.C: Decreased traction of the wheels to the road.

q-6352.explanation: Correct answer: C. Harsh braking in such conditions reduces the grip of the wheels on the road: the wheels may lock or slide, and the vehicle loses steering and carries on almost in a straight line. Brake gently and early enough.

q-6353.text: What can you expect when driving onto a bridge marked with this sign?

options.C: Frosted road or black ice, even if they do not occur on other sections of the road.

q-6353.explanation: Correct answer: C. The sign warns of a stretch particularly prone to becoming slippery. A bridge is cooled by the air from below as well, so frost and black ice appear on it earlier than on the rest of the road. Slow down and avoid sudden manoeuvres.

q-6354.text: What should you expect if you turn at an intersection covered with ice?

options.A: That traction will be the same, if you drive within the permitted speed limit.
options.B: That traction will be worse, making it difficult for you to turn.
options.C: That traction will be the same, if the car is equipped with an anti-lock braking system (ABS).

q-6354.explanation: Correct answer: B. On an icy surface tyre grip drops sharply, and when turning the centrifugal force pushes the vehicle towards the outside of the curve. Neither ABS nor driving at the permitted speed restores grip, so you must enter the junction slowly and steer smoothly.

q-6355.text: What can you expect on a road marked this way?

options.A: That there is a collision-free passage for wild animals underneath the road.
options.B: That wild animals may be running across the road.
options.C: That animals may be herded across the road.

q-6355.explanation: Correct answer: B. The sign warns of a stretch where wild animals often run across the carriageway. Slow down and watch the verges and the edge of the forest, because animals move in groups and the first is usually followed by more.

q-6356.text: How can you maintain a proper course when driving on an express road in thick fog?

options.A: By following road markings designating the lanes.
options.B: By watching out for traffic signs.

q-6356.explanation: Correct answer: A. In fog the nearest and most reliable reference is the road markings on the carriageway, that is, the lines marking the lane and the edge of the carriageway. Vertical signs appear only here and there, and navigation does not show the vehicle's actual position in the lane.

q-6357.text: How should you react if you enter a section of the road covered with puddles?

options.B: Reduce speed, because you can expect skidding.

q-6357.explanation: Correct answer: B. A layer of water can lift the tyres off the surface, that is, cause aquaplaning: the wheels lose contact with the road, and the vehicle stops responding to the steering and the brakes. Speed must be reduced before entering puddles, driving smoothly and without sudden manoeuvres.

q-6358.text: If, at night, you pass another car lighting the road with its lights, can this stop you from noticing any obstacles on the road?

options.A: Yes, because there is a possibility of being temporarily blinded by the lights.
options.B: No, the lights of the car coming from the opposite direction always improve visibility on the road.
options.C: No, this does not affect the visibility on the road.

q-6358.explanation: Correct answer: A. The lights of an oncoming vehicle dazzle, and the eye needs time to readjust. At that moment a dark obstacle, a pedestrian or a cyclist can vanish from the field of vision. Look towards the right edge of the carriageway and slow down.

q-6360.text: Should you be more alert when you're driving at night?

options.A: Yes, because visibility at night is limited.
options.B: No, because there is less traffic on the road at night.
options.C: No, because at night one can turn on high-beam lights.

q-6360.explanation: Correct answer: A. At night the driver sees only as much as their lights illuminate, colours and outlines blur, and judging distance is harder. That is why speed must be adapted to the lit stretch and attention increased, despite the lighter traffic.

q-6361.text: When must you switch high-beam lights to low-beam lights?

options.A: When another car approaches from the opposite direction.
options.C: When you enter a built-up area.

q-6361.explanation: Correct answer: A. Main beam must be switched to dipped whenever it could dazzle another road user, above all the driver of an oncoming vehicle. Rain by itself, or entering a built-up area by itself, creates no such duty.

q-6362.text: When must you switch high-beam lights to low-beam lights?

options.A: Always when you see the car in front of you.
options.B: Always when there is a possibility of blinding the driver of the car in front of you.
options.C: Always when you see a single pedestrian on the road.

q-6362.explanation: Correct answer: B. Main beam also dazzles the driver of the vehicle ahead, because its glare reflects in their mirrors. What decides is the real possibility of dazzling, not merely noticing a vehicle ahead or a single pedestrian.

q-6363.text: When must you turn off the rear anti-fog light?
q-6363.explanation: Correct answer: C. Rear fog lights may be used only when visibility is reduced to about 50 m; once it rises above 50 m they must be switched off. Their strong light dazzles drivers behind and masks the brake-light signal.

q-6364.text: What sort of driving should you avoid in these road conditions?

options.B: Maintaining a steady and low speed.

q-6364.explanation: Correct answer: A. In difficult road conditions grip falls and visibility worsens, so the greatest danger is high speed: it lengthens the braking distance and takes away time to react. A steady, low speed and engine braking help keep the vehicle stable.

q-6365.text: What should you pay special attention to while reversing the car?

options.A: Any objects which are around and which are approaching the car.
options.B: That you firmly keep your hand on the gear stick.
options.C: The positioning of the steering wheel in order to determine the driving trajectory.

q-6365.explanation: Correct answer: A. When reversing, the driver must watch the surroundings the whole time and give way to all other road users. A large part of the area behind the vehicle is invisible, and pedestrians or children may appear there. When observation is not possible, ask another person for help.

q-6366.text: In what way should you observe your surroundings while driving on a motorway?

options.A: Look only in front of you.
options.B: Pay the same amount of attention to observing the road in front of and behind the vehicle.
options.C: Look to the front and from time to time monitor the road behind the vehicle using the side mirrors.

q-6366.explanation: Correct answer: C. On a motorway the main attention belongs to the road ahead, where speeds are highest, but the mirrors must be checked regularly, because vehicles behind close in very fast. Knowing the situation behind is necessary before every lane change.

q-6367.text: When can you return to the right lane after you complete the overtaking manoeuvre on a one-way road with two lanes?

options.A: Immediately after you can see the edge of the overtaken car in your external mirror.
options.B: Immediately after you can see the lights of the overtaken car in the external mirror.
options.C: After you've made sure that this will not force the driver of the overtaken car to brake or change its trajectory of driving.

q-6367.explanation: Correct answer: C. Returning to the right lane is allowed only when it will not force the driver of the overtaken vehicle to brake or change course. Seeing the vehicle in the mirror is only a hint; what decides is a real, sufficiently large gap.

q-6368.text: What position behind the wheel will help to reduce the effect of the so-called blind spot in the mirrors which occurs when you watch the road?

options.A: Static - sitting in a stiff position, without moving your body or head.
options.B: Dynamic - bending your body and head away from the seat, as required by the circumstances.
options.C: Any position - as long as it guarantees comfort of driving.

q-6368.explanation: Correct answer: B. The blind spot is a permanent feature of mirrors, but moving the head and torso shifts the field of view and lets you uncover it. That is why a dynamic posture is recommended, and before a lane change an additional look over the shoulder.

q-6369.text: How should you behave before you start overtaking in good visibility in order to ensure that you have sufficient visibility of the road?

options.A: I must come as close as possible to the car in front of me.
options.B: I will keep a sufficient distance from the car in front of me to allow me to watch the road.
options.C: I will use the horn to force the driver of the car in front of me to move to the shoulder or an emergency lane.

q-6369.explanation: Correct answer: B. Getting too close hides the road ahead of the vehicle in front and shortens the time to abandon the manoeuvre. A larger distance lets you assess the opposite lane and begin overtaking with speed already gained. The horn is not for forcing others to make room.

q-6370.text: How should you observe the road when you drive the car in the road traffic?

options.A: In such a way as to get a wide field of vision.
options.B: By concentrating on a narrow space immediately in front of the car.
options.C: Without paying any attention to the situation behind the car.

q-6370.explanation: Correct answer: A. In city traffic hazards also come from the sides: from pedestrians, cyclists and vehicles pulling out of driveways. So look far ahead, sweep your eyes across the sides and check the mirrors. Focusing on the space just in front of the bonnet leads to a late reaction.

q-6371.text: What should you see in a properly-positioned rear-view mirror?

options.A: The child sitting in the child safety seat behind the passenger's seat.
options.B: The reflection of the driver's own face.
options.C: The rear car window and the road behind the car.

q-6371.explanation: Correct answer: C. The interior mirror serves to watch the road behind the vehicle and should take in the whole rear window. Aiming it at a child or at your own face deprives the driver of the picture of what is happening behind and makes it harder to judge the situation before a lane change or braking.

q-6372.text: How should you properly position the rear-view mirror?

options.A: In any position, depending what you want to see.
options.B: In such a way as to see the rear car window and the road behind the car.
options.C: In such a way as to see the passenger sitting at the back.

q-6372.explanation: Correct answer: B. The interior mirror is adjusted in the driving position, without lifting the back off the backrest, so that its frame takes in the whole rear window and the road behind the vehicle. Set this way it complements the picture from the exterior mirrors and reduces the blind spot.

q-6373.text: How will you position the driver's seat before you start driving?

options.A: In such a way as to have free access to the equipment of the car used to drive and steer the car.
options.B: In such a way so that my back is not positioned tight against the back of the seat.
options.C: In such a way that my arms, holding the steering wheel, are fully straightened-up in the elbows.

q-6373.explanation: Correct answer: A. The seat is set so that you can reach the pedals and switches freely, with your back against the backrest and arms slightly bent at the elbows. Straight arms and a back off the seat limit control of the vehicle and increase the risk of injury in a collision.

q-6375.text: In what order should you perform the following activities when preparing to drive a vehicle?

options.A: Fasten the seat belts, position the mirrors and the driver's seat.
options.B: Position the mirrors, the driver's seat and fasten the seat belts.
options.C: Position the driver's seat, mirrors and fasten the seat belts.

q-6375.explanation: Correct answer: C. The seat is set first, because its position changes the height of the head and thus the field of view in the mirrors. Only then are the mirrors adjusted, and finally the seat belt is fastened, in the final position behind the wheel.

q-6377.text: In what gear should you start driving on a dry surface?
q-6377.explanation: Correct answer: B. Moving off in the lowest gear gives the greatest torque at the wheels, so the vehicle starts smoothly without excessive clutch slip. A higher gear is used exceptionally, on a slippery surface, to limit wheelspin of the driven wheels.

q-6378.text: While driving a passenger car, what should you see in properly-adjusted external mirrors ("rear-view mirrors")?

options.A: Only the sides of the car.
options.B: The area behind the car and the sides of the car.

q-6378.explanation: Correct answer: B. An exterior mirror should show the road behind the vehicle together with a narrow strip of your own side, which gives a reference point for judging distance. Set this way it also covers the neighbouring lane and reduces the blind spot.

q-6379.text: In what way should you brake in an emergency situation, if the vehicle is equipped with anti-lock braking system (ABS)?

options.A: Firmly press on the brake pedal without releasing it when the ABS system is activated.
options.B: Firmly press on the brake pedal and slightly let up on it while the ABS system is activated.
options.C: Press on the brake pedal using a pulsating action until the ABS system is activated.

q-6379.explanation: Correct answer: A. Emergency braking with ABS means pressing the pedal hard and keeping up the pressure until the vehicle stops; vibration and pulsing of the pedal mean the system is working. Easing off or pumping the brake interrupts its operation and lengthens the braking distance.

q-6380.text: At what point, while driving a passenger car, will you press the clutch pedal if you want to routinely (intentionally) brake when you're travelling at high speed?

options.A: Before I press the brake pedal.
options.C: When the speed drops to the minimum speed for the gear I'm going in.

q-6380.explanation: Correct answer: C. As long as a gear is engaged, the engine assists braking and the vehicle keeps its stability and better grip at the driven wheels. The clutch is pressed only just before the engine would stall, that is, when speed drops to the minimum for the current gear.

q-6381.text: How will you counteract the centrifugal force while turning left in a four-wheeled vehicle?

options.A: I will bend the upper part of my body to the right.
options.B: I will brace my right foot against the footrest.
options.C: I will keep my body along the longitudinal axis of the car.

q-6381.explanation: Correct answer: B. During a left turn the centrifugal force pushes the body towards the outside of the curve, that is, to the right. Bracing the right foot against the footrest plate gives stable support, lets you keep your position and steer confidently, while leaning the body into the bend.

q-6383.text: What body position should you maintain when going down a hill in a four-wheeled vehicle?

options.A: A sitting position, with the body weight shifted towards the rear axle.
options.B: A standing position, perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the car.
options.C: A sitting position, with the body leaned forward.

q-6383.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a descent the load shifts to the front axle, and the rear of the vehicle becomes light and prone to sliding out. A seated position with the body weight shifted rearwards restores balance, improves the grip of the rear wheels and reduces the risk of tipping over the front.

q-6384.text: What body position should you maintain when going up a hill in a four-wheeled vehicle?

options.A: A sitting position, perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the car.
options.B: A standing position, with the body leaned towards the front axle.
options.C: A sitting position, with the body leaned towards the rear axle.

q-6384.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a climb the load shifts to the rear axle, and the front of the vehicle becomes light and may begin to lift. A standing position with the body leaning towards the front axle moves the weight forward, presses the front wheels down and keeps steering.

q-6385.text: What is not recommended to do when you go around a bend in a four-wheeled vehicle?

options.A: To maintain a low, regular speed.
options.C: To suddenly close or open the throttle.

q-6385.explanation: Correct answer: C. A sudden change of throttle in a bend shifts the load between the axles abruptly and may break grip: closing the throttle makes the rear slide out, and opening it pushes the vehicle to the outside of the curve. You enter the bend at a steady speed and add throttle smoothly.

q-6386.text: How many persons, including yourself, can you transport when you drive a passenger car?

options.A: As many persons as the number of seats specified on the registration card plus one child aged up to 3.
options.B: As many persons as the number of seats specified on the registration card plus one child aged up to 7.
options.C: As many persons as the number of seats specified on the registration card.

q-6386.explanation: Correct answer: C. The number of people carried may not exceed the number of seats entered in the registration document. Every person, a child included, takes one seat and must wear a belt or travel in a child seat. No rule allows an extra passenger beyond that number.

q-6387.text: Which of the following documents specifies the permitted number of persons transported in the car?

options.C: A document confirming the valid obligatory third party civil liability insurance.

q-6387.explanation: Correct answer: A. The number of seats, and thus the permitted number of people carried, is entered in the vehicle's registration document. The driving licence only specifies the categories of vehicle you may drive, and the insurance document concerns liability for damage caused.

q-6388.text: Who is obliged to use seat belts?

options.A: Only the driver and a passenger sitting in the front seat.
options.B: The driver and the passenger - always in the front seat - and in the back seat when the car goes outside a built-up area.
options.C: The driver and all the passengers.

q-6388.explanation: Correct answer: C. The duty to fasten seat belts covers the driver and every passenger, in the front and in the back, in town and outside it. The exceptions are few and concern, among others, people with an appropriate medical certificate and children carried in child seats.

q-6389.text: Is an adult passenger of a passenger car transported in the back seat obliged to use the seat belts?

options.B: Yes, but only when the car goes outside a built-up area.

q-6389.explanation: Correct answer: C. The duty to fasten seat belts also applies to the rear seats, regardless of where you are driving. In a collision an unbelted rear passenger strikes the back of the front seat with a force of many tonnes and endangers the person sitting in front.

q-6390.text: Do you violate the provisions of traffic law, if, while driving a car, you talk on a phone by holding the phone in your hand?

options.A: No, as long as I maintain the control of the car.
options.B: No, as long as I hold the telephone away from my ear and I have switched on the loudspeaker mode.
options.C: Yes, even if I hold the telephone away from my ear and I have switched on the loudspeaker mode.

q-6390.explanation: Correct answer: C. Using a phone while driving is prohibited if it requires holding the handset or microphone in the hand. Switching on the loudspeaker mode changes nothing, because the hand is occupied and attention divided. Only a kit that does not require holding the phone is allowed.

q-6391.text: What is the maximum number of persons, including yourself, that you may transport if you have a B-category driving licence?
q-6391.explanation: Correct answer: B. Category B entitles you to drive a vehicle designed to carry no more than eight people besides the driver, that is, nine people including the driver. A vehicle with more seats requires a category D1 or D licence.

q-6393.text: On what public roads is wearing seatbelts mandatory?

options.C: Only on roads outside built-up areas.

q-6393.explanation: Correct answer: A. The duty to fasten seat belts applies on all public roads, regardless of the type of surface and whether it is a built-up area. The type of road does not change the physics of a collision: even at low speed an unbelted body is thrown forward.

q-6397.text: Can you transport a preschooler on the lap of an adult person?

options.A: Yes, but only in the back seat.
options.C: Yes, if you fasten your seat belts.

q-6397.explanation: Correct answer: B. A child is carried in a child seat matched to its weight and height, correctly fitted to the seat. On an adult's lap, under braking or in a collision, it is crushed by that person's weight, and their belt gives it no protection at all.

q-6398.text: Can you transport an infant on the lap of an adult person?

options.B: Yes, but only in the back seat.
options.C: Yes, if such person has the seat belts fastened.

q-6398.explanation: Correct answer: A. An infant may be carried only in a child seat matched to its weight and height, correctly fitted in the vehicle. No arms will hold a child under braking or in an impact, and an adult's belt then crushes it with enormous force.

q-6399.text: How is it recommended to transport an infant in a passenger car?

options.A: In any baby carrier, as long as the infant is fastened with seat belts.
options.B: In a child safety seat suitable for infants.
options.C: On the lap of an adult person who has the seat belts fastened.

q-6399.explanation: Correct answer: B. A newborn is carried in a child seat matched to its weight and height, correctly fitted in the vehicle, usually rear-facing, which best protects the head and neck. A random carrier or an adult's lap gives no such protection.

q-6400.text: Can you, while driving a four-wheeled vehicle (microcar, quad), transport a child aged up to 6?

options.B: Yes, but only with the speed of up to 40 km/h.

q-6400.explanation: Correct answer: B. A child up to 6 years old may be carried in a quadricycle only when the speed does not exceed 40 km/h. The restriction follows from the modest protection such a vehicle gives, so the driving must be calm, without sudden manoeuvres.

q-6401.text: Which of the following combination vehicles can you drive if you have a B-category driving licence?

options.A: A truck with gross vehicle weight of 2.5 t, with a light trailer.
options.B: A farm tractor with two trailers.
options.C: A passenger car with a trailer, as long as their gross vehicle weight amounts to up to 4.5 t.

q-6401.explanation: Correct answer: A. Category B allows you to drive a vehicle with a maximum permissible mass of up to 3.5 t together with a light trailer, that is, one whose maximum permissible mass does not exceed 750 kg. A tractor with trailers requires category T, and a combination of 4.5 t exceeds the basic entitlement.

q-6402.text: What is the maximum overhang of a load transported in a motor vehicle, counting from the rear outline of the car?
q-6402.explanation: Correct answer: A. A load may protrude at the rear by no more than 2 m beyond the rear plane of the vehicle's outline. The protruding end must be clearly marked, and in conditions of insufficient visibility additionally with a red light and a red reflector.

q-6403.text: What is the maximum length of a combination vehicle consisting of a passenger car and a caravan?
q-6403.explanation: Correct answer: A. A combination of a car and a trailer may be no more than 18.75 m long. Exceeding that value is not permitted, and the longer the combination, the harder it is to manoeuvre, overtake and fit round bends.

q-6404.text: What are responsibilities of the person involved in the traffic accident in which there are victims?

options.A: Promptly remove the vehicle from the road so as not to block traffic.
options.B: Promptly remove any damaged vehicle parts from the road so as not to impede traffic.
options.C: Offer assistance to victims of the accident as well as call an ambulance and the Police.

q-6404.explanation: Correct answer: C. When there are injured people, help comes first: secure the scene, give first aid and call an ambulance and the Police. Vehicles and traces may not be moved until the Police arrive, unless it is necessary to save a life.

q-6405.text: At what distance behind a broken-down passenger car, parked on a motorway, should you place a warning triangle?
q-6405.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a motorway and an expressway the warning triangle is placed 100 m behind the vehicle, so that those approaching at high speed have time to change lane. On other roads outside a built-up area the distance is 30–50 m.

q-6406.text: What do we call a combination vehicle?

options.A: A passenger car with a trailer.
options.B: A motorbike with a side car.
options.C: Motor vehicles combined for the purpose of towing.

q-6406.explanation: Correct answer: A. A combination of vehicles is a motor vehicle together with a trailer coupled to it, for example a car with a trailer. A motorcycle with a sidecar is a single vehicle, and vehicles joined for towing do not form a combination in this sense.

q-6407.text: Which of the following are mandatory equipment in each passenger car?
q-6407.explanation: Correct answer: C. The compulsory equipment of a car is a fire extinguisher and a reflective warning triangle. A first-aid kit and a spare wheel can be useful, but they are not required. The extinguisher must be easily accessible and have a valid inspection, otherwise it will be useless in a fire.

q-6408.text: Is it permitted to move away from the car when the engine is running?

options.B: Yes, as long as the car remains within the field of vision.
options.C: Yes, for no more than 1 minute.

q-6408.explanation: Correct answer: A. The driver may not leave the vehicle while the engine is running. Before walking away, switch off the engine and secure the vehicle against moving off on its own, because a car left unattended may roll away or be taken by an unauthorised person.

q-6409.text: What must you not do if you're involved in an accident where there are fatalities?

options.A: Remove the car from the road so that it does not cause an obstacle to traffic.
options.B: Provide the necessary assistance to the victims of the accident.

q-6409.explanation: Correct answer: A. In an accident with people killed or injured, the position of the vehicles and the traces may not be changed until the Police arrive; moving is permitted only when it serves to save a life. Giving help and calling the services always remain a duty.

q-6410.text: Which of the following elements belongs to the mandatory equipment of each passenger car?
q-6410.explanation: Correct answer: B. Every car must have a reflective warning triangle and a fire extinguisher. A jack and a reflective vest are recommended but not compulsory. The triangle should be kept in an easily accessible place, because it serves to mark an immobilised vehicle.

q-6411.text: Which of the following are mandatory equipment in each passenger car?

options.C: A loud-speaking device for the telephone.

q-6411.explanation: Correct answer: A. The compulsory equipment of a car includes a reflective warning triangle and a fire extinguisher. Spare bulbs and a hands-free kit can be useful, but the rules do not require them. The triangle marks a stopped vehicle so as to warn others early enough.

q-6412.text: Which of the following are mandatory equipment in each passenger car?

options.C: A device for cutting the seat belts.

q-6412.explanation: Correct answer: A. A fire extinguisher, alongside a reflective warning triangle, is part of a car's compulsory equipment. Satellite navigation and a belt cutter can come in handy, but the rules do not require them. The extinguisher must be within the driver's reach and in working order.

q-6413.text: When should you conduct a periodic technical check-up of a passenger car?

options.C: Before the lapse of a deadline specified on the registration card of the car.

q-6413.explanation: Correct answer: C. The date of the next technical inspection is entered in the registration document, and it is that date that sets the owner's obligation, not a fixed two- or three-year cycle. The inspection must be carried out no later than the day given in the document.

q-6414.text: Can you drive a passenger car if you hold an expired driving licence?

options.A: Yes, for 7 days after the expiry date.
options.B: Yes, for 14 days after the expiry date.

q-6414.explanation: Correct answer: C. The moment its validity expires, a driving licence stops entitling you to drive, and there is no transitional period. The document must be replaced before that date, otherwise driving is treated as driving without entitlement.

q-6416.text: In what circumstances must you carry out an additional technical check-up of a passenger car?

options.A: After the owner of the car changes.
options.B: If so directed by a traffic control authority.
options.C: After expiry of the third-party civil liability insurance policy.

q-6416.explanation: Correct answer: B. An additional technical inspection is carried out, among other cases, when a traffic enforcement authority orders it, for example after faults are found or after an accident. A change of owner alone, or the expiry of the insurance policy, does not require such an inspection.

q-6417.text: What should the owner of a passenger car do if one of the registration plates of the car is lost?

options.B: Immediately replace the registration plate with a new plate without a legalization mark.
options.C: Apply for an issue of a legalized duplicate of the registration plate.

q-6417.explanation: Correct answer: C. After losing a plate, the owner must apply to the office for a legalised duplicate; only a plate with the official legalisation mark is valid. Driving with one plate, or with a plate without legalisation, is not permitted.

q-6419.text: Where should you perform periodic technical inspections of a vehicle?

options.B: In an authorized repair shop that services vehicles.
options.C: At a local or regional vehicle inspection station.

q-6419.explanation: Correct answer: C. A technical inspection may be carried out only by an authorised vehicle inspection station — basic or district — because only it has licensed inspectors and makes the entry in the documents. A repair workshop, however well equipped, has no such authority.

q-6422.text: Can you drive the proper motor vehicle for a B1-category driving licence if it is expired?

options.A: Yes, for 7 days after the expiry date.
options.B: Yes, for 14 days after the expiry date.

q-6422.explanation: Correct answer: C. An invalid driving licence gives no entitlement to drive any vehicle covered by the category in question, a quadricycle included, and there is no grace period here. The document must be replaced before its validity expires.

q-6423.text: In what circumstances must you conduct an additional technical check-up of a four-wheeled motor vehicle having a curb weight of 500 kg?

options.A: After the owner of the car changes.
options.B: If so directed by a traffic control authority.
options.C: After expiry of the third-party civil liability insurance policy.

q-6423.explanation: Correct answer: B. The basis for an additional technical inspection is a referral issued by a traffic enforcement authority, for example after faults are found or after involvement in an incident. A change of owner or the end of the insurance policy gives rise to no such duty.

q-6426.text: Which of the following concentration of alcohol in blood is a value forbidding one to drive a motor vehicle with a curb weight of 500 kg?
q-6426.explanation: Correct answer: A. The state after alcohol consumption begins at 0.2‰ in the blood, and from that value driving a vehicle is prohibited. The lower readings given in the other answers do not mark the threshold adopted in the rules.

q-6427.text: Where should you perform the periodic check-up of a motor vehicle with a curb weight of up to 550 kg?

options.B: In an authorized repair shop which services the car.
options.C: In the basic or district vehicle control station.

q-6427.explanation: Correct answer: C. A periodic technical inspection is carried out only by an authorised vehicle inspection station, basic or district, which employs an inspector and confirms the result in the vehicle's documents. An ordinary workshop, however well equipped, cannot do it.

q-6430.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive if you have a B1-category driving licence?

options.A: A motorbike with a side car.
options.C: Any motor vehicle with a curb weight of 650 kg.

q-6430.explanation: Correct answer: B. Category B1 covers quadricycles, that is, light motor vehicles of limited unladen mass. A motorcycle with a sidecar belongs to a motorcycle category, and a heavier motor vehicle requires category B.

q-6431.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive if you have a B1-category driving licence?
q-6431.explanation: Correct answer: B. A category B1 entitlement also covers driving a moped, because it is a lighter and slower vehicle than those covered by that category. A car requires category B, and an agricultural tractor — category T.

q-6432.text: What may be the consequences of a driver's failure to fasten their seat belts?

options.A: More damage to the car in the event of a collision.
options.B: More bodily injuries suffered by the driver in the event of an accident.

q-6432.explanation: Correct answer: B. The seat belt keeps the driver's body in place and spreads the forces of a collision, so without it the risk of serious injuries grows — from striking the steering wheel, the windscreen or the interior. The belt has no effect on damage to the vehicle itself or on the airbag.

q-6434.text: What does it mean when the braking pedal sinks down when you start the engine as you press the pedal?

options.A: That the power brake system is working.
options.B: That there is a high level of brake fluid in the master cylinder reservoir.
options.C: That the ant-lock braking system (ABS) is working.

q-6434.explanation: Correct answer: A. After the engine is started, a vacuum builds up to feed the brake servo, so a pressed pedal sinks slightly. This is a normal symptom; the absence of such movement may mean a fault in the servo.

q-6436.text: What may be a cause of the excessive free play of the steering wheel in the car?
q-6436.explanation: Correct answer: A. Play at the steering wheel comes from worn joints in the steering system, above all the ball joints and track rod ends. Worn tyres or unbalanced wheels give different symptoms — noise, vibration, uneven tread wear.

q-6437.text: What might be the cause of a vehicle pulling to the left while driving in a straight line?

options.A: Operation of the power steering system.
options.C: Low air pressure in the right front tyre.

q-6437.explanation: Correct answer: B. Incorrectly set wheel alignment makes the vehicle constantly drift to one side even though the steering wheel is held straight. Too little pressure in the right tyre would pull to the right, and power steering does not change the direction of travel.

q-6438.text: How is braking on a wet road affected by using tyres having tread wear exceeding maximum safety limits?

options.B: The shortening of the braking distance.
options.C: Decrease of friction and the lengthening of the braking distance.

q-6438.explanation: Correct answer: C. Worn tread does not clear water from under the tyre, so grip falls and the braking distance grows; the risk of aquaplaning also increases. On a wet surface the effects are much stronger than on a dry one.

q-6439.text: What may be the effect of worn shock absorbers on the front wheels?

options.B: Decreased tyre grip and steerability of the vehicle.

q-6439.explanation: Correct answer: B. Worn shock absorbers do not damp vibrations, so the wheel loses even contact with the road and the vehicle responds worse to the steering. The result is less grip, poorer handling and a longer braking distance.

q-6440.text: What may be the effect of not balancing the wheels of the vehicle?
q-6440.explanation: Correct answer: C. An unbalanced wheel vibrates while driving and presses the tyre onto the road unevenly, which locally speeds up tread wear. Vibration at the steering wheel and faster wear of suspension parts are felt as well.

q-6441.text: What would be most affected by wrong adjustment of external mirrors in a motor vehicle?
q-6441.explanation: Correct answer: B. The exterior mirrors show what is happening behind and to the side, so setting them wrongly enlarges the blind spot and makes it harder to assess the situation before changing lane. Before such a manoeuvre a look over the shoulder is necessary too.

q-6442.text: What is the purpose of the position lights of a vehicle?

options.B: To indicate the position of the vehicle.
options.C: To signal the fact of changing lanes.

q-6442.explanation: Correct answer: B. Position lights are meant to show other road users where the vehicle is standing or travelling and how wide it is. They do not light the road, and a lane change is signalled with the indicator.

q-6443.text: What may be the effect of wrong adjustment of low-beam lights?

options.C: Blinding the drivers approaching from the opposite direction.

q-6443.explanation: Correct answer: C. Headlamps set too high direct the beam into the eyes of oncoming drivers, depriving them of vision for a moment. Headlamp adjustment has nothing to do with fuel or bulb consumption.

q-6444.text: How should low-beam lights be aimed in a motor vehicle?

options.A: In such a way as to light the road 30 m ahead of the vehicle.
options.B: In such a way that they symmetrically light the whole road.
options.C: In such a way that they light the road asymmetrically.

q-6444.explanation: Correct answer: C. Dipped headlights shine asymmetrically: they light the right side and the verge more strongly, and on the left have a clearly lowered cut-off so as not to dazzle oncoming drivers. This distribution is a design feature of the headlamps.

q-6445.text: What is the purpose of the rear anti-fog lights of a passenger car?

options.A: They increase the effectiveness of signalling the fact of braking in fog.
options.C: They improve the visibility of the car in fog.

q-6445.explanation: Correct answer: C. Rear fog lights shine very intensely, so the vehicle is seen from a greater distance in dense fog that limits visibility to 50 m. Once visibility improves they must be switched off, because they dazzle drivers behind.

q-6446.text: What is the function of reversing lights in a motor vehicle?

options.A: They light the road ahead of the vehicle.
options.B: They light the road at the back of the vehicle and they signal the reversing manoeuvre.
options.C: They light the registration plate at the back of the vehicle.

q-6446.explanation: Correct answer: B. Reversing lights come on when reverse gear is engaged: they light the road behind the vehicle and at the same time tell others that the manoeuvre is starting. They do not, however, release the driver from making sure nobody is behind the vehicle.

q-6447.text: What may be the effect if you use damaged or worn wiper blades in a passenger car?

options.C: Deterioration of road visibility in the rain.

q-6447.explanation: Correct answer: C. Worn wiper blades leave streaks and unremoved water on the windscreen, which in rain seriously limits visibility, especially after dark and in the light of other vehicles. They have no effect on washer fluid or battery consumption.

q-6448.text: What auditory signals can you emit from a motor vehicle?
q-6448.explanation: Correct answer: C. An ordinary vehicle may have only a horn with a continuous, non-piercing tone. Signals with a varying tone are reserved for emergency vehicles, and fitting them to another vehicle is prohibited.

q-6449.text: What may be the effect a leaking exhaust system in a motor vehicle?

options.B: Increased level of noise produced by the vehicle.

q-6449.explanation: Correct answer: B. A leaking exhaust system lets exhaust gases out before the silencer, so the vehicle becomes much louder. Exhaust gases may also get into the cabin, which is dangerous for the occupants; engine capacity and oil consumption are unaffected.

q-6450.text: What may be a cause of a significantly increased flashing frequency of the turnsignals?

options.A: A short circuit in the turnsignal circuit.
options.B: A failure of one of the turnsignal bulbs.

q-6450.explanation: Correct answer: B. A blown bulb reduces the load on the circuit, and the control unit signals this by a clearly faster flashing of the warning light and the remaining lamps. That is a sign to check the indicators and replace the failed bulb.

q-6451.text: What may be the effect of wrong adjustment of low-beam lights?

options.B: Deterioration of road visibility at night.

q-6451.explanation: Correct answer: B. Headlamps aimed too low shorten the lit stretch of road, so at night the driver sees an obstacle too late. Headlamp adjustment does not, however, affect fuel consumption or bulb life.

q-6452.text: Is a first-aid kit a piece of obligatory equipment in any motor vehicle?

options.B: No, but it's good to have it.
