options.C: Yes, if the vehicle is equipped with a gas installation.

q-6452.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a car a first-aid kit is not part of the compulsory equipment, although it is very useful when giving first aid. It must be carried by, among others, buses and certain special vehicles.

q-6453.text: Which of the following actions towards a person injured in an accident may entail penal liability?

options.C: Any unprofessional and incorrectly performed rescue action.

q-6453.explanation: Correct answer: A. It is punishable not to help a person whose life or health is in danger when help can be given without endangering yourself. Help given in good faith, however clumsy, gives rise to no criminal liability.

q-6454.text: What is the most relevant information for paramedics when indicating the location of the road accident?

options.A: Name of street and house number or name of road and the name of the nearest town, kilometre marker.

q-6454.explanation: Correct answer: A. The rescuers must reach a specific point, so what counts is the exact location: the street and number, or the road number, the nearest locality and the kilometre marker. The name of the locality alone is too general to find the casualties quickly.

q-6456.text: What should a person travelling on a highway do if they experience the following: shortness of breath, chills, numbness of the arms, pain around the stomach area and humming in the ears.

options.A: He should speed up and drive to a hospital.
options.B: He should carefully enter the emergency lane, call the ambulance and unfasten his seat belts.
options.C: He should open his window and drive to a hospital.

q-6456.explanation: Correct answer: B. Such symptoms may indicate a serious cardiovascular incident, so driving on endangers the driver and others. Calmly pull onto the hard shoulder, stop the vehicle, call medical help and loosen your clothing and the belts.

q-6457.text: What should you do if a fall from a four-wheeled vehicle (microcar, quad) entails a head injury with visible nose-bleeding or ear-bleeding?

options.A: Immobilize the head and the neck section of the spine, and apply a protective dressing.
options.B: Apply pressure dressing on the wound.

q-6457.explanation: Correct answer: A. Bloody discharge from the nose or ear indicates a skull injury, which is often accompanied by damage to the cervical spine. The head and neck must be immobilised and the wound only covered — a pressure dressing at this place is not acceptable.

q-6458.text: What injuries are usually associated with severe head injuries which occur after a fall from a four-wheeled vehicle (microcar, quad)?

options.A: Injuries of the abdominal section of the spine.
options.B: Injuries of the chest section of the spine.
options.C: Injuries of the neck section of the spine and the skull.

q-6458.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a fall the head is thrown violently, so together with a skull injury the cervical section of the spine is most often damaged. That is why the casualty's head and neck are immobilised and their position is not changed without need.

q-6459.text: Which of the following numbers should you call in order to call an ambulance to the scene of a road accident?
q-6459.explanation: Correct answer: C. The ambulance service is called on 999 or on the common emergency number 112, which passes the report to the appropriate service. The numbers 997 and 998 are the police and the fire brigade.

q-6461.text: Which of the following actions apply to drivers involved in a motor vehicle accident in which there are fatalities or victims?

options.A: Confirm the circumstances of the accident.
options.B: Confirm which party is responsible for the accident.
options.C: Remain at the scene of the accident.

q-6461.explanation: Correct answer: C. In an accident with victims the driver must stop the vehicle, give help, call the services and stay at the scene until they arrive. Establishing what happened and who was at fault is for the police, not the participants.

q-6463.text: While driving a car in wintertime and you see a blue, half-conscious, freezing person on the shoulder, how should you help him?

options.C: Take him to the car, cover him and have him warm up slowly.

q-6463.explanation: Correct answer: C. A hypothermic, semi-conscious person must be moved to a warm place, covered and warmed slowly while the emergency medical team is called. They are given no fluids, and certainly no alcohol, because of the risk of choking and further loss of heat.

q-6465.text: Is everyone obliged to give first aid to victims of accidents?

options.A: No, because aid may be given only persons with medical training.
options.B: Yes, because one can independently perform some of the first-aid activities.
options.C: No, because penal liability may be imposed for any committed mistakes.

q-6465.explanation: Correct answer: B. The duty to give first aid rests on everyone who can do so without endangering themselves; calling the services, securing the scene or chest compressions need no medical training. Nobody is held liable for help given in good faith.

q-6466.text: What should you do if you identify an open fracture?
q-6466.explanation: Correct answer: B. A broken limb is immobilised together with the two neighbouring joints so that the bone fragments do not move. The wound must not be dressed with cotton wool, and the limb must not be set or pulled — that is the rescue team's job.

q-6467.text: What should you use as a dressing of severely-bleeding wounds?

options.B: A pressure dressing of gauze, cloth and bandage.

q-6467.explanation: Correct answer: B. Heavy bleeding is stemmed with a pressure dressing: sterile gauze is placed on the wound and pressed down firmly with a bandage. Antiseptics such as iodine will not stop a haemorrhage, and gauze alone without pressure quickly soaks through.

q-6468.text: Why is the side position is a safe position for unconscious as well as breathing persons?

options.A: Because it provides the victim with the greatest comfort while waiting for the ambulance.
options.B: Because it protects against injuries of the neck section of the spine.
options.C: Because it prevents any blocking of the respiratory tract and choking.

q-6468.explanation: Correct answer: C. In an unconscious person lying on their back, the tongue may fall back and close the airway, and stomach contents may get into the lungs. Placing them on their side keeps the airway open and lets secretions drain freely.

q-6469.text: Which of the following actions apply to drivers involved in a motor vehicle accident in which there are no fatalities or victims?

options.A: Remain at the scene of the accident.
options.C: Remove the vehicle from the scene of the accident so as not to impede traffic.

q-6469.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a collision with no injuries, the driver should remove the vehicle from the scene so that it does not endanger others or obstruct traffic, and exchange details with the other participant. Calling the police is not compulsory then.

q-6470.text: What should be your first reaction when a child fastened in a child safety seat chokes on food?

options.A: Go to hospital as quickly as possible.
options.B: Stop the car, take out the child and, holding it head downwards, pat it on the back.
options.C: Call an ambulance by telephone, without offering any help to the child.

q-6470.explanation: Correct answer: B. Choking must be dealt with immediately, because seconds count: stop the vehicle in a safe place, take the child out, tilt it head down and strike between the shoulder blades. Driving to hospital or just waiting for help loses precious time.

q-6471.text: What's the maximum speed at which you can ride a motorcycle, once you drive past these signs?
q-6471.explanation: Correct answer: B. The signs in the material lead onto the road with the highest permitted limit, on which a motorcycle may travel at no more than 140 km/h. Higher values are not permitted on any public road.

q-6472.text: At what speed can you ride a motorcycle on a dual carriage express road?
q-6472.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a dual-carriageway expressway a limit of 120 km/h applies, so of the values given only 105 km/h is within it. The other speeds exceed that limit.

q-6473.text: What's the maximum speed at which you can ride a motorcycle once you go past these signs on the road?
q-6473.explanation: Correct answer: C. The signs in the material lead onto a dual-carriageway expressway, where the permitted speed for a motorcycle is 120 km/h. The lower values correspond to other kinds of road.

q-6474.text: At which of the following speeds can you ride a motorcycle if you carry a six-year-old child?
q-6474.explanation: Correct answer: C. Carrying a child under seven on a motorcycle is permitted only at a clearly reduced speed, so of the values given only the lowest falls within it. The other speeds are too high.

q-6477.text: What's the maximum speed at which you can ride a motorcycle once you go past this sign, if you carry a five-year-old child?
q-6477.explanation: Correct answer: A. The lower of the values always applies: the limit arising from the sign shown in the material and the reduced limit when carrying a child under seven. Here 20 km/h is binding.

q-6478.text: Can you ride a motorcycle in a lane designated for buses?

options.A: Yes, you can use it to bypass vehicles in a traffic jam.
options.B: Yes, you can follow the bus in order to avoid obstacles on the road.

q-6478.explanation: Correct answer: C. A lane designated for buses is reserved for the vehicles indicated on the sign; a motorcycle may use it only when the sign expressly allows it. A traffic jam is no reason that justifies entering that lane.

q-6479.text: Which of these signs tells you not to exceed the speed of 40 km/h?
q-6479.explanation: Correct answer: C. A speed limit is introduced by a prohibition sign with a number giving the permitted speed in km/h. The other signs shown in the material have different meanings and establish no such limit.

q-6480.text: Which of the following vehicles must you not overtake if you ride a motorcycle on the road, once you go past this sign?
q-6480.explanation: Correct answer: C. The sign in the material prohibits overtaking multi-track motor vehicles, and a car is exactly such a vehicle. Two-wheeled vehicles, including a moped and a two-wheeled motorcycle, may still be overtaken.

q-6481.text: Which of the following vehicles can you overtake if you ride a motorcycle on the road, once you go past this sign?
q-6481.explanation: Correct answer: B. The overtaking ban in the material concerns multi-track motor vehicles, and a two-wheeled motorcycle is not one of them, so it may be overtaken. An agricultural tractor and a light quadricycle are multi-track and remain covered by the ban.

q-6482.text: Which of the following vehicles can you overtake if you ride a motorcycle on the road, once you go past this sign?

options.B: A motorcycle with a side car.

q-6482.explanation: Correct answer: C. The ban covers multi-track motor vehicles, so a tractor and a motorcycle with a sidecar may not be overtaken. A moped is a two-wheeled vehicle and is not covered by the ban.

q-6483.text: Which of the following vehicles may enter the road once you go past this sign?

options.B: A three-wheeled motorcycle with symmetrical wheel arrangement.

q-6483.explanation: Correct answer: A. The sign in the material closes the road to motor vehicles and makes an exception solely for two-wheeled motorcycles. A three-wheeled motorcycle and a light quadricycle are not covered by that exception.

q-6484.text: Which of the following vehicles may not enter the road once you go past this sign?

options.C: A motorcycle with a side car.

q-6484.explanation: Correct answer: C. The ban in the material concerns motorcycles, and a motorcycle with a sidecar remains a motorcycle, so it may not enter there. A moped and a light quadricycle do not belong to that group of vehicles.

q-6485.text: If you ride a single-track motorcycle, can you use the lane designated for bicycles?

options.A: Yes, only to the nearest intersection.
options.B: Yes, if I exercise special caution.

q-6485.explanation: Correct answer: C. A cycle lane is intended for bicycles and other vehicles indicated by the rules or a sign; a motorcycle is not among them. Careful riding or a short stretch does not entitle you to use that lane.

q-6488.text: Which of the following speeds can you ride a moped, if you carry a six-year-old child?
q-6488.explanation: Correct answer: C. Carrying a child under seven on a moped is permitted only at a clearly reduced speed, so of the values given only the lowest falls within it. The other speeds are too high.

q-6492.text: What maximum speed can you ride a moped past this sign, if you’re transporting a five-year-old child?
q-6492.explanation: Correct answer: A. The lower of the values is always binding: the limit arising from the sign shown in the material and the reduced limit in force when carrying a child under seven. Here 20 km/h is permitted.

q-6493.text: What's the maximum number of mopeds that can form an organized column?
q-6493.explanation: Correct answer: A. An organised column of mopeds may number at most 10 vehicles. The limit is meant to give other drivers the possibility of overtaking the whole group safely.

q-6494.text: Which of the following vehicles can you overtake when you're riding a light four-wheeled vehicle (microcar, quad) on the road, once you go past this sign?
q-6494.explanation: Correct answer: B. The sign prohibits overtaking multi-track motor vehicles, so a tractor or another quadricycle may not be overtaken. A two-wheeled motorcycle does not belong to that group and may be overtaken.

q-6495.text: Which of the following vehicles can you overtake when you're riding a light four-wheeled vehicle (microcar, quad) on the road, once you go past this sign?

options.B: A motorcycle with a side car.

q-6495.explanation: Correct answer: C. The ban covers multi-track motor vehicles, and an agricultural tractor and a motorcycle with a sidecar are such vehicles. A moped is two-wheeled, so overtaking it remains allowed.

q-6496.text: Which of the following vehicles may enter the road once you go past this sign?
q-6496.explanation: Correct answer: A. The sign in the material closes the road to motor vehicles, and a moped does not belong to that group and may enter. A car and a light quadricycle are motor vehicles, so the ban covers them.

q-6497.text: If you're riding a moped, can you use the lane designated for bicycles?

options.A: Yes, only to the nearest intersection.
options.B: Yes, if I exercise special caution.

q-6497.explanation: Correct answer: C. A cycle lane is intended for bicycles; a moped may use it only when a sign expressly allows it. In the situation in the material there is no such permission, so entering that lane is not permitted.

q-6498.text: If you're riding a moped, can you use the lane designated for bicycles?

options.B: Yes, as long as I give the right of way to cyclists.
options.C: Yes, if I exercise special caution.

q-6498.explanation: Correct answer: A. A moped is not a bicycle, so it may not use a cycle lane unless a sign allows it. Neither declared care nor giving way to cyclists confers such an entitlement.

q-6499.text: Which of the following elements are obligatory equipment on a motorcycle?
q-6499.explanation: Correct answer: A. Every motorcycle must have a working device for giving a sound signal, because it serves to warn other road users. A fire extinguisher and a first-aid kit are not part of its compulsory equipment.

q-6500.text: Which of the following elements are obligatory equipment on a single-track motorcycle whose maximum speed is more than 100 km/h?
q-6500.explanation: Correct answer: C. A two-wheeled motorcycle faster than 100 km/h must have at least two exterior mirrors, because at such speeds watching the road behind the vehicle is particularly important. A fire extinguisher and a triangle are not required for it.

q-6501.text: Must a motorcycle be equipped with emergency lights?
q-6501.explanation: Correct answer: C. A motorcycle does not have to be fitted with hazard lights, but fitting them is allowed. If the vehicle has them, the rider uses them in situations where others must be warned of a danger or of a stop in a dangerous place.

q-6502.text: Which of the following reflectors are obligatory equipment on a motorcycle?
q-6502.explanation: Correct answer: B. A motorcycle must have a rear reflector of a shape other than a triangle. Triangular reflectors are reserved for trailers, so that it can be seen from afar that a combination is being towed behind the vehicle.

q-6503.text: What may be the minimum tread depth of a motorcycle's tyre if it is not equipped with wear indicators?
q-6503.explanation: Correct answer: B. The minimum permitted tread depth is 1.6 mm; below that value the tyre loses its ability to clear water and the vehicle may not be admitted to traffic. The lower values in the answers are not permitted.

q-6504.text: Which of the following elements are obligatory equipment on a motorcycle with a side car?
q-6504.explanation: Correct answer: B. A motorcycle with a sidecar is a multi-track vehicle, so it must carry a warning triangle for marking a vehicle immobilised on the road. A first-aid kit and a fire extinguisher are not compulsory for it.

q-6505.text: What lights may be placed on the side car of a motorcycle?
q-6505.explanation: Correct answer: A. A sidecar may have position lights at the front and rear, because their job is to show the real width of the outfit. Dipped and main-beam headlights stay on the motorcycle itself.

q-6506.text: Which of the following outfits offer the most effective protection in the event a motorcycle falls over?

options.C: Overalls with protective patches, long boots, gloves.

q-6506.explanation: Correct answer: C. A suit with protectors, high boots and gloves protect the joints from impact and the skin from abrasion while sliding along the surface. Ordinary clothes and light footwear give no such protection.

q-6507.text: Do you have to wear a helmet if you ride a motorcycle?

options.B: Yes, unless I ride a motorcycle factory equipped with safety belts.
options.C: No, if I ride any motorcycle with a side car.

q-6507.explanation: Correct answer: B. A motorcyclist must wear a protective helmet, and the only exception concerns a motorcycle factory-fitted with seat belts, where the vehicle's structure provides the protection. A sidecar alone does not release you from this duty.

q-6508.text: Which of the following elements are obligatory equipment on a moped?
q-6508.explanation: Correct answer: A. A moped must have a working device for giving a sound signal, which allows other road users to be warned. A fire extinguisher and a first-aid kit are not part of its compulsory equipment.

q-6509.text: What may be the minimum tread depth of a moped's tyre if it is not equipped with wear indicators?
q-6509.explanation: Correct answer: B. A moped tyre without a wear indicator must have a tread pattern at least 1.6 mm deep. Shallower tread does not clear water from under the wheel and clearly lengthens the braking distance on a wet surface.

q-6510.text: Which of the following elements are obligatory equipment on a moped?

options.C: At least one rear-view mirror on the left.

q-6510.explanation: Correct answer: C. A moped must have at least one rear-view mirror on the left side, giving the rider a view of the road behind the vehicle. A warning triangle and a fire extinguisher belong to a car's equipment, not a two-wheeler's.

q-6512.text: Which of the following reflectors are obligatory equipment on a moped?
q-6512.explanation: Correct answer: B. The compulsory equipment of a moped includes a rear reflector of a shape other than a triangle. The triangular reflector is reserved for trailers, so placing one on a moped would mislead other drivers.

q-6513.text: Which of the following elements are obligatory equipment on a moped?

options.C: White light installed at the front.

q-6513.explanation: Correct answer: C. A moped must have a white light at the front, with which it lights the road and is visible after dusk and in conditions of reduced clarity of the air. A fire extinguisher and a warning triangle are not required for it.

q-6514.text: Which of the following outfits offer the most effective protection in the event of a fall from a moped?

options.C: Overalls with protective patches, long boots, gloves.

q-6514.explanation: Correct answer: C. The most effective protection is a suit with protectors, boots with a high shaft and gloves — the protectors absorb impacts to the joints, and the tough material prevents extensive abrasions. Ordinary clothes and light footwear wear through at the first contact with the surface.

q-6515.text: What is the main factor determining the braking distance of a motorcycle?

options.C: The type of surface on which the vehicle is moving.

q-6515.explanation: Correct answer: C. The braking distance is decided above all by grip, and that is determined by the type and state of the surface. Reaction time lengthens the whole stopping distance but not the braking itself, and electronic systems cannot create more grip than the road provides.

q-6516.text: Approximately, how much does the braking distance of a motorcycle increase if its speed doubles?
q-6516.explanation: Correct answer: C. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed, so doubling it makes that distance roughly four times longer. That is why a seemingly small excess of speed considerably moves the point at which the motorcycle is able to stop.

q-6518.text: What distance should you keep from a vehicle in front of you if you ride a motorcycle in a built-up area?

options.B: A distance necessary to avoid a crash in the event of the preceeding vehicle stopping.
options.C: A distance corresponding to the length of the motorcycle.

q-6518.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a built-up area the rules give no metres: the distance must be such as to avoid a collision if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It is chosen according to speed, visibility and the state of the surface.

q-6519.text: What distance should you keep while riding a motorcycle and overtaking a vehicle outside a built-up area?

options.A: At least 2 m while overtaking a pedestrian.
options.B: At least 2 m while overtaking a cyclist.
options.C: At least 1 m while overtaking another motorcycle.

q-6519.explanation: Correct answer: C. When overtaking a two-wheeler, the driver must keep a safe distance of no less than 1 m, not 2 m. The same minimum distance applies to a bicycle, a moped and a pedestrian walking on the verge.

q-6520.text: What's the minimum distance between moving motorcycle columns?
q-6520.explanation: Correct answer: C. Columns of motorcycles travelling on the same road must be separated by at least 500 m. Thanks to that gap another driver can overtake one column and calmly return to their lane before the next.

q-6521.text: What minimum distance should you keep from the vehicle in front of you when you get stucked in a traffic jam in a tunnel?
q-6521.explanation: Correct answer: B. Standing in a traffic jam in a tunnel, the driver must keep a distance of at least 5 m from the vehicle ahead. That free space makes it easier to evacuate people and for the rescue services to get through in the event of a fire.

q-6522.text: While riding a motorcycle, when should you start braking if you intend to go round a sharp bend on the road?

options.B: When I come out of the bend.
options.C: Sufficiently in advance in order to avoid braking while I'm turning.

q-6522.explanation: Correct answer: C. Braking should be finished before entering the curve, because in a leaning motorcycle the tyres' grip is already being used to hold the line. Braking further in the curve easily ends in a skid or running off the bend.

q-6523.text: What should the position of the motorcycle be in order to achieve optimum effectiveness of braking?
q-6523.explanation: Correct answer: A. The greatest braking force can be transmitted when the motorcycle is upright and travelling straight — all the tyres' grip then serves to stop. When leaning, part of the grip is taken up by the lateral force, and the wheel locks sooner.

q-6524.text: What should you do while riding a motorcycle, immediately before you enter a sharp bend?

options.A: Adjust the speed in such a way as to avoid braking while I'm turning.
options.B: Accelerate in order to take advantage of the centrifugal force.
options.C: Go as close as possible to the edge of the road in order to use the whole width of the road while turning.

q-6524.explanation: Correct answer: A. Speed is chosen before the curve so that it can be ridden without braking. Accelerating increases the centrifugal force pushing the motorcycle outwards, and moving towards the left edge of the carriageway puts it under oncoming vehicles.

q-6525.text: What distance should you keep from a vehicle in front of you if you ride a moped in a built-up area?

options.B: A distance necessary to avoid a crash in the event that the vehicle in front of me stops.
options.C: A distance corresponding to twice the length of the moped.

q-6525.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a built-up area the distance is not expressed in metres — it must be enough to avoid a collision if the vehicle in front brakes suddenly. The moped rider chooses it according to speed, visibility and the grip of the surface.

q-6526.text: While riding a moped, when should you start braking if you intend to go round a sharp bend on the road?

options.B: When I come out of the bend.
options.C: Sufficiently in advance in order to avoid braking while I'm turning.

q-6526.explanation: Correct answer: C. The moped should be slowed down before the curve, because when leaning the grip of the narrow tyres is already used up on steering through the bend. Braking during the curve leads to the wheel sliding and the two-wheeler falling over.

q-6527.text: What is the main factor determining the braking distance of a moped?

options.A: The quantity of fuel in the tank.
options.C: The type of surface on which the vehicle is moving.

q-6527.explanation: Correct answer: C. The braking distance is decided by the grip of the tyres on the surface, that is, its type and state. On a wet, sandy or icy carriageway a moped will stop much further on than on dry asphalt, regardless of the amount of fuel and the size of the vehicle.

q-6528.text: Approximately, how does the braking distance of a moped increase if its speed doubles?
q-6528.explanation: Correct answer: C. The braking distance depends on the square of the speed, so doubling it makes that distance roughly four times longer. This rule applies to every vehicle, including a light moped of low mass.

q-6529.text: What factor should you particularly pay attention to while riding a moped, in order to keep a proper distance from the vehicle in front of you?

options.A: The condition of the surface of the road.
options.C: The speed limit applicable along the given section of the road.

q-6529.explanation: Correct answer: A. A safe distance follows above all from grip, and that is determined by the state of the surface — on a wet, muddy or loose carriageway a moped takes clearly longer to brake. Engine power and the speed limit in force do not shorten the braking distance.

q-6530.text: What distance should you keep while riding a moped and overtaking a vehicle outside a built-up area?
q-6530.explanation: Correct answer: C. When overtaking a two-wheeler, a safe distance of no less than 1 m applies, not 2 m. The same value applies to a bicycle, a motorcycle and a pedestrian moving along the verge.

q-6531.text: What's the minimum distance between moving moped columns?
q-6531.explanation: Correct answer: A. The distance between moving columns of mopeds may not be less than 200 m. That gap lets other drivers overtake a single column and return safely to their lane.

q-6532.text: What's the minimum distance you should maintain from the vehicle in front of you when you get stucked in a traffic jam in a tunnel?
q-6532.explanation: Correct answer: B. Stopping in a tunnel because of a traffic jam, the driver keeps at least 5 m from the vehicle ahead. The free space allows pulling out from between the vehicles and makes access easier for the rescue services.

q-6533.text: What should the position of a moped be in order to achieve the optimum effectiveness of braking?
q-6533.explanation: Correct answer: A. A moped brakes most effectively when upright and travelling straight — all the tyres' grip can then be devoted to shedding speed. When leaning, part of the grip is taken up by steering through the curve, and the wheel locks sooner.

q-6534.text: What should you do while riding a moped, immediately before you enter a sharp bend?

options.A: Adjust the speed in such a way as to avoid braking while I'm turning.
options.B: Accelerate in order to take advantage of the centrifugal force.
options.C: Go as close as possible to the edge of the road in order to use the whole width of the road while turning.

q-6534.explanation: Correct answer: A. Speed must be reduced before the bend, so that it can be ridden smoothly, without braking. The centrifugal force does not help through the curve but pushes the vehicle outwards, and riding at the edge of the carriageway removes the room to correct the line.

q-6535.text: How should you cross a railway line on a motorcycle?

options.A: At an angle close to a straight angle.
options.B: At an acute angle, regardless of the position of the railway line in relation to the road.
options.C: By changing the gear to a higher one, in order to accelerate.

q-6535.explanation: Correct answer: A. Rails are crossed at an angle close to a right angle, so that the wheel does not fall into the rail groove and slide along the smooth steel. Cutting across a tramway at a slant, especially on a wet surface, risks losing grip and the motorcycle falling over.

q-6536.text: Can riding a motorcycle on road markings be dangerous?

options.B: Yes, road markings may be slippery regardless of weather conditions.
options.C: Yes, but only during a rainfall.

q-6536.explanation: Correct answer: B. The paint and compound that road markings are made of have less grip than asphalt, even when dry and clean. For a two-wheeler this means a risk of skidding when braking, accelerating and leaning.

q-6538.text: How should you brake if you ride a motorcycle in a mountainous area?

options.A: By using only the rear-wheel brake.
options.B: By using only the front-wheel brake.
options.C: By using both brakes and braking with the engine.

q-6538.explanation: Correct answer: C. On long descents both brakes are combined with engine braking in a lower gear. The engine takes over part of the work, so the discs and linings do not overheat and the brakes stay effective to the end of the descent.

q-6539.text: How should you ride a motorcycle on a dirt road?

options.A: By raising yourself lightly on the footrests.
options.B: By moving as far away from the handlebar as possible.
options.C: By speeding up, in order to improve the stability of the motorcycle.

q-6539.explanation: Correct answer: A. Rising slightly on the footpegs lowers the centre of gravity of the rider–motorcycle system and lets the legs absorb bumps, so the machine holds its line more easily. Moving away from the handlebars and accelerating on loose ground only worsen control of the vehicle.

q-6540.text: How should you go over a drain when riding a moped?

options.A: By avoiding riding over the metal elements of the drain.
options.B: By riding as close as possible to the middle of the metal elements.
options.C: By braking while going over the drain.

q-6540.explanation: Correct answer: A. Metal manhole covers have much less grip than asphalt, especially when wet or dirty. It is safest to avoid them, and if that is impossible — to cross them straight, without braking and without leaning the two-wheeler.

q-6541.text: How should you cross a railway line on a moped?

options.A: At an angle close to a straight angle.
options.B: At an acute angle, regardless of the position of the railway line in relation to the road.
options.C: By changing the gear to a higher one, in order to accelerate.

q-6541.explanation: Correct answer: A. Tracks are crossed at an angle close to a right angle, so that the moped's narrow wheel does not fall into the rail groove and slide along the smooth steel. Riding at a slant across rails, especially wet ones, often ends in loss of grip and a fall.

q-6542.text: Can riding a moped on road markings be dangerous?

options.B: Yes, road markings may be slippery regardless of weather conditions.

q-6542.explanation: Correct answer: B. The surface of road markings is smoother than asphalt and has less grip even when dry. A light moped on narrow tyres loses grip on it particularly easily — when braking, moving off and in a bend.

q-6543.text: How should you brake if you ride a moped in a mountainous area?

options.A: By using only the rear-wheel brake.
options.B: By using only the front-wheel brake.
options.C: By using both brakes and braking with the engine.

q-6543.explanation: Correct answer: C. In mountainous terrain on long descents both brakes are used together with engine braking. Thanks to that the braking system does not overheat, and speed stays under control on the following steep stretches too.

q-6544.text: How should you ride a moped on a dirt road?

options.A: By raising yourself lightly on the footrests.
options.B: By moving as far away from the handlebar as possible.
options.C: The same way as on a hard road, with a dry and clean surface.

q-6544.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a loose surface the wheels change their line, so the rider rises slightly on the footpegs — the legs then work like additional suspension, and the vehicle keeps its balance more easily. Riding technique on unmade ground differs from riding on a dry paved road.

q-6545.text: If you ride on a motorway and are not performing any manoeuvres, should you observe the road behind the motorcycle?

options.B: Yes, by looking in the mirrors.
options.C: Yes, by turning the head in order to observe it directly.

q-6545.explanation: Correct answer: B. The situation behind is checked continuously in the mirrors, even when no manoeuvre is being carried out — on a motorway vehicles close in very fast. Turning the head at high speed takes the eyes off the road ahead of the motorcycle.

q-6546.text: What may limit your field of vision when you ride a motorcycle?
q-6546.explanation: Correct answer: A. A badly chosen helmet and goggles narrow the field of vision, especially to the sides, so the rider notices vehicles approaching from the side later. The visor and lenses must also be kept clean, because scratches scatter light and dazzle after dark.

q-6547.text: Where do you look when turning on a motorcycle?

options.A: At the road straight ahead of the front wheel.
options.C: In the direction you intend to go.

q-6547.explanation: Correct answer: C. A two-wheeler goes where the rider looks, so the eyes are directed deep into the bend, at the exit of the curve. Looking just in front of the wheel shortens the field of observation and causes nervous, late corrections of the line.

q-6548.text: When you're changing lanes, how should you observe the surrounding area?

options.A: By turning my head in order to observe the road directly behind the motorcycle.
options.B: By looking in the mirrors, which allow you to see the road behind the motorcycle.
options.C: By looking in the mirrors and turning the head slightly in order to eliminate the so-called "blind spot".

q-6548.explanation: Correct answer: C. Mirrors do not show the whole area to the side and behind, so before changing lane a glance in the mirrors is combined with a brief turn of the head. Turning the head alone, in turn, removes control over what is happening ahead.

q-6549.text: If you approach a railway crossing on a motorcycle, how will you make sure that a train is not approaching?

options.A: By looking ahead and observing the railway line out of the corner of my eye.
options.B: By turning the head and observing the railway line directly.
options.C: By holding my head straight and moving my eyes only.

q-6549.explanation: Correct answer: B. Before a level crossing you must turn your head and look along the tracks in both directions, because peripheral vision judges the speed of an approaching train poorly. The helmet additionally limits the field of vision, so moving the eyes alone is not enough.

q-6550.text: If you ride outside a built-up area and you do not make any manoeuvres, should you observe the road behind your moped?

options.B: Yes, by looking in the mirrors.
options.C: Yes, by turning your head in order to see it directly.

q-6550.explanation: Correct answer: B. A moped is slower than most vehicles, so outside a built-up area the rider regularly checks in the mirror who is catching up and intends to overtake. Turning the head on a busy road takes away attention needed ahead.

q-6552.text: What may limit your field of vision when you ride a moped?
q-6552.explanation: Correct answer: A. The field of vision is limited by what is directly in front of the eyes: an ill-fitting helmet and unsuitable goggles narrow side vision. The size of the vehicle and the cut of clothing do not block the view of the road.

q-6553.text: Where do you look when turning on a moped?

options.A: At the road straight ahead of the front wheel.
options.C: In the direction you intend to go.

q-6553.explanation: Correct answer: C. The eyes are directed where you intend to go — a two-wheeler naturally follows the gaze, and the rider sees obstacles on their line earlier. Looking at the wheel or the instruments deprives them of that information at the most important moment.

q-6554.text: If you approach a railway crossing on a moped, how will you make sure that a train is not approaching?

options.A: By looking ahead and observing the railway line out of the corner of my eye.
options.B: By turning your head and observing the railway line directly.
options.C: By holding my head straight and moving my eyes only.

q-6554.explanation: Correct answer: B. You can make sure only by looking along the tracks in both directions, that is, by turning your head. Seeing out of the corner of the eye does not allow the distance or speed of a train to be judged, and the crossing may be crossed only when nothing is approaching.

q-6555.text: What may happen if you start moving and you release the clutch too abruptly?

options.A: The front wheel will go up or the engine will stall.
options.B: You will be thrust forward on the seat.
options.C: The front wheel will have better traction.

q-6555.explanation: Correct answer: A. Dropping the clutch suddenly transfers the whole torque to the rear wheel at once: at high revs the front of the motorcycle lifts, and at revs that are too low the engine stalls. Moving off requires smoothly combining the clutch with adding throttle.

q-6556.text: Where is the neutral position most commonly found in motorcycles equipped with a manual gear box?

options.B: Between the first and second gear.
options.C: Between the fifth and fourth gear.

q-6556.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a typical sequential motorcycle gearbox, neutral lies between first and second gear, at half the lever's travel. That is why before stopping it is selected with a gentle upward movement from first, and its engagement is confirmed by the indicator light.

q-6557.text: When riding a motorcycle, how can you achieve an engine braking effect?

options.A: By reducing acceleration and not using the clutch.

q-6557.explanation: Correct answer: A. Engine braking works only while the wheel remains connected to the engine, that is, after closing the throttle without squeezing the clutch lever. Pulling in the clutch or selecting neutral breaks that connection and the vehicle coasts on under its momentum.

q-6558.text: How will you brake on a wet surface?

options.A: Using the front and rear brakes.
options.B: By using the engine and my feet.
options.C: By using the rear wheel brake.

q-6558.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a slippery surface too you brake with both brakes at the same time, only more gently and earlier, because the braking force is then spread over two wheels. Using one brake overloads it and locks the wheel sooner.

q-6559.text: What will happen if, while braking on a motorcycle, the anti-lock braking system is initiated (ABS)?

options.A: This will help me to reduce the braking distance in all circumstances.
options.B: This will help me to bypass obstacles without releasing the brake.

q-6559.explanation: Correct answer: B. ABS does not let the wheels lock, so the front wheel keeps rolling and the motorcycle stays steerable — you can steer round an obstacle without easing off the brake. On loose or uneven ground, however, the braking distance with ABS can be longer.

q-6561.text: How will you behave if you are engaged in an overtaking manoeuvre on a motorcycle?

options.A: I will change the gear to a higher one in order to achieve better acceleration.
options.B: I will set a speed that will allow me travel along the opposite lane for as long as possible.
options.C: In the event of a potential danger, I will refrain from this manoeuvre.

q-6561.explanation: Correct answer: C. Overtaking may be started only when there is no doubt whatsoever about safety; at any sign of danger the manoeuvre is not undertaken. A higher gear weakens acceleration, and prolonging travel in the opposite lane increases the risk of a head-on collision.

q-6562.text: What should you do before you carry a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.A: I will reduce the stiffness of the suspension.
options.B: I will instruct the passenger as to how he should behave on a motorcycle.
options.C: I will reduce the air pressure in the tyres.

q-6562.explanation: Correct answer: B. A passenger affects the balance of a two-wheeler, so before the ride they must be told how to get on, where to keep their feet and hands and to lean together with the motorcycle. The extra load calls rather for firmer suspension and correct tyre pressure.

q-6563.text: How should you brake on a wet surface?

options.A: With the front and rear whee brakes.
options.B: By using the engine and my feet.
options.C: By using the rear wheel brake only.

q-6563.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a slippery surface a moped is braked with both brakes at once, gently and early enough, so that the braking force is spread over both wheels. Bracing with the feet does not stop the vehicle and risks injury to the legs.

q-6566.text: What should you do before you carry a passenger on a moped?

options.A: I will reduce the stiffness of the suspension.
options.B: I will instruct the passenger how he should behave on a moped.
options.C: I will reduce the air pressure in the tyres.

q-6566.explanation: Correct answer: B. A passenger changes the balance of a moped, so before the ride they must be told how to get on, where to rest their feet and hands and that they lean together with the vehicle. Lowering tyre pressure and softening the suspension only worsen the handling.

q-6567.text: When you ride a motorcycle with a side car, can you carry a passenger who has consumed alcohol?
q-6567.explanation: Correct answer: A. The ban on carrying a person after alcohol consumption concerns a two-wheeler, because a passenger on the pillion seat has a share in the vehicle's balance. In a sidecar such a person does not affect the stability of the outfit, so carrying them is permitted.

q-6568.text: If you ride a motorcycle that is not factory equipped with safety belts, can you carry a passenger without a helmet?
q-6568.explanation: Correct answer: C. If the motorcycle has no factory-fitted seat belts, both the rider and the passenger carried must wear a protective helmet — the one in the sidecar too. Without a helmet, carrying a person is not permitted, regardless of distance and speed.

q-6569.text: How should you transport a ten-year-old child on a two-seat motorcycle?

options.A: Wearing a helmet, on the passenger's seat.
options.B: In front of me, on the fuel tank.
options.C: Between myself and another adult passenger.

q-6569.explanation: Correct answer: A. A child is carried in a protective helmet, on the passenger seat intended for it and only when its feet reach the footrests. A two-seat motorcycle may carry one such person, so a place on the fuel tank or between two people is ruled out.

q-6571.text: What's the maximum length of a combination vehicle consisting of a motorcycle and a trailer?
q-6571.explanation: Correct answer: B. A combination of a motorcycle and a trailer may be no longer than 4 m. A longer combination would be hard to control when turning and turning round, and with the mass of the towing vehicle also unstable.

q-6573.text: Which of the following conditions should be met by a trailer pulled by the motorcycle?

options.A: It should be marked with a red flag.
options.B: It should have its own registration plate with a number different than the registration plate of the motorcycle.
options.C: It should be equipped with the registration plate transferred from the motorcycle.

q-6573.explanation: Correct answer: C. A trailer towed by a motorcycle has no separate number — the number plate transferred from the motorcycle is placed at its rear, because the vehicle's own plate is then hidden. A flag does not replace registration marking.

q-6575.text: How can you place a load transported on a moped?

options.A: In such a way that it partially obscures the registration plate.
options.C: In such a way that it obscures the rear position light.

q-6575.explanation: Correct answer: B. The load must be fastened so that it can neither shift nor fall off, because a shift of weight immediately upsets the balance of a two-wheeler. The lights and the number plate must not be covered either.

q-6576.text: When you ride a moped, can you transport a passenger that has consumed alcohol?

options.B: Yes, on the back seat of the moped.
options.C: Yes, as long as you don't travel at a speed of more than 20 km/h.

q-6576.explanation: Correct answer: A. A person after alcohol consumption may not be carried on a moped in any circumstances. A passenger on a two-wheeler shares in keeping the balance, and impaired coordination risks the vehicle falling over; reducing speed does not lift this ban.

q-6577.text: If you ride a moped, can you carry a passenger without a helmet?

options.B: Yes, if I travel at a low speed.

q-6577.explanation: Correct answer: C. On a moped both the rider and the passenger must wear a protective helmet — without exception. Even a fall at low speed ends with the head striking the surface, and a helmet is the only real protection in such a situation.

q-6578.text: What must you not allow a passenger to do when you transport him on a moped?

options.A: To talk on a mobile telephone.

q-6578.explanation: Correct answer: C. A moped passenger may not ride without a protective helmet; the duty to wear one covers them just as it does the rider. Talking to the rider or using their own phone is not prohibited for a passenger.

q-6579.text: How can you place a load transported on a motorcycle?

options.A: In such a way that it partially obscures the registration plate.
options.C: In such a way that it obscures the rear position light.

q-6579.explanation: Correct answer: B. A carried load is secured against shifting and falling off, because even a small shift of mass changes the motorcycle's behaviour in a bend and under braking. Covering the number plate and the lights is prohibited.

q-6580.text: What must you mostly pay attention to when you secure a load being transported on a motorcycle?

options.A: That it is fixed in such a way that it does not affect the stability of the motorcycle.
options.B: To providing an easy access to its contents while riding.
options.C: That it is fixed in such a way that it reduces air resistance.

q-6580.explanation: Correct answer: A. A load is fastened above all so as not to impair the motorcycle's stability — low, close to the vehicle's axis and symmetrically. Reaching into the luggage while riding is not acceptable, and aerodynamics is of secondary importance here.

q-6581.text: Can you tow another motorcycle with your motorcycle?

options.A: Yes, by using a flexible coupling providing for easy disconnection.
options.B: Yes, by using a flexible coupling excluding a possibility of disconnection.
options.C: Yes, by means of a rigid coupling that allows for easy disconnection.

q-6581.explanation: Correct answer: A. A motorcycle is towed only on a flexible connection that can be released quickly — if either vehicle loses balance, the rope must let go at once. A rigid connection between two two-wheelers is not permitted.

q-6582.text: Is it permitted to tow a motorcycle?

options.A: Yes, if you use a rigid coupling preventing disconnection during the journey.
options.C: Yes, if you use a flexible coupling providing for easy disconnection.

q-6582.explanation: Correct answer: C. Towing a motorcycle is allowed, but only on a flexible connection that can easily be released. The rider of the towed two-wheeler must be able to free themselves immediately when they begin to lose balance.

q-6583.text: What should you mainly pay attention to when you fill up a motorcycle with fuel?

options.A: That I do not fill up more than 3/4 of the capacity of the tank.
options.B: That I do not spill fuel on the hot engine or hot elements of the exhaustion system.
options.C: That the engine of the motorcycle is switched on.

q-6583.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a motorcycle the tank sits just above the engine and close to the exhaust, so spilt petrol lands on hot parts and may ignite. That is why you refuel with the engine off and take care that fuel does not overflow the filler.

q-6584.text: When you ride a single-track motorcycle, can you transport a passenger who has consumed alcohol?

options.A: Yes, if in my opinion he shows proper co-ordination of his motion.
options.B: Yes, if I reduce speed to 40 km/h.

q-6584.explanation: Correct answer: C. A person after alcohol consumption may not be carried on a two-wheeled motorcycle. The rider's own assessment does not replace this ban, and a speed limit does not lift it — a passenger with impaired coordination can tip the vehicle at the worst moment.

q-6585.text: If you ride a single-track motorcycle, can you transport a passenger who is intoxicated?

options.B: Yes, if I reduce speed to 40 km/h.
options.C: Yes, if in my opinion he shows proper co-ordination of his motion.

q-6585.explanation: Correct answer: A. An intoxicated person may not be carried on a two-wheeled motorcycle in any variant. Such a passenger does not control their own movements and shifts their body weight independently of the rider, which risks the vehicle falling over.

q-6586.text: If you ride a moped, can you transport a passenger who is intoxicated?

options.B: Yes, if I reduce speed to 20 km/h.
options.C: Yes, if in my opinion he shows proper co-ordination of motion.

q-6586.explanation: Correct answer: A. An intoxicated person may not be carried on a moped. The balance of a two-wheeler also depends on the passenger, and their unpredictable movements can topple the vehicle; neither slow riding nor the rider's own judgement lifts this ban.

q-6587.text: Which of the following activities are forbidden when you ride a moped?

options.B: Using a mobile telephone while riding, if this requires holding the phone in my hand.

q-6587.explanation: Correct answer: B. While riding you may not use a phone that has to be held in the hand — the moped rider then loses one hand on the handlebars and control of the throttle or brake. A hands-free kit is not prohibited.

q-6588.text: What's the maximum length of a combination vehicle consisting of a moped and a trailer?
q-6588.explanation: Correct answer: B. A combination of a moped and a trailer may be at most 4 m long. With so light a towing vehicle, a longer trailer would begin to dictate the line of travel, especially under braking and in bends.

q-6589.text: What must you mostly pay attention to when you secure a load to be transported on a moped?

options.A: That it is fixed in such a way that it does not affect the stability of the moped.
options.B: To provide easy access to its contents while riding.
options.C: That it is fixed in such a way that it reduces air resistance.

q-6589.explanation: Correct answer: A. With so light a vehicle every badly placed weight changes its behaviour, so the load is fastened low and symmetrically so as not to impair the moped's stability. Access to the luggage while riding and aerodynamics are irrelevant here.

q-6590.text: What should you mainly pay attention to when you fill up a moped with fuel?

options.A: That I do not fill up more than 3/4 of the capacity of the tank.
options.B: That I do not spill fuel on the hot engine or hot elements of the exhaustion system.
options.C: That the engine is turned on.

q-6590.explanation: Correct answer: B. Petrol spilt on a hot engine or silencer evaporates and may ignite, so you refuel carefully and with the engine off. The tank is filled to the level provided for by the manufacturer, not to an arbitrary fraction of its capacity.

q-6592.text: Within what period of time are you obliged to notify the starost's office of purchasing a previously registered motorcycle?
q-6592.explanation: Correct answer: A. The owner notifies the starosta of the acquisition of a registered motorcycle within 30 days of the purchase. The notification updates the data in the register, so that responsibility for the vehicle passes to the new owner.

q-6594.text: Within what period of time are you obliged to notify the starost office of a change of circumstances requiring an amendment to the vehicle registration card?
q-6594.explanation: Correct answer: C. A change of circumstances requiring the data in the registration document to be corrected is reported to the starosta within 30 days. This concerns, for example, a change of the owner's address or structural changes to the vehicle.

q-6595.text: If you're the owner of a registered motorcycle, within what period of time are you required to perform the periodic technical inspection?

options.A: Before the lapse of a check-up deadline, as specified in the registration card.
options.B: Every time, after the lapse of 6 months from the previous check-up.
options.C: Every 3 years, regardless of the date of the first registration.

q-6595.explanation: Correct answer: A. The technical inspection must be carried out no later than the day entered in the registration document as the date of the next inspection. After that date the vehicle is not admitted to traffic, and a roadside check may retain the registration document.

q-6599.text: Which of the following vehicles can you ride when you hold an A-category driving licence?

options.A: A motorcycle with a side car.
options.B: A four-wheeled motor vehicle whose kerb weight does not exceed 550 kg.

q-6599.explanation: Correct answer: A. Category A entitles you to drive any motorcycle, including a combination of a motorcycle and a sidecar. A quadricycle and a slow-moving vehicle require other entitlements, so category A alone is not enough to drive them.

q-6604.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive when you hold an A1-category driving licence?

options.A: A three-wheeled motorcycle whose power does not exceed 15 kW.
options.B: A four-wheeled motor vehicle whose kerb weight does not exceed 550 kg.

q-6604.explanation: Correct answer: A. Category A1 covers three-wheeled motorcycles with a power not exceeding 15 kW. A quadricycle with an unladen mass of 550 kg and a slow-moving vehicle do not fall within these entitlements and require another category of driving licence.

q-6605.text: What's the maximum displacement of the engine of a motorcycle that you can ride holding an A1-category driving licence?
q-6605.explanation: Correct answer: A. A category A1 driving licence allows you to ride a motorcycle with an engine capacity of up to 125 cm³. A motorcycle with a larger capacity requires category A2 or A, depending on its power and power-to-weight ratio.

q-6606.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive if you hold an A1-category driving licence?
q-6606.explanation: Correct answer: C. Every driving-licence category covering motorcycles also confers the entitlement to ride a moped, so a holder of category A1 may ride a moped. A slow-moving vehicle and any quadricycle remain outside these entitlements.

q-6608.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive when you hold an A2-category driving licence?

options.A: A three-wheeled motorcycle whose power does not exceed 15 kW.
options.B: A four-wheeled motor vehicle (microcar, quad) whose kerb weight does not exceed 550 kg.

q-6608.explanation: Correct answer: A. Category A2 includes the entitlements of category A1, and therefore also a three-wheeled motorcycle with a power not exceeding 15 kW. A quadricycle with an unladen mass of 550 kg and a slow-moving vehicle require entirely different categories.

q-6609.text: What's the maximum power of the engine of a motorcycle that you can ride if you hold an A2-category driving licence?
q-6609.explanation: Correct answer: A. Category A2 allows you to ride a motorcycle with a power of up to 35 kW, with the power-to-unladen-mass ratio also limited. A more powerful motorcycle requires full category A.

q-6610.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive if you hold an A2-category driving licence?
q-6610.explanation: Correct answer: C. Motorcycle entitlements also cover riding a moped, so a holder of category A2 may ride a moped. A slow-moving vehicle and any quadricycle remain outside the scope of this category.

q-6613.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive when you hold an AM-category driving licence?
q-6613.explanation: Correct answer: C. Category AM entitles you to drive a moped and a light quadricycle, that is, a vehicle of small unladen mass and limited power. A three-wheeled motorcycle and the other quadricycles require higher categories.

q-6614.text: What's the maximum engine power of an electric moped that you can ride if you hold an AM-category driving licence?
q-6614.explanation: Correct answer: B. An electrically powered moped may have a motor with a power of no more than 4 kW. A vehicle with a more powerful motor is no longer a moped, and category AM is not enough to drive it.

q-6617.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive if you hold an AM-category driving licence?
q-6617.explanation: Correct answer: B. Category AM covers a moped and a light quadricycle. A three-wheeled motorcycle and any quadricycle without mass and power limits go beyond these entitlements and require a higher category of driving licence.

q-6618.text: Which of the following vehicles can you ride when you hold an AM-category driving licence?
q-6618.explanation: Correct answer: B. Category AM allows you to drive a light quadricycle and, among scooters, only those that meet the conditions for a moped. A scooter of larger capacity or power and a three-wheeled motorcycle require a motorcycle category.

q-6619.text: What's the maximum displacement of a combustion engine of a moped that you can ride when you hold an AM-category driving licence?
q-6619.explanation: Correct answer: B. A moped with a combustion engine has a capacity not exceeding 50 cm³ and a limited design speed. A vehicle with a larger capacity is already a motorcycle and requires the appropriate category of driving licence.

q-6620.text: What can you use this switch for?

options.A: To turn on the high-beam lights of the motorcycle.

q-6620.explanation: Correct answer: B. The switch shown in the material is for switching off the engine in an emergency without reaching for the ignition. The rider may use it in a situation of danger or after the vehicle has fallen over, when the engine must be stopped immediately.

q-6621.text: When should you regulate the tension of the drive chain of the motorcycle?

options.A: According to the manufacturer's recommendations, regardless of whether or not it's too loose.
options.B: Immediately after you determine that it's too loose.
options.C: No more frequently than every 10,000 km.

q-6621.explanation: Correct answer: B. Excessive chain slack must be removed as soon as it is found, because a loose chain can come off or lock the rear wheel. The manufacturer's recommendations set the check intervals but do not excuse you from reacting to a fault you have noticed.

q-6622.text: What may weaken the effectiveness of the front braking system of the motorcycle?

options.A: A change in the level of the brake fluid within max/min norms of the fluid reservoir.
options.B: Leakage of brake fluid from a brake line.
options.C: Pressing the brake with excessive strength.

q-6622.explanation: Correct answer: B. The braking system works on fluid pressure, so any leak from a pipe reduces braking effectiveness up to a complete loss of the brake. Changes in the fluid level within the normal range and firm pressure at the lever are normal phenomena.

q-6623.text: Which of the following activities should you perform before you start riding a motorcycle?

options.A: Visually check the condition of the tyres.
options.C: Check the level of electrolyte in the battery.

q-6623.explanation: Correct answer: A. Before riding, a quick visual check is made, and the state of the tyres is the most important thing here, because a motorcycle rests on two small contact patches with the road. Adjusting the lights and checking the electrolyte are periodic servicing tasks.

q-6624.text: What should you do if the oil pressure control light comes on while you're riding a motorcycle?

options.A: I will stop and turn off the engine.
options.B: I will stop and leave the engine running in the neutral gear.
options.C: I will continue riding without overloading the engine.

q-6624.explanation: Correct answer: A. A lit oil-pressure light means there is no proper lubrication, and keeping the engine running risks seizing it. Pull over to a safe place, switch off the engine and establish the cause before continuing.

q-6625.text: What should you first of all do before you set off on a long journey on a motorcycle?

options.C: Check the level of the brake fluid.

q-6625.explanation: Correct answer: C. Before a longer trip you check above all the items responsible for safety, and the brake fluid level decides the effectiveness of braking. The air filter and the spark plug affect the engine's running, not the ability to stop the vehicle.

q-6626.text: What may be the consequence of insufficient air pressure in the tyres?

options.A: An improvement of control over the vehicle while turning.
options.B: An increased durability of the tyres.

q-6626.explanation: Correct answer: C. Too low a pressure deforms the tyre, so its tread does not sit evenly on the surface and grip falls. The vehicle responds more sluggishly to the handlebars, and the tyre wears and overheats faster.

q-6627.text: What can you use this switch for?

options.C: To turn on the emergency lights of the motorcycle.

q-6627.explanation: Correct answer: A. The switch shown in the material is the engine cut-off switch, placed within reach of the thumb so that it can be used without letting go of the handlebars. Gears are changed with the foot lever, and the hazard lights have their own switch.

q-6628.text: What may be the cause of the need to frequently adjust the tension of the drive chain of the motorcycle?

options.A: If you frequently drive at high speeds.
options.B: If you frequently drive at low speeds.

q-6628.explanation: Correct answer: C. Sharp acceleration puts large, jerky forces on the chain, which stretch its links and wear the sprockets faster. So with such a riding style the tension must be checked and adjusted more often than usual.

q-6629.text: What may be the consequence of insufficient air pressure in the tyres?

options.A: An improvement of vehicle handling while turning.
options.B: An increased durability of the tyres.

q-6629.explanation: Correct answer: C. Too low a pressure deforms the tyre, so its tread does not sit evenly on the surface and grip falls. The vehicle responds more sluggishly to the handlebars, and the tyre wears and overheats faster.

q-6630.text: What should you do before you check the oil level in the engine?

options.A: Put a moped on the side rest.
options.C: Switch off the engine and wait a few minutes.

q-6630.explanation: Correct answer: C. Oil distributed around a running engine must drain back to the sump, so the measurement is taken after switching off the engine and waiting a few minutes. The vehicle should stand level, because a tilt falsifies the reading.

q-6631.text: What may weaken the effectiveness of the front braking system of a moped?

options.A: A change in the level of the brake fluid within max/min norms of the fluid reservoir.
options.B: Leakage of brake fluid from a brake line.
options.C: Pressing the brake with excessive strength.

q-6631.explanation: Correct answer: B. A hydraulic brake works on fluid pressure, so a leaking pipe reduces braking effectiveness, and with a larger leak the brake may stop working altogether. Fluctuations of the level within the normal range are not a fault.

q-6632.text: Which of the following activities should you perform before you start riding a moped?

options.A: Visually check the condition of the tyres.
options.C: Check the level of electrolyte in the battery.

q-6632.explanation: Correct answer: A. Before every ride a short visual inspection is enough, in which the state of the tyres is the most important: their damage or too low pressure directly threatens the stability of a two-wheeler. Adjusting the lights and checking the electrolyte belong to periodic servicing.

q-6633.text: What should you first of all do before you set off on a long journey on a moped?

options.C: Check the level of the brake fluid.

q-6633.explanation: Correct answer: C. First you check what safety depends on, that is, the brake fluid level, because its loss weakens braking. The air filter and the spark plug affect only the engine's running and performance.

q-6635.text: What should you do with a victim who probably broke his leg in an accident?

options.A: I should temporarily immobilize the fracture by tying both legs together and wait for the ambulance.
options.B: I should make fracture-stabilizing rails with any material (e.g. wood panels) and take the victim to hospital.
options.C: I do not have to stabilize the leg, but I should take the victim to hospital.

q-6635.explanation: Correct answer: A. A broken lower limb is most simply immobilised by tying it to the healthy leg, which limits movement of the fragments and the pain. The casualty is not transported in your own vehicle; you wait for the emergency medical team.

q-6636.text: When should you cease any resuscitation activities towards a person who is a victim of an accident?

options.A: In the event of a broken rib.
options.B: After the restoration of life functions (pulse, breathing).

q-6636.explanation: Correct answer: B. Resuscitation is continued without breaks until breathing and circulation return or the casualty is taken over by rescuers. A rib broken during chest compressions happens often and is no reason to stop.

q-6637.text: What should you do if a fall from a single-track vehicle results in a head injury with visible nose-bleeding or ear-bleeding?

options.A: Immobilize the head and the neck section of the spine, and apply a protective dressing.
options.B: Apply pressure dressing on the bleeding spot.

q-6637.explanation: Correct answer: A. Bloody discharge from the nose or ear indicates a severe skull injury, so the head and cervical spine must be immobilised and the wound only covered with a dressing. The discharge must not be stemmed with pressure, because that raises the pressure inside the skull.

q-6638.text: What injuries usually accompany severe head injuries suffered after a fall from a single-track vehicle?

options.A: Injuries to the abdominal section of the spine.
options.B: Injuries to the chest section of the spine.
options.C: Injuries to the neck section of the spine and the skull.

q-6638.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a fall from a two-wheeler a blow to the head throws it violently relative to the torso, so together with a skull injury damage to the cervical section of the spine most often occurs. That is why such a casualty's head is treated as a cervical spine injury.

q-6639.text: How should you administer first aid to a victim of an accident who still has a pulse, but is not breathing?

options.A: I should not touch the victim, but call help.
options.B: I should immediately start a heart massage.
options.C: I should clear the respiratory tract, and if this is ineffective, I should commence resuscitation.

q-6639.explanation: Correct answer: C. The most common cause of apnoea in an unconscious person is the tongue falling back, so you begin by tilting the head and opening the airway. If breathing still does not return, resuscitation is started immediately.

q-6641.text: What should a driver do when he experiences a severe, burning pain in his chest?

options.A: He should immediately stop, call the ambulance, because he might be having a heart attack.
options.B: He should immediately drink a cup of strong coffee.
options.C: He should take painkillers and continue driving.

q-6641.explanation: Correct answer: A. Sudden, severe chest pain may mean a heart attack, and losing consciousness at the wheel risks an accident. Stop the vehicle safely, call medical help and do not continue driving.

q-6642.text: Is everyone obliged to administer first aid to victims of accidents?

options.A: No, because aid may be given only by persons with medical training.
options.B: Yes, because one can independently perform some of the first-aid activities.
options.C: No, because penal liability may be imposed for mistakes.

q-6642.explanation: Correct answer: B. The duty to give first aid rests on everyone who can do so without endangering themselves, and the basic actions — calling for help, opening the airway, pressing on a bleed — need no medical training. Help given in good faith carries no criminal liability.

q-6644.text: What should you do if you identify an open fracture?
q-6644.explanation: Correct answer: B. A fracture is immobilised together with the two neighbouring joints, because only then do the bone fragments stop moving. The wound is covered with a sterile dressing; the limb is not set and cotton wool, which sticks to the wound, is not used.

q-6645.text: What should you do, if a victim of an accident regains consciousness and wants to go home after a few minutes?

options.A: I should give the victim something to drink and painkillers.
options.B: I should encourage the victim to stay, watch the victim carefully and call medical help.
options.C: I should allow the victim to go home, recommending a visit to the doctor.

q-6645.explanation: Correct answer: B. A brief loss of consciousness indicates a head injury, and the casualty's condition may worsen even after several hours. That is why they are persuaded to stay put, observed and medical help is called; they are given no drink or medicines.

q-6646.text: What should you use as a dressing for severely-bleeding wounds?

options.B: A pressure dressing of gauze, cloth and bandage.

q-6646.explanation: Correct answer: B. Heavy bleeding is stopped with a pressure dressing: sterile gauze is placed on the wound, rolled-up material on top of it, and the whole is bandaged firmly. Gauze alone exerts no pressure, and antiseptics do not close wounds.

q-6648.text: What's the maximum speed at which you can drive a tractor with a trailer once you go past this sign?
q-6648.explanation: Correct answer: B. The sign shown in the material marks an area in which the permitted speed for all vehicles is 20 km/h. The restriction also applies to an agricultural tractor with a trailer and lasts until the cancelling sign.

q-6651.text: What's the maximum speed at which you can drive a tractor if you transport a team of labourers in a trailer?
q-6651.explanation: Correct answer: A. Carrying people in a trailer towed by an agricultural tractor is permitted only at a speed not exceeding 20 km/h. The restriction follows from the lack of protection for the passengers and applies regardless of the general limit on the road.

q-6652.text: How many persons, constituting a team of labourers, can you transport in a trailer pulled by a tractor?
q-6652.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a trailer towed by an agricultural tractor a work crew of at most 5 people may be carried. The carriage must take place at a limited speed, and the people may not ride on the load or outside the designated places.

q-6653.text: Which of the following groups of people can you transport in a trailer pulled by a tractor?

options.A: A team of labourers consisting of 7 persons.
options.B: 3 escort guards in a sitting position, between the cargo and the front wall of the trailer.
options.C: 4 persons performing loading activities, going in a standing position holding on to handles.

q-6653.explanation: Correct answer: C. People carrying out loading work may ride standing in the trailer if they hold on to the handholds and their number is within the permitted limit. A crew of seven exceeds that limit, and the carriage of escorts with the load does not concern an agricultural tractor's trailer.

q-6654.text: If you drive a tractor with a trailer, can you enter a road marked with this sign?

options.A: Yes, if the weight of transported cargo exceeds 2.5 t.
options.B: Yes, if the gross weight of the combination vehicle exceeds 2.5 t.
options.C: Yes, if the gross weight of the combination vehicle does not exceed 2.5 t.

q-6654.explanation: Correct answer: C. The sign prohibits entry to vehicles whose actual total mass exceeds the value given on it, that is, 2.5 t. With a tractor and trailer, the mass of the whole combination together with its load counts, not the weight of the goods carried alone.

q-6656.text: How can you turn right with a tractor and trailer, if the dimensions of the combination vehicle do not make it possible for you to start the manoeuvre from the right edge of the road?

options.A: You can start the manoeuvre without keeping to the right edge of the road.
options.B: You can drive onto the sidewalk with your front wheels as long as you exercise special caution.
options.C: You can cross a solid line (road marking).

q-6656.explanation: Correct answer: A. If the dimensions of the combination do not allow turning from the right edge of the carriageway, the manoeuvre may be started from another position, taking special care. This does not, however, give the right to drive onto the pavement or cross a solid line.

q-6657.text: Which of the following vehicles can you tow with a tractor?

options.B: A passenger car, by using a flexible coupling, if the two braking systems of the car are not functional.
options.C: A motorcycle, by using a flexible coupling, providing for easy disconnection.

q-6657.explanation: Correct answer: C. Towing on a flexible connection is permitted when the towed vehicle has working brakes and the connection can easily be released. A vehicle with a faulty braking system may not be towed on a rope, and towing a combination with a trailer is prohibited.

q-6659.text: When you drive a tractor, what is your duty when you perform maintenance works on the road?

options.A: I should turn on the yellow flashing light.
options.B: I should follow regulations concerning stopping and parking.
options.C: I should have with me a permit allowing me to drive on sidewalks.

q-6659.explanation: Correct answer: A. A vehicle carrying out cleaning work on the road must have its yellow flashing light on, because only then do other drivers recognise its unusual line of travel. This signal is a condition of using the concessions provided for such vehicles.

q-6661.text: If you drive a tractor, in which of the following cases can you enter the road once you go past this sign?

options.A: When I perform road works on such road.
options.B: When I transport children to school.
options.C: When trying to reach a nearby field.

q-6661.explanation: Correct answer: A. The prohibition expressed by the sign does not cover a vehicle carrying out works on that very road — without such an exception the works would be impossible. Access to a field or carrying children is no reason entitling you to break the prohibition.

q-6662.text: When you drive a tractor for the purpose of performing maintenance work, which of the following provisions are you excused from adhering to?

options.B: Prohibition to reverse on a motorway.
options.C: Giving the right of way to rail vehicles.

q-6662.explanation: Correct answer: A. A vehicle carrying out cleaning work on the road, travelling with its yellow flashing light on and taking special care, may also move off the carriageway. The ban on reversing on a motorway and the duty to give way to trams still apply.

q-6663.text: If you drive a tractor, can you pull a trailer without side reflectors?

options.C: Yes, but only if it's shorter than 6 m.

q-6663.explanation: Correct answer: B. A trailer must be equipped with side reflectors, thanks to which it is visible from the side, especially after dark at junctions. Towing a trailer lacking the required equipment is not allowed regardless of its length.

q-6664.text: How many mirrors should a tractor be equipped with?

options.A: One external mirror on the left.
options.B: At least two external mirrors, one on the left, and one on the right.
options.C: Three mirrors - external on the left and right, and an internal one.

q-6664.explanation: Correct answer: B. An agricultural tractor must have at least two exterior mirrors — on the left and on the right — because a towed machine or trailer blocks the view behind. An interior mirror is not required in such a vehicle.

q-6665.text: What is the colour of the power cable in trailers with a two-circuit pneumatic braking system?
q-6665.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a two-line system the coupling and the supply line, which brings compressed air to the trailer's reservoir, are marked in red. Yellow is assigned to the control line, which is meant to prevent the two couplings being mixed up when coupling.

q-6666.text: What is the colour of the control cable in trailers with a two-circuit pneumatic braking system?
q-6666.explanation: Correct answer: B. The control line, which passes to the trailer the signal that the brake in the tractor has been applied, is marked in yellow. Red is reserved for the supply line, so the colours allow the couplings to be connected correctly.

q-6667.text: What will be the effect of disconnecting the power cable of a trailer with two-circuit pneumatic braking system from a tractor?

options.A: The switching on of the trailer's brakes.
options.B: The switching off of the trailer's brakes.
options.C: This will not affect the operation of the trailer's brakes.
