q-6667.explanation: Correct answer: A. A drop in pressure in the supply line causes the trailer to brake automatically with the air stored in its reservoir. As a result a trailer that breaks away from the tractor stops by itself instead of rolling on out of control.

q-6668.text: When must you check the level of the brake fluid?

options.A: Always, before I start the engine.
options.B: If the lamp signalling a low level of the brake fluid does not turn off or comes on while driving.
options.C: Each time, before I connect the trailer.

q-6668.explanation: Correct answer: B. A brake-fluid warning light that comes on or does not go out usually means a loss of fluid, that is, a leak in the system or worn pads. The level and the cause must then be checked before braking effectiveness falls noticeably.

q-6669.text: What should be the shape of the rear reflectors of a trailer pulled by a tractor?
q-6669.explanation: Correct answer: C. A trailer's rear reflectors are triangular, which distinguishes it from a motor vehicle and lets you recognise from afar that a combination of vehicles is ahead. Round and rectangular reflectors are used elsewhere on the vehicle.

q-6670.text: How should a tractor be marked?
q-6670.explanation: Correct answer: B. An agricultural tractor is marked at the rear with the triangular distinguishing plate for slow-moving vehicles, so that drivers can see from afar that they are catching up with a slower vehicle. The warning triangle serves solely to mark an immobilised vehicle.

q-6671.text: How should a combination vehicle consisting of a tractor and a trailer be marked?
q-6671.explanation: Correct answer: B. A combination with an agricultural tractor moves slowly, so at the rear it must have the triangular distinguishing plate, visible to those approaching from behind. The plate is placed on the last vehicle of the combination, that is, on the trailer.

q-6673.text: What is the main factor determining the emergency braking distance of a tractor?

options.A: The reaction time of the driver.
options.B: The type of surface on which the vehicle is travelling.
options.C: The type of brake fluid used in the vehicle.

q-6673.explanation: Correct answer: B. The length of the braking distance is decided above all by grip, and that depends on the type and state of the surface. Reaction time lengthens the stopping distance but not the braking distance itself, and the brake fluid is irrelevant here.

q-6674.text: What should you first of all pay attention to when adapting the distance of a tractor from the vehicle driving in front of it?

options.B: To prevailing weather conditions and the type of road surface.
options.C: To the intensity of traffic only.

q-6674.explanation: Correct answer: B. The distance is chosen so that the combination of vehicles can be stopped before an obstacle, and that is decided by the weather and the type of surface together. Rain, mud or ice lengthen the braking distance, so the distance from the vehicle ahead must then be increased.

q-6675.text: What is the main factor determining the grip of a tractor's tyres on a dry road?

options.B: The type of surface of such road.
options.C: The efficiency of the steering system.

q-6675.explanation: Correct answer: B. Grip arises at the contact of tyre and surface, so it depends above all on whether that is asphalt, concrete, cobbles or an unmade road. Engine power and the state of the steering affect driving but do not create grip.

q-6676.text: What may be the consequences of a reduced grip of the tyres of a tractor, caused by a change in the condition of the surface?

options.A: The lengthening of the braking distance.
options.B: The shortening of the braking distance.

q-6676.explanation: Correct answer: A. Less grip means less force the wheels can pass to the surface, so the vehicle needs a longer stretch to stop. Braking is still possible, but requires earlier and gentler use of the brake.

q-6677.text: Which of the following lights of a tractor may adversely affect visibility, if they are turned on while driving in fog?
q-6677.explanation: Correct answer: A. Main-beam headlights light up the water droplets suspended in the air, and the reflected light returns to the driver's eyes and forms a bright wall in front of the vehicle. In fog you use dipped headlights and, if necessary, fog lights.

q-6678.text: Which gear should you use in order to start moving a tractor on an icy surface?

options.C: The gear which requires you to apply the lowest possible driving force of the wheels.

q-6678.explanation: Correct answer: C. On ice the wheels lose grip under too much driving force, so you move off in a gear giving only as much force as is needed to set the vehicle in motion. The clutch is released gently, without adding throttle.

q-6680.text: If you go straight in a tractor with a trailer, what should you see in properly-adjusted external mirrors?

options.A: The side of the tractor and the front of the trailer in the middle of the mirror.
options.B: The area behind the combination vehicle, on both sides, and the edge of the trailer.
options.C: The drive wheel of the tractor.

q-6680.explanation: Correct answer: B. The mirrors are set so that on both sides you can see the road behind the combination, with the edge of the trailer visible only at the edge of the mirror as a reference point. Too large a piece of your own vehicle in the mirror enlarges the blind spot.

q-6682.text: What is the order of emergency braking, of a combination vehicle consisting of a tractor and a trailer equipped with a pneumatic braking system?

options.A: The tractor and the trailer will start braking at the same time.
options.B: The trailer will start braking first.
options.C: The trailer will start braking second.

q-6682.explanation: Correct answer: B. The pneumatic system is designed so that the trailer's brakes act slightly earlier than the tractor's. Thanks to this the combination stays stretched out and the trailer does not push against the tractor, which would risk the vehicles jack-knifing.

q-6683.text: How will you achieve the greatest efficiency of engine braking if you drive a combination vehicle consisting of a tractor and a trailer?

options.A: I will put the vehicle in the first gear.
options.B: I will press and hold the clutch.
options.C: I will put the vehicle in the lowest gear possible, taking into account the rotations of the engine.

q-6683.explanation: Correct answer: C. The lower the gear, the greater the engine resistance passed to the wheels, so engine braking is more effective; the gear is chosen so as not to exceed the permitted revs. A pressed clutch cuts off that effect completely.

q-6684.text: When driving a tractor with a loaded trailer, what should you do before entering a long section of the road going upwards?

options.A: Engage such a gear that guarantees that it will get to the top without reducing gears.
options.B: Speed up the combination vehicle in the highest gear and try to drive to the top with this gear.
options.C: In any case, reduce the gears to the field mode.

q-6684.explanation: Correct answer: A. The gear is chosen before the climb, because changing down on a steep ascent with a heavy trailer causes loss of speed, and even stopping and the combination rolling back. The gear chosen should allow a steady speed to be held right to the top.

q-6686.text: What should you do if you drive a tractor with a trailer on a slippery surface?

options.A: I should turn on the front drive, if the tractor is equipped with one.
options.B: I should engage the vehicle field or crawling mode.
options.C: I should move the load on the trailer to the back in order to relieve the drive.

q-6686.explanation: Correct answer: A. Drive to both axles spreads the driving force over more wheels, so on a slippery surface the wheels spin less and the combination handles more stably. Shifting the load rearwards unloads the driven axle and worsens grip.

q-6687.text: How should you observe the road behind a tractor with a trailer while reversing?

options.A: Through the rear windshield, and in the external mirrors, by observing the trajectory of the tractor and trailer.
options.B: By looking back, without analysing the trajectory of the front of the tractor.
options.C: By looking at the steering wheel and on the basis of its position, observe the trajectory of the tractor.

q-6687.explanation: Correct answer: A. When reversing, you must see the space behind the trailer and at the same time check the path of both vehicles in the mirrors, because the trailer turns the opposite way to the steering wheel and the front of the tractor swings in a wide arc. With limited visibility, the help of another person is used.

q-6688.text: How should you observe the surrounding area while driving a tractor with a trailer forward?

options.A: By looking ahead, without checking the road behind the combination vehicle.
options.B: By simultaneously observing the road ahead and behind the combination vehicle.
options.C: By looking ahead and, from time to time, observing the road behind the combination vehicle in rear-view mirrors.

q-6688.explanation: Correct answer: C. The driver's attention is focused on the road ahead, and the mirrors are checked regularly with short glances, to know who intends to overtake the slow-moving combination. Constant watching of the rear would draw the eyes away from what is happening ahead.

q-6689.text: Can you leave a tractor without supervision, if the equipment attached to it are raised?

options.C: Yes, but only for up to five minutes.

q-6689.explanation: Correct answer: B. A raised implement can drop on its own because of a leak in the hydraulic system and crush a person who ends up beneath it. Before walking away from the tractor, lower the implement to the ground, apply the parking brake and switch off the engine.

q-6691.text: What should a driver of a tractor do when being overtaken by another vehicle?

options.A: Go as far to the right as possible.

q-6691.explanation: Correct answer: A. The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must move as far right as possible and not increase speed, so as to shorten the duration of the manoeuvre. Stopping suddenly on the carriageway would be dangerous for the overtaking driver and for vehicles behind.

q-6693.text: What should you do if the front part of the tractor rises after a heavy tool is attached thereto?

options.A: Install weights on the front wheels.
options.B: Install weights on the back wheels.
options.C: Reduce air pressure in the tyres.

q-6693.explanation: Correct answer: A. A heavy implement hitched at the rear unloads the front axle, so the tractor loses steering and in the extreme case may tip over backwards. The load on the front is restored by fitting weights to the front wheels or the front of the tractor.

q-6694.text: How should you transport loose cargo?

options.A: In a tight container, with appropriate covers.
options.C: In any container covered with tarpaulin.

q-6694.explanation: Correct answer: A. A loose load is carried in a sealed body with curtains, because material spilling onto the carriageway reduces grip and can strike vehicles behind. A tarpaulin alone on a leaky body will not stop spillage from below.

q-6695.text: Can you transport a load on the trailer of a tractor that exceeds its recommended capacity?

options.B: Yes, but only when you drive on unpaved public roads.

q-6695.explanation: Correct answer: C. The permitted payload may not be exceeded on any road, because an overloaded trailer has a longer braking distance, overloads the axle and the hitch and damages the surface. The type of road does not change this ban.

q-6696.text: Are you allowed to carry a passenger in a tractor?

options.A: Yes, in a sitting position on the mudguard.
options.C: Yes, on the rear coupling, provided that the passenger uses the handgrip.

q-6696.explanation: Correct answer: B. A passenger may be carried only on the seat intended for it, if the tractor is fitted with one. Riding on the mudguard, the hitch or another part of the structure risks falling under the wheels and is prohibited.

q-6707.text: When do you have to conduct a periodic technical check-up of a tractor?

options.C: Before the lapse of the deadline specified in the registration card of the vehicle.

q-6707.explanation: Correct answer: C. The date of the next technical inspection is entered in the registration document by the inspector, and that is what binds. After that date the vehicle may not be used on the road, so the inspection is carried out beforehand.

q-6708.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive when you have a T-category driving licence?
q-6708.explanation: Correct answer: C. Category T entitles you to drive an agricultural tractor, also with trailers, and a slow-moving vehicle. A car requires category B, and a motorcycle the appropriate motorcycle category.

q-6709.text: Which of the following vehicles can you drive if you have a T-category driving licence?
q-6709.explanation: Correct answer: A. Category T entitles you to drive an agricultural tractor, also with a trailer. A tractor unit requires category C, and a quadricycle does not fall within the entitlements of category T.

q-6710.text: What does it indicate when the engine lubrication control light comes on?

options.A: That the oil needs to be replaced.
options.B: That the oil pressure is too low.
options.C: That the oil filter is dirty.

q-6710.explanation: Correct answer: B. The lubrication light responds to oil pressure and comes on when it falls below the permissible level. You must then stop the vehicle immediately and switch off the engine, because it risks seizing. It does not tell you when to change the oil or about the filter.

q-6711.text: What is the main role of the low-beam lights in a tractor?

options.A: Lighting of the road ahead of the tractor in a manner which does not cause the blinding of the drivers coming from the opposite direction.
options.B: Lighting of the road for no more than 10 m ahead of the vehicle.
options.C: Lighting of the road for at least 100 m ahead of the vehicle.

q-6711.explanation: Correct answer: A. Dipped headlights are meant to light the road ahead of the tractor without dazzling oncoming drivers. Lighting a stretch of at least 100 m is the job of main-beam headlights, and a range of 10 m corresponds to no lights at all.

q-6712.text: What should you do if the engine coolant of a tractor is not visible in the reservoir?

options.A: Check the level of the liquid in the reservoir.
options.C: Reduce the pressure in the cooling system by turning the pressure cap in the reservoir.

q-6712.explanation: Correct answer: A. No visible coolant in the expansion tank means it has been lost, so the level in the radiator is checked with the engine cold. The cap of a hot radiator must not be unscrewed — a burst of steam and boiling water risks scalding.

q-6715.text: In what position of a tractor will you correctly check the oil level in the engine?

options.A: When the tractor is leaning in the direction of the side on which the oil level indicator is placed.
options.B: After parking the tractor in any position.
options.C: After parking on a flat surface.

q-6715.explanation: Correct answer: C. The dipstick reading is reliable only when the vehicle stands on a level surface; a tilt shifts the oil in the sump and falsifies the measurement. It is checked a short while after switching off the engine, once the oil has drained to the sump.

q-6716.text: When checking the oil level, which part on the dipstick should have oil on it in order to indicate that the oil level is correct?
q-6716.explanation: Correct answer: B. The correct oil level lies between the MIN and MAX marks. Below MIN there is not enough oil; above MAX the excess foams and loads the seals. The measurement is taken with a dipstick wiped dry, on level ground.

q-6717.text: Which section on the dipstick should bear an oil mark in order to indicate that the oil level is incorrect?
q-6717.explanation: Correct answer: A. A level above the MAX mark is incorrect: excess oil foams, and pressure and the load on the seals rise. A reading between MIN and MAX, including just above MIN, is considered correct.

q-6718.text: When checking the oil level, which part on the dipstick should have oil on it in order to indicate that the oil level is correct?
q-6718.explanation: Correct answer: C. A level below the MIN mark is incorrect — there is too little oil, lubrication and cooling of the parts deteriorate, and the engine risks seizing. A reading between MIN and MAX, including just below MAX, is correct.

q-6719.text: Can you start the engine of a tractor if the oil level on the dipstick is below the "MIN" level?

options.C: Yes, but only for the duration of getting to the nearest service station.

q-6719.explanation: Correct answer: B. A tractor with the oil level below the MIN mark may not be operated — lubrication is insufficient and the engine can seize in a short time. The oil must be topped up before moving off, even before driving to the workshop.

q-6720.text: Which of the following control lights indicates that the position lights are on?
q-6720.explanation: Correct answer: B. The position-light indicator is a green symbol of two lamps emitting light to the sides; in the set it corresponds to variant B. The green colour of indicator lights signals a correctly working, switched-on function.

q-6721.text: Which of the following control lights indicates that the high-beam lights are on?
q-6721.explanation: Correct answer: C. The main-beam indicator shines blue and has a headlamp symbol with straight, horizontal rays; variant C corresponds to it. Dipped headlights are marked by a symbol with rays pointing diagonally downwards.

q-6722.text: Which of the following control lights indicates that the emergency lights are on?
q-6722.explanation: Correct answer: A. Hazard lights in use are signalled by a red triangle symbol flashing together with all the indicators; variant A corresponds to it. Hazard lights are used when stopped because of a breakdown and when creating a danger.

q-6723.text: Which of the following control lights indicates that the battery is not charging?
q-6723.explanation: Correct answer: A. No battery charging is signalled by a red light with a battery symbol and pole markings; in the set that is variant A. If it shines with the engine running, the charging system is faulty and driving must be limited.

q-6724.text: Which of the following control lights indicates that the oil level in the engine is too low?
q-6724.explanation: Correct answer: B. Too low an engine oil level is signalled by a red light with an oil-can symbol and a drop; in the set variant B corresponds to it. When it comes on, the engine should be switched off and the oil level checked with the dipstick.

q-6725.text: Which of the following control lights indicates that the emergency brake is on?
q-6725.explanation: Correct answer: C. An applied emergency brake lever is signalled by a red light with an exclamation mark or the letter P in a circle; in the set that is variant C. Driving with the brake applied overheats and destroys the brake mechanisms.

q-6726.text: How should you protect a person who, while driving without his safety belts fastened, has suffered an injury to the face and probably of the neck spine, but is conscious?

options.A: Hold his head and, if available, put on a cervical collar.
options.B: Immediately remove the person from the vehicle.
options.C: Do not touch the person at all in order not to worsen the injury.

q-6726.explanation: Correct answer: A. With a suspected cervical spine injury the casualty's head is held with the hands in a neutral position until the rescuers arrive. Pulling them out of the vehicle is acceptable only with an immediate threat to life; doing nothing also does harm.

q-6727.text: What measures should you take in case of face burns suffered while removing the radiator cap?

options.B: Apply a lot of egg white or linseed oil.
options.C: Cool the face with cold water, cover with sterile gauze or hydrogel.

q-6727.explanation: Correct answer: C. A burn is cooled with clean, cold water for several minutes or covered with a hydrogel dressing. Fats, ointments and home remedies trap heat, contaminate the wound and hinder further treatment.

q-6728.text: What should you do if some foreign matter has impaled itself into a passenger's forearm?

options.A: Remove the foreign matter and apply a dressing.
options.B: Seal the edges of the wound with a dressing and do not remove the foreign matter from the wound.

q-6728.explanation: Correct answer: B. A foreign object is left in the wound, because it partly closes the damaged vessels, and pulling it out increases the bleeding. The edges of the wound are packed with a dressing that stabilises the object, and an ambulance is called.

q-6729.text: When should you cease to perform resuscitation to a person who is a victim of an accident?

options.A: In the event of a broken rib.
options.B: After restoration of life functions (pulse, breathing).

q-6729.explanation: Correct answer: B. Resuscitation is stopped when the casualty's breathing and circulation return or when the emergency services that have arrived take over. A rib broken during compressions is no reason to stop, and a phone call for help alone does not replace action.

q-6730.text: Which of the following numbers should you call in order to call an ambulance to the scene of a road accident?
q-6730.explanation: Correct answer: C. An ambulance is called on 999. The number 997 is the Police, and 998 the fire brigade. When reporting an incident, give the exact location, the number of casualties and their condition.

q-6731.text: How should you provide first aid to a victim of an accident who still has a pulse, but is not breathing?

options.A: I should not touch the victim, but call for help.
options.B: I should immediately start a heart massage.
options.C: I should clear the respiratory tract, and if this is ineffective, commence resuscitation.

q-6731.explanation: Correct answer: C. First the head is tilted and the jaw lifted, opening the airway — this action alone often restores breathing. If breathing does not return, resuscitation is started and an ambulance called.

q-6732.text: Does the use of tranquilisers or painkillers affect the driver?

options.B: Yes, it may lead to deterioration in the ability to drive.
options.C: It does not have any such effect if it has been prescribed by a doctor.

q-6732.explanation: Correct answer: B. Sedatives and painkillers slow reactions, cause drowsiness and weaken concentration. A doctor's recommendation does not change that — before driving, read the leaflet and ask the doctor about the medicine's effect on driving.

q-6734.text: What may be the consequences if a driver suffering from diabetes does not control their blood sugar level?

options.B: A need to have frequent rests during the journey.

q-6734.explanation: Correct answer: A. A sudden drop in blood sugar in a driver with diabetes causes weakness and impaired consciousness and can end in a sudden loss of consciousness at the wheel. Before driving, blood sugar is checked and a supply of carbohydrates is carried.

q-6735.text: Is everyone obliged to administer first aid to victims of accidents?

options.A: No, because aid may be given only by persons with medical training.
options.B: Yes, because one can independently perform some of the first-aid activities.
options.C: No, because penal liability may be imposed for any mistakes made.

q-6735.explanation: Correct answer: B. The duty to give first aid rests on everyone who can do so without endangering themselves, and the basic actions — calling for help, opening the airway, pressing on a bleed — need no medical training. Help given in good faith carries no criminal liability.

q-6736.text: How should you secure a victim of an open limb fracture?
q-6736.explanation: Correct answer: B. A broken limb is immobilised together with the two neighbouring joints — above and below the fracture — and the wound is covered with a sterile dressing. Setting the bone or pulling the limb is not acceptable.

q-6737.text: What should you do, if a victim of an accident regains consciousness after a few minutes and wants to go home?

options.A: I should give the victim something to drink and painkillers.
options.B: I should encourage the victim to stay, watch the victim carefully and call for medical help.
options.C: I should allow the victim to go home, recommending a visit to the doctor.

q-6737.explanation: Correct answer: B. A brief loss of consciousness indicates a head injury, and the casualty's condition may worsen even after several hours. That is why they are persuaded to stay put, observed and medical help is called; they are given no drink or medicines.

q-6738.text: What should you use to dress severely-bleeding wounds?

options.B: A pressure dressing of gauze, cloth and bandage.

q-6738.explanation: Correct answer: B. Heavy bleeding is stemmed with a pressure dressing: sterile gauze or clean cloth is pressed onto the wound and bound firmly with a bandage. Gauze alone without pressure is not enough, and iodine is not poured into such a wound.

q-6739.text: If you drive a truck with a gross vehicle weight of over 3.5 t, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive on the road once you go past this sign?
q-6739.explanation: Correct answer: C. Beyond the sign shown in the material a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 80 km/h — that is the limit on an expressway and on a two-way dual carriageway outside a built-up area.

q-6740.text: If you drive a truck with a gross vehicle weight of over 3.5 t, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive on the road once you go past this sign?
q-6740.explanation: Correct answer: C. Outside a built-up area, on the road indicated by the sign in the material, a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 70 km/h. On an expressway and a dual carriageway the limit is higher.

q-6741.text: If you drive a truck with a gross vehicle weight of over 3.5 t in a built-up area, can you drive at a speed of 70 km/h once you go past this sign?

options.C: Yes, but only between 23.00 and 5.00 hrs.

q-6741.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a built-up area a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may not exceed 50 km/h, so driving at 70 km/h is not allowed. The time of day does not change this restriction.

q-6742.text: If you drive a truck with a gross vehicle weight of over 3.5 t, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive on an express road?
q-6742.explanation: Correct answer: A. On an expressway a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 80 km/h. Speed-limit signs may lower that limit; they never raise it.

q-6743.text: If you drive a truck with a gross vehicle weight of over 3.5 t, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive once you go past this sign?
q-6743.explanation: Correct answer: A. A combination of a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t and a trailer may travel on the road indicated by the sign at no more than 70 km/h. The higher limit applies to motorways and dual-carriageway expressways.

q-6748.text: If you drive a truck with a gross vehicle weight of over 3 t, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive on a motorway?
q-6748.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a motorway a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 80 km/h. The higher speeds allowed on a motorway concern cars and light vehicles.

q-6749.text: What is the function of the anti-lock braking system (ABS)?

options.A: It prevents the loss of tyre grip while accelerating.
options.B: It helps to maintain the ability to manoeuvre while braking.
options.C: It shortens the braking distance in all conditions.

q-6749.explanation: Correct answer: B. ABS does not let the wheels lock under braking, so the wheels keep rolling and the vehicle stays steerable. It does not shorten the braking distance in all conditions — on gravel or fresh snow it can even lengthen it.

q-6751.text: What's the maximum permissible height of a truck with cargo?
q-6751.explanation: Correct answer: C. A lorry together with its load may be no higher than 4 m. Exceeding that height means an oversize vehicle and requires a permit, and also risks striking a flyover or an overhead line.

q-6752.text: What is the maximum length of a combination vehicle consisting of a motor car and a trailer?
q-6752.explanation: Correct answer: A. A combination of a motor vehicle and a towed trailer may be at most 18.75 m long. A longer combination is an oversize vehicle and may move only on the basis of a permit.

q-6754.text: What’s the maximum permissible load on a single drive axle of a vehicle travelling on public roads?
q-6754.explanation: Correct answer: B. The load on a single driven axle of a vehicle using public roads may not exceed 11.5 tonnes. A greater load damages the surface and requires a permit for an oversize vehicle.

q-6755.text: A truck with a gross vehicle weight exceeding 3.5 t is pulling a trailer. By what percentage may the gross weight of the trailer exceed the actual weight of the car pulling it?
q-6755.explanation: Correct answer: C. The actual mass of a trailer towed by a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may exceed the actual mass of the towing vehicle by at most 40%. A heavier trailer worsens the stability and braking of the combination.

q-6759.text: What's the maximum working time of a driver in a given day, if the work is performed at night?
q-6759.explanation: Correct answer: B. If a driver works at night, their working time in a given 24-hour period may not exceed 10 hours. The limit covers not only driving but also loading, servicing the vehicle and other duties.

q-6760.text: What's the maximum, non-extended daily driving time of a driver working in road transport?
q-6760.explanation: Correct answer: B. The daily driving time is 9 hours as standard. It may be extended to 10 hours, but only on a limited number of days a week, so the unextended value remains 9 hours.

q-6761.text: What's the maximum weekly driving time of a driver working in road transport?
q-6761.explanation: Correct answer: C. Weekly driving time may not exceed 56 hours. In addition, the total driving time in two consecutive weeks is limited, so a maximum week must be followed by a shorter one.

q-6762.text: What's the minimum regular and daily rest period of a driver working in road transport?
q-6762.explanation: Correct answer: B. A regular daily rest period lasts at least 11 consecutive hours. It may be reduced only in a limited number of cases, and it is taken within the 24-hour period counted from the end of the previous rest.

q-6763.text: What length of rest is a driver, engaged in road transport, entitled to after 4.5 hours of driving?

options.B: Two rest periods totalling 30 minutes, between which other work is performed.

q-6763.explanation: Correct answer: C. After four and a half hours of uninterrupted driving the driver is entitled to a break lasting at least 45 minutes. It may be split into two parts: the first lasting at least 15 minutes and the second at least 30 minutes.

q-6764.text: How many hours should a regular weekly rest period of a driver working in road transport last?
q-6764.explanation: Correct answer: C. A regular weekly rest period lasts at least 45 consecutive hours. It must begin no later than after six 24-hour periods counted from the end of the previous weekly rest.

q-6765.text: How many hours should a shortened weekly rest period of a driver working in road transport last?
q-6765.explanation: Correct answer: B. A reduced weekly rest period lasts at least 24 consecutive hours. The reduction is an exception and requires the missing hours to be compensated later, attached to another rest period.

q-6766.text: How often should you collect the data from a driver's card?
q-6766.explanation: Correct answer: B. Data from the driver card is downloaded no less often than every 28 days, so that the records are not overwritten and remain available for checks. Data from the digital tachograph is downloaded less often, but also at set intervals.

q-6767.text: In what position should the tachograph switch be placed if a driver supervises the loading of a truck for one hour?
q-6767.explanation: Correct answer: A. Supervising loading is neither driving nor rest but other work, so the tachograph switch is set to the position meaning other work — in the material variant A corresponds to it. The wrong choice understates the recorded working time.

q-6768.text: To what maximum period of time may a traffic control apply when checking the working time of a driver working in road transport?

options.B: The current day and preceding 15 days.
options.C: The current day and preceding 28 days.

q-6768.explanation: Correct answer: C. A roadside check of a driver's working time may cover the current day and the 28 preceding days. The driver must have with them the record sheets, certificates and driver card documenting that whole period.

q-6769.text: How many hours should a shortened daily rest period of a driver working in road transport last?
q-6769.explanation: Correct answer: B. A reduced daily rest period is at least 9 consecutive hours. It may be used at most three times between two weekly rest periods; the rule remains the longer rest.

q-6770.text: How many times per week may the daily driving time be extended by a driver engaged in road transport?
q-6770.explanation: Correct answer: A. The daily driving time may be extended at most twice a week. On the other days the basic time applies, and exceeding the limit is a breach detected when the tachograph data is read.

q-6771.text: A driver working in road transport should be able to present documents for inspection. What period of time must be covered by the documents?

options.A: The current day and preceding 28 days.
options.B: The current day and preceding 15 days.

q-6771.explanation: Correct answer: A. The driver must have with them documents covering the current day and the 28 preceding days. These are record sheets, driver card records and certificates of days off or of other work performed.

q-6772.text: What type of the driver's activity is replacement of a wheel in the vehicle classified as?
q-6772.explanation: Correct answer: A. Changing a wheel is an activity performed for the employer, so it counts as other work, not as a break or a period of availability. This time is recorded with the appropriate setting of the tachograph switch.

q-6775.text: By approximately how much does the braking distance of a truck increase if the speed doubles?
q-6775.explanation: Correct answer: C. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed, so doubling it makes the distance roughly four times longer. In a lorry the large mass and the longer build-up of braking force add to this, lengthening the stop further.

q-6777.text: What factors may obstruct a truck driver's field of vision?

options.A: Proper positioning of the steering column.
options.B: Flashing lights with the name of the driver placed on the windscreen.
options.C: Advertisements placed on the sides of the vehicle.

q-6777.explanation: Correct answer: B. Illuminated items on the windscreen hide part of the field of vision and additionally reflect in the glass, worsening visibility after dark. A correctly adjusted steering column and adverts on the sides of the body do not limit observation of the road ahead.

q-6778.text: Which of the following measures may improve safety while driving a truck in fog?

options.B: Keeping a safe distance from the preceding vehicle.
options.C: Turning on anti-fog rear lights, regardless of the visibility on the road.

q-6778.explanation: Correct answer: B. In fog the driver sees an obstacle later, so a greater distance gives time to react and stop a heavy vehicle. Main-beam headlights reflect off the droplets and dazzle the driver themselves, and rear fog lights may be switched on only in severely limited visibility.

q-6779.text: Can an increase of speed affect a truck driver's perception?

options.A: Yes, a higher speed causes a change of perception.
options.B: No, perception in case of high speed does not differ from perception in case of lower speed.
options.C: Yes, but only when driving in conditions of limited visibility.

q-6779.explanation: Correct answer: A. As speed increases the field of vision narrows, the eyes concentrate far ahead of the vehicle and the picture at the sides blurs. The driver notices pedestrians and signs beside the carriageway later, even though visibility conditions remain good.

q-6780.text: What factors may affect the proper observation of the road while driving a truck at night?

options.A: Inability to distinguish shapes in the dark and sensitivity to being blinded.
options.B: Use of glasses suitable for driving at night.
options.C: Proper visual acuity of the driver.

q-6780.explanation: Correct answer: A. At night the eye distinguishes shapes and contrast less well, and after being dazzled by lights it needs several seconds to recover — during that time the driver practically does not see the road. Suitable glasses and good visual acuity make observation easier, not harder.

q-6781.text: When can you use high-beam lights while driving a truck from dusk till dawn?

options.A: Always, as long as this does not blind other drivers.
options.B: On unlit roads, as long as this does not blind other drivers.
options.C: In thick fog which limits visibility to less than 50 m.

q-6781.explanation: Correct answer: B. Main-beam headlights may be used on unlit roads and only when they do not dazzle other drivers or pedestrians. In fog they are prohibited, because they reflect off the water droplets and worsen the driver's own visibility.

q-6782.text: While driving a truck, when are you obliged to switch from high-beam to low-beam lights?

options.A: When another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction.
options.C: When you enter a built-up area.

q-6782.explanation: Correct answer: A. Main beam must be switched to dipped whenever it could dazzle another road user — above all the driver of an oncoming vehicle. Rain by itself, or entering a built-up area, does not directly create such a duty.

q-6785.text: In what order should you perform activities preparing you to drive the truck?

options.A: Fasten the seat belts, position the mirrors and the driver's seat.
options.B: Position the driver's seat, adjust the mirrors and fasten the seat belts if the truck is equipped therewith.
options.C: Adjust the mirrors, position the driver's seat and then fasten the seat belts.

q-6785.explanation: Correct answer: B. The seat is set first, because changing its position changes the field of view in the mirrors, then the mirrors are adjusted, and finally the seat belt is fastened, if the vehicle is fitted with one. The reverse order forces the settings to be corrected again.

q-6786.text: While driving a truck, what should you see in properly-adjusted external mirrors ("rear-view mirrors")?

options.A: Only the sides of the truck.
options.B: The area behind the truck and the sides of the truck.

q-6786.explanation: Correct answer: B. The exterior mirrors are set to take in the area behind the vehicle and a narrow strip of your own side as a reference point. This setting reduces the blind spot when changing lane and turning, although it does not eliminate it entirely.

q-6787.text: What is the correct position of the hands on a steering wheel while driving a truck on a motorway?

options.A: Both hands at the top of the steering wheel (in the "12 o'clock" position).
options.B: Left hand on "9 o'clock", right hand on "3 o'clock".
options.C: Both hands at the bottom of the steering wheel (in the "6 o'clock" position).

q-6787.explanation: Correct answer: B. A grip at 9 and 3 o'clock gives the surest control of the steering wheel and lets you carry out a sudden evasive manoeuvre without changing your hold. Hands at the top or bottom of the wheel are unstable and delay reaction at high speed.

q-6788.text: How should you proceed when driving a loaded truck downhill?

options.C: Use the retarder to brake or brake with the engine.

q-6788.explanation: Correct answer: C. On a long descent speed is held with the retarder or the engine brake, so that the service brakes do not overheat and keep their effectiveness. A higher gear lets a loaded vehicle gather speed, and the emergency brake is only for emergencies.

q-6789.text: While driving a truck, at which point will you press the clutch if you intend to brake?

options.C: When the speed of the vehicle drops to minimum for the current gear.

q-6789.explanation: Correct answer: C. The clutch is pressed only when speed drops to the minimum for the engaged gear, just before the engine would stall. Disconnecting the drive earlier deprives the vehicle of engine braking and lengthens the stopping distance of a loaded lorry.

q-6790.text: What should you do if you have to perform an emergency braking manoeuvre with a truck equipped with anti-lock braking system (ABS)?

options.A: Firmly press the brake and clutch pedals and do not release them untill the ABS system activates.
options.B: Firmly press the brake pedal and reduce the pressure the moment the ABS system activates.
options.C: Pulse brake until the ABS system activates.

q-6790.explanation: Correct answer: A. In emergency braking the brake and clutch pedals are pressed hard and held until the vehicle stops, despite vibration and pulsing of the pedal — that is the normal working of the system. Easing the pressure or pumping the brake lengthens the braking distance and is not needed.

q-6791.text: Which of the following conditions must be met to activate the cruise control?

options.A: The vehicle has attained the minimum speed specified by the manufacturer.
options.B: The clutch pedal has been pressed.
options.C: The vehicle speed limit function has been turned on.

q-6791.explanation: Correct answer: A. Cruise control can be switched on only after reaching the minimum speed specified by the vehicle's manufacturer. Pressing the clutch does the opposite — it switches cruise control off, and the speed limiter is a separate function and not a condition of its operation.

q-6811.text: Which of the following documents should a driver transporting cargo have on him?

options.A: A licence authorizing him to perform road transport of cargo.
options.B: A certificate indicating reasons for the lack of record sheets or non-use of the driver's card.
options.C: A medical certificate confirming that there are no counter-indications to perform the profession of a driver.

q-6811.explanation: Correct answer: B. The driver must have with them the working-time records for the recent period, and days without a tachograph record are confirmed by a certificate of the reasons for missing record sheets or not using the driver card. The licence is the operator's document, and the medical certificate concerns professional entitlements.

q-6815.text: What document should you carry on you when driving a non-standard vehicle?

options.A: Authorization of the appropriate category for passage of the non-standard vehicle.
options.B: A document that shows proof of valid motor own damage (AC) insurance.
options.C: Authorization to perform the job of a driver.

q-6815.explanation: Correct answer: A. A journey by a vehicle exceeding the permitted dimensions, mass or axle loads requires a permit of the appropriate category, which the driver carries and shows for a check. Voluntary insurance or the employer's consent does not make such a journey lawful.

q-6816.text: Who issues category I authorizations for passage of non-standard vehicles?

options.A: The administrator of the road on which the vehicle will drive.

q-6816.explanation: Correct answer: A. A category I permit is issued by the road authority responsible for the section along which the journey is to take place, because it is the one that assesses the load-bearing capacity of the surface and the engineering structures. The employer and the Police do not issue such permits.

q-6817.text: Which of the following documents certifies that a truck is authorized to be driven on public roads?
q-6817.explanation: Correct answer: B. A vehicle's admission to traffic is confirmed by the registration document, in which a valid technical inspection result is recorded. The driving licence concerns the driver's entitlements, and the consignment note the load carried, not the vehicle's legal status.

q-6818.text: What does it signify, where the tire tread in a truck is worn to the depth of less than 1.6 mm?

options.A: That the tyres are in a good condition.
options.B: That the tyres are excessively worn.
options.C: That it's possible to continue using the tyres.

q-6818.explanation: Correct answer: B. A tread depth below 1.6 mm means excessive tyre wear and disqualifies the tyre. Shallow tread does not clear water from under the wheel, so the risk of aquaplaning grows and the braking distance on a wet surface clearly lengthens.

q-6819.text: What minimum section of the road ahead of the truck should be lit by properly-adjusted high-beam lights?
q-6819.explanation: Correct answer: B. Correctly adjusted main-beam headlights must light the road for at least 100 m ahead of the vehicle. A shorter range indicates misadjusted or worn headlamps and shortens the time the driver has to notice an obstacle at night.

q-6820.text: What minimum section of the road ahead of the truck should be lit by properly-adjusted low-beam lights?
q-6820.explanation: Correct answer: B. Correctly adjusted dipped headlights light the road for at least 40 m ahead of the vehicle without dazzling oncoming traffic. The limited range of these lights requires a speed at night that lets the vehicle stop within the visible distance.

q-6821.text: What should be the intensity of the STOP brake lights in a truck?

options.A: Significantly higher than the rear position lights.
options.B: Significantly lower than the rear position lights.
options.C: The same as the rear position lights.

q-6821.explanation: Correct answer: A. Brake lights must shine clearly brighter than the rear position lights, so that the driver behind immediately recognises braking, not just the presence of the vehicle. Brake lights that are too weak delay their reaction and risk a rear-end collision.

q-6823.text: What may be the reason for a difficulty in maintaining a straight trajectory of a truck?

options.A: The wearing and excessive clearance in the steering system.
options.B: The wearing of the friction lining in the braking system.

q-6823.explanation: Correct answer: A. A worn steering gear and excessive play mean that a movement of the steering wheel is not immediately translated into a turn of the wheels, so the vehicle drifts off line and needs constant correction. Worn brake linings affect braking, not straight-line driving.

q-6824.text: What may be the effect of too low oil level in the combustion engine?

options.B: Wear of the crankshaft, pistons and valves.
options.C: A drop in the working temperature of the engine.

q-6824.explanation: Correct answer: B. Too little oil means no continuous lubricating film, so the crankshaft journals, bearings and pistons run dry, overheat and may seize. Oil pressure then drops, and the engine temperature rises rather than falls.

q-6825.text: What may be the effect of too low level of the cooling liquid in the combustion engine?

options.A: A drop in the temperature of the engine.
options.C: An increase in the temperature of the engine.

q-6825.explanation: Correct answer: C. Too little coolant in the cooling system means poorer removal of heat from the engine, so its temperature rises and threatens overheating and serious damage. The coolant level is checked before driving, and the temperature gauge is watched on the road.

q-6827.text: What may be the result of oil leakage from a mechanical gear box?

options.A: A change in the gear ratio.
options.C: A drop in the temperature of the gear box.

q-6827.explanation: Correct answer: B. Oil in the gearbox lubricates and cools the gears and bearings. A leak lowers its level and increases friction and temperature, which leads to seizure and damage to the gearbox. Stains under the vehicle must be checked before driving.

q-6829.text: How should the asymmetric low-beam lights in a truck illuminate the road?

options.A: For a distance higher on the right than on the left.
options.B: For a distance higher on the left than on the right.
options.C: Equally on the right and on the left.

q-6829.explanation: Correct answer: A. Dipped headlights have an asymmetric pattern: on the right side they light the road further, so the driver sees the verge, pedestrians and signs. On the left the range is shorter, so as not to dazzle oncoming traffic.

q-6830.text: What may be the cause of an extended braking distance of a truck?

options.A: Excessive pressure on the braking pedal.
options.B: High pressure in the pneumatic system.
options.C: Contamination of the friction elements of the braking system with oil or lubricant.

q-6830.explanation: Correct answer: C. Brakes work through friction of the linings on the drums or discs. Oil or grease on the friction parts greatly reduces the coefficient of friction, so at the same pedal pressure the deceleration is weaker and the braking distance longer.

q-6832.text: Where on a vehicle should the warning sign be placed to indicate transport of dangerous goods?

options.C: Both at the back and front.

q-6832.explanation: Correct answer: C. A vehicle carrying dangerous goods is marked with plates placed at the front and the rear, so that they are visible from both directions. Thanks to this, other drivers and the rescue services know at once what load they are dealing with.

q-6842.text: What's the maximum speed limit for a bus which does not meet the additional technical conditions on a road marked like this?
q-6842.explanation: Correct answer: A. A bus that does not meet the additional technical conditions may not exceed 80 km/h regardless of the type of road, including one marked with the sign shown in the material. The higher limit is available only to buses that meet those conditions.

q-6843.text: If you drive a bus, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive once you go past this sign?
q-6843.explanation: Correct answer: C. Beyond the sign shown in the material a limit of 70 km/h applies, and the bus driver must comply with it. A speed set by a sign overrides the general limit provided for that type of road.

q-6844.text: If you drive a bus in a built-up area, can you drive at a speed of 80 km/h on a road marked like this?

options.C: Yes, but only between 23.00 and 5.00 hrs.

q-6844.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a built-up area a speed limit clearly lower than 80 km/h applies, and it covers all vehicles, buses included. The time of day changes nothing here, and the road's signing does not raise the limit by itself.

q-6845.text: If you drive a bus with a light trailer, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive once you go past this sign?
q-6845.explanation: Correct answer: A. A combination of a bus and a light trailer may travel on a road marked with the sign in the material at no more than 80 km/h. A trailer lengthens the braking distance and worsens stability, so the limit for the combination is no higher than for the bus alone.

q-6846.text: If you drive a bus whose maximum speed limit is up to 100 km/h, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive on the road once you go past this sign?
q-6846.explanation: Correct answer: B. A bus meeting the additional technical conditions may use the raised limit of 100 km/h only on a motorway and a dual-carriageway expressway. On a road marked with the sign shown in the material it is bound by 80 km/h.

q-6847.text: If you drive a bus whose maximum speed limit is up to 100 km/h, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive on the road once you go past this sign?
q-6847.explanation: Correct answer: A. A bus's ability to travel at 100 km/h does not by itself mean it may do so everywhere. On a road marked with the sign in the material it is bound by 80 km/h; the higher value may be used only on a motorway and a dual-carriageway expressway.

q-6848.text: What's the maximum speed at which you can drive a bus on a motorway, if the bus meets the additional technical conditions?
q-6848.explanation: Correct answer: A. A bus meeting the additional technical conditions laid down in the rules may travel on a motorway at up to 100 km/h. Other buses are bound there by the lower limit of 80 km/h.

q-6849.text: If you drive a car whose length is up to 6 m, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive on a road once you go past this sign?
q-6849.explanation: Correct answer: C. The length of the bus does not change the permitted speed. On a road marked with the sign in the material it is bound by 80 km/h, and a higher value may be used only by buses meeting additional technical conditions and only on selected roads.

q-6850.text: If you drive a car with up to 15 seats, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive on the road once you go past this sign?
q-6850.explanation: Correct answer: C. The number of seats in a bus does not affect the permitted speed. On a road marked with the sign in the material, 80 km/h applies, and the raised limit depends solely on meeting the additional technical conditions.

q-6852.text: If you drive a bus with up to 15 seats, what's the maximum speed at which you can drive on the motorway?
q-6852.explanation: Correct answer: C. On a motorway a bus may travel at 80 km/h, and the number of seats does not change that. Faster, up to 100 km/h, may be driven only by buses meeting the additional technical conditions laid down in the rules.

q-6853.text: If you drive a bus that meets the additional technical conditions, what’s the maximum speed at which you can drive on the road once you go past this sign?
q-6853.explanation: Correct answer: C. A bus meeting the additional technical conditions may travel at up to 100 km/h on a road marked with the sign in the material. This is the highest speed provided for buses; higher values concern cars.

q-6854.text: Which of the following elements should a school bus be equipped with?

options.A: An external acoustic sound warning that the vehicle is reversing.
options.B: Three portable bollards to be placed behind the bus.
options.C: A driver's cabin separated from the space for passengers.

q-6854.explanation: Correct answer: A. A school bus must have a sound signal warning the surroundings that it is reversing, because there is a large area behind the vehicle invisible to the driver, and children are nearby. Cones or a separate cab are not required equipment.

q-6855.text: Which of the following elements should a city bus used in public transport be equipped with?

options.A: Curtains in the side windows, if the bus is not equipped with shaded windshield.
options.C: A rear-view mirror in which the driver can see the interior of the bus.

q-6855.explanation: Correct answer: C. A city bus must have an interior mirror letting the driver watch the inside of the vehicle, especially the area by the doors. Thanks to it the driver sees passengers getting on and off and can close the doors and move off safely.

q-6856.text: Before you start driving a bus equipped with emergency exits, must you make sure that access to such exits are not obstructed?

options.B: No, if the number of passenger seats is lower than 35.

q-6856.explanation: Correct answer: C. Before moving off, the driver must check that access to the emergency exits is clear and that neither luggage nor standing passengers block them. This duty does not depend on the number of seats in the bus.

q-6857.text: What may be the maximum length of a combination vehicle consisting of a bus and a trailer?
q-6857.explanation: Correct answer: B. A combination of a bus and a trailer may be at most 18.75 m long. A longer combination would not fit properly round curves and junctions, so exceeding that value is not permitted.

q-6858.text: When will safety belts serve their function?

options.A: When they are properly adjusted and fastened.
options.B: When they are fastened in such a way that they remain loose in the hip section.
options.C: When the chest section is at the level of the neck.

q-6858.explanation: Correct answer: A. The belt protects only when it is fastened and correctly positioned: the lap part low across the hips, the shoulder part across the middle of the collarbone, without slack and without a twist in the webbing. A loose belt or webbing across the neck increases the risk of serious injury.

q-6859.text: How many passengers can you carry in a public transport bus?

options.A: 10 more than the number of seats specified in the registration card.
options.B: As many as will fit into the bus.
options.C: As many as specified by a note indicating the permitted number of seats and standing places.

q-6859.explanation: Correct answer: C. The number of people carried may not exceed the value given in the notice stating the permitted number of seated and standing places. Overloading a bus worsens its stability and braking and hinders the evacuation of passengers.

q-6860.text: In which of the following cases can you use an emergency switch-off of the engine?

options.A: When driving along a sharp mountain bend.
options.B: In case of damaged brakes while driving downhill.

q-6860.explanation: Correct answer: C. The emergency engine cut-off serves to cut the supply with the vehicle stationary, for example after a breakdown or in the event of fire. Using it while driving deprives the driver of steering and brake assistance, which risks losing control of the bus.

q-6861.text: For what purpose will you use a parking brake?

options.A: To immobilize the vehicle on a road with a slope of over 10%.
options.B: To reduce a demand for compressed air during stops at the bus stop.
options.C: To reduce speed when approaching a bus stop.

q-6861.explanation: Correct answer: B. The stop brake immobilises the bus while passengers get on and off and limits the use of compressed air, because the driver does not have to keep the brake pedal pressed. It serves neither for slowing down in traffic nor for a long stop.

q-6862.text: How do you activate the parking brake?

options.A: By pressing and holding the brake pedal.
options.B: By pulling the parking brake lever halfway up.
options.C: By opening of the bus door.

q-6862.explanation: Correct answer: C. The stop brake engages automatically when the bus doors are opened and releases when they are closed. Thanks to this the vehicle stands still while passengers get on and off, without the brake pedal being used.

q-6863.text: In which of the following cases can you use the emergency switch-off of the engine?
q-6863.explanation: Correct answer: C. The emergency engine cut-off is used with the vehicle stationary, to cut the supply after a breakdown or in the event of fire. While driving, using it removes steering and brake assistance, so it is prohibited.

q-6865.text: How many hours in total may a driver performing road transport drive a vehicle in two consecutive weeks?
q-6865.explanation: Correct answer: A. In two consecutive weeks the total driving time may not exceed 90 hours. In a single week the limit is 56 hours, so after a maximum week correspondingly less remains for the next.

q-6866.text: Which of the following driving schedules is permissible?

options.A: "2 hours of driving, 10 minutes break; 2.5 hours of driving, 35 minutes break."
options.B: "2 hours of driving, 15 minutes break; 2.5 hours of driving, 15 minutes break."
options.C: "2 hours of driving, 15 minutes break; 2.5 hours of driving, 30 minutes break."

q-6866.explanation: Correct answer: C. After an uninterrupted driving period of no more than 4.5 hours the driver must take a break of at least 45 minutes. It may be split into 15 minutes and then 30 minutes — only in that order and of those lengths.

q-6868.text: What is the maximum time that a traffic control of the bus driver's working time may apply to?

options.A: The current day and the preceding 28 days.
options.B: The current day and the preceding 14 days.
options.C: The current and the preceding week.

q-6868.explanation: Correct answer: A. A roadside check may cover the current day and the 28 previous days. That is why the driver must have with them the driver card and, if necessary, record sheets or printouts from that whole period.

q-6869.text: How often should you collect data from a driver's card?
q-6869.explanation: Correct answer: C. Data from the driver card is downloaded no less often than every 28 days. The card's memory is limited and once full the oldest records are overwritten, and the operator must keep full working-time records.

q-6870.text: What type of the driver's activity is the maintenance of the bus in a clean condition classified as?
q-6870.explanation: Correct answer: B. Cleaning and washing the bus is an activity performed for the employer, so it counts as other work. It is neither a break, in which the driver freely disposes of their time, nor a period of availability.

q-6871.text: In what position should the tachograph switch be set, while the driver is cleaning the bus?
q-6871.explanation: Correct answer: A. Keeping the bus clean is other work, so the tachograph switch is set to the position marked A in the material, corresponding to other work, not to rest or a period of availability.

q-6873.text: What's the minimum number of hours that a bus driver has to rest per day?
q-6873.explanation: Correct answer: B. A regular daily rest period is at least 11 consecutive hours. It may be taken in two parts — a shorter one and then a longer one — and a reduced rest, no shorter than 9 hours, is allowed only a limited number of times.

q-6874.text: Can the hours of time off taken as compensation for a shortened weekly rest be divided?

options.B: Yes, depending on the driver's decision.

q-6874.explanation: Correct answer: C. Compensation hours are taken in one go, in full, attached to another rest period lasting at least 9 hours. Splitting them into parts is not allowed, because it would not give the driver full recovery.

q-6875.text: How many hours of compensation time-off does a driver have left, if he has used 35 hours of a shortened weekly rest?
q-6875.explanation: Correct answer: B. A regular weekly rest lasts 45 hours, so after 35 hours have been taken, 10 hours remain to be taken. The compensation is taken in full, attached to another rest period.

q-6876.text: How many hours of compensation time-off does a driver have left, if he has used 24 hours of a shortened weekly rest?
q-6876.explanation: Correct answer: C. From the full weekly rest of 45 hours we subtract the 24 hours taken, which gives 21 hours of compensation. It must be taken in full, together with another rest period.

q-6879.text: By approximately how much does the braking distance of a bus increase if the speed doubles?
q-6879.explanation: Correct answer: C. The braking distance grows in proportion to the square of the speed, so doubling it makes the distance roughly four times longer. On top of that comes the distance covered during the reaction time, which is why a heavy bus needs a large gap.

q-6880.text: What is the main factor determining the grip of a bus's tyres on a dry road?

options.A: The type of surface of such road.
options.C: The good working order of the steering system.

q-6880.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a dry road grip is decided above all by the type of surface — asphalt, paving or concrete give different coefficients of friction. Engine power and the state of the steering affect the vehicle's handling but not grip itself.

q-6881.text: At what speed can you drive a bus?

options.A: At a speed that ensures control over the vehicle.
options.B: The permissible speed on a given section of the road, regardless of the conditions prevailing on the road.
options.C: At a speed specified by the speed limiter, regardless of the conditions prevailing on the road.

q-6881.explanation: Correct answer: A. Speed is chosen according to conditions: the state of the road, visibility, traffic and the load, so as to control the vehicle and stop it before an obstacle. The limit from a sign or the speed limiter is only an upper bound, not a recommendation.

q-6882.text: At what speed can you drive a bus?

options.A: At a speed permitted by the speed limiter, regardless of the traffic intensity.
options.B: At a speed permitted on a given section, regardless of the conditions prevailing on the road.
options.C: At a speed, which does not cause an obstacle to other drivers.

q-6882.explanation: Correct answer: C. The driver must travel at a speed suited to conditions while at the same time not obstructing others — driving too slowly without justification is prohibited. Limits from signs and the speed limiter set only the upper bound.

q-6883.text: What minimum distance must you keep from a preceding vehicle if you drive a bus outside a built-up area, in a tunnel whose length exceeds 500 m?
q-6883.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a tunnel longer than 500 m outside a built-up area, a bus driver keeps a distance of at least 50 m from the vehicle ahead. This distance makes evacuation and access for the services easier if an incident occurs in the tunnel.

q-6884.text: What distance should you keep from the preceding vehicle on the road once you go past this sign and if you drive a bus whose length is over 7 m?

options.A: A distance allowing the vehicles overtaking to safely go in front of the bus.

q-6884.explanation: Correct answer: A. Outside a built-up area the driver of a vehicle longer than 7 m keeps a distance that lets an overtaking driver pull in safely in front of them. This does not apply on roads with two lanes in one direction or in places where overtaking is prohibited.

q-6885.text: What distance from the preceding vehicle should you keep if you drive a bus in a built-up area?

options.A: A distance allowing the overtaking vehicles to safely go in front of the bus.
options.B: At least 50 m on a single carriageway.
options.C: A distance necessary to avoid a collision in the event that the preceding vehicle brakes.

q-6885.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a built-up area the general rule applies: the distance must be enough to avoid a collision if the vehicle ahead begins to brake. The duty to let overtaking drivers pull in ahead of the vehicle applies to driving outside a built-up area.

q-6886.text: What distance should be maintained between two organized columns of buses?
q-6886.explanation: Correct answer: C. Between organised columns of buses a distance of at least 500 m is kept. Thanks to this, a driver who has overtaken one column can calmly return to their lane before reaching the next.

q-6887.text: What factors may obstruct the field of vision of a truck driver?

options.A: A proper way of positioning the steering column.
options.B: Flashing lights with the name of the driver placed on the windscreen.
options.C: Advertisements placed on the sides of the vehicle.

q-6887.explanation: Correct answer: B. Any object placed on the windscreen hides part of the field of vision, and illuminated items additionally reflect in the glass and tire the eyes after dark. Adverts on the sides do not limit the view ahead.

q-6888.text: Which of the following activities may improve safety while driving a bus in fog?

options.B: Keeping a larger distance from the preceding vehicle.
options.C: Turning on the rear anti-fog lights, regardless of the prevailing visibility.

q-6888.explanation: Correct answer: B. In fog much less can be seen, so a greater distance gives time to react and stop a heavy bus. Main-beam headlights reflect off the water droplets and worsen visibility, and rear fog lights may be switched on only in limited visibility.

q-6889.text: Which of the following factors may affect a bus driver's ability to observe the road?

options.A: Tiredness, reducing the efficiency of sight.

q-6889.explanation: Correct answer: A. Tiredness weakens visual acuity, narrows the field of attention and lengthens reaction time, so the driver notices hazards later. That is why breaks and rest periods must be observed, and at the first signs of drowsiness you must stop.

q-6890.text: What factors may affect a proper observation of the road while driving a bus at night?

options.A: Inability to distinguish shapes in the dark and sensitivity to being blinded.
options.B: Use of glasses suitable for driving at night.
options.C: Proper visual acuity of the driver.

q-6890.explanation: Correct answer: A. At night the eye recognises shapes and contrasts less well, and after being dazzled by lights it needs time to readapt to the dark. Well-chosen glasses and correct visual acuity make observation easier, not harder.

q-6891.text: When can you use high-beam lights when driving from dusk till dawn?

options.A: Always, as long as this does not blind other drivers.
options.B: On unlit roads, as long as this does not blind other drivers.
options.C: In thick fog which limits visibility to less than 50 m.

q-6891.explanation: Correct answer: B. Main-beam headlights are used on unlit roads and only when they dazzle nobody — neither oncoming traffic nor the vehicle ahead. In fog their light reflects off the water droplets and worsens visibility further.

q-6892.text: While driving a bus, when do you have to turn off the rear anti-fog lights?
q-6892.explanation: Correct answer: C. Rear fog lights are used only when visibility is less than 50 m. Once it improves above that value they must be switched off, because they dazzle the driver behind and blur the picture of the brake lights.

q-6893.text: While driving a bus, when do you have to switch from high-beam to low-beam lights?

options.A: When another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction.
options.C: When you enter a built-up area.

q-6893.explanation: Correct answer: A. On seeing an oncoming vehicle you must immediately switch main beam to dipped so as not to dazzle its driver. The same duty applies when following another vehicle, when the light glares in its mirrors.

q-6894.text: When must you switch from high-beam to low-beam lights?

options.A: Always when you see the vehicle in front of you.
options.B: Always when there is a possibility of blinding the driver of the vehicle in front of you.
options.C: Always when you see a single pedestrian on the road.

q-6894.explanation: Correct answer: B. Main-beam headlights must be switched off whenever they could dazzle another driver, including one ahead of you — via their mirrors. Merely spotting a vehicle ahead or a single pedestrian is not a criterion in itself.

q-6895.text: What should be the position of the seat of a bus driver?

options.A: Such that the back of the driver does not rest against the backrest.
options.B: Such that the leg is fully straightened when pressing the clutch.
options.C: Such that the leg is slightly bent at the knee when pressing the clutch pedal all the way down.

q-6895.explanation: Correct answer: C. The seat is set so that with the clutch pedal pressed fully down the leg stays slightly bent at the knee — the driver then has full range of movement and force of pressure. A fully straight leg means the seat is too far back.

q-6896.text: While driving a bus, what should you see in properly-adjusted external mirrors ("rear-view mirrors")?

options.A: Only the sides of the car.
options.B: The area behind the car and the sides of the car.

q-6896.explanation: Correct answer: B. The exterior mirrors should take in the area behind the vehicle and a narrow strip of your own side as a reference point. In a long bus this setting is essential when changing lane and turning, because it reduces the extensive blind spot.

q-6897.text: In which gear will a bus start moving forward in good road conditions, on a flat surface?

options.A: The lowest gear, as specified by the manufacturer.
options.B: The third gear, unless the bus is loaded.
options.C: The first gear of the upper gear box.

q-6897.explanation: Correct answer: A. Moving off is done in the lowest gear specified by the manufacturer for the vehicle, because only then is the torque sufficient to set a heavy bus smoothly in motion. Moving off in a higher gear overloads the clutch and causes jerking.

q-6898.text: What is the most effective way of speeding up a bus?

options.A: By reaching the maximum RPM of the engine in all subsequent gears.
options.B: By changing gears in such a way that the RPM of the engine is not lower than the starting value of the green area on the tachometer.
options.C: By using all gears successively, even if the tachometer indicator is in the red area.

q-6898.explanation: Correct answer: B. A bus is accelerated most effectively by changing gear within the green band of the rev counter, that is, where the engine has the greatest torque and the lowest fuel consumption. Revving the engine to the maximum or running in the red band only damages it.

q-6902.text: While driving a bus, how will you turn right at the intersection?

options.A: You will turn at an angle as close to the straight angle as possible, using the auxiliary brake at the same time.
options.B: You will turn right after coming as close as possible to the right edge of the road, regardless of the size of the vehicle.
options.C: You will choose the trajectory, taking into account that the back of the bus wings to the side during a turn.

q-6902.explanation: Correct answer: C. A long vehicle turns on a different path from a car: the rear swings out on the outside, and the rear wheels run closer to the kerb than the front ones. The line must be chosen so as not to catch the kerb, pedestrians or vehicles alongside.

q-6903.text: What should a bus driver do before he starts reversing?

options.A: If necessary, ask another person to help.
options.B: look through the rear windshield to see if there are any obstacles on the road, return to the driver's seat and start the manoeuvre.
options.C: Turn on the rear anti-fog lights.

q-6903.explanation: Correct answer: A. When reversing, the driver must be certain there is nobody behind the vehicle, and when they cannot take in the whole path of the manoeuvre themselves, they must use the help of another person. A single glance backwards gives no such certainty.

q-6904.text: While driving a bus, which of the following activities should be performed in order to achieve the highest efficiency of braking with the engine?

options.C: If possible engage the lowest gear.

q-6904.explanation: Correct answer: C. Engine braking is more effective the lower the gear engaged, because the engine's resistance slows the wheels more strongly. Pressing the clutch disconnects the drive and removes that effect entirely, and a higher gear weakens it.

q-6905.text: Which of the safety systems applied in buses is responsible for the most effective method of braking?

options.A: The electronic stability control system (ESC or ESP).
options.B: The traction control system (TCS or ASR)

q-6905.explanation: Correct answer: C. More effective braking is the job of the anti-lock system, which does not let the wheels lock, so the vehicle keeps its steering and can be steered round an obstacle. Traction control works when accelerating, and stability control — in a skid.

q-6906.text: What is the function of a retarder applied in buses?

options.A: It contributes to a more effective speeding-up of the bus.
options.B: It offers the possibility of an alternative method of braking.
options.C: It protects against skidding which may occur at the time of breaking.

q-6906.explanation: Correct answer: B. A retarder is an additional, friction-free way of reducing speed, used especially on long descents. It relieves the service brakes and protects them from overheating, but does not replace them in emergency braking or prevent skidding.

q-6907.text: Should an adult person transported in a bus, sitting in a seat equipped with safety seat belts, use such seat belts?

options.B: Yes, but only when there are no other seats in front of such seat.
options.C: No, because this obligation does not apply to a bus.

q-6907.explanation: Correct answer: A. The duty to fasten belts applies to every seat fitted with them, in a bus too, and does not depend on whether there is another seat in front of the passenger. The backrest of the seat in front does not protect against the effects of harsh braking or a rollover.

q-6908.text: What may be the total weight of people and their luggage transported in a bus?

options.A: As much as the maximum gross capacity of the bus.
options.B: As much as the gross vehicle weight.
options.C: As much as the empty weight of the bus.

q-6908.explanation: Correct answer: A. Passengers together with their luggage constitute the vehicle's load, so their combined mass may not exceed the bus's permitted payload. The maximum permissible mass also includes the vehicle's unladen mass, so it is not a measure of the load itself.

q-6909.text: Where should luggage be transported in a tourist bus?
q-6909.explanation: Correct answer: C. Luggage is carried in the compartments intended for it, where it is secured against shifting. Items left on the seats or in the aisle injure passengers under braking and block the escape route in an accident.

q-6910.text: How should luggage be transported in a tourist bus if it has sharp edges?
q-6910.explanation: Correct answer: B. Luggage with sharp edges is particularly dangerous for passengers, so it must travel in the luggage compartments, separated from the passenger area. Placed in the aisle or under a seat, it shifts under braking and can cause serious injury.

q-6911.text: What must a bus driver carrying passengers not do?
q-6911.explanation: Correct answer: C. The driver of a bus carrying passengers may not smoke while driving. It occupies the hands and attention, and the smoke harms the travellers. A hands-free kit and the radio are allowed, provided they do not distract the driver.

q-6912.text: What must you not do when you drive a bus transporting passengers?
q-6912.explanation: Correct answer: A. The driver of a bus with passengers may not eat while driving, because it takes a hand off the wheel and attention off the road. Navigation and a CB radio are permitted, provided operating them does not interfere with driving.

q-6913.text: What must a bus driver transporting passengers do before driving off?

options.A: Always turn on the direction indicator.
options.B: Make sure that all doors are closed in the bus.
options.C: Inform the passengers of the next stop.

q-6913.explanation: Correct answer: B. Before moving off, the driver must make sure all the doors are closed, because driving with the doors open risks a passenger falling out. The indicator is switched on only when the manoeuvre requires it, and announcing the stop is not a condition of moving off.

q-6921.text: What necessary activities should be performed by a bus driver while replacing a wheel on the road?

options.B: Raise the vehicle with a jack to a sufficient height to create a distance between the tyre and the surface.
options.C: Release the parking brake, in order to ensure free movement of the wheel.
