q-6921.explanation: Correct answer: B. The vehicle is raised with the jack just enough to leave a gap under the tyre sufficient to fit the good wheel. The engine should be off and the parking brake applied — releasing it risks the vehicle slipping off the jack.

q-6922.text: What necessary activities should be performed by a bus driver while replacing a wheel?

options.A: Place the jack in a place indicated by the producer.
options.C: After replacement, tighten the screws on the wheel with maximum force, without paying any attention to the recommended torque.

q-6922.explanation: Correct answer: A. The jack is placed only at the point indicated by the manufacturer, because only there does the structure bear the vehicle's weight. The wheel bolts, in turn, are tightened to the recommended torque — too much force can stretch them or damage the thread.

q-6923.text: What fuel should be used in diesel engines commonly found in buses?

options.B: Diesel oil meeting the relevant standards.
options.C: Diesel oil with kerosene, in all temperature conditions.

q-6923.explanation: Correct answer: B. A diesel engine uses only diesel fuel meeting the applicable standard, also chosen for the season. Heating oil and adding paraffin yourself destroy the injection equipment and are not allowed.

q-6924.text: Can you add water to the cooling system of a bus engine?

options.A: Yes, but only in emergency situations and when ambient temperature is above zero.
options.B: Yes, but only when ambient temperature is below zero.

q-6924.explanation: Correct answer: A. Water may be added only as a stopgap when coolant has run out, and only at an ambient temperature above zero. Diluted coolant loses its antifreeze and anti-corrosion properties, so at the first opportunity the system must be topped up with the proper fluid.

q-6925.text: What will you use to dilute the concentrate, which is the main component of the cooling liquid?
q-6925.explanation: Correct answer: A. Concentrate is diluted with distilled water, free of mineral salts. Water rich in minerals causes scale to build up in the cooling passages and the radiator, which worsens heat removal and leads to the engine overheating.

q-6926.text: Which sub-assemblies of the bus are lubricated with gear oil?
q-6926.explanation: Correct answer: B. Gear oil lubricates the gearbox and other gear trains, because it withstands the very high pressures between gear teeth. The engine needs engine oil, and pins and joints are usually lubricated with grease.

q-6928.text: What causes ignition in a diesel oil?
q-6928.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a diesel engine the air is compressed strongly and reaches a high temperature, at which the injected fuel ignites on its own. There are no spark plugs, so low compression pressure or a low temperature makes it impossible to start the engine.

q-6929.text: When you drive a bus, how can you identify excessive clearance of the steering mechanism?

options.A: By an increased idle movement of the steering wheel.
options.B: By excessive wearing of a tyre on one of the rear wheels.

q-6929.explanation: Correct answer: A. Excessive play is recognised by increased free movement of the steering wheel: it can be turned through a noticeable angle before the wheels begin to turn. The vehicle holds its line worse and needs constant correction, so the fault must be fixed immediately.

q-6930.text: What symptom indicates a malfunction of the power steering system in a bus?

options.A: Significantly reduced resistance of the steering wheel movement.
options.B: Drifting of the front wheels sideways while driving on a bend.
options.C: Significantly increased resistance of the steering wheel movement.

q-6930.explanation: Correct answer: C. Power steering is meant to reduce the force needed to turn the steering wheel, so its failure shows as clearly greater resistance at the wheel, especially at low speed and when manoeuvring. Too little resistance is not a symptom of a power-steering fault.

q-6931.text: What symptoms observed while driving a bus indicates that there is excessive clearance in the universal joints of the steering system?

options.A: Difficulty in maintaining a straight trajectory of motion.
options.B: Increased resistance of the steering wheel.
options.C: Ease of maintaining a straight trajectory of motion.

q-6931.explanation: Correct answer: A. Excessive play in the joints means a movement of the steering wheel is not immediately translated into a turn of the wheels, so the vehicle wanders and has to be corrected constantly. The symptom is difficulty holding a straight line, not greater resistance at the wheel.

q-6932.text: What may be the cause of lack of tightness in the pneumatic braking system applied in buses?

options.B: Excessive clearance on brake shoes spreaders/star wheel adjusters.

q-6932.explanation: Correct answer: A. A leak is an escape of compressed air, so its source is the parts that carry air — damaged valves, pipes or connections. Play in the brake mechanism and worn discs worsen braking but do not cause the system to lose its tightness.

q-6933.text: Which of the following symptoms may indicate a malfunction of the air compressor of the brake system in the bus?

options.A: Audible air hissing in the diaphragm actuator while braking.
options.B: Reduced pressure in the pneumatic system.
options.C: Sudden increase in pressure in the braking system.

q-6933.explanation: Correct answer: B. The compressor's job is to maintain the correct pressure in the tanks, so its failure shows as pressure that is too low and builds slowly. Hissing air indicates a leak, not a compressor fault.

q-6934.text: What should you do in the event of an aggressive behaviour of a passenger towards you or other passengers, making it difficult for you to drive?

options.A: Continue driving to the nearest police station.
options.B: Stop the vehicle and call the relevant forces.
options.C: I do not have to take any action.

q-6934.explanation: Correct answer: B. The bus driver is responsible for the safety of the people carried, and behaviour that hinders driving makes safe driving impossible. Stop the vehicle in a safe place and call the appropriate services instead of driving on.

q-6935.text: At what distance behind the vehicle should you place a warning triangle in order to secure an accident scene on an express road?
q-6935.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a motorway and an expressway the warning triangle is placed 100 m behind the vehicle, because high speeds require earlier warning of approaching traffic. Shorter distances apply to other roads.

q-6936.text: What should you primarily take care of in the event of a fire in the bus you are driving?

options.A: My safety and that of my passengers'

q-6936.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a fire the priority is human life and health, so the driver first stops the vehicle and organises the evacuation, and only then thinks about property. Luggage and the state of the vehicle may never delay leaving the coach.

q-6938.text: How should you behave in case of a fire inside a bus during the journey?

options.A: Go to the nearest car park and start evacuating passengers.
options.B: Stop the vehicle, activate the extinguisher and try to extinguish the fire alone.
options.C: Stop the vehicle, switch off the engine and start evacuating passengers.

q-6938.explanation: Correct answer: C. Fire in a coach develops very quickly, so you must stop the vehicle immediately, switch off the engine and get the passengers outside. Fighting the fire may be attempted only once the people are already safe.

q-6939.text: Does this sign prohibit other vehicles on the road from overtaking the tram?
q-6939.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material does not introduce a ban on a tram overtaking other vehicles. Overtaking remains permitted under the general rules, provided traffic conditions and visibility allow it.

q-6941.text: When approaching a place marked with this sign, should you reduce the speed so as not to endanger the safety of pedestrians or cyclists on the pedestrian crossing or level crossing?
q-6941.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign gives notice of a place where pedestrians or cyclists appear, so approach at a speed that allows the vehicle to be stopped before the crossing. Special care and watching people waiting beside the carriageway apply here.

q-6942.text: When you approach a place marked with this sign, should you reduce the speed so as not to endanger the safety of cyclists entering it?
q-6942.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces a place where cyclists enter, and a bicycle moves faster than a pedestrian and appears in the field of view with little warning. Speed should be chosen so that you can stop the vehicle before the crossing.

q-6943.text: Does this sign inform you of a pedestrian crossing that may be used by cyclists?
q-6943.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material concerns an arrangement other than a pedestrian crossing with cycling permitted. A cycle crossing is marked separately, and a pedestrian crossing itself serves pedestrians only.

q-6945.text: Is the permissible speed for a tram on the road marked with this sign 25 km/h?
q-6945.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material does not set a speed of 25 km/h for the tram. The permitted speed follows from the value given on the sign or from the general rules applying on the road in question.

q-6946.text: Does this speed limit apply to the tram driver?
q-6946.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A speed limit expressed by a sign applies to all drivers of vehicles travelling on the road in question, and a tram is a vehicle too. Exceptions can follow only from a plate limiting the scope of the sign.

q-6948.text: Does this sign oblige you to stop the tram before a railroad switch in every situation?
q-6948.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign requiring a stop before the switch applies unconditionally — the tram must stop regardless of whether the track appears clear, and only then enter the switch. This allows the driver to make sure the blades are set correctly.

q-6949.text: Does this sign warn you of a multilateral rail switch?
q-6949.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material warns of a different element of the track than a multi-way switch. The type of switch and the way to pass over it follow from the separate signing used in tram operation.

q-6950.text: Does this sign forbid you to enter the rail switch without stopping?
q-6950.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material requires the tram to stop before the switch, so entering it without stopping is not permitted. Only after stopping and checking the setting of the switch may the journey continue.

q-6952.text: Does this sign warn you of approaching a place, where tram traffic is directed by traffic lights?
q-6952.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign gives notice of a place where tram traffic is controlled by light signals, so the driver must watch the signal head in advance and adjust speed. This makes it possible to stop before a signal requiring a stop.

q-6953.text: Does this sign inform of a approaching a junction, where the tram induces a phase dedicated for it?
q-6953.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign informs that the tram itself triggers its own signal phase, so the permitting signal appears only once it has been called. The driver should approach at a speed that allows stopping before the signal head.

q-6954.text: Does this sign warn of approaching a significant elevation of the tram track by the value provided in the sign?
q-6954.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material does not warn of a rising track — the value on it concerns another feature of the track's longitudinal profile. A rise and a fall are marked with separate signs that must be told apart.

q-6955.text: Does this sign inform you of a significant longitudinal drop in the tram track by the value given on the sign?
q-6955.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign gives notice of a considerable downward gradient of the track, and the number states its value. On a descent the tram's braking distance grows, so speed must be reduced early enough, before the descent begins.

q-6956.text: Does this sign inform you of a significant elevation of the tram track by the value given on the sign?
q-6956.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces a considerable rise in the track, and the number gives its value. A climb requires a suitable choice of speed and tractive effort, and when stopping on the rise — securing the vehicle against rolling back.

q-6957.text: Does this sign inform you of approaching an intersection with traffic lights, whereby turning upon leaving the intersection, you are obliged to yield the right of way to traffic users going straight ahead?
q-6957.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign gives notice of a junction where the signals permit turning and going straight ahead at the same time, so a turning driver leaving the junction must give way to those going straight. This also applies to pedestrians and cyclists crossing the carriageway being entered.

q-6958.text: Does this sign oblige you to exercise particular caution?
q-6958.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A warning sign informs of a dangerous stretch or place and obliges the driver to pay more attention and adapt speed to the expected hazard. The duty lasts until the place the sign refers to has been passed.

q-6959.text: Does this sign prohibit you from exceeding the speed limit specified on the sign?
q-6959.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A speed-limit sign prohibits driving faster than the value shown on it and applies from where it stands. If road conditions are worse, speed must be reduced further still, because the value on the sign is an upper limit.

q-6960.text: Is the prohibition expressed by this sign valid from the point of its location to the nearest crossroads?
q-6960.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition expressed by this sign does not end at the nearest junction — it applies until the place indicated by a cancelling sign or until the end of the stretch defined by the signing. The "until the junction" rule does not cover all prohibition signs.

q-6961.text: Is the prohibition expressed by this sign valid from its location to the nearest rail intersection?
q-6961.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The prohibition expressed by this sign concerns a stretch of track and ends at the nearest crossing of the tracks. The further part of the route needs separate signing if the restriction is to apply beyond that place as well.

q-6962.text: Does this sign prohibit you from entering the rail switch until it is unblocked?
q-6962.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material does not make entering the switch conditional on its being unlocked — its content concerns a different requirement placed on the tram driver. The conditions for entering the switch follow from the signing and signals used on the track.

q-6963.text: Can you drive at a speed of 20 km/h beyond this sign?
q-6963.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A speed of 20 km/h does not exceed the value arising from the sign shown in the material, so driving at that speed is permitted. The sign sets an upper limit, and the driver may go slower if conditions require it.

q-6964.text: In this situation, are you allowed to enter beyond the signalling device?
q-6964.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown in the material permits continuing, so passing the signal head is allowed. Before moving off, however, make sure there is room beyond the junction to leave it without stopping on it.

q-6966.text: In this situation, can you continue driving despite the lack of a tram signalling unit?
q-6966.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Where there is no signal head intended for the tram, the driver follows the general signals in force at that approach. If they permit travel, the tram may continue across, taking care at the junction.

q-6967.text: In this situation, can you turn right at the intersection?
q-6967.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown in the material permits going right, so carrying out this manoeuvre is allowed. Turning, watch pedestrians and vehicles on the road you are entering and, if necessary, give way to them.

q-6968.text: Seeing this signal, can you turn right?
q-6968.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown in the material does not permit going right, and you may go only in the direction indicated by the signal given. A right turn will be possible only once the signal permitting that direction appears.

q-6969.text: Seeing this signal, can you turn left?
q-6969.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown in the material permits going left, so this manoeuvre may be carried out. Entering the junction, you must be sure you will be able to leave it, and watch the road users on the side road.

q-6970.text: Seeing this signal, do you have the right to enter beyond the signalling unit?
q-6970.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown in the material prohibits travel, so you must stop before the signal head or before the line marking the stopping place. You may move off only once the signal permitting travel is given.

q-6971.text: Does this signal indicate that when turning left, there will be no collision with other traffic users?
q-6971.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown in the material permits the tram to turn left as a conflict-free manoeuvre — the other road users then have a signal prohibiting travel. Even so, the driver watches the junction, because someone may enter it against the signal.

q-6972.text: Does this signal indicate that when turning left there shall be a collision with other traffic users?
q-6972.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown in the material means a left turn without conflict with other road users, who at that time have a signal prohibiting travel. The driver still watches the junction, however, and reacts to behaviour contrary to the signals.

q-6973.text: When driving a tram, are you obliged to stop upon a signal given by a police offer?
q-6973.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Instructions and signals given by a person directing traffic or authorised to carry out checks override signs and signals and also bind a tram driver. The stop must be made safely, at the indicated place.

q-6974.text: In this situation, do you have priority over the passenger car signalling the intention to turn left?
q-6974.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning left must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction and going straight ahead, including a tram. The car may begin the manoeuvre only after letting the tram through, and the tram driver watches its behaviour anyway.

q-6975.text: When driving a tram and turning left at the intersection marked with this sign, do you have priority over motor vehicles?
q-6975.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a junction where priority follows from signs, a tram has priority over other vehicles regardless of the direction in which it turns. The driver uses this right, but must make sure the other drivers have noticed them.

q-6976.text: You are driving a tram. Upon approaching an intersection marked with this sign, are you obliged to yield the right of way to motor vehicles coming from the right side?
q-6976.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material grants priority to the vehicles travelling along it, so the right-hand rule does not operate here and the tram does not give way to vehicles from the minor road. You must still watch whether it will actually be respected.

q-6977.text: You are driving a tram and approaching an intersection marked with this sign, are you obliged to give way to motor vehicles coming from the left side?
q-6977.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material grants priority to vehicles travelling along this road, so the tram does not give way to vehicles approaching from the minor road on the left. Care is still needed, because drivers may fail to respect the priority.

q-6978.text: In this situation, do you have priority over vehicles approaching from the right side?
q-6978.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs shown in the material make your road the road with priority, and the right-hand rule then gives way to the signing. The vehicle approaching from the right must let you through, which does not excuse you from watching its behaviour.

q-6979.text: Should you in this situation, yield the right of way to vehicles approaching from the right side?
q-6979.explanation: Correct answer: NO. From the signing shown in the material it follows that the tram has priority, so the rule of giving way to vehicles from the right does not apply here. The driver should nevertheless watch the side road and be ready to brake.

q-6980.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle coming from the right?
q-6980.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority at this junction follows from the signing shown in the material and belongs to the tram, so it does not give way to the vehicle approaching from the right. You must, however, watch whether that vehicle's driver really is slowing down.

q-6981.text: In this situation, do you have priority over the vehicle approaching from the right side?
q-6981.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs shown in the material make your road the road with priority, and the right-hand rule then gives way to the signing. The vehicle approaching from the right must let you through, which does not excuse you from watching its behaviour.

q-6982.text: In this situation, do you have priority over vehicles travelling on the transverse road?
q-6982.explanation: Correct answer: NO. From the signing shown in the material it follows that the side road is the road with priority, so the tram has no advantage here over the vehicles travelling along it. Approach the junction at a speed that allows stopping before it.

q-6983.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the transverse road?
q-6983.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material imposes on the vehicle entering a duty to give way to vehicles travelling along the side road. Entering the junction is possible only when that will not force them to change speed or direction.

q-6984.text: In this situation, should you stop immediately before the signaling device without paying attention to the vehicle traffic on the road?
q-6984.explanation: Correct answer: NO. No manoeuvre, stopping included, may be carried out without watching the other road users — sudden braking without assessing the situation risks being run into from behind. A stop is made smoothly, at the right place and after checking the surroundings.

q-6985.text: In this situation, are you allowed to enter the intersection?
q-6985.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal in force permits entry, and the intended passage does not conflict with vehicles that have priority. You may enter provided the junction can be left without stopping on it.

q-6986.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop before the traffic signal?
q-6986.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal given in the situation shown permits travel, so no duty to stop before the signal head arises. Continuing, however, you must watch the junction and make sure it can be left without stopping.

q-6987.text: In this situation, are you obliged to enter beyond the traffic signal?
q-6987.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal head is showing a signal prohibiting further travel, so you may not pass it. Stop before the stop line or, where there is none, before the signal head, and wait for the permitting signal.

q-6988.text: In this situation, are you allowed to leave the intersection without stopping?
q-6988.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle that entered the junction in accordance with the signal has the right to leave it without stopping, and the other road users should let it. Stopping on the junction would block traffic from the other directions.

q-6989.text: In this situation, intending toturn left, are you allowed to enter beyond the traffic signal?
q-6989.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal given for this direction does not permit turning left, so you may not pass the signal head, even if other directions have a clear passage. The manoeuvre may be carried out only once the signal for a left turn is given.

q-6991.text: In this situation, are you allowed to enter beyond the traffic signal?
q-6991.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal head is showing a signal prohibiting further travel, so you may not pass it. Stop before the stop line or, where there is none, before the signal head, and wait for the permitting signal.

q-6992.text: If you see such a posturę of the traffic control police oficer, can you enter the intersection?
q-6992.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The stance of the person directing traffic shown in the material means no entry to the junction and corresponds to a red signal for this direction. You may enter only once the stance changes to one permitting travel.

q-6993.text: If you see such a stance of the traffic control police oficer, can you go straight through the intersection?
q-6993.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The stance of the person directing traffic shown in the material permits going straight ahead across the junction and corresponds to a green signal for this direction. Crossing, you must watch the other road users and take care.

q-6994.text: If you see such a posturę of the traffic control police officer, are you allowed to enter the intersection with the intention of turning right?
q-6994.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The stance of the person directing traffic shown in the material does not permit entering the junction from this direction, so intending to turn right changes nothing. You may move off only once the stance changes to one permitting travel.

q-6995.text: Are you allowed to continue driving in this situation?
q-6995.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The conditions shown in the material require you to give way to road users who are already on the carriageway, above all pedestrians. You may move only once they have cleared the way and would not have to be forced to stop.

q-6996.text: Are you obliged to stop in this situation?
q-6996.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop follows from the sign, signal or instruction shown in the material and binds regardless of whether the road appears clear. The stop is made before the line or before the place that duty refers to.

q-6997.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn left without stopping?
q-6997.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material requires a stop before carrying out the manoeuvre, so a left turn without stopping is not permitted. Only after stopping and assessing the situation may you continue in the chosen direction.

q-6998.text: In this situation, turning left to the depot, do you have priority over the vehicle coming in the opposite direction?
q-6998.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A rail vehicle has priority over other vehicles regardless of the direction in which it turns, so a tram turning left does not let the oncoming vehicle through. The driver should, however, make sure the oncoming driver has noticed that priority.

q-6999.text: When leaving the depot, do you have priority over vehicles moving on the transverse road?
q-6999.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Leaving the depot onto the road is joining the traffic, and the one joining gives way to all road users travelling along that road. This applies to a tram as well, despite the priority it has at junctions.

q-7000.text: In this situation, when leaving the terminus are you obliged to yield priority in the event of a tram approaching from the right?
q-7000.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving the loop onto the route is joining the traffic, so the driver gives way to vehicles already moving on it, including the tram approaching from the right. You may move off only after it has passed.

q-7001.text: In this situation, turning left into the depot, are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle coming in the opposite direction?
q-7001.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A tram enjoys priority over other vehicles regardless of its direction of travel, so when turning left it does not have to let the oncoming vehicle through. The manoeuvre must still be started after making sure it will be read correctly.

q-7002.text: When turning in this situation, are you obliged to signal your intention to change the driving direction?
q-7002.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intention to change direction is signalled in advance and clearly, so that the other road users can anticipate the tram's manoeuvre. Signalling ends once the manoeuvre is carried out and does not release you from watching your surroundings.

q-7003.text: In this situation, are obliged to signal your intention to turn?
q-7003.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Following a curve in the track, when the layout of the tracks gives no possibility of choosing another direction, is not a change of direction requiring signalling. That duty arises where the tram actually chooses one of the directions.

q-7004.text: When turning left in this situation, are obliged to give way to vehicles approaching from the opposite direction?
q-7004.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A rail vehicle's priority over other vehicles applies regardless of its direction of travel, so a tram turning left does not give way to oncoming vehicles. Special care and readiness to stop still apply.

q-7005.text: In this situation, are you obliged to signal the intention to turn?
q-7005.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a place where the track allows travel in different directions, the tram chooses its direction and must signal that intention. The signal is given early enough for the other road users to adjust their behaviour.

q-7006.text: Does the rail switch positioned in such a way allow for a turning manoeuvre to the right at the intersection?
q-7006.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A tram's direction of travel is set by the position of the switch, and the setting shown in the material leads in a direction other than right. Attempting to turn without resetting the switch risks derailment, so entry is not permitted.

q-7007.text: Is it always prohibited to reverse a two-coach tram?
q-7007.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Reversing a two-car tram is not absolutely prohibited — it is permitted when the traffic situation requires it and the manoeuvre is carried out safely, if necessary with the help of another person. It is prohibited, however, in places where it would endanger safety.

q-7008.text: Are you allowed to stop a two-coach tram on the rail switch while reversing?
q-7008.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping the set on a switch while reversing is not permitted, because the cars then stand on the turnout and moving off again risks derailment. The manoeuvre must be planned so that the switch is passed over completely without stopping.

q-7009.text: In this situation, are you allowed to overtake the cyclist?
q-7009.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In the situation shown no overtaking ban applies, so the manoeuvre is permitted. When overtaking a cyclist, keep a safe distance of no less than 1 m and make sure you will not force them to change course.

q-7010.text: In this situation, driving a tram, are you allowed to overtake the cyclist just before the pedestrian crossing sign?
q-7010.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In the situation shown the manoeuvre is not covered by the overtaking ban that applies directly before a pedestrian crossing, so the tram may overtake the cyclist. Special care and watching people approaching the crossing are necessary.

q-7011.text: In this situation, in a built-up area, are you allowed to overtake the municipal police vehicle flashing blue signal lights and sound signal with a changing tone?
q-7011.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A vehicle emitting a blue flashing light and a sound signal of varying tone is an emergency vehicle, and in a built-up area overtaking such a vehicle is prohibited. You must make its passage easier and, if necessary, make room for it.

q-7012.text: Are you allowed to overtake the emergency services vehicle in a built-up area?
q-7012.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In a built-up area you may not overtake an emergency vehicle, because its route is unpredictable and it may suddenly change course or speed. Instead of overtaking, make its passage easier.

q-7013.text: In this situation, are you allowed to overtake the motorcyclist while maintaining a distance of 1 m?
q-7013.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When overtaking a motorcyclist a safe distance of no less than 1 m applies, so keeping such a distance meets the requirement of the rules. The same rule applies to overtaking a bicycle, a moped, an electric scooter and a pedestrian.

q-7014.text: Are you allowed to increase speed while being overtaken by another vehicle?
q-7014.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The one being overtaken must not increase speed or hinder the manoeuvre, because lengthening the overtaking distance exposes the overtaking driver to a head-on collision. If necessary, you should even slow down and move closer to the right edge.

q-7015.text: Are you allowed to exceed the permissible speed binding in a given section of the road when overtaking?
q-7015.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking does not entitle you to exceed the permitted speed — it applies at all times on a given stretch of road. If the manoeuvre cannot be carried out without exceeding the limit, it must be abandoned.

q-7018.text: When driving a tram, are you allowed to use the high beam lights on an unlit road if you do not blind other drivers?
q-7018.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On an unlit road main-beam headlights may be used, provided you do not dazzle the drivers of other vehicles or pedestrians. The lights must be switched to dipped as soon as such a possibility of dazzling arises.

q-7020.text: When driving a tram during a stop resulting from the traffic conditions, under reduced air transparency, can you use the front fog lights?
q-7020.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Front fog lights may be used when the clarity of the air is reduced, also during a stop resulting from traffic conditions, because they improve the vehicle's visibility. Once conditions improve, these lights must be switched off.

q-7021.text: During a tram stop resulting from road traffic conditions, are you allowed to turn on the emergency lights?
q-7021.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A stop resulting from traffic conditions is a normal part of driving and does not require the hazard lights. The hazard warning serves to warn of an immobilised vehicle or another danger on the road.

q-7023.text: When driving a tram from dusk to down on an unlit road in a built-up area, are you allowed to use the high beam lights?
q-7023.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban on main-beam headlights in a built-up area concerns lit roads; on an unlit road from dusk to dawn the tram driver may use them. The condition is switching to dipped headlights immediately whenever others could be dazzled.

q-7025.text: When driving a tram with the high beam lights turned on, are you obliged to switch to the low beam lights in the eventuality of blinding pedestrians walking in a column?
q-7025.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle other road users, including pedestrians walking in a column. The tram driver switches to dipped headlights early enough, before the column is in the beam.

q-7027.text: Can you in this situation use the sound signal?
q-7027.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sound signal may be used when it is needed to warn of danger, and the situation in the material requires it. A tram cannot steer round an obstacle, so a sound warning is sometimes the only way to avoid a collision.

q-7028.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-7028.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-7029.text: When leaving the depot onto a road, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-7029.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving the depot onto the road is joining the traffic, which requires special care and giving way to all road users on the road. You may move off only after making sure you will cut in on nobody.

q-7030.text: In this situtaion, should you start braking?
q-7030.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation in the material heralds a need to reduce speed, and a tram brakes over a much longer stretch than a car and cannot leave the track. Braking must therefore begin early and smoothly.

q-7031.text: Are you allowed to use the sound signal, in ths situation?
q-7031.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The tram driver has the right to use the sound signal when it serves to warn of the danger shown in the material. The signal does not, however, replace reducing speed or readiness to brake.

q-7032.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution, in this situation?
q-7032.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every driver must take care throughout the journey: watch the road and behave so as not to create a hazard. In the situation shown nothing removes that duty.

q-7033.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution in this situation?
q-7033.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-7034.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop in the place indicated by the conditional stop line?
q-7034.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A conditional stop line marks the place where the driver stops if they must give way, and in the situation shown that is necessary. The stop is made before the line, not on it.

q-7035.text: In this situation, do you have the right to continue driving provided you yield the right of way to pedestrians?
q-7035.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal or sign shown in the material that applies at this place prohibits travel, and giving way to pedestrians does not lift that prohibition. You may move off only when the signal or the traffic arrangement permits it.

q-7036.text: In this situation, should you prepare yourself for braking?
q-7036.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation in the material heralds a possible danger, so the tram driver should reduce speed earlier and be ready to brake immediately. Readiness shortens the reaction time, which with a tram's long braking distance is decisive.

q-7037.text: In this situation, should you carefully observe pedestrians at the bus stop?
q-7037.explanation: Correct answer: YES. People waiting at a stop often step onto the tramway without checking whether a tram is coming. The tram driver must watch them closely, slow down and be ready to stop.

q-7038.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to pedestrians?
q-7038.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The pedestrians shown in the material have priority, so the driver must give way to them — they may not drive into their path or force them to speed up or stop. If necessary, they stop the vehicle.

q-7039.text: When driving a tram in this situation, are you allowed to use the sound signal?
q-7039.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In the situation shown the sound signal serves to warn a person who may not notice the approaching tram. It may be used when it is necessary for safety, not to hurry others along.

q-7040.text: In this situation, when driving a tram, are you obliged to yield the right of way to a cyclist riding on a bicycle lane?
q-7040.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver crossing a cycle path must give way to a cyclist riding along it. A tram's priority over other vehicles does not release it from that duty.

q-7041.text: Are you allowed to overtake a cyclist, if the distance between the tram and the cyclist is 0.5 m?
q-7041.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When overtaking a cyclist, the driver must keep a safe distance of no less than 1 m. A distance of 0.5 m is too small, so the manoeuvre may not be carried out — follow the cyclist to a place where the required distance will be possible.

q-7042.text: Are you obliged to make sure that all passengers have left the tram, before entering into the depot?
q-7042.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before entering the depot premises, the tram driver checks that no passenger has remained in the cars. The depot is not a place accessible to travellers, and a person left there would be exposed to the movement of rail vehicles.

q-7043.text: Are you allowed to enter the premises of the depot without making sure that all passengers have left the tram?
q-7043.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Entering the depot is permitted only after checking that no passenger has remained in the cars. Shunting takes place on the depot premises, in which an outsider would be in serious danger.

q-7044.text: Are you obliged to secure the tram from self-moving, if you intend to move away from it?
q-7044.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When walking away from the tram, the driver must secure it against moving off on its own, that is, immobilise it with the parking brake. An unsecured rail vehicle can roll away down a gradient in the track and create a very serious hazard.

q-7045.text: Prior to moving away from the tram, are you obliged to secure it from being started by an unauthorized person?
q-7045.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before walking away from the tram, it must also be secured against being started by an unauthorised person: switch off the traction circuits and take the items that allow them to be switched on. The parking brake alone is not enough here.

q-7046.text: If you are involved in a road accident in which there are injured persons, are you allowed to move away from the scene of the incident after calling the emergency services?
q-7046.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When there are injured people in an accident, the participant remains at the scene until the Police arrive, and calling the emergency services does not lift that duty. You may leave solely to fetch help, if there is no other way.

q-7047.text: If you are involved in a road accident in which there are injured persons, are you allowed to move the vehicle away from the intersection not to obstruct the movement of other vehicles?
q-7047.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In an accident with injured people the vehicles are not moved, because that would destroy the traces needed to establish what happened. Traffic disruption gives way to the duty to keep the scene unchanged; the Police, once there, will direct traffic.

q-7048.text: If you are involved in a road accident in which there are injured persons, are you obliged to leave the tram at the scene of the incident?
q-7048.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In an accident with injured people the tram stays at the scene, and the driver does not change its position until the Police arrive. The position of the vehicles and the traces serve to establish later what happened.

q-7049.text: If you are involved in a road accident in which there are no casualties or injured persons, are you obliged to call the police?
q-7049.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When nobody is killed or injured, it is a collision: the participants remove the vehicle from the place where it obstructs traffic and exchange details, and calling the Police is not compulsory. It is worth calling them when there is no agreement about what happened.

q-7051.text: If you are involved in a road accident, are you obliged to provide your personal details at the request of another person involved in the accident?
q-7051.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident must give their personal details and the details of the vehicle's owner or keeper at the request of another person involved in the incident. Refusing would make it impossible for the injured to pursue claims.

q-7052.text: You are involved in a road accident. Are you obliged to provide necessary assistance to the injured person even though you do not have qualification as a paramedic?
q-7052.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to give the injured the necessary help applies to every participant in an accident, regardless of medical qualifications. Help is given within the limits of your own skills, and its basis is calling the services and securing the scene.

q-7053.text: You are involved in an accident. Are you obliged to provide your personal details at the request of the tram passenger who is also involved in the accident?
q-7053.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A tram passenger involved in an accident is a participant in it, so at their request the tram driver gives their personal details. This duty does not depend on whether the passenger was injured.

q-7054.text: Can the use of amphetamine increase the driver's inclination to risky and aggressive behavior?
q-7054.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Amphetamine stimulates, inflates the assessment of one's own abilities and weakens criticism, so the tram driver is inclined to drive faster and make risky decisions. When the stimulation wears off, severe tiredness and a drop in concentration follow.

q-7055.text: Can the use of sedatives or sleeping pills affect the way of driving a tram?
q-7055.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Sedatives and sleeping pills lengthen reaction time, cause drowsiness and weaken concentration, and their effect often lasts many hours after taking them. Before driving, check whether the medicine in question rules out driving.

q-7056.text: Can alcohol consumed induce changes in a tram driver's field of vision?
q-7056.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Alcohol narrows the field of vision, weakens peripheral vision and makes it harder to judge distance and speed. The tram driver notices a pedestrian stepping onto the tramway from the side later, and their reaction is delayed.

q-7057.text: Do psychoactive substances affect the ability to safely drive a tram, even by an experienced tram driver?
q-7057.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Psychoactive substances alter perception, reaction time and the assessment of situations, and neither experience nor routine compensates for that. Ingrained habits then work too slowly and are sometimes triggered at the wrong moment.

q-7058.text: Can you in any circumstances, drive a tram after taking a drug prescribed by a doctor?
q-7058.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A medicine prescribed by a doctor may also cause drowsiness, dizziness or slowed reactions and rule out driving. What decides is the content of the leaflet and the doctor's advice, not the mere fact that the medicine is on prescription.

q-7059.text: Intending to drive a tram after taking medication, should you make sure that they do not have a negative impact on your psychophysical state?
q-7059.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The tram driver is responsible for their psychophysical state before driving, so they must check the leaflet or ask a doctor about the medicine's effect on driving. With any doubt whatsoever, driving must not be started.

q-7060.text: With what maximum permissible speed can you drive a tram on single carriageway with one traffic lane in each direction, marked with this sign?
q-7060.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a road marked with the sign shown in the material, single-carriageway with one lane in each direction, a tram may travel at up to 70 km/h. This is a limit value — in worse conditions speed must be reduced further.

q-7061.text: To what place does the maximum speed indicated on this sign apply to?

options.B: The place indicating its end with the help of an appropriate sign.

q-7061.explanation: Correct answer: B. The speed limit applies until the place where it is cancelled by the appropriate sign. Neither a fork in the tracks nor the nearest junction ends it by itself, so until it is cancelled it must be observed.

q-7062.text: At what speed should you drive past the tram rail switch?

options.A: At a speed not less than indicated by the sign.
options.C: At a speed taking into account the speed of the tram you are passing.

q-7062.explanation: Correct answer: B. A crossing frog is passed at a safe speed, suited to the state of the track and the load of the car, because the wheels cross a gap in the rail there. Passing too fast risks blows to the wheelset and derailment.

q-7064.text: To what place does the maximum speed indicated by this sign apply to?
q-7064.explanation: Correct answer: A. The restriction from this sign concerns a section ending at the fork in the tracks — there it stops applying. A pedestrian crossing or a road junction has no effect on its extent.

q-7065.text: What is the permissible speed of the tram on a road marked by this sign in a built-up area in the hours 5:00 - 23:00?
q-7065.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a road marked with this sign, in a built-up area, the permitted speed for a tram is 50 km/h. This is a maximum value — in heavy traffic, on a curve of the track or on a slippery rail you must drive slower.

q-7067.text: At what speed can you drive a tram on a road marked by this sign, in a built-up area in the hours 5:00 - 23:00?
q-7067.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a built-up area a tram may travel at no more than 50 km/h; the higher values in the other answers do not apply in such a place. Before stops and where pedestrians may step onto the tramway, speed must be reduced further still.

q-7068.text: In what situation, is it most difficult to assess the distance from a vehicle being passed or parked?

options.C: When the roadway or track is covered in snow.

q-7068.explanation: Correct answer: C. Snow covers the rails and the edges of the carriageway, so the tram driver loses reference points and cannot see exactly where the track will lead. Judging the distance from a parked vehicle is then hardest and requires slowing down markedly.

q-7069.text: What distance should you maintain from the preceding tram?

options.A: 30-50 m when driving at a speed of 50 km/h.
options.C: Safe, necessary to avoid a collision.

q-7069.explanation: Correct answer: C. There is no fixed number of metres: the distance must be safe, that is, allow you to stop without hitting the tram ahead. It depends on speed, the state of the rails, the gradient of the track and the load of the car.

q-7070.text: How do you perform service braking in a tram?

options.A: By seamlessly pressing the brake pedal no further than the limiter, to stop at a particular place with a single pressing of the pedal.
options.B: By releasing the dead man's switch and pressing the brake pedal beyond the limiter.
options.C: By releasing the dead man's pedal.

q-7070.explanation: Correct answer: A. Service braking is carried out with smooth pressure on the brake pedal, no further than the stop, so as to stop at the planned place in one movement. Going past the stop triggers emergency braking, dangerous for standing passengers.

q-7071.text: In this situation, is driving both trams straight on simultaneously permitted?

options.B: Yes, provided you do not exceed the speed of 5 km/h.

q-7071.explanation: Correct answer: C. Both trams going straight ahead at the same time is ruled out at this place, because their paths would cross. Only the one with priority may pass, and the other waits; no speed changes that.

q-7072.text: What could be the reasons for the switch points not clinging?

options.A: Foreign objects located in between the track.

q-7072.explanation: Correct answer: C. Snow and ice packed between the blade and the stock rail do not let the blade fit exactly, which risks the switch being run through and a derailment. Before passing, the groove must be cleaned and the position of the blade checked.

q-7073.text: What could be the reason for excessive skidding?
q-7073.explanation: Correct answer: A. Crushed leaves form a greasy, very slippery film on the rail head that drastically lowers wheel grip. Starting and braking must then be carried out gently, and the sander used if necessary.

q-7074.text: What could be the reason for excessive skidding of the tram during start-upand braking?
q-7074.explanation: Correct answer: A. The black, greasy film on the rail head, known as rail slime, greatly reduces grip, so the wheels spin on starting and slide on braking. Gentle handling of the controller and sanding the rail help.

q-7075.text: In what situation is it recommended to use sandboxes constituting an equipment on the tram?

options.A: Only on surfaces covered with water.
options.B: Only on surfaces covered with snow.

q-7075.explanation: Correct answer: C. The sander is used whenever the rail is slippery, regardless of whether the cause is leaves, moisture, frost or snow. Sand increases grip, makes starting easier and shortens the braking distance.

q-7076.text: What factors might limit the tram driver's field of vision?

options.C: Ads placed on the sides of the tram.

q-7076.explanation: Correct answer: A. People in the cab hide part of the windows and distract the tram driver, so they directly reduce their field of vision. Adverts on the sides of the car do not block the road, and weather conditions are only one of many causes.

q-7077.text: Which of the mentioned factors may have an impact on reducing the driver's field of vision?
q-7077.explanation: Correct answer: B. A person standing or sitting in the cab hides part of the field of vision and draws attention away from the road. The ergonomics of the seat affect tiredness, and an answer limited to precipitation alone is too narrow.

q-7078.text: Can the increase in speed have an impact on the perception of the tram driver?

options.A: Yes, a higher speed results in a change of perception.
options.B: No, the perception at high speed does not differ from perception at lower speeds.
options.C: Yes, but only when driving in poor visibility.

q-7078.explanation: Correct answer: A. As speed increases, the field of vision narrows and the eyes focus ever further ahead of the vehicle, so objects at the side are noticed later. This happens in all conditions, not only in limited visibility.

q-7079.text: What factor may impede proper observation of the road while driving a tram at night?

options.A: Inability to distinguish shapes in the dark.
options.B: Using properly selected glasses for night driving.
options.C: Proper visual acuity of the driver.

q-7079.explanation: Correct answer: A. In the dark the eye distinguishes shapes and contrasts less well, so an obstacle is recognised much later than in daylight. Well-chosen glasses and correct visual acuity make observation easier, not harder.

q-7080.text: Can you drive through the section isolator with the drive pedal depressed (acceleration)?

options.B: No, because this may cause damage to the overhead line and the pantograph.

q-7080.explanation: Correct answer: B. Under a section insulator the current draw must be interrupted: with a loaded pantograph a strong electric arc forms that burns out the overhead line and the pantograph strip. The traction pedal is released before the insulator and pressed again only beyond it.

q-7081.text: Which railroad switch is responsible when driving on/under the switch points?
q-7081.explanation: Correct answer: B. Facing-point running occurs at a facing switch, which the wheels enter from the blade end, so it is the blades' position that decides the direction of travel. Before entering, make sure the blade fits exactly against the stock rail.

q-7082.text: What should be taken into consideration when passing through the tram frog?

options.A: The number of passengers in the tram
options.C: The speed of the preceeding and following tram.

q-7082.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a crossing frog the guiding grooves are shallow, so the wheel flange loses sure guidance and may climb onto the rail. It is passed slowly and smoothly, without harsh braking or acceleration.

q-7084.text: What setting of the reverser may cause the inability to drive a two-carriage tram?

options.A: In the first carriage it is set to "P" in the second carriage to "0".
options.B: In the first carriageit is set to "P" in the second carriage to "P".
options.C: In the first carriage it is set to "T" in the second carriage to "0".

q-7084.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a two-car set the direction is set with the reverser of the leading car, and the reverser of the second car must remain in the zero position. Setting both to the same working position does not let the control circuit close, and the set will not move.

q-7085.text: What setting of the reverser may cause the inability to drive a single-carriage tram?
q-7085.explanation: Correct answer: A. The zero position is neutral — no direction of travel has been selected, so the traction circuit stays open and the car will not move. Before setting off, the reverser is set to the position for the intended direction.

q-7086.text: What setting of the reverser may cause the inability to drive a double-carriage tram?

options.A: In the first carriage the reverser is set to "P" and in the second carriage to "0".
options.B: In the first carriage the reverser is set to "P" and in the second carriage to "T".
options.C: In the first carriage the reverser is set to "T" and in the second carriage to "0".

q-7086.explanation: Correct answer: B. The reverser of the second car should stand in the zero position; setting opposite directions in the first and second cars means contradictory commands and prevents the circuit from closing, so the set stays put.

q-7087.text: What should you do upon occurrence of an excessive wheel slip (Spinning) during start-up?

options.A: Stop the carriages and then start moving.
options.B: Reduce the intensity of the tram's acceleration.
options.C: Increase the intensity of the tram's acceleration.

q-7087.explanation: Correct answer: B. Wheel spin means the tractive force has exceeded the grip of wheel on rail, so the intensity of acceleration must be reduced until the wheels regain grip. Increasing the drive deepens the slip and polishes the running surface.

q-7088.text: How should you set the hydraulically controlled facing-point switch in the event of the necessity to drive when reversing a double carriage tram?

options.A: Set it to the desired driving direction.
options.C: Do not set it, because it sets itself under the weight of the passing tram.

q-7088.explanation: Correct answer: A. A facing switch does not set itself — before passing it must be set to the required direction and the blade checked for fit. Running onto a wrongly set switch risks it being run through and the cars derailing.

q-7089.text: How should you set the trailing-point switch in the event of the necessity to drive while reversing the tram?

options.A: Set it to the opposite drive direction
options.C: Do not set it, because it sets itself under the weight of the passing tram.

q-7089.explanation: Correct answer: C. At a trailing switch the wheels pass through from the frog end and push the blade aside themselves, so it sets under the car's weight. Manual setting is not needed, but you must drive slowly and without jerks.

q-7090.text: What do you use to change the position of the switch points in a mechanically-controlled railroad switch?
q-7090.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a mechanically operated switch the blade is moved with the point setter, inserted into the switch and throwing the blade to the other position. The reverser selects the car's direction of travel, and the controller regulates speed — neither of them moves the blade.

q-7091.text: What do you use to change the driving speed?
q-7091.explanation: Correct answer: B. The controller is the main control element: its position decides the tractive force and braking, and thus the car's speed. The reverser serves only to select direction, and the point setter to move the switch blade.

q-7092.text: What enables the tram to drive backwards?
q-7092.explanation: Correct answer: A. Reversing is possible after setting the reverser to the position for that direction — the traction motors then run the other way. Reversing is an exceptional manoeuvre, carried out slowly and after making sure the track behind the car is clear.

q-7093.text: Can you continue driving with passengers, after noticing a breakdown in the door closing mechanism, in the first wagon?

options.B: Yes, after blocking the damaged door and turning off the "drive lock".
options.C: Yes, with the doors open, but only to the nearest tram terminus.

q-7093.explanation: Correct answer: A. A faulty door-closing mechanism means people cannot be carried safely — driving on with passengers is not allowed. The fault is reported and the operator's instructions followed; switching off the traction interlock is not acceptable.

q-7094.text: Which of the following types of brakes can not be checked at the depot?
q-7094.explanation: Correct answer: B. The electrodynamic brake works only while driving, when the motors act as generators, so on the depot premises, at a standstill and at minimal speeds, its effectiveness cannot be assessed. The shoe brakes and track brakes are checked on the spot.

q-7095.text: Which, of the following types of brakes, cannot be checked at the depot?
q-7095.explanation: Correct answer: C. The effectiveness of the electrodynamic brake shows only when driving at an adequate speed, when the motors give up energy. In the depot, on the other hand, the operation of the safety brake and the track brakes can be checked.

q-7096.text: What, among others, should be checked before you set about driving a double-carriage tram?

options.B: The condition of the coupler between the carriages.
options.C: That the carriage is equipped with a reflective warning triangle.

q-7096.explanation: Correct answer: B. Before driving a two-car set, the state and security of the coupling are checked, because it transmits the tractive and braking forces, and a faulty connection risks the set parting. The other items listed do not decide whether the cars are correctly connected.

q-7097.text: What, among others, should be checked before you set about driving a tram?

options.A: The condition of the bodywork, fastening of the passenger seats and handrails.
options.B: Validity of the tram's registration document.
options.C: That the tram is equipped with a reflective warning triangle.

q-7097.explanation: Correct answer: A. Pre-departure servicing covers the technical state of the car and the passenger area: the body and the fastening of the seats and handrails, because loose parts injure travellers under braking. The other documents and equipment listed do not apply to a tram.

q-7098.text: In what position should the coupling be when connecting tram carriages?

options.C: The position of the coupling is irrelevant.

q-7098.explanation: Correct answer: B. Before coupling, the coupler must be unfolded to its working position so that the heads meet and lock correctly. Attempting to couple with the coupler folded ends in damaging it or in an apparent, unreliable connection of the cars.

q-7099.text: What you should you not do when coupling two carriages?

options.A: Loosen the shoe brakes of the carriage to be coupled.
options.C: Open the door in the second carriage.

q-7099.explanation: Correct answer: A. The car being coupled must remain braked until the coupling locks. Releasing the shoe brakes lets it move along the track and risks crushing the person working between the cars. Lights and open doors create no such danger.

q-7100.text: What you should you not do when coupling two carriages?

options.A: Release the thrustor of the carriage to be coupled.
options.B: Turn on the side marker lights.
options.C: Adhere to the priinciples of Occupational Safety and Health (OSH)

q-7100.explanation: Correct answer: A. Releasing the brake release devices unbrakes the car being coupled, so it may roll along the track and crush a person between the cars. Marker lights are permitted, and observing the rules of safe working is a duty.

q-7101.text: What could be the cause of the diconnection of the linear contactor on the tram?

options.C: Short-circuit in the circuits of one of the engines.

q-7101.explanation: Correct answer: C. The line contactor breaks the circuit on excessive current, and such a current arises with a short circuit in the traction motor circuits — this is a protective action against damage to the equipment. Faults in the converter or the reverser show themselves differently.

q-7102.text: Which document entitles you to drive a tram?
q-7102.explanation: Correct answer: C. Driving a tram requires a separate permit, issued after completing training and passing an examination and after medical checks confirming no contraindications. A category B or C driving licence gives no such entitlement.

q-7105.text: What may cause low edges of the driving wheels?

options.A: The wheels falling off the trackway.

q-7105.explanation: Correct answer: A. It is the flange that keeps the wheel on the rail; a worn, too low flange loses its ability to guide, and the wheelset can climb onto the rail head and leave the track, especially on curves and switches. That is why flange height is checked.

q-7106.text: What might cause a chipped insert of pantograph's graphite?

options.A: A significant increase in the tram's rolling resistance.
options.B: A rockinmg of the overhead line.
options.C: Failure in operation of the power supply battery.

q-7106.explanation: Correct answer: B. A chipped insert slides unevenly along the wire, the pantograph bounces and sets the overhead line swaying, accompanied by sparking and further damage. Such an insert must be replaced before going out on the route.

q-7107.text: What may be the cause of automatic activation of the rail brakes?

options.A: Damage to the drive shaft in the rear wheelset.
options.C: Pulling of the safety brake lever by a passenger.

q-7107.explanation: Correct answer: C. A passenger pulling the safety brake lever engages the track brakes — this action is provided for and leads to a quick stop. After stopping, the cause must be established and the operator's instructions followed.

q-7108.text: What should you do if there is no response from the remote controlled rail switch?

options.B: Reverse the wagon behind the adjusting point and drive through again.
options.C: Drive according to the preset direction, assuming that the rail switch is locked.

q-7108.explanation: Correct answer: A. When a remotely controlled switch fails to operate, the driver sets it by hand and, before passing, checks that the blade fits exactly. Running onto a switch of undetermined position risks it being run through and the car derailing.

q-7110.text: What should be the distance of the lower edge of the Skimmer from the railhead?
q-7110.explanation: Correct answer: C. The lower edge of the guard should be 100 mm above the rail head. Too large a clearance will not remove an obstacle from in front of the wheel, and too small a one risks catching on the track and damaging the device.

q-7111.text: What might cause the escape of smoke from the Bogie?

options.A: Wrongly positioned reversing switch in the second wagon.
options.B: A short circuit in the motor windings.

q-7111.explanation: Correct answer: B. Smoke from under the motor bogie most often means a short circuit in the traction motor windings and burning insulation. Stop the tram, lower the pantograph and report the fault — driving on risks a fire.

q-7112.text: Can driving be continued, in the event of burn-out of one of the cable shunts in the the pantograph?

options.B: No, because further driving may lead to a short circuit of the cable with the tram's bodywork.
options.C: No, because it may lead to burn out of the second cable of the pantograph.

q-7112.explanation: Correct answer: C. When one shunt cable burns out, the whole current flows through the remaining one, which is overloaded and burns out as well. That is why the journey may not be continued — the fault must be reported and repaired.

q-7113.text: How should you execute sudden braking of the tram?

options.A: In the first phase of braking, press the brake pedal to the limiter and then release the dead man's pedal.
options.B: Press the brake pedal beyond the limiter without releasing the dead man's lever.
options.C: Press the brake pedal beyond the limiter and release the dead man's lever.

q-7113.explanation: Correct answer: C. Sudden braking is obtained by pressing the brake pedal past the stop and at the same time releasing the dead man's lever, which engages the track brakes. Only combining both actions gives the full braking deceleration.

q-7114.text: What might cause damaged to the spinning converter?

options.B: Inability to reset the reversing switch.
options.C: No cooling of the electrical equipment.

q-7114.explanation: Correct answer: C. The rotary converter powers the auxiliary circuits, including the fans cooling the electrical equipment. Its failure means no cooling, rapid overheating of the equipment and the need to break off the journey.

q-7115.text: In what situation is it recommended to use sandboxes fitted on a tram?

options.B: Only on a surface covered with water.

q-7115.explanation: Correct answer: C. Sand applied under the wheels increases grip at the contact of wheel and rail and shortens the braking distance, so it is used in sudden emergency braking. Using the sanders at every braking is unnecessary and quickly empties the hoppers.

q-7116.text: What should the driver of a tram equipped with sandboxes do in the absence of sand in the containers?

options.A: Stop the tram and wait technical service.
options.B: Fill up the sandboxes with gravel.
options.C: Top up the sandboxes at the nearest end.

q-7116.explanation: Correct answer: C. Only dry sand intended for the purpose may be put into the sanders, and it is topped up at the nearest terminus. Gravel would damage the device and the track, and stopping the set on the route would block traffic.

q-7117.text: What should you remember to do before you start towing tram carriages damaged due to a collision?

options.A: To place the warning triangle at the rear of the second carriage.
options.B: To place a yellow flashing signal.
options.C: To couple in a way that prevents uncoupling while driving.

q-7117.explanation: Correct answer: C. Before towing, check that the coupling joins both vehicles securely and will not part while moving. The connection parting on the route would mean the damaged car running out of control and an immediate danger.

q-7118.text: What should you remember before you go about pushing tram carriages damaged due to a collision?

options.A: To turn on the emergency lights in the first carriage.
options.B: To discharge the brake release in the damaged carriage.
options.C: To settle the passengers into seating positions.

q-7118.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a car being pushed the brake release valves must be opened, that is, the brakes released, otherwise the wheels stay clamped. Pushing a set with the brakes applied destroys the wheels and rails and makes moving off impossible.

q-7119.text: What should you remember when pushing tram carriages damaged as a result of collision?

options.B: To place a reflective warning triangle at the rear of second carriage?
options.C: To settle the passengers on seating positions.

q-7119.explanation: Correct answer: A. A pushed set increases the mass of the combination, and only the pushing vehicle brakes, so the braking distance grows clearly. Speed must be lowered and braking begun well in advance.

q-7120.text: What should you do in the event of an aggressive passenger behavior towards you or other passengers, if this makes driving difficult?

options.A: Continue driving to the nearest police station.
options.B: Stop the vehicle and call the relevant policing service.

q-7120.explanation: Correct answer: B. A driver who cannot concentrate on driving must stop safely and call the appropriate services. Continuing to drive in such a situation endangers the passengers and other road users.

q-7121.text: What must you most of all ensure in the event of a tram fire while driving?

options.A: Your safety and that of the passengers.
options.C: Driving in accordance with the timetable.

q-7121.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a fire, human life and health always come first: stop the vehicle, get the passengers out and see to your own safety. Property and the timetable are irrelevant in this situation.

q-7122.text: How should you about evacuating passengers, if the door gets blocked as a result of a road accident.
q-7122.explanation: Correct answer: B. When the doors are jammed, passengers are got out immediately through the emergency exits, marked in the vehicle and equipped with hammers for breaking the windows. Waiting for the services to arrive needlessly prolongs the danger.

q-7123.text: How should you behave in the event of a fire inside the tram while driving?

options.A: Drive to the nearest tram stop and begin evacuation of passengers.
options.B: Stop the vehicle, activate the fire extinguisher and independently try to extingusih the fire.
options.C: Stop the vehicle, relieve the pantograph, open the doors and commence evacuation of passengers.

q-7123.explanation: Correct answer: C. With a fire in the car you must stop immediately, lower the pantograph to cut off the power, open the doors and get the passengers out. Driving on to the stop or fighting the fire yourself before evacuation only increases the danger.

q-7124.text: In this situation, can you make a U-turn at the intersection?
q-7124.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around at this place is prohibited — this follows from the sign, signal or traffic arrangement in force at this intersection. The manoeuvre must be performed at another, permitted place, where it will not obstruct traffic.

q-7127.text: Can you use the horn in this situation to warn the pedestrian of danger?
q-7127.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The horn may be used when it is necessary to warn of an immediate danger. Warning a pedestrian who is at risk of being hit falls within this exception, but does not release you from braking and giving way to them.

q-7128.text: Should you change to the middle lane in this situation when you intend to go straight on?
q-7128.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The permitted directions of travel from individual lanes are set by the direction arrows on the roadway and the signs above it. Since going straight ahead is possible only from the middle lane, you must change lanes early enough and after checking the traffic beside you.

q-7129.text: Can you use the horn in this situation to warn the pedestrian of danger?
q-7129.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The horn may be used when it is necessary to warn of an immediate danger. Warning a pedestrian who is at risk of being hit falls within this exception, but does not release you from braking and giving way to them.

q-7130.text: When using the car extinguisher, is it proper to avoid full opening of the bonnet?
q-7130.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Opening the bonnet fully feeds the fire with oxygen and may cause a sudden flare-up. The extinguishing agent is applied through the gap of the slightly opened bonnet, standing to the side, never over the engine compartment.

q-7131.text: Is it fully justifiable in the presented situation to check if the accident perpetrator had applied emergency brake and turned off the engine?
q-7131.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Securing the scene includes immobilising the vehicles: a set handbrake and a switched-off engine reduce the risk of the car rolling away and of fire from spilt fuel. Everyone giving help checks this, not only the person at fault.

q-7132.text: Are you warned in this situation of a danger following from an unexpected change in the traffic direction?
q-7132.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning follows from the sign visible in the material — it announces an unexpected change in the direction of the road further on. You should reduce speed and exercise particular caution even before entering that place.

q-7133.text: Does this sign warn you of approaching an intersection with a one-way street without right of way from which traffic flows from the left side?
q-7133.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign visible in the material warns of a different situation than the one described in the question — not of a one-way subordinate road joining from the left. The meaning of a warning sign is read from its symbol, not from guesses about the road layout.

q-7135.text: Does this sign indicate that you must turn right at the nearest intersection if you drive a passenger car?
q-7135.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign visible in the material does not oblige the driver of a passenger car to turn right at the nearest intersection. A duty to travel in a specific direction follows only from a mandatory sign, not from every sign placed by the road.

q-7136.text: While driving a passenger car, can you turn right into the road marked this way?
q-7136.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material do not prohibit a passenger car from entering, so a right turn into this road is permitted. The manoeuvre is performed after making sure you will not cut in front of other road users.

q-7139.text: In this situation, while driving straight, do you have to give the right of way to the emergency vehicle turning left?
q-7139.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An emergency vehicle signalling its status must be allowed to pass: you give way regardless of your own direction of travel and stop if necessary. This also applies when going straight through an intersection.

q-7140.text: In this situation, do you have the right of way over the tram?
q-7140.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place the tram has priority, so you must give way and let it pass in front of you. A rail vehicle has a longer braking distance and cannot steer around an obstacle, which is why the rules often give it the advantage.

q-7141.text: In this situation, should you give the right of way to the tram?
q-7141.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In this situation the rail vehicle has priority, so you must let it pass and not enter its path. A tram takes much longer to brake than a car and cannot leave the tracks, so forcing your way in front of it is particularly dangerous.

q-7142.text: Does the green light you see at the intersection indicate a collision-free left turn?
q-7142.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A general green signal permits entry to the intersection, but does not release you from giving way to vehicles coming straight from the opposite direction and to pedestrians on the roadway you are turning into. Only a separate directional signal ensures a conflict-free passage.

q-7143.text: In this situation, can you leave the intersection?
