q-7143.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver who has entered the junction should leave it as soon as the situation ahead allows — even if the signal has already changed. Clearing the junction prevents traffic on the conflicting directions from being blocked.

q-7147.text: In this situation, intending to turn left, can you enter this intersection from any lane?
q-7147.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Before turning left you must in good time take the lane intended for travel in that direction, marked by arrows on the roadway or signs above it. Entering the intersection from any lane surprises other drivers and holds up traffic.

q-7148.text: In this situation, can you stop the car in the middle lane?
q-7148.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the middle lane of the roadway stopping is not permitted: the vehicle creates an obstacle there in a place where other drivers do not expect a stationary car. You may stop by the right edge of the roadway or off the roadway.

q-7149.text: At this intersection, can you turn left from the lane you are occupying?
q-7149.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material permit a left turn from the lane you are in. The manoeuvre must be signalled with the indicator, and way given to vehicles going straight from the opposite direction and to pedestrians on the roadway you are entering.

q-7150.text: At this intersection, can you make a U-turn from the left lane?
q-7150.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material do not prohibit turning around, and this manoeuvre is performed from the left lane. Before turning around you must signal your intention and give way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

q-7151.text: In this situation, can you overtake the tram on the left?
q-7151.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A rail vehicle running on a track near the centre of the roadway is overtaken on the right; moving out to the left would mean driving on the part of the roadway intended for the opposite direction. Overtaking on the left is therefore not permitted here and dangerous.

q-7153.text: Are you allowed to overtake the emergency vehicle beyond this sign?
q-7153.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban on overtaking an emergency vehicle applies in a built-up area. Beyond the sign visible in the material this restriction does not apply, so the manoeuvre is permitted if visibility and the general rules of overtaking allow it.

q-7156.text: While driving behind a learner driver, do you have to exercise special caution?
q-7156.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-7157.text: In this situation, are you obliged to give right of way to the pedestrians?
q-7157.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The pedestrians visible in the material have priority, so the driver must give way to them — they may not enter their path or force them to hurry or stop. If necessary, they stop the vehicle.

q-7158.text: In this situation, can you drive in front of the pedestrians?
q-7158.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Pedestrians who are stepping onto the crossing or are already on it must be given way to, and if necessary the vehicle stopped. Driving in front of them is prohibited, even if it seems there is enough time.

q-7159.text: In this situation, should you exercise special caution and, if necessary, stop?
q-7159.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the danger. When it is uncertain how the situation will develop, the only safe solution is often to reduce speed, even to a complete stop.

q-7160.text: In this situation, can you overtake the cyclist?
q-7160.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking may be started only when visibility, the width of the roadway and the situation around allow it, and the cyclist must be given a safe lateral distance of not less than 1 m. At this place the conditions do not make this possible.

q-7161.text: Did the driver properly secure the car before leaving it?
q-7161.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before leaving the vehicle, the driver must secure it against moving off by itself: apply the parking brake, leave a gear or lock engaged and secure the car against use by an unauthorised person. These conditions have been met.

q-7162.text: Did the driver properly secure the car for the duration of the stopover?
q-7162.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A parked vehicle must be secured against moving off by itself and against use by an unauthorised person. In this case one of these conditions has not been met, so the securing is incorrect.

q-7163.text: Is the conduct of the diver, who left the parked car, correct?
q-7163.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver who leaves a vehicle parked is responsible for securing it properly and for ensuring it does not obstruct traffic or create a danger. The conduct shown in the material does not meet these requirements.

q-7166.text: If you need to park the car on a road marked like this because it has broken down, are you obliged to place a warning triangle behind it within a distance of 100 m?
q-7166.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On a road marked as in the material the reflective warning triangle is placed on the roadway 100 m behind the immobilised vehicle. The hazard lights must also be on throughout the stop.

q-7167.text: Are you obliged to indicate a break-down of a motor vehicle on the express road throughout the time the vehicle remains parked there?
q-7167.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A motor vehicle immobilised due to a breakdown must be signalled for the whole time it is stationary: with the hazard lights, and when there are none or they do not work — with a reflective triangle. At high speeds this is the only chance for others to notice it in time.

q-7168.text: When do you have to carry out a periodic technical check-up of a passenger car?

options.C: Before the lapse of the deadline indicated in the registration card of the car.

q-7168.explanation: Correct answer: C. The date of the next technical inspection is entered in the registration document, and that is what binds the driver — the intervals are not the same for all vehicles. Driving after that date means a vehicle without a valid inspection.

q-7169.text: What is the maximum number of motorcycles which may ride in an organized column?
q-7169.explanation: Correct answer: A. An organised column of motorcycles may number at most 10 vehicles. The limit lets other drivers overtake the group safely and join the traffic, because too long a string of vehicles would practically block the road.

q-7170.text: Which of the following activities are you not allowed to perform while riding a motorcycle?

options.B: Using a mobile phone while riding, if this requires you to hold the phone in your hand.

q-7170.explanation: Correct answer: B. While driving, the driver may not use a phone that has to be held in the hand — it takes the hand off the steering wheel and attention off the road. Hands-free kits and navigation that do not occupy a hand are allowed.

q-7171.text: Can you ride a towed motorcycle if you do not hold a motorcycle licence?

options.B: Yes, if the motorcycle is towed by means of a rigid coupling.
options.C: Yes, regardless of the type of coupling.

q-7171.explanation: Correct answer: A. The person sitting at the controls of a towed motorcycle is still riding it, so they must hold the entitlement of the appropriate category. The type of connection — rigid or flexible — changes nothing here.

q-7173.text: What should you do before you check the level of oil in the engine?

options.A: Put the motorcycle on the side rest.
options.C: Turn off the engine and wait a few minutes.

q-7173.explanation: Correct answer: C. After switching off the engine the oil must drain back to the sump, otherwise the measurement will read low. The motorcycle is stood upright for this, because leaning on the side stand also falsifies the reading.

q-7176.text: In which of the following vehicles can you enter the road marked this way?

options.A: In a light, four-wheeled vehicle, regardless of the purpose.
options.B: In a moped, going to the next exit.
options.C: In a tractor, if you are performing a cleaning job on the road.

q-7176.explanation: Correct answer: C. Vehicles slower than the traffic on it may not enter a road signed this way, including mopeds and light quadricycles. The exception concerns vehicles carrying out cleaning or maintenance work on that road.

q-7177.text: Should a tractor be equipped with a fire extinguisher?

options.C: Only if it is carrying a trailer.

q-7177.explanation: Correct answer: A. An agricultural tractor must be equipped with a fire extinguisher regardless of whether it is towing a trailer. The extinguisher should be placed in an easily accessible place and be in working order with a current inspection.

q-7178.text: What distance should you keep from the car travelling in front of you?

options.A: It solely depends on your skills and experience.
options.B: The distance necessary to avoid a crash in the event that the car in front of you brakes or stops.
options.C: A distance equal to at least twice the length of your car, regardless of the speed and conditions on the road.

q-7178.explanation: Correct answer: B. The distance is chosen so that you can stop without a collision if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly. It depends on speed, the state of the surface and visibility, not on a fixed number of vehicle lengths.

q-7179.text: Approximately, by how much does the braking distance increase if speed is doubled?
q-7179.explanation: Correct answer: A. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed, so doubling it makes that distance roughly four times longer. On top of that comes the stretch covered during the reaction time, which grows in direct proportion to speed.

q-7180.text: What should you pay most attention to when passing another vehicle?

options.A: To proper positioning of your hands on the steering wheel.

q-7180.explanation: Correct answer: C. When passing oncoming traffic the vehicles drive past each other in opposite directions, so a safe lateral distance decides; with large, wide vehicles it must be increased and speed reduced if necessary. The position of the hands alone does not protect against a scrape.

q-7181.text: What does the safe distance you are required to keep while driving behind another car depend on?

options.A: On the speed with which you're driving.
options.B: On the power of your engine.
options.C: On the width of the road.

q-7181.explanation: Correct answer: A. The higher the speed, the longer the distance covered during the reaction time and the longer the braking distance, so the gap from the vehicle ahead must grow with speed. Engine power and the width of the carriageway do not decide a safe distance.

q-7182.text: What can you expect while braking forcefully in these road conditions?

options.A: Increased traction of the wheels to the road.
options.C: Decreased traction of the wheels to the road.

q-7182.explanation: Correct answer: C. Under harsh braking in unfavourable conditions the wheels easily lose grip and may lock, so the braking distance grows and the vehicle stops responding to the steering. Brake early and smoothly.

q-7183.text: What is the distance of the agricultural tractor from the preceding vehicle dependent on?

options.A: The situation on the road and the reaction time of the driver.
options.C: Only the type of surface of the road.

q-7183.explanation: Correct answer: A. The distance is chosen according to the conditions as a whole — speed, weather, the state of the surface and the load — allowing for the time the driver needs to react and stop a heavy combination. The weather alone or the type of surface alone does not describe the whole situation.

q-7185.text: If, at night, you pass another car lighting the road with its lights, can this stop you from noticing any obstacles on the road?

options.A: Yes, because there is a possibility of being temporarily blinded by the lights.
options.B: No, the lights of the car coming from the opposite direction always improve visibility on the road.
options.C: No, this does not affect the visibility on the road.

q-7185.explanation: Correct answer: A. The lights of an oncoming vehicle cause momentary dazzle, after which the eye cannot distinguish objects in the dark part of the road for several seconds. That is why you should look at the right edge of the carriageway and slow down.

q-7186.text: Should you be more alert when you're driving at night?

options.A: Yes, because visibility at night is limited.
options.B: No, because there is less traffic on the road at night.
options.C: No, because at night one can turn on high-beam lights.

q-7186.explanation: Correct answer: A. At night the driver sees only the stretch lit by the lights, judges distances worse and notices pedestrians and obstacles later. Lighter traffic and the possibility of using main beam do not make up for that, so attention must be greater.

q-7187.text: Which of the following factors may affect the observation of the road by a driver of a farm tractor?

options.B: The type of surface on which the tractor is moving.

q-7187.explanation: Correct answer: A. Tiredness weakens visual acuity, narrows the field of observation and lengthens reaction time, so the driver notices changes on the road later. The type of surface and the width of the lane affect the handling of the tractor, not the ability to observe.

q-7188.text: What factors may be an obstacle for proper observation of the road by a driver of a farm tractor driving at night?

options.A: Inability to distinguish shapes in the dark and sensitivity to being blinded.
options.B: The use of proper glasses for driving at night.
options.C: The sharpness of the driver’s vision.

q-7188.explanation: Correct answer: A. In the dark the eye distinguishes shapes and contrasts less well, and sensitivity to dazzle from lights worsens perception further. Good visual acuity and the right glasses make observation easier, so they cannot disturb it.

q-7189.text: What endorsement is required in a registration card for a tractor constituting a part of trackless train to be considered roadworthy?

options.A: On structural speed limit of 25 km/h.
options.B: On being equipped with an additional hydraulic brake.
options.C: On a permit to transport passengers for tourist purposes.

q-7189.explanation: Correct answer: A. A tractor pulling a tourist road train is admitted to traffic only when the registration document carries an entry limiting the design speed to 25 km/h. This condition follows from the safety of the people carried in the trailers.

q-7191.text: Which of the following documents is required to register a tractor?

options.A: A certificate of payment of an accident (AC) insurance of the tractor.
options.B: The ownership title of the tractor.
options.C: A statement of the owner confirming the payment of the tax.

q-7191.explanation: Correct answer: B. To register, ownership of the vehicle must be proved, for example with a purchase agreement or an invoice. Voluntary comprehensive insurance and a declaration of tax paid are not registration documents.

q-7192.text: When must you conduct periodic technical inspection of a tractor trailer subject to registration?

options.B: Before the lapse of the deadline indicated in the registration card.
options.C: Only when the registration card is confiscated by a police officer.

q-7192.explanation: Correct answer: B. The date of the next technical inspection is entered in the registration document, and the inspection must be carried out before it passes. There is no fixed "every two years" rule, and retention of the document by a police officer is a consequence of a breach, not a deadline.

q-7198.text: How many times a week may the daily driving time of a driver working in road transport be extended to 10 hours?
q-7198.explanation: Correct answer: B. The basic daily driving time is 9 hours, and at most twice a week it may be extended to 10 hours. This is an exception, and its use can be seen in the tachograph records.

q-7199.text: What type of driver's activity does supervision of unloading constitute?
q-7199.explanation: Correct answer: B. Supervising unloading is performing work duties, so this time counts as other work, not as a break or a period of availability. The appropriate mode must be set on the tachograph.

q-7202.text: What can you expect during sudden braking in these road conditions?

options.A: Increased traction of the wheels to the road.
options.C: Decreased traction of the wheels to the road.

q-7202.explanation: Correct answer: C. Harsh braking in such conditions reduces the grip of the wheels on the road: the wheels may lock or slide, and the vehicle loses steering and carries on almost in a straight line. Brake gently and early enough.

q-7210.text: Which of the following elements constitute the equipment of a bus whose permissible speed limit is 100 km/h?

options.A: Tyres with a tread of at least 6 mm.
options.C: Three-point safety belts on all seats.

q-7210.explanation: Correct answer: B. A bus for which a speed of 100 km/h is permitted must be equipped with a first-aid kit. The 6 mm tread and three-point belts on all seats mentioned in the other answers are not among those requirements.

q-7211.text: What is the maximum speed set by a certified speed limiter, which forms a part of the equipment of a bus?
q-7211.explanation: Correct answer: A. The type-approved limiter fitted in a bus is set so that the vehicle cannot exceed 100 km/h. The device limits the fuel supply and works independently of the limit in force on the road in question.

q-7213.text: What is the maximum number of hours by which the daily period of driving of a vehicle performing road transport maybe extended?
q-7213.explanation: Correct answer: A. The daily driving time is 9 hours and may be extended to at most 10 hours, and no more often than twice a week. The rules on drivers' working time allow no higher values.

q-7214.text: What type of a driver's work is the checking and gathering of documents concerning the transport?
q-7214.explanation: Correct answer: A. Preparing and checking transport documents is performing work duties, so it counts as other work. It is not a break, because the driver is not resting during that time, nor a period of availability.

q-7215.text: How should you drive a bus on a bend of the road?

options.A: Smoothly adjust the trajectory, taking into account the angle of the bend.
options.B: Follow the bend with the clutch pedal pressed down.
options.C: Maintain the maximum RPM along the whole length of the bend.

q-7215.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a curve the line is steered smoothly, without jerking the wheel, adapting it to the curvature — that way the long body does not stray into the neighbouring lane and the passengers keep their balance. Driving with the clutch pressed deprives the vehicle of drive and control.

q-7216.text: What type of engine oil should you use in diesel engines used in buses?

options.C: As specified by the bus manufacturer.

q-7216.explanation: Correct answer: C. The grade and type of oil are specified by the bus manufacturer in the owner's manual, because the parameters are matched to the particular engine design. A random oil speeds up wear and may lead to failure of the power unit.

q-7217.text: What oil should be used to top up oil in a bus engine?

options.A: Oil characterised by significantly higher stickiness than the oil in the engine.
options.B: Oil of the same class as the oil in the engine.

q-7217.explanation: Correct answer: B. Top up with oil of the same grade as the oil already in the engine, because a mixture of different oils loses its properties and protects the parts less well. Changing the grade is possible only with a full oil change.

q-7218.text: If you change lanes once you go past this sign, are you obliged to indicate your intention of making such a manoeuvre?
q-7218.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intention to change lane is signalled in advance with the indicator, and the indicator is switched off right after the manoeuvre is completed. A road sign does not lift this duty — the signal is given regardless of whether other road users are nearby.

q-7219.text: In this situation, as you continue driving, are you obliged to indicate your intention of changing lanes?
q-7219.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intended lane change must be shown in advance with the indicator, and after the manoeuvre the signal switched off. A switched-on indicator gives no priority — you must still make sure the lane change will obstruct no one.

q-7221.text: In this situation, can you bypass the car which has stopped in order to give way to a pedestrian?
q-7221.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Passing a vehicle that has stopped before a crossing to give way to a pedestrian is prohibited: the view is blocked and the pedestrian is already on the roadway. You should stop and wait until they have crossed.

q-7223.text: Are you obliged to exercise particular caution when passing the tram stop situated as shown?
q-7223.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a tram stop passengers get on and off, often straight from the roadway, so the driver must exercise particular caution, reduce speed and be ready to stop. Pedestrians walking to and from the tram must be allowed to cross.

q-7224.text: In this situation, can you drive past the traffic lights, if stopping in front of them would require rapid braking?
q-7224.explanation: Correct answer: YES. If at the moment the signal changes the vehicle is so close to the traffic light that stopping would require harsh braking, you may pass the traffic light. Such braking could cause a rear-end collision, which is why the rule allows you to continue.

q-7225.text: Does a special trailer, designed only to be pulled by a tractor or a slow-moving vehicle, require registration?

options.C: Yes, if it is subject to annual technical check-up.

q-7225.explanation: Correct answer: B. A special trailer adapted solely for towing by an agricultural tractor or a slow-moving vehicle is not subject to registration. The exemption follows from its purpose, not from whether it undergoes a technical inspection.

q-7230.text: Should you take into consideration the probability of the pedestrian bursting onto the road in this situation?
q-7230.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver is obliged to anticipate the behaviour of pedestrians and to allow for their sudden step onto the roadway, especially where visibility is limited. Speed should be chosen so as to be able to stop the vehicle before the pedestrian.

q-7231.text: While overtaking a cyclist in conditions of limited visibility, outside a built-up area, should you use short horn signals?
q-7231.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Outside a built-up area, with reduced air transparency, a brief horn signal warns the cyclist that they are being overtaken and reduces the risk of them suddenly swerving left. The manoeuvre itself is performed with a safe lateral distance.

q-7232.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise caution?
q-7232.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every driver is obliged to exercise caution throughout the journey: to watch the road and behave so as not to create a danger. Nothing in the situation shown removes this duty.

q-7235.text: When driving in a state of emotional arousal, does the precision and accuracy of your reactions in dangerous situation improve?
q-7235.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Strong emotional arousal narrows the field of attention and impairs the assessment of situations, so reactions become hasty and less precise. Before driving it is worth calming down, and if necessary breaking the journey.

q-7236.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the tram?
q-7236.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking a tram is permitted when no overtaking ban applies at this place and the manoeuvre endangers no one. A rail vehicle running on tracks located in the middle of the roadway is overtaken on its right side.

q-7237.text: Which of the following speeds is not allowed in a residential area?
q-7237.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a residential zone the permitted speed is 20 km/h, so 25 km/h is already over the limit, while 10 and 15 km/h are within it. In this zone the pedestrian has priority and may use the whole width of the road.

q-7241.text: You have participated in a car accident with casualties. Are you allowed to undertake actions which might hinder establishing the course of the accident?
q-7241.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A participant in an accident with injured people may not do anything that makes it harder to establish what happened, including moving the vehicles and traces without need. The vehicle may be moved only after its position has been marked, when saving a life or clearing traffic requires it.

q-7243.text: Are you allowed in this place to change your lane to the lane by the right edge of the road?
q-7243.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A lane change must not be made where the markings visible in the material prohibit it, for example a solid line separating the lanes. The manoeuvre is also not permitted when it would force another driver to brake harshly.

q-7247.text: In this situation in a built-up area, are you obliged to allow the bus join traffic if the driver signals such an intention?
q-7247.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area the driver is obliged to allow a bus to move off from a marked stop when its driver signals that intention with the indicator. The driver giving way should slow down or stop, and the bus driver must not force their way in.

q-7248.text: When driving a motor vehicle with a gross weight of 2.5 t, in a built-up area as marked on the road, can you drive at a speed of 70 km/h?

options.C: No, if you are driving in the hour 5.00 - 23.00.

q-7248.explanation: Correct answer: A. The speed at this place is decided by the sign shown in the material, which raises the limit applying in the built-up area, so driving at 70 km/h in a vehicle with a maximum permissible mass of 2.5 t is allowed. The time of day is irrelevant here.

q-7249.text: At what maximum speed limit can you drive a passenger car of maximum permissible weight 3 t, on a single-carriage expressway?
q-7249.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a single-carriageway expressway a car may travel at no more than 100 km/h. The speed of 120 km/h applies to a dual-carriageway expressway, and 90 km/h to other roads outside a built-up area.

q-7251.text: While turning left, should you give the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction?
q-7251.explanation: Correct answer: NO. As a rule the driver turning left gives way to vehicles going straight from the opposite direction, but in this situation the order of passage is decided by the sign or signal visible in the material, which gives priority to you. Even so, make sure the oncoming vehicle really is slowing down.

q-7253.text: What must you not allow a passenger to do when you transport him on a motorcycle?

options.A: To talk on a mobile telephone.

q-7253.explanation: Correct answer: C. A passenger carried on a motorcycle must wear a fastened protective helmet, so the rider may not allow them to ride without one. Talking to the rider or on the phone is not prohibited for a passenger.

q-7254.text: In this situation, can you turn right in front of the tram?
q-7254.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A right turn would require passing in front of the tram, to which in this situation you must give way. A rail vehicle has a longer braking distance and cannot steer around an obstacle, so entering its path is not permitted.

q-7256.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have the right of way over the motorcyclist turning left?
q-7256.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The order of passage here is decided by the road layout and the signs visible in the material, from which it follows that the motorcyclist turning left must give way. Turn smoothly, watching whether they really are slowing down.

q-7257.text: In this situation, are you being warned of an intersection with a side road?
q-7257.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign visible in the material announces an intersection where the cross road is subordinate, and you are on the road with priority. Even so, approach carefully, because the driver from the side road may fail to give way.

q-7258.text: In this situation, are you approaching a road narrowing on the right?
q-7258.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign shown in the material announces a narrowing of the carriageway on the right side, that is, a loss of width from that edge. Slow down and expect to have to yield space to vehicles travelling alongside.

q-7259.text: In this situation, are you being warned of a road narrowing on the left?
q-7259.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign shown in the material announces a narrowing of the carriageway on the left side, that is, a loss of width from that edge. Slow down, take care and do not begin overtaking just before the narrowing.

q-7260.text: In this situation, are you being warned of two dangerous bends, the first to the right?
q-7260.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign shown in the material announces two dangerous bends following directly one after the other, the first leading to the right. Speed should be reduced before entering the curve, without braking sharply in the bend.

q-7261.text: Does the plate under the warning sign indicate an unexpected change in the driving direction?
q-7261.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate placed under the warning sign warns that the course of the road differs from what its previous direction would suggest, i.e. that the change of direction comes unexpectedly. Speed must be reduced before this place.

q-7262.text: In this situation, are you approaching a multi-track level crossing?
q-7262.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign visible in the material announces a railway crossing with more than one track. Approach the crossing with particular caution and do not enter the tracks unless you are certain you will be able to leave them.

q-7264.text: Does the plate under the warning sign indicate an unexpected change in the driving direction?
q-7264.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate under the warning sign informs that the road changes direction in a way unexpected for a driver who would assume it continues as before. You must slow down in advance and watch the signs ahead carefully.

q-7265.text: In this situation, are you being warned of an intersection with a major road on the right?
q-7265.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The warning sign visible in the material has a different meaning than stated in the question — it does not announce an intersection with a road with priority on the right. Always assess the order of passage on the basis of the signs in force directly before the intersection.

q-7266.text: Does this warning sign mean that you are approaching several dangerous bends, the first of which is to the right?
q-7266.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible warning sign has a different meaning than described in the question — either the number of bends or the direction of the first one does not match. Regardless, reduce speed before every bend and do not stray onto the opposite lane.

q-7267.text: Does this warning sign mean that you are approaching a place where two-way traffic starts?
q-7267.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign visible in the material warns that one-way travel ends and that beyond this point oncoming vehicles will appear. You must keep to the right side of the roadway and exercise particular caution.

q-7270.text: In this situation, are you obliged to drive straight ahead?
q-7270.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to go straight ahead follows from the mandatory sign or the lane markings visible in the material, and the driver must comply with the indicated direction. Turning contrary to such an indication is not permitted even on an empty road.

q-7271.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive, at the intersection, in the direction opposite to the direction shown on the mandatory traffic sign?
q-7271.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A mandatory sign indicates the only permitted direction of travel, and driving contrary to it is prohibited. A different direction may be chosen only where the order ceases to apply.

q-7272.text: Are you allowed to stop in the section of the roadway in front of this sign?
q-7272.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A no-stopping prohibition applies on this stretch, and it also covers a brief stop to let a passenger out. The passenger may be dropped off only at a place where stopping is allowed.

q-7273.text: In this situation, does the traffic light prohibit you to make a U-turn at this intersection?
q-7273.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A signal permitting travel does not by itself prohibit turning around at the intersection. When performing this manoeuvre, you must give way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and make sure that a sign or the traffic arrangement does not prohibit the U-turn.

q-7274.text: In this situation, are you allowed to make a U-turn at the nearest intersection?
q-7274.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition follows from the sign or the traffic arrangement visible in the material — at this intersection turning around is not permitted. The manoeuvre may be performed only where the prohibition no longer applies.

q-7276.text: In this situation, are you required to stop the vehicle in front of the pedestrian crossing?
q-7276.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping before the crossing is necessary when a pedestrian is on it or stepping onto it; in this situation there is no such need. You must, however, still exercise particular caution and be ready to brake.

q-7277.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn in this situation?
q-7277.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place turning around is prohibited, as follows from the sign or the traffic arrangement visible in the material. The manoeuvre must be moved to where it is permitted and visibility allows it to be performed safely.

q-7279.text: Does the prohibitory sign on the left side of the roadway also prohibit making a U-turn at the nearest intersection?
q-7279.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The prohibition expressed by this sign also covers turning around at the intersection before which the sign is installed. You may start travelling in the opposite direction only further on, beyond the reach of this prohibition.

q-7280.text: Are you allowed to turn right without stopping in this situation?
q-7280.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Before the turn, stopping the vehicle is required, as follows from the sign or signal visible in the material. The stop is made before the line or before the edge of the roadway of the cross road, and only then may you move off, giving way.

q-7281.text: Do you have to yield the right of way only to vehicles approaching from the right in this situation?
q-7281.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Way must be given to all entitled road users — vehicles approaching from both sides, and also the tram and pedestrians. Limiting this duty to the right side only would be a mistake.

q-7282.text: In this situation, are you required to give way to the cyclist?
q-7282.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this situation priority belongs to you, and the cyclist is obliged to give way. Even so, you must watch them and be ready to brake should they ride into your path after all.

q-7283.text: Does the prohibition expressed by this sign apply only to the side of the road on which the sign is located?
q-7283.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A prohibition sign concerning stopping or parking applies only on the side of the road on which it is installed. On the opposite side the prohibition applies only if there is a sign of its own there.

q-7284.text: You stopped in front of a pedestrian crossing. Are you also obliged to stop in front of the line immediately beyond the crossing?
q-7284.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The line directly beyond the crossing marks a separate mandatory stopping point, and stopping before the crossing does not replace it. Once the pedestrians have crossed, you must stop again, at that line.

q-7285.text: In this situation, are you being informed of the end of a road with the right of way?
q-7285.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material inform of the end of the road with priority. From this point, at the following intersections the general rules apply or priority follows from other signs, so they must be read carefully.

q-7286.text: Does the plate under this sign indicate the real course of the road with the right of way across the intersection?
q-7286.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate under the priority sign shows which way the road with priority actually runs through the intersection when it changes direction. This drawing must be taken into account when assessing to whom you must give way.

q-7287.text: Does this sign inform you about the location of a youth hostel?
q-7287.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This is an information sign from the group of facilities useful to travellers and indicates the location of a youth hostel. Signs of this kind introduce no prohibitions or orders; they only inform about a facility nearby.

q-7288.text: Does the sign on the right side of the roadway indicate the permitted driving directions from the individual traffic lanes?
q-7288.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign shows with arrows in which directions you may travel from each of the lanes. The correct lane must be taken in advance, before the intersection, because later a change of decision is no longer possible.

q-7289.text: Does the plate under this warning sign indicate the distance between the sign and a dangerous place?
q-7289.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate under a warning sign states after what distance the dangerous place begins. It is used when the sign stands further from or closer to it than usual, so that speed can be reduced in advance.

q-7290.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn left from the traffic lane you are in?
q-7290.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A left turn is not permitted from this lane — the permitted directions are set by the signs and road markings on this section. To turn, you must first move to a lane from which such a manoeuvre is allowed.

q-7291.text: Does this sign inform you of approaching the end of the motorway?
q-7291.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns that you are approaching the end of the motorway. Beyond this point the rules specific to a motorway cease to apply, so you must reduce speed in advance and allow for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

q-7292.text: Are you allowed to turn left at the nearest intersection from the traffic lane you are in?
q-7292.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The lane you are in is not intended for turning left; the permitted directions follow from the signs and road markings on this section. You must move to the correct lane in advance, before entering the intersection.

q-7293.text: Are you allowed to turn right from the traffic lane you are occupying at this intersection?
q-7293.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A right turn is not permitted from this lane — the permitted directions are defined by the traffic arrangement on this section. To turn, you must first take a lane from which the manoeuvre is allowed.

q-7294.text: In this situation, do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction?
q-7294.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The traffic arrangement in force at this place gives you priority over the oncoming vehicle. You may move off, however, only when you are sure the driver approaching from the opposite direction is taking this into account — priority does not release you from caution.

q-7296.text: Does the vertical sign on the right side inform you about a place where cyclists ride across the road?
q-7296.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a place where cyclists cross the road. Approaching it, you must take special care, slow down and be ready to give way at the cycle crossing.

q-7297.text: Does this vertical sign inform you that you are approaching a restaurant and a hotel?
q-7297.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This is an information sign about facilities for road users, and its symbols indicate a restaurant and a hotel. Signs of this group introduce no prohibitions or orders — they only inform that such facilities are nearby.

q-7299.text: In this situation, are you allowed to start overtaking?
q-7299.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Starting to overtake at this place is not permitted because of the prohibition in force here or the limited visibility of the section of road. You may overtake only when enough road can be seen to complete the manoeuvre without obstruction.

q-7300.text: In this situation, are you required to change lanes?
q-7300.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The lane you are in does not allow you to continue in the chosen direction, so you must move to the adjacent one. The lane change is made in advance, signalling it with the indicator and giving way to those travelling in that lane.

q-7301.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive over the double solid line on the roadway?
q-7301.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A double solid line separates the directions of traffic and must not be driven on, let alone crossed. You must drive on the right of the line without touching it with the wheels.

q-7302.text: In this situation, are you required to change lanes?
q-7302.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The lane you are in does not allow you to continue in the chosen direction, so you must move to the adjacent one. The lane change is made in advance, signalling it with the indicator and giving way to those travelling in that lane.

q-7303.text: In this situation, are you required to drive straight ahead at the intersection?
q-7303.explanation: Correct answer: YES. From this lane only going straight ahead is permitted — the direction is set by the signs and road markings on the approach to the intersection. If a turn was needed, the lane should have been changed earlier.

q-7304.text: In this situation, are you required to indicate your intention to change the traffic lane?
q-7304.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intended lane change is signalled with the indicator in advance and clearly, regardless of the volume of traffic and of whether anyone is travelling alongside. After the manoeuvre the signal must be switched off.

q-7305.text: Are you allowed to change to the left lane in this place?
q-7305.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place the lanes are separated by a line that must not be crossed, so moving to the left lane is prohibited. A lane change will be possible only further on, when the line becomes broken.

q-7307.text: In this situation, are you allowed to stop the vehicle on the surface closed to traffic?
q-7307.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An area closed to traffic serves neither for driving nor for stopping. It separates the streams of vehicles and is to remain free, so as not to obscure visibility and not to surprise other drivers.

q-7308.text: Are you allowed at this intersection to make a U-turn from the traffic lane you are in?
q-7308.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Turning around at the intersection is permitted from this lane, because the traffic arrangement in force here allows it. When performing the manoeuvre, you must give way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

q-7309.text: In this situation, are you driving on a one-way roadway?
q-7309.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The road is two-way, as follows from the signs and road markings shown in the material. One-way traffic is indicated by the appropriate sign at the start of the stretch, not by the number of lanes.

q-7310.text: Are you allowed only to turn left at this intersection?
q-7310.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A left turn is not the only permitted direction here — the permitted directions are shown by the signs and road markings before the intersection. The chosen direction must be signalled with the indicator.

q-7311.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn left from the traffic lane you are in?
q-7311.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The lane you are in is not intended for turning left — the permitted directions are defined by the signs and road markings. You must move to the correct lane in advance, before entering the intersection.

q-7312.text: Are you allowed to start overtaking a vehicle at this section of the road?
q-7312.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On this section overtaking is prohibited, as follows from the sign or road markings in force here. The manoeuvre may be started only where the prohibition ends and visibility allows a safe return to your lane.

q-7313.text: Are you allowed to start overtaking a vehicle at this section of the road?
q-7313.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On this section overtaking is prohibited, as follows from the sign or road markings in force here. The manoeuvre may be started only where the prohibition ends and visibility allows a safe return to your lane.

q-7314.text: Are you allowed at this intersection to turn right from the traffic lane you are in?
q-7314.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A right turn is not permitted from this lane — the permitted directions are set by the signs and road markings before the intersection. The correct lane must be taken early enough.

q-7316.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive onto the roadway surface on the left side?
q-7316.explanation: Correct answer: NO. This part of the roadway is closed to traffic and must not be entered — neither to drive on it nor to bypass a queue of vehicles. It is meant to separate the traffic streams and remain clear.

q-7317.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn left in order to park the vehicle on the pavement?
q-7317.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A left turn is prohibited at this place, and the wish to park does not lift this prohibition. Besides, parking on the pavement is permitted only where it is expressly allowed and where enough room is left for pedestrians.

q-7318.text: In this situation, are you allowed to use the surface on the left side to park the vehicle?
q-7318.explanation: Correct answer: NO. This area is closed to traffic and is not a parking place, so leaving a vehicle there is prohibited. You may park only where parking is permitted and does not obstruct others.

q-7319.text: Does this traffic light indicate that there is no collision with other traffic users when turning left?
q-7319.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An ordinary signal permitting travel does not guarantee that the road is clear. When turning left, you must give way to vehicles approaching from the opposite direction and to pedestrians crossing the roadway you are entering.

q-7320.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive straight ahead at the intersection without stopping?
q-7320.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Stopping is not mandatory here — the signal or sign in force at the approach allows you to pass through the intersection without stopping. You only need to make sure the way is clear and no one will be obstructed.

q-7321.text: In this situation, does the flashing light prohibit you from driving beyond the traffic lights?
q-7321.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A flashing yellow signal does not prohibit travel; it warns of a danger or obstruction. You must pass through the intersection with particular caution, applying the general rules of priority and the signs installed on the approaches.

q-7322.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive across the pedestrian crossing without stopping?
q-7322.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You must stop when a pedestrian is on the crossing or stepping onto it; here that is not the case. You still drive through the crossing with special care, watching the pavement and the verge.

q-7323.text: In this situation, does the flashing light warn about a danger or a traffic disruption?
q-7323.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A flashing yellow signal warns of a danger or an obstruction to traffic at this place. It does not grant priority — you must pass with particular caution and according to the general rules of priority.

q-7325.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn right at this intersection?
q-7325.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A right turn at this intersection is not permitted, as follows from the sign or signal in force at the approach. You may travel only in the direction that is allowed.

q-7327.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive beyond the traffic lights without stopping?
q-7327.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal currently in force permits travel, so stopping before the traffic light is not required. It is, however, worth passing it only when there is room beyond the intersection and you will not be left stranded on it.

q-7328.text: In this situation, are you required to stop in front of this transverse line?
q-7328.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The transverse line marks the place where the driver must stop, and it may not be crossed before stopping. You may move off after stopping, when the way is clear and priority has been given.

q-7329.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn right without stopping?
q-7329.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Before the turn, stopping the vehicle is required, as follows from the sign or signal visible in the material. The stop is made before the line or before the edge of the roadway of the cross road, and only then may you move off, giving way.

q-7330.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn right after making sure that this manoeuvre, will not obstruct other traffic users?
q-7330.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A right turn is prohibited at this place, and the absence of obstruction to others does not lift this prohibition. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the road is clear.

q-7334.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive into the intersection?
q-7334.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal in force permits entry, and the intended passage does not conflict with vehicles that have priority. You may enter on condition that the intersection can be left without stopping on it.

q-7335.text: You intend to go straight on, and the driver of the oncoming vehicle intends to turn left. Do you have to yield the right of way to him?
q-7335.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The one going straight ahead has priority, and the driver turning left must give way to oncoming vehicles. Even so, it is worth watching them and being ready to brake in case they start the manoeuvre anyway.

q-7336.text: Are you joining the traffic by driving into the transverse road in this situation?
q-7336.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Entering the cross road from a place that is not a road means joining the traffic. The driver is then obliged to give way to all road users, including pedestrians.

q-7337.text: When turning left, do you have to yield the right of way to the oncoming vehicle?
q-7337.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When turning left, the driver crosses the path of oncoming vehicles, so they are obliged to let them pass. Way must also be given to pedestrians on the crossing of the road into which you are turning.

q-7338.text: Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicles travelling along the paved road in this situation?
q-7338.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver entering a paved road from an unpaved road is always obliged to give way to vehicles travelling on that road. Joining the traffic requires particular caution and making sure that no one will be forced to brake or change their path.

q-7339.text: You intend to turn right. Do you have the right of way over vehicles travelling along the transverse road?
q-7339.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The intention to turn right alone gives no priority — the order is decided by the signs at the intersection or the right-hand rule. Travelling on a subordinate road, you must give way to all vehicles on the cross road, including those approaching from the right.

q-7341.text: Do you have to yield the right of way to vehicles approaching from the left in this situation?
q-7341.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to give way to vehicles approaching from the left follows from the signs at the intersection visible in the material — the road you are on is subordinate. You should enter only when you will not force anyone to change speed or direction.

q-7347.text: Does the plate under this sign indicate the layout of non-priority roads?
q-7347.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate placed under the priority-road sign shows the actual layout of the intersection: the thicker line marks the course of the road with priority, the thinner ones — the subordinate roads. Thanks to it the driver knows from where vehicles obliged to give way may come.

q-7348.text: Does the visible prohibitory sign prohibit you from turning right at the nearest intersection?
q-7348.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The no-right-turn sign applies at the nearest intersection before which it is installed and concerns every driver travelling on that roadway. The prohibition does not, however, apply to exits onto adjacent premises, e.g. a property or car park.

q-7349.text: Does the blinking light signal prohibit you from driving onto the tram crossing in this situation?
q-7349.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A flashing yellow signal does not prohibit passage — it warns of a particularly dangerous place and requires particular caution. Entering the tram crossing is permitted after making sure that no tram is approaching and that there is room beyond the crossing to clear the tracks.

q-7350.text: Do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the right in this situation?
q-7350.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material designate your road as the road with priority, and the right-hand rule then yields to the signs. The vehicle approaching from the right is obliged to let you pass, which does not release you from watching its behaviour.

q-7351.text: Do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the left in this situation?
q-7351.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority at an intersection is decided by signs, signals and the hierarchy of roads, not by the side from which another vehicle approaches. In this situation the vehicle on the left has priority, so you must stop and let it pass.

q-7352.text: Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left in this situation?
q-7352.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The vehicle approaching from the left has priority at this place, so you must let it pass. Giving way means refraining from moving if moving off would force another driver to change direction or speed.

q-7355.text: Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right in this situation?
q-7355.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At an intersection of equal roads, not marked with priority signs, the right-hand rule applies — the vehicle approaching from the right has priority. Your own direction of travel, including going straight ahead, does not change this order.

q-7356.text: You intend to turn left, and the driver of the oncoming vehicle intends to go straight on. Do you have the right of way over him?
q-7356.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning left, you cross the path of the oncoming vehicle, so it has priority when it is going straight ahead or turning right. The manoeuvre may be started only after letting such a vehicle pass.

q-7357.text: Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left in this situation?
q-7357.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The vehicle approaching from the left has priority at this place, so you must let it pass. Giving way means refraining from moving if moving off would force another driver to change direction or speed.

q-7359.text: Does this sign indicate that, after turning left at the intersection, you will continue moving on the major road?
q-7359.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate under the priority-road sign shows its actual course through the intersection — the thicker line bends to the left, so you keep priority when travelling in that direction. You must, however, signal the turn with the indicator and give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction on the road with priority.

q-7360.text: In this situation, when turning left, do you have to yield the right of way to oncoming vehicles going straight on?
q-7360.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning left crosses the path of oncoming vehicles, so they must give way to them. This also applies to rail vehicles and to oncoming vehicles turning right.

q-7361.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn right after making sure that you do not impede the movement of other road users?
q-7361.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The green arrow for a conditional turn allows a right turn despite the red signal, but only after stopping before the traffic light. The turn is permitted only when it will not obstruct vehicles and pedestrians that have priority.

q-7362.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-7362.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority belongs to you, and the vehicle approaching from the left is obliged to give way. When turning left, however, you must let pass vehicles coming straight from the opposite direction and pedestrians stepping onto the cross roadway.

q-7363.text: Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left in this situation?
q-7363.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The vehicle approaching from the left has priority at this place, so you must let it pass. Giving way means refraining from moving if moving off would force another driver to change direction or speed.

q-7364.text: Does the light signal being displayed allow you to go beyond the traffic lights in this situation?
q-7364.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal visible in the material prohibits passing the traffic light. The vehicle must be stopped before the traffic light, or before the stop line if one is marked, and wait for the signal permitting travel.

q-7365.text: Does the light signal displayed prohibit you from going beyond the traffic lights in this situation?
q-7365.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown prohibits passing the traffic light, so the driver must stop the vehicle before the stop line, and in its absence before the traffic light itself. The absence of other vehicles does not release you from this duty.

q-7366.text: In this situation, does the light signal displayed indicate that there is no collision with other road users when turning left?
q-7366.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A permitting signal shown by a directional traffic light concerns only travel in the direction indicated by the arrow and means that the paths of the other road users are held at that time. Even so, you should watch the intersection, because a conflict-free passage does not release you from caution.

q-7368.text: Are you allowed to go past the traffic lights in this situation?
q-7368.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You may pass the traffic light when the signal shown permits it, and also when, at a yellow signal, the vehicle is already so close that it cannot be safely stopped before the traffic light. You must then clear the intersection promptly.

q-7369.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn at the intersection in this situation?
q-7369.explanation: Correct answer: YES. No ban on turning around applies at this intersection, and the signal in force permits travel, so the manoeuvre is allowed. The driver turning around gives way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians on the crossing.

q-7371.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn at the intersection in this situation?
q-7371.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around at this place is prohibited — this follows from the sign, signal or traffic arrangement in force at this intersection. The manoeuvre must be performed at another, permitted place, where it will not obstruct traffic.

q-7372.text: In this situation, are you required to stop the vehicle for the time needed by the pedestrian to freely reach the pavement?
q-7372.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver is obliged to give way to a pedestrian on the crossing, and giving way means allowing them to cross calmly to the other side and step onto the pavement. Moving off earlier would force the pedestrian to hurry or stop, which is not permitted.

q-7373.text: Are you allowed to start driving once the pedestrians have walked onto the pavement?
q-7373.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to give way ends the moment the pedestrian leaves the crossing and steps onto the pavement — they are then no longer part of the traffic on the carriageway. Before moving off, check that nobody else is stepping onto the crossing.

q-7374.text: In this situation, are you allowed to park the vehicle on the pavement on the right side at the distance of 11 meters from the sign indicating a bus stop?
q-7374.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Near a stop a no-stopping prohibition applies within 15 m of the post or board marking the stop, and at a stop with a bay — along its whole length and 15 m before and beyond it. A distance of 11 m falls within this zone.

q-7375.text: Are you allowed to reverse beyond this information sign?
q-7375.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Beyond this sign begins a section of road on which reversing is prohibited. The ban on reversing applies, among other places, in a tunnel, on a bridge and a viaduct, and on a motorway and an expressway, because the manoeuvre creates an immediate danger there.

q-7376.text: In this situation, are you allowed to stop the vehicle in the bay?
q-7376.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The bay at a stop is intended exclusively for public transport vehicles, so other drivers must not stop in it. Occupying the bay would force the bus to stop on the roadway and block passengers getting on and off.

q-7377.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop and wait until the bus drives out of the bay?
q-7377.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver only has to let the bus merge into traffic, that is, slow down if necessary — they do not have to stop the vehicle and wait. Stopping without need could take drivers behind by surprise.

q-7379.text: In this situation, in a built-up area, are you obliged to allow the bus driver to drive out of the bay onto the roadway?
q-7379.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area the driver is obliged to allow a bus or trolleybus to join the traffic from a marked stop. If necessary, you should reduce speed or even stop the vehicle, exercising particular caution.

q-7380.text: In this situation, are you allowed to occupy more than one lane?
q-7380.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a roadway with marked lanes the driver is obliged to drive within one lane. Occupying two lanes at once is permitted only momentarily while changing lanes or when the width of the vehicle or its load requires it.

q-7381.text: Are you allowed to park the vehicle on the roadway in this place?
q-7381.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place parking on the roadway is prohibited — this follows from the signs and the shape of the road visible in the material. A vehicle left here would restrict visibility or narrow the passage, forcing others into dangerous passing manoeuvres.

q-7382.text: Are you allowed to stop the vehicle on the roadway in this place?
q-7382.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs and the shape of the road visible in the material indicate a place where a no-stopping prohibition applies. Stopping a vehicle here would obscure visibility or prevent other road users from passing freely, so it is not permitted even for a short moment.

q-7383.text: In a built-up area, on a two-way roadway with low traffic, are you allowed to park the vehicle at the left edge of the roadway?
q-7383.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Parking by the left edge of a two-way roadway is permitted in a built-up area, on a road with little traffic. The vehicle must then stand as close as possible to the edge and must not obstruct traffic or restrict visibility.

q-7384.text: Are you allowed to park the vehicle in the cycle lane shown on the left side?
q-7384.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A cycle path is intended solely for bicycle traffic, and a motor vehicle may not stand on it. Blocking it would force cyclists onto the carriageway or the pavement, which directly endangers them.

q-7385.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive on the roadway occupying its entire width?
q-7385.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver must drive as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway so as not to obstruct oncoming vehicles or those behind. Occupying the whole width of the carriageway is not permitted.

q-7386.text: You intend to turn left. In this situation, are you obliged to approach the centre of the roadway?
q-7386.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before turning left the driver is obliged to take, in good time, a position as close as possible to the centre of the roadway, and on a one-way roadway — close to its left edge. Such positioning shows others the intended manoeuvre and does not block those going straight.

q-7387.text: On the presented two-way road, are you allowed to park the vehicle by the right edge of the roadway immediately past the pedestrian crossing?
q-7387.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a two-way road with two lanes, parking is prohibited not only before a pedestrian crossing but also directly beyond it. A standing vehicle would hide pedestrians from drivers coming from the opposite direction.

q-7388.text: Do traffic rules apply in a car park located in a traffic zone?
q-7388.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A traffic zone is an area marked with signs, with internal roads, where the road traffic regulations apply. In a car park within such a zone the rules of priority, speed limits and the requirement that the driver be sober therefore apply.

q-7389.text: In this situation, before changing the lane, are you obliged to use direction-indicator signal?
q-7389.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A lane change is a manoeuvre of which others must be notified in advance and clearly with the indicator. The signal is given before the manoeuvre begins, not during it, and switched off immediately after it is completed.

q-7390.text: In this situation, when changing the traffic lane, do you have priority over the vehicles moving in the left lane?
q-7390.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver changing lanes is obliged to give way to vehicles already travelling in the lane they are entering. A lane change is permitted only when it will not force others to brake or change direction.

q-7391.text: In this situation, when changing the traffic lane, do you have the right of way over the vehicles moving in the right lane?
q-7391.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority belongs to the vehicles travelling in the lane you intend to enter — even when it is the right-hand lane. The manoeuvre may be performed only after making sure it will obstruct no one.

q-7393.text: In this situation, are you allowed to change the traffic lane without prior signaling of this manoeuvre?
q-7393.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Every lane change must be signalled beforehand with the indicator so that other road users have time to adapt their driving. The signal itself, however, gives no priority — before the manoeuvre you must still check the mirrors and the blind spot.

q-7394.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn on a road beyond this information sign?
q-7394.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The information sign visible in the material indicates a road or a place where turning around is not permitted. The prohibition applies from this sign until it is cancelled, regardless of whether the roadway appears empty.

q-7395.text: In this situation, when changing to the left lane, are you obliged to give the right of way to the vehicle in that lane?
q-7395.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When changing to the left lane, you give way to the vehicles already travelling in it. Entering is permitted only when the gap allows you to merge without forcing others to brake.

q-7396.text: In this situation, having changed the traffic lane, are you required to switch off the direction-indicator immediately?
q-7396.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The indicator is switched off immediately after the manoeuvre is completed. Left on, it misleads others, because it suggests another lane change or a turn that the driver has no intention of making.

q-7397.text: In this situation, having completed overtaking, are you obliged to return to the right traffic lane?
q-7397.explanation: Correct answer: YES. After overtaking you should return to the right lane as soon as you can do so without obstructing the vehicle overtaken. The left lane is for overtaking, not for continuous driving, and must remain free for faster vehicles.

q-7398.text: Are you allowed to accelerate when you are being overtaken?
q-7398.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver of the vehicle being overtaken is obliged not to increase speed and, if necessary, to move further to the right to make the manoeuvre easier. Accelerating prolongs the time the overtaking driver spends on the opposite lane and risks a head-on collision.

q-7399.text: In this situation, are you allowed to overtake the lorry?
q-7399.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is prohibited at this place — this follows from the signs, the road markings or the limited visibility of the road ahead of the vehicle. In addition, a long lorry needs a very long stretch of clear road, which is lacking here.

q-7403.text: In this situation, before you start overtaking, are you obliged to make sure that the driver behind you has not started the same manoeuvre?
q-7403.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before starting to overtake, the driver must make sure the driver behind has not already begun the same manoeuvre. This is done by looking in the mirrors and checking the blind spot before moving into the left lane.

q-7405.text: In this situation, are you allowed to overtake several vehicles at once?
q-7405.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The rules do not limit the number of vehicles overtaken in one manoeuvre. The condition is a sufficiently long, clear and clearly visible section of road and no overtaking ban; after completing the manoeuvre you must return to the right lane.

q-7406.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-7406.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-7407.text: In this situation, are you allowed to overtake the vehicle shown?
q-7407.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs and conditions visible in the material do not stand in the way of overtaking, and the section ahead of the vehicle is clear and clearly visible. Before the manoeuvre you must signal your intention, check that no one is overtaking from behind, and keep a safe distance.

q-7408.text: In this situation, are you allowed to overtake the vehicle shown from the right side?
q-7408.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On a roadway with several marked lanes in the same direction, overtaking on the right is permitted. The driver must, however, stay in their lane, exercise particular caution and allow for a lane change by the vehicle being overtaken.

q-7409.text: In this situation, are you allowed to overtake the biker if this requires driving over a double solid line?
q-7409.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A double solid line separates the directions of traffic and must not be driven on or crossed. If overtaking the cyclist with a safe distance would require driving onto that line, you must stay behind and wait for a place where it is permitted.

q-7410.text: In this situation, are you allowed to overtake the vehicle moving in the right lane?
q-7410.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking a vehicle travelling in the right lane is done on its left side, i.e. in accordance with the general rule. The conditions are no overtaking ban, a clear left lane and signalling the manoeuvre with the indicator.

q-7411.text: In this situation, are you allowed to exceed the permitted speed in order to complete the overtaking sooner?
q-7411.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An overtaking manoeuvre does not release you from the duty to observe the permitted speed. If you cannot overtake without exceeding it, the speed difference is too small and the manoeuvre should not be started at all.

q-7413.text: In this situation, are you allowed to overtake the bus?
q-7413.explanation: Correct answer: YES. No ban on overtaking applies at this place, and the visibility and the clear lane allow the manoeuvre to be completed safely. A bus is long, so you must assess the needed stretch of road in advance and keep a safe lateral distance.

q-7414.text: Are you allowed to use high beam lights in this situation?
q-7414.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle another driver — an oncoming one, one ahead, or the driver of a train or a ship. In such conditions you drive on dipped headlights.

q-7416.text: Are you allowed to use high-beam lights in this situation?
q-7416.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used where they would dazzle others: with an oncoming vehicle, when following another vehicle, and in fog or precipitation, when the light reflects off water droplets. You then drive on dipped headlights.

q-7419.text: In this situation, are you required to signal your intention to cross this dotted line with the direction-indicator?
q-7419.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Crossing a broken line means changing lanes, and every such manoeuvre must be signalled in advance with the indicator. The signal is given early enough for others to react and switched off as soon as the manoeuvre is completed.

q-7420.text: In this situation, are you required to signal your intention to return to the right lane with the direction-indicator?
q-7420.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Returning to the right lane after overtaking is also a lane change and requires signalling with the right indicator. Beforehand you must see the whole overtaken vehicle in the mirror so as not to cut in front of it.

q-7421.text: In this situation, are you obliged to give way to the pedestrian?
q-7421.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver approaching a pedestrian crossing must take special care and give way to a pedestrian who is stepping onto it or already walking across. If necessary, the vehicle must be stopped before the crossing.

q-7422.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop the vehicle to let the pedestrian cross the street?
q-7422.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver approaching a pedestrian crossing must give way to the pedestrian. If they could not otherwise cross the carriageway safely, the vehicle must be stopped before the crossing and you wait.

q-7423.text: In this situation, do you have the right of way over the pedestrians?
q-7423.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the circumstances shown, the pedestrians have priority and the driver must give way to them. Driving into their path or forcing them to quicken their step is not permitted, even when the vehicle is moving very slowly.

q-7424.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-7424.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-7425.text: In this situation, are you obliged to give way to the pedestrians?
q-7425.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The pedestrians shown in the material have priority, so the driver must give way to them — you may not drive into their path or force them to speed up or stop. If necessary, you stop the vehicle.

q-7428.text: In this situation, are you allowed to use the horn?
q-7428.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In a built-up area the horn may be used solely to prevent an immediate danger. In the situation shown there is no such threat, so the horn would be unnecessary and could frighten other road users.

q-7429.text: In this situation, are you obliged to observe the cyclist's behaviour carefully?
q-7429.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A cyclist is a vulnerable road user, easily loses balance and may suddenly swerve around a bump or an obstacle. The driver must watch their behaviour, keep a safe distance and be ready to slow down.

q-7430.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise particular caution?
q-7430.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means raising your attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop immediately.

q-7431.text: Are you obliged to stop in front of this level crossing even when you are sure that no train is approaching?
q-7431.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop unconditionally follows from the sign or signal shown in the material and does not depend on the driver's judgement. The vehicle stops before the designated place, and only then do you assess whether it is safe to proceed.

q-7433.text: Is switching on the emergency lights and placing a warning triangle at the distance of 50-70 m behind the vehicle the right way to indicate that it has broken-down on a motorway?
q-7433.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a motorway the warning triangle is placed at a distance of 100 m behind the immobilised vehicle, not 50–70 m. The hazard lights themselves are switched on correctly, but the stated distance for placing the triangle is too small.

q-7434.text: You intend to turn right. Do you have the right of way over the pedestrians?
q-7434.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver turning into a side road must give way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway of the road they are entering. The manoeuvre is complete only when the pedestrians have safely left the vehicle's path.

q-7438.text: Are you warned of a significant elevation of the road in this situation?
q-7438.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign shown in the material announces a considerable rise in the road. The driver should select gear and speed in advance, remembering that visibility beyond the crest is limited and overtaking in such a place is dangerous.
