q-7441.text: Which of the following persons are exempted from the obligation to use safety belts when travelling in a passenger car?

options.A: Every passenger at the back seat of the vehicle.

q-7441.explanation: Correct answer: C. A woman who is visibly pregnant is exempt from the duty to fasten seat belts. A place on the rear seat or eating a meal gives no such exemption — belts are compulsory in every seat fitted with them.

q-7443.text: Do instructions and signs given by persons directing traffic have priority over road signs?
q-7443.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The instructions and signals of a person directing traffic take precedence over road signs and traffic lights. The driver must comply with them even when they contradict the signs on the section of road concerned.

q-7444.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive into the intersection without stopping in front of the line consisting of triangles?
q-7444.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A line made up of triangles marks the place of conditional giving way, not of a mandatory stop. If the road you are entering is clear, you may pass without stopping, exercising particular caution.

q-7445.text: To which of the following activities aren't you allowed to use a passenger car?

options.B: To tow another passenger car in the built-up area.
options.C: To pull children on a sleigh.

q-7445.explanation: Correct answer: C. Towing behind a vehicle a person on a sledge, skis, roller skates or a similar device is prohibited. Towing a light trailer and towing another car are — once the conditions are met — allowed.

q-7446.text: What distance from the preceding car are you required to keep when stopping in a traffic jam in a tunnel?
q-7446.explanation: Correct answer: B. When stopping in a traffic jam in a tunnel, the driver must keep a distance of no less than 5 metres from the vehicle ahead. This gap makes it easier to leave the column and for the rescue services to get through in the event of a fire or accident.

q-7447.text: Which of the following activities is prohibited while driving a vehicle?

options.C: Talking on a telephone that requires the user to hold a receiver or microphone in his hand.

q-7447.explanation: Correct answer: C. While driving it is prohibited to use a phone if that requires holding the handset or microphone in the hand. Operating the radio and the navigation is not banned, but it must not distract the driver from the road.

q-7449.text: You are involved in an accident in which only your vehicle was damaged. Are you obliged to remove it from the place of the accident, so that it does not block the traffic or pose a threat to other traffic users?
q-7449.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When nobody has been injured, a participant in the incident must immediately remove the damaged vehicle from the scene so that it does not create a hazard or obstruct traffic. Beforehand, it is worth recording the circumstances for insurance purposes.

q-7450.text: Are you obliged to comply with the instructions and signs given by a person performing road works upon the order of the road administrator?
q-7450.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Those authorised to give instructions and signals to road users also include a worker carrying out roadworks on behalf of the road authority. Their directions are binding and take precedence over the signing on that stretch.

q-7451.text: What should be the colour of a flag that you use for marking a load protruding from the back of a passenger car?
q-7451.explanation: Correct answer: C. A load protruding from the rear of the vehicle is marked with a red flag. In conditions of insufficient visibility, a red light and a reflector are used instead of the flag.

q-7452.text: The actual total weight of a trailer pulled by a passenger car must not exceed:

options.B: gross vehicle weight of the car.
options.C: gross vehicle weight of the car decreased by 40%.

q-7452.explanation: Correct answer: B. The actual total mass of a trailer towed by a car may not exceed the actual total mass of that car. The restriction protects the stability of the combination and the effectiveness of braking.

q-7454.text: You must not haul another vehicle with your passenger car:
q-7454.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a motorway towing another vehicle is prohibited — an immobilised vehicle may only be brought to the nearest exit. On an expressway and in a residential zone towing remains allowed under the general rules.

q-7455.text: At what maximum speed are you allowed to drive on the road beyond this sign if you are hauling another passenger car?
q-7455.explanation: Correct answer: A. When towing another vehicle, a speed of up to 30 km/h applies in a built-up area and up to 60 km/h outside it. This limit is binding even when the general limit on the stretch is higher.

q-7457.text: You are allowed to use snow chains only when:

options.A: you drive a vehicle in the period from the beginning of December till the end of February, irrespective of whether the road is covered with snow.
options.B: the air temperature is lower than 0 Celsius degrees, irrespective of whether the road is covered with snow.
options.C: the road is covered with snow.

q-7457.explanation: Correct answer: C. Snow chains may be used only when the road is covered with snow. Neither the season nor a temperature below zero in itself entitles you to use them, because on a bare surface chains damage the road and worsen the vehicle's handling.

q-7458.text: Can leaves lying on a roadway have an impact on the braking distance of a vehicle?

options.A: Yes, because they may reduce the braking distance.
options.B: Yes, because they may extend the braking distance.
options.C: They do not have an impact on the braking distance.

q-7458.explanation: Correct answer: B. A layer of leaves, especially wet ones, clearly reduces the grip of the tyres on the surface, so the braking distance grows. On such a stretch slow down, increase the distance and avoid harsh braking and sudden manoeuvres.

q-7459.text: Are you allowed to switch on emergency lights when you are driving a hauled vehicle?
q-7459.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A towed vehicle is marked at the rear with a warning triangle, not with hazard lights. Hazard lights serve to signal a vehicle immobilised on the carriageway or another sudden danger in traffic.

q-7461.text: The braking distance is the longest on:
q-7461.explanation: Correct answer: C. The braking distance is longer the lower the grip of the tyres on the surface; on ice grip is lowest and that distance grows the most. That is why on an icy road you reduce speed and clearly increase the distance.

q-7462.text: After parking a vehicle, are you allowed to move away from it for no longer than one minute when the engine is running?
q-7462.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When leaving the vehicle, the driver is obliged to switch off the engine and secure the vehicle against moving off by itself and against use by an unauthorised person. An unattended running engine creates a danger and pollutes the air.

q-7463.text: What is the function of the ABS (anti-lock brake system) in a vehicle?

options.A: It prevents wheels from skidding when starting off.
options.B: It allows the driver to control the vehicle at the time of sudden braking.
options.C: It always reduces the braking distance.

q-7463.explanation: Correct answer: B. ABS does not let the wheels lock under hard braking, so the vehicle stays steerable and you can steer round an obstacle. The braking distance is not always shorter — on loose snow or gravel it can even be longer.

q-7464.text: Are you allowed to use low-beam lights and front fog lights at the same time during these weather conditions?
q-7464.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Front fog lights may be used in fog, heavy rain or snow, and they are switched on together with dipped headlights. They must be switched off as soon as visibility improves, so as not to dazzle others.

q-7465.text: Are you obliged to secure the vehicle parked on a hill against rolling down?
q-7465.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When leaving a vehicle on a hill, the driver must secure it against moving by itself: apply the parking brake and leave a gear or the park position engaged. On a steep slope you additionally turn the wheels towards the edge of the roadway and use chocks.

q-7466.text: Are you allowed to drive with daytime running lights switched on in these weather conditions?
q-7466.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Daytime running lights may be used only when the air is normally clear. When conditions worsen, dipped headlights must be switched on, because daytime lights do not light the road and do not switch on the rear position lights.

q-7467.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to pedestrians when in the traffic zone?
q-7467.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Road traffic rules apply in a traffic zone, so the driver must give way to pedestrians just as on an ordinary road. In such areas pedestrians appear suddenly between vehicles, so you drive slowly and ready to stop.

q-7468.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn immediately beyond the informatory sign in this situation?
q-7468.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An information sign by itself does not create a place where U-turns are permitted, and the traffic arrangement visible in the material rules out this manoeuvre at this point. You may turn around only where the signs allow it and where it does not endanger other road users.

q-7469.text: Are you allowed to use high-beam lights in this situation?
q-7469.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used where they would dazzle others: with an oncoming vehicle, when following another vehicle, and in fog or precipitation, when the light reflects off water droplets. You then drive on dipped headlights.

q-7470.text: Are you obliged to use low-beam lights in this situation?
q-7470.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A moving vehicle must be lit around the clock, all year round. After dusk, in a tunnel and when the clarity of the air is reduced, dipped headlights are compulsory, not daytime running lights alone.

q-7471.text: In this situation, are you allowed to use the horn in order to induce the driver of the preceding vehicle to leave the intersection faster?
q-7471.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn serves solely to warn of danger, not to hurry other drivers along. In a built-up area it may be used only when necessary to avoid an accident.

q-7509.text: Is it allowed to carry an intoxicated passenger:

options.A: Yes, on the back seat of a motorcycle
options.B: Yes, in a trailer pulled by a motorcycle.

q-7509.explanation: Correct answer: C. An intoxicated person may be carried on a motorcycle only in a sidecar. On the pillion seat such a passenger will neither keep their balance nor respond to the vehicle leaning, which risks the motorcycle falling over.

q-7510.text: You intend to haul a motorcycle by means of another motorcycle. How should both vehicles be connected?

options.A: With a flexible connection device, in a manner excluding the possibility of its disengagement.
options.B: With a flexible connection device, in a manner allowing for easy disengagement.

q-7510.explanation: Correct answer: B. Motorcycles are joined with a flexible connection that can be released instantly. When one of the riders loses balance, the other vehicle must not be pulled along by them — that is why quick release is a condition of safety.

q-7511.text: Gross vehicle weight of a trailer pulled by a motorcycle must not exceed:

options.A: the kerb weight of the motorcycle; however, it must not be larger than 100 kg.
options.B: the gross vehicle weight of the motorcycle.
options.C: the gross vehicle weight of the motorcycle decreased by 40%.

q-7511.explanation: Correct answer: A. A trailer towed by a motorcycle may not weigh more than the unladen mass of that motorcycle and in no case more than 100 kg. A heavier trailer would set the two-wheeler swaying and lengthen its braking distance.

q-7512.text: A hauled passenger car may be marked by:

options.B: placing a reflective warning triangle on the left behind the car.
options.C: switching on the rear fog light.

q-7512.explanation: Correct answer: B. A towed car is marked with a reflective warning triangle placed at the rear on the left side. Switching on the hazard lights or the rear fog light does not replace this marking.

q-7513.text: As the owner of a vehicle, are you obliged to indicate at the request of an authorised body to whom you entrusted the vehicle for driving or use at a specific time?

options.A: Yes, unless it is a vehicle used for business purposes.
options.B: Yes, unless the vehicle was used contrary to your will and without your knowledge by an unknown person, which you could not prevent.
options.C: I am not obliged to do so.

q-7513.explanation: Correct answer: B. The owner must indicate, at the request of an authorised body, to whom they entrusted the vehicle at a given time. They are released from this only when the vehicle was used by an unknown person against their will and knowledge and they could not have prevented it.

q-7515.text: Are you allowed to drive a vehicle with an invisible number plate?

options.B: Yes, if the plate is covered by a protruding load.

q-7515.explanation: Correct answer: C. The number plate must be visible and legible at all times, so driving with a covered plate is prohibited. A protruding load is no excuse — it must be arranged so that the plate stays uncovered.

q-7516.text: Are you allowed to stick onto a vehicle an identification mark of any state other than the one in which the vehicle was registered?

options.B: Yes, but only if the vehicle has a number plate with the designation "PL".

q-7516.explanation: Correct answer: C. The country identification mark on a vehicle must correspond to the country of registration. A sticker indicating another country is misleading and prohibited, regardless of the mark shown on the number plate.

q-7517.text: This blue control light informs you that the following lights are switched on:
q-7517.explanation: Correct answer: C. A blue warning light on the dashboard always signals that main-beam headlights are on. Position lights and dipped headlights have green lights, so on noticing the blue one you must switch the lights so as not to dazzle other drivers.

q-7518.text: What must be checked when the control light of indicators began to blink much faster?

options.C: The condition of direction indicator bulbs.

q-7518.explanation: Correct answer: C. Clearly faster flashing of the indicator warning light is the typical signal of a blown bulb in one of the indicators. Check the indicators on both sides and replace the failed bulb, because other road users will not read your intended manoeuvre.

q-7519.text: For which of the following states of the engine should the oil level in the engine be checked?

options.B: Immediately after the engine is switched off.
options.C: Before the cold engine is started or at least a few minutes after switching it off.

q-7519.explanation: Correct answer: C. The oil level is measured when the oil has drained back into the sump: on a cold engine before starting, or a few minutes after switching it off. Measuring with the engine running or immediately after switching off gives a low, unreliable reading.

q-7520.text: At what maximum speed are you allowed to drive on the road beyond this sign if you are driving a lorry of gross vehicle weight rating over 3.5 tons?
q-7520.explanation: Correct answer: A. A lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel on this road at no more than 80 km/h, even though for cars the limit is higher. The driver always applies the lower value — the one provided for their type of vehicle.

q-7521.text: You are driving a lorry of gross vehicle weight rating over 3.5 t outside a built-up area. What is the maximum speed permitted beyond this prohibitory sign?
q-7521.explanation: Correct answer: B. A speed-limit sign does not lift the limits set for particular types of vehicle. A lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may not go faster than 80 km/h outside a built-up area, so the lower of the two values applies.

q-7527.text: Are you allowed to transport people in a trailer pulled by a lorry?

options.A: Yes, always when you don't transport a load in the trailer.
options.B: Yes, if these are persons performing loading operations.
options.C: No, it is prohibited unless the persons are being carried by vehicles of certain services, e.g., the Police.

q-7527.explanation: Correct answer: C. Carrying people in a trailer towed by a lorry is prohibited, because there are no seats, belts or protection in a collision there. The exception concerns solely the vehicles of certain services, for example the Police.

q-7529.text: Which of the following conditions must be met for you to carry persons outside the driver's cab in a lorry?

options.A: Persons are being carried in standing room.
options.B: Persons are being carried on seats.
options.C: Persons are situated between the load and the driver's cab.

q-7529.explanation: Correct answer: B. Outside the driver's cab, people may be carried only in seats. Riding standing is not permitted, and placing people between the load and the cab risks crushing when the load shifts under braking.

q-7531.text: Any long wood may protrude from the back part of a timber transport trailer at a distance not larger than:
q-7531.explanation: Correct answer: B. Long timber carried on a stanchion trailer may protrude at the rear by at most 5 m. The protruding end must be marked, because other drivers misjudge the real length of the combination, especially when overtaking and at junctions.

q-7532.text: When are you required to mark a load that protrudes beyond the front surface of the extreme outline of a lorry?

options.B: Only when it protrudes at a distance longer than 0.5m.
options.C: Only when it protrudes at a distance longer than 1m.

q-7532.explanation: Correct answer: A. A load protruding beyond the vehicle's outline is always marked, without any threshold length. The driver cannot see such a protrusion from their seat, and other road users must notice it early enough.

q-7533.text: What should be the colour of a flag for marking a load protruding from the front part of a lorry?
q-7533.explanation: Correct answer: B. A load protruding in front of the vehicle is marked with an orange flag, clearly visible in daylight. Neither yellow nor red is provided for this, and after dusk the protruding part must additionally be lit.

q-7534.text: Which of the following activities is prohibited if you are carrying persons outside the driver's cab in a lorry?

options.A: Carrying another passenger in the cab.

q-7534.explanation: Correct answer: C. The driver of a vehicle carrying people outside the cab may neither eat nor smoke while driving. They must be in full control of the vehicle and drive smoothly, because those carried are not protected like passengers in the cab.

q-7535.text: The speed limiter fitted in a bus should limit its maximum speed to:
q-7535.explanation: Correct answer: B. The speed limiter in a bus is set so that the vehicle does not exceed 100 km/h. This is a technical upper limit; the actual speed is still determined by the signs and the limits set for the road in question.

q-7536.text: How many fire extinguishers should be fitted in a lorry longer than 6 metres?
q-7536.explanation: Correct answer: B. A bus longer than 6 metres must be equipped with two fire extinguishers: one near the driver's seat, the other in the passenger area. Shorter buses need only one extinguisher.

q-7537.text: How many fire extinguishers should a bus of length not exceeding 6 metres be fitted with?
q-7537.explanation: Correct answer: A. A bus no longer than 6 metres must be equipped with at least one fire extinguisher. Longer buses require more of them, and the extinguisher itself must be in working order, secured and easily accessible.

q-7538.text: Are you allowed to eat while driving a bus?

options.B: Yes, if another person is not transported in the bus.

q-7538.explanation: Correct answer: B. A bus driver may not eat while driving when carrying other people. When nobody is in the vehicle the ban does not apply, but eating still must not distract from driving.

options.A: a bus with an external boot.

q-7539.explanation: Correct answer: B. A bus with a trailer coupled to it may not be towed — such a combination would be excessively long and hard to control. The trailer must be uncoupled and towed separately.

q-7540.text: Are you allowed to haul a lorry with a trailer by means of a bus?

options.A: Yes, but only outside a motorway.

q-7540.explanation: Correct answer: C. Towing a vehicle with a trailer attached is prohibited regardless of the type of road. A three-part combination would be too long and unstable, so the trailer must be uncoupled and moved separately.

q-7541.text: The design speed of an agricultural tractor being a part of a trackless train should be limited to:
q-7541.explanation: Correct answer: B. An agricultural tractor forming part of a tourist road train must have its design speed limited to 25 km/h. The low speed protects the trailer passengers, who have neither seat belts nor an enclosed body.

q-7542.text: How are you allowed to carry persons in the trailer of a trackless train?

options.B: In standing places and on seats.

q-7542.explanation: Correct answer: C. In the trailer of a tourist road train people are carried only in seats. A standing passenger easily loses balance under braking or on a bend and may fall out of the trailer.

q-7543.text: Are you obliged in this situation to get closer to the middle of the roadway before turning left?
q-7543.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before turning left the driver is obliged to move in good time towards the centre of the roadway, and on a one-way roadway — towards its left edge. Such positioning announces the manoeuvre and does not block vehicles going straight.

q-7545.text: How should you act when an accident casualty regains consciousness and wants to move away?

options.A: Start a conversation and try to convince the person to remain on the scene until emergency services arrive.
options.B: Recommend contacting primary care doctor and allow the person to move away.
options.C: Give tranquilizers or analgesics to the person and recommend waiting for the arrival of emergency medical services.

q-7545.explanation: Correct answer: A. After a loss of consciousness the casualty's condition may deteriorate suddenly, so they must be kept at the scene by talking to them and observed until the ambulance arrives. They must not be given medicines or allowed to walk off alone.

q-7546.text: How should you dress a heavily bleeding wound?

options.A: Apply a pressure dressing with gauze and bandage.
options.B: Decontaminate the wound with iodine or gentian.
options.C: Cover the wound with sterile gauze.

q-7546.explanation: Correct answer: A. Heavy bleeding is stemmed with a pressure dressing: gauze is placed on the wound and bandaged firmly. Disinfecting or merely covering the wound will not stop the bleeding; when the dressing soaks through, another is put on top.

q-7547.text: The correct telephone call for help to the scene of a road accident consists in:

options.A: Informing the operator only about the scene of the accident.
options.B: Making sure that the operator received the complete information about the accident.
options.C: Informing the operator only about the kind of incident and the number of casualties.

q-7547.explanation: Correct answer: B. The caller gives the location and type of incident, the number and condition of the casualties, and answers the dispatcher's questions. The caller does not end the call first — you must make sure all the information has been received.

q-7548.text: How long should you keep checking whether the unconscious person is breathing?
q-7548.explanation: Correct answer: B. Breathing is checked for no longer than 10 seconds: after tilting the head, you look for movement of the chest, listen and feel for the flow of air. If breathing is absent or abnormal, resuscitation is started immediately.

q-7550.text: When giving first aid to a person, where must hands be applied during chest compressions?

options.A: Only on the lower part of the chest.
options.B: Only on the top part of the chest.
options.C: In the center of the chest.

q-7550.explanation: Correct answer: C. The hands are placed in the centre of the chest and compressions are given with straight arms, rhythmically and to the right depth. Compressing elsewhere is ineffective and risks damaging the ribs and internal organs.

q-7551.text: In what circumstances should an injured person be placed in the recovery position?

options.A: When the person is unconscious and is not breathing.
options.B: When the person is unconscious and is breathing.
options.C: When the person is conscious and physically exhausted.

q-7551.explanation: Correct answer: B. The recovery position is used for an unconscious person who is breathing and has no visible injuries — it protects the airway from the tongue falling back and from stomach contents. If breathing is absent, resuscitation is started immediately.

q-7552.text: If, when riding a motorcycle the need to check the oil level arises, what should you do after stopping and turning off the vehicle engine:

options.A: place the motorcycle on the side kickstand and immediately proceed to check.
options.B: lay the motorcycle on the side and proceed to check.
options.C: place the motorcycle in an upright position and after a few minutes proceed to check.

q-7552.explanation: Correct answer: C. The oil level is measured with the engine off and the motorcycle upright, after a few minutes — that is how long the oil takes to drain to the sump. Measuring on the side stand or with the motorcycle lying on its side gives a false result.

q-7553.text: Which of the following may be the result of too high pressure in the motorcycle tyres?
q-7553.explanation: Correct answer: A. Too high a pressure reduces the tyre's contact area with the surface, so grip and braking effectiveness fall. The motorcycle becomes harsher, absorbs bumps worse and loses contact with the road more easily.

q-7554.text: In what way does too low tyre pressure affect the safe operation of a motorcycle?

options.A: It increases the durability of a tyre.
options.B: It may impair the stability of the vehicle in motion.

q-7554.explanation: Correct answer: B. With too low a pressure the tyre deforms, the motorcycle holds its line worse and responds sluggishly to the handlebars, especially in curves. The tyre additionally overheats and wears faster.

q-7555.text: Which of the following actions is part of the daily maintenance of a motorcycle?

options.B: Checking the operation of brake ‘stop’ lights.
options.C: Checking the electrolyte level in the battery.

q-7555.explanation: Correct answer: B. Daily servicing consists of simple checks before departure, including checking that the brake lights work. The electrolyte level is checked periodically, and an emergency braking test is not a servicing task.

q-7556.text: Which of the following actions should you primarily do before a long motorcycle ride?

options.C: Check the condition of the spark plugs.

q-7556.explanation: Correct answer: B. Before a longer journey the tyre pressures are checked first, because they directly affect stability, handling and the braking distance. The air filter and spark plugs belong to periodic servicing.

q-7558.text: How do faulty shock absorbers affect a ride on a moped?

options.A: They decrease the riding comfort with no effect on riding safety.
options.B: They may result in an accident.
options.C: They slightly impair the riding stability with no effect on riding safety.

q-7558.explanation: Correct answer: B. Faulty shock absorbers worsen the wheels' contact with the road — the vehicle bounces, holds its line worse and takes longer to brake. This is a direct threat to safety that can end in an accident.

q-7560.text: Which of the following vehicle are you entitled to drive with an A-category driving licence?

options.B: A four-wheeled motor vehicle with its unladen weight of 550 kg.

q-7560.explanation: Correct answer: A. Category A covers motorcycles without a power limit, including a motorcycle with a sidecar. Four-wheeled motor vehicles and slow-moving vehicles require entitlements of other categories.

q-7563.text: You are required to submit your motorcycle for a periodic motor vehicle inspection at the technical inspection station:

options.A: annually, after preparing the motorcycle for the summer season.
options.B: before the lapse of the date entered in the vehicle registration card.
options.C: annually, after the autumn vehicle checkup.

q-7563.explanation: Correct answer: B. The date of the next technical inspection is entered in the registration document, and the inspection must be carried out before it passes. Driving after the date means the vehicle is not admitted to traffic.

q-7566.text: Which of the following rules should you follow when refuelling a motorcycle?

options.A: The petrol tank should be around 60 per cent filled.
options.B: Petrol should not be spilled on the hot elements of the exhaust system.
options.C: The motorcycle engine should be running.

q-7566.explanation: Correct answer: B. Fuel spilt on a hot exhaust system ignites easily, so you refuel carefully and with the engine off. There is no rule requiring the tank to be filled only partly.

q-7567.text: Are you allowed to carry a passenger under the influence of substances with similar effects as alcohol on a single track motorcycle?

options.A: Yes, if you think it will not endanger the riding safety.
options.B: Yes, on condition that you are riding on a dirt road.

q-7567.explanation: Correct answer: C. Carrying such a passenger on a two-wheeled motorcycle is prohibited — they do not keep their balance and can cause the vehicle to fall over by their behaviour. Only carrying them in a sidecar is permitted.

q-7568.text: In what conditions are you allowed to carry an intoxicated passenger on a motorcycle?

options.B: Only when the person is carried in a sidecar.
options.C: Only when you reduce the speed to 30 km/h.

q-7568.explanation: Correct answer: B. An intoxicated passenger may be carried on a motorcycle only in a sidecar, where they do not affect the vehicle's balance. On the pillion behind the rider such carriage is prohibited regardless of speed.

q-7569.text: How should you respond to the side skidding of the front wheel when riding a motorcycle on a dirt road?

options.A: Ballast the rear wheel by moving backward on the saddle.
options.B: Balance the weight of your body and appropriately operate the throttle grip and the handlebars.
options.C: Ballast the front wheel by moving forward on the saddle.

q-7569.explanation: Correct answer: B. On an unmade surface the front wheel easily slides sideways, so the rider keeps balance with their body weight and works the throttle and handlebars smoothly. A sudden steering movement or braking with the front brake deepens the slide.

q-7570.text: Which of the following reactions of the moped can you expect, if while starting abruptly, you release the clutch lever without increasing the engine revolutions?
q-7570.explanation: Correct answer: A. Releasing the clutch lever too quickly at low revs deprives the engine of the torque needed to move off, and the unit stalls. Move off by engaging the clutch smoothly while gently adding throttle at the same time.

q-7572.text: Which of the following reactions of the moped can you expect, if you use the front brake too abruptly?
q-7572.explanation: Correct answer: B. Grabbing the front brake suddenly locks the steered wheel and shifts the vehicle's weight forward, so the two-wheeler loses steering and may fall over. The front brake is applied gradually, supported by the rear brake.

q-7573.text: Which of the following methods of braking is the most effective for a moped on a slippery surface?
q-7573.explanation: Correct answer: C. On a slippery surface grip is low, so the braking force must be spread over both wheels. Using both brakes at the same time and gently shortens the braking distance and reduces the risk of a wheel locking and skidding.

q-7574.text: Which of the following factors can limit your field of vision on the road when riding a motorcycle during the day?

options.B: Badly positioned lights in the motorcycle

q-7574.explanation: Correct answer: A. A badly chosen helmet shifts on the head and hides part of the field of vision, and its visor may distort the picture. In daylight the headlamp setting does not affect the range of vision, and a tight suit restricts movement but does not narrow the field of vision.

q-7575.text: With increasing speed of the vehicle the motorcyclist’s angle of view:
q-7575.explanation: Correct answer: B. The higher the speed, the more strongly the eyes concentrate on a point far ahead of the vehicle, and peripheral vision narrows. At high speed it is therefore easy to miss a pedestrian or a vehicle entering from the side.

q-7577.text: Which of the following ways of braking should be used if there is a need to abruptly decrease the speed of the motorcycle on a long downhill ride?

options.A: Braking with the rear brake only.
options.B: Braking with the front brake only.
options.C: Engine braking and simultaneously braking with the front and rear brakes.

q-7577.explanation: Correct answer: C. On a long descent the brakes heat up and lose effectiveness, so they are supported with engine braking, and the force is spread over both wheels. This combination gives the shortest braking distance and keeps the two-wheeler stable.

q-7578.text: Which of the following riding techniques should you apply while riding a motorcycle on a dirt road with a sand setting bed?

options.A: Rising up with the legs bent and supported on footrests and balancing the body to keep the balance.
options.B: Firmly settling on the motorcycle seat and maintaining constant speed.
options.C: Assuming an upright sitting position and using the legs as support to maintain balance.

q-7578.explanation: Correct answer: A. On sand the front wheel wanders sideways, so the front must be unloaded and freedom of movement kept: the rider rises on bent legs resting on the footpegs and balances with the body. Bracing with the feet risks injury and gives no stability.

q-7579.text: You are riding a motorcycle from behind the acoustic screen which ends on the left side of the road. In this situation should you expect:

options.A: a gust of wind from the left side of the road.
options.B: a gust of wind from the right side of the road.
options.C: a gust of wind from both the left and right sides of the road.

q-7579.explanation: Correct answer: A. The screen shelters the two-wheeler from the wind, and where it ends the gust strikes from that very side — the left. Reduce speed beforehand and hold the handlebars firmly, because the motorcycle will be pushed sideways.

q-7581.text: You are riding a motorcycle. What danger should you expect when passing an oncoming bus?

options.A: A gust of wind from behind.
options.B: A gust of wind first towards the middle of the road and then towards its right edge.
options.C: A gust of wind first towards the right edge of the road and then towards the middle.

q-7581.explanation: Correct answer: C. An approaching bus pushes a cushion of air ahead of it that pushes the two-wheeler towards the right edge, and after passing sucks it towards the middle of the road. Reduce speed, hold the handlebars firmly and increase the lateral distance.

q-7583.text: What distance from the vehicle being overtaken or another traffic user must you keep while riding a motorcycle outside a built-up area?

options.A: At least 1.5 metres if you are overtaking a column of pedestrians.
options.B: At least 2 meters if you are overtaking a bicycle.
options.C: At least 1 meter if you are overtaking a motorcycle.

q-7583.explanation: Correct answer: C. When overtaking a two-wheeler — a motorcycle, a moped or a bicycle — and also a pedestrian or a column of pedestrians, the driver must keep a safe distance of no less than 1 m. The values given in the other answers do not follow from the rules.

q-7585.text: Which of the following factors has the greatest effect on the motorcycle braking distance when riding in good weather conditions?

options.B: The speed at which the motorcycle is moving.
options.C: The outfit used by the motocyclist.

q-7585.explanation: Correct answer: B. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed, so speed decides it to the greatest degree. Reaction time lengthens the total stopping distance but not the braking itself, and clothing is of no significance here.

q-7586.text: What minimal distance should be kept between columns of mopeds?
q-7586.explanation: Correct answer: B. Two-wheelers riding in a group form columns, and between successive columns a distance of at least 200 m is kept. Thanks to that gap other vehicles can overtake a single group and return safely to their lane.

q-7587.text: What distance should be kept while overtaking a column of pedestrians with a moped?

options.A: Safe, but not shorter than 1 meter.
options.C: Any distance. The rules do not stipulate this.

q-7587.explanation: Correct answer: A. When overtaking a column of pedestrians, a moped rider must keep a safe distance, that is, no less than 1 m. The same minimum distance applies to a bicycle, a moped and a motorcycle, so the other answers are wrong.

q-7588.text: While riding a motorcycle, are you obliged to use a crash helmet?

options.A: Yes, but only when carrying a passenger.
options.B: No, but wearing it is recommended.
options.C: Yes, unless the motorcycle is originally fitted with safety belts.

q-7588.explanation: Correct answer: C. A motorcyclist and the passenger carried must wear a protective helmet meeting the applicable technical requirements. The exception is a vehicle factory-fitted with seat belts, where the vehicle's structure and a fastened belt provide the protection.

q-7589.text: Which of the following effects should you take into account during a long ride on a single-track vehicle in sodden clothes?

options.C: Only the deterioration of the well-being resulting from dampness.

q-7589.explanation: Correct answer: B. Wet clothing and the airstream draw off heat very quickly, so a long ride on a two-wheeler leads to the body cooling down. Concentration and precision of movement then fall, so waterproof clothing and a break to warm up are needed.

q-7591.text: Which of the following functions should the gloves worn by a motorcyclist primarily perform?

options.A: Increase the strength with which he holds the handlebars.
options.B: Ensure the professional appearance, matching a motorcycle suit.
options.C: Protect the hands in case of a fall.

q-7591.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a fall the hands hit the surface first, so the basic task of gloves is protecting the hands from abrasions and injuries. Looks or a firmer grip on the handlebars are secondary to the protective function.

q-7592.text: Which of the following functions should a motorcycle suit primarily perform?

options.A: Ensure aesthetic appearance of the person’s figure.
options.B: Decrease the sensitivity to the lateral gusts of wind.
options.C: Protect against injuries in case of a fall.

q-7592.explanation: Correct answer: C. A motorcycle suit is protective clothing: its reinforcements and protectors are meant to protect the body from abrasions and injuries in a fall. Looks and lower air resistance are extras, not the basic task of such clothing.

q-7593.text: When riding a moped on the road behind this sign, are you obliged to use a crash helmet?

options.A: No, because the road is not a public one.
options.B: No, if there is no paved surface on the road.

q-7593.explanation: Correct answer: C. The duty of a moped rider and the passenger carried to wear a protective helmet applies regardless of the type of road and its surface. The sign shown in the material does not release you from this duty, because it concerns the traffic arrangement, not the rider's equipment.

q-7596.text: Which of the following vehicles are you allowed to drive if you hold an AM category driving licence?
q-7596.explanation: Correct answer: B. Category AM entitles you to drive a moped and a light quadricycle, not every quadricycle. A motorcycle requires category A1, A2 or A, depending on its power and engine capacity.

q-7599.text: If the braking distance of the motorcycle you are riding at the speed of 30 km/h is 6 metres, increasing the speed to 60 km/h will result in:

options.A: increasing the braking distance to 12 metres.
options.B: increasing the braking distance to 24 metres.
options.C: increasing the braking distance to 36 metres.

q-7599.explanation: Correct answer: B. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed: twice the speed means roughly four times the distance, that is, about 24 metres instead of 6. That is why even a small increase in speed very quickly lengthens the stretch needed to stop.

q-7602.text: An agricultural tractor without a trailer should be marked with:

options.B: a triangular reflecting marking board with the tip of the triangle pointing downwards.
options.C: a triangular reflecting marking board with the tip of the triangle pointing upwards.

q-7602.explanation: Correct answer: C. An agricultural tractor is marked at the rear with the triangular plate distinguishing a slow-moving vehicle, set point upwards. Triangular reflectors are reserved for trailers, so a tractor without a trailer does not use them.

q-7603.text: Which of the following requirements should tyres of an agricultural tractor meet?

options.A: Their tread pattern depth should be at least 3 mm.
options.B: The tyres on wheels on one axle should have the same construction and tread pattern.
options.C: They should have a tread pattern enabling off-road driving only.

q-7603.explanation: Correct answer: B. The tyres on the wheels of one axle must be of the same type and have the same tread, because different grip on the wheels of the same axle pulls the combination sideways and causes loss of stability under braking. The other answers give requirements that the rules do not impose.

q-7604.text: Appropriately adjusted external mirror of an agricultural tractor shows:

options.A: only the area beside the vehicle.
options.B: a part of the vehicle side and the area behind the vehicle corresponding to the vehicle side.
options.C: only the area behind the vehicle.

q-7604.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a well-set exterior mirror you can see a narrow strip of the vehicle's side, which gives a reference point, and the space behind the vehicle on the same side. Without a piece of your own body it is hard to judge the distance of vehicles behind.

q-7606.text: Which of the following options should you choose when driving a tractor on a muddy terrain?
q-7606.explanation: Correct answer: B. The differential lock forces the wheels of one axle to turn at the same rate, so the wheel standing on firmer ground transmits drive and the tractor does not spin its wheels. High revs and slaloming only deepen the ruts and dig the wheels in.

q-7607.text: How can a driver of an agricultural tractor with a trailer control the vehicle trajectory while reversing?

options.A: Looking through the rear windshield and in the external mirrors.
options.B: Looking only through the rear windshield.
options.C: Looking only in the external mirrors.

q-7607.explanation: Correct answer: A. The trailer blocks the view through the rear window, and the mirrors show only the sides of the combination, so both sources of the picture must be used at the same time. With limited visibility the driver should additionally get the help of another person.

q-7608.text: While driving an agricultural tractor on a winding road, is it recommended to turn on a differential lock?

options.B: No, because it may damage the mechanism.
options.C: Yes, on condition that the driving speed is up to 12 km/h.

q-7608.explanation: Correct answer: B. A locked differential forces the wheels of one axle to turn at the same rate, and in a turn the outer wheel covers a longer distance than the inner one. Large stresses then arise that can damage the drivetrain and make turning harder.

q-7609.text: When should you not turn on the front wheel drive of an agricultural tractor?

options.A: When driving on a paved road, unless it is necessary to overcome temporary resistance.
options.B: When the rear wheels are skidding.
options.C: When driving on a boggy terrain.

q-7609.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a hard surface the wheels of both axles have good grip and turn at slightly different speeds, so permanently engaged front-wheel drive causes stresses in the system and rapid tyre wear. It is engaged only briefly, when greater resistance has to be overcome.

q-7610.text: In which of the following cases is it not recommended to turn on a differential lock in an agricultural tractor?

options.A: While driving on a boggy terrain.
options.B: While driving on a winding road.

q-7610.explanation: Correct answer: B. The lock forces the wheels of one axle to turn at the same rate, and in a turn the outer wheel has to travel further than the inner one. The tractor then loses its ability to turn and the risk of damaging the mechanism grows; the lock is used on soft ground.

q-7612.text: Which of the following techniques should you use when driving downhill?

options.A: Engage a lower gear, the greater the slope.
options.B: Drive downhill with the gear off.
options.C: Engage a higher gear, the greater the slope.

q-7612.explanation: Correct answer: A. The steeper the descent, the lower the gear — the engine then brakes the vehicle and relieves the brakes, which on a long descent could overheat and lose effectiveness. Descending in neutral removes engine braking and ends with the combination running away.

q-7613.text: While driving an agricultural tractor with one-axle trailer through a curve, you should take into account that:

options.A: the trailer is moving on a smaller radius than the tractor.
options.B: the trailer is moving on a greater radius than the tractor.
options.C: both vehicles are moving along the same trajectory.

q-7613.explanation: Correct answer: A. The trailer cuts the curve and runs closer to the inner edge than the tractor, so the bend must be taken wider. Otherwise its wheels catch the kerb, the verge or an obstacle standing on the inside of the bend.

q-7614.text: Is it allowed to leave a parked agricultural tractor with the plough raised?

options.B: Yes, regardless of the time for which it is left.
options.C: Yes, but only for a time up to five minutes.

q-7614.explanation: Correct answer: A. A raised plough is a heavy, sharp implement that can drop on its own and injure a person beside the vehicle. A machine left parked is lowered to the ground and secured against accidental starting.

q-7615.text: When driving on a public road, can you carry in a trailer pulled by an agricultural tractor a cargo exceeding its permissible loading capacity?

options.A: Yes, if the permissible loading capacity does not exceed its nominal size by more than 40%.
options.C: Yes, but only on a route of no more than 5 km.

q-7615.explanation: Correct answer: B. The payload given by the manufacturer is a limit value, following from the strength of the trailer's frame, axle, tyres and brakes. Exceeding it lengthens the braking distance and risks a failure, so the rules allow no tolerance here.

q-7617.text: In what circumstances should a cargo protruding from the back of a trailer pulled by an agricultural tractor be marked?

options.A: If it protrudes over 0.5 meter behind the rear surface contour of the vehicle.
options.C: Only when driving on a paved road.

q-7617.explanation: Correct answer: A. A load protruding more than 0.5 m beyond the rear of the vehicle's outline must be marked, so that those behind can judge the real length of the combination. The marking must be clearly visible after dusk and in conditions of reduced clarity of the air as well.

q-7621.text: A registration card of a trailer states:

options.A: that it is allowed for traffic on public roads.
options.B: that it can be coupled to any other vehicle.
options.C: that it is efficient over its lifetime.

q-7621.explanation: Correct answer: A. The registration document confirms that the trailer has been registered and admitted to traffic on public roads. It certifies neither its current technical state nor that it may be coupled to any vehicle.

q-7622.text: Which of the following actions are you obliged to take as the owner of an agricultural tractor?

options.A: To have personal accident insurance policy (NW).
options.B: To notify the starost office (district head) within 30 days of the sale of the vehicle.
options.C: To perform all repairs at an authorized car service center.

q-7622.explanation: Correct answer: B. The owner of a registered vehicle must notify the starosta of its sale within 30 days. Personal accident insurance is voluntary, and repairs do not have to be carried out at an authorised service.

q-7625.text: Which of the following vehicles are you entitled to drive with driving licence category T?

options.B: A farm tractor or a slow moving vehicle.
options.C: A motor vehicle with its unladen weight of up to 550kg, except for a motorcycle.

q-7625.explanation: Correct answer: B. Category T entitles you to drive an agricultural tractor and a slow-moving vehicle, also with trailers. A lorry requires category C, and a light motor vehicle of small unladen mass — category B1.

q-7626.text: Which of the following vehicles are you entitled to drive with driving licence category T?

options.A: An agricultural tractor with two trailers.

q-7626.explanation: Correct answer: A. Category T covers an agricultural tractor and a slow-moving vehicle together with trailers, including two. A ballast tractor belongs to another group of motor vehicles, and a motorcycle requires category A1, A2 or A.

q-7627.text: Which of the following actions is a farm tractor owner’s responsibility after the sale of the tractor?

options.A: Returning the registration card to the office.
options.B: Handing the registration card over to the new owner.
options.C: Returning the vehicle registration plates to the office.

q-7627.explanation: Correct answer: B. The vehicle's documents, including the registration document, pass to the buyer together with the tractor, because they are needed to re-register and drive it. The seller, for their part, reports the sale to the appropriate office.

q-7628.text: Which of the following factors determines to the greatest extent the length of an agricultural tractor's braking distance during emergency braking?

options.A: The type of the road surface.
options.B: The weight of the tractor driver.
options.C: Gross vehicle weight rating of the tractor.

q-7628.explanation: Correct answer: A. The effectiveness of braking is decided by wheel grip, and that depends above all on the type and state of the surface and the weather. On a wet, muddy or icy road the same vehicle will stop over a clearly longer stretch.

q-7629.text: Which of the following factors should you take into account when adjusting the distance from the preceding vehicle during a drive?

options.A: The type of the road surface and conditions on the road.
options.B: Only the strength of the lateral wind.
options.C: Only the intensity of the road traffic.

q-7629.explanation: Correct answer: A. The distance from the vehicle ahead must be enough to stop without running into it, and that is decided by grip, that is, the type of surface and the conditions on the road. On a wet or slippery carriageway the distance must be clearly increased.

q-7630.text: Which of the following factors does the agricultural tractor's tyres grip depend on?

options.A: The weight of a passenger transported.
options.C: The type and condition of the road surface.

q-7630.explanation: Correct answer: C. Grip arises at the contact of tyre and carriageway, so it depends on what the surface is made of and what state it is in — dry, wet, muddy or icy. Neither engine power nor a passenger's mass decides it.

q-7631.text: Which of the following factors has an impact on the increase of the braking distance of an agricultural tractor?

options.A: Decrease of the grip the tyres have on the road.
options.B: Increase of the grip the tyres have on the road.

q-7631.explanation: Correct answer: A. The lower the tyres' grip, the less braking force can be transmitted to the road and the longer the braking distance. Better grip shortens it, and driving uphill additionally helps shed speed.

q-7632.text: How does a wet road after the rain affect the braking distance?

options.C: The braking distance does not depend on the road condition.

q-7632.explanation: Correct answer: B. A layer of water reduces the grip of the tyres on the surface, so the wheels lock more easily and the braking distance grows. After rain reduce speed and increase the distance from the vehicle ahead.

q-7633.text: The distance between the moving columns of agricultural tractors cannot be shorter than:
q-7633.explanation: Correct answer: C. Vehicles travelling in a group are divided into columns, and between successive columns a distance of at least 200 m is kept. Thanks to that gap other drivers can overtake one column and return safely to their lane.

q-7634.text: How many meters distance from the vehicle in front are you obliged to keep while stopping in a tunnel?
q-7634.explanation: Correct answer: A. Stopping in a tunnel because of traffic conditions, the driver must keep a distance of at least 5 m from the vehicle ahead. The free space allows pulling out of the column and makes access easier for the rescue services.

q-7635.text: While driving an agricultural tractor in a thick fog you should not use:
q-7635.explanation: Correct answer: B. Main-beam headlights reflect off the water droplets and form a bright wall that dazzles the driver themselves and worsens visibility. In fog you use dipped headlights or front fog lights, and rear fog lights — in very limited visibility.

q-7639.text: In which of the following cases are you obliged to give short sound signals when driving an agricultural tractor in the fog?

options.A: While passing a stationary vehicle or object outside a built up area.
options.B: While passing an oncoming vehicle outside a built up area.
options.C: While passing a stationary vehicle or object in a built up area.

q-7639.explanation: Correct answer: A. When the clarity of the air is reduced, a driver passing an obstacle outside a built-up area warns others with a short sound signal. In a built-up area the horn is used only in the event of an immediate danger.

q-7640.text: In the presented situation, are you allowed to keep the distance of 0.5 metre between your vehicle and the cyclist being overtaken?
q-7640.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When overtaking a cyclist, the driver must keep a safe distance of no less than 1 m. Half a metre is too little — at that distance a gust of air or the slightest wobble of the bicycle ends in contact with the vehicle.

q-7642.text: Is turning on the warning lights permissible on the towing car?
q-7642.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The hazard lights are switched on by the towed vehicle, because it is the one that is unroadworthy and needs marking. The towing vehicle signals the tow with its dipped headlights on, in daytime too; swapping them round would mislead other drivers.

q-7643.text: When looking for the persons who might have been injured in a car accident, should you check all spaces of the crashed car, including the car boot?
q-7643.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A casualty may have been thrown from the seat or been travelling in the luggage space, and after a collision is often unconscious and not calling for help. That is why every space in the vehicle and its immediate surroundings are checked.

q-7645.text: You are on your own on the scene of an accident in which an injured person needs resuscitation. Should you proceed to performing resuscitation without a prior call for help?
q-7645.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Alone at the scene, you call for help first and only then begin resuscitation — without a rescue team and equipment, chest compressions alone rarely restore circulation. The call takes a moment and shortens the services' journey time.

q-7646.text: When reporting a traffic accident to the alarm numer of the emergency services, should you provide your personal data?
q-7646.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The dispatcher must know who is reporting the incident in order to call back, pin down the location and obtain further information about the casualties. Giving your details also limits the number of false reports that tie up the emergency services.

q-7647.text: Does covering a person injured in a road accident with a thermal insulation blanket with the golden side up protect him from heat loss?
q-7647.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A thermal blanket reflects heat back towards the body and shields the casualty from wind and moisture. A hypothermic person is wrapped with the gold side outwards, because then the foil keeps in their own heat.

q-7648.text: Should a person who has regained his breath but is unconscious be placed in the recovery position?
q-7648.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An unconscious person who is breathing has slack muscles and may suffocate on their own tongue or stomach contents. The recovery position keeps the airway open; until the services arrive, breathing must be checked continuously.

q-7649.text: Can you pour cold water onto a burn?
q-7649.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A burn is cooled with clean, cool water for ten to twenty minutes — this limits the depth of the injury and reduces pain. Clothing stuck to the burn is not pulled off, blisters are not pierced, and no fats or home-made ointments are applied.

q-7650.text: Can you put a sterile gauze compress directly on the wound?
q-7650.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Sterile gauze is intended for direct contact with the wound: it protects it from contamination and helps to stem bleeding. The dressing is not touched on the side that will lie on the wound, and the whole is fixed with a bandage.

q-7661.text: Which of the following objects is a mandatory equipment for buses used in public transport?
q-7661.explanation: Correct answer: C. A bus must be equipped with a warning triangle, with which a vehicle immobilised on the road is marked. The rules do not, however, oblige a city bus to carry a spare wheel or a first-aid kit.

q-7662.text: In which of the following cases are the safety belts properly fastened?

options.A: When they are close-fitting to the neck.
options.B: When they are fastened at all, irrespective of the manner in which they are positioned.
options.C: When they are close-fitting to the body below the neck.

q-7662.explanation: Correct answer: C. The belt webbing must lie against the body below the neck: across the middle of the collarbone, the chest and low across the hips. A belt resting on the neck risks serious injury under harsh braking, and a loose one will not hold the body in the seat.

q-7663.text: How many persons are you allowed to carry on an articulated bus used for public transport?

options.A: Not more than the number specified by the carrier.
options.B: Not more than the capacity specified in the registration card.
options.C: As many as the vehicle can actually fit, provided that the doors can be closed.

q-7663.explanation: Correct answer: B. The number of people carried may not exceed the number of seats entered in the registration document, because it follows from the vehicle's design and its permissible mass. An overloaded bus takes longer to brake and loses stability.

q-7664.text: What is the purpose of using a parking brake in a bus?

options.A: To stop the bus in an emergency.
options.B: To immobilize a vehicle at a bus stop.
options.C: Only to immobilize a vehicle during a longer stopover.

q-7664.explanation: Correct answer: B. The stop brake immobilises the bus while passengers get on and off, so that the vehicle does not move with the doors open. The service brake serves for emergency braking, and the parking brake for a longer stop.

q-7665.text: What is the maximum total duration of driving a bus during two consecutive weeks?

options.C: It is specified exclusively by the employment contract.

q-7665.explanation: Correct answer: B. The total driving time in two consecutive weeks may not exceed 90 hours. The limit applies regardless of the terms of the employment contract and is meant to prevent tiredness, which lengthens the driver's reaction time.

q-7666.text: Compensation for the shortened weekly rest period of the driver is an additional rest which should be taken:
q-7666.explanation: Correct answer: C. Compensatory rest for a reduced week is taken in one go, in full, attached to another rest period. Splitting this compensation into parts is not allowed, because it would not ensure full recovery.

q-7667.text: You are performing a road transport by bus. What period should be covered by charts, manual entries and printouts that record your activities and which you are required to have with you?

options.A: The current day and the preceding 45 days.
options.B: The current day and the preceding 28 days.
options.C: The current and the preceding month.

q-7667.explanation: Correct answer: B. The driver must have with them the records of their activity for the current day and the previous 28 days and show them during a roadside check. They include record sheets, manual entries and tachograph printouts.

q-7668.text: How long rest period is a driver required to take as a compensation for the shortened weekly rest period that lasted 24 hours?
q-7668.explanation: Correct answer: B. A regular weekly rest lasts 45 hours, so after reducing it to 24 hours the missing 21 hours must be taken as compensatory rest. It is taken in one go, attached to another rest period.

q-7671.text: How many times will the braking distance lengthen if you double the speed of the bus that you are driving?
q-7671.explanation: Correct answer: B. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed, so doubling it makes that distance four times longer. In a heavy, fully loaded bus this means a very large difference in where the vehicle comes to a stop.

q-7673.text: In which of the following cases are you required to give short horn blasts while driving a bus in the fog?

options.A: While overtaking in a built-up area.
options.B: While overtaking outside a built-up area.
options.C: While passing a stationary object in a built-up area.

q-7673.explanation: Correct answer: B. When the clarity of the air is reduced, a driver overtaking outside a built-up area warns others with a short sound signal. In a built-up area the horn is used only in the event of an immediate danger.

q-7674.text: Which of the following factors can cause incorrect assessment of the situation on the road by the bus driver?
q-7674.explanation: Correct answer: C. Rain, fog, snow or a dazzling sun limit visibility and distort the judgement of the distance and speed of other vehicles. In such conditions slow down, increase the distance and look further ahead.

q-7675.text: In which of the following cases are you allowed to use the rear fog lights while driving a bus?

options.A: In the rain, irrespective of the distance to which visibility is limited.
options.B: In the fog which limits visibility to a distance shorter than 50 meters.
options.C: In the snowfall which limits visibility to a distance of 100 meters.

q-7675.explanation: Correct answer: B. Rear fog lights may be used when fog limits visibility to less than 50 m. They are very bright, so in better visibility they would dazzle drivers behind and must then be switched off.

q-7676.text: In which of the following situations are you required to switch from high beam to low beam lights while driving a bus?

options.A: When you see the parking lights of the vehicle parked in the hard shoulder.
options.B: When you see low beam or high beam lights of the vehicle coming from the opposite direction?
options.C: When you see a pedestrian going in the same direction as you are driving.

q-7676.explanation: Correct answer: B. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle the driver of an oncoming vehicle — they must then be switched to dipped. The same duty applies when driving close behind another vehicle.

q-7677.text: In which of the following situations should you use the speed retarder when driving a bus in a mountainous terrain?

options.B: Only when driving on the bends.
options.C: Only when approaching the top of a hill.

q-7677.explanation: Correct answer: A. In mountainous terrain the retarder assists every braking, so the service brakes heat up less and do not lose effectiveness on long descents. Wear of the brake linings is reduced at the same time.

q-7678.text: In which of the following situations can the ABS of a bus be ineffective when braking?

options.B: When driving on uneven road surfaces.
options.C: When driving on a dry road surface.

q-7678.explanation: Correct answer: B. Over numerous bumps the wheels momentarily lose contact with the surface, and the ABS system reads this as locking and reduces the braking force. The braking distance grows, so on a bumpy road you must drive slower.

q-7679.text: In what position should you adjust the driver’s seat when preparing to drive a bus?

options.A: Always as high as possible, then you can see the road in front of the vehicle better.
options.B: In such a position relative to the steering equipment so that you can press the clutch pedal with the leg slightly bent.
options.C: In any case, as far as possible from the steering wheel, ensuring yourself comfort.

q-7679.explanation: Correct answer: B. The seat is set relative to the pedals and the steering wheel so that the clutch pedal can be pressed fully down with a slightly bent leg. A straight leg loses force and precision, and too great a distance makes confident handling of the steering wheel harder.

q-7680.text: A properly adjusted external mirror on the bus shows:

options.A: Only the space beside the vehicle.
options.B: Only the space behind the vehicle.
options.C: A part of the vehicle side and the space behind it corresponding to the vehicle side

q-7680.explanation: Correct answer: C. A narrow strip of the bus's side must be visible in the mirror as a reference point, together with the space behind the vehicle on the same side. This lets you judge the distance of vehicles behind and change lane safely.

q-7682.text: How should you increase speed when driving a bus, if you want to drive economically?

options.A: So choosing the gear that the tachometer needle remains within the green area.
options.B: Obtaining as fast as possible the maximum speed at each gear.
options.C: Sequentially changing gear when the tachometer needle approaches maximum.

q-7682.explanation: Correct answer: A. Economical driving means keeping the revs in the green range of the rev counter, where the engine works most efficiently. Changing up too early labours the engine, and accelerating at maximum revs needlessly increases fuel consumption.

q-7683.text: Which of the following ways of stopping the bus before the intersection on a dry road surface is appropriate?

options.A: Depressing the clutch pedal and then the brake.
options.B: Simultaneously depressing the clutch and brake pedals.
options.C: Depressing the brake pedal and in the final braking stage the clutch pedal.

q-7683.explanation: Correct answer: C. First you brake with the brake pedal, also using the engine's drag, and press the clutch only just before stopping so that the engine does not stall. Disconnecting the drive earlier lengthens the braking distance and worsens the vehicle's stability.

q-7684.text: In which of the following cases do you get the most effective braking in a bus with a retarder?

options.C: At low speed of the bus.

q-7684.explanation: Correct answer: B. The engine brake works more effectively the higher the engine revs, because the resistance of the air compressed in the cylinders grows. That is why before a long descent you change down and keep the revs high, without exceeding the range permitted by the manufacturer.

q-7685.text: Which of the following activities should you do to initiate engine braking?

options.A: Shift to a higher gear so that the engine runs on low revolutions.
options.C: Shift down gear so that engine revolutions increase.

q-7685.explanation: Correct answer: C. Engine braking is obtained by changing down to a lower gear, which raises the engine revs and increases its resistance. Neutral or a higher gear do the opposite — on a descent the vehicle then gathers speed.

q-7686.text: Which of the following activities should you perform when braking rapidly in an emergency?

options.A: First use the retarder to brake and then depress the service brake.
options.B: First depress the clutch and then depress the service brake.
options.C: Simultaneously depress the brake and clutch pedals.

q-7686.explanation: Correct answer: C. In emergency braking the brake pedal and the clutch pedal are pressed fully down at the same time — this gives maximum deceleration, and the engine does not stall. Throughout, the driver corrects the vehicle's path with the steering wheel.

q-7687.text: Which of the following functions does the retarder in a bus serve?

options.B: It stabilises the trajectory on a slippery road.
options.C: It ensures constant braking during a lengthy downhill drive.

q-7687.explanation: Correct answer: C. A retarder is an additional brake that maintains steady braking on a long descent and protects the service brakes from overheating. It does not increase speed and does not stabilise the vehicle's path.

q-7688.text: Which of the following activities must you not perform when carrying passengers on the bus?

options.B: Talk on the phone in a manner that does not require holding a receiver or a microphone in the hand.

q-7688.explanation: Correct answer: A. A bus driver may not eat while carrying passengers — it occupies the hands and draws attention away from the road. A conversation on a hands-free kit and listening to the radio are not prohibited in themselves.

q-7693.text: Which of the following factors may result in decrease in the level of the cooling system liquid?

options.A: Work of the engine at high revolutions.
options.C: Damage to the water pump drive belt.

q-7693.explanation: Correct answer: B. The level of coolant in the cooling system drops above all when the system leaks and coolant escapes or evaporates. A damaged pump belt causes the engine to overheat, but in itself does not reduce the amount of coolant.

q-7694.text: Should you check the oil level in the engine in an agricultural tractor immediately after the engine immobilisation?

options.B: No, you should wait for the period indicated in the manual by the manufacturer.
options.C: No, you should always wait for an hour.

q-7694.explanation: Correct answer: B. Immediately after switching off the engine the oil is still draining to the sump, so the reading would be low. Wait the time given by the manufacturer in the owner's manual and measure the level on level ground.

q-7695.text: In which of the following situations should you not start the engine in an agricultural tractor?

options.B: If the level of oil in the engine is below the minimum level mark on the dipstick.
options.C: If the fuel tank is not fully filled up.

q-7695.explanation: Correct answer: B. With the oil level below the minimum, lubrication is insufficient and starting the engine risks seizing it. The oil must be topped up before starting; rain or a partly full fuel tank is no obstacle.

q-7697.text: What does the activated control lamp indicated in the photo by the red arrow signal?

options.A: Air pressure in the tyres is too low.
options.B: The emergency brake lever is pulled up.
options.C: Rear drive axle lock is switched on.

q-7697.explanation: Correct answer: B. The light indicated signals that the emergency brake lever remains applied. Before moving off it must be fully released, because driving with the brake acting overheats the linings and increases fuel consumption.

q-7698.text: How should you dress a heavily bleeding wound to stop the bleeding?

options.B: Pour iodine or gentian on the wound.
options.C: Apply a usual dressing, e.g.: gauze or bandage.

q-7698.explanation: Correct answer: A. Heavy bleeding is stemmed with a pressure dressing: sterile material is placed on the wound, pressed down with an additional layer and bandaged firmly. An ordinary dressing quickly soaks through, and pouring antiseptics over the wound will not stop the bleeding.

q-7699.text: In which of the following situation should you resolve to removing a casualty out of the crashed vehicle before the arrival of emergency serves, if you have reasons to believe that he has suffered a spine injury?

options.A: When requested by the person being rescued.
options.B: When there is threat to life of the injured person.
options.C: When requested by the family of the person being rescued.

q-7699.explanation: Correct answer: B. With a suspected spinal injury the injured person is left in the vehicle until the rescuers arrive. The exception is an immediate threat to life, for example fire or absence of breathing — then evacuation is necessary despite the risk.

q-7700.text: Which of the following substances must you not use to clean the wound?
q-7700.explanation: Correct answer: A. Surgical spirit is not used to wash wounds — alcohol damages the tissue, causes severe pain and hinders healing. A wound is washed with clean water or hydrogen peroxide, and spirit-based products are only for the skin around the wound.

q-7701.text: Which of the following actions is not appropriate in nosebleed treatment?

options.A: Tilting the injured person’s head backwards.
options.B: Leaning the injured person’s head forwards.
options.C: Placing a cold compress on the injured person’s neck.

q-7701.explanation: Correct answer: A. Tilting the head back with a nosebleed is a mistake — the blood runs down the throat and risks choking and vomiting. The head is tilted forward, the sides of the nose are pinched, and a cold compress may be applied to the back of the neck.

q-7702.text: How should you treat an injured person with a severe bleeding from the forearm?

options.A: Place a sterile dressing on the wound, bind it with a bandage and press firmly with a bandage roll, then raise the limb up.
options.B: Remove the dressings soaked with blood and replace them with new ones.
options.C: If the injured person is conscious let him do the first aid himself.

q-7702.explanation: Correct answer: A. Bleeding from the forearm is stemmed with a sterile dressing, a bandage and additional pressure, for example from a roll of bandage, and the limb is raised above the level of the heart. Soaked dressings are not removed — further layers are added.

q-7703.text: If you suspect a limb fracture, you should immobilise the casualty’s:

options.A: only the joint closest to the fractured area.
options.C: both the fractured area and the joints above and below this area.

q-7703.explanation: Correct answer: C. With a suspected limb fracture, the site of the injury itself and the two neighbouring joints — below and above the fracture — are immobilised. Only that extent blocks movement of the fragments and reduces pain and the risk of further damage.

q-7705.text: How should you treat the victim who has suffered a burn?

options.B: Cover it tightly with a bandage.

q-7705.explanation: Correct answer: C. A burn is cooled with clean, cool water until the pain subsides, and then covered with a loose sterile dressing. Smearing with fat and tight bandaging deepen the injury and hinder later treatment.

q-7706.text: In which of the following situations should you stop cardiopulmonary resuscitation?

options.A: When the injured person starts breathing spontaneously.
options.C: When you see the medical service ambulance approaching.

q-7706.explanation: Correct answer: A. Resuscitation is stopped when the casualty begins to breathe on their own, and also when rescuers take over or the rescuer is exhausted. The mere sight of an approaching ambulance, or a set amount of time passing, is no reason to stop.

q-7708.text: Which gear is appropriate to start driving a passenger car on a dry surface?

options.C: The one in which the driving stopped.

q-7708.explanation: Correct answer: B. A car moves off in first gear, because it gives the greatest driving force at low speed. Second gear on a dry surface risks a jolt and a stalled engine.

q-7709.text: A properly adjusted external mirror on a passenger car shows:

options.A: only the space beside the vehicle.
options.B: only the space behind the vehicle.
options.C: a part of the vehicle side and the space behind it corresponding to the vehicle side.

q-7709.explanation: Correct answer: C. A well-adjusted exterior mirror shows a narrow strip of your own vehicle's side as a reference point and the space behind the vehicle on that side. This setting reduces the blind spot, which must still be checked with a look over the shoulder.

q-7710.text: Which of the following emergency braking techniques should be applied in a passenger car fitted with ABS?

options.A: Quickly and firmly depress the brake pedal.
options.B: Smoothly depress the brake pedal, gradually increasing the pressure until the ABS activates.

q-7710.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a vehicle with ABS, emergency braking means pressing the brake pedal quickly and hard and keeping up the pressure — the system itself prevents the wheels from locking. Pumping the brake or increasing the pressure gradually only lengthens the braking distance.

q-7712.text: In the presented situation, should you increase the distance when passing these vehicles?
q-7712.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing vehicles standing on the road, you must increase the lateral distance and reduce speed, because a pedestrian may step out from behind them or a door may open. A greater distance gives time to react and stop safely.

q-7713.text: How should you proceed, if there is an embedded object (wire, stick, knife) in the leg of an accident victim?

options.A: Remove the embedded object from the leg, dress the wound and call for help.
options.B: Do not remove the embedded object, do not touch the wound, call for help.
options.C: Do not remove the embedded object, securely protect the wound by immobilizing the embedded object, call for help.

q-7713.explanation: Correct answer: C. An embedded foreign object is not removed — pulling it out risks sudden haemorrhage and a deeper injury. The object is stabilised with dressings at its sides, the wound around it is protected, and help is called while the casualty's condition is monitored.

q-7714.text: In what road conditions is the technique of engine braking particularly recommended when driving an agricultural tractor?

options.B: Only when driving in the mountains.
