options.C: Only when driving in a boggy terrain.

q-7714.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a slippery surface engine braking is particularly recommended, because it slows the vehicle gently and evenly, without the risk of the wheels locking. Sudden use of the service brake may put the tractor into a skid.

q-7715.text: Which of the following braking techniques should you use to considerably decrease the speed of an agricultural tractor driven on a very slippery surface?

options.B: Using the brake with the clutch off.

q-7715.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a very slippery surface speed is reduced by engine braking, that is, by changing down. The brake with the clutch pressed easily locks the wheels, and a higher gear does not slow the tractor at all.

q-7716.text: While driving a farm tractor downhill should you turn off the gear?

options.B: Yes, over the entire length of the hill.
options.C: Yes, but only on a distance not exceeding 200 meters.

q-7716.explanation: Correct answer: A. Descending a hill, you must not disengage the gear or coast in neutral — you then lose engine braking, the vehicle gathers speed and the brakes quickly overheat. The descent is taken in a gear suited to the steepness.

q-7717.text: In what way does doubling of the motorcycle speed affect the braking distance?

options.C: It does not change the braking distance.

q-7717.explanation: Correct answer: B. The braking distance grows in proportion to the square of the speed, so driving twice as fast makes it four times longer. On top of that comes the distance covered during the reaction time, which grows in direct proportion to speed.

q-7718.text: Are you allowed in this place to turn right from the lane you are taking?
q-7718.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The permitted directions of travel from a given lane are decided by the signs and markings visible in the material — a right turn from the lane you are in is not permitted. To turn, you must first change to the correct lane.

q-7725.text: A load carried must not protrude from the front of the vehicle at a distance:

options.A: longer than 0.23 m from the front surface of its outline and longer than 1m from the driver’s seat.
options.B: longer than 0.5 m from the front surface of its outline and longer than 1m from the driver’s seat.
options.C: longer than 0.5 m from the front surface of its outline and longer than 1.5m from the driver’s seat.

q-7725.explanation: Correct answer: C. A load may not protrude at the front more than 0.5 m beyond the front plane of the vehicle's outline, nor more than 1.5 m from the driver's seat. A load extending further limits the field of vision and makes judging dimensions harder.

q-7726.text: You may use a shortened day rest period:

options.C: three times between two-week rest periods.

q-7726.explanation: Correct answer: C. A driver may use a reduced daily rest period at most three times between two weekly rest periods. The other daily rests in that interval must be of the full, regular length.

q-7727.text: How long should a regular weekly rest period of a lorry driver performing road transport be?
q-7727.explanation: Correct answer: B. A regular weekly rest period lasts at least 45 hours. A shorter, reduced weekly rest is allowed only exceptionally and requires the missing time to be taken later.

q-7728.text: When you are supervising unloading of your vehicle, the tachograph switch should be in the mode:
q-7728.explanation: Correct answer: A. Supervising unloading is a work activity that is not driving, so the tachograph switch is set to "other work". A period of availability is recorded when the driver is only waiting and performing no tasks.

q-7731.text: Which of the following factors has the greatest impact on the grip of the truck tyre to the ground?

options.B: The engine power of a vehicle.
options.C: The type and condition of the road surface.

q-7731.explanation: Correct answer: C. Grip is decided above all by the type and state of the surface — dry, wet, icy or muddy asphalt behaves differently. Tyre size and engine power do not in themselves create grip.

q-7746.text: Which of the following rules should you apply when placing or fastening a load in a lorry?

options.A: The center of gravity of the whole load should be as close as possible to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
options.B: Heavier items should be placed above and lighter ones below.
options.C: The method of fastening the load is independent of the characteristics of the load.

q-7746.explanation: Correct answer: A. The load's centre of gravity is placed as close as possible to the vehicle's longitudinal axis, so that the wheels are loaded evenly and the vehicle is stable. Heavier items are placed low, and the method of fastening is matched to the load's properties.

q-7748.text: How does the centre of gravity of a load affect the method of securing the load?

options.A: It does not affect the method of securing the load.
options.B: The high centre of gravity of the load may require the use of additional techniques to secure the load.
options.C: The low centre of gravity of the load means that the load does not need to be secured.

q-7748.explanation: Correct answer: B. A high centre of gravity makes the load prone to tipping over in bends and under braking, so it often requires additional straps, braces or supports. A low centre of gravity does not release you from the duty to fasten it.

q-7764.text: Which of the following documents are you required to have on you, if you drive a bus carrying persons as part of a scheduled transport?

options.B: A training certificate in Health and Safety at Work.

q-7764.explanation: Correct answer: C. On a regular service the bus driver must have the timetable with them — it is used to check the route, the stops and the times of the run. The other certificates listed do not have to be carried in the vehicle.

q-7765.text: Which of the following actions should be performed prior to changing a wheel on a bus?

options.A: Place chocks under the opposite wheel.
options.C: Set the gear to neutral position.

q-7765.explanation: Correct answer: A. Before raising the bus with a jack, chocks are placed under the opposite wheel so that the vehicle does not move. The parking brake stays applied, and the gearbox is not put into neutral.

q-7766.text: Is it advisable in winter time to pour petrol into the tank of a diesel engine bus?

options.A: Yes it is advisable due to the decrease in petrol clogging.
options.B: Yes, it the amount of the petrol poured in is not greater than 10% of the tank volume.
options.C: No, because it leads to a damage of the power supply system and the engine.

q-7766.explanation: Correct answer: C. Petrol worsens the lubricating properties of diesel fuel and destroys parts of the fuel system and the engine. In winter you fill up with winter-grade diesel or use additives approved by the manufacturer.

q-7767.text: What function in a diesel engine does a glow plug perform?

options.A: It makes the start of a cold engine easier.
options.B: It heats up the fuel in the tank.
options.C: It heats up the cooling liquid.

q-7767.explanation: Correct answer: A. A glow plug heats the air in the combustion chamber, so a cold diesel engine starts more easily and runs more evenly after starting. It heats neither the fuel in the tank nor the coolant.

q-7769.text: Which of the following symptoms may indicate a deficiency of fluid in the power steering on the bus?

options.B: Side skidding of the vehicle front during braking.
options.C: Louder operation of the power steering pump when maneuvering the steering wheel with the engine on.

q-7769.explanation: Correct answer: C. With too little fluid the power-steering pump draws in air, and when the wheel is turned it runs clearly louder and the steering offers more resistance. The fluid level must be checked and the leak found.

q-7770.text: Which of the following symptoms most indicates the clutch disc wear?

options.A: Clear resistance of the lever when changing gears.
options.B: Difficulties in engaging the first or reverse gear.
options.C: Abrupt increase in the engine revolutions without an increase in speed during acceleration.

q-7770.explanation: Correct answer: C. A worn clutch plate slips, so when throttle is added the engine revs rise sharply but the vehicle does not accelerate. This shows most strongly under load, on a climb and in the higher gears.

q-7771.text: While carrying passengers on a tourist bus you notice smoke coming out from the engine compartment. Which of the following actions should you take immediately after stopping the vehicle?

options.B: Move away from the bus as quickly as possible.

q-7771.explanation: Correct answer: C. First the passengers are taken to a safe place, because fire and smoke spread very quickly in a bus. Fighting the fire is attempted only after the evacuation and only when it does not endanger the rescuer.

q-7772.text: Where on the road should you stop your vehicle, when you see in front of you injured persons, crashed vehicles and emergency services vehicles approaching them?

options.A: As close to the accident casualties as possible.
options.B: In a place that provides an unobstructed access for the emergency services vehicles to the casualties and crashed vehicles.
options.C: As close to the crashed vehicles as possible.

q-7772.explanation: Correct answer: B. The vehicle is stopped so as not to block the rescue services' access to the injured and the wrecked vehicles. Pulling up right beside the scene hinders the rescuers' work and increases the risk of another collision.

q-7773.text: While performing resuscitation to an adult you should perform chest compressions at the rate of:
q-7773.explanation: Correct answer: A. An adult's chest is compressed at a rate of 100–120 compressions per minute, letting it return fully to its original shape each time. A slower or faster rhythm does not provide sufficient blood flow.

q-7774.text: Which method of chest compressions is correct when performing a cardiac massage to an adult?

options.A: Pressing downwards with two hands placed in the centre of the chest.
options.B: Pressing downwards with one hand placed just below the sternum.
options.C: Pressing downwards with two fingers placed on the chest above the heart.

q-7774.explanation: Correct answer: A. In an adult the centre of the chest is compressed with both hands placed one on top of the other, with the elbows straight and the pressure coming from the shoulders. One hand or two fingers are techniques used in children.

q-7775.text: What is the symptom of excessive total clearance in the steering system?

options.A: The tendency for an automatic return of the turned wheels to their central position.
options.B: The absence of vibrations in the front suspension.
options.C: A deterioration in the steerability and stability of the vehicle.

q-7775.explanation: Correct answer: C. Too much play means a movement of the steering wheel is not immediately translated into a turn of the wheels — the vehicle reacts late and is harder to keep on its line. Such a technical state disqualifies the vehicle from use on the road.

q-7777.text: In this situation, when approaching the top of the hill on a two-way road, are you allowed to overtake the motorcycle?
q-7777.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a two-way road you must not overtake when approaching the crest of a hill, because the opposite lane is not visible and an oncoming vehicle appears suddenly. The manoeuvre may be performed only after regaining sufficient visibility.

q-7778.text: While driving a bus, are you allowed to consume food?

options.A: Yes, when you are not carrying passengers.
options.B: Yes, when you are carrying only one passenger.
options.C: No, if you are driving on a motorway or express-way, regardless of the number of passengers carried.

q-7778.explanation: Correct answer: A. The ban on eating at the wheel of a bus concerns the carriage of passengers, so when driving without them the driver may eat. When passengers are on board the ban applies regardless of the type of road.

q-7779.text: In this situation, does the flashing yellow light allow you to drive beyond the traffic lights without stopping?
q-7779.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A flashing yellow signal does not stop traffic — it warns that the intersection is not currently controlled by traffic lights. Passage is permitted without stopping, but with particular caution and according to the general rules of priority.

q-7780.text: At what maximum speed are you allowed to drive on the road beyond these signs if you are hauling another passenger car?
q-7780.explanation: Correct answer: B. When towing another vehicle outside a built-up area, speed may not exceed 60 km/h — and that is exactly the stretch of road the signs in the material define. In a built-up area a lower limit applies to towing.

q-7782.text: You are driving on the right lane. Are you allowed to turn right at the intersection?
q-7782.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A right turn is permitted from the right lane, as follows from the signs and markings visible in the material. Before the manoeuvre you must switch on the indicator in advance, move towards the right edge of the roadway and give way to pedestrians.

q-7821.text: Are you allowed in this situation to turn right onto the presented road?
q-7821.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning right into this road is prohibited by the signs visible in the material. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the road seems clear — you may turn only where it is permitted.

q-7823.text: Which of the following activities are you obliged to perform before driving the vehicle shown?

options.A: Only wipe off snow on the front windscreen of the vehicle.
options.B: Only wipe off snow on the car glass.
options.C: Wipe off snow on the car glass, engine cover, roof and mirrors.

q-7823.explanation: Correct answer: C. Before driving, snow must be removed from all the windows, the bonnet, the roof and the mirrors. A lingering layer limits visibility, and under braking it slides onto the windscreen or falls onto other road users.

q-7828.text: You are driving a motorcycle in the rain. How should you react when you notice that the rear tyre of your vehicle is losing grip?

options.B: Slow down immediately, reducing first of all the engine rpm.

q-7828.explanation: Correct answer: B. When the rear wheel loses grip, speed is reduced gently, above all by easing off the throttle. Harsh braking or changing down deepens the slide and can lead to the motorcycle falling over.

q-7833.text: How should you observe the road while riding your motorcycle, if you intend to enter the traffic lane on your left?

options.A: By just looking into the left mirror.
options.C: By looking into the left mirror, and if necessary, turning your head.

q-7833.explanation: Correct answer: C. A mirror does not cover the whole space beside the vehicle — a blind spot remains, in which another vehicle may be travelling. That is why you first look in the left mirror and, if necessary, also turn your head, and only then change lane.

q-7834.text: Which of the these actions should you perform when riding a motorcycle, and need to overcome a sharp bend of the road?

options.A: Reduce the gear at the bend of the road?
options.B: Adjust the speed early enough so as not to apply the brake at the bendof the road .
options.C: Apply the brake the moment you enter the bend of the road .

q-7834.explanation: Correct answer: B. Speed and gear are chosen before entering the curve, and the curve itself is ridden evenly, without braking. Braking with the motorcycle leaning easily causes loss of grip and pushes the vehicle to the outside of the bend.

q-7850.text: Which of the following information is a mandatory entry on the tachograph record sheet?

options.A: Daily rest period of the driver.

q-7850.explanation: Correct answer: A. A tachograph records driving time, other work, periods of availability and breaks and rest, including the driver's daily rest. Engine revs and the mass of the load are not recorded on the record sheet.

q-7851.text: Under which of the symbols shown does the tachograph record intervals during work and daily rest periods?
q-7851.explanation: Correct answer: C. Breaks from work and daily rest are recorded by the tachograph under the symbol marked C in the material. It is reserved for time in which the driver performs no tasks and freely disposes of their time.

q-7852.text: For how long are you allowed to use the record sheets?

options.A: For a period of up to 10% longer than that for which it is intended.
options.B: For a period not longer than that for which it is intended.

q-7852.explanation: Correct answer: B. A tachograph chart is used only for the period for which it is intended. Using it longer causes the records to overlap, making them illegible, and the record of the driver's working time is kept incorrectly.

q-7855.text: How many metres distance from the preceding vehicle should you maintain when stopping in the tunnel due to a traffic jam?
q-7855.explanation: Correct answer: B. When stopping in a tunnel because of a traffic jam, a distance of at least 5 metres from the vehicle ahead is kept. Such a gap allows pulling out of the column and makes it easier for the rescue services' vehicles to get through.

q-7856.text: In which of these cases, does the engine brake turn off automatically?

options.A: When the engine speed is less than 1500 rpm.
options.B: When the vehicle speed is less than 30 km/h.
options.C: When the ABS system turns on

q-7856.explanation: Correct answer: C. The moment the ABS system operates, the engine brake switches off automatically so that additional braking of the driven wheels does not interfere with the metering of the braking force. As a result the wheels do not lock and the vehicle stays steerable.

q-7859.text: What may be the consequence of a long bus drive, when the tachometre indicator is constantly in the red field?
q-7859.explanation: Correct answer: B. The red band of the rev counter is the range of revs above the value permitted by the manufacturer. Prolonged driving in that range overloads and overheats the engine, leading to damage, and fuel consumption rises as well.

q-7883.text: Should you signal your intention to turn right in this situation?
q-7883.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver is obliged to signal an intended change of direction in advance and clearly with the indicator. The signal is switched on early enough and switched off immediately after the manoeuvre is completed.

q-7884.text: Are you obliged to use low-beam lights in this situation?
q-7884.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A moving vehicle must be lit around the clock, all year round. After dusk, in a tunnel and when the clarity of the air is reduced, dipped headlights are compulsory, not daytime running lights alone.

q-8062.text: Does this sign warn you that you are approaching an intersection where traffic merges from the left?
q-8062.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible sign does not convey what the question asks about. Warning signs before an intersection show the road layout and the side from which the subordinate road joins, but do not say that it is one-way.

q-8064.text: In the situation presented, are you approaching a level crossing without a barrier?
q-8064.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material does not announce a level crossing without barriers. The type of crossing is recognised by the warning sign — two different signs are used for a crossing with barriers and one without.

q-8068.text: In this situation, are you approaching a crossroads, where the right of way is determined by road signs?
q-8068.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority at this intersection is not set by signs, so the general rule applies — you give way to the vehicle approaching from the right. Such an intersection is approached with particular caution.

q-8070.text: Are you obliged in each case, to stop the vehicle before entering such an intersection?
q-8070.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to give way does not mean a duty to stop every time — you must stop when the situation on the road requires it. An absolute stop is required before an intersection marked with a STOP sign.

q-8073.text: In this situation, are you warned that you are approaching a pedestrian crossing?
q-8073.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible signing does not warn of a pedestrian crossing. A separate warning sign announces that a crossing is ahead, and the crossing itself is marked with an information sign and road markings on the carriageway.

q-8074.text: If you drive straight ahead, are you approaching a place where a two-way traffic begins?
q-8074.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material announce the beginning of a section with two-way traffic. Further on, vehicles coming from the opposite direction will appear, so you must keep to the right, reduce speed and refrain from overtaking.

q-8075.text: In the situation presented, are you approaching a level-crossing with barriers?
q-8075.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material announces a level crossing with barriers. You must slow down and be ready to stop before the crossing, because the barriers may begin to lower at any moment.

q-8080.text: Does the visible sign warn you of a level-crossing with barriers?
q-8080.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible signs warn precisely of a railway crossing with barriers. Different signs are used for guarded and unguarded crossings, so from a distance you already know what kind of protection to expect.

q-8081.text: In this situation, are you warned of the possibility of black ice occurring on the road?
q-8081.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible signing warns of the possibility of black ice. On such a stretch you must slow down, increase the distance from the vehicle ahead and avoid harsh braking and sudden steering movements.

q-8084.text: In this situation, are you approaching a road with the right of way?
q-8084.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material inform that the cross road ahead of you is the road with priority. You should reduce speed, assess the situation and give way to vehicles travelling on it, stopping if necessary.

q-8085.text: In this situation, do you have the right of way at the nearest intersection over vehicles approaching from the left side?
q-8085.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At the nearest intersection priority is on your side, so vehicles approaching from the left must give way to you. Even so, you must approach carefully and make sure the driver on the left really is giving way.

q-8086.text: Should you in this situation, after driving 80 m, yield way to vehicles travelling on the transverse road?
q-8086.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material announce that in 80 m there is an intersection where you must give way to vehicles travelling on the cross road. The stated distance lets you slow down and look around in advance.

q-8094.text: Is it allowed to stop a passenger car on a road dedicated to bicycles, if you have at least 1.5 m width left for cyclists?
q-8094.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping a car on a cycle path is prohibited regardless of how much room is left for cyclists. That path is intended for them, and a standing vehicle forces them onto the carriageway.

q-8098.text: In this situation, are you permitted to stop the vehicle for a while on the roadway in order to drop off a passenger?
q-8098.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force at this place prohibit stopping, and this prohibition also covers a short halt to drop off a passenger. A passenger may be dropped off only where stopping the vehicle is permitted and does not obstruct traffic.

q-8101.text: In this situation, are allowed to stop the vehicle on the hard shoulder?
q-8101.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The no-stopping prohibition in force here covers the whole road on the side where the sign is installed, and therefore also the shoulder. Pulling onto the shoulder is not a way of getting around the prohibition.

q-8102.text: Are you allowed in this situation to park a motor vehicle on the roadway behind the sign?
q-8102.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign visible in the material prohibits parking on this section, so leaving a motor vehicle on the roadway beyond the sign is not permitted. The prohibition applies from the sign up to the nearest intersection or to the place where it is cancelled.

q-8103.text: Is it permitted behind the visible prohibition sign to stop a motor vehicle on the pavement?
q-8103.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition arising from the signs visible in the material covers the whole road on this section, and therefore also the pavement running alongside the roadway. Parking a motor vehicle on the pavement is permitted only where no sign prohibits it.

q-8108.text: In this situation, are you obliged after performing an overtaking manoeuvre to enter the right traffic lane?
q-8108.explanation: Correct answer: YES. After overtaking, the driver is obliged to return to the previously occupied right lane as soon as they can do so without obstructing the vehicle overtaken. Staying in the left lane without need blocks faster drivers and prolongs their manoeuvres.

q-8114.text: Is it prohibited in this situation, to stop the vehicle on the right hard shoulder of this road?
q-8114.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The no-stopping prohibition in force on this section covers the full width of the road, and therefore also the shoulder, not only the roadway. Stopping is permitted here only when forced by a breakdown or another unforeseen event.

q-8116.text: In the visible situation, are you on a two-way single-carriageway with four traffic lanes?
q-8116.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The road has one roadway, because the directions of traffic are not separated by a dividing strip or a barrier, traffic moves in both directions, and the road markings mark four lanes on it. The number of roadways is decided by physical separation, not by the number of lanes.

q-8122.text: Are you permitted to drive on the solid line in th presented situation?
q-8122.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A solid line must not be crossed or driven on — it marks a place where changing lanes or moving into the opposite direction is dangerous. The manoeuvre may be performed only where the line turns into a broken one.

q-8133.text: Are you allowed in the visible situation to change to the right traffic lane in order to continue driving straight on?
q-8133.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The right lane at this place is intended for another direction of travel, as follows from the direction arrows on the roadway or the sign above the lane. You continue straight ahead from a lane that permits that direction.

q-8144.text: In this situation, are you allowed to change to the right traffic lane?
q-8144.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Changing to the right lane is not prohibited at this place either by road markings or by vertical signs. Before the manoeuvre you must signal your intention with the indicator, check the situation behind and give way to those travelling in the right lane.

q-8159.text: In the visible situation, is it necessary to turn on the direction indicators to signal change of traffic lane?
q-8159.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver is obliged to signal an intended lane change in advance and clearly with the indicator so that other road users can adapt their behaviour. Signalling ends immediately after the manoeuvre is completed.

q-8163.text: When approaching the stopping place for a school bus outside the built-up area, are you obliged to allow the driver of the bus to enter the roadway, if it signals the intention to perform such a manoeuvre?
q-8163.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver approaching the stopping place of a school bus outside a built-up area must allow it to join the traffic if the bus signals that intention. You should reduce speed and, if necessary, stop the vehicle.

q-8183.text: Is it allowed to overtake a motor vehicle in such a place on the road?
q-8183.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place overtaking a motor vehicle is prohibited — this follows from the signs in force here and from the limited visibility of the section of road ahead. The manoeuvre may be started only where a sufficiently long, clear section can be seen.

q-8184.text: Are you allowed to start an overtaking manoeuvre in the situation shown?
q-8184.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The conditions on this section do not allow you to safely move onto the opposite lane and return to your own before the approaching vehicle. Overtaking may be started only when the driver is certain of completing the manoeuvre without obstructing others.

q-8186.text: Are you allowed to overtake at this intersection?
q-8186.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban on overtaking at an intersection does not apply where traffic is directed or where you are on a road with priority indicated by the appropriate sign. The manoeuvre remains permitted provided the general safety rules are observed.

q-8203.text: In the visible situation, can an overtaking manoeuvre result in the vehicle skidding and cusing a road accident?
q-8203.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On a slippery or dirty surface, sudden acceleration and a change of path easily cause a loss of grip. A skid on the opposite lane usually ends in a collision, so in such conditions it is better to forgo overtaking.

q-8204.text: Are you allowed in this situation to overtake the preceding vehicle at the intersection?
q-8204.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking at an intersection is permitted when you are on a road with priority or when traffic is directed by traffic lights or an authorised person. Before the manoeuvre you must check that the vehicle in front is not signalling a left turn.

q-8213.text: In this situation, when driving past the stationary vehicle are you performing an evasive manoeuvre?
q-8213.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Driving past a vehicle that is standing is passing. Passing an oncoming vehicle concerns exclusively driving past a vehicle travelling from the opposite direction. When passing, you must keep a safe distance and allow for a pedestrian stepping out from behind the vehicle.

q-8214.text: Are you performing an evasive manoeuvre when driving past the cyclist?
q-8214.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The cyclist is travelling in the same direction, so passing them is overtaking, not passing an oncoming vehicle. Passing in the other sense applies only to a vehicle coming towards you. When overtaking a cyclist, a distance of no less than 1 m applies.

q-8216.text: Are you permitted to perform a reverse manoeuvre in this situation?
q-8216.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place reversing is prohibited — it must not be performed, among other places, in a tunnel, on a bridge, on a viaduct, on a motorway and an expressway, or within an intersection. The manoeuvre must be performed at another, permitted place.

q-8217.text: In the visible situation, can you continue driving in front of the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction?
q-8217.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The obstacle or narrowing is on your side of the roadway, so it is you who must give way to the oncoming vehicle. You continue only after that vehicle has passed, stopping before the obstacle if necessary.

q-8218.text: Is it prohibited to reverse on a one-way road?
q-8218.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Reversing on a one-way road is not prohibited as such. The manoeuvre is permitted if the driver does not endanger safety or obstruct others and, where visibility is insufficient, uses the help of another person.

q-8220.text: When assuming a safe distance from parked vehicles, should you take into account the possibility of one of the vehicles' doors opening?
q-8220.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Next to parked vehicles a door may always suddenly open or a person step onto the roadway. That is why the lateral distance is chosen with a margin, and the speed so that you can brake in time or safely get around the obstacle if necessary.

q-8223.text: Do they cars coming in the opposite direction have the right of way in this situation?
q-8223.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The obstacle or narrowing of the roadway is on your side, so it is you who must give way. The oncoming vehicle passes first, and you stop before the obstacle and wait for the way to be clear.

q-8228.text: In this situation, are you performing an evasive manoeuvre when driving past a stationary public transport vehicle?
q-8228.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Driving past a vehicle that is not moving is passing — regardless of whether it is a city bus or another vehicle. Next to a stationary bus you must exercise particular caution, because pedestrians may step out from behind it.

q-8236.text: Is it prohibited to reverse a vehicle in a tunel, on the bridge and flyover?
q-8236.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Reversing in a tunnel, on a bridge and on a viaduct is prohibited, because there is no room for the manoeuvre there, and visibility and the possibility of getting around the vehicle are very limited. The same prohibition applies on a motorway and an expressway.

q-8238.text: Are you permitted to use the rear fog lights, if fog restricts visibility to a distance of 100 m?
q-8238.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Rear fog lights may be used only when fog, precipitation or smoke reduce visibility to less than 50 m. At 100 m visibility they dazzle drivers behind and make it harder for them to judge distance.

q-8245.text: Are you allowed to use the rear fog lights if the fog restricts visibility to a distance less than 50 m?
q-8245.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Rear fog lights are used when fog, precipitation or smoke reduce visibility to less than 50 m. Once visibility improves they must be switched off immediately, because they dazzle drivers behind.

q-8246.text: Is it prohibited during the day to give warning signal with the main beam headlights, if this may cause blinding to other drivers?
q-8246.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Warning with main-beam headlights during the day is permitted only when it will not dazzle other drivers. If the flash could dazzle anyone on the road, you should forgo such a signal and warn in another way.

q-8251.text: In this situation, are you allowed to enter behind the traffic lights if you do not hinder pedestrian traffic?
q-8251.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A red signal prohibits passing the traffic light without any exceptions — neither the absence of pedestrians nor the belief that no one will be obstructed lifts it. The stop is made before the conditional stop line or before the traffic light.

q-8260.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise special caution?
q-8260.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material is one in which the regulations require particular caution: you must raise your attention, adjust your speed to the conditions and be ready to react immediately to a change in the situation on the road.

q-8266.text: Should you exercise special caution in this situation?
q-8266.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material is one in which the regulations require particular caution — attention must increase and the driver must be ready to react immediately. In practice this means easing off the accelerator and watching the surroundings closely.

q-8267.text: Should you exercise special caution in this situation?
q-8267.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material is one in which the regulations require particular caution — attention must increase and the driver must be ready to react immediately. In practice this means easing off the accelerator and watching the surroundings closely.

q-8274.text: Are you obliged in the visible situation to exercise special caution?
q-8274.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The place shown in the material is one of those where the rules require special care — the driver must pay more attention and be ready to react immediately. This usually means slowing down and watching the surroundings closely.

q-8275.text: In the visible situation, are you obliged to exercise special caution?
q-8275.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The place shown in the material is one of those where the rules require special care — the driver must pay more attention and be ready to react immediately. This usually means slowing down and watching the surroundings closely.

q-8282.text: In this situation, do you have priority over the cyclist after turning right?
q-8282.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver turning right cuts across the path of a bicycle going straight ahead and must give way to it. A cyclist going straight along a cycle path or cycle lane keeps priority over a turning vehicle.

q-8284.text: In this situation, are you obliged to use the sound signal to urge the cyclist to drive faster?
q-8284.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn is used solely to warn of danger, never to hurry other road users along. Urging a cyclist on with the horn may startle them and cause them to lose balance and fall.

q-8285.text: Upon turning right at this intersection, are you obliged to stop before the traffic light?
q-8285.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The red signal also applies to drivers turning right if there is no additional traffic light with a green arrow. The vehicle stops before the conditional stop line or before the traffic light and waits for the permitting signal.

q-8286.text: In the presented situation, should you refrain from overtaking the cyclist?
q-8286.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Conditions on this stretch do not allow the bicycle to be overtaken with the required lateral distance without entering the opposite lane. It is safer to follow the cyclist and wait for a place where the manoeuvre can be carried out without risk.

q-8288.text: In the presented situation, when turning right should you yield priority to the cyclist?
q-8288.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Turning right, you cut across the path of a bicycle going straight ahead on its own part of the road, so you must give way to it. Before turning, check the blind spot and make sure nobody is coming up on the right.

q-8292.text: When driving slowly during a traffic jam, should you anticipate that a cyclist may overtake you from the right?
q-8292.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A cyclist may overtake slow-moving or queuing vehicles on the right, so you have to expect such a manoeuvre. Before changing lane, turning right or opening a door, check the space on the right.

q-8294.text: Should you while driving in this situation exercise special caution?
q-8294.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In this place the regulations require particular caution, i.e. heightened attention and readiness to react immediately to changing conditions. Speed is chosen so that the vehicle can be stopped before an obstacle that appears.

q-8296.text: Upon turning right in this situation, should you yield priority to the cyclist?
q-8296.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle turning right cuts across the path of a bicycle going straight ahead, so the driver must give way to the cyclist. This applies both to a cycle crossing and to a cycle lane along the right edge of the carriageway.

q-8300.text: In this situation, should you allow a pedestrian to freely exit the pedestrian crossing?
q-8300.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A pedestrian who has already stepped onto the crossing has priority and must be able to walk calmly to the end. The driver waits until the pedestrian leaves the carriageway, and neither hurries them nor drives past right behind them.

q-8304.text: In the presented situation, do you have the right to enter the level crossing without stopping after making sure that no rail vehicle is coming?
q-8304.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing in force here requires the vehicle to stop unconditionally before the crossing, regardless of whether the tracks are clear. Only after stopping and making sure nothing is approaching may you move off.

q-8305.text: In the presented situation, do you have the right to enter the level crossing?
q-8305.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Entering the crossing is prohibited at this moment — you may not enter when a prohibiting signal is shown, the barriers are closing or lowered, or there is no room beyond the crossing to continue. You must stop before the crossing.

q-8306.text: In the presented situation, are you approaching a level crossing without a barrier?
q-8306.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material does not announce a level crossing without barriers. The type of crossing is recognised by the warning sign — two different signs are used for a crossing with barriers and one without.

q-8309.text: Are you permitted to enter the level crossing while the barrier is being lifted by the railway worker?
q-8309.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Entering the crossing is allowed only once the barriers are fully raised and the signals do not prohibit passing. While being raised, the barriers may still be stopped or lowered again.

q-8311.text: When passing through a level crossing, do you have priority over an oncoming rail vehicle?
q-8311.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a level crossing the rail vehicle always has priority, whether or not the crossing is guarded. A train cannot stop within a short distance or steer around an obstacle on the tracks.

q-8314.text: In this situation, are you permitted to enter the level crossing while exercising special caution?
q-8314.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition on entering the crossing that applies here is absolute and cannot be bypassed by care alone. Until the signals or the position of the barriers permit passing, the vehicle must remain before the crossing.

q-8315.text: In the situation shown, are you in front of a single-rail level crossing?
q-8315.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing placed before this crossing indicates more than one track, so it is not a single-track crossing. After the first train has passed, another may be approaching on the neighbouring track, so you must not move off hastily.

q-8316.text: Upon passage of the rail vehicle, half of the barrier is lifted. Are you allowed in this situation to start driving on to the rail tracks?
q-8316.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You may move off only once the half-barriers are fully raised and the signals do not prohibit passing. While being raised they may still come down again, because another rail vehicle may be approaching on the second track.

q-8317.text: In the presented situation, are you approaching a level crossing with barriers?
q-8317.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material announces a level crossing with barriers. You must slow down and be ready to stop before the crossing, because the barriers may begin to lower at any moment.

q-8320.text: Is it permitted on a one-way road to overtake a rail vehicle from the left?
q-8320.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A rail vehicle is, as a rule, overtaken on the right, but on a one-way roadway overtaking it on the left is also permitted. There is no oncoming traffic there, so the manoeuvre does not lead to a head-on collision.

q-8322.text: Should you make sure that no rail vehicle is approaching before entering onto the rail tracks?
q-8322.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before entering the tracks, the driver is obliged to make sure no rail vehicle is approaching, because it has unconditional priority there. You should look in both directions and move off only when the crossing is clear.

q-8323.text: In the event of immobilisation of a vehicle on a level crossing, are you obliged to warn the rail vehicle driver if it impossible to remove the vehicle from the level crossing?
q-8323.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When the vehicle cannot be removed from the crossing, the driver must immediately warn the train driver and other road users, for example with a light signal visible from afar. The passengers should first leave the vehicle and move away from the tracks.

q-8326.text: Are you obliged in this situation to stop before the traffic light?
q-8326.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown prohibits passing the traffic light, so the driver must stop the vehicle before the conditional stop line, and where there is none — before the traffic light. Travel is resumed only after the permitting signal appears.

q-8328.text: Are you permitted, in this situation to enter the level crossing only after making sure that no rail vehicle is approaching?
q-8328.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before entering the crossing, the driver must take special care and make sure no rail vehicle is approaching, because it has absolute priority. Look both ways along the tracks.

q-8329.text: In the situation presented. are you obliged to exercise special caution, stop the vehicle and make sure that no rail vehicle is approaching?
q-8329.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing in force before this crossing requires the vehicle to stop unconditionally, and only then may the situation on the tracks be assessed. You may move off only when no rail vehicle is approaching.

q-8333.text: When approaching a level crossing, are you obliged to apply the principle of special caution?
q-8333.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A level crossing is one of the places where the rules require special care — the driver slows down, watches the tracks and is ready to stop the vehicle immediately. A rail vehicle always has priority there.

q-8352.text: You are involved in a motor accident in such a place on the road in a built-up area. Are you obliged to signal the stop of the motor vehicle?
q-8352.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle immobilised on the roadway after an accident must be marked with a warning triangle and the hazard lights switched on, so that other drivers notice the obstacle early enough. In a built-up area the triangle is placed directly behind the vehicle.

q-8353.text: Does this sign inform you of the minimum speed at which you are allowed to travel?
q-8353.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible sign sets the maximum speed that must not be exceeded on this section, not a lower speed limit. A minimum speed is imposed by a separate mandatory sign, with a different appearance and meaning.

q-8356.text: In the presented situation, do you have the right to stop the vehicle on the roadway on the bridge?
q-8356.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping a vehicle on the roadway on a bridge is prohibited, because it narrows the passage and creates an obstacle in a place that cannot be safely got around. You may stop only beyond the structure, at a permitted place.

q-8359.text: In the presented situation, are you allowed to make a U-turn at the intersection?
q-8359.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around at this intersection is prohibited by the signs in force here, and besides, the manoeuvre would require crossing the path of other vehicles. You may turn around only at a place where there is no such prohibition.

q-8360.text: In this situation, are you informed of travelling on a one-way road?
q-8360.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible signing has a different meaning and does not indicate that the road is one-way. One-way traffic is indicated by a separate information sign, confirmed by the absence of oncoming vehicles and the corresponding road markings.

q-8361.text: In this situation, do you have the right of way at the narrowed section of the roadway?
q-8361.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force here grant priority to drivers approaching from the opposite direction, so at the narrowing you must give way to them. You should stop before the narrowed section and enter it only when it is clear.

q-8363.text: Are you entitled in this situation, to enter the road beyond this vertical sign, if you do not pose a traffic problem to other vehicles?
q-8363.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A prohibition sign applies unconditionally — neither the absence of other vehicles nor the belief that no one will be obstructed lifts it. Passing such a sign is an offence and risks driving against the flow.

q-8364.text: In this situation, do you have a right to enter the intersection without stopping?
q-8364.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force before this intersection order an absolute stop of the vehicle, regardless of whether the cross road is clear. Only after stopping is the situation assessed and way given.

q-8365.text: In this situation, do you have the right to drive straight ahead through the intersection?
q-8365.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing in force here indicates the permitted directions of travel and does not allow you to go straight across the junction. The driver must go in a direction that this order permits.

q-8366.text: In this situation, should stopping the vehicle in order to yield the right of way occur each time before the "STOP" sign?
q-8366.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to stop remains, but the vehicle stops before the absolute stop line marked on the roadway, if such a line has been painted. Only when there is none does the stop take place at the sign itself.

q-8367.text: In this situation, when turning right can you enter the intersection without stopping?
q-8367.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The order to stop absolutely applies regardless of the intended direction of travel, so also when turning right. You may move off only after stopping the vehicle and giving way to road users on the cross road.

q-8368.text: Does the visible sign indicate that you should turn right at the nearest roadway?
q-8368.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible signs have a different meaning and do not order a right turn into the nearest roadway. A duty to go right is expressed by a separate mandatory sign, and the driver complies with it only where it is installed.

q-8371.text: Does the prohibition expressed by this vertical sign prohibit you from turning left at the nearest intersection?
q-8371.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition expressed by this sign concerns a different manoeuvre and does not cover a left turn at the nearest intersection. A left turn would be prohibited only by a separate no-left-turn sign installed before that intersection.

q-8373.text: Is it permitted at this intersection to turn right without stopping?
q-8373.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Before this intersection an absolute stop is required, and it applies to every direction of travel, including a right turn. The vehicle must come to a complete stop, and only then may you give way and enter the intersection.

q-8374.text: Stopping the vehicle at this intersection should occur before the "STOP" sign?
q-8374.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When an absolute stop line has been marked on the roadway, the vehicle stops before that line, not at the sign itself. The stopping place should also give a view of the road to which you are giving way.

q-8378.text: Are you obliged in this situation, to stop before the "STOP" sign if you intend to continue driving straight through the intersection?
q-8378.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping is of course necessary, but it is done before the absolute stop line marked on the roadway, not at the sign itself. The direction of further travel does not change the place where the vehicle must come to a halt.

q-8380.text: Are you permitted in the presented situation to make a U-turn?
q-8380.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force at this place prohibit turning around, and this prohibition does not depend on the volume of traffic or the width of the roadway. You may turn around only where the prohibition ceases to apply and the manoeuvre endangers no one.

q-8383.text: In the situation presented, are you entitled to drive through the level crossing without stopping, if there is no rail vehicle approaching?
q-8383.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing before this crossing requires the vehicle to stop unconditionally, so clear tracks do not release you from that duty. You stop before the line or the sign, and only then assess the situation on the tracks.

q-8386.text: In the visible situation, do you have the right to drive onto the level crossing, if there is no rail vehicle approaching?
q-8386.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A stop requirement applies before this crossing, and the absence of an approaching train does not lift it. Only after the vehicle has come to a complete stop and you have made sure the tracks are clear may you cross them.

q-8387.text: In the presenetd situation, are you entitled to make a U-turn at the nearest intersection?
q-8387.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force here prohibit turning around at the nearest intersection, so the manoeuvre must be performed elsewhere. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the road happens to be clear.

q-8388.text: In the presented situation, are you entitled to make a U-turn at the nearest intersection?
q-8388.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force here prohibit turning around at the nearest intersection, so the manoeuvre must be performed elsewhere. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the road happens to be clear.

q-8389.text: In the presented situation, are you entitled to make a U-turn at the nearest intersection?
q-8389.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs in force here prohibit turning around at the nearest intersection, so the manoeuvre must be performed elsewhere. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the road happens to be clear.

q-8391.text: In the presented situation, are you entitled to make a U-turn at the nearest intersection?
q-8391.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around at this intersection is prohibited by the signs in force, and the driver may not disregard this for convenience. The manoeuvre is performed only where the prohibition does not apply and visibility allows it.

q-8392.text: In the visible situation, when transmitting this light signal do you have the right to turn left at the intersection?
q-8392.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown does not permit a left turn — it allows only the direction it indicates. To turn left you must wait for a signal permitting that manoeuvre and give way when the situation requires it.

q-8393.text: Does the visible prohibition sign forbid you from turning left at the intersection?
q-8393.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible prohibition sign covers a manoeuvre other than a left turn, so turning left at this intersection remains permitted. A prohibition applies exactly to the extent that follows from its symbol and cannot be extended.

q-8400.text: In this situation, are you obliged each time to stop your vehicle before entering the intersection?
q-8400.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material orders an absolute stop before every entry to the intersection, regardless of whether other vehicles are approaching. The vehicle stops before the line, and where none is marked — before the edge of the cross roadway.

q-8401.text: In this situation, should you continue driving straight ahead through the intersection?
q-8401.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The lane markings and signals shown in the material permit going straight ahead, and the situation on the road does not require a stop. You drive across the junction smoothly, with special care and without stopping on it unnecessarily.

q-8402.text: Are you obliged in this situation, prior to turning right to stop before the transverse roadway?
q-8402.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop follows from the sign visible in the material and applies to every direction of further travel, including a right turn. Only after stopping before the cross roadway does the driver assess the situation and give way.

q-8403.text: Is it prohibited in this situation to enter the roadway beyond this vertical sign?
q-8403.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible vertical sign prohibits entry onto the roadway beyond it, so the driver may not enter there. The prohibition applies from the place where the sign is installed and concerns all vehicles, unless a plate introduces an exception.

q-8406.text: In this situation, does the vertical sign "stopping prohibited" apply also to a soft shoulder?
q-8406.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The no-stopping prohibition applies on the side of the road where the sign is installed and covers both the roadway and the shoulder — including an unpaved one. Pulling the wheels off the roadway therefore does not release you from this prohibition.

q-8414.text: In the presented situation, can you enter the narrowed section of the roadway?
q-8414.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material grant priority on the narrowed section to your direction of travel, so you may enter it without giving way to oncoming vehicles. Even so, you must make sure the driver coming the other way really is stopping.

q-8416.text: Are you allowed to drive a vehicle if the presence of alcohol in your breath exceeds 0.1 mg/dm³?
q-8416.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An alcohol content in exhaled air above 0.1 mg per dm³ means at least the state after alcohol consumption, and driving in that state is prohibited. The driver must be sober for the whole journey.

q-8417.text: Are you entitled to drive a vehicle if the blood alcohol concentration in your body exceeds 0.2 ‰?
q-8417.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A blood alcohol concentration above 0.2‰ means at least the state after alcohol consumption, in which driving is prohibited and punishable. Alcohol lengthens reaction time and impairs the judgement of speed and distance.

q-8418.text: Are you entitled to drive a vehicle after any drug available without a prescription?
q-8418.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Many over-the-counter medicines cause drowsiness, slowed reactions or visual disturbances, so you may not drive after every one of them. Before driving, read the leaflet, and in case of doubt ask a doctor or pharmacist.

q-8419.text: Is driving a vehicle under the influence of alcohol subject to violation?
q-8419.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Driving in the state after alcohol consumption is an offence punishable by, among other things, a fine and a driving ban. A higher alcohol concentration already means the state of intoxication and stricter criminal liability.

q-8424.text: After entering the road marked with these vertical signs, do you have the right to continue driving at a speed of 30 km/h?
q-8424.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material introduce a permitted speed lower than 30 km/h, so continuing at that speed would exceed the limit. The limit applies from the place where the sign is installed until it is cancelled.

q-8426.text: Is it allowed to reverse a vehicle in a place marked with this information sign?
q-8426.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The information sign visible in the material marks a section of road on which reversing is prohibited because of the speed and character of the traffic. This manoeuvre may be performed only outside the area marked in this way.

q-8428.text: Are you entering the motorway in the presented situation?
q-8428.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign visible in the material does not mark the beginning of a motorway, but of a road of a different category, where separate rules and speed limits apply. Only the proper information sign at the entry decides that a road is a motorway.

q-8435.text: While driving on this traffic lane, do you have the right to continue driving straight ahead?
q-8435.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings of the lane you are in do not permit going straight ahead — you must leave the intersection in the direction indicated by the arrows. The correct lane is chosen early enough, before reaching the intersection.

q-8439.text: You intend to make a U-turn at this intersection. Are you on the right traffic lane?
q-8439.explanation: Correct answer: NO. To turn around you must in good time take the lane closest to the centre of the roadway, i.e. the outer left lane intended for turning left. The lane you are in does not allow this manoeuvre, so you should change it before the intersection.

q-8440.text: Can you perform a U-turn manoeuvre at this intersection from the outermost right traffic lane?
q-8440.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around at an intersection is done from the outer left lane, from which a left turn is permitted. Starting the manoeuvre from the outer right lane would mean crossing the path of other vehicles and is not permitted.

q-8448.text: In this situation, seeing this horizontal sign in the form of triangles, are you obliged each time to stop before entering a road with priority?
q-8448.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A road marking in the form of triangles announces the duty to give way, not an absolute stop. If the road with priority is clear, you may enter without stopping; you must stop only when the traffic on that road requires it.

q-8455.text: Do you have the right to drive straight through the intersection from this traffic lane?
q-8455.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings of this lane permit travel only in the directions indicated by the arrows, and going straight ahead is not among them. To pass straight through the intersection, you must first change to the correct lane.

q-8464.text: In this situation, do vehicles coming from the opposite direction have the right of way at the narrowed section of the roadway?
q-8464.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material give priority on the narrowed section to your direction of travel, and the driver approaching from the opposite direction is obliged to give way. Priority does not, however, release you from watching whether the other side really is stopping.

q-8470.text: In the visible situation, do you have the right to change lanes and drive straight through the intersection?
q-8470.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The road markings at this place prohibit moving from lane to lane, so you must not change lanes in order to go straight ahead. The correct lane must be taken earlier, before such markings begin.

q-8471.text: In the visible situation, do you have the right to change lanes to the left while exercising extreme caution?
q-8471.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Changing to the left lane is prohibited at this place by the road markings, and exercising particular caution does not lift this prohibition. Caution is an additional duty of the driver, not permission for a manoeuvre the rules prohibit.

q-8472.text: In the visible situation, do you have the right to change lanes to the right?
q-8472.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The road markings at this place do not allow moving to the lane on the right. The manoeuvre may be performed only where the line separating the lanes allows it, after signalling the intention beforehand with the indicator.

q-8479.text: In this situation, are you warned that turning right beyond the sign you will run into a dead-end road?
q-8479.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material warns that the road branching off to the right has no through passage and is a dead end. Thanks to this you can choose another route in advance, because from such a road you will have to return by the same roadway.

q-8484.text: In this situation, are you on a road with the right of way?
q-8484.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material indicates that you are on the road with priority, and drivers entering from the cross roads are obliged to give way to you. Priority does not, however, release you from watching the intersection and being ready for another driver's mistake.

q-8497.text: In this situation, stopping the vehicle to yield the right of way should occur directly before the mandatory stop line?
q-8497.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Where an absolute stop line is marked, the vehicle stops directly before it and does not cross it with any part. Such positioning gives the best view of the road with priority before the decision to enter.

q-8498.text: Do the visible horizontal signs in the form of arrows on the roadway, impose driving solely in the indicated direction from the traffic lanes on which they are currently driving?
q-8498.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Direction arrows define the permitted directions of travel from the lane on which they are painted, and they are binding on the driver. The lane must therefore be chosen before the intersection, according to the intended direction of further travel.

q-8501.text: Does the visible horizontal sign separate traffic lanes designated for pedestrian traffic in the same direction?
q-8501.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible line separates adjacent lanes intended for vehicles travelling in the same direction, not opposite directions. Lines separating opposite directions of traffic look different and have a different meaning.

q-8504.text: You are on this lane. Are you only allowed to drive straight through the intersection?
q-8504.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The markings of this lane indicate only going straight ahead, so neither a left nor a right turn is permitted from it. A driver who wants to turn must first take the lane intended for the chosen direction.

q-8511.text: Are you obliged, on an internal road marked with the relevant road sign to adhere to the road signs presented here?
q-8511.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Signs installed on an internal road are binding just like signs on a public road, and the driver must comply with them. The internal character of the road itself does not exempt you from observing the signs or the traffic rules.

q-8515.text: In the situation presented, are you on a road with the right of way?
q-8515.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material grant priority to the road you are on, so vehicles from the cross roads must give way to you. Priority must, however, be confirmed by observation, because other drivers may disregard it.

q-8516.text: In this situation, are you approaching a place where cyclists may cross a transverse road?
q-8516.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material announces a cycle crossing, a place where cyclists cross the carriageway. Approaching it, you must take special care and be ready to give way.

q-8517.text: In this situation, are you approaching a crossing for cyclists and pedestrians?
q-8517.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing in the material indicates a pedestrian crossing and a cycle crossing next to each other. In such a place special care applies, overtaking is prohibited, and you must be ready to stop for a pedestrian or a cyclist.

q-8519.text: In the visible situation, are obliged to quickly return to the right side of the roadway?
q-8519.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Driving on the left part of the carriageway is permitted only for the time needed to carry out the manoeuvre, after which you must return to the right side as soon as possible. Staying on the left obstructs traffic and risks a head-on collision.

q-8521.text: In the visible situation, do the horizontal signs on the roadway allow you to change lanes to the left?
q-8521.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The line separating the lanes is broken at this point, and such a line may be crossed, so changing to the left lane is permitted. The manoeuvre is preceded by signalling with the indicator and making sure it will not obstruct others.

q-8522.text: Are merging into traffic behind this information signs?
q-8522.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Leaving an area marked with these signs onto an ordinary road is joining the traffic, so you must give way to all other road users. The manoeuvre also requires particular caution.

q-8524.text: Are you entitled to turn left at the intersection from this lane after the traffic lights turn green?
q-8524.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The markings of this lane permit a left turn, and the green signal permits entering the intersection. When turning, you must give way to vehicles going straight from the opposite direction and to pedestrians on the crossing you are crossing.

q-8528.text: When driving a motor vehicle, are you obliged to adhere to the orders and signals given at night outside a built-up area by the railway worker at the level crossing?
q-8528.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The instructions and signals of a person directing traffic, including a railway employee at a crossing, take precedence over signs and traffic lights. They apply at any time of day and in any place, at night outside a built-up area too.

q-8538.text: You intend to turn right in this situation. Are you obliged to stop before the intersection?
q-8538.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place there is no sign or signal ordering an absolute stop, so the right turn may be made without stopping the vehicle. Stopping becomes necessary only when you have to give way to other road users.

q-8555.text: In this situation, when entering the roadway of a public road are you obliged to observe the rules for merging into traffic?
q-8555.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Entering a public road from an internal road, a property or a similar place is joining the traffic. The driver must then exercise particular caution and give way to all other road users.

q-8559.text: Does a vehicle entering an intersection marked in such a way have priority over a vehicle moving around the central Island?
q-8559.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs at such an intersection give priority to vehicles already travelling around the central island, and the one entering must give way to them. Entry is possible only when it will not force those on the roundabout to brake or change their path.

q-8562.text: In this situation, do you have priority over the vehicle on the left side?
q-8562.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material put you on a subordinate road, so the vehicle on the left has priority and you must give way to it. The rule of priority for the vehicle on the right applies only at an intersection of equal roads.

q-8564.text: In the presented situation, should you yield priority to the vehicle on the right?
q-8564.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material grant priority to the road you are on, so the vehicle approaching from the right must give way to you. The right-hand rule applies only where no sign determines priority.

q-8565.text: In the presented situation, is it mandatory to stop before entering this intersection?
q-8565.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An absolute stop is required only by an appropriate sign or signal, and there is none at this place, so you may enter without stopping. Caution and careful observation of the cross roads still apply, however.

q-8573.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield priority to the vehicle on the right when turning left at the intersection?
q-8573.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You are on the road with priority indicated by the signs, so the vehicle approaching from the subordinate road on the right must give way to you. When turning left, however, you give way to vehicles going straight from the opposite direction.

q-8576.text: In this situation, are you approaching an uncontrolled intersection?
q-8576.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority at this intersection is determined by signs, so it is not an intersection of equal roads. An intersection is one of equal roads only when no sign or signal establishes the order of passage.

q-8579.text: When entering this intersection, do you have priority over the vehicle on the left?
q-8579.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs indicate that you are entering from a subordinate road, and the vehicle on the left is travelling on the road with priority. You must therefore give way to it regardless of the side from which it approaches.

q-8584.text: You intend to drive straight on through the intersection. Do you have priority over other traffic users in this situation?
q-8584.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material impose the duty to give way, so going straight ahead gives you no advantage over other road users. You may enter the intersection only after letting the vehicles on the road with priority pass.

q-8586.text: In the visible situation, do you have priority over the vehicle travelling on the transverse roadway?
q-8586.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The cross road has priority at this place, so the vehicle travelling on it goes first, and you must give way to it. Entering the intersection is permitted only when you will not force it to brake or change direction.

q-8587.text: When entering the visible roundabout, do you have priority in relations to traffic users who are already in the intersection?
q-8587.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a roundabout marked in this way, vehicles already travelling on the roundabout's roadway have priority. The one entering gives way to them and joins only when it will not obstruct their travel.

q-8588.text: You intend to drive straight on through this intersection. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to vehicles coming from the right?
q-8588.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs indicate that you are on the road with priority, so vehicles from the cross road on the right must give way to you. The duty to give way to vehicles from the right applies only at intersections where no sign determines priority.

q-8591.text: You intend to turn right at the visible intersection. Are you therefore obliged to yield the right of way to vehicles approaching from the left?
q-8591.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You are on the road with priority, so vehicles approaching from the left from the subordinate road must give way to you. The intention to turn right alone creates no duty to give way.

q-8592.text: When driving straight on through this intersection, do you have priority over the vehicle on the right?
q-8592.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs grant priority to the road you are on, so the vehicle from the cross road on the right is obliged to give way to you. Even so, before entering you must make sure it really is slowing down or standing.

q-8595.text: Should you exercise special caution when turning left at this intersection?
q-8595.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A left turn requires crossing the path of oncoming vehicles and passing over crossings, so particular caution applies. The manoeuvre must be signalled beforehand and performed from the correct lane.

q-8598.text: In the presented situation, do you have priority over the vehicle on the right?
q-8598.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material put you on the road with priority, and the vehicle on the right is coming out of a subordinate road. Priority should, however, be used carefully, watching whether the other driver intends to give way.

q-8614.text: Are you obliged to signal a left turn if you intend to continue driving on a road with priority?
q-8614.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this intersection the road with priority changes direction to the left, so staying on it is a change of direction and requires signalling with the indicator. The signal lets others read your intention, even though you have priority.

q-8620.text: Are entering a road with priority if you turn right at the intersection?
q-8620.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs at the intersection show that the road with priority branches off to the right, so after the turn you will be precisely on it. Before making the turn, however, you must give way to vehicles travelling on that road.

q-8627.text: You intend to drive straight on through the visible intersection. Are you in this situation obliged to yield the right of way to vehicles approaching form the left?
q-8627.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs put you on a subordinate road, so you must give way to vehicles travelling on the road with priority regardless of the side from which they approach. Entering the intersection is possible only after letting them pass.

q-8630.text: Are you allowed in the presented situation to make a U-turn at the intersection?
q-8630.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material rule out turning around at this intersection, so the manoeuvre must be performed at another, permitted place. You may turn around only where neither signs nor the rules prohibit it.

q-8631.text: Is it mandatory in the presented situation to stop before entering the intersection?
q-8631.explanation: Correct answer: NO. There is no sign or signal here ordering an absolute stop, so you may enter the intersection without stopping the vehicle. Giving way remains necessary if the traffic on the cross road requires it.

q-8633.text: In this situation, are you allowed to enter the intersection before the red signal lights turn on?
q-8633.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal visible in the material announces a change to red and prohibits passing the traffic light. You may continue only if stopping would require harsh braking; a vehicle that can stop safely must stop.

q-8638.text: In this situation, does the light signal emitted for your traffic direction allow you to enter beyond the traffic signal?
q-8638.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown for your direction prohibits passing the traffic light, so the vehicle must be stopped before the stop line, and where there is none — before the traffic light. You may set off only after the signal changes to a permitting one.

q-8646.text: Does this signal permit you to turn right without stopping?
q-8646.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible signal permits a right turn only conditionally: first you must stop before the traffic light, and then give way to vehicles and pedestrians. Turning without stopping is a violation of the rules, even when the road seems clear.

q-8648.text: In the situation presented, are you allowed to make a U-turn at this intersection?
q-8648.explanation: Correct answer: YES. No sign and no markings at this place prohibit turning around, so the manoeuvre is permitted. It is performed from the lane closest to the centre of the roadway, after signalling the intention and giving way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

q-8654.text: In this situation, do you have the right to drive behind the signalling device?
q-8654.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal visible in the material permits continuing, so passing the traffic light is allowed. Before moving off, however, you must make sure there is room beyond the intersection to leave it without stopping on it.

q-8660.text: In this situation, is it permissible to turn left and then make a U-turn at the intersection?
q-8660.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs at this intersection permit both a left turn and a U-turn from the lane intended for turning left. Both manoeuvres require giving way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians on the crossing being crossed.

q-8662.text: Are you obliged in this situation to wait for entry to the intersection?
