q-8662.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal and the situation at the intersection do not currently allow entry, so you must wait before it. You must also not enter when there is no room beyond the intersection and the vehicle would block the cross traffic.

q-8723.text: How can you improve visibility when approaching a turn with limited visibility on the right?

options.A: I'll go close to the axis of the roadway.
options.B: I'll go close to the right edge of the roardway
options.C: I'll travel in the middle of the traffic lane.

q-8723.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a right-hand bend with limited visibility the field of vision widens when the motorcyclist positions themselves closer to the centre line, that is, further from the inner edge of the curve. The line must, however, be corrected so as not to get close to the opposite lane.

q-8726.text: When riding a motorcycle, what effect do you obtain from engine braking?

options.A: slightly releasing the accelerator without using the clutch lever.
options.B: pushing the clutch lever and completely releasing the accelerator.

q-8726.explanation: Correct answer: A. Engine braking works only while the drive remains connected to the wheel, that is, with a gear engaged and the clutch lever released. Pulling in the clutch or neutral breaks that connection and the motorcycle rolls freely.

q-8735.text: You can ride a motorcycle in an organized column provided that it does not exceed:
q-8735.explanation: Correct answer: B. An organised column of motorcycles may number at most 10 vehicles. A larger group must be divided into smaller columns, keeping a distance between them that lets other drivers overtake and join the traffic safely.

q-8745.text: What must you check before engaging on a long-distance ride on a motorcycle?
q-8745.explanation: Correct answer: A. Tyre pressure decides the grip, stability and braking distance of a motorcycle, and with two wheels every error is felt immediately. The air filter and spark plugs are checked as part of periodic servicing, not before every longer trip.

q-8801.text: Are you allowed to carry a child over 150 cm in height in the front seat of a lorry cabin?

options.B: Yes, exclusively in a special car safety seat or other child restraint suitable for the mass and body weight that complies with additional technical requirements.
options.C: Yes, provided that the child sits on the laps of anothers adult.

q-8801.explanation: Correct answer: A. A child taller than 150 cm is carried like an adult passenger, that is, in a seat with the seat belt fastened, without a child seat. The duty to use a restraint concerns children shorter than 150 cm.

q-8812.text: In which of these places can you stop a lorry on the highway when you feel tired?
q-8812.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a motorway a rest is planned only in places intended for it, that is, at a service area. The hard shoulder and the exit slip road serve only for emergencies, and stopping on them risks being run into by another vehicle.

q-8813.text: You have been driving a lorry without a break from 6:00 am to 10:00 am. In how many minutes will you have to stop the vehicle, not to violate the laws in force in the European Union?
q-8813.explanation: Correct answer: B. Uninterrupted driving may last at most four and a half hours, and four hours have passed since 6.00. So 30 minutes remain before the permitted driving time is used up, after which a break must be taken.

q-8817.text: Which commercial road transport vehicle should be fitted with a tachograph?

options.A: Vehicle of gross weight rating 3450 kg
options.B: Vehicle of gross weight rating 2800 kg
options.C: Vehicle of gross weight rating 2800 kg, pulling a trailer of gross weight 750kg.

q-8817.explanation: Correct answer: C. Whether a tachograph must be used is decided by the sum of the maximum permissible masses of the vehicle and the trailer: 2,800 kg and 750 kg give 3,550 kg, that is, more than 3.5 t. The vehicles of 3,450 kg and 2,800 kg alone do not exceed that threshold.

q-8852.text: In which of these places can you stop the bus when you feel tired, while driving on the highway?
q-8852.explanation: Correct answer: B. A bus stops for a rest only at a service area, adapted for parked vehicles and the presence of passengers. The hard shoulder and the exit slip road are reserved for emergencies, and stopping on them risks being run into.

q-8857.text: How do you effectively stop a vehicle with an ABS?

options.B: By pressing the brake pedal all the way.
options.C: Not pressing the brake pedal all the way.

q-8857.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a vehicle with ABS you brake with firm, continuous pressure on the brake pedal — the system itself prevents the wheels from locking and keeps the vehicle steerable. Pumping the brake is used in vehicles without ABS.

q-8864.text: How should you behave upon missing an exit on a road with heightened traffic?

options.A: Stop the the vehicle at the next traffic lights to ask pedestrians for further direction.
options.B: Check on a road map for the way back while still driving.
options.C: Drive further to a place where you can safely stop the vehicle.

q-8864.explanation: Correct answer: C. A missed exit is no reason to stop in traffic, reverse or deal with a map while driving. Calmly drive on and only in a place where stopping is allowed and safe plan the way back.

q-8866.text: How should you behave when forced to continue driving behind a driving lesson vehicle, without the possibility of overtaking?

options.A: Maintain an appropriate distance, bearing in mind what kins of mistakes the driver might make.
options.B: Use the sound signal to draw the attention of the driver.
options.C: Switch-on the emrgency lights at an appropriate distance from the driver.

q-8866.explanation: Correct answer: A. The driver of a learner vehicle is still practising, so they may slow down sharply, stall the engine or move off late. An increased distance gives time to react, while the horn and hazard lights will only put them off.

q-8867.text: You are travelling on a road at the maximum permitted speed, and in spite of that you see a vehicle approaching from behind and blinking the lights. What do you do in this situation?

options.A: Shortly press the brake pedal to show the brake lights.
options.B: Increase speed to keep a distance between the vehicles.
options.C: I'll drive to the edge of the road to allow for an ovetaking manoeuvre.

q-8867.explanation: Correct answer: C. The driver may not hinder overtaking or punish another driver by braking, nor may they exceed the permitted speed. The right thing is to move closer to the right edge of the carriageway and allow safe overtaking.

q-8868.text: What do you do if another vehicle suddenly appears in front of you at an intersection, forcing the right of way?

options.A: Avoid it with a zig zag manoeuvre and tirn on the sound signal.
options.B: Bilnk the lights and drive close to the vehicle.
options.C: Limit the speed and prepare for sudden braking.

q-8868.explanation: Correct answer: C. When someone forces priority, what counts is avoiding a collision, not asserting your rights. Reducing speed and being ready to stop is the only safe solution; zigzagging around or getting close to the offender increases the risk.

q-8870.text: In what way can you reduce air pollution during a stop at the bus station?

options.A: I'll keep the engine revolution low.
options.B: I'll keep the engine revolution high.

q-8870.explanation: Correct answer: C. At a bus station an engine running while stationary emits exhaust and noise to no purpose. The most effective way of limiting pollution is to switch it off while waiting; the level of revs is irrelevant here.

q-8876.text: You are driving a passenger car on dual carriage expressway. At what speed are permitted drive?
q-8876.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a dual-carriageway expressway a car may travel at no more than 120 km/h. On a single-carriageway expressway a lower limit applies, and 130 km/h concerns motorways only.

q-8891.text: You are driving a passenger vehicle with a trailer on the highway. What speed must you not exceed?
q-8891.explanation: Correct answer: A. A combination consisting of a car and a trailer may not exceed 80 km/h on a motorway. The higher motorway limits apply to vehicles without a trailer. A trailer changes the handling, and the limit applies regardless of its mass.

q-8898.text: At what permissible speed are you allowed to travel when driving a passenger car pulling a light trailer on the highway?
q-8898.explanation: Correct answer: A. A light trailer does not change the limit either: a combination with a car may travel on a motorway at no more than 80 km/h. The trailer's lower mass does not entitle you to drive faster.

q-8935.text: Which of these damages to the safety belts indicates an absolute need to replace the belt with a new one?

options.A: Twisting or curling of the seat belts.
options.B: Abrasion, tear and narrowing of the seat belts.
options.C: Persistent dirt and stains on the belts.

q-8935.explanation: Correct answer: B. Abrasion, narrowing and tears in the webbing reduce its strength, so the belt may snap under load in a collision. Such a belt must be replaced with a new one; a twisted belt or stains are not in themselves a reason for replacement.

q-8939.text: Which of the mentioned body parts is the headrest on the vehicle seat designed to protect?
q-8939.explanation: Correct answer: A. The head restraint protects the cervical spine by limiting the violent backward movement of the head in an impact, especially from behind. It works effectively only when its upper edge reaches roughly the top of the head and sits close to it.

q-8957.text: Which of these factors has a direct influence on the braking distance?
q-8957.explanation: Correct answer: A. The braking distance depends directly on speed and grows much faster than proportionally — twice the speed means roughly four times the distance. Signing and visibility affect the driver's decisions, but not the physics of braking itself.

q-8961.text: Which of these factors has a direct influence on the braking distance?
q-8961.explanation: Correct answer: B. Worn pads, air in the system or uneven braking lengthen the braking distance, because the vehicle sheds speed more slowly. Road markings and signs inform the driver, but in themselves neither shorten nor lengthen that distance.

q-8972.text: What factors have an influence on the total perception and reaction time of a vehicle driver?

options.B: Visibility on the road, the complexity of the traffic situation.

q-8972.explanation: Correct answer: B. Perception and reaction time depends on how quickly the driver notices the hazard and makes a decision, and it is worsened by poor visibility and a complex traffic situation. The state of the tyres and the mass of the vehicle only affect the braking itself.

q-8979.text: What distance should you maintain when overtaking a cyclist or a moped?
q-8979.explanation: Correct answer: A. When overtaking a cyclist or a moped rider, the driver must keep a distance of no less than 1 m. The same distance applies to an electric scooter and a pedestrian walking on the verge, because a two-wheeler may wobble on a bump.

q-8986.text: What distance from the preceding vehicle should you maintain standing before an interection, waiting for the green signal?

options.C: Maximum of 3 m, minimum of 1 m

q-8986.explanation: Correct answer: B. The rules give no figure in metres here — a safe distance is required, that is, one that allows you to drive round the vehicle ahead if it does not move off, and protects you from hitting it if you are run into from behind.

q-8988.text: What distance from the preceding vehicle should you maintain standing before an interection, waiting for the green signal?

options.B: Maximum of 10 m, minimum of 1 m.

q-8988.explanation: Correct answer: C. The rules set no distance in metres here — a safe distance applies. It should allow you to drive round the vehicle ahead if it does not move off, and reduce the consequences of being run into from behind.

q-8991.text: What distance must you maintain from the obsatcle you are driving past?
q-8991.explanation: Correct answer: B. When passing an obstacle, the rules require a safe distance, without giving a specific value in metres. The distance is chosen according to speed and the type of obstacle: the higher the speed and the more unpredictable the obstacle, the greater the distance must be.

q-8992.text: What distance must you maintain when driving past?
q-8992.explanation: Correct answer: C. When passing an oncoming vehicle, a safe distance is required, not a predetermined number of metres. It depends on the speed of both vehicles, their width and the state and width of the carriageway.

q-8993.text: Which of the these elements of equipments or vehicle construction has a significant effect on safety during braking?
q-8993.explanation: Correct answer: C. The ABS system does not let the wheels lock under hard braking, so the vehicle stays steerable and you can steer round an obstacle. Cruise control only holds a set speed and does not help with braking.

q-8995.text: How does the braking distance of the vehicle change dependent on the speed increase?

options.A: The braking distance increases with an increase in speed.
options.B: The braking distance is decreses with an increase in speed.
options.C: The driving speed has no influence on the braking distance.

q-8995.explanation: Correct answer: A. The braking distance grows with speed, and much faster than the speed itself — at twice the speed it is roughly four times longer. That is why even a small excess of speed decides whether the vehicle manages to stop.

q-8998.text: What factors and circumstances should be taken into account when choosing a safe speed for the prevailing road conditions?

options.B: Type of surface and the prevailing road conditions.
options.C: Only the driving speed of other traffic users.

q-8998.explanation: Correct answer: B. A safe speed is not just the number on the sign — it is chosen according to the type and state of the surface, visibility, weather and traffic. It must allow you to stop the vehicle before an obstacle that can be seen.

q-9012.text: Which of these factors dependent on the vehicle driver has a significant influence on the driver's vision?

options.B: Condition of the road surface, time of day or night.
options.C: Attention span, current well-being and health.

q-9012.explanation: Correct answer: C. Of those listed, only concentration, how you feel and your state of health depend on the driver themselves and directly impair visual acuity — tiredness, illness or medicines weaken eyesight. Air temperature and the time of day are beyond the driver's control.

q-9035.text: What influence does driving speed have on the vehicle driver's field of vision?

options.A: As speed increases, the field of view narrows
options.B: As speed increases, the field of view expand
options.C: Driving speed has no influence on the driver's field of vision

q-9035.explanation: Correct answer: A. The faster the vehicle travels, the more the eyes concentrate on a point far ahead and the field of vision narrows to a thin cone. The driver then stops noticing what is happening at the side of the road.

q-9058.text: Using the vehicle in a a manner that causes discomfort associated with excessive emissions to the environment or excessive noise is:
q-9058.explanation: Correct answer: B. The ban on using a vehicle in a way that is a nuisance through excessive exhaust fumes or noise applies everywhere, not only in a built-up area or a residential zone. It covers, among other things, an engine running unnecessarily while parked and a damaged exhaust system.

q-9065.text: In which of these dangerous circumstances on the road does a vehicle equipped with the so-called ASR i.e. anti-skid system for a running vehicle come in handy?

options.A: In the case of downhill driving.
options.B: In the case of downhill driving on a road with heavy traffic.
options.C: In the case of sudden acceleration on a wet surface.

q-9065.explanation: Correct answer: C. The ASR system works during acceleration: it detects spin of the driven wheels and limits drive torque, and a wet surface favours loss of grip. When descending a hill, slowing down is the job of the brakes and other systems.

q-9067.text: In which of these dangerous situations does a vehicle equipped with the so-called ASR, i.e. Acceleration slip regulation system designed to prevent loss of traction of driven road wheels perform well?

options.A: In the case of downhill drive on a road with heavy traffic.
options.B: In a situation where it is necessary to drive uphill
options.C: In the case of sudden starts on slippery surfaces.

q-9067.explanation: Correct answer: C. ASR is most useful when moving off sharply on a slippery surface, because the driven wheels then spin easily and the rear of the vehicle can swing out. The system then limits the drive and lets you move off smoothly.

q-9068.text: In which of these dangerous situations on the road does a car equipped with the so-called ESP, i.e. the electronic stability program perform well?

options.A: In the case of overcoming a sharp turn and difficulties in maintaining the desired trajectory.
options.B: In the case of a necessity for sudden acceleration on a dirt road.
options.C: In the case of the need to maintain a constant speed.

q-9068.explanation: Correct answer: A. ESP compares the path set by the steering wheel with the vehicle's actual movement and brakes individual wheels when the car begins to run wide in a bend or to skid. It is precisely in a sharp bend that this correction is most needed.

q-9070.text: In which of these dangerous situations on the road does a car equipped with the so-called ESP, i.e. the electronic stability program perform well?

options.A: In the case of a necessity to maintain a constant speed.
options.B: In the case of a need to drive up a hill.
options.C: In the case of a necessity to overcome several consecutive turns.

q-9070.explanation: Correct answer: C. Through several bends in succession the body leans first one way and then the other, and the rear easily swings out. ESP then corrects the vehicle's path by braking selected wheels; at a steady speed there is nothing to stabilise.

q-9087.text: What should you do upon determining improper engine oil pressure?

options.B: Check the oil level and eventaully replenish.
options.C: Always turn on the hazard warning lights.

q-9087.explanation: Correct answer: B. First check the oil level with the dipstick and, if necessary, top up with oil of the specification recommended by the manufacturer — just any oil may worsen lubrication. Hazard lights are switched on only when the stopped vehicle endangers others.

q-9089.text: Which of the control lights in the illustration informs you that the dipped headlights are turned on?
q-9089.explanation: Correct answer: C. Dipped headlights are signalled by a green light with a headlamp symbol whose beam points diagonally downwards — that light is marked C in the material. A horizontal beam would mean main-beam headlights.

q-9090.text: Which the control lights visible in the illustration informs you that the direction indicators are enabled?
q-9090.explanation: Correct answer: A. An indicator in use is shown by a green flashing arrow pointing left or right — in the material that is light A. Both arrows flashing at once would mean the hazard lights.

q-9092.text: Which of the control lights visible in the illustration informs you that the running lights are enabled?
q-9092.explanation: Correct answer: C. Position lights are signalled by a green light with a symbol of two lamps sending rays out to the sides — in the material it is marked C. Position lights alone are not enough for driving after dusk.

q-9093.text: Which of the control lights visible in the illustration applies to the front fog lights?
q-9093.explanation: Correct answer: B. Front fog lights have a green light with a lamp symbol whose straight rays are crossed by a wavy line — in the material that is light B. They may be used only in fog or precipitation, or dense fog limiting visibility.

q-9094.text: which of the control lights visible in the illustration informs you that direction indicators are enabled?
q-9094.explanation: Correct answer: A. An indicator in use is shown by a green flashing arrow pointing left or right — in the material that is light A. Both arrows flashing at once would mean the hazard lights.

q-9095.text: Which of the control lights visible in the illustration informs you that the rear fog lights are enabled?
q-9095.explanation: Correct answer: A. Rear fog lights have an orange light with a lamp whose rays point backwards and are crossed by a wavy line — in the material that is light A. Once visibility improves they must be switched off, because they dazzle drivers behind.

q-9096.text: Which of the control lights visible in the illustration informs you that the main beam lights are enabled?
q-9096.explanation: Correct answer: B. Main-beam headlights are signalled by a blue light with a headlamp and a horizontal, straight beam of rays — in the material that is light B. The blue colour is a reminder that they must be switched off for other road users.

q-9102.text: Which of the control lights visible in the illustration indicates that the safety seat belts are not fastened?
q-9102.explanation: Correct answer: B. Unfastened seat belts are signalled by a red light with the silhouette of a seated person with a belt across them, often together with a sound — in the material that is light B. It goes out only once the belts are fastened.

q-9105.text: Which of the control lights visible in the illustration upon lighting up, requires you to stop immediately and rectify the fault?
q-9105.explanation: Correct answer: B. A red warning light means a fault that threatens safety or risks destroying the engine, so when it comes on you should stop the vehicle safely and remove the cause. In the material such a light is B; lights in other colours usually only inform.

q-9110.text: Which of the control lights visible in the illustration informs you that the rear windscreen heater is enabled?
q-9110.explanation: Correct answer: B. Rear-window heating is signalled by a light with a rectangle of the window and wavy arrows pointing upwards — in the material that is light B. It is a comfort function, not a fault warning; once the window has demisted it is worth switching off.

q-9132.text: In the situation presented, are you warned of the transverse unevenness of the road surface caused by potholes?
q-9132.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The warning of transverse unevenness of the carriageway caused by surface damage has its own sign, and the sign shown in the material concerns a different hazard. The meaning of a sign is read from its symbol, not guessed from the state of the road.

q-9133.text: In the situation presented, does the visible sign warn you of two dangerous bends, the first of which is to the direction indicated on the sign, and the second of which may be to the left or to the right?
q-9133.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The description in the question matches the sign warning of several dangerous bends, while the material shows a sign with a different meaning. The sign for two bends has a symbol with two successive curves.

q-9138.text: In the situation presented, does the visible sign warn you of frequent snowfall over a distance of 2 kilometres?
q-9138.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Warning signs do not inform about the frequency of snowfall — the visible sign warns of a different danger. A plate with the length of the section may appear under the sign, but it does not change the meaning of the symbol itself.

q-9141.text: In the situation presented, does the visible sign warn you of a dangerous bend to the right?
q-9141.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a bend to the right where keeping your line may be harder than on an ordinary curve. Speed must be reduced before entering the bend, not during it; caution when overtaking also applies.

q-9142.text: In the situation presented, does the visible sign warn you of driving through tram tracks?
q-9142.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a place where the road crosses tram tracks. You should approach with caution, allow for the tram's longer braking distance and not enter the tracks unless you can leave them immediately.

q-9144.text: In the situation presented, does the visible sign warn you of the possibility of encountering frost or black ice on the road?
q-9144.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a section where frost or black ice may occur on the roadway, i.e. extremely low grip. Speed should be reduced and braking and steering done gently; the warning applies even when the surface looks dry.

q-9145.text: Does the visible sign warn you of the possibility of encountering wild animals on the road?
q-9145.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a section where wild animals often cross the road. You must reduce speed and watch the verges, especially at dawn and dusk; one animal is usually followed by others.

q-9149.text: Does the sign in the situation presented, warn you of a narrowing on both sides of the road, which may pose an obstruction traffic?
q-9149.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a narrowing of the roadway on both sides, where there may not be enough room to pass freely. You should reduce speed and be ready to give room to a vehicle coming from the opposite direction.

q-9152.text: Does the sign visible in the situation presented, warn you of the possibility of encountering wild animals on the road?
q-9152.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign informs of a section of road where you may encounter wild animals coming out of the forest or fields. It requires reducing speed and watching the road surroundings, because an animal appears suddenly and often not alone.

q-9153.text: Does the visible sign in the situation presented, warn you of the possibility of encountering frost or black ice on the road?
q-9153.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign informs of possible frost or black ice on the roadway, i.e. a sudden loss of grip. Bridges, viaducts and shaded sections are particularly exposed, so speed must be reduced and manoeuvres performed smoothly.

q-9154.text: Does the visible sign in the situation presented, warn drivers travelling on a one-way road of approaching a point where a two-way road begins?
q-9154.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns drivers on a one-way roadway that from the indicated point traffic in the opposite direction will appear. You must return to the right side of the roadway and allow for oncoming vehicles.

q-9191.text: In the presented situation, are you taking the proper traffic lane if you intend to turn left at the nearest intersection?
q-9191.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before turning left the driver takes in good time the lane closest to the centre of the roadway or the lane indicated by direction arrows. The lane you are in permits a left turn, so a lane change is not needed.

q-9200.text: You intend to drive straight on at the nearest intersection in the presented situation. Are you taking the proper traffic lane?
q-9200.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The lane you are in is intended for going straight ahead, as follows from the direction arrows and the markings visible in the material. The lane is chosen in advance, before reaching the intersection, not just before the entry itself.

q-9203.text: In the presented situation, intending to turn right into a residential area do you have to signal this manoeuvre?
q-9203.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every change of direction is signalled with the indicator early enough, also when turning off the road into a residential zone. Signalling ends directly after the manoeuvre is completed.

q-9223.text: Are you permitted in the situation presented, to begin overtaking the vehicle travelling in the right lane?
q-9223.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On this section no overtaking ban or other restriction that would rule out this manoeuvre applies. Before moving into the left lane you must check the mirrors and the blind spot and signal the lane change.

q-9225.text: Is it allowed to overtake in the presented situation?
q-9225.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Neither a sign, nor road markings, nor the place where you are exclude overtaking here. The driver must, however, judge for themselves whether they have enough visibility and room to return to their lane without obstructing traffic.

q-9234.text: Is it prohibited to reverse on a two-way road?
q-9234.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Reversing is not prohibited as such; it is prohibited in the places specified in the rules, among others in a tunnel, on a bridge and a viaduct, on a motorway and an expressway, and at an intersection. Elsewhere you may reverse, exercising particular caution and giving way to others.

q-9254.text: When passing by a vehicle in the presented situation, are you obliged to exercise special caution and anticipate that someone from the bus may run into the roadway?
q-9254.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A stationary bus blocks the view, and alighting passengers often cross the roadway right in front of or behind it. When passing it, you must reduce speed and be ready to stop immediately.

q-9255.text: Are you allowed in this situation to use the sound signal to urge on stationary vehicles?
q-9255.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn may be used only when necessary to warn of danger, and in a built-up area its use is otherwise prohibited. Hurrying other drivers along is not a warning of danger.

q-9261.text: Are you allowed in this situation to use the sound signal to urge on the cyclist?
q-9261.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn serves solely to warn of danger, not to hurry other road users along. A cyclist startled by the noise may veer off their line or fall, so such behaviour creates a hazard.

q-9306.text: Is it necessary to exercise special caution in the presented situation?
q-9306.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material is one in which the regulations require particular caution. This means raising your attention, adapting your behaviour to the changing conditions and being ready to react immediately.

q-9310.text: Are you required in the presented situation to exercise special caution beyond the visible warning sign?
q-9310.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A warning sign announces a danger beyond it and obliges the driver to raise their attention and adjust their speed to the expected conditions. The duty lasts for the whole section the sign refers to.

q-9330.text: In the situation presented, does the green signal exempt you from the necessity to exercise special caution at a pedestrian crossing?
q-9330.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A green signal permits entry, but does not lift your duties towards pedestrians. You must allow people already on the crossing to finish crossing, and expect pedestrians stepping out despite the red light.

q-9347.text: Must you always stop when approaching a road designated to bicycles?
q-9347.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When driving across a cycle path, the driver must give way to cyclists, but stopping is necessary only when it cannot be done otherwise. When nobody is approaching, you may drive across, taking special care.

q-9352.text: Is it prohibited to overtake cyclists at all intersections?
q-9352.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The ban on overtaking at a junction is not absolute — among other cases, it does not apply at a roundabout or at a junction where you are travelling on the road with priority. You must always keep a distance of at least 1 m and judge whether the manoeuvre is safe.

q-9360.text: In the presented situation, do you see the end of a traffic lane for cyclists?
q-9360.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing shown in the material indicates the end of the lane reserved for cyclists. At such a place cyclists merge into the traffic on the remaining lanes, so you must watch for them in advance and let them safely take their place on the carriageway.

q-9362.text: Does the visible sign warn you of approaching a crossing that runs through tram tracks?
q-9362.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces a place where the road crosses tram tracks. You must reduce speed, make sure no tram is approaching, and remember that a tram has a longer braking distance and cannot steer around an obstacle.

q-9365.text: In the presented situation, are you allowed to pull over by the kerb before the sign?
q-9365.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping in this place is prohibited, which follows from the sign and the situation visible in the material. You may stop the vehicle only where no prohibition applies and where the stationary vehicle endangers no one and does not obstruct traffic.

q-9366.text: In the presented situation, are you permitted to stop on the pavement before the sign?
q-9366.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The pavement is intended for pedestrians, and a vehicle may be stopped on it only where a sign or a rule allows it, subject to additional conditions. Here the prohibition also covers the pavement, so stopping is not allowed.

q-9371.text: In the presented situation, are you allowed to drive straight through the intersection?
q-9371.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign or the lane markings visible in the material order travel in a direction other than straight ahead, and the driver must follow the direction indicated for their lane. Going straight ahead at this place would be a breach of the rules.

q-9372.text: In the presented situation, are you allowed beyond the visible sign to stop with the wheels of one side on the pavement?
q-9372.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition arising from the sign covers the whole side of the road on which the sign stands, including the shoulder and the pavement. Putting the wheels of one side onto the pavement changes nothing — the vehicle is still standing in a place covered by the prohibition.

q-9375.text: In the presented situation, are you allowed to stop the vehicle with the wheels of one of the sides on the bicycle lane?
q-9375.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A cycle path is intended solely for bicycle traffic, and a vehicle may not be stopped on it, not even partly. A vehicle standing with even the wheels of one side on it forces cyclists onto the carriageway.

q-9376.text: Does the visible sign presented in this situation indicate a traffic prohibition for vehicles, which their height (including load) exceeds 3.1 metres?
q-9376.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign prohibits the movement of vehicles whose height together with the load exceeds the value given on the sign, i.e. 3.1 m. The driver must know the actual height of the vehicle with its load, because it decides whether passage is possible.

q-9377.text: Does the prohibition sign placed under the built-up area sign indicate that the prohibition applies to the entire built-up area with the exception of the section of the road on which it has been replaced or cancelled?
q-9377.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A prohibition sign placed under the sign marking the start of a built-up area applies zonally — on all roads in that area. Only another sign installed on a specific section of road can change or cancel it.

q-9379.text: In the presented situation, does the stop prohibition apply also to the pavement?
q-9379.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The no-stopping prohibition covers the side of the road on which the sign is placed, that is the carriageway together with the verge and the pavement. Driving onto the pavement therefore does not get around the prohibition.

q-9382.text: You are driving a vehicle in a built-up area. Does the visible prohibition sign apply to passenger cars?
q-9382.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible prohibition sign applies to all vehicles, and therefore also to passenger cars. Excluding any group of vehicles would have to follow from a symbol on the sign or from a plate placed under it.

q-9383.text: You are driving a vehicle in a built-up area. Does the visible prohibition sign apply to motorcycles?
q-9383.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The prohibition sign visible in the material covers motorcycles, because the prohibition applies to all vehicles that have not been excluded by a symbol or a plate under the sign. A motorcyclist must comply with it just like a car driver.

q-9391.text: Are you merging into traffic when exiting a public road into a car park??
q-9391.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Joining the traffic is entering a road from a place that is not a road — a car park, a property or an unpaved road. Turning off the road into a car park is the reverse manoeuvre, so it is not joining the traffic; you must, however, signal the intention and give way to pedestrians.

q-9424.text: In the presented situation, do you have to exercise special caution when entering a paved road from a dirt road?
q-9424.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Entering a paved road from an unpaved road is joining the traffic, and that requires particular caution and giving way to all road users on the paved road. The manoeuvre may be started only when it forces no one to brake.

q-9425.text: In the presented situation, are you approaching an the intersection where you must yield the right of way to vehicles coming from the right?
q-9425.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The right-hand rule applies only at an intersection of equal roads. Here priority is decided by the signs visible in the material — you are on the road with priority, so it is the driver from the cross road who is obliged to give way.

q-9426.text: In the presented situation, are you approaching an uncontrolled intersection?
q-9426.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An intersection is one of equal roads only when priority is determined neither by signs nor by traffic lights. In the material priority is set by signs, so the roads have different rank and the right-hand rule does not apply here.

q-9427.text: In this situation, does the vehicle coming from the right have the right of way at the nearest intersection?
q-9427.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The vehicle approaching from the right is entering from a subordinate road, so it is the one that gives way. The right-hand rule works only where priority is not decided by signs or signals — here it is decided by the signs.

q-9430.text: You intend to turn right at the nearest intersection in the situation presented. Do you have to yield the right of way to cyclists from the opposite direction turning left?
q-9430.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning right, you do not give way to traffic coming from the opposite direction. It is the driver turning left, a cyclist included, who must give way to oncoming vehicles going straight ahead and turning right.

q-9431.text: You intend to turn left at the nearest intersection in the situation presented here. Do you have to yield the right of way to the vehicle coming from the right?
q-9431.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority at this intersection is decided by the signs, not by the right-hand rule, so the driver from the cross road gives way to you. When turning left, however, you must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

q-9434.text: In the presented situation, are you exiting a road with priority if you turn left behind the visible sign?
q-9434.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Which way the road with priority runs is decided by the signs visible in the material; here it leads to the left, so by turning left you are still travelling on it. It is the driver who chooses a different direction who leaves the road with priority.

q-9443.text: Does the "Stop" sign visible in the presented situation indicate the mandatory place to stop the vehicle before entering the intersection?
q-9443.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The "Stop" sign imposes the duty to stop, but does not itself designate the point at which the stop is to be made. You stop before the absolute stop line, and where there is none — before the edge of the cross roadway, so as to see the road.

q-9446.text: You intend to drive straight on in the presented situation. Are you obliged to stop before entering the intersection?
q-9446.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping before an intersection is mandatory only when ordered by a "Stop" sign, a red signal, the instruction of a person directing traffic, or the situation on the road. Here there is no such order — it is enough to remain cautious and give way if necessary.

q-9447.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have priority over the pedestrian in the presented situation?
q-9447.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver turning at a junction must give way to a pedestrian crossing the carriageway of the road they are entering. This duty exists even where no pedestrian crossing is marked there.

q-9448.text: Are you obliged in the presented situation to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-9448.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority at this intersection is determined by signs, so the right-hand rule does not apply. You are on the road with priority, and the driver approaching from the right is entering from a subordinate road, so it is they who must give way.

q-9454.text: In the presented situation, does the visible sign "Yield way" apply only to the nearest intersection?
q-9454.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The "Give way" sign refers to the intersection before which it is installed. At the following intersections priority is determined anew — according to the signs there, the traffic lights or the right-hand rule.

q-9455.text: You intend to turn left at the nearest intersection in the presented situation. Do you have to yield priority to cyclists coming straight from the opposite direction?
q-9455.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Turning left, you give way to everyone coming from the opposite direction and going straight ahead, and a bicycle is a vehicle. A cyclist is easy to overlook, so before turning you must deliberately look for one.

q-9466.text: You intend to turn right in the presented situation. Do you have to stop at the designated place before entering the intersection?
q-9466.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop follows from the sign or signal visible in the material and applies to every direction of travel, including a right turn. The vehicle must come to a complete stop at the designated place, even if the road seems clear.

q-9467.text: In the presented situation, when driving further straight through the next intersection do you have priority over vehicles approaching from the right?
q-9467.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You are on the road with priority, as follows from the signs visible in the material, so the driver approaching from the right must give way to you. The right-hand rule applies only where priority is not decided by signs or signals.

q-9489.text: How should you secure a conscious victim who has suffered a head injury as a consequence of an accident?

options.A: Place the victim lying on a flat surface and apply a sterile gauze dressing on the wound.
options.B: Place the victim in a half-sitting position, apply a sterile gauze dressing on the wound and calm the victim down.
options.C: Place the victim in a side lying position (safe position), without applying any dressing.

q-9489.explanation: Correct answer: B. A conscious casualty with a bleeding head wound is placed in a half-sitting position, which reduces the bleeding, a sterile dressing is put on the wound and they are reassured. The recovery position is intended for an unconscious person who is breathing.

q-9496.text: When turning left in this situation, are you obliged to yield priority to the vehicle coming from the opposite direction?
q-9496.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When turning left, the driver gives way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction that are going straight ahead or turning right. The manoeuvre may be performed only when it will not force anyone to change direction or speed.

q-9514.text: Can you stop the vehicle on the hard shoulder in the presented situation?
q-9514.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place stopping is prohibited, and the prohibition covers the whole road, not only the roadway — the shoulder too. Pulling onto the shoulder therefore does not release you from the prohibition; you may stop the vehicle only where it is permitted.

q-9541.text: In this situation, the minimum distance you should keep from the cyclist when overtaking is 1 m?
q-9541.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When overtaking a cyclist, the driver must keep a safe distance of no less than 1 m. The same distance applies when overtaking a moped, a motorcycle and a pedestrian, and at higher speed the distance should be correspondingly greater.

q-9549.text: When approaching a level crossing in this situation, are you obliged to stop the vehicle before the STOP sign?
q-9549.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An absolute stop before a railway crossing is required only when a "Stop" sign stands there, when a red signal is displayed, or when the barriers are being lowered or are lowered. Here there is no such requirement, but you must exercise particular caution.

q-9554.text: Turning right in the presented situation, are you obliged to yield priority to pedestrians?
q-9554.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning right must give way to a pedestrian crossing the carriageway of the road they are entering. The turn may be completed only once the pedestrian will not be forced to stop or speed up.

q-9555.text: In the presented situation, are you obliged to yield way to the vehicle coming from the right?
q-9555.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The right-hand rule works only at an intersection of equal roads. Here priority is decided by the signs: you are on the road with priority, and the vehicle on the right is entering from a subordinate road, so it is the one that gives way.

q-9556.text: In the presented situation, do you have priority over the vehicle coming from the right?
q-9556.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority follows from the signs visible in the material — the road you are on is the road with priority, and the driver on the right is obliged to give way. Even so, watch them and be ready to react if they do not stop.

q-9560.text: In the presented situation, can you overtake the cyclist if it will require slightly crossing the solid line?
q-9560.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A double solid line must not be crossed or driven on, even when overtaking a cyclist. If the required distance cannot be kept without breaching the line, you must follow the cyclist to a place where the manoeuvre will be permitted.

q-9564.text: In the presented situation, can you stop the vehicle on the shoulder beyond the sign?
q-9564.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The prohibition in force on this section ends where the sign is placed, so beyond it you may stop the vehicle on the shoulder. You must, however, stop so as not to obstruct other traffic and leave others enough room.

q-9565.text: In the presented situation, can you stop the vehicle on the shoulder before the sign?
q-9565.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Before the sign the prohibition still applies, and it covers the whole road at this place — not only the roadway but also the shoulder. You may stop only where the prohibition ends.

q-9601.text: You intend to turn right. Will you in the presented situation stop at the traffic signals?
q-9601.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A red signal prohibits passing the traffic light even when you intend to turn right. If an additional green arrow is lit, the turn is permitted only after stopping the vehicle and giving way to other road users.

q-9603.text: Is it allowed in this situation to turn left?
q-9603.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A left turn is prohibited at this place, as follows from the signs visible in the material. You must go in the permitted direction and change direction only where the manoeuvre is not prohibited.

q-9614.text: Is it permitted in the presented situation to overtake the vehicle visible?
q-9614.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this place no sign or road markings prohibit overtaking, and the conditions allow the manoeuvre to be performed safely. Before starting it, you must make sure the lane is clear for a sufficient length and that the return will take place without forcing others to brake.

q-9633.text: In the presented situation, is it allowed to make a U-turn?
q-9633.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning around is prohibited at this place, as follows from the signs visible in the material. The manoeuvre may be performed only where the prohibition ceases to apply and where it will not force other drivers to change speed or direction.

q-9634.text: Does the visible prohibition sign apply only to the nearest intersection inclusive?
q-9634.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A prohibition sign applies up to and including the nearest intersection, unless it is cancelled earlier by a cancelling sign or a plate defining a different range. Beyond the intersection the prohibition must be repeated for it to remain in force.

q-9640.text: Can the person performing roadworks on a road on behalf of or with the consent of the road administration give commands or signals to road users?
q-9640.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A person carrying out works on behalf of or with the consent of the road authority is authorised to give instructions and signals to road users. Such instructions take precedence over signs and traffic lights, so they must be followed.

q-9649.text: In the presented situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle in the roundabout?
q-9649.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The entry to this roundabout is preceded by a give-way sign, so vehicles already travelling on the roundabout's roadway have priority. You may enter only when the manoeuvre will not force anyone to brake or change direction.

q-9652.text: In the presented situation, can you turn left at the visible intersection?
q-9652.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this intersection a left turn is prohibited, as follows from the signs visible in the material. You must continue in the permitted direction and turn around or turn where it is allowed.

q-9668.text: On the presented road, does the sign prohibiting overtaking cease to apply at the end of the bend?
q-9668.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The overtaking ban does not end where the bend ends. It applies up to the sign cancelling the ban or up to the nearest intersection, unless a plate under the sign gives the length of the section covered by the ban.

q-9690.text: Is it allowed in the presented situation to stop the vehicle on the roadway?
q-9690.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place stopping a vehicle on the roadway is prohibited, as follows from the signs visible in the material. A vehicle standing on the roadway would restrict visibility and force others to get around it, so you must drive on.

q-9696.text: Does the visible prohibition sign only apply to the pavement?
q-9696.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A prohibition sign applies to the road on the side where it is installed, so it covers not only the pavement but also the roadway and the shoulder. Parking partly on the pavement does not release you from the prohibition.

q-9706.text: In the presented situation, do you yield priority to the cyclist?
q-9706.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In this situation the cyclist has priority, so you must give way — that is, not force them to stop or change direction or speed. You may continue the manoeuvre only once the cyclist has passed.

q-9710.text: In this situation, when turning left at the nearest intersection are you entering a no through road?
q-9710.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material inform that the road branching off to the left has no through passage — it ends and cannot be driven along any further. Entering it means having to return by the same road.

q-9738.text: In the presented situation, do the signs warn you of an unexpected change in the traffic direction?
q-9738.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material warn that the further course of the road changes in a way the driver may not expect. You must reduce speed and drive the vehicle so as to adapt to the new course of the roadway without sudden manoeuvres.

q-9791.text: Is the vehicle driver obliged to signal the stop of a motor vehicle or trailer as a result of damage or an accident on the highway?
q-9791.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An immobilised vehicle must be marked: switch on the hazard lights and place a warning triangle 100 m behind the vehicle. The point is that a driver approaching at high speed notices the obstacle early enough.

q-9792.text: Is the vehicle driver obliged to signal the stop of a motor vehicle or trailer due to damage or an accident on the expressway?
q-9792.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On an expressway the same rules apply as on a motorway: hazard lights switched on and a warning triangle placed 100 m behind the immobilised vehicle. Marking is necessary because of the high speed of the approaching vehicles.

q-9979.text: Can you turn right in the presented situation?
q-9979.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A right turn is prohibited at this place, as follows from the signs visible in the material. You must drive on in the permitted direction and turn only where the manoeuvre is allowed.

q-10030.text: Upon stopping a vehicle for inspection, can the driver exit the vehicle without the permission of the traffic officer?
q-10030.explanation: Correct answer: NO. After being stopped for a check, the driver remains in the vehicle and may get out only on the instruction or with the consent of the officer carrying out the check. This rule protects both the officer and the driver, who would otherwise find themselves on the road.

q-10032.text: Upon stopping a vehicle for inspection, should the driver keep his or her hands on the steering wheel?
q-10032.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Until permitted by the officer, the driver keeps their hands on the steering wheel and makes no sudden movements. The officer must be able to see the driver's hands, because their safety and the calm course of the check depend on it.

q-10034.text: Which of the values below should you take into account when establishing the distance between the vehicle in front?
q-10034.explanation: Correct answer: A. The distance from the vehicle ahead depends above all on speed: the faster you drive, the further you travel during the reaction time and the longer the braking distance. The width and length of the vehicles have no bearing on this distance.

q-10035.text: As a driver, can you walk away from a vehicle while the engine is running?
q-10035.explanation: Correct answer: C. The driver may not leave the vehicle while the engine is running. Before walking away, switch off the engine and secure the vehicle against moving off on its own, because an unattended vehicle with the engine running creates a real hazard.

q-10038.text: Is there a specified maximum speed limit for passenger cars on this road?
q-10038.explanation: Correct answer: C. For a car the limit here is 140 km/h — the highest permitted speed for this type of road. The absence of a sign with a number does not mean anything goes, and in rain or fog speed must be reduced anyway.

q-10040.text: Does the provisions of the Law on road traffic allow you to move away from the vehicle while the engine is running?

options.A: Yes, but only up to a distance of 15 mteres from the vehicle.
options.C: Yes, but only up to 5 mteres from the vehicle.

q-10040.explanation: Correct answer: B. The rules do not allow you to walk away from the vehicle while the engine is running — no distance is permitted here. Before walking away, switch off the engine and secure the vehicle against moving off on its own.

q-10041.text: Is the condition of the vehicle a factor that you should take into consideration when selecting the speed on the road?

options.B: Yes, but only when driving in a built-up area.
options.C: Yes, but only outside a built-up area.

q-10041.explanation: Correct answer: A. Speed is chosen according to conditions, and those include the vehicle's technical state: worn tyres, weaker brakes or a load lengthen the stopping distance. This rule applies on every road, regardless of the built-up area.

q-10046.text: What can you not do when involved in an accident in which there are casualties?

options.C: Move the vehicle to the hard shoulder.

q-10046.explanation: Correct answer: C. In an accident with people killed or injured, the position of the vehicles and the traces may not be changed, because they are evidence for the services. The vehicle stays put until the police arrive; at the same time you must give help and call the rescue services.

q-10048.text: What is the purpose of the triangle, which is a mandatory equipment for passenger cars?

options.A: Marking the load on the roof rack of the vehicle.
options.B: Warning of an immobilized vehicle on the road due to breakdown.
options.C: Warning of faulty rear position lamps of a moving vehicle.

q-10048.explanation: Correct answer: B. The warning triangle serves to mark a vehicle immobilised on the road, for example after a breakdown, so that other drivers notice the obstacle early enough. It is placed behind the vehicle, and the required distance depends on the type of road.

q-10050.text: With which system in a passenger car does the anti-lock "ABS" operate?
q-10050.explanation: Correct answer: B. ABS is part of the braking system: sensors detect a wheel locking and automatically reduce the braking force on it. As a result the wheels keep turning and the driver retains the ability to steer the vehicle while braking.

q-10053.text: What distance should you maintain when overtaking a motorcyclist?
q-10053.explanation: Correct answer: C. When overtaking a motorcyclist you must keep a distance of no less than 1 m. The same minimum applies to a cyclist, a moped rider and a pedestrian, and at higher speed the distance should be correspondingly greater.

q-10054.text: Which braking method do you apply in the event of an ABS failure on a slippery surface?

options.B: Pushing the brake pedal all the way down.

q-10054.explanation: Correct answer: A. Without working ABS the wheels lock easily, and a vehicle with locked wheels loses steering. Pumping the brake, that is, alternately pressing and releasing the pedal, lets you slow down while keeping control of your course.

q-10055.text: When are you obliged to change to the right lane after an overtaking monoeuvre?

options.A: When I see the rear of the vehicle being overtaken in the right reverse mirror.
options.B: When the overtaken vehicle is 100 m behind me.
options.C: When i'm sure that there is no risk of "cutting in" on the vehicle being overtaking.

q-10055.explanation: Correct answer: C. You return to the right lane only when you will not cut in on the overtaken vehicle, that is, not force it to brake or change direction. Merely seeing the vehicle in the mirror does not guarantee that, and a fixed distance is not a rule.

q-10056.text: Whic of these factors has a direct impact on the total stopping distance of a passenger car?

options.A: The amount of fuel in the tank.
options.B: The condition of the steering system.
options.C: The reaction time of the vehicle driver.

q-10056.explanation: Correct answer: C. The total stopping distance is the distance covered during the driver's reaction time plus the braking distance. The longer the reaction takes, the greater the stretch the vehicle covers before it even begins to slow down.

q-10057.text: Which of these factors has a decisive influence on the determination of the distance from the vehicle in front of us?
q-10057.explanation: Correct answer: C. The required distance is decided above all by speed: the faster you drive, the longer the stretch covered during the reaction time and the longer the braking distance. The dimensions of the vehicle have no bearing on this distance.

q-10058.text: Which of these factors should you take into account when executing an overtaking manoeuvre?
q-10058.explanation: Correct answer: B. When overtaking, the most important thing is keeping a safe distance from the vehicle being overtaken — lateral while passing and longitudinal when returning to the lane. Passing too close can blow a cyclist or motorcyclist off their line.

q-10059.text: By how much does the braking distance increase, if you double the speed?
q-10059.explanation: Correct answer: C. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed, so twice the speed means four times the braking distance. On top of that, the stretch covered during the driver's reaction time also gets longer.

q-10060.text: You are travelling on the highway and intend to exit it. At what point do you start braking before the exit from the highway?

options.B: After entering the start of the exit lane (exit).
options.C: At any point on the highway.

q-10060.explanation: Correct answer: B. Speed is reduced only after entering the deceleration lane, because that is what it is for. Braking on the main carriageway, where vehicles travel very fast, risks being run into from behind.

q-10061.text: Is the lie of the land a factor that you should take into account when choosing your speed on a road?

options.A: Not if you are driving at a speed of 60 km/h.

q-10061.explanation: Correct answer: C. Rises, descents and curves in the road limit visibility and change the vehicle's behaviour — on a descent the braking distance grows. Speed must be chosen so that you can stop within the stretch you can actually see.

q-10062.text: What may be the result of using worn out wiper blades in a passenger car?

options.B: Reduced visibility of the road druring rain.
options.C: Less consumption of the windscreen washer fluid.

q-10062.explanation: Correct answer: B. Worn blades do not clear water evenly and leave streaks, so in rain the picture of the road becomes blurred. Poorer visibility delays recognising an obstacle, so the blades are replaced as soon as they begin to streak.

q-10063.text: What kind of danger does the presented vertical sign warn you of?

options.B: Strong wind gusts occuring only on the right side.

q-10063.explanation: Correct answer: A. The sign warns of a strong crosswind that can push the vehicle off its line, especially on bridges, flyovers and in open country. Gusts can come from any side, so slow down and hold the steering wheel firmly.

q-10064.text: In which phase of intensive rain is the asphalt roadway more slippery?
q-10064.explanation: Correct answer: A. The most dangerous are the first minutes of rain: water mixes with dust, oil and rubber particles, forming a slippery layer on the asphalt. Further rain washes this residue away, so grip gradually improves.

q-10065.text: In which of these circumstances are you obliged to change from the beam headlights to low beam?

options.A: When approaching a pedestrian going in the same direction.
options.B: When approaching a vehicle coming from a transverse road.
options.C: When approaching a moving vehicle in front of you and there is a possibility of blinding the driver.

q-10065.explanation: Correct answer: C. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle another driver — including the one travelling ahead, because the light hits their mirrors. Once you close up on the vehicle ahead, you must switch to dipped headlights.

q-10066.text: What should you do in this situation?

options.A: You have the right to change traffic lanes to the left.
options.B: You should remain on the traffic lane you are taking.
options.C: When changing lanes you need not exercise special caution.

q-10066.explanation: Correct answer: B. In this situation changing to the left lane is not permitted, so you must continue in the lane you occupy. Any lane change in any case requires special care and giving way to vehicles in the lane you are moving into.

q-10067.text: Does the towed vehicle have an effect on the field of vision of the driver?

options.A: It has no effect on limiting the field of vision.
options.B: Only when executing a U-turn manoeuvre at an intersection.
options.C: It has an effect on limiting the field of vision.

q-10067.explanation: Correct answer: C. A towed vehicle blocks the view in the rear-view mirror and makes it harder to judge what is happening behind. The driver must then use the exterior mirrors more often, drive more slowly and leave more room for manoeuvres.

q-10068.text: Does the transparency of windscreen have an influence on the field of vision of the driver?

options.A: It has an effect on limiting the field of vision.
options.B: Only in conditions of reduced air transparency.
options.C: It has no effect on limiting the field of vision.

q-10068.explanation: Correct answer: A. Dirty, misted or iced windows scatter light and reduce the area the driver actually sees. Before driving, the windows must be cleaned and demisted, because their condition limits visibility throughout the journey, not only in fog.

q-10069.text: What factor causes a decrease in a vehicle drivers's field of vision?
q-10069.explanation: Correct answer: A. As speed increases, the eyes focus on a point ever further ahead of the vehicle, and the field of vision narrows to a thin corridor. The driver notices pedestrians and vehicles appearing from the side later.

q-10070.text: What factors influence the improvement of the field of vision?

options.C: The stress level of the driver.

q-10070.explanation: Correct answer: B. Reducing speed widens the field of vision: the driver takes in a larger section of the road and notices earlier what is happening at the sides. High speed and strong stress do the opposite — they narrow observation.

q-10071.text: Which of the following road elements should you observe when driving on the highway?

options.A: Only the traffic lane in front of your vehicle.
options.B: The entire roadway and hard shoulder in front and behind the vehicle.
options.C: Only your traffic lane and the right hard shoulder in front of the vehicle.

q-10071.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a motorway speed differences are large, so observation must cover the whole carriageway and the hard shoulder, both ahead of the vehicle and behind it. Regular glances in the mirrors let you notice faster vehicles and obstacles on the shoulder in time.

q-10072.text: How should the external mirrors of the passenger car be positioned?

options.A: Such that half of the mirror is visible through the window of the front doors.
options.B: Such that the side of the car is not visible in the mirror.
options.C: Such that a fragment of the side of the car and and the road behind is visible in the mirror.

q-10072.explanation: Correct answer: C. An exterior mirror is set so that a small strip of the vehicle's side is visible at its inner edge, with the rest showing the road behind. Such a reference point makes it easier to judge distance and reduces the blind spot.

q-10073.text: In what way does the speed of the car affect the field of vision?

options.A: The field of vision decreases along with an increase in speed.
options.B: The field of vision increases along with an increase in speed.

q-10073.explanation: Correct answer: A. The higher the speed, the narrower the angle in which the driver recognises detail — the eyes focus on a distant point and the side zone drops out of the field of vision. That is why at high speed it is easy to miss a pedestrian or a sign at the side.

q-10074.text: How should you behave when entering a section of a road covered with puddles?

options.C: Take the traffic lane reserved for vehicles coming in the opposite direction.

q-10074.explanation: Correct answer: A. In puddles the tyres lose contact with the surface — aquaplaning sets in and the vehicle stops responding to the steering and the brakes. Speed should be reduced early and smoothly, without harsh braking or turning the wheels.

q-10075.text: Which driving lane should you take in the initial stage when performing a manoeuvre at the left turn shown here?

options.A: Go as far as possible to the centre of the roadway, crossing the double solid line.
options.B: Go to the centre of the roadway, but not crossing the double solid line.
options.C: Go close to the right edge of the roadway.

q-10075.explanation: Correct answer: C. Before a left-hand bend the vehicle is kept closer to the right edge of the carriageway — the view round the curve opens up earlier, and the radius of the curve driven is larger. Drifting to the middle of the carriageway, let alone onto the double solid line, is not permitted.

q-10076.text: Which of these driving techniques applies to the term "eco-driving"?

options.A: Using only the service brake to reduce speed.
options.B: Using the engine to reduce driving speed.
options.C: Changing gears frequently to maintain a high engine revolution.

q-10076.explanation: Correct answer: B. Engine braking, that is, lifting off the accelerator with a gear engaged, cuts off the fuel supply in modern vehicles and at the same time spares the brakes. Constant use of the service brake alone and high engine speed increase fuel consumption.

q-10077.text: Whic of these driving techniques applies to the the term "eco-driving"?

options.A: Frequent use of the service brake.

q-10077.explanation: Correct answer: B. Economical driving is smooth driving: every sharp acceleration burns excess fuel, and every hard braking turns energy into heat. A calm style with anticipation of the situation lowers fuel consumption and reduces wear on components.

q-10078.text: What should the proper driving technique involve in this road situation?

options.B: Driving in the middle of the roadway.
options.C: Driving at the lowest possible gear.

q-10078.explanation: Correct answer: A. The basis of safe driving technique is a speed matched to the state of the road, visibility and traffic — one that allows the vehicle to be stopped within the visible stretch. Occupying the middle of the carriageway or driving in the lowest gear is no substitute.

q-10079.text: How can you make it easier to drive a passenger car out of a sticky snow?

options.A: By reversing a few times and moving forward.
options.B: By starting off at high engine revolutions.
options.C: By rapidly releasing the clutch pedal.

q-10079.explanation: Correct answer: A. Rocking the vehicle, that is, alternately reversing and moving forward a short way, packs the snow and creates a footing under the wheels. High revs and dropping the clutch suddenly only make the wheels spin and dig the vehicle in.

q-10080.text: Is it allowed to tow a passenger car on the highway to the nearest exit or rest area?

options.C: Yes, but only if you drive at a maximum speed of 20 km/h.

q-10080.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a motorway a broken-down vehicle may be towed to the nearest exit or service area only by a vehicle designed for towing, that is, roadside assistance. An ordinary car is prohibited from towing in these conditions.

q-10081.text: Is it allowed to tow a vehicle using a rigid coupling if the vehicle has a faulty steering wheel system?

options.B: Yes, but only in an unbuilt area.
options.C: Yes, but only in a built-up area.

q-10081.explanation: Correct answer: A. A vehicle with a faulty steering system may not be towed, because even with a rigid coupling the driver of the towed vehicle has to steer it. Such a vehicle is carried on a flatbed or with the axle raised, so that steering is not needed.

q-10083.text: Whe transporting a 6-year-old passenger on a moped, are you allowed to travel at a speed of 50 km/h?
q-10083.explanation: Correct answer: C. A moped is by definition a vehicle with a design speed not exceeding 45 km/h, so riding at 50 km/h is not permitted regardless of whether a passenger is carried and at what time of day.

q-10084.text: What is the maximum permissible length of the combination vehicle consisting of a truck with a GVWR up to 3.5 tons and a caravan?
q-10084.explanation: Correct answer: B. The permitted length of a combination consisting of a car and a trailer is 18.75 metres. It is measured for the whole combination including the coupling device, and the fact that the trailer is a caravan changes nothing.

q-10085.text: Which of these circumstances is the proper way of transporting cargo on a trailer pulled by a passenger car?

options.A: The cargo is protected from moving.
options.B: The cargo is not protected from displacement.
options.C: The cargo is not protected from displacement, if driving speed is not greater than 30 km/h.

q-10085.explanation: Correct answer: A. A load on a trailer must always be fastened so that it does not shift under acceleration, braking and on bends. No speed releases you from this duty — a shifted load changes the distribution of mass and can make the trailer sway.

q-10086.text: How should you transport cargo in a trailer pulled by a passenger car?

options.A: The cargo should not be protected from displacement.
options.B: The cargo may block some of the trailer's lights.
options.C: The cargo cannot have any effects on the stability of the vehicle.

q-10086.explanation: Correct answer: C. The load is arranged so as not to impair the stability of the combination — placed too high or unevenly, it makes the trailer sway. Apart from that it must be fastened and must not cover the lights or the number plate.

q-10087.text: Can an international driving licence be issued for a period longer than 3 years?

options.A: Yes, subject to a medical certificate.

q-10087.explanation: Correct answer: C. An international driving permit is issued for a period no longer than 3 years and in no case longer than the validity of the national driving licence on the basis of which it was issued. A medical certificate does not extend that period.

q-10089.text: Are allowed to drive, if your driving licence is invalid?

options.A: Yes, if it has only been invalid for a week.
options.B: Yes, because you have 30 days to update data.

q-10089.explanation: Correct answer: C. An invalid driving licence gives no entitlement to drive — from the moment it expires the driver is treated as a person without entitlement. The rules provide for no transitional period here, neither a week nor thirty days.

q-10090.text: You are a holder of driving licence - cat. B. Are you entitled to drive an agricultural tractor beyond the borders of the State?

options.B: Yes, but only in a built-up area.

q-10090.explanation: Correct answer: C. The entitlement to drive an agricultural tractor on the basis of category B applies only on the territory of Poland. Abroad this extension is not recognised — there the appropriate category of driving licence is needed for a tractor.

q-10091.text: You are a driving licence - cat. B holder for at least three years. Are you permitted to ride a motorcycle with a cylinder capacity not greater than 125 cm3?

options.C: Yes, provided you ride at a maximum speed of 30 km/h.

q-10091.explanation: Correct answer: A. A driver who has held category B for at least 3 years may ride a motorcycle with an engine capacity of up to 125 cm³ and limited power. This entitlement applies in Poland and involves no additional speed limit.

q-10093.text: Does the driving licence - cat. B entitle you to drive a combination vehicle consisting of a passenger car and trailer, which the total gross vehicle weight rating does not exceed 3.5 tons?

options.B: Only provided you do not exceed the speed of 30 km/h.

q-10093.explanation: Correct answer: C. Category B allows you to drive a combination of a car and a trailer if the combined maximum permissible mass does not exceed 3.5 tonnes. This entitlement is not subject to a condition of driving at up to 30 km/h.

q-10094.text: Should you apply to the Provincial governor to obtain an international driving licence?

options.A: No, such driving licence is issued by the Starost.
options.B: Yes, but you have to pay a registration fee.

q-10094.explanation: Correct answer: A. An international driving permit is issued by the starosta, the same authority that issues the national driving licence, at the driver's request and on the basis of a valid national document. The voivode does not deal with these matters.

q-10095.text: Where do you find information on the permitted number of persons that can be transported in a passenger car?
q-10095.explanation: Correct answer: A. The permitted number of people carried is entered in the vehicle's registration document, alongside other technical data. It may not be exceeded, even if there is physically enough room in the cabin.

q-10098.text: What failure is indicated by a rapidly flashing turn signal?

options.B: Short circuit in high voltage wires.

q-10098.explanation: Correct answer: C. Faster flashing of the indicator is the standard way of telling the driver that one of the bulbs in that circuit has stopped working. The fault must be fixed, because an unsignalled manoeuvre is dangerous for other road users.

q-10099.text: What may be the sign of a broken brake cable in a passenger car?

options.A: Increase in the braking force at uniform pressing on the brake pedal.
options.B: Little or no resistance of the brake pedal u[pon pressing.
options.C: A very high resistance of the brake pedal upon pressing.

q-10099.explanation: Correct answer: B. When a pipe fails, brake fluid leaks out, no pressure builds and the pedal sinks with almost no resistance. You may not drive with such a fault — the vehicle is stopped with the parking brake and engine braking.

q-10100.text: Which of these, causes the failure of the compression ignition engine from achieving starter rotation?
q-10100.explanation: Correct answer: A. The starter motor turns the crankshaft at the speed needed for starting, so its failure makes starting impossible. A charged battery does not hinder starting, and a loose alternator belt affects charging, not turning the engine over.

q-10101.text: Which of these factors may be the reason for the car pulling to the left?

options.A: Incorrect toe-in of the front wheels.
options.B: Uniform air pressure in the car wheels.
options.C: Malfunction of the electronic handbrake module.

q-10101.explanation: Correct answer: A. Disturbed front suspension geometry, especially incorrect wheel alignment, makes the vehicle pull to one side and forces constant correction at the steering wheel. Equal tyre pressures do the opposite — they eliminate pulling.

q-10102.text: Which of these factors may cause rapid wear of the tires on the front wheels of a passenger car?

options.A: Slight overload of the vehic's lfront axle.

q-10102.explanation: Correct answer: B. With incorrect wheel alignment the wheels do not roll exactly in the direction of travel, so the tread constantly scrubs on the surface and wears quickly and unevenly. The characteristic symptom is wear mainly on the inner or the outer edge of the tyre.

q-10103.text: How do the dipped headlights illuminate the road in front of a passengers car?
q-10103.explanation: Correct answer: C.
