Dipped headlights have an asymmetric cut-off between light and shadow: on the right side they light the road further, and on the left they are lowered so as not to dazzle oncoming drivers. This makes the right edge of the carriageway and pedestrians walking along it easier to see.

q-10104.text: In which of these cases are you obliged to replace the tyre with a new one in a passenger car?

options.A: When the air vent is damaged.
options.B: When there is a thin nail on the head of the tyre.
options.C: When disformations are visible on the sides of the tyre.

q-10104.explanation: Correct answer: C. Bulges and deformations in the sidewall mean damage to the tyre's carcass; such a tyre can burst at speed at any moment and cannot be repaired. A damaged valve is replaced separately, and a puncture in the tread may be repaired professionally.

q-10107.text: In this situation, does the traffic police officer permit you to turn left at the intersection?
q-10107.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signals of a person directing traffic take precedence over traffic lights and signs, so the driver follows precisely them. The posture and gestures visible in the material indicate permission to turn left; before the manoeuvre you must let those already on the intersection pass.

q-10108.text: Does the driving licence - cat. B entitle you to ride a moped or a light 4-wheel vehicle?

options.A: Yes, but only outside a built-up area.

q-10108.explanation: Correct answer: B. Category B includes the entitlement to drive a moped and a light quadricycle, so a separate category AM is not needed. The entitlement is not limited to a built-up area or to the area outside it.

q-10109.text: When towing a motocycle, should the two braking systems be in good working order?

options.A: Yes, but only at a speed above 20 km/h.

q-10109.explanation: Correct answer: B. Only a vehicle with working braking and steering systems may be towed, because the rider of a towed motorcycle must be able to stop it. The requirement applies at any speed, not only above 20 km/h.

q-10110.text: In this situation, do you have priority over the cyclist coming from the left?
q-10110.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the situation shown, the cyclist approaching from the left has priority, so you must give way. A bicycle is a full road user, and the priority rules apply to it in the same way as to a car.

q-10111.text: Does this sign warn you of a danger?
q-10111.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign shown belongs to the warning signs: it informs of a place on the road where a danger may occur and obliges you to raise your attention. The driver's response is to reduce speed and be ready for a change in the situation beyond the sign.

q-10112.text: Does this sign warn of possible road frosting or doves on the road?
q-10112.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a section where frost or black ice may occur on the roadway — typically bridges, shaded places and dips in the terrain. Grip drops sharply there, so speed is reduced in advance and the steering wheel and pedals are operated smoothly.

q-10117.text: In this situation, are you on a road with priority?
q-10117.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material designates a road with priority, so at the nearest intersection drivers coming out of the side roads must give way. Priority does not, however, release you from watching and being ready for someone else's mistake.

q-10118.text: In this situation, are you approaching an intersection of roads where the priority is determined by road signs?
q-10118.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The order of passage at this intersection is set by the road signs visible in the material, not by the general right-hand rule. The signs apply as long as traffic is not directed by an authorised person and no traffic lights are operating.

q-10120.text: In this situation, are you warned of approaching a crossroads without right of way?
q-10120.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material warns that you are approaching an intersection with a subordinate road, i.e. you are on the road with priority. Even so, you must watch the mouths of the side roads and expect that someone may fail to give way.

q-10122.text: Does this sign warn you of approaching a crossroads with a side road to the left?
q-10122.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The drawing on the sign shows from which side the subordinate road joins; here it is the left side. You are on the road with priority, but your attention must be directed precisely at the left mouth of the side road.

q-10123.text: In this situation, are you warned of a place on a road that is particularly frequented by children or of the proximity of such a place?
q-10123.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a place where children often appear on the road, for example near a school or a playground. A child's behaviour can be unpredictable, so you must slow down and be ready to brake immediately.

q-10124.text: In this situation, are you warned of a designated pedestrian crossing?
q-10124.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material has a different meaning and does not warn of a marked pedestrian crossing. A crossing is announced by a separate warning sign with a pedestrian silhouette on a triangular background.

q-10126.text: In this situation, are you warned of a narrowing on both sides of the road that could impede traffic?
q-10126.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a narrowing of the carriageway on both sides, which may leave no room for passing oncoming traffic freely. Speed is reduced early, and if necessary you give way to the oncoming vehicle.

q-10127.text: In this situation, are you warned of road narrowing that may impede traffic?
q-10127.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign informs of a narrowing of the carriageway that may hinder traffic, including passing oncoming vehicles. Slow down, judge the width of the passage and give way if necessary.

q-10136.text: In this situation, are you warned of road narrowing that may impede traffic?
q-10136.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign informs of a narrowing of the carriageway that may hinder traffic, including passing oncoming vehicles. Slow down, judge the width of the passage and give way if necessary.

q-10138.text: In this situation, are you approaching a crossroads with circular traffic?
q-10138.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material informs of a roundabout, where vehicles travel around an island in one direction. Before entering, you should choose the correct lane and comply with the established priority.

q-10140.text: In this situation, do you have to stop exactly before the vertical sign "Stop"?
q-10140.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You must stop before the absolute stop line, and where there is none — at a point from which the road with priority can be seen, not at the signpost itself. The sign merely establishes the duty to bring the vehicle to a complete stop.

q-10141.text: Are you allowed to continue driving right without stopping?
q-10141.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An unconditional stop applies at this place, and it covers every direction of travel, including a right turn. Only after stopping and assessing the situation may you continue, giving way.

q-10152.text: In this situation, can you turn left without stopping?
q-10152.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to stop applies to every chosen direction, so before turning left you must bring the vehicle to a complete stop. Only then do you give way and perform the manoeuvre when it is safe.

q-10154.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-10154.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority at this intersection follows from the signs visible in the material and belongs to the tram, so it does not give way to the vehicle approaching from the right. You must, however, watch whether the driver of that vehicle really is slowing down.

q-10156.text: Is vehicle traffic permitted around the roundabout in both directions at the nearest intersection?
q-10156.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a roundabout vehicles go round the island in one direction only, as indicated by the sign. Driving against the flow on such a junction is prohibited and risks a head-on collision.

q-10158.text: Does the visible sign indicate that you are entering a one-way traffic?
q-10158.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible sign has a different meaning and does not inform about the beginning of a one-way road. Such a road is indicated by a separate information sign with a white arrow on a blue background.

q-10160.text: Does the visible sign indicate the end of the motorway?
q-10160.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown does not mean the end of the motorway. The end of a motorway is announced by a separate sign repeating its symbol crossed out with a red line, after which the special rules of that road cease to apply.

q-10161.text: Does the visible sign indicate the end of the expressway?
q-10161.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces the end of the expressway: beyond it the special rules of that road cease to apply, including the higher permitted speed limit. Further on, the general rules applicable to the section you are entering apply.

q-10164.text: Can you expect not to see warning signs behind the visible sign compelling drivers to drive slowly?
q-10164.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign introduces a zone in which speed humps and other traffic-calming devices need not be preceded by separate warning signs. The driver must keep a speed appropriate to the character of such a zone on their own.

q-10165.text: Does this sign indicate the end of the expressway?
q-10165.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown has a different meaning and does not announce the end of the expressway. The end of that road is indicated by a separate sign repeating its symbol crossed out with a red line, after which the special traffic rules cease to apply.

q-10168.text: Are you allowed to turn left from the lane you are occupying at the nearest crossroads?
q-10168.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The permitted directions of travel from a given lane are decided by the signs and the direction arrows on the roadway visible in the material, and a left turn from the lane you are in is not permitted. The lane change is made earlier, after making sure it is safe and signalling the manoeuvre.

q-10174.text: In this situation, are you being warned of three dangerous bends?
q-10174.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign with the plate shown in the material warns of a series of three dangerous bends following one after another. Speed is reduced before the first curve and care is kept up until leaving the last one, without overtaking.

q-10175.text: Do you always have the right of way when turning left at this crossroads?
q-10175.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When turning left, you must give way to vehicles going straight or turning right from the opposite direction, and also to pedestrians stepping onto the roadway you are entering. Travelling on a road with priority does not lift this duty.

q-10178.text: When driving a passenger car, are you allowed to turn right after this sign?
q-10178.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The restriction arising from the sign visible in the material does not cover a passenger car, so a right turn beyond the sign is permitted. The manoeuvre is signalled with the indicator and performed after giving way to pedestrians and cyclists.

q-10179.text: Are you approaching a crossroads from a road with right of way?
q-10179.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material indicates that you are on the road with priority, so drivers coming out of the cross roads are obliged to give way to you. Priority does not, however, release you from watching the intersection and being ready to brake.

q-10183.text: In this situation, does the expressway end immediately after the visible sign?
q-10183.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign visible in the material only announces that the end of the expressway is approaching, and its rules still apply on the section beyond the sign. The end of that road is announced only by the sign placed where it actually ends.

q-10189.text: In this situation, are you allowed to perform a U-turn?
q-10189.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place turning around is prohibited, as follows from the sign or the traffic arrangement visible in the material. The manoeuvre must be moved to where it is permitted and visibility allows it to be performed safely.

q-10190.text: Does the visible double continuous line separate lanes for traffic travelling in the same direction?
q-10190.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A double solid line separates lanes intended for opposite directions of traffic and prohibits crossing it or driving on it. Lanes of the same direction are separated by a broken line, which may be crossed when changing lanes.

q-10191.text: In this situation, can you continue driving in the left lane if the right lane is free?
q-10191.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area, on a roadway with at least two lanes for a given direction, the driver may use any of them. The requirement to drive as close as possible to the right edge applies outside built-up areas.

q-10192.text: In this situation, are you driving on a one-way traffic road?
q-10192.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The elements shown in the material indicate that the carriageway serves both directions of traffic, so it is not a one-way road. You must expect oncoming vehicles and not occupy the left part of the carriageway.

q-10193.text: In this situation, are you driving on a two-lane carriageway?
q-10193.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The width of the roadway and the road markings visible in the material mark out two lanes on it. The number of lanes decides where you may position yourself and how to perform manoeuvres, so it must be read from the markings, not from habit.

q-10197.text: In this situation, are you entitled to continue driving without stopping?
q-10197.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs and signals shown in the material impose no duty to stop, and the road ahead of the vehicle is clear, so you may continue. Care and a speed suited to the conditions still apply.

q-10208.text: Are you obliged to keep a safe distance from the vehicle you are overtaking?
q-10208.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When overtaking, you must keep a safe lateral distance from the road user being overtaken, because they may change their path or be pushed sideways by a gust of air. The distance is chosen according to speed and the type of vehicle being overtaken.

q-10212.text: In this situation, do you have to signal your intention to return to the right lane with a right turn signal?
q-10212.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Returning to the right lane after overtaking is a lane change, and every change of direction or lane is signalled with the appropriate indicator. The signal is switched on before the manoeuvre and off as soon as it is completed.

q-10213.text: Is it permitted to stop here?
q-10213.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The no-parking prohibition at this place follows from the sign or markings visible in the material, so leaving the vehicle there is not permitted regardless of how much free room there is. You look for parking outside the area covered by the prohibition.

q-10214.text: Is it permitted to stop here?
q-10214.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place a no-stopping prohibition arising from the sign or markings visible in the material applies, and such a prohibition covers even a short immobilisation of the vehicle. Dropping off a passenger or briefly occupying the spot is also not permitted.

q-10223.text: In this situation, should you stop before the visible line of absolute stop - stop?
q-10223.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The line itself creates no duty to stop — it only marks the place where you must stop when a sign or signal orders it. In the situation shown no such order applies to you, so you may continue, taking care.

q-10224.text: In this situation, are you allowed to use the sound signal?
q-10224.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In a built-up area the horn may be used only when necessary to warn of an immediate danger. In the situation shown there is no such need, so the horn stays unused.

q-10225.text: You intend to turn right. Do you have to signal your intention with a right turn signal?
q-10225.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intended change of direction is signalled with the appropriate indicator early enough and clearly, so that other road users can adapt their behaviour. The signal is switched off directly after the manoeuvre is completed.

q-10229.text: Is overtaking allowed at the visible pedestrian crossing?
q-10229.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking on a pedestrian crossing and directly before it is prohibited, because the vehicle being overtaken hides a pedestrian stepping onto the carriageway. The ban applies whether or not someone happens to be crossing.

q-10237.text: In this situation, are you allowed to stop the vehicle at the roadside?
q-10237.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The no-stopping prohibition in force at this place follows from the sign visible in the material and also covers the shoulder, not only the roadway. You may stop only beyond the section covered by the prohibition, at a place that endangers no one.

q-10242.text: Are you allowed to enter a level crossing if the barriers have not been completely lifted?
q-10242.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Entering a level crossing is allowed only after the barriers have been fully raised and the prohibiting signals have gone out. Moving off while they are being raised risks striking the barrier or trapping the vehicle on the tracks.

q-10243.text: If you intend to turn left at the nearest junction, do you have to signal this manoeuvre with a turn signal?
q-10243.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intended left turn must be signalled with the left indicator early enough, even before approaching the intersection. The signal informs vehicles behind and oncoming, and pedestrians, of the planned path.

q-10247.text: In this situation, when turning left, do you have the right of way over the vehicle driving straight ahead from the opposite direction?
q-10247.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A driver turning left gives way to vehicles going straight from the opposite direction, because they cross their path. The manoeuvre is performed only when the way straight ahead is clear, and the vehicle waits inside the intersection with its wheels pointing straight.

q-10248.text: In this situation, are you obliged to observe the cyclist's behaviour?
q-10248.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A cyclist is a vulnerable road user and may suddenly change their line, swerving around a bump or turning, so they must be watched continuously. Observing the surroundings is part of the care required of a driver.

q-10249.text: In this situation, should you yield the right of way to the pedestrian?
q-10249.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver approaching a pedestrian crossing must take special care, slow down and give way to a pedestrian on the crossing. The pedestrian's priority also applies when you are turning into a side road.

q-10250.text: In this situation, are you entitled to exceed the speed limit to complete the overtaking manoeuvre as quickly as possible?
q-10250.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An overtaking manoeuvre does not release you from the duty to observe the permitted speed. If you cannot overtake without exceeding it, the speed difference is too small and the manoeuvre should not be started at all.

q-10251.text: In this situation, is it permitted to stop at the right edge of the roadway?
q-10251.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition on stopping at this place follows from the sign or from the nature of the place visible in the material. Regardless of the signs, you must not stop the vehicle where it would obstruct others or restrict visibility.

q-10252.text: Are you allowed to make a U-turn in this situation?
q-10252.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place turning around is prohibited, as follows from the sign or the traffic arrangement visible in the material. The manoeuvre must be moved to where it is permitted and visibility allows it to be performed safely.

q-10253.text: In this situation, can you continue driving in the left lane?
q-10253.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signs visible in the material exclude the left lane from further travel in your direction, so you must move to the right lane. The lane change is made early, with the indicator and after checking the mirrors and the blind spot.

q-10258.text: In this situation, are you allowed to park your vehicle at the roadside?
q-10258.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place a no-parking prohibition applies, and it covers the whole road on the side of the sign, so also the shoulder. You may park only where the prohibition ends.

q-10270.text: In this situation, are you obliged to keep a safe distance from the horse-drawn vehicle you are driving past?
q-10270.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing an oncoming vehicle, the driver is obliged to keep a safe lateral distance from it. With a horse-drawn vehicle the distance should be greater and the speed lower, because the animal may be startled by noise or a gust of air.

q-10277.text: You intend to turn right, and the driver approaching from the opposite direction plans to turn left. Do you have have the right of way?
q-10277.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning left is obliged to give way to oncoming vehicles, including those turning right. The right turn is made by the right edge of the roadway, without entering the path of the oncoming vehicle.

q-10278.text: You intend to turn left, and the driver of the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction plans to drive straight ahead. Do you have the right of way?
q-10278.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The vehicle going straight from the opposite direction has priority, and the driver turning left must give way to it. The manoeuvre is performed only when passing will not force the approaching driver to brake or change their path.

q-10279.text: You intend to turn left, and the driver of the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction plans to drive straight ahead. Are you obliged to yield the right of way?
q-10279.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When turning left, the driver is obliged to give way to the vehicle going straight from the opposite direction. You must stop at a place where you do not block the passage of other road users and do not enter the pedestrian crossing.

q-10285.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-10285.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At an intersection you give way to vehicles approaching from the right or travelling on the road with priority, not to the vehicle from the left. Although there is no duty, it is worth watching that driver and making sure they respect the signs.

q-10287.text: In this situation, are you allowed to drive straight ahead through the crossroads?
q-10287.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Going straight ahead is ruled out at this place by the sign or signal visible in the material, which sets the permitted directions of travel. The driver must comply with these signs even when the road straight ahead seems clear.

q-10293.text: In this situation, are you allowed to continue driving straight ahead when driving a passenger car?
q-10293.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The restriction arising from the sign visible in the material does not cover a passenger car, so going straight ahead is permitted. Before entering, however, you must make sure the manoeuvre will not force other road users to brake harshly.

q-10294.text: You are driving a passenger car with a lightweight trailer. Are you allowed to drive on a road beyond the visible prohibition sign?
q-10294.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible restriction does not apply to a combination consisting of a passenger car and a light trailer, i.e. one with a maximum authorised mass not exceeding 750 kg. With a heavier trailer, entering this place would already be prohibited.

q-10296.text: You intend to drive straight ahead, and the driver of the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction plans to turn left. Do you have the right of way?
q-10296.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle going straight ahead has priority over an oncoming vehicle turning left. Even so, you must watch that driver, because their misjudging of distance and speed is a frequent cause of collisions at intersections.

q-10299.text: Should you in all situations stop before the sign "giving priority to vehicles approaching from the opposite direction"?
q-10299.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign orders you to give way to vehicles approaching from the opposite direction on the narrowed section, but does not order a stop every time. When no one is coming the other way, you may pass without stopping; you need to stop only when passing each other is impossible.

q-10304.text: In this situation, are you driving on a road with right of way?
q-10304.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority at the following intersections follows from the sign visible in the material and applies until the sign ending the road with priority. Priority does not, however, release you from watching the cross roads or from careful driving.

q-10310.text: In this situation, is the outermost right lane only intended for rail vehicles?
q-10310.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Tracks laid in the roadway do not make a lane a road exclusively for rail vehicles; other vehicles may also use it, unless a sign prohibits it. You must, however, not obstruct the tram and give way to it where it has priority.

q-10312.text: In this situation, are you allowed to continue driving straight ahead in the outermost right lane?
q-10312.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material permit going straight ahead from this lane, so the driver may continue without changing lanes. The condition is remaining cautious and not obstructing vehicles running on the tracks in this lane.

q-10314.text: In this situation, are you obliged to allow passengers to exit the tram that stopped at the tram stop?
q-10314.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a stop without an island, a driver approaching a standing tram must stop and let passengers safely reach the tram and get off it. You may move off only when nobody is on the carriageway any more.

q-10318.text: In this situation, are you allowed to continue driving through the crossroads?
q-10318.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign or signal shown in the material permits driving through the junction, so the driver does not have to stop. You may enter, however, only when there is room beyond the junction to leave it without blocking others.

q-10336.text: Does the visible sign indicate that vehicles with a height (including cargo) greater than 3 metres are prohibited from traffic?
q-10336.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A height-limit sign prohibits the movement of vehicles whose height exceeds the value given on the sign, here 3 metres. Height is always counted together with the load, the roof rack and everything that protrudes above the vehicle.

q-10340.text: After the visible sign, are you allowed to stop the vehicle for more than 1 minute?
q-10340.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An immobilisation of the vehicle lasting longer than 1 minute is already parking, and the visible sign prohibits it. A shorter stop resulting from traffic conditions remains permitted, provided it does not obstruct others.

q-10346.text: In this situation, are you obliged to use the sound signal to warn children not to run into the roadway?
q-10346.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn is a warning device used when needed, and in a built-up area it may be used only to prevent danger; there is no duty to use it. The right reaction is special care and slowing down, because a horn may only frighten the children further.

q-10347.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop just before the pedestrian crossing?
q-10347.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Approaching a crossing, the driver must take special care, slow down and give way to a pedestrian, but stopping is necessary only when the pedestrian could not otherwise cross safely. If nobody is stepping onto the carriageway, you may drive on.

q-10352.text: You are driving a passenger car with bikes attached to the roof of a total height of 2.6 meters. Can you continue driving straight ahead safely with the load?
q-10352.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The permitted height in force on this road is less than 2.6 metres, so driving straight ahead would risk damaging the bicycles and the obstacle above the carriageway. A vehicle's height is counted together with its load, so another route must be chosen.

q-10356.text: When changing lanes on an unmarked roadway, are you exempt from signalling this manoeuvre with the appropriate turn signal?
q-10356.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A lane change always requires signalling in advance and clearly with the indicator, regardless of whether the lanes are marked with signs. The indicator is switched on before the manoeuvre and off after it is completed.

q-10358.text: Should you exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-10358.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means heightened attention and readiness to react immediately, and it is required in places of increased risk such as the one shown in the material. In practice it comes down to reducing speed and watching the surroundings closely.

q-10360.text: In this situation, are you approaching a crossroad with a side road to the left?
q-10360.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign visible in the material announces an intersection where the subordinate road joins from the left, and the driver is on the road with priority. Priority does not, however, release you from watching the side approach and being ready to brake.

q-10361.text: In the presented situation, are you approaching a crossroad with a side road?
q-10361.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material announce an intersection where the cross road is subordinate, and the driver is on the road with priority. Priority must, however, be confirmed by watching the side approach, because another driver may fail to respect it.

q-10363.text: In this situation, when turning right are you obliged to signal this manoeuvre with a turn signal?
q-10363.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver must signal every change of direction in advance and clearly with the appropriate indicator, even when they see no other vehicles nearby. The indicator is switched off immediately after the manoeuvre is completed.

q-10369.text: You intend to turn right into the gate. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the pedestrian?
q-10369.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver turning into a gateway or onto roadside premises leaves the road and must give way to pedestrians walking on the pavement they drive across. The manoeuvre is carried out slowly, ready to stop before the pavement.

q-10383.text: Should you exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-10383.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means heightened attention and readiness to react immediately, and it is required in places of increased risk such as the one shown in the material. In practice it comes down to reducing speed and watching the surroundings closely.

q-10392.text: You are driving a vehicle with an LPG installation. Does the visible sign on the right tell you to turn right in 150 metres?
q-10392.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible sign is not a mandatory sign and does not impose a direction of travel; it informs about a restriction concerning specific vehicles. The plate with the distance only says after what section the content of the sign will take effect.

q-10394.text: Does this sign apply to vehicles with explosives or flammable materials?
q-10394.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This sign is addressed to vehicles carrying explosive or highly flammable materials and restricts their movement on the section of road concerned. It does not apply to drivers of other vehicles, but they should expect a designated diversion route for such transports.

q-10395.text: In this situation, can you change to the right lane?
q-10395.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The markings at this place do not prohibit changing to the right lane, so the manoeuvre is permitted. Before performing it, you must signal your intention with the indicator, check the mirrors and the blind spot, and give way to vehicles travelling in that lane.

q-10398.text: In this situation, when entering the tunnel, are you obliged to keep a distance of at least 100 meters from the preceding vehicle?
q-10398.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The minimum distance in a tunnel outside a built-up area is 50 m for vehicles with a maximum authorised mass up to 3.5 t and buses, and 80 m for other vehicles. A value of 100 m is not required at this place, although a greater distance is always safer.

q-10399.text: In this situation, are you approaching a crossroad with a one-way side road to the right?
q-10399.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign visible in the material announces an intersection with a subordinate road joining from the right, and its one-way character follows from the signs used. The driver is on the road with priority, but should watch that approach.

q-10406.text: Are you allowed to use the headlights in this situation?
q-10406.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used where they could dazzle others: with an oncoming vehicle, with one travelling ahead, and in conditions of good visibility. In such a situation you drive on dipped headlights.

q-10411.text: In this situation, does the yellow flashing signal permit entry beyond the signalling device?
q-10411.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A flashing yellow signal means that the traffic lights are not controlling traffic in the usual way; passing the traffic light is permitted with particular caution. Priority is then determined by the signs, and where there are none — by the right-hand rule.

q-10412.text: Should you exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-10412.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means heightened attention and readiness to react immediately, and it is required in places of increased risk such as the one shown in the material. In practice it comes down to reducing speed and watching the surroundings closely.

q-10413.text: You intend to turn right at the crossroads. Must you signal this manoeuvre with a right turn signal?
q-10413.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intended right turn is signalled with the right indicator early enough so that other road users have time to read the intention. Signalling gives no priority, however — you must still give way to pedestrians and cyclists crossing the road you are turning into.

q-10419.text: In this situation, are you exiting a residential area?
q-10419.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The end of a residential zone is marked by a separate sign, and the visible signs concern a different kind of place. The distinction matters, because in a residential zone a pedestrian has priority across the full width of the road and speed is limited to 20 km/h.

q-10420.text: Can you travel at any speed beyond this sign?
q-10420.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The lifting of a limit arising from a sign does not mean anything goes — the permitted speeds arising from the rules for the given type of road and vehicle still apply. Speed must moreover be adapted to visibility, the surface and the volume of traffic.

q-10421.text: In this situation, are you entering a built-up area?
q-10421.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The beginning of a built-up area is indicated by a separate sign, and the visible signs have a different meaning. The distinction decides the permitted speed, because in a built-up area it is 50 km/h and outside it is higher.

q-10428.text: In this situation, are you required to use a sound signal to alert children that you are approaching the pedestrian crossing?
q-10428.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The rules impose no duty to warn pedestrians with the horn, and in a built-up area the horn may be used only to prevent danger. At a crossing the right reaction is to slow down, take special care and be ready to stop.

q-10432.text: In this situation, are you allowed to stop at the left edge of the roadway?
q-10432.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Stopping by the left edge of the roadway is permitted on a one-way road, and such conditions apply at this place. The vehicle should be positioned parallel to the edge and as close to it as possible, without obstructing others.

q-10434.text: Does the visible sign indicate lanes intended for driving in the given directions?
q-10434.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A sign of this kind informs which lane you may use to go in a given direction and lets you take the correct lane before the intersection. After entering the intersection a lane change is often no longer possible, which is why the decision is made early.

q-10435.text: Can you perform a U-turn in this situation?
q-10435.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place turning around is prohibited, as follows from the sign or the traffic arrangement visible in the material. The manoeuvre must be moved to where it is permitted and visibility allows it to be performed safely.

q-10437.text: Can you turn left at the nearest crossroads?
q-10437.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material permit a left turn at this intersection. Before the manoeuvre you must take the correct lane, signal your intention with the indicator and give way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians on the cross road.

q-10440.text: Does this sign indicate the end of a road with right of way?
q-10440.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The end of a road with priority is marked by a separate sign, and the visible signs have a different meaning. Losing priority matters, because from that point the order at intersections is decided by signs or by the right-hand rule.

q-10441.text: In this situation, are you approaching a crossroad with a side road?
q-10441.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible in the material announces an intersection with a subordinate road, i.e. one from which drivers must give way. Travelling on the road with priority does not, however, release you from watching the side approaches and being ready to react.

q-10442.text: In this situation, are you approaching a railway crossing?
q-10442.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A level crossing is announced by different signs from those visible in the material, which warn of another dangerous place. The distinction matters, because additional prohibitions apply before a level crossing, among them a ban on overtaking.

q-10446.text: In this situation, will the next signal for your lane be a red signal?
q-10446.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The order of signals is fixed: after green comes yellow, and directly after it red. The yellow signal warns of the approaching prohibition on entry, so you should prepare to stop before the traffic light.

q-10450.text: Does the visible plate under the warning sign indicate the layout of the tracks and roads at the tram crossing?
q-10450.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate placed under the warning sign shows the relative position of the tracks and the road, so the driver knows at what angle they will cross the tracks. This makes it easier to judge visibility and choose a speed before the crossing.

q-10451.text: Should you exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-10451.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means heightened attention and readiness to react immediately, and it is required in places of increased risk such as the one shown in the material. In practice it comes down to reducing speed and watching the surroundings closely.

q-10454.text: In this situation, can you turn right without stopping before the signalling device?
q-10454.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal visible in the material permits a right turn only after the vehicle has stopped before the traffic light. The manoeuvre may then be performed, giving way to the other road users, including pedestrians.

q-10455.text: In this situation, can you turn right before the pedestrian enters your lane?
q-10455.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A pedestrian who has already stepped onto the crossing must be given way across its whole width, not only in your own lane. Cutting in front of the pedestrian forces them to change pace and is prohibited.

q-10459.text: Does the flashing yellow signal indicate that the green signal is about to come on?
q-10459.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A flashing yellow does not announce green; it means that the traffic lights are not controlling traffic and particular caution is required. The order of passage is then determined by the signs, and in their absence — by the rule of priority from the right.

q-10460.text: Does a yellow flashing signal indicate that the red signal is about to come on?
q-10460.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A flashing yellow does not announce red; it informs that the traffic lights are not controlling traffic and that particular caution applies. The order of passage is then decided by the signs, and where there are none — by the priority of the vehicle approaching from the right.

q-10466.text: In this situation, does the speed limit apply only to the outermost right lane?
q-10466.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A speed limit applies across the full width of the roadway and concerns all lanes, unless a plate expressly assigns it to a selected lane. Changing lanes therefore does not release you from the duty to drive at the permitted speed.

q-10469.text: You intend to turn left at the crossroads. Must you signal this manoeuvre with a left turn signal?
q-10469.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intended left turn is signalled with the left indicator early enough, even before taking the position on the roadway appropriate for this manoeuvre. Signalling gives no priority — you must still let oncoming vehicles and pedestrians pass.

q-10472.text: Should you exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-10472.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution means heightened attention and readiness to react immediately, and it is required in places of increased risk such as the one shown in the material. In practice it comes down to reducing speed and watching the surroundings closely.

q-10474.text: In this situation, should you exercise extreme caution even though there are no pedestrians around the crossing?
q-10474.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty of special care at a pedestrian crossing does not depend on whether anyone is currently standing at the kerb. A pedestrian may step out from behind a vehicle or an obstacle at the last moment, so you must slow down and watch the area around the crossing.

q-10475.text: Should you always stop before a pedestrian crossing marked as such?
q-10475.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Before a crossing, special care, slowing down and giving way to a pedestrian apply, but stopping is necessary only when the pedestrian's safe passage requires it. When nobody is using the crossing and nobody is approaching it, you may drive on.

q-10476.text: In this situation, are you approaching a vehicle service station?
q-10476.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The information sign shown in the material indicates a facility where the vehicle can be serviced. Such signs impose no duties; they make it easier to plan a stop and a repair during the journey.

q-10480.text: In this situation, are you allowed to stop at the right edge of the roadway?
q-10480.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place stopping by the right edge is prohibited by the signs in force there. Regardless of the signs, you must not stop the vehicle where it would obscure signs or force others to change their path.

q-10481.text: You are travelling on the highway and intend to exit it. Will you start braking when you enter the exit lane?
q-10481.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Slowing down begins only after moving into the deceleration lane, because braking in a motorway traffic lane creates a danger for those behind. The deceleration lane exists precisely so that speed can be shed before the curve of the exit.

q-10487.text: In this situation, can you change lanes to the left?
q-10487.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings in force at this place do not allow moving to the left lane, so the manoeuvre would not be permitted. A lane change is planned earlier, on the section where the line separating the lanes allows it.

q-10488.text: In this situation, can you stop at the yellow line on the right?
q-10488.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A continuous yellow line at the edge of the carriageway means no stopping on that stretch. The prohibition applies along its whole length, even when the stop would be very short.

q-10495.text: Can you begin an overtaking manoeuvre under the flyover?
q-10495.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The rules do not prohibit overtaking under a viaduct; the prohibitions concern, among others, pedestrian crossings, railway crossings and intersections. The conditions remain sufficient visibility, a free lane for overtaking and no sign prohibiting this manoeuvre.

q-10497.text: In this situation, can you continue driving on this lane if the two lanes on the right are free?
q-10497.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs and traffic conditions at this place do not require a lane change, so driving in the lane you are in is permitted. You must not, however, obstruct faster vehicles and should give them room when they approach from behind.

q-10499.text: Are you allowed to drive in any lane on the motorway regardless of the traffic situation?
q-10499.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a motorway you drive in the right lane, and the lanes to the left are for overtaking; once it is finished you should return to the right. Occupying the left lane without need obstructs faster vehicles and forces overtaking on the wrong side.

q-10505.text: You intend to exit the motorway in the direction towards Pruszków. Should you change lanes to the right?
q-10505.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The motorway exit leads off on the right, so the lane must be changed early enough, after signalling the intention with the indicator. A late lane change and braking just before the exit are a typical cause of dangerous situations.

q-10508.text: In this situation, do the signs notify you of the end of the lane on the right side of the roadway?
q-10508.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible signs do not announce the end of the lane on the right, but inform of a different change in the traffic arrangement. Reading which lane ends decides when and in which direction you need to move over.

q-10509.text: In this situation, do the signs notify you of the end of the lane on the left of the roadway?
q-10509.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible signs announce the end of the left lane, so those travelling in it must move to the adjacent lane in good time. The lane change is made smoothly, with the indicator, without cutting in front of vehicles already travelling in that lane.

q-10511.text: In this situation, do the signs notify you of the end of the expressway?
q-10511.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material inform about the end of the expressway, and with it the rules specific to this category of road cease to apply. Among other things the permitted speeds change, so you must slow down in good time.

q-10513.text: You are driving at 110 km/h. Are you required in this situation to reduce your speed?
q-10513.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A speed of 110 km/h is within the limit in force on this road, and the conditions visible in the material do not require reducing it. The duty to slow down arises only when visibility or grip deteriorates or an obstacle appears.

q-10524.text: In this situation, can you still change lanes to the right?
q-10524.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The road markings at this place separate the lanes in a way that prohibits crossing them, so it is already too late for a lane change. The decision to take the correct lane must be made earlier, before the line becomes solid.

q-10526.text: You are driving a passenger car. In this situation, are you allowed to overtake after the visible sign?
q-10526.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible prohibition is addressed to a group of vehicles other than passenger cars, so it does not restrict the driver of one. Overtaking remains permitted provided there is good visibility, a free lane and certainty that the manoeuvre can be completed safely.

q-10529.text: In this situation, are you allowed to continue driving in the middle lane?
q-10529.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material permit travel in the middle lane in the chosen direction, so a lane change is not necessary. You must, however, watch the adjacent lanes and not obstruct vehicles travelling faster.

q-10531.text: In this situation, should you signal the overtaking manoeuvre with the appropriate turn signal?
q-10531.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking involves a lane change, and every such change is signalled with the indicator: the left one when pulling out to overtake and the right one when returning to your lane. The signal is switched on before the manoeuvre, not during it.

q-10532.text: In this situation, should you stop before the signalling device?
q-10532.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown for this direction permits passage, so stopping before the traffic light is not required and would obstruct those behind. You may enter, however, only when there is room beyond the intersection to leave it.

q-10533.text: In this situation, should you signal your intention to change lanes with the right turn signal?
q-10533.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intention to move to the lane on the right is signalled with the right indicator before the vehicle begins to change its path. Before the manoeuvre you must also check the mirrors and the blind spot and give way to those travelling in that lane.

q-10536.text: In this situation, are you entering the motorway?
q-10536.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The beginning of a motorway is indicated by a separate sign, and the visible signs concern a road of a different category. The distinction matters, because the permitted speeds and which vehicles may use the road depend on its category.

q-10698.text: In the presented situation, do the drivers of the red and green vehicles in compliance with the regulations ensure the passage of the emergency vehicle by creating the so-called "emergency corridor"?
q-10698.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An emergency corridor is formed by vehicles in the far left lane moving as far left as possible and all the others as far right as possible, leaving a clear space between them. Here no clear passage is created, so the arrangement is wrong.

q-10699.text: In the presented situation, did the driver of the combination vehicles no. 1 act accordingly?
q-10699.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver of the vehicle combination positioned it so as not to block the path of the emergency vehicle. A long combination must also move as far as possible towards the edge of its lane, otherwise the corridor narrows and passage becomes impossible.

q-10700.text: In the presented situation, did the drivers, in accordance with the regulations, facilitate the free passage of the emergency vehicle, by creating the so-called "emergency corridor"?
q-10700.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The vehicles in the far left lane have moved as far left as possible and the others to the right, creating a clear passage between them. The corridor is formed as soon as traffic slows down considerably, without waiting for an emergency vehicle to appear.

q-10701.text: In this situation, is it allowed to drive any vehicle directly behind the emergency vehicle?
q-10701.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The passage created for an emergency vehicle may be used only by emergency vehicles and vehicles taking part in the rescue operation. Following them in to cut your time in the jam is prohibited and punishable.

q-10702.text: In conditions of a significant reduction in speed on the roadway, will the driver of vehicle 3 drive ahead of vehicle 2?
q-10702.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When speed drops significantly, alternate merging — the "zipper" rule — applies: the vehicle from the ending lane moves in ahead of the vehicle in the adjacent lane. The driver of vehicle no. 3 lets vehicle no. 2 in and follows behind it.

q-10703.text: In conditions of a significant reduction in speed on the roadway, will the driver of vehicle 2 drive ahead of vehicle 3?
q-10703.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When speed drops significantly, the "zipper" rule applies: the vehicle from the ending lane moves in ahead of the vehicle in the adjacent lane. Vehicle no. 2 therefore goes ahead of vehicle no. 3, which lets it in.

q-10704.text: In conditions of a significant reduction in speed on the roadway, will the driver of vehicle 3 drive ahead of vehicle 2?
q-10704.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When speed drops significantly, alternate merging — the "zipper" rule — applies: the vehicle from the ending lane moves in ahead of the vehicle in the adjacent lane. The driver of vehicle no. 3 lets vehicle no. 2 in and follows behind it.

q-10705.text: In conditions of a significant reduction in speed on the roadway, is the driver of vehicle 3 required to allow the driver of vehicle 2 to change lanes?
q-10705.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When speed drops significantly, the driver in the lane that continues is obliged to let one vehicle from the ending lane in ahead of them. This is not courtesy but a duty arising from the "zipper" rule.

q-10706.text: In conditions of a significant reduction in speed on the roadway, will the driver of Vehicle 4 drive ahead of the driver of Vehicle 2?
q-10706.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The "zipper" rule means letting vehicles in one at a time and alternately: first vehicle no. 2 merges, and only behind it goes vehicle no. 4. Forcing an earlier passage breaks this order.

q-10707.text: Has the driver of the combination of vehicles, who stopped in the middle of this roadway, behaved appropriately towards the driver of the emergency fire service vehicle?
q-10707.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping in the middle of the carriageway closes the emergency vehicle's path. The driver should move as far as possible towards the edge of the carriageway and stop only there, leaving room for it to pass.

q-10709.text: Did the vehicle drivers properly ensure the free passage of the emergency vehicle?
q-10709.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Slowing down alone is not enough — you must move as far as possible towards the edge of your lane and, if necessary, stop, so that a continuous clear passage is created. If even one driver fails to do so, the emergency vehicle is blocked.

q-10710.text: Do all drivers properly ensure the free passage of the emergency vehicle?
q-10710.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A clear passage is created only when all drivers move as far as possible towards the edges of their lanes. It takes just one vehicle staying in the middle for the corridor to be broken and the emergency vehicle to have to brake.

q-10711.text: Can the emergency route created as shown in the picture for an emergency vehicle be used by the driver of an emergency roadside assistance vehicle taking part in a rescue operation?
q-10711.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The passage created may be used not only by emergency vehicles but also by vehicles taking part in the rescue operation — including roadside assistance called to the scene. Other drivers still have no right to it.

q-10713.text: Is the driver of a tractor unit with a tanker driving in the left lane obliged to allow the vehicle in front of you to change lanes to the adjacent one?
q-10713.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to let in a vehicle from the ending lane arises only directly before the point where that lane disappears and when speed is significantly reduced. Before that, a driver in the adjacent lane has no such duty.

q-10715.text: Is the driver of the vehicle driving in the adjacent lane obliged to allow the vehicle in front of you to change to the right lane immediately before the lane disappears?
q-10715.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Directly before the point where the lane ends, with speed significantly reduced, the "zipper" rule applies. The driver in the adjacent lane must let one vehicle from the disappearing lane in ahead of them.

q-10716.text: In this situation, is the driver of the vehicle travelling in the right lane obliged to allow you change lanes?
q-10716.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You are directly before the point where your lane ends, and traffic is slowed — the "zipper" rule then operates. The driver in the lane that continues must let one vehicle in ahead of them.

q-10717.text: Is the driver in the right lane obliged to allow the vehicle in front of you to change lanes at this point?
q-10717.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place the lane still continues, and the duty to let in arises only directly before it disappears and when speed is significantly reduced. An earlier lane change is possible, but only after giving way to those travelling in the adjacent lane.

q-10718.text: Is the driver of the vehicle in the right lane obliged to allow you change lanes after driving past this sign?
q-10718.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Merely passing the sign does not yet create a duty to let anyone in — the sign only warns of a change in the traffic arrangement. The "zipper" rule applies directly before the point where the lane actually ends and with speed significantly reduced.

q-10719.text: Did the driver of the white vehicle in the left lane properly facilitate the passage of the emergency vehicle?
q-10719.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver in the outer left lane is to move as far left as possible, and vehicles in the other lanes — to the right; a free passage then forms between them. The white vehicle is behaving in exactly this way.

q-10720.text: Does the situation shown represent a properly created "emergency corridor"?
q-10720.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The emergency corridor runs between the far left lane and the lane next to it: vehicles in the left lane stand as close as possible to the left edge, and all the others as close as possible to the right. It is formed as soon as traffic slows down considerably.

q-10721.text: In the presented situation, can the yellow road assistance vehicle taking part in the rescue operation drive on the passage for emergency vehicles?
q-10721.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Besides emergency vehicles, the passage created may also be used by vehicles taking part in the rescue operation, including roadside assistance sent to the scene. For other drivers that passage remains closed.

q-10723.text: In this situation, is the driver of vehicle 1 obliged to move away from the passage for the emergency vehicle?
q-10723.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On seeing or hearing an emergency vehicle, every driver is obliged to make its passage easier: to get out of its way and, if necessary, stop. This also applies to the vehicle travelling first in a column.

q-10724.text: In this situation, is the driver of vehicle 1 obliged to drive to the right?
q-10724.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Making way for an emergency vehicle consists above all in pulling over to the right, up to the edge of the roadway, and if necessary stopping there. The manoeuvre must be performed calmly, without braking harshly in front of others.

q-10730.text: Have the drivers of these vehicles facilitated the free passage of emergency vehicles by creating the so-called "emergency corridor"?
q-10730.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The drivers have positioned their vehicles so that a continuous clear passage has formed between the far left lane and the one next to it. Such a corridor is formed in advance, when traffic stops or slows considerably, not only at the emergency vehicle's signal.

q-10731.text: By stopping at this spot, has the driver of the truck complied with the existing regulations?
q-10731.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping at this place closes the passage prepared for the emergency vehicle. The lorry driver should move as far as possible towards the edge of their lane and stop only there, leaving free space.

q-10732.text: Did the drivers clear the way for the emergency vehicle in accordance with applicable regulations?
q-10732.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Getting out of the way means moving as far as possible towards the edge and leaving a continuous clear lane along the whole length of the jam. Here the passage remains broken, so the emergency vehicle has to slow down or manoeuvre.

q-10737.text: Is the driver obliged to apply the so-called "zipper merge" when there is no significant speed reduction ?
q-10737.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The "zipper" rule applies only in conditions of significantly reduced speed, in a jam or slowly moving traffic. When traffic is flowing, a lane change takes place under the general rules, giving way to those travelling in the target lane.

q-10753.text: In this situation, are you allowed to turn right at the crossroads?
q-10753.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal visible in the material permits travel to the right, so performing this manoeuvre is allowed. When turning, you must watch pedestrians and vehicles on the road you are entering and give way to them if necessary.

q-10754.text: In the present situation, are you obliged to be particularly careful?
q-10754.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material increases the risk, so it requires particular caution: close observation of the surroundings, heightened attention and readiness to react immediately, up to stopping the vehicle. Ordinary caution is not enough in such circumstances.

q-10756.text: Are you allowed to park in the marked areas for disabled people, if the parking time does not exceed 15 minutes?
q-10756.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Spaces designated for disabled people are reserved for entitled holders of a valid parking card, and the length of the stay makes no difference. Even a short stop without entitlement is an offence and risks a fine and the vehicle being towed away.

q-10757.text: Are you allowed to park on the marked parking areas for disabled people, if your parking ticket expired?

options.A: Yes, unless the time period since that didn't exceed 7 days.
options.B: Yes, unless the time period since that didn't exceed 14 days.

q-10757.explanation: Correct answer: C. The right to park in a space for disabled people is given solely by a valid parking card placed behind the windscreen. Once its validity expires the entitlement disappears at once — there is no transitional period counted in days.

q-10761.text: Are you allowed to drive within "emergency corridor" created by other drivers, if you are driving a single-track vehicle?
q-10761.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The clear passage is intended solely for emergency vehicles and vehicles taking part in the rescue operation. Neither a motorcyclist nor a moped rider has the right to use it, even though physically they fit between the columns of vehicles.

q-10762.text: Are you obliged to near the right edge of the way, to allow the emergency vehicle, coming from behind, to pass?
q-10762.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The driver is obliged to make way for an emergency vehicle: move towards the right edge of the roadway and, if necessary, stop. The manoeuvre is performed smoothly, without harsh braking and without entering the pedestrian crossing.

q-10767.text: Does the signal mean that in a while the green signal comes on?
q-10767.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown announces that the green light is about to come on and lets you prepare the vehicle to move off. It does not yet permit passing the traffic light — you may move off only after the green signal appears.

q-10768.text: Does the signal mean that in a while the red signal comes on?
q-10768.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown announces that the green light, not the red one, is about to come on — it informs of the approaching permission to go. Until green appears, passing the traffic light is still prohibited.

q-10779.text: In the present situation, is the driver allowed to switch on the driving beam?
q-10779.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle other road users — the driver of an oncoming vehicle, one travelling ahead, and also a pedestrian. In such conditions you drive on dipped headlights.

q-10793.text: If you are driving an overnormative vehicle, shall you carry and show to authorised personal the passing permission?

options.C: It depends on the permission's content.

q-10793.explanation: Correct answer: A. A journey by an oversize vehicle is allowed only on the basis of a permit of the appropriate category, so the document must be in the vehicle while driving. The driver shows it at the request of persons authorised to carry out checks.

q-10794.text: If you are driving an overnormative vehicle with the total laden weight over 80 t, are you obliged to be piloted by two assisting pilot vehicles?

options.C: Yes, but only in time period between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.

q-10794.explanation: Correct answer: A. With an actual total mass above 80 tonnes the journey requires piloting by two pilot vehicles — one in front of the combination, the other behind it. This duty covers the whole route, regardless of the time of day.

q-10795.text: If you are driving an overnormative vehicle with the width exceeding 3,6 m, are you obliged to be piloted by two assisting pilot vehicles?

options.C: yes, but only in the time period 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.

q-10795.explanation: Correct answer: A. A width over 3.6 m means the vehicle occupies more than one lane, so two pilot vehicles are required — in front and behind. Piloting applies throughout the journey, in daytime too.

q-10796.text: If you are driving an overnormative vehicle with the length exceeding 30 m, are you obliged to be piloted by two assisting pilot vehicles?

options.C: yes, but only in the time period 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.

q-10796.explanation: Correct answer: A. A combination longer than 30 m needs a very long stretch to be overtaken and to cross a junction, so it must be piloted by two vehicles — a leading and a closing one. The rule applies at any time.

q-10797.text: If you are driving an overnormative vehicle with the total laden weight exceeding 60 t, are you obliged to be piloted by assisting pilot vehicles?

options.C: yes, but only in the time period 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.

q-10797.explanation: Correct answer: A. Exceeding an actual total mass of 60 tonnes gives rise to a duty to pilot the journey. The pilot warns other drivers and leads the combination through difficult places, and the duty is not limited to night hours.

q-10798.text: If you are driving an overnormative vehicle with the width exceeding 3,2 m, are you obliged to be piloted by assisting pilot vehicles?

options.C: yes, but only in the time period 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.

q-10798.explanation: Correct answer: A. A width exceeding 3.2 m gives rise to a duty to pilot the journey. Such a vehicle does not fit in a typical lane, so the pilot must warn other drivers regardless of the time of day.

q-10799.text: If you are driving an overnormative vehicle with the length exceeding 23 m, are you obliged to be piloted by assisting pilot vehicles?

options.C: yes, but only in the time period 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.

q-10799.explanation: Correct answer: A. A length over 23 m means a duty to pilot the journey. So long a combination takes up a lot of room on curves and at junctions, and the pilot warns other drivers at any time of day.

q-10800.text: If you are driving an overnormative vehicle, are you obliged to comply with the passing conditions enumerated in the permission of the category given?

options.C: yes, but only when the load is divisable

q-10800.explanation: Correct answer: A. The permit specifies, among other things, the route, the permitted vehicle parameters, the time of the journey and the manner of piloting, and the driver must comply with all of them. Whether the load is divisible is of no significance here.

q-10801.text: If you are driving an overnormative vehicle, are you obliged to be especially careful?

options.C: yes, but only in the time period 10 p.m. to 5 a.m.

q-10801.explanation: Correct answer: A. An oversize vehicle is large, heavy and has a long braking distance, so its driver must take special care throughout the journey. The duty does not depend on the time of day or the density of traffic.

q-10802.text: If you are driving a vehicle group with the height exceeding 4 m, do you need a permission?

options.C: yes, but only if the load is divisible

q-10802.explanation: Correct answer: A. Exceeding a height of 4 m makes the combination an oversize vehicle, and its journey requires a permit of the appropriate category. This follows from clearance limits under flyovers, bridges and overhead lines; the divisibility of the load does not release you from the duty.

q-10804.text: If you are driving a vehicle with the total laden weight 50 t or more, shall you have the passing permission for the overnormative vehicle of the category given?

options.C: yes, but only on national roads

q-10804.explanation: Correct answer: A. An actual total mass of 50 tonnes or more exceeds the values permitted for ordinary traffic, so the journey takes place solely on the basis of a permit of the appropriate category. The duty applies to all roads, not only national ones.

q-10805.text: Are you obliged to follow instructions or signs given by the pilot of the overnormative vehicle?
q-10805.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The pilot of an oversize vehicle has the right to give instructions and signals to other road users, and they must comply with them. The pilot's instructions take precedence over signs and traffic lights on the section concerned.

q-10806.text: Carrying a child in a rearward-facing safety seat mounted on the front seat of a motor vehicle equipped with a passenger airbag is:

options.C: permitted if the airbag is disabled during transport.

q-10806.explanation: Correct answer: C. A rear-facing child seat may be placed on the front seat only when the passenger airbag is switched off. An inflating airbag would strike the back of the child seat, that is, the child's head, with enormous force.

q-10807.text: Carrying a child seated in a rear-facing position in a child restraint system fitted in the front seat of a vehicle equipped with an airbag is:

options.A: Permissible if the airbag is not enabled during transport.

q-10807.explanation: Correct answer: A. Carrying a child rear-facing on the front seat is permitted only with the airbag switched off. The airbag deploys at great speed and would strike the back of the restraint, endangering the child's life.

q-10808.text: Transporting a child under the age of 3 in a passenger car is:

options.A: Permitted if the vehicle is not fitted with safety belts.
options.B: Permitted if the vehicle is fitted with safety belts and a child safety seat.

q-10808.explanation: Correct answer: B. A child under 3 may be carried in a car only when the vehicle has seat belts and the child is placed in a child seat or another restraint matched to its height and weight.

q-10809.text: Carrying a child under the age of three in a passenger car not equipped with a seat belt and a child safety seat or with a seat belt and other child restraint is:

options.C: Permitted, if the child is held in the arms of an adult passenger.

q-10809.explanation: Correct answer: A. Without seat belts and a child seat or another restraint, carrying a child under three is prohibited. Holding the child in your arms is no substitute for a child seat — in a collision an adult is unable to hold on to it.

q-10810.text: Transporting a child in the front seat of a car without a child safety seat is:

options.A: Prohibited if the child is less than 150 cm tall.
options.C: Permitted if the child is not less than 140 cm tall.

q-10810.explanation: Correct answer: A. The threshold is a height of 150 cm: a shorter child must travel in a child seat or another restraint, on the front seat too. A taller child may use the seat belts alone, and age is of no significance here.

q-10811.text: The obligation to use seat belts:

options.A: Applies to the driver of a taxi when transporting a passenger.
options.B: Does not apply to a child under 3 years old transported by bus.
options.C: Applies to a woman with a visible pregnancy.

q-10811.explanation: Correct answer: B. Exempt from the duty to fasten seat belts is, among others, a child under 3 carried in a bus. A taxi driver while carrying a passenger and a woman who is visibly pregnant are exempt from this duty, so the other answers are wrong.

q-10812.text: A child less than 150 cm tall, transported in a passenger car equipped with seatbelts, should be seated in a child safety seat appropriate to:

options.A: The weight and height of the child and the appropriate technical conditions specified in EU legislation.
options.B: The weight and height of the child.

q-10812.explanation: Correct answer: A. A child seat is matched to the child's weight and height, and in addition must meet the technical conditions laid down in EU rules, which is confirmed by the approval mark on the label. The child's age alone is not a criterion here.

q-10813.text: If two children are being transported in the rear seat of a passenger car in safety seats and it is not possible to install a third safety seat, then:

options.A: It is impossible to transport the third child.
options.B: The third child may be transported if it is at least 3 years old and is restrained by means of a seat belt.
options.C: The third child may be transported if it is at least 5 years old.

q-10813.explanation: Correct answer: B. When two child seats occupy the rear seat and a third physically does not fit, a third child may be carried on the rear seat in the seat belts alone, provided it is at least 3 years old.

q-10814.text: Transporting a child restrained by a seatbelt in the rear seat of a passenger car is:

options.A: Permissible if the child is at least 135 cm tall and it is impossible to provide the child with a safety seat because of its height and weight.
options.C: Permitted if the child is at least 125 cm tall and it is impossible to provide the child with a safety seat because of its height and weight.

q-10814.explanation: Correct answer: A. The exception concerns a child at least 135 cm tall for whom, because of height and weight, no suitable child seat can be found — it then travels on the rear seat secured with the seat belts alone.

q-10815.text: Child safety seats and other child restraints must be installed in the vehicle:

options.A: in a safe and aesthetic manner.
options.B: so as to allow easy access to the child.
options.C: according to the recommendations of the device manufacturer.

q-10815.explanation: Correct answer: C. A child restraint protects the child only when it has been fitted exactly as the manufacturer intended — facing the indicated direction, with the belts or anchorages routed correctly. Looks and convenient access to the child are not the criteria.

q-10816.text: A police officer will retain a driver's licence subject to a receipt upon detection of an act of:

options.A: driving at a speed exceeding the permitted 50 km/h in a built-up area.
options.B: driving at a speed exceeding the permitted speed by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area.
options.C: driving at a speed exceeding the permitted 50 km/h outside a built-up area.

q-10816.explanation: Correct answer: B. A driving licence is taken away against a receipt when the driver exceeds the permitted speed by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. Exceeding it by exactly 50 km/h, or the same excess outside a built-up area, does not result in the document being taken.

q-10818.text: A retention receipt for a driving licence issued in the country for exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area shall entitle the driver to drive the vehicle for:

options.A: 7 days from the date of its retention.
options.B: 72 hours from the moment of its retention.
options.C: 24 hours from the moment of its retention.

q-10818.explanation: Correct answer: C. The receipt for a retained national driving licence allows you to drive a vehicle for only 24 hours from the moment of retention. After that time, driving on means driving without the required entitlement.

q-10819.text: The starost will issue an administrative decision to withhold a driving license where a driver has exceeded the speed limit by:

options.A: more than 50 km/h in a built-up area.

q-10819.explanation: Correct answer: A. The administrative decision to retain a driving licence is issued when the permitted speed is exceeded by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. Outside a built-up area such an excess results in a fine and points, but not in that decision.

q-10822.text: Where a driver has exceeded the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area, the starost shall issue an administrative decision to withhold the driving licence for:
q-10822.explanation: Correct answer: C. For exceeding the permitted speed by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area, the driving licence is retained for 3 months. That period runs from the actual surrender of the document, and driving despite the ban extends it.

q-10825.text: A police officer shall retain a driving licence issued by a state other than the Republic of Poland, against a receipt, if proven that the passenger car transports:

options.A: 1 person more than specified in the registration document.
options.B: 3 persons more than specified in the registration document.
options.C: 2 persons more than specified in the registration document.

q-10825.explanation: Correct answer: B. A foreign driving licence is retained against a receipt when a car has been carrying 3 people more than the registration document indicates. A smaller excess of passengers is punished but does not result in the document being retained.

q-10826.text: The driver of a vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland is obliged to carry and present a document for inspection:

options.A: Acknowledging the conclusion of compulsory third party liability insurance.
options.B: Acknowledging approval of the vehicle for traffic use.
