options.C: Confirming the calibration of the alcohol interlock, if the obligation to have such interlock is indicated in the driving licence.

q-10826.explanation: Correct answer: C. The checking authority verifies the vehicle's admission to traffic and its third-party insurance in the registers, so those documents need not be carried. A driver whose licence carries an alcohol-interlock requirement must, however, have with them confirmation of its calibration.

q-10827.text: The driver of a vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland is obliged to carry and present at the request of a competent authority:

options.A: A driving licence retention receipt or a temporary permit.
options.B: A document stating the vehicle's roadworthiness.
options.C: A document confirming the conclusion of a third-party liability insurance contract for the vehicle owner.

q-10827.explanation: Correct answer: A. If the registration document or the temporary permit has been retained, the driver carries the receipt for that retention and shows it for a check. The registration document itself and the third-party policy need not be carried.

q-10828.text: The obligation to carry a driving licence, issued on the territory of the Republic of Poland, applies to:

options.B: The driver of a passenger car.
options.C: There is no such obligation, regardless of the type of vehicle being driven.

q-10828.explanation: Correct answer: C. Driving entitlements issued in Poland are visible in the central register, so a national driving licence need not be carried or shown. This does not, however, release you from the duty to actually hold valid entitlements.

q-10829.text: The document certifying that a vehicle is approved for traffic is:
q-10829.explanation: Correct answer: A. A vehicle's admission to traffic is confirmed by the registration document, in which the result of the technical inspection is recorded. The vehicle card documents its history, and the control sticker on the window admits nothing by itself.

q-10832.text: A police officer will retain the vehicle registration document if it is found that:

options.A: The technical inspection was carried out by an unauthorised entity.
options.B: The vehicle has faulty registration plate lighting.
options.C: The driver does not have a registration document while driving.

q-10832.explanation: Correct answer: A. An inspection carried out by an unauthorised unit is invalid, so the vehicle is treated as not admitted to traffic and the registration document is subject to retention. A faulty number-plate light is a minor fault, and the document need not be carried anyway.

q-10833.text: Keeping registration plates in good condition and ensuring their legibility:

options.A: Is not obligatory, it is only due to care for the aesthetic condition of the vehicle.
options.B: Is the responsibility of the driver.
options.C: Is the responsibility of the vehicle owner.

q-10833.explanation: Correct answer: B. It is the driver who is responsible for the plates being legible and clean at the moment of driving — mud or snow must be removed before moving off. An illegible plate makes it impossible to identify the vehicle and is an offence.

q-10834.text: The driver of a vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland is obliged to carry and present at the request of a competent authority:

options.A: A document certifying the right to drive.
options.B: A document certifying the right to drive a vehicle other than a national driving licence.
options.C: A document certifying to the vehicle's roadworthiness.

q-10834.explanation: Correct answer: B. A national driving licence need not be carried, because the entitlement is visible in the register. If, however, the driver relies on another document entitling them to drive, for example one issued abroad, they must have it with them and show it.

q-10835.text: The driver of a vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland and possessing a driving licence issued by the authorities of the Republic of Poland is obliged to carry and present at the request of a competent authority:

options.A: A valid driving licence retention receipt.
options.B: A document certifying to the right to drive.
options.C: A proof of payment of the premium for the compulsory civil liability insurance of the vehicle owner.

q-10835.explanation: Correct answer: A. When the driving licence has been retained, the driver drives on the basis of the receipt and must have it with them for the whole of its validity. The driving licence itself and proof of payment of the third-party premium need not be carried.

q-10836.text: The driver of a vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland who holds a driving licence issued by the authorities of the Republic of Poland is obliged to carry and present at the request of a competent authority:

options.A: A proof of payment of the premium for the compulsory civil liability insurance of the vehicle owner.
options.B: A document certifying to the right to drive.
options.C: Other documents, if such an obligation results from a separate legislation.

q-10836.explanation: Correct answer: C. Apart from the documents under the road traffic rules, the driver must carry those required by other acts, for example concerning road haulage or the carriage of dangerous goods. A national driving licence and proof of payment of the third-party premium need not be carried.

q-10837.text: A vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland is removed from the road at the owner's expense if:

options.A: The vehicle is left in a prohibited place and does not jeopardise safety.
options.B: The driver fails to present a document confirming the conclusion of a civil liability contract.
options.C: It is driven by a person unauthorised to drive and where it is impossible to secure the vehicle by handing it over to the person inside the vehicle who is authorised to drive it.

q-10837.explanation: Correct answer: C. The vehicle is towed away at the owner's expense when it was driven by a person without entitlement and there is nobody to hand the driving over to — nobody in the car holds the appropriate entitlement. Further driving of such a vehicle would be a direct hazard.

q-10838.text: The driver of a passenger car registered abroad and participating in road traffic on the territory of the Republic of Poland is obliged to carry and present at the request of a competent authority:

options.A: A document acknowledging the right to drive a vehicle other than a national driving licence.
options.B: Passport issued by the country in which the vehicle is registered.
options.C: a document confirming completion of the technical inspection.

q-10838.explanation: Correct answer: A. The exemption from carrying the document concerns only a national driving licence visible in the Polish register. A driver relying on an entitlement issued elsewhere must have that document with them and show it on request.

q-10839.text: The driver of a vehicle performing a test drive using a professional registration document is obliged to carry and present at the request of a competent authority:

options.A: A document confirming the right to drive a vehicle, issued on the territory of Poland.
options.B: A document confirming the vehicle's roadworthiness.
options.C: Proof of payment of the premium for compulsory third party insurance.

q-10839.explanation: Correct answer: B. During a test drive the vehicle is not registered under the ordinary rules, so the driver must carry the document admitting it to traffic, that is, the professional registration document together with the form. A national driving licence need not be shown.

q-10840.text: How do you transport a child less than 150 cm tall in the front seat of a five-seater passenger car?

options.B: In a safety seat or other child restraint system.
options.C: In a rear-facing safety seat if the vehicle has an active passenger airbag.

q-10840.explanation: Correct answer: B. A child under 150 cm tall is carried in a child seat or another restraint matched to its height and weight. Holding it on a lap is prohibited, and a rear-facing seat requires the airbag to be switched off.

q-10841.text: The driver of a vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland and possessing the rights issued by the authorities of the Republic of Poland is obliged to carry and present at the request of a competent authority:

options.A: A document confirming the vehicle's roadworthiness.
options.B: A document attesting to the right to drive.
options.C: A certificate attesting to a successful technical inspection in terms of equipping the vehicle with an alcohol interlock.

q-10841.explanation: Correct answer: C. A driver whose entitlement has been restricted to vehicles with an alcohol interlock must carry a certificate of a positive technical check of that interlock. A national driving licence or the registration document need not be shown.

q-10842.text: They lack of a driving licence issued in Poland when driving a passenger car on public roads in Poland:

options.A: Does not result in any legal ramifications.
options.B: Results in the imposition of a penalty notice.
options.C: Results in a request for punishment.

q-10842.explanation: Correct answer: A. A driver who holds a driving licence issued in Poland does not have to carry it — the person checking verifies their entitlements in the central register. Not having the document on you therefore carries no penalty by itself.

q-10843.text: The driver of a vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland and possessing the rights issued by the authorities of the Republic of Poland is obliged to carry and present at the request of a competent authority:

options.B: A document confirming the calibration of the alcohol interlock if the obligation to have an alcohol interlock results from the driver's licence.
options.C: A document certifying the right to drive.

q-10843.explanation: Correct answer: B. A national driving licence and the registration document of a Polish vehicle need not be carried, because the data are checked in the registers. What must be carried is the document on the calibration of the alcohol interlock, if the duty to use one follows from the driving licence.

q-10844.text: What is a police officer entitled to during traffic control?

options.A: To establish the identity of the vehicle's driver based on data from the National Identification Register.
options.B: To request the driver to provide a driving licence issued in the country.
options.C: To request the driver presents a document confirming the conclusion of a civil liability contract for a vehicle registered in the territory of Poland.

q-10844.explanation: Correct answer: A. A police officer may establish the driver's identity from data in the state registers, including the identity-card register. They may not, however, demand a national driving licence or the third-party policy of a Polish vehicle, because they check that information electronically.

q-10846.text: Can you drive straight ahead through the crossroads in this situation?
q-10846.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign or signal shown in the material does not permit crossing the junction straight ahead. A clear road changes nothing here — you may go only in the permitted direction, or once the signal changes to a permitting one.

q-10847.text: Will you be merging into traffic if you move, once the signal changes to green?
q-10847.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Joining the traffic is entering the road from premises, a pavement, a car park or an unsurfaced road, and moving off after a stop not forced by traffic conditions. Moving off at a green light is continuing an interrupted journey.

q-10848.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-10848.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-10849.text: Does this signal permit a right turn at the intersection?
q-10849.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible signal does not permit a right turn — you may go in that direction only once the signal for that direction permits it. Until then you wait before the conditional stop line or the signal head.

q-10851.text: Can you turn right in this situation?
q-10851.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign or signal shown in the material prohibits a right turn at this place. Even a clear road does not entitle you to carry out the manoeuvre against such an indication, so you must go in the permitted direction.

q-10852.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise utmost caution?
q-10852.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-10853.text: Can you turn right in this situation?
q-10853.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign or signal shown in the material permits a right turn. Before the manoeuvre, take up position at the right edge of the carriageway in advance, signal your intention with the indicator and give way to pedestrians and cyclists crossing the road you are entering.

q-10854.text: Will a red signal light up after these signals?
q-10854.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The order of the signals is fixed: after red shown together with amber comes green, which permits entry. Red will appear only later, after the amber that ends the green phase.

q-10855.text: Will the green signal light up after these signals?
q-10855.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Red shown at the same time as amber means that green is about to come on. It is a signal to prepare to move — you may move off only once green appears.

q-10856.text: Should the driver prepare to resume driving in this situation?
q-10856.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Red together with amber gives notice that green is about to come on, so the driver prepares to move off. The conditional stop line may, however, be crossed only once the green signal appears.

q-10857.text: In this situation, can you drive straight ahead through the intersection?
q-10857.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign or signal shown in the material permits crossing the junction straight ahead. Before entering, still make sure there is room to stop beyond the junction, and let through those finishing their passage.

q-10858.text: Does this signal permit you to turn right at a crossroads?
q-10858.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible signal permits travel in the direction of a right turn. Before the manoeuvre, take up position at the right edge of the carriageway, signal your intention with the indicator and give way to pedestrians and cyclists crossing the road you are entering.

q-10859.text: In this situation, if you are going to turn right at the intersection, are you obliged to stop before the signaling device?
q-10859.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown in the material permits going right, so stopping before the signal head is not required. The duty to stop concerns a red signal and a conditional green arrow.

q-10860.text: In this situation, are you merging into traffic when you drive off the pavement?
q-10860.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Driving off the pavement onto the carriageway is joining the traffic. You must then take special care and give way to all other road users, cyclists and pedestrians included.

q-10861.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution when merging into the traffic?
q-10861.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When joining the traffic, the driver must take special care: watch the surroundings attentively and be ready to react immediately. At the same time they give way to all other road users.

q-10862.text: Are you obliged to yield the right of way to other road users when merging into the traffic?
q-10862.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver joining the traffic has no priority — they must give way to all other road users and not force them to change speed or direction. Special care is required of them in addition.

q-10863.text: Are you merging into traffic in this situation?
q-10863.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Joining the traffic is entering the road from premises, a pavement, a car park or an unsurfaced road. Continuing along the same road, including after a stop forced by traffic conditions, is not such a manoeuvre.

q-10864.text: When turning left at this junction, are you obliged to give priority to vehicles approaching from the right?
q-10864.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a junction where priority is not defined by signs, the right-hand rule applies — the one approaching from the right has priority. A left turn does not lift that rule, so such vehicles must be given way.

q-10865.text: When turning left at the intersection, do you have the right of way over vehicles approaching from the right?
q-10865.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a junction of equal roads the vehicle approaching from the right has priority. Turning left, you must let it through, and also give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction going straight ahead or turning right.

q-10866.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-10866.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-10868.text: In this situation, are you approaching an intersection where priority is not indicated by road signs?
q-10868.explanation: Correct answer: YES. There are no signs before this junction establishing priority, so it is a junction of equal roads. The right-hand rule then applies: you must give way to the vehicle approaching from the right.

q-10869.text: How do you transport a child less than 150 cm tall in a passenger car with five seating places?

options.A: In the front seat without a safety seat or other child restraint system.
options.B: In the front seat in a child restraint other than a safety seat.
options.C: In the rear seat without the seat belt fastened.

q-10869.explanation: Correct answer: B. A child shorter than 150 cm is carried in a child seat or in another restraint matched to its weight and height. Such a device may also be placed on the front seat; carrying the child without one, or without belts fastened, is prohibited.

q-10870.text: In this situation, when turning left at the intersection, do you have priority over vehicles approaching from the right?
q-10870.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When priority is not defined by signs, the right-hand rule applies at the junction. A driver turning left gives way to vehicles approaching from the right, and also to those coming from the opposite direction going straight ahead or turning right.

q-10871.text: How do you install a child safety seat in your vehicle?

options.A: In a way that is comfortable for the child.
options.B: In a way that is convenient for you.
options.C: As recommended by the device manufacturer.

q-10871.explanation: Correct answer: C. A child seat protects the child only when it is fitted exactly according to the manufacturer's instructions: by the correct method of fastening, facing the correct direction and in a permitted seat. The comfort of the child or the driver is not a fitting criterion.

q-10872.text: How will you install a child restraint in the vehicle to transport a child?

options.B: In a way that is convenient for you.
options.C: As recommended by the device manufacturer.

q-10872.explanation: Correct answer: C. A restraint does its job only when it is fitted in the way the manufacturer indicates: with the correct fastening, orientation and place in the vehicle. The child's wishes or the driver's convenience do not decide.

q-10873.text: When turning right at this intersection, must you yield the right of way to vehicles approaching from the left?
q-10873.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a junction where priority is not defined by signs, you give way to those approaching from the right. Turning right, you do not cut across the path of vehicles from the left, so you do not give way to them.

q-10874.text: What conditions must be met by a passenger car with which you want to transport a child under the age of three?

options.A: It must be equipped with seat belts and a safety seat.
options.B: It may not have a seat belt.
options.C: It does not have to be equipped with seat belts and a safety seat.

q-10874.explanation: Correct answer: A. A child under three may be carried only in a car fitted with seat belts and only in a child seat or another restraint. Such a child may not be carried in a vehicle without belts.

q-10875.text: In this situation, when turning right at the intersection, are you obliged to yield priority to vehicles approaching from the left?
q-10875.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The right-hand rule requires giving way to those approaching from the right. A right turn does not cut across the path of vehicles approaching from the left, so they do not have priority.

q-10876.text: What should you consider when choosing a safety seat or child restraint system for transporting a child?

options.B: The appropriate technical specifications for these devices.

q-10876.explanation: Correct answer: B. A child seat or restraint must meet the technical requirements: bear the required approval marking and be matched to the child's weight and height. Looks and comfort may decide only among devices that meet those conditions.

q-10877.text: Does this sign warn of an uncontrolled intersection?
q-10877.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign gives notice of a junction where priority is not defined by signs, so the right-hand rule applies there. Slow down in advance and take special care.

q-10878.text: What conditions must be met when transporting a child in the back seat of a passenger car?

options.A: The child being carried is at least 135 cm tall and fastened only with seat belts, as the weight and height precludes carriage in a safety seat or other child restraint systems.
options.B: The child being carried is at least 125 cm tall and is only fastened with seat belts, as its weight and height precludes carriage in a safety seat.
options.C: The speed must not exceed 50 km/h.

q-10878.explanation: Correct answer: A. The rule is that a child shorter than 150 cm is carried in a child seat or another restraint. The exception concerns the rear seat: at a height of at least 135 cm, when weight and height make using a restraint impossible, seat belts are enough.

q-10879.text: When turning left at this intersection, are you obliged to give priority to vehicles that could be approaching from the right?
q-10879.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Since priority is not defined by signs, this is a junction of equal roads and the right-hand rule applies. A driver turning left cuts across the path of vehicles from the right, so they must give way to them.

q-10880.text: What conditions must you meet if you wish to carry a child in the rear seat of a passenger car?

options.A: The child being carried is at least 125 cm tall and fastened only with seat belts, as the weight and height precludes carriage in a child restraint system.
options.B: The speed must not exceed 40 km/h.
options.C: The child being carried is at least 135 cm tall and is only fastened with seat belts, as the weight and height precludes carriage in a child restraint system.

q-10880.explanation: Correct answer: C. A restraint may be dispensed with only on the rear seat and only once the child is at least 135 cm tall, when its weight and height make using such a device impossible. The child is then secured with the seat belts.

q-10881.text: When turning right at a crossroads, are you obliged to yield way to vehicles approaching from the left?
q-10881.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a junction of equal roads priority belongs to those approaching from the right, not from the left. A right turn does not conflict with their path, but you must give way to pedestrians and cyclists crossing the road you are turning into.

q-10882.text: What do you have to do to carry a three-year-old child in the rear seat of a passenger car with two children already sitting in safety seats and it is impossible to install a third safety seat?

options.A: You must secure the child with a seat belt.
options.B: You should sit the child on an adult's lap.
options.C: You must lock the rear doors to prevent them from being opened from the outside.

q-10882.explanation: Correct answer: A. When two child seats are already fitted on the rear seat and a third cannot be installed, a third child who has turned three is carried secured with the seat belts. Carrying it on an adult's lap is prohibited.

q-10883.text: What must you do if you want to carry a three-year-old child in the rear seat of a passenger car with two children already sitting in child restraints and it is impossible to install a third device?

options.A: You should provide your child with a leg stand.
options.B: You must secure your child with seat belts.
options.C: You should place your child in the middle of the rear seat.

q-10883.explanation: Correct answer: B. If two restraints already occupy the rear seat and a third cannot be fitted, a third child who has turned three travels secured with the seat belts. A footrest or the middle seat alone is no substitute.

q-10885.text: What documents are you obliged to carry with you and present at the request of the competent authorities during roadside inspections?

options.A: Confirmation of payment of the mandatory civil liability insurance.
options.B: Receipt of retention of the registration document for the period it authorises the use of the vehicle.
options.C: In all cases, a certificate indicating the car has undergone a technical inspection.

q-10885.explanation: Correct answer: B. Neither the registration document of a Polish vehicle nor the insurance policy needs to be carried, because the data are in the registers. You must, however, have with you the receipt for a retained registration document, as long as it entitles you to use the vehicle.

q-10886.text: What documents are you obliged to carry with you and present at the request of the competent authorities during roadside inspections?

options.A: Confirmation of payment of a third party insurance policy.
options.B: Receipt of temporary permission for the period it authorises to use the vehicle.
options.C: Certificate confirming that the vehicle has undergone a technical inspection, if it is powered by gas.

q-10886.explanation: Correct answer: B. You must have with you the receipt for a retained temporary permit for the period in which it entitles you to use the vehicle. Confirmation of voluntary insurance and a technical inspection certificate are not required while driving.

q-10887.text: What documents are you obliged to carry with you and present at the request of the competent authorities during roadside inspections?

options.B: Receipt of retention of the registration document for the period it authorises the use of the vehicle.
options.C: Certificate of compliance with technical specifications.

q-10887.explanation: Correct answer: B. The registration document of a Polish vehicle itself need not be carried — it is checked in the register. What is compulsory is the receipt for its retention, as long as that document entitles you to use the vehicle.

q-10888.text: What documents are you obliged to carry with you and present at the request of the competent authorities during roadside inspections?

options.A: Receipt of temporary permission for the period it authorises to use the vehicle.

q-10888.explanation: Correct answer: A. The driver carries the receipt for a retained temporary permit as long as it replaces the document admitting the vehicle to traffic. A certificate of conformity or the registration document of a Polish vehicle need not be carried.

q-10889.text: What documents must you carry with you and present at the request of a competent authority when driving a vehicle registered abroad in the territory of the Republic of Poland?

options.A: A document certifying that the vehicle is roadworthy.
options.B: A document confirming the conclusion of an accident insurance policy.
options.C: Copy of a certificate attesting to the completion of a technical inspection.

q-10889.explanation: Correct answer: A. A vehicle registered abroad is not visible in the Polish registers, so the driver must carry the document admitting it to traffic and show it on request. Personal accident insurance is voluntary and not required.

q-10890.text: What documents are you obliged to carry with you and present at the request of a competent authority when driving a vehicle registered abroad in the territory of the Republic of Poland?

options.B: Document confirming the conclusion of a compulsory civil liability insurance contract by the vehicle owner.
options.C: A document confirming payment of the stamp duty.

q-10890.explanation: Correct answer: B. With a vehicle registered abroad, the Polish services cannot check the insurance in their system, so the driver carries the document confirming compulsory third-party insurance. Proof of ownership and stamp duty are irrelevant here.

q-10891.text: What documents are you obliged to carry with you and present at the request of a competent authority when driving a vehicle registered abroad in the territory of the Republic of Poland?

options.B: Proof of payment of the premium for the compulsory civil liability insurance.
options.C: A document confirming payment for the use of motorways and expressways.

q-10891.explanation: Correct answer: B. When driving a vehicle registered abroad, you must have with you proof of payment of the compulsory third-party insurance premium. Road tolls are settled separately and are not the subject of this duty.

q-10892.text: What documents do you have to carry with you and present at the request of the relevant authority during a roadside inspection?

options.B: A different document certifying the right to drive other than a national driving licence.

q-10892.explanation: Correct answer: B. A national driving licence need not be carried, because the entitlements are in the register. If, however, you drive on the basis of another document confirming entitlement, for example one issued abroad, you must have it with you.

q-10893.text: What documents are you obliged to carry with you and present at the request of the relevant authority during roadside inspections?

options.A: A medical certificate if you are involved in commercial passenger transport.
options.B: A driving license retention receipt for the period it permits the driver to drive.

q-10893.explanation: Correct answer: B. When a driving licence has been retained, the document entitling you to drive is the receipt, and you must have it with you for the period in which it entitles you to drive. Medical and psychological certificates are not carried by the driver.

q-10894.text: What documents are you obliged to carry with you and present at the request of the relevant authority during roadside inspections?

options.A: A psychological fitness certificate if you are involved in commercial passenger transport.
options.B: A driving licence retention receipt for the period it permits the driver to drive.

q-10894.explanation: Correct answer: B. You must have with you the receipt for a retained driving licence for the period in which it entitles you to drive the vehicle. The psychological and medical certificates are kept outside the vehicle — they are not needed for a roadside check.

q-10895.text: What document are you obliged to carry with you and present at the request of a competent authority?

options.A: Proof of participation in a pre-qualification training course.
options.B: A document certifying the right to drive a vehicle other than a national driving licence.
options.C: Document confirming the completion of pre-medical first aid training.

q-10895.explanation: Correct answer: B. The duty to carry applies to a document confirming entitlement to drive other than a national driving licence, because only national entitlements appear in the register. Course certificates are not required while driving.

q-10898.text: For which road traffic violation will a police officer withhold a driving licence?

options.A: For overtaking in violation of the single continuous line.
options.B: For transporting two passengers in excess of the number of seats specified in the passenger car registration document.
options.C: For overtaking at a railway crossing.

q-10898.explanation: Correct answer: B. Carrying a number of people exceeding by two the number of seats entered in the registration document results in the driving licence being retained. The other breaches listed are punished with a fine and points, but the document itself is not taken for them.

q-10899.text: For which road traffic violation will a police officer retain a driving licence?

options.A: For overtaking before the pedestrian crossing where traffic is directed.
options.B: For transporting two passengers in excess of the number of seats specified in the temporary permit of a passenger car.
options.C: For overtaking at crossings for cyclists.

q-10899.explanation: Correct answer: B. The driving licence is retained when the number of people carried exceeds by two the number of seats specified in the temporary permit. The other behaviours listed end in a fine and points, not in the document being taken.

q-10900.text: In this situation, are you on a road with right of way?
q-10900.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority on a road follows solely from the appropriate sign, and the road you are on is not marked with it. You must therefore reckon with the right-hand rule or with a duty to give way.

q-10901.text: In this situation, are you approaching a road with the right of way?
q-10901.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The marking shown in the material announces a road that has priority, so you are on a minor road. Before entering, you must give way to vehicles travelling on the road with priority.

q-10902.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop before the stop line?
q-10902.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop follows from the sign or signal shown in the material and concerns the place before the stop line. The vehicle must be brought to a halt even when the cross road appears empty.

q-10903.text: In this situation, when driving straight ahead through the intersection, are you obliged to yield way to the vehicles approaching from the right?
q-10903.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority is not defined by signs here, so the right-hand rule applies. Going straight ahead gives no advantage — you must give way to the vehicle approaching from the right.

q-10904.text: In this situation, when turning right at the intersection, do you have priority over vehicles approaching from the left?
q-10904.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Entering this junction, you must give way to vehicles travelling on the side road, so you have no advantage over those approaching from the left. A right turn does not lift that duty.

q-10905.text: In this situation, when turning left at the crossroads, do you have priority over vehicles approaching from the opposite direction?
q-10905.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Turning left, you cut across the path of vehicles coming from the opposite direction, so you must let them through. The rule applies regardless of whether the road has priority or is a minor road.

q-10906.text: When turning right in this situation, do you have the right of way?
q-10906.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing at this place grants priority to the road you are on, so when turning right you do not give way to vehicles from the side road. You must, however, let through pedestrians and cyclists crossing the road you are turning into.

q-10907.text: In this situation, are you on a road with right of way?
q-10907.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority on a road follows solely from the appropriate sign, and the road you are on is not marked with it. You must therefore reckon with the right-hand rule or with a duty to give way.

q-10908.text: In this situation, when turning right at an intersection, are you obliged to yield way to vehicles approaching from the left?
q-10908.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Your road is the minor one here, so before entering the junction you give way to everyone travelling on the road with priority, including those from the left. A right turn does not release you from that duty.

q-10909.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to vehicles moving on a circular traffic intersection?
q-10909.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Entering this roundabout is preceded by a duty to give way, so you let through the vehicles already travelling on its carriageway. You may join only when the manoeuvre will not force them to brake.

q-10911.text: In this situation, are you on a side road?
q-10911.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The road you are on is not marked as a minor road, so no duty to give way rests on you before this junction. Even so, watch the vehicles entering from the side road.

q-10912.text: In this situation, are you on a road with the right of way?
q-10912.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority on a road follows solely from the appropriate sign, and the road you are on is not marked with it. You must therefore reckon with the right-hand rule or with a duty to give way.

q-10913.text: When turning left at an intersection, are you obliged to give the right of way to vehicles that could approach from the right?
q-10913.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority is not established by signs here, so the junction is one of equal roads and is governed by the right-hand rule. Turning left, you give way to vehicles from the right and to those coming from the opposite direction going straight ahead or turning right.

q-10914.text: In this situation, when turning right at the intersection, do you have priority over vehicles coming from the left?
q-10914.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Before this junction you must give way to vehicles travelling on the side road, so you have no advantage over those approaching from the left. The direction of your turn changes nothing in that order.

q-10915.text: When you see this signal, can you continue driving straight ahead through an intersection?
q-10915.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible signal permits going straight ahead across the junction. You may enter, however, only when there is room to stop beyond the junction and once you have let through those finishing their passage.

q-10916.text: Does this signal allow you to turn right at an intersection from the right lane?
q-10916.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal permits a right turn made from the right lane. The manoeuvre must be preceded by signalling with the indicator, and pedestrians and cyclists crossing the side road must be given way.

q-10917.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-10917.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-10918.text: In this situation, can you drive straight ahead through the intersection?
q-10918.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign or signal shown in the material does not permit crossing the junction straight ahead. A clear road changes nothing here — you may go only in the permitted direction, or once the signal changes to a permitting one.

q-10919.text: Prior to turning right, do you have to stop before the traffic light to ensure that you do not obstruct other traffic participants?
q-10919.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A conditional green arrow allows you to turn only after the vehicle has come to a complete stop before the signal head. After stopping, you must give way to vehicles and pedestrians and not obstruct them.

q-10920.text: In this situation, if you want to turn right at the intersection, are you obliged to stop the vehicle before the traffic light?
q-10920.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The right turn here is permitted on a conditional basis, so the vehicle must first be stopped before the signal head. Only then, giving way, may the manoeuvre be carried out.

q-10921.text: In this situation, when turning right at the intersection, do you have the right of way over vehicles approaching from the left?
q-10921.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority here belongs to the vehicles travelling on the side road, and you must give way to them, including those from the left. Turning right, you enter only when you will not force them to brake.

q-10922.text: In this situation, can you turn right at the intersection?
q-10922.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown in the material does not permit a right turn, so the manoeuvre may not be carried out. Stop before the stop line or the signal head and wait for the permitting signal.

q-10923.text: Does this signal permit you to drive straight ahead through the intersection?
q-10923.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible signal does not concern going straight ahead, so you may not enter the junction in that direction. You may go only in the direction for which the signal head gives permission.

q-10924.text: In this situation, can you turn right at the intersection without stopping the vehicle?
q-10924.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal permits a right turn without stopping, because the duty to stop arises only with a red signal or a conditional green arrow. You must, however, let through pedestrians and cyclists on the side road.

q-10925.text: In this situation, when turning right at the intersection, are you obliged to yield way to vehicles approaching from the left?
q-10925.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The right-hand rule requires giving way to those approaching from the right. A right turn does not cut across the path of vehicles approaching from the left, so they do not have priority.

q-10926.text: In this situation, if you want to turn right at the intersection, are you obliged to stop before the traffic light?
q-10926.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal permits going right, so stopping before the signal head is not required. The duty to stop arises at a red signal or at a conditional green arrow.

q-10927.text: Does this signal permit you to drive straight through the intersection?
q-10927.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal does not cover the straight-ahead direction, so crossing the junction in that direction is prohibited. Stop before the stop line and wait for the signal for that direction.

q-10928.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise extreme caution when turning right?
q-10928.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When changing direction, the driver must take special care, because they cut across the path of pedestrians and cyclists. They must also take up the correct position on the carriageway in advance and signal the manoeuvre.

q-10929.text: In this situation, when turning right at the intersection, are you obliged to stop before the traffic signal?
q-10929.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal shown in the material permits a right turn, so stopping before the signal head is not compulsory. You must stop at a red signal and when the turn is permitted by a conditional green arrow.

q-10930.text: What is the validity of a Polish driving licence retention receipt issued to you by a police officer for exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area?
q-10930.explanation: Correct answer: B. In such a case the receipt for a retained national driving licence entitles you to drive for a further 24 hours. After that time, driving on is already driving without entitlement.

q-10931.text: What is the validity period of a driving licence retention receipt issued by a police officer for transporting two passengers in excess of the number of seats specified in the passenger car registration document?
q-10931.explanation: Correct answer: B. Also when the licence is retained for carrying too many people, the receipt allows you to drive the vehicle for 24 hours. After that the document must be recovered, and driving without it is driving without entitlement.

q-10933.text: Is overtaking allowed at this intersection?
q-10933.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban on overtaking a motor vehicle at a junction does not apply at a roundabout or where traffic is directed by signals or by an authorised person. The manoeuvre is then allowed, but still requires making sure the road is clear.

q-10937.text: Is it permissible to overtake other vehicles at this intersection?
q-10937.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a junction there is a ban on overtaking motor vehicles; the exception is a roundabout and a junction where traffic is directed. Here the exception does not apply, so the manoeuvre must be put off until the stretch beyond the junction.

q-10939.text: Should you keep a safe distance of at least 1 metre from the vehicle ahead when you intend to overtake it?
q-10939.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A distance of no less than 1 m applies when overtaking a bicycle, a moped, an electric scooter, a personal transporter and a pedestrian. When overtaking a motor vehicle, a safe distance is required, which the rules do not define with a specific figure.

q-10940.text: Must you always keep a safe distance from the vehicle in front of you when you intend to overtake it?
q-10940.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The overtaking driver must always keep a safe distance from the vehicle being overtaken — lateral while passing it and longitudinal before returning to their lane. The size of the distance depends on speed, the width of the carriageway and conditions, not on a fixed figure.

q-10941.text: Should you in this situation keep a safe distance of at least 1m from the vehicle when overtaking it?
q-10941.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The fixed distance of 1 m concerns overtaking a bicycle, a moped, an electric scooter, a personal transporter and a pedestrian. When overtaking a motor vehicle, a safe distance applies, suited to speed and the width of the carriageway, without a specified figure.

q-10947.text: Should a safe distance of not less than 1 metre be maintained when overtaking a vehicle on the right?
q-10947.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When overtaking a road user moving along the right edge of the carriageway — a bicycle, a moped, an electric scooter or a personal transporter — you must keep a distance of no less than 1 m. If such a distance cannot be ensured, the manoeuvre may not be started.

q-10949.text: In this situation, is it permitted to overtake the vehicle on the right?
q-10949.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On the right you may overtake a vehicle signalling an intention to turn left, and also vehicles moving in designated lanes in the same direction. Before the manoeuvre, make sure the lane on the right is clear.

q-10950.text: Is overtaking allowed at this intersection?
q-10950.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban on overtaking a motor vehicle at a junction does not apply at a roundabout or where traffic is directed by signals or by an authorised person. The manoeuvre is then allowed, but still requires making sure the road is clear.

q-10952.text: Are you obliged when attempting to overtake, in this situation, to ensure that you do not get in the way of a vehicle travelling in the right lane?
q-10952.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When changing lane in order to overtake, the driver must give way to the vehicle travelling in the lane they are entering and must not cut in on it. That is why the mirrors and the area they do not show are checked before the manoeuvre.

q-10953.text: Are you obliged, in this situation, to signal in advance your intention to manoeuvre?
q-10953.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intention to change lane or direction is signalled early and clearly with the indicator, and after the manoeuvre the signal is switched off. The signal alone gives no priority, though — you must still give way to those travelling in the target lane.

q-10954.text: Are you obliged, in this situation, to ensure that no other vehicle is approaching from the lane you intend to drive into?
q-10954.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before changing lane, the driver must make sure — by looking in the mirrors and checking the area the mirrors do not show — that no other vehicle is coming along that lane. The manoeuvre may be started only when it will obstruct nobody.

q-10955.text: Should you exercise extreme caution when passing by the visible tram stop?
q-10955.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a marked tram stop where passengers step onto the carriageway, the driver must take special care. If necessary, stop the vehicle and allow safe access to the tram and safe alighting from it.

q-10956.text: Should you exercise extreme caution when passing by the visible bus stop?
q-10956.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The rules tie the requirement of special care to a marked tram stop at which passengers step onto the carriageway; at a bus stop ordinary care is enough. In a built-up area, however, you must let a bus join the traffic from a stop.

q-10960.text: What will a police officer do if, during a roadside inspection,it is established that you have exceeded the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area, but this was done in order to save someone's life?

options.B: Caution and refer you to take a control exam.
options.C: Will not withhold your driving licence.

q-10960.explanation: Correct answer: C. Exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area usually ends with the driving licence being retained, but this is not applied when the driver acted to save a person's life or health. The police officer then does not retain the document.

q-10961.text: What will happen if a police officer discovers during a roadside inspection that you have exceeded the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area, but that this was done in order to save somebody's life?

options.A: The police officer will withhold your driving licence.
options.B: The Police officer will refer you to an instructor for additional training.
options.C: The police officer will refrain from retaining your driving licence.

q-10961.explanation: Correct answer: C. Retention of the driving licence for exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area is not applied if the driver exceeded the speed while saving a person's life or health. The police officer then refrains from retaining the document.

q-10962.text: In this situation, are you obliged to keep a safe distance from the vehicles you are passing by?
q-10962.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing standing vehicles, keep a safe distance from them, because a pedestrian may step out from behind them and a door may be opened suddenly. The distance is chosen according to speed and the width of the free part of the carriageway.

q-10963.text: Should you exercise extreme caution when avoiding a vehicle parked on the lane you are driving?
q-10963.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Passing a vehicle standing in your lane requires special care: a pedestrian may step out from behind it, and the vehicle itself may move off. You must also make sure that moving onto the neighbouring part of the carriageway will endanger nobody.

q-10966.text: Are you obliged, if necessary, to go to the right when driving past?
q-10966.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing an oncoming vehicle, the driver must keep a safe distance from it and, if necessary, move to the right, closer to the edge of the carriageway. On a narrow road this usually also means reducing speed.

q-10969.text: Is it permitted to carry a child at least 135 cm tall and protected only by seat belts in the front seat of a vehicle?

options.A: Yes, because the rules permit it if it is impossible to provide a child restraint system due to the weight of the child.
options.B: No, because the rules on the transport of children permit the transport of children at least 135 cm tall without a safety seat or other child restraint system only in the rear seat of the vehicle.
options.C: Yes, if the vehicle is not equipped with rear seats.

q-10969.explanation: Correct answer: B. A child at least 135 cm tall, secured with the seat belts alone, may be carried only on the rear seat of the vehicle. Carrying such a child on the front seat without a restraint is not allowed.

q-10971.text: Is it permissible to reverse a light quadricycle on this section of the road?
q-10971.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Reversing is prohibited in a tunnel, on a bridge, on a flyover, on a motorway and on an expressway; none of those prohibitions applies on this stretch. The manoeuvre must still be carried out giving way to others and watching the road behind the vehicle.

q-10972.text: Is it permitted to reverse a light quadricycle on the bridge?
q-10972.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Reversing is prohibited in a tunnel, on a bridge and a flyover, and also on a motorway and an expressway. On a bridge the manoeuvre may not be carried out regardless of the type of vehicle and whether other road users are nearby.

q-10973.text: Must you exercise extreme caution when performing this manoeuvre with a light quadricycle?
q-10973.explanation: Correct answer: YES. This manoeuvre requires special care: the driver must watch the whole surroundings of the vehicle and give way to other road users. As long as there is no certainty that it endangers nobody, the manoeuvre may not be started.

q-10974.text: Can you use daytime running lights in these road conditions, when driving a motorbike or light quadricycle?
q-10974.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Daytime running lights may be used only during the day, from dawn to dusk, when the air is clear. In worse conditions — rain, fog or at dusk — dipped headlights apply, which light the road and show the vehicle better.

q-10976.text: When driving a moped during the day, from dawn to dusk, with good air clarity, can you use daytime running lights instead of dipped beam lights?
q-10976.explanation: Correct answer: YES. During the day, from dawn to dusk and when the air is clear, daytime running lights may be used instead of dipped headlights. As soon as conditions worsen, dipped headlights must be switched on without delay.

q-10979.text: Can a moped driver use daytime running lights in deteriorating weather conditions?
q-10979.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Daytime running lights are permitted only during the day when the air is clear. When weather conditions worsen, a moped rider must switch on dipped headlights, because only they light the road and make the vehicle clearly visible.

q-10980.text: Can you use high beam lights on this stretch of road when driving a light quadricycle?
q-10980.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle a driver coming towards you or travelling ahead, and also in fog. In such conditions you drive on dipped headlights.

q-10981.text: Should you use the sound signal when driving past the bus in the adjacent lane?
q-10981.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn may be used only when necessary to warn of danger, and in a built-up area — to prevent an accident. Simply passing a vehicle travelling in the neighbouring lane does not require such a signal.

q-10982.text: In this situation, should you use the sound or light signal when approaching the pedestrian crossing?
q-10982.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Approaching a pedestrian crossing, the driver must take special care, slow down and give way to the pedestrian, not hurry them along with signals. The horn may be used only to warn of an immediate danger.

q-10983.text: Can you use position lights on this section of the road when driving a motorbike not equipped with daytime running lights?
q-10983.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A moving vehicle must have dipped headlights on or — if it is fitted with them — daytime running lights. Position lights alone do not meet this duty, because they do not light the road and show the vehicle poorly to others.

q-10986.text: In this situation, can a moped driver use the sound signal to hurry up a person crossing the road?
q-10986.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The horn serves solely to warn of danger; it may not be used to hurry or frighten a pedestrian. The driver must wait until the person has safely left the carriageway.

q-10992.text: Under what circumstances can you carry a third child, under 135 cm in height, in the rear seat of a car or truck, restrained only by seat belts?

options.A: If two children are transported in safety seats and it is impossible to install a third seat and the third child is over 3 years old.
options.B: Only if the third child is at least 100 cm tall.
options.C: Only if the third child is 15 years old.

q-10992.explanation: Correct answer: A. A third child under 135 cm may be carried on the rear seat in the belts alone only when the other two are in child seats, a third seat cannot be fitted, and the child has turned 3.

q-10994.text: When is it permitted to carry a child under 150 cm tall in the front seat of a lorry, only restrained by means of seat belts?

options.A: If the child is at least 135 cm tall.
options.B: If it is impossible to fit a safety seat in the vehicle.
options.C: If the child has a medical certificate indicating that it is cannot be transported in a safety seat.

q-10994.explanation: Correct answer: C. A child under 150 cm may be carried without a restraint, in the belts alone, when it has a medical certificate stating a contraindication to using a child seat. Lack of room for a seat, or height alone, gives no such grounds.

q-10999.text: Which of these documents must you carry with you and present at the request of the competent authorities if you are engaged in the commercial transport of goods by lorry with a maximum permissible weight exceeding 12 t?

options.B: Confirmation that the vehicle owner has concluded a contract for compulsory third party insurance or proof of payment of insurance premium.
options.C: Vehicle registration document receipt for the period it authorises its use,

q-10999.explanation: Correct answer: C. When the registration document has been retained, its role is played by the receipt, and that is what must be in the vehicle for the time it entitles you to drive. The driver need not carry a national driving licence or third-party confirmation — the data are in the registers.

q-11001.text: Which of these documents must the driver of a vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland carry and present at the request of an authorised body?

options.A: Which of these documents must the driver of a vehicle registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland carry and present at the request of an authorised body?
options.B: Proof of payment of the compulsory third-party liability insurance of the vehicle owner.
options.C: If the driver has a driving licence limited to a vehicle fitted with an alcohol interlock, a certificate of satisfactory technical examination in this regard.

q-11001.explanation: Correct answer: C. The driver of a vehicle registered in Poland need not carry the registration document or proof of third-party insurance, because those data are in the registers. They must, however, have the certificate of the technical check of the alcohol interlock if their entitlement is restricted to such a vehicle.

q-11003.text: When inspecting a vehicle that performs road transport, does a road transport inspector have the right to verify the vehicle data in the Central Register of Vehicles?

options.A: Yes, they have the same rights as the police in this respect.
options.B: No, only the police have such authority.
options.C: No, only the police, border guards and customs and fiscal services are authorised to verify vehicle data in the Central Register of Vehicles.

q-11003.explanation: Correct answer: A. A road transport inspector checking a vehicle engaged in road transport has the same powers in that respect as the police and may check the vehicle's data in the central register. The driver should allow such a check to be carried out.

q-11005.text: Who can give back the registration document if it is retained during a traffic control, on the grounds that the vehicle is a danger to traffic order?

options.A: A body authorised to carry out technical tests following a technical examination appropriate to the reason for the retention of the registration document.

q-11005.explanation: Correct answer: A. A registration document retained because of the vehicle's technical condition is returned by a unit authorised to carry out technical inspections, after an inspection corresponding to the reason for retention. Neither the municipal guard nor the road authority has such powers.

q-11017.text: For how long will the driving licence of a driver who has exceeded the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area be retained?
q-11017.explanation: Correct answer: A. For exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area, the driving licence is retained for 3 months. That period may be extended if the driver drives a vehicle during that time despite the document being retained.

q-11018.text: For how long does a driving licence retention receipt for exceeding the speed limit in a built-up area by more than 50 km/h entitle one to drive?

options.A: For a period of 24 hours from the moment the licence is withheld.
options.B: For 7 days from the date the licence is withheld.
options.C: For 72 hours from the moment the licence is withheld.

q-11018.explanation: Correct answer: A. In such a case the receipt for the retained driving licence allows you to drive for a further 24 hours from the moment the document was taken. After that time, driving on means driving without entitlement.

q-11022.text: In what circumstance will the driving licence not be withheld for exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area?

options.A: If the driver of the vehicle has committed an infringement in order to ward off an imminent danger to an asset protected by law.
options.B: If the driver of the vehicle behind uses warning lights and sound signals to indicate a need to increase speed.
options.C: If the driver increased speed so as to quickly exit the intersection of roads while the green signal lights are on.

q-11022.explanation: Correct answer: A. The driving licence is not retained when the driver exceeded the speed while acting to avert an immediate danger to an interest protected by law. Pressure from another driver, or wanting to clear a junction faster, is no such justification.

q-11027.text: In these road conditions, can a moped driver use the high beam lights?
q-11027.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle a driver coming towards you or travelling ahead, and also in fog. In such conditions dipped headlights apply.

q-11028.text: You want to transport a child in the front seat of a vehicle fitted with a front passenger airbag that is active. How would you proceed?

options.A: Carry the child in a rearward-facing safety seat.
options.B: Carry the child in a forward-facing safety seat.
options.C: Carry the child in another rearward-facing child restraint system.

q-11028.explanation: Correct answer: B. With the front passenger airbag active, a child may be carried on the front seat only in a forward-facing child seat. A rear-facing seat may be placed there only once the airbag has been switched off.

q-11029.text: The document certifying that a motorbike has been approved for use is:
q-11029.explanation: Correct answer: A. A motorcycle's admission to traffic is confirmed by the registration document and, before it is issued, by the temporary permit. The driving licence concerns the rider's entitlements, and the identity card solely the person's identity.

q-11037.text: Which of these documents certifies that an agricultural tractor is approved for road traffic?

options.B: Report from the Central Register of Vehicles.

q-11037.explanation: Correct answer: C. A vehicle's admission to traffic is confirmed by the registration document and, until it is issued, by the temporary permit. The vehicle card documents its history, and a report from the register is only information about the data.

q-11039.text: In the situation shown in the clip, can the driver of the vehicle drive into the intersection?
q-11039.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The ban on entry follows from the signal, sign or situation shown in the material — the driver must stop before the junction. You may enter the junction only when you can leave it without stopping and without obstructing traffic.

q-11041.text: The driver of an agricultural tractor with a trailer registered in the territory of the Republic of Poland is obliged to carry and present at the request of a competent authority:

options.A: The registration document for an agricultural tractor.
options.B: The registration document retention receipt of the towed trailer for the period it authorises the use of the trailer.
options.C: A certificate attesting that the tractor successfully completed its last technical inspection.

q-11041.explanation: Correct answer: B. The registration document of a vehicle registered in Poland and a technical inspection certificate need not be carried, because those data are in the registers. If, however, the trailer's document has been retained, the driver must have the receipt for the time it entitles them to drive.

q-11042.text: Within what time limit is the owner of an agricultural tractor obliged to collect the decision on vehicle registration and the registration document?

options.A: 30 days from the date of application for vehicle registration.
options.B: 35 days from the date of application for vehicle registration.
options.C: 30 days from the day the agricultural tractor takes to the road for the first time.

q-11042.explanation: Correct answer: A. The owner is to collect the registration decision and the registration document within 30 days of the day the registration application was submitted. The period runs from the application, not from the vehicle's first outing on the road.

q-11046.text: You are in a built-up area. Are you in this situation obliged to allow the bus driver to merge into the traffic?
q-11046.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area the driver must let a bus or trolleybus pull out of a marked stop when its driver signals an intention to join the traffic. If necessary, slow down or stop.

q-11047.text: What document certifies that one is authorised to drive an agricultural tractor?

options.A: Category T driving licence issued in the country.
options.C: Image of the driving licence in the mDocuments App.

q-11047.explanation: Correct answer: A. The entitlement to drive an agricultural tractor is confirmed by a category T driving licence issued in Poland. The vehicle card concerns the vehicle itself, and an image of the document in an app does not replace holding the required entitlements.

q-11050.text: You are in a built-up area. Are you obliged in this situation to slow down and, if necessary, stop?
q-11050.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Enabling another road user's manoeuvre requires real action: reducing speed and, when necessary, stopping the vehicle. Merely pulling aside is not enough if it gives no certainty of a safe passage.

q-11055.text: You are in a built-up area. Have you acted accordingly by allowing the bus driver to merge into traffic?
q-11055.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area giving way to a bus pulling out of a marked stop is a duty, not a courtesy. The bus driver, for their part, must move off carefully and not force others to brake sharply.

q-11059.text: Which of the following documents certifies that you are licensed to ride a motorbike:

options.A: A valid driving licence appropriate to the type of motorbike.
options.B: An image of the driving licence in the mDocuments App.
options.C: A temporary permit issued in the country.

q-11059.explanation: Correct answer: A. The entitlement to ride a motorcycle is confirmed by a valid driving licence of the appropriate category, matched to the type of motorcycle. A temporary permit concerns the vehicle's admission to traffic, not the rider's entitlements.

q-11060.text: Which of these vehicles does a category A1 licence entitle one to drive?

options.B: A three-wheel motorbike with power not exceeding 15 kW.

q-11060.explanation: Correct answer: B. Category A1 covers light motorcycles and three-wheeled motorcycles with a power not exceeding 15 kW. A slow-moving vehicle and a quadricycle require other entitlements and do not fall within the scope of this category.

q-11061.text: The holder of a category A1 driving licence may drive, among others:

options.B: A motorbike with power not exceeding 45 kW and power-to-weight ratio not exceeding 0,2 kW/kg.

q-11061.explanation: Correct answer: C. Category A1 includes the entitlements of category AM, so it allows you to drive a moped and a light quadricycle. A motorcycle with a power of up to 45 kW requires category A2, and a slow-moving vehicle other entitlements.

q-11064.text: Is it permissible to perform a u-turn from the occupied lane at this intersection?
q-11064.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Whether a U-turn is allowed is decided by the purpose of the lane and the signs shown in the material — since you may turn left from this lane and there is no ban on U-turns, the manoeuvre is permitted. You must give way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

q-11066.text: Is it permitted to turn left from the occupied lane or make a U-turn at this intersection?
q-11066.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A lane intended for turning left also allows a U-turn, if the signing does not prohibit it. Before the manoeuvre, take up the correct position on the carriageway, signal your intention and give way to oncoming traffic.

q-11069.text: Can you turn right at this intersection from the occupied lane?
q-11069.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A right turn is made from the lane closest to the right edge of the carriageway or from the lane designated for that direction — as is the case here. The manoeuvre requires signalling and giving way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway.

q-11070.text: The holder of a driving licence for categories AM, A1, A2, and A is obliged to notify the starost of damage to the document to the extent that it is illegible, within:

options.A: 30 days of occurrence of the incident;
options.B: 33 days of occurrence of the incident;
options.C: 14 days of occurrence of the incident;

q-11070.explanation: Correct answer: A. Destruction of a driving licence to the point of illegibility is reported to the starosta within 30 days of the event. The report is the basis for issuing a duplicate of the document.

q-11072.text: Can you change lane from the one you are currently occupying so that you can turn right?
q-11072.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material does not allow you to leave the lane you occupy at this place — the lane matching your intended direction must be taken up earlier. The driver should continue in their lane and turn where it is allowed.

q-11073.text: The starost shall issue an administrative decision to withhold a category A driving licence for a period of 3 months, making it immediately enforceable if:

options.A: The driver of a motorbike in a built-up area exceeded the speed limit by more than 50 km/h.
options.B: The driver of a motorbike in a built-up area exceeded the speed limit by 45 km/h.
options.C: The driver of a motorbike in a built-up area exceeded the speed limit by 40 km/h.

q-11073.explanation: Correct answer: A. The driving licence is retained for 3 months when the driver has exceeded the permitted speed by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. Smaller excesses, such as 45 or 40 km/h, have no such effect, although they remain an offence.

q-11075.text: The starost shall issue an administrative decision to withhold a category A driving licence for a period of 3 months, making it immediately enforceable if the motorbike driver drives in a built-up area on a road with a speed limit of 40 km/h:
q-11075.explanation: Correct answer: A. Retention of the driving licence for 3 months follows exceeding the permitted speed by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. With a limit of 40 km/h, that threshold is crossed only by driving faster than 90 km/h.

q-11076.text: Are you permitted to make a U-turn from the occupied lane at the visible intersection?
q-11076.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A U-turn is ruled out here, because it is prohibited by the signing or by the purpose of the occupied lane shown in the material. The manoeuvre may also not be carried out where it would endanger safety or obstruct traffic.

q-11077.text: The starost shall issue an administrative decision to withhold a category A driving licence for a period of 3 months, making it immediately enforceable if the driver drives a motorbike in an area with a speed limit of 30 km/h:

options.A: travels at speeds in excess of 80 km/h;

q-11077.explanation: Correct answer: A. For the driving licence to be retained for 3 months, the permitted speed must be exceeded by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. In a 30 km/h zone that means driving faster than 80 km/h.

q-11079.text: Should you go close to the middle of the road if you intend to turn left onto the visible two-way traffic road?
q-11079.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before turning left on a two-way road the driver moves towards the middle of the carriageway, and on a one-way carriageway — towards its left edge. Taking the correct position makes it easier for others to pass the vehicle and shows the intention clearly.

q-11080.text: The starost shall issue an administrative decision to withhold a category A driving licence for a period of 3 months, making it immediately enforceable if:

options.A: the driver of a motorbike transports persons in excess of the number of seats specified on the registration document of the motorbike;
options.B: the driver of a motorbike drives during the day in a built-up area at a speed of 90 km/h;
options.C: the driver of a motorbike drives on an express road at 180 km/h.

q-11080.explanation: Correct answer: A. The driving licence is also retained for 3 months when the driver carries more people than the number of seats entered in the registration document. Exceeding the speed limit outside a built-up area has no such effect.

q-11081.text: Should you approach the left edge of the roadway if you intend to turn left onto the visible two-way traffic road?
q-11081.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Only a driver on a one-way carriageway moves towards its left edge. On a two-way road you must take up position near the middle of the carriageway, because the left part is intended for oncoming traffic.

q-11085.text: If the starost has issued an administrative decision to hold a category A driving licence for a period of 3 months; then due to the lack of obligation to carry a driving licence when riding a motorbike:

options.A: you can only drive a motorbike within the boundaries of the relevant county;
options.B: you can only drive a motorbike within the boundaries of your town of permanent residence;
options.C: you are not permitted to drive a motorbike for the period the licence has been retained.

q-11085.explanation: Correct answer: C. The decision to retain the driving licence takes away the right to drive, not just the document itself, so for the whole of that period riding a motorcycle is prohibited. Breaking the ban results in the retention period being extended.

q-11086.text: You intend to change lanes to the left. Are you obliged to yield way to vehicles in the left lane?
q-11086.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver changing lane must give way to vehicles travelling in the lane they intend to enter. The manoeuvre may be started only when nobody will have to brake or change course.

q-11087.text: You intend to change lanes to the left. Do you have the right of way over vehicles travelling in this lane?
q-11087.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority belongs to the vehicles travelling in the lane you want to enter; the one changing lane always gives way to them. A switched-on indicator informs of the intention but gives no right to force the manoeuvre.

q-11088.text: You intend to change lanes to the left. Should you clearly signal this change in advance?
q-11088.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An intention to change lane is signalled early and clearly with the indicator, so that other drivers have time to adjust their driving. The signal does not, however, release you from giving way to those travelling in the target lane.

q-11089.text: Should you exercise extreme caution when changing lanes?
q-11089.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Changing lane requires special care: watching the mirrors, checking the area the mirrors do not show and judging the speed of vehicles coming from behind. Only then can you change course smoothly.

q-11090.text: You change lanes by signalling this accordingly. Are you obliged to stop signalling a lane change manoeuvre as soon as it is done?
q-11090.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Signalling a manoeuvre ends immediately after it is carried out. An indicator left on misleads others and may prompt them to act in a way that leads to a collision.

q-11093.text: After turning right at the nearest intersection, will you be driving towards Nadarzyn?
q-11093.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The direction of travel after the turn follows from the direction sign shown in the material, which assigns that town to the road leading off to the right. Direction and place-name signs are read before the junction, choosing the correct lane in advance.

q-11094.text: You are driving on a one-way road and intend to turn left. Should you move closer to the left edge of the road you are occupying?
q-11094.explanation: Correct answer: YES. On a one-way carriageway, before turning left you take up position as close as possible to its left edge. There is no oncoming traffic there, and such positioning lets other vehicles continue on the right.

q-11096.text: Can you make a U-turn from the lane you are occupying at the nearest roadway link?
q-11096.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A U-turn through the gap between the carriageways is permitted if neither a sign nor the purpose of the lane prohibits it. The driver must give way to vehicles travelling on the other carriageway and carry out the manoeuvre without obstructing traffic.

q-11097.text: In this situation, can you drive into the intersection and continue driving?
