q-11097.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The ban on entering the junction follows from the signal, sign or instruction shown in the material — the driver must stop the vehicle before the junction. You may continue only after receiving a permitting signal.

q-11098.text: Can you drive into the intersection when you see a policeman standing on it facing you?
q-11098.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The stance of a person directing traffic facing the driver with their front or back corresponds to a red signal and means no entry to the junction. Stop before the junction and wait for the stance to change or for a clear instruction.

q-11099.text: Can you drive into a crossroads when you see a policeman standing in such a position?
q-11099.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signal given by the police officer's stance shown in the material prohibits entering the junction. The instructions and signals of a person directing traffic take precedence over light signals and signs, so you must stop and wait for a permitting signal.

q-11100.text: Can you drive into a crossroads when you see a policeman standing sideways to you?
q-11100.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The stance of a police officer turned side-on to the driver corresponds to a signal permitting passage, like a green light. You enter with care and only when the junction can be left.

q-11102.text: Will you soon be able to enter the intersection if you see a policeman standing in such a position?
q-11102.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal shown in the material announces a change to a permitting one, like an amber light after red. You may move off only when the person directing traffic actually gives the signal permitting entry.

q-11107.text: In this situation, are you allowed to stop on the roadway?
q-11107.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Stopping on the carriageway at this place is prohibited — that follows from the signing or the nature of the place shown in the material. You may stop where the vehicle does not limit visibility or obstruct others.

q-11108.text: In this situation, are you allowed to stop the vehicle at the shoulder?
q-11108.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The no-stopping prohibition in force at this place follows from the sign shown in the material and also covers the verge, not only the carriageway. You may stop only beyond the stretch covered by the prohibition, in a place that does not endanger others.

q-11109.text: In the presented traffic situation, can you stop at the side of the road?
q-11109.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Parking on the verge at this place is not allowed, which follows from the signing or the nature of the place shown in the material. A vehicle left there would limit visibility or obstruct traffic, so another place must be chosen.

q-11111.text: Are you allowed to make a stop at the left edge of a low-traffic two-way street in a built-up area?
q-11111.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Parking at the left edge of a two-way carriageway is permitted only in a built-up area on a road with light traffic. Outside a built-up area, or with heavier traffic, the vehicle may not be parked that way.

q-11112.text: Are you obliged to enter the right traffic lane after changing direction to the left?
q-11112.explanation: Correct answer: NO. After turning left the driver does not have to move to the right lane — they may take any lane of the carriageway they are entering. Special care applies, and forcing others to change direction or speed is prohibited.

q-11113.text: Can you take any lane on the road you are entering after changing direction to the left?
q-11113.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Completing a left turn, the driver may enter any lane of the cross carriageway. They must, however, take special care and carry out the manoeuvre so as not to force other drivers to change direction or speed.

q-11119.text: Is it only permitted to stop in the designated areas, in the area you have entered?
q-11119.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The zone sign shown in the material introduces the rule that parking is allowed only in places designated for it. That is the case in a residential zone — leaving a vehicle outside a designated place is an offence.

q-11120.text: You are in a built-up area. Are you obliged in this situation to slow down and, if necessary, stop to permit the bus driver to merge into traffic?
q-11120.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area the driver must reduce speed and, if necessary, stop in order to let a bus pull away from a marked stop when the bus driver signals an intention to join the traffic.

q-11122.text: You are in a built-up area. Are you in this situation obliged to permit the bus driver to merge into the traffic?
q-11122.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area you must let a bus pulling away from a marked stop and signalling that intention join the traffic. Outside a built-up area there is no such duty — there, vehicles travelling along the road have priority.

q-11123.text: You are outside a built-up area. Are you obliged to allow the bus driver to merge into traffic?
q-11123.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The concession for a bus pulling away from a stop applies only in a built-up area. Outside it, the bus driver joining the traffic gives way — even so, it is worth anticipating their manoeuvre and watching the stop.

q-11124.text: You are in a built-up area. Were you obliged in this situation to allow the bus driver to merge into traffic?
q-11124.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a built-up area there was a duty to let the bus join the traffic from the marked stop once its driver signalled that intention. Speed should have been reduced and, if necessary, the vehicle stopped.

q-11125.text: Will you be driving on a one-way street beyond this road sign?
q-11125.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material does not introduce one-way traffic — a separate sign informs of that. Beyond it you must therefore expect oncoming vehicles and keep to the right side of the carriageway.

q-11126.text: Do pedestrians using the road in this area have priority over the vehicle?
q-11126.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In the zone marked in the material a pedestrian may use the whole width of the road and has priority over a vehicle. The driver must drive slowly and be ready to stop, also because of children playing.

q-11127.text: Can you expect unlabeled speed bumps in a zone marked as such?
q-11127.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In the zone marked in the material, speed humps and other slowing devices do not have to be additionally marked with signs. Speed must therefore be chosen so that an unexpected obstacle can be crossed safely.

q-11128.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop the vehicle before the level crossing?
q-11128.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An unconditional stop before the crossing is required by a sign ordering a stop, by lowered or lowering barriers and by a red signal. There is no such order here — special care and making sure the track is clear are enough.

q-11129.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution at a level crossing marked as such?
q-11129.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care applies at every level crossing, regardless of its signing and whether it has barriers. Before entering, make sure the track is clear and that there is room beyond the crossing to drive off it.

q-11130.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution at a level crossing marked as such?
q-11130.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Every level crossing requires special care, regardless of signing and whether it is equipped with barriers. The driver must watch the track from both sides and enter only when certain of being able to leave the crossing safely.

q-11131.text: Are you obliged to provide first aid when involved in an accident in which someone is injured?
q-11131.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident with an injured person must give first aid as far as they are able and call an ambulance and the police. The scene must also be secured, and you must not leave it.

q-11132.text: Does the visible sign warn of two dangerous turns, the first to the right and the second to the left?
q-11132.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign defines the direction of the first bend only; it does not determine the direction of the next one. The second bend may be to the left or to the right, so the claim that it must be to the left is wrong.

q-11133.text: Does the visible sign warn of two dangerous turns, of which the first is right and the second may be to the left?
q-11133.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of at least two dangerous bends and indicates the direction of only the first — to the right. The next may lead left or right, so speed should be reduced before the whole stretch.

q-11134.text: This sign warns of two dangerous turns, both of which may be to the right.
q-11134.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign only settles the direction of the first bend — to the right — and the next may be to the left or to the right. A situation in which both bends lead to the right is therefore entirely possible.

q-11135.text: Does the visible sign warn you that you are approaching a ferry crossing?
q-11135.explanation: Correct answer: NO. This sign does not concern a ferry crossing — that is announced by a separate warning sign. The visible sign warns of a stretch of road running along a quay or the shore of a body of water.

q-11136.text: Does the visible sign warn about a section of road leading along a water reservoir?
q-11136.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a stretch of road running along a quay or the shore of a body of water, where leaving the carriageway risks ending up in the water. Slow down and do not get close to the edge.

q-11138.text: Does the visible sign warn of a railway crossing equipped with half-barriers?
q-11138.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material warns of a level crossing without barriers or half-barriers — a crossing equipped with barriers is announced by a separate sign. At such a crossing safety depends solely on the driver watching the track.

q-11139.text: Does the visible sign warn of a level crossing that may be equipped with traffic lights?
q-11139.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A crossing without barriers, which this sign warns of, may be equipped with light signals. A red light, including a flashing one, absolutely prohibits entry; the absence of signals does not release you from special care.

q-11142.text: Does the visible sign warn of a bulge on the roadway designed to slow down vehicle traffic?
q-11142.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a speed hump, that is, a raised section laid on the carriageway to force slower driving. Speed must be reduced before the obstacle, because crossing it at high speed risks losing control of the vehicle.

q-11144.text: Are you obliged at the nearest intersection behind this sign to give the right of way to a vehicle approaching from the right?
q-11144.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign shown in the material does not grant priority, so the right-hand rule applies at the nearest junction: you give way to the vehicle approaching from the right. Approach the junction at a speed that allows you to stop.

q-11145.text: Do you have the right of way at the nearest intersection over the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-11145.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign shown in the material informs that you are travelling on a road with priority, so at the nearest junction the vehicle approaching from the right must give way. Priority must not be forced, though — watch whether it has actually been given.

q-11146.text: Does the visible sign warn of two dangerous turns, the first of which is to the right?
q-11146.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign does warn of dangerous bends, but the first of them leads to the left, not the right. The direction of the first bend always matches the drawing on the sign; the direction of the next is not defined by the sign.

q-11147.text: In this situation, do you have priority over the driver approaching from the opposite direction?
q-11147.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing shown in the material gives priority to drivers approaching from the opposite direction. You must therefore stop before the narrowing and enter only when nobody is coming the other way.

q-11148.text: Does this sign, if not previously revoked by a sign indicating the end of a speed limit zone, apply to the nearest intersection?
q-11148.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A speed limit introduced in a zone applies right up to the sign marking its end and is not cancelled by junctions passed along the way. It covers the whole area of the zone, side streets included.

q-11149.text: Does the depicted sign revoke the ban expressed by the B-35 "no stopping"?
q-11149.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown has no such meaning and does not end the no-parking prohibition. The prohibition ceases only at the place indicated by the sign marking its end, or at the nearest junction, unless provided otherwise.

q-11150.text: Does this sign, along with the plaque, prohibit stopping in front of it on the side of the road on which it is located?
q-11150.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign with the plate shown in the material does not extend the prohibition to the stretch before it — stopping remains allowed at this place. The extent and direction of the prohibition are indicated by the plate, so it must be read together with the sign.

q-11151.text: Does this sign, along with the plate, forbid stopping in front of it on the side of the road on which it is located?
q-11151.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The plate beneath the sign extends the prohibition to the stretch before the sign as well, on the side of the road where the sign stands. Stopping the vehicle at this place is therefore not permitted.

q-11152.text: Does this sign forbid you from making a U-turn at the nearest intersection?
q-11152.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The prohibition expressed by this sign does not cover turning round at the nearest junction — prohibition signs apply up to the nearest junction, unless provided otherwise. The manoeuvre itself requires special care and giving way.

q-11156.text: Does the presented sign apply to a moped driver?
q-11156.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign applies to all drivers of vehicles, and therefore to a moped rider too. Exclusions concern only those road users who are expressly indicated on the sign itself or on the plate beneath it.

q-11157.text: In this situation, are you obliged to turn right at the nearest intersection?
q-11157.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign shown in the material does not impose a right turn at the nearest junction. An order to travel in a specified direction at a junction is introduced by a separate mandatory sign placed before that junction.

q-11158.text: This sign indicates a road for pedestrians, which cannot be used by cyclists.
q-11158.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A road marked with this sign is not closed to cyclists — a cyclist may use it. They must give way to pedestrians while doing so and adapt their speed to pedestrian traffic.

q-11160.text: On seeing this sign, can the driver drive on its left or right?
q-11160.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign orders you to pass the indicated place and permits passing it on either the left or the right side. The choice of side is the driver's, but the manoeuvre is carried out without obstructing others.

q-11161.text: Does this sign oblige the driver to turn right at the nearest intersection?
q-11161.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The mandatory sign indicates the only permitted direction of travel at the nearest junction — to the right. Going straight ahead or left is then an offence, so you must move into the correct lane early enough.

q-11163.text: Is it permitted to drive straight ahead or right from a lane with the visible horizontal sign?
q-11163.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Arrows painted on a lane bindingly define the directions of travel permitted from it, and the visible marking permits a direction other than straight ahead and right. Move into the correct lane before the junction.

q-11166.text: Does the visible line consisting of rectangles indicate a place of absolute stop before the pedestrian crossing?
q-11166.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A line made up of rectangles is a conditional stop line — it indicates the stopping place only when a duty to stop actually arises. An unconditional stop is marked by the solid line used with the sign requiring a stop.

q-11172.text: The visible line separating traffic lanes is a line that can be crossed by drivers travelling in the opposite direction.
q-11172.explanation: Correct answer: NO. For drivers coming from the opposite direction this line may not be crossed — from that side driving over it is prohibited. It may be crossed only from the side on which crossing it has been permitted.

q-11173.text: Is the visible line separating traffic lanes where the lines are longer than the gaps a broken line?
q-11173.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A broken line whose dashes are longer than the gaps is a warning line and remains crossable. It announces, however, that a solid line or a dangerous place is approaching, so manoeuvres must be completed early.

q-11175.text: Does the visible "bus stop line" signify a roadway on which driving is prohibited?
q-11175.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A stop line marks the place where public transport vehicles stop, not an area excluded from traffic. Driving over it is allowed; what is prohibited is other vehicles stopping on it.

q-11176.text: When changing lanes to the left, in this situation, do you have the right of way over vehicles in the lane you intend to enter?
q-11176.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When changing lane, the driver gives way to vehicles travelling in the lane they intend to enter. Signal the manoeuvre with the indicator and check the mirrors and the blind spot.

q-11177.text: Does the visible horizontal line indicate the stopping point of a vehicle only when a red signal flashes?
q-11177.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The line marks the stopping place whenever a duty to stop arises — at a red signal, a sign requiring a stop, closing barriers or an instruction from a person directing traffic. A flashing red is only one of those cases.

q-11178.text: Are you always obliged to stop before the designated line prior to entering the visible intersection?
q-11178.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing of this junction orders an unconditional stop before the marked line, even when the road appears clear. Only after stopping can you assess the situation and give way to approaching vehicles.

q-11179.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise extreme caution when driving into the petrol station?
q-11179.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Turning off the road into roadside premises is a change of direction that requires special care. Signal the manoeuvre and give way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians and cyclists on the path being crossed.

q-11180.text: In this situation, are you obliged, notwithstanding your right of way, to exercise extreme caution?
q-11180.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Having priority does not release you from watching the situation and being ready to react. Make sure the other road users really are giving way, because priority must not be forced.

q-11194.text: Can you drive a light quadricycle after using soft drugs such as marijuana?
q-11194.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Driving any vehicle after using intoxicants is prohibited, and the division into soft and hard drugs has no legal significance. Such substances lengthen reaction time and impair the judgement of distance and speed.

q-11198.text: In this situation, are you obliged to adopt a cautious approach?
q-11198.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The principle of limited trust applies whenever the behaviour of another road user indicates that they may act incorrectly. You must then slow down, watch that road user closely and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-11201.text: In this situation, are you obliged to reduce speed, even though there are no pedestrians at the pedestrian crossing?
q-11201.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Approaching a pedestrian crossing, the driver must take special care and slow down so as not to expose pedestrians to danger. This also applies to people only just approaching the crossing.

q-11203.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-11203.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-11206.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-11206.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The situation shown in the material is one where the rules require special care. This means paying more attention, adapting speed to the conditions and being ready to stop the vehicle immediately.

q-11209.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-11209.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-11210.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution when turning into a roadside facility?
q-11210.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Turning into premises beside the road is a change of direction, for which special care applies. The driver signals the manoeuvre, gives way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and does not cut in on vehicles behind.

q-11211.text: Can you overtake the cyclist in this situation?
q-11211.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking may be started only when visibility, the width of the carriageway and the situation around allow it, and the cyclist must be given a safe lateral distance of no less than 1 m. At this place the conditions do not make that possible.

q-11212.text: In this situation, are you obliged to adopt a cautious approach?
q-11212.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The principle of limited trust is applied when the behaviour or characteristics of another road user indicate that they may act incorrectly. In this situation there are no such grounds, although ordinary care always applies.

q-11213.text: Are you obliged to maintain cautious approach towards pedestrians walking on the pavement?
q-11213.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A pedestrian walking on the pavement is moving in a place intended for them and in itself gives no grounds for anticipating a mistake. Limited trust applies, among others, to children, elderly people and people with disabilities.

q-11214.text: In this situation, is it permitted to overtake the cyclist from the right?
q-11214.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is done on the left; on the right you may overtake only a vehicle signalling an intention to turn left and positioned accordingly for that manoeuvre. Here that condition is not met.

q-11215.text: In this situation, are you entitled to overtake the cyclist from the right?
q-11215.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The right to overtake on the right exists only in relation to a vehicle that is signalling a left turn and has moved towards the middle of the carriageway. In this situation the cyclist is not carrying out such a manoeuvre, so overtaking is allowed only on the left.

q-11216.text: Is it permissible in this situation to overtake the cyclist?
q-11216.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is prohibited at this place — the ban follows from the signing or the nature of the place shown in the material. The manoeuvre must be put off until a stretch where it is allowed and possible without danger.

q-11218.text: Are you obliged to stop the moped?
q-11218.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop follows from the sign, signal or instruction shown in the material, and a moped rider must comply with it. The stop is made before the line or before the place the order refers to.

q-11219.text: Are you entitled to continue driving in this situation?
q-11219.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The conditions shown in the material require you to give way to road users who are already on the carriageway, above all pedestrians. You may move only once they have cleared the way and would not have to be forced to stop.

q-11220.text: Are you obliged to stop, even though the bus is running on the tram tracks?
q-11220.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop follows from the situation shown in the material, and the fact that the bus is using the tramway changes nothing about it. The driver must stop whenever driving on would endanger other road users.

q-11222.text: In this situation, do you have the right of way over the cyclist?
q-11222.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this situation the cyclist has priority, so the driver must slow down and let them pass. Approaching a cycle crossing or cutting across a bicycle's path, you take special care.

q-11223.text: In this situation, can you overtake the cyclist from the right?
q-11223.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking on the right is permitted in relation to a road user who is signalling an intention to turn left and has taken up a position suited to that manoeuvre. Keep a safe distance while doing so and watch whether the cyclist changes their mind.

q-11224.text: In this situation, can you overtake the cyclist on the left if you keep a distance of no less than 1 metre?
q-11224.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Keeping a distance of no less than 1 m does not make this manoeuvre permissible, because the cyclist is signalling a left turn and is positioned for that manoeuvre. Such a road user is overtaken only on the right.

q-11225.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution when changing driving directions?
q-11225.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A change of direction always requires special care: signal the manoeuvre in advance, check the mirrors and the blind spot and make sure you will cut in on nobody. The pedestrian and the cyclist on the path being crossed have priority.

q-11226.text: Are you obliged in this situation to exercise extreme caution?
q-11226.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The circumstances shown are among those where the rules require special care. Pay more attention, watch the whole surroundings of the vehicle and choose a speed that lets you react to a change in the situation.

q-11227.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-11227.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In the situation shown in the material the rules require special care, that is, attention increased to a degree matching the conditions. Speed must allow the vehicle to be stopped before an obstacle that can be seen.

q-11228.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution in this situation?
q-11228.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-11229.text: Does the absence of other vehicles in the lane you are driving into exempt you from the obligation to exercise extreme caution?
q-11229.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty of special care follows from the kind of manoeuvre being carried out, not from whether other vehicles happen to be visible. The situation changes quickly — a motorcycle or a cyclist, easy to miss in the blind spot, may be coming up from behind.

q-11230.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution when switching lanes in this situation?
q-11230.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Changing lane requires special care — signal the manoeuvre, check the mirrors and the blind spot and give way to vehicles travelling in the lane you are entering.

q-11231.text: Are you obliged in this situation to exercise extreme caution when turning into the petrol station?
q-11231.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Turning into a petrol station is leaving the road, that is, a change of direction covered by the duty of special care. Signal the manoeuvre in advance and give way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians and cyclists on the path being crossed.

q-11232.text: In this situation, must you continue to exercise extreme caution after giving the right of way to vehicles travelling from the opposite direction?
q-11232.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The manoeuvre does not end the moment the oncoming vehicles have been let through — you must go on watching pedestrians and cyclists on the road being crossed and vehicles coming from behind. Special care applies until the manoeuvre is safely completed.

q-11234.text: Are you entitled to overtake a car that is in the left lane?
q-11234.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is done on the left, so a vehicle travelling in the left lane may not be overtaken on the right. The only exception is a vehicle signalling an intention to turn left and positioned accordingly for that manoeuvre.

q-11236.text: In this situation, should you adopt a cautious approach to the pedestrian?
q-11236.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The pedestrian's behaviour in this situation gives grounds for expecting them to act incorrectly, for example by stepping onto the carriageway. So slow down and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-11237.text: Can you continue driving in this situation?
q-11237.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the circumstances shown, driving on is not permitted — the duty to stop follows from the sign, signal or situation shown in the material. You may move off only when the reason for the stop is gone and the way is clear.

q-11238.text: Have you acted accordingly by stopping the moped on this spot?
q-11238.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Stopping is allowed where neither signs nor rules prohibit it, and the vehicle does not endanger safety or obstruct others. At the place shown in the material those conditions are met.

q-11241.text: Can you overtake the cyclist in this situation?
q-11241.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the conditions shown the cyclist cannot be overtaken safely — there is no room for an adequate lateral distance, or visibility and the traffic arrangement do not allow it. The manoeuvre must be put off until a more suitable place.

q-11242.text: In this situation, can you overtake the cyclist without keeping a lateral distance of 1 metre?
q-11242.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When overtaking a cyclist, the driver must keep a distance that is safe and no less than 1 m. The same requirement applies to a moped rider, a person on an electric scooter and a pedestrian walking on the verge.

q-11244.text: Pay attention to the mandatory signs. Is riding a bicycle on this road compliant with the regulations?
q-11244.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A mandatory sign designating a cycle path obliges a cyclist to use it. When such a path is designated and runs in the direction of travel, riding on the carriageway is contrary to the rules.

q-11246.text: After turning left at the nearest intersection, will you be travelling in the direction of Prażmów?
q-11246.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The direction to the town named is given by the direction and place-name sign, and it is assigned to a different exit of the junction than the left turn. A name is always read together with the arrow it belongs to.

q-11247.text: Does this sign indicate that you are entering a built-up area?
q-11247.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign marking the start of a built-up area informs that you are entering it. From that point the traffic rules provided for built-up areas apply, including the lower speed limit.

q-11250.text: Are you obliged to provide first aid to the injured party when involved in a road accident?
q-11250.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an accident must give the casualty first aid within their abilities and call the ambulance service. Failing to help is a separate, serious breach of the law.

q-11251.text: Are you obliged to signal a car parked because of a breakdown in a built-up area where it is prohibited?
q-11251.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A vehicle immobilised by a breakdown in a place where parking is prohibited must be marked — switch on the hazard lights and, if the vehicle has none, set up a warning triangle. The point is an early warning to other drivers.

q-11254.text: Is an injured party in a traffic accident entitled to request personal data of the offender?
q-11254.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A participant in an incident must give the other participants their personal details, the details of the vehicle's owner and the insurance details. Without them the injured party could not seek compensation for the damage.

q-11255.text: Will you be protecting the victim of an accident by covering him/her with a thermal insulating blanket?
q-11255.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A thermal blanket limits heat loss and protects the casualty from hypothermia, which matters greatly with injuries and shock. It does not, however, replace calling for help or the other rescue actions.

q-11256.text: Are you obliged to remove a moped from the road when you are involved in an accident in which someone is killed or injured?
q-11256.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When someone has been killed or injured in an incident, the vehicles and traces may not be moved unless saving a life requires it. Secure the scene, call the services and wait for the Police.

q-11258.text: When involved in a road accident in which there are no dead or injured persons, are you obliged to remove the vehicle from the road?
q-11258.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When nobody has been killed or injured, the participants must remove the vehicle from the scene so that it does not cause danger or obstruct traffic. Details and insurance information are exchanged off the carriageway.

q-11259.text: When involved in a road accident, are you obliged to stop the moped without endangering safety?
q-11259.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The first duty of a participant in an accident is to stop the vehicle in a way that does not endanger traffic. Only then is the scene secured and help given to the injured.

q-11261.text: When involved in an accident where there are no casualties, are you obliged to summon the police?
q-11261.explanation: Correct answer: NO. With material damage only, writing a statement and exchanging details is enough, and calling the Police is not compulsory. It becomes necessary when there are injured or killed, or when the participants disagree about what happened.

q-11262.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise extreme caution?
q-11262.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care means increasing attention and readiness to react to a degree appropriate to the conditions. The situation shown in the material raises the risk, so the driver must be prepared to slow down or stop the vehicle immediately.

q-11264.text: In this situation, can you drive through the level crossing without stopping?
q-11264.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Stopping before the crossing is necessary only when a sign, a signal, barriers or half-barriers order it. When there is nothing of the kind, you drive across without stopping, taking special care and making sure the track is clear.

q-11265.text: Can you drive through a level crossing without stopping if a train is not approaching?
q-11265.explanation: Correct answer: NO. If a sign requiring a stop has been placed before the crossing, that duty is unconditional — you must stop every time, even when no train can be seen. Only after stopping and making sure the track is clear may you move off.

q-11266.text: When turning right, are you obliged to make sure that no rail vehicle is approaching?
q-11266.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before turning right, when the track runs along the road or crosses your path, the driver must check that no rail vehicle is approaching. The check covers both sides, because a tram may also run against the general direction.

q-11268.text: When turning right, are you obliged to give priority to the rail vehicle?
q-11268.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A rail vehicle has priority over vehicles that are not rail vehicles, regardless of which side it approaches from. Turning right across the track, you must therefore give way to the tram and let it pass.

q-11269.text: Are you always obliged to stop before this crossing?
q-11269.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign visible before this crossing orders an unconditional stop, so that duty does not depend on whether a train is in sight. You may move off only after stopping and checking that the tracks are clear.

q-11270.text: In this situation, are you driving into a multi-track level crossing?
q-11270.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The number of tracks is indicated by the cross placed at the crossing: a single one means one track, a double one a multi-track crossing. At such a crossing, after one train has passed the neighbouring track may still be occupied.

q-11271.text: In the situation presented, are you arriving at a single-track crossing?
q-11271.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The cross at the crossing tells you the number of tracks: a single one means a single-track crossing, a double one a multi-track one. In the situation shown the marking indicates more than one track, so after the train has passed you must keep checking the neighbouring track.

q-11274.text: Does vehicle traffic move in only one direction beyond the nearest visible sign?
q-11274.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible sign does not designate a one-way road, so beyond it you must still expect oncoming vehicles. One-way traffic is indicated by a separate information sign with a white arrow on a blue background.

q-11307.text: How can the danger of driving a vehicle in heavy fog be minimised?

options.B: Increase the distance between you and the preceding vehicle.
options.C: Reduce the distance between you and the preceding vehicle.

q-11307.explanation: Correct answer: B. In fog the driver sees the vehicle ahead very late, so a larger distance gives time to react and stop. Reducing the distance or increasing speed leads straight to a rear-end collision and chain collisions.

q-11309.text: What negative effects can snow or ice on the roadway have on the driver?

options.A: Increased tyre grip on the road.
options.B: Reduced tyre grip on the road.

q-11309.explanation: Correct answer: B. Snow and ice form a layer with low friction, so the grip of the tyres on the road falls. The result is a longer braking distance and skidding more easily, so speed and distances must be changed clearly.

q-11310.text: What negative effects can snow or ice on the roadway have on the driver?

options.B: Increased tyre grip on the road.

q-11310.explanation: Correct answer: A. On snow and ice tyre grip is low, so the wheels easily lose contact with the road and the vehicle skids. The braking distance grows at the same time, so you drive more slowly and without sudden steering movements.

q-11314.text: What behaviour increases the risk of skidding on icy road surfaces?
q-11314.explanation: Correct answer: A. Sudden, hard braking exceeds the small grip of ice, the wheels lock and the vehicle stops responding to the steering. On an icy carriageway you brake early, gently and in a straight line.

q-11315.text: What behaviour increases the risk of skidding on icy road surfaces?
q-11315.explanation: Correct answer: B. A sudden increase in speed makes the driven wheels spin and lose contact with the ice, and the rear of the vehicle can slide out sideways. On a slippery surface you accelerate gently and smoothly.

q-11316.text: What behaviour increases the risk of skidding on icy road surfaces?

options.C: Violent turning of the steering wheel.

q-11316.explanation: Correct answer: C. A sudden turn of the steering wheel demands a lateral force from the tyres that ice cannot provide, so the vehicle starts to slide straight on or skids. The steering wheel is handled calmly, without jerks.

q-11317.text: What behaviour increases the risk of skidding on icy road surfaces?

options.A: Maintaining too high speed, particularly in bends.

q-11317.explanation: Correct answer: A. Too high a speed, and on a curve additionally the centrifugal force, exceeds the grip ice can offer and the vehicle slides off its line. Speed is chosen according to the state of the surface, not the signs.

q-11402.text: Is it allowed beyond this sign to overtake a cyclist?
q-11402.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The overtaking ban arising from this sign does not cover two-wheeled vehicles, so a bicycle may be overtaken. The manoeuvre is carried out with a lateral distance of no less than 1 m and only in good visibility.

q-11408.text: In this situation, should the driver pass the vehicle and reduce speed if necessary?
q-11408.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing a vehicle, the driver must keep a safe distance and, if necessary, reduce speed. A lower speed gives time to react when a pedestrian steps out from behind the obstacle or a door opens.

q-11409.text: In this situation, should you assume that a road worker may unexpectedly step onto the road from behind a vehicle undertaking road repair work?
q-11409.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At roadworks, workers move about on and near the carriageway, and a works vehicle hides their figures. The principle of limited trust requires anticipating such a step onto the road, slowing down and increasing the distance.

q-11412.text: In this situation, are you exempt from the obligation to apply a cautious approach to children, because they are in the care of an adult?
q-11412.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The presence of a carer does not release the driver from care, because a child can pull free and suddenly run onto the carriageway. Towards children the principle of limited trust and readiness to brake always apply.

q-11413.text: In this situation, should you keep a close eye on pedestrians and adopt a cautious approach towards children?
q-11413.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Pedestrians, and children in particular, must be watched the whole time you approach them, because their behaviour can be unpredictable. The principle of limited trust means being ready for their mistake and driving correspondingly slower.

q-11415.text: In this situation, should the driver anticipate that a child might suddenly run onto the road from behind the vehicle?
q-11415.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A standing vehicle hides part of the carriageway and the pavement, and a child is short and steps onto the road without assessing the situation. So slow down, move away from the obstacle and be ready to stop.

q-11417.text: Is it always prohibited to drive a moped under the influence of alcohol or substances of similar effect to alcohol?
q-11417.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The ban covers the driver of every vehicle, a moped included, and applies without exception — regardless of the type of road, the time of day and the length of the ride. Breaking it carries liability even when no incident occurred.

q-11418.text: Does alcohol induce excessive self-confidence in a moped driver, which leads to bravado on the road as well as impairs distance assessment and increases reaction time?
q-11418.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Alcohol weakens self-criticism and raises the appetite for risk, while at the same time impairing the judgement of distance and speed and lengthening reaction time. The driver feels more confident, though in reality they control the vehicle worse.

q-11419.text: Does consumption of alcohol by a driver impair the ability to correctly assess risks on the road when driving a quadricycle?
q-11419.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Alcohol impairs attention, perception and the soundness of decisions, so the driver recognises hazards worse and overestimates their own skills. This applies to every vehicle, including a quadricycle, which easily loses stability.

q-11420.text: Should you refrain from driving a moped if you have taken medication of which you have no knowledge or information about how it affects the body and safe driving?
q-11420.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Many medicines cause drowsiness, slowed reactions or visual disturbances, and the driver is responsible for their own psychophysical state. Without knowledge of a preparation's effects, check the leaflet, ask a doctor or do not drive.

q-11422.text: What should you not do when assessing whether an accident victim is conscious or not?

options.B: Check if he reacts to your voice.
options.C: Gently shake him by the shoulders.

q-11422.explanation: Correct answer: A. Consciousness is checked with a loud question and a gentle shake of the shoulders. Splashing water on the face achieves nothing, risks choking and hypothermia, and with a spinal injury may worsen the casualty's condition.

q-11425.text: What is the first thing you should do in case of leakage of dangerous substances from a vehicle?

options.A: Save life and health of people.
options.C: Prevent the leakage of dangerous substances.

q-11425.explanation: Correct answer: A. Human life and health always come first: move away and move others away from the leak, positioning yourselves upwind, and call the services. Protecting the environment and stemming the leak are jobs for rescuers with equipment.

q-11426.text: Which of the following authorities will you call in order to commence rescue operations consisting of neutralization of dangerous substances on the road?
q-11426.explanation: Correct answer: C. Chemical rescue and the neutralisation of hazardous substances are the job of the State Fire Service, which has the equipment and training for it. The Police secure the scene and the traffic, and the Road Transport Inspectorate checks the carriage.

q-11427.text: Can you extinguish fire from a cistern transporting gasoline, by yourself?

options.C: Yes, only by means of a powder extinguisher.

q-11427.explanation: Correct answer: B. Burning fuel in a tanker risks a sudden flare-up and explosion, and a hand-held extinguisher is useless against such a fire. Move away to a safe distance, warn others and call the fire brigade.

q-11428.text: Which of the following numbers must you call in order to report a car accident involving a vehicle transporting dangerous goods?
q-11428.explanation: Correct answer: C. The incident is reported on the emergency number 112 or directly to the fire brigade on 998. The dispatcher must be told the location, the type of vehicle, the markings on the tanker and the number of casualties.

q-11429.text: If a victim has mistakenly swallowed a caustic substance, should you induce vomiting?

options.C: Yes, but only if the corrosive substance was highly diluted.

q-11429.explanation: Correct answer: B. Vomiting takes a corrosive substance through the oesophagus a second time, deepening the burn and risking choking. Vomiting is not induced in the casualty; instead help is called and the dispatcher's instructions are followed.

q-11432.text: After what time the does the ischemic brain of an accident casualty die?
q-11432.explanation: Correct answer: A. Without circulation the brain cells stop receiving oxygen, and after about 4–5 minutes irreversible damage occurs. That is why resuscitation is started immediately, in parallel with calling an ambulance.

q-11433.text: The recovery position is deemed safe for the person injured in a road accident because:

options.A: it is comfortable for the injured person.
options.B: it is stable, it provides a clear airway and prevents the injured person from choking.
options.C: it enables the rescuer to perform resuscitation.

q-11433.explanation: Correct answer: B. In an unconscious person who is breathing, the recovery position keeps the airway open, prevents the tongue from falling back and lets fluid drain from the mouth. The position is stable, so the casualty does not roll onto their back.

q-11434.text: How long should you perform cardiac massage and artificial respiration to a person injured in an accident?

options.B: Until the person regains their breath or is handed over to a paramedic.

q-11434.explanation: Correct answer: B. Resuscitation is carried out without breaks until normal breathing returns or the casualty is taken over by the emergency medical team. Predetermined time limits, such as 5 or 60 minutes, have no justification.

q-11436.text: What is the maximum front overhang of a load transported in a motor vehicle, counting from the driver's seat?
q-11436.explanation: Correct answer: B. A load may not protrude in front of the vehicle further than 1.5 m measured from the driver's seat. A longer overhang limits the field of vision and makes it harder to judge distance during manoeuvres.

q-11437.text: Will the airbag serve its function during an accident, if you fail to fasten the seatbelts?

options.A: Yes, they are two independent safety systems.
options.B: No, if the airbag opens, this will expose you to head or spine injuries.
options.C: Yes, the airbag substitutes for the use of seat belts.

q-11437.explanation: Correct answer: B. The airbag is a system supplementing the belts, not a replacement for them. Without belts fastened, the body moves forward and meets the inflating airbag, which risks serious injury to the head or spine.

q-11438.text: The height of a vehicle with a load must not exceed:
q-11438.explanation: Correct answer: C. A vehicle together with its load may not exceed 4 m in height. Regardless of this, remember flyovers and tunnels where a sign gives a lower permitted value.

q-11440.text: The speed limiter fitted in a lorry of gross vehicle weight rating of over 3.5 tons should limit the maximum speed to:
q-11440.explanation: Correct answer: A. The limiter in a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t is set to 90 km/h. This does not release the driver from observing the lower limits in force on the road in question.

q-11442.text: How many fire extinguishers should be fitted in a lorry in which you carry persons outside the driver's cab?
q-11442.explanation: Correct answer: B. A lorry carrying people outside the driver's cab must be equipped with two fire extinguishers. They are placed so as to be easily accessible and kept in a condition fit for immediate use.

q-11443.text: Are you allowed to carry loose material in a lorry, when the vehicle height together with the load is 4.5 m?

options.A: Yes, but only on a motorway.
options.B: Yes, on all roads except in a built-up area.
options.C: No, it is forbidden on all roads.

q-11443.explanation: Correct answer: C. The permitted height of a vehicle with its load is 4 m, so a combination measuring 4.5 m may not travel on any road. The type of road changes nothing here — the load must be reloaded or lowered.

q-11444.text: You are carrying a load of 3m in width in a lorry of 2.55m in width. How far can the load protrude from one side of the vehicle?
q-11444.explanation: Correct answer: C. A load may not protrude sideways further than 23 cm from the plane of the vehicle's outline, so it must be arranged symmetrically. A greater overhang requires a permit for the journey of an oversize vehicle.

q-11445.text: The pressure on a single non-drive axle must not exceed:
q-11445.explanation: Correct answer: B. The load on a single non-driven axle may not exceed 10 tonnes. On particular roads the permitted load is sometimes lower, as signs inform, and exceeding it requires a permit.

q-11447.text: When driving a lorry what distance are you obliged to keep while overtaking another lorry?
q-11447.explanation: Correct answer: A. When overtaking another vehicle, the rules require a safe distance, without giving a figure. A fixed dimension, no less than 1 m, applies to overtaking a cyclist, a moped rider and a pedestrian.

q-11450.text: Which of the following factors has the greatest impact on the grip of the truck tyre to the ground?

options.B: The engine power of a vehicle.
options.C: The type and condition of the road surface.

q-11450.explanation: Correct answer: C. Grip is decided above all by the type and state of the surface — dry, wet, icy or muddy asphalt behaves differently. Tyre size and engine power do not in themselves create grip.

q-11452.text: With overheating of the brakes the braking performance:

options.C: does not change, regardless of the degree of overheating.

q-11452.explanation: Correct answer: B. Overheated linings lose their coefficient of friction, so at the same pedal pressure the brakes work more weakly and the braking distance grows. On long descents you brake with the engine or the retarder, sparing the service brakes.

q-11453.text: Too high pressure in the lorry tyres:

options.A: may shorten the braking distance of the vehicle.
options.B: may lengthen the braking distance of the vehicle.
options.C: does not change the braking distance of the vehicle.

q-11453.explanation: Correct answer: B. An over-inflated tyre touches the carriageway with a smaller area, so grip falls and the braking distance grows. Pressure is set according to the manufacturer's recommendations and the vehicle's current load.

q-11457.text: While driving a truck, when do you have to turn off the rear anti-fog lights?
q-11457.explanation: Correct answer: C. Rear fog lights are used only in severely limited visibility; once it rises to 60 m they must be switched off. They shine very brightly and dazzle drivers behind.

q-11463.text: How should you behave in the event of missing an exit on a road with heightened traffic?

options.A: Stop at the next traffic lights to ask pedestrians for further direction.
options.B: While driving, check for a return road on a road map.
options.C: Continue driving to a place where can safely stop the vehicle.

q-11463.explanation: Correct answer: C. A missed exit never justifies harsh braking, reversing or stopping on the carriageway. You drive on and plan the return to the right route only in a safe place.

q-11464.text: How should you negotiate a bend when driving a truck?

options.A: By smoothly adjusting the trajectory, taking the bend into account.
options.B: By negotiating the bend with the clutch pedal pressed.
options.C: By maintaining the engine's maximum RPM along the whole length of the bend.

q-11464.explanation: Correct answer: A. Smooth steering through a curve does not upset the load and keeps the vehicle within its lane. Driving with the clutch pressed removes control of the drive, and high revs only increase the risk of a skid.

q-11467.text: What is the most effective method of acceleration in a truck?

options.A: By reaching the maximum rotations of the engine in all subsequent gears.
options.B: By changing gears in such a way that the RPM's of the engines are not lower than the value at which the green area on the speedometer starts.
options.C: By using all gears successively, even though the speedometer indicator is in the red area.

q-11467.explanation: Correct answer: B. The green band of the rev counter marks the range of most favourable torque, so changing gear within it gives the best acceleration. Revving the engine to the maximum or entering the red band only increases fuel consumption and the load on the mechanisms.

q-11469.text: In which of the following cases is the use of a cruise control most justified?

options.A: While driving on roads in a mountainous area.
options.C: While driving for a long time at constant speed.

q-11469.explanation: Correct answer: C. Cruise control comes into its own on long stretches with steady traffic, because it holds a constant speed and reduces fuel consumption. In town and in the mountains speed has to change constantly, so the device is then a hindrance.

q-11471.text: What is the function of the ABS in a lorry?

options.A: It shortens the braking distance in all weather conditions.
options.B: It is insensitive to the type of road surface.
options.C: It enables driving during emergency braking.

q-11471.explanation: Correct answer: C. ABS does not let the wheels lock, so the tyres keep their lateral force and the vehicle still responds to the steering during emergency braking. The system does not shorten the braking distance in all conditions — on gravel or snow it can even be longer.

q-11472.text: Which of these methods of braking a lorry equipped with an ABS system guarantees the fastest way of stopping the vehicle?

options.A: Pulse pressing of the brake pedal.
options.B: Simultaneously pressing the brake and clutch pedals as strong as possible.

q-11472.explanation: Correct answer: B. In a vehicle with ABS you brake with full force, because the system makes sure the wheels do not lock, and the pressed clutch prevents the engine from stalling. Pulsing and gradually increasing the pedal pressure only lengthen the braking distance.

q-11474.text: Can a cargo cause a truck to exceed the maximum permissible capacity of the vehicle?

options.A: Yes, but by no more than 20%.
options.B: Yes, as long as the permitted axle load on the road is not exceeded.

q-11474.explanation: Correct answer: C. The payload specified by the manufacturer is a design limit and may not be exceeded in any way. An overloaded vehicle brakes and handles worse, and its components and the road surface wear out faster.

q-11475.text: How should a load be placed in a truck?

options.A: In a way, so that it does not exceed the total width of the vehicle.
options.B: In a way, so that it does not overhang at the back for more than 1 meter from the rear outline of the vehicle.
options.C: In a way, so that it does not affect the stability of the vehicle and does not obstruct driving.

q-11475.explanation: Correct answer: C. The basic condition is that the load must not impair the vehicle's stability or hinder steering. It is distributed evenly and as low as possible, secured against shifting, and so that it does not cover the lights and plates.

q-11476.text: Which of the following methods of marking a load overhanging for more than 0.5 m from the rear outline of the truck is correct?

options.A: A red flag with the dimensions of 30cm x 30cm.
options.C: A plaque with white-and-red stripes with a total surface area of no less than 1000 cm2.

q-11476.explanation: Correct answer: C. A load protruding more than 0.5 m at the rear is marked with a red-and-white striped panel with an area of at least 1,000 cm², placed at its end. After dusk a red light and a reflective element are added.

q-11477.text: Can you drive a truck whose width, including the cargo, exceeds the maximum permissible width?

options.A: Yes, without an additional permit, if the route allows it.
options.C: Yes, but provided you obtain a suitable permit.

q-11477.explanation: Correct answer: C. Exceeding the permitted width makes the combination an oversize vehicle, which may travel only once a permit has been obtained. The permit specifies the route and the conditions of the journey, for example marking and piloting.

q-11480.text: Does the location of the centre of gravity of a load transported by a truck affect the stability of the truck?

options.A: Yes, it may reduce the stability of the vehicle.
options.C: Yes, but only on sharp bends.

q-11480.explanation: Correct answer: A. A high or asymmetric centre of gravity increases the vehicle's tendency to lean when turning, braking and in a crosswind. The load is therefore arranged low and evenly on both sides.

q-11482.text: Can a liquid cargo in partly-filled containers or cisterns affect the stability of the vehicle?

options.A: No, if the volume of the load does not exceed a half of the container.

q-11482.explanation: Correct answer: C. Liquid in a partly filled tank sloshes freely and, under braking and on a bend, strikes the tanker's wall with its mass, changing the distribution of the load. That is why you drive smoothly, with a margin of speed and distance.

q-11483.text: When you transport heavy working machines or construction equipment, are you obliged to use steel ropes and wedges?

options.B: No, if the parking brake is put on in the transported vehicles.
options.C: No, such load may be transported without securing it for short distances.

q-11483.explanation: Correct answer: A. Heavy machines must be immobilised with lashings and chocks, because under braking enormous inertial forces act on them. An applied parking brake alone will not hold the machine, and the length of the route is of no significance here.

q-11486.text: Can you drive a truck whose weight, including the cargo, is higher than the admissible weight along a given section of the road?

options.B: Yes, but provided that a relevant permit is obtained.
options.C: Yes, but provided that a special fee is paid to the head of the commune (vogt).

q-11486.explanation: Correct answer: B. The journey of a vehicle heavier than a given stretch of road allows requires a permit, in which the route and the conditions of carriage are specified. No fee paid on your own initiative replaces such a permit.

q-11487.text: Can you drive a truck whose height, including the cargo, exceeds the permissible height?

options.A: Yes, but provided that a relevant permit is obtained.

q-11487.explanation: Correct answer: A. Exceeding the permitted height requires a permit for the journey of an oversize vehicle, in which a route is set that avoids flyovers, tunnels and overhead lines that are too low. Without such a document, driving is prohibited.

q-11488.text: While driving a truck, in what circumstances should you make sure that the transported cargo is properly secured?
q-11488.explanation: Correct answer: B. Harsh braking may shift or loosen the load, so before driving on the driver checks its fastening and arrangement. The criterion is an event that may have disturbed the fastening, not the distance covered as such.

q-11489.text: How is the failure of the anti-block system (ABS) indicated?

options.A: By a control light on the dashboard.
options.C: By activation of the emergency lights.

q-11489.explanation: Correct answer: A. A fault in the anti-lock system is signalled by a warning light on the dashboard that comes on and does not go out. The brakes still work, but without protection against the wheels locking, so on a slippery surface you must brake more carefully.

q-11490.text: What may be the consequences of a leakage of liquid from the hydraulic shock absorber?

options.A: Increased damping of chassis vibrations on uneven road.
options.C: Reduced wheel traction on uneven road.

q-11490.explanation: Correct answer: C. A leaking shock absorber stops damping vibrations, so the wheel bounces over bumps and loses contact with the surface. The result is less grip, a longer braking distance and worse stability of the vehicle.

q-11491.text: What might be the result of a damage to one of the direction indicator bulbs?

options.A: The other indicator bulbs will also stop working.
options.B: Indicator breaker will operate at an increased rate.

q-11491.explanation: Correct answer: B. After one bulb burns out, the load on the circuit changes and the flasher begins to flash clearly faster — a fault signal for the driver. The other indicators keep working, and the failed bulb should be replaced immediately.

q-11492.text: What is the minimum permissible depth of the tyre tread pattern of a lorry?
q-11492.explanation: Correct answer: B. The minimum permitted tread depth is 1.6 mm. Shallower tread clears water from under the wheel less well and loses grip abruptly, especially on a wet surface.

q-11493.text: Which of the following actions should be taken when the red warning light of the cooling liquid temperature comes on during a drive?

options.A: Stop the vehicle and switch off the engine.

q-11493.explanation: Correct answer: A. A red coolant temperature light means the engine is overheating. Stop the vehicle as quickly and safely as possible and switch off the engine, because driving on risks serious damage to it.

q-11494.text: Which of the following actions should be taken when the red warning light of the engine oil pressure comes on during a drive?

options.A: Stop the vehicle and switch off the engine.

q-11494.explanation: Correct answer: A. A red oil-pressure light means the engine's lubrication is not assured. Stop the vehicle immediately and safely and switch off the engine, because running without oil pressure destroys it in a very short time.

q-11496.text: You need rest. Are you allowed to pull over for a short while on the presented hard shoulder?
q-11496.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In this place stopping on the shoulder is not permitted — this follows from the sign or from the type of road visible in the material. For a rest you should use a designated car park or a service area.

q-11497.text: Are you allowed to continue driving straight on the current lane if there are no other vehicles on the right half of the road?
q-11497.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The direction of travel from a given lane is set by signs or arrows on the roadway, and the driver must comply with them. The lane you are in does not allow going straight ahead here, so you must change it early enough.

q-11498.text: Is it proper in this situation to continue driving on the same lane?
q-11498.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The lane you are in allows travel in the chosen direction, and the signs and road markings do not require changing it. Unnecessary moving between lanes is an additional manoeuvre that only increases the risk.

q-11499.text: Intending to leave this intersection, did you change the lane in the right moment?
q-11499.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The lane consistent with the intended direction is taken early enough, before the manoeuvre becomes necessary, after checking the situation behind and signalling with the indicator. A last-moment lane change forces others to brake.

q-11500.text: You intend to turn left at the nearest junction. Should you immediately start changing lanes?
q-11500.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before turning left you must take the correct position on the roadway in good time, i.e. the lane closest to its central part. The earlier you begin the manoeuvre, the more time you have to observe and the less you surprise others.

q-11501.text: In this situation, can you resign from using the indicator when changing lanes?
q-11501.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver is obliged to signal an intended lane change in advance and clearly with the indicator, regardless of whether they see other road users beside them. The signal is switched off as soon as the manoeuvre is completed.

q-11502.text: You are driving a combination of vehicles whose length is 10 metres, and carrying a load which protrudes from the back of the trailer at 0.5 metres. Are you allowed to drive onto the road beyond this sign?
q-11502.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign prohibits entry to vehicles longer than the value given on it, and a load protruding beyond the outline is included in the length. The vehicle combination here therefore measures 10.5 metres and exceeds the permitted length.

q-11503.text: Does the value given on this sign refer to the gross vehicle weight of the vehicle?
q-11503.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The value given on the sign refers to the actual total mass, that is, the mass of the vehicle together with its load, driver and passengers at that moment. What counts is therefore not the permissible value in the registration document but the actual state.

q-11504.text: You intend to turn left. Do you have the right of way over the vehicle approaching from the left?
q-11504.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority belongs to you, and the vehicle approaching from the left is obliged to give way. When turning left, however, you must let pass vehicles coming straight from the opposite direction and pedestrians stepping onto the cross roadway.

q-11505.text: You intend to turn left. Are you obliged to yield the right of way to the vehicle approaching from the right?
q-11505.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority at this intersection follows from the signs visible in the material and belongs to the tram, so it does not give way to the vehicle approaching from the right. You must, however, watch whether the driver of that vehicle really is slowing down.

q-11506.text: Are you allowed to haul a vehicle being driven by an intoxicated person?
q-11506.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Towing is prohibited when the towed vehicle is driven by a person in the state after alcohol consumption. Such a driver is still driving the vehicle, braking and holding its course, so they must be sober just like the driver of the towing vehicle.

q-11507.text: Can taking soporifics or sedatives affect the capability of driving a vehicle?
q-11507.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Sleeping pills and sedatives lengthen reaction time, weaken concentration and cause drowsiness, and their effect can still be felt many hours after taking them. Before driving, check the leaflet or ask a doctor.

q-11508.text: Can placing decorative elements in such a way limit visibility of the road and distract the driver’s attention?
q-11508.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Objects placed in the field of view hide part of the road and draw the eye, especially when they move. The windows and mirrors must stay clear, and the driver is responsible for ensuring adequate visibility.

q-11509.text: Can snow-covered windows and mirrors on the car you are going to drive affect your assessment of the situation on the road?
q-11509.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Snow on the windows and mirrors hides other road users, and the most dangerous thing is what the driver does not see at all. Before moving off, clear all the windows, mirrors, lights and number plates.

q-11510.text: Should you refrain from driving a vehicle in the morning, if the night before you consumed a large amount of alcohol?
q-11510.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Alcohol is removed from the body slowly, so after heavy drinking you may still have it in your blood in the morning, on top of tiredness and slower reactions. You may get behind the wheel only when fully sober.

q-11513.text: What should you do, if you notice that an unconscious victim of a road accident is not breathing?

options.A: For fear of a possible spinal injury, leave the injured in the vehicle until the emergency medical services arrive.
options.B: Remove the injured from the crashed vehicle and commence resuscitation.
options.C: Leave the injured in the vehicle, cover him with a thermal insulation blanket and wait for the emergency medical services to arrive.

q-11513.explanation: Correct answer: B. Absence of breathing is an immediate threat to life, and effective resuscitation cannot be carried out in a vehicle seat. The casualty must be got out, protecting the head and spine as far as possible, laid on a hard surface, and chest compressions begun at once.

q-11515.text: While driving a truck, when must you switch from high-beam to low-beam lights?

options.A: Always when you see a vehicle in front of you.
options.B: Always when there is a possibility of blinding the driver of the vehicle in front of you.
options.C: Always when you see a single pedestrian on the road.

q-11515.explanation: Correct answer: B. Main-beam headlights may not be used when they could dazzle another driver — including one ahead of you, via their mirrors. The criterion is the possibility of dazzling, not merely the fact of seeing someone on the road.

q-11516.text: You intend to drive a truck for the purpose of transporting goods. Are you obliged to make sure that the transported cargo is properly secured?

options.A: Yes, you have to check the safety and correctness of cargo positioning.
options.B: Yes, but only in the event of doubts regarding the safety of the cargo transportation.
options.C: No, the driver is not responsible for the cargo itself, but only for its transport.

q-11516.explanation: Correct answer: A. Before setting off, the driver checks that the load is correctly arranged and fastened, so that it does not shift, fall off or impair the vehicle's stability. The check is always compulsory, not only when doubts arise.

q-11517.text: Which of the following methods of marking a load overhanging more than 0.5 m from the rear outline of the truck is correct?

options.A: A white flag with the dimensions of 33cm x 34cm.
options.B: A geometric solid with white-and-red stripes, with a total capacity of at least 1000 cm2.

q-11517.explanation: Correct answer: B. A load protruding more than 0.5 m at the rear is marked with a clearly visible red-and-white striped geometric shape with a total area of no less than 1,000 cm². A white flag or a steady orange light does not serve for this marking.

q-11518.text: Which of the following methods of marking a load overhanging more than 0.5 m from the rear outline of the truck is correct?

options.A: White-and-red stripes with a total surface area of at least 1000cm2, placed directly on the load.
options.B: A plaque with the dimensions of at least 50x50 cm with black-and-yellow stripes.
options.C: A geometric solid with red-and-white stripes.

q-11518.explanation: Correct answer: A. A load protruding more than 0.5 m at the rear is marked with red-and-white stripes with a total area of at least 1,000 cm², placed directly on the load. Black-and-yellow and black-and-white colours are not correct in this case.

q-11519.text: The gross vehicle weight of a trailer pulled by a lorry of gross vehicle weight rating over 3.5 tons must not exceed:

options.A: the kerb weight of the lorry.
options.B: the gross vehicle weight of the lorry.
options.C: the gross vehicle weight of the lorry increased by 40%.

q-11519.explanation: Correct answer: C. The actual total mass of a trailer towed by a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may not exceed the actual total mass of that lorry plus 40%. Too heavy a trailer pushes the towing vehicle and lengthens the braking distance.

q-11520.text: Passage of the combination of vehicles consisting of a lorry and two trailers:

options.A: does not require a permit regardless of the load being carried.
options.B: does not require a permit, if no load is being carried on the trailers.

q-11520.explanation: Correct answer: C. As a rule a lorry may tow one trailer, so a combination with two trailers is allowed only on the basis of a permit. It makes no difference whether the trailers are loaded or empty.

q-11521.text: How does doubling of the lorry speed influence the length of the braking distance?

options.B: It increases the braking distance by four times.
options.C: It does not change the length of the braking distance.

q-11521.explanation: Correct answer: B. The braking distance grows with the square of the speed, so doubling it makes that distance roughly four times longer. In a loaded lorry the effect is even more pronounced because of the large mass.

q-11524.text: When driving in fog, the braking distance:

options.A: may increase due to the wet road.
options.B: may decrease due to the increase of the tyre grip to the road surface.
options.C: neither increases nor decreases, because both fog or wetness have no impact on it.

q-11524.explanation: Correct answer: A. Fog settles on the surface, the carriageway becomes damp, tyre grip falls and the braking distance grows. Limited visibility adds to this, so speed must be reduced early enough.

q-11526.text: How should you hold a steering wheel when driving a truck straight on?

options.A: With both hands in any place on the steering wheel.
options.B: With the left hand holding the steering wheel between 9 and 10 o'clock, and the right hand in any place on the steering wheel.
options.C: With the left hand holding the steering wheel between 9 and 10 o'clock and the right hand between 2 and 3 o'clock.

q-11526.explanation: Correct answer: C. A symmetrical grip — left hand between 9 and 10 o'clock, right between 2 and 3 — gives the greatest control of the line and allows an immediate reaction without shuffling the hands. This position is also safer when the airbag deploys.

q-11527.text: Which of the following driving techniques is the best when driving a loaded lorry downhill?

options.A: Driving downhill with an appropriately chosen gear and using the retarder.
options.B: Driving downhill with the highest possible gear and adjusting the speed by using the service brake.
options.C: Driving downhill with the neutral gear and adjusting the speed by using the service brake.

q-11527.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a descent speed is held with engine braking in a suitably low gear and with the retarder, and the service brake stays in reserve. Continuous braking with it overheats the system and reduces its effectiveness, and neutral deprives the vehicle of controlled slowing.

q-11528.text: What is the penalty for a lorry driver carrying three persons more than the number of seats stated on the vehicle's registration document?

options.A: Retention of driving licence for 3 months.
options.B: Retention of driving licence for 3 months and a driver qualification check.
options.C: Retention of driving licence for 6 months.

q-11528.explanation: Correct answer: A. Carrying more people than entered in the registration document by more than two results in the driving licence being retained for 3 months. An additional check of qualifications is not provided for in this case.

q-11531.text: You are driving on a priority road. In this situation, should you refrain from driving further, if necessary?
q-11531.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Priority does not release you from the duty to avoid danger — if another road user forces their way through or the situation becomes dangerous, you must refrain from continuing. Priority gives an entitlement, not an order to drive at all costs.

q-12478.text: What is the penalty for a bus driver, excluding a municipal public transport bus with designated standing places, for carrying more than five persons in excess of the number of seats stated in the vehicle registration document?

options.A: Retention of driving licence for 3 months.
options.C: A fine of PLN 500 and 10 penalty points.

q-12478.explanation: Correct answer: A. Carrying in a bus more people than entered in the registration document by more than five results in the driving licence being retained for 3 months. The exception is public transport buses with standing places provided for.

q-12528.text: Are you required to exercise extreme caution when merging into traffic?
q-12528.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver joining the traffic — leaving a car park or an internal road, or moving off from the edge of the roadway — is obliged to exercise particular caution and give way to all road users already travelling on the road.

q-12556.text: Is it prohibited to stop a vehicle directly behind a visible indicator post?
