q-12556.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Marker posts announce a railway crossing, and in its vicinity a prohibition on stopping and parking applies. A vehicle standing at this place would obscure the view of the tracks and hinder evacuation from the crossing.

q-12562.text: Are you required to permit a lorry to merge into traffic in this situation?
q-12562.explanation: Correct answer: NO. It is the driver joining the traffic who gives way, and the driver on the road has no duty to let them in. You may make the manoeuvre easier for them out of courtesy, but only when this creates no obstruction or danger to others.

q-12564.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop your vehicle before the level crossing?
q-12564.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An unconditional stop before the crossing is required only when a sign, a light signal or a lowered barrier orders it. There is no such order here, but you must approach with special care and make sure the track is clear.

q-12575.text: In this situation, is it permissible to continue driving in the left lane if the right lane is free?
q-12575.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a road with several lanes in one direction, the left lane serves primarily for overtaking. Since the right lane is clear, you must return to it, because occupying the left one without need obstructs other drivers.

q-12605.text: Should you exercise caution in this situation and keep a safe distance from the passing vehicle coming from the opposite direction?
q-12605.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing an oncoming vehicle, you must remain cautious and keep a safe lateral distance, chosen according to the width of the roadway, the size of both vehicles and the state of the shoulder. When there is little room, you must additionally reduce speed.

q-12618.text: Are you allowed to increase your speed to 130 km/h beyond this sign?
q-12618.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A speed of 130 km/h is permitted only on a motorway and only for selected vehicles. The sign visible in the material does not introduce such permission, so a lower limit applies, and speed must in any case be adapted to the conditions.

q-12640.text: Are you permitted to change lanes at a point marked in this way?
q-12640.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The markings at this place prohibit crossing the line separating the lanes, and without that a lane change is impossible. The manoeuvre will be permitted only beyond the section covered by the prohibition.

q-12714.text: Should you expect three dangerous bends beyond this sign, all of which may be to the left?
q-12714.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a series of at least three dangerous bends, and its drawing shows only the direction of the first one. The following ones may go either way, so all three may turn out to be bends to the left.

q-12737.text: Does this sign warn of the possibility of ice on the roadway?
q-12737.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces a section where black ice or icing may occur on the roadway, especially on bridges, in dips and in shaded places. You should reduce speed, lengthen the distance and avoid sudden braking and steering.

q-12741.text: Does this sign warn of a dangerous turn to the right?
q-12741.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a bend in the direction in which the arrow on its drawing is curved, i.e. to the right. Speed is reduced before entering the curve, not during it, because braking in a bend easily leads to a skid.

q-12779.text: Do you have to exercise extra caution when overtaking the cyclist?
q-12779.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking a cyclist requires special care and a safe lateral distance of no less than 1 m. The cyclist may drift off their line because of a bump or a gust of wind, so you slow down before the manoeuvre.

q-12786.text: Are you obliged to yield the right of way to vehicles approaching from the left at the nearest junction?
q-12786.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to give way to vehicles from the left follows from the sign or signal in force before this intersection. You should approach at a speed that allows you to stop and watch the road on both sides.

q-12825.text: Are you permitted to overtake a rail vehicle in this situation?
q-12825.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking a rail vehicle is permitted if neither a sign nor road markings prohibit it; one running on tracks in the middle of the roadway is overtaken on the right. You must watch out for passengers getting on and off.

q-12826.text: Is it prohibited to overtake a rail vehicle in this situation?
q-12826.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place overtaking is prohibited neither by a sign, nor by road markings, nor by the nature of the road. The manoeuvre is performed with particular caution, after making sure the road ahead of the vehicle is clear and no one is stepping onto the tracks.

q-12832.text: When approaching a pedestrian crossing, are you obliged to observe the surrounding area?
q-12832.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Approaching a crossing, the driver takes special care and looks not only at the crossing itself but also at the pavement and the verge beside it, from where a pedestrian may step out. The speed must allow you to stop before the crossing.

q-12890.text: Should speed and distance from other road users be adapted to the road surface condition?

options.A: Yes, but only in built-up areas.
options.B: Yes, because the condition of the road surface has a significant impact on braking distances.

q-12890.explanation: Correct answer: B. The state of the surface decides grip, and thus the length of the braking distance and the distance needed from the vehicle ahead. The duty to adapt speed always applies — outside a built-up area too, and in all weather.

q-12942.text: Does the 50 km/h speed limit apply 24 hours a day in built-up areas?

options.B: No, only from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.
options.C: No, only from dusk to dawn.

q-12942.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a built-up area the 50 km/h limit applies around the clock, and the time of day has no effect on it. It runs from the sign marking the start of the built-up area to the sign marking its end, unless another sign introduces a different value.

q-13005.text: When approaching a pedestrian crossing, are you obliged to observe the surrounding area?
q-13005.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care at a crossing means also watching what is happening beside it — on the pavement, the verge and behind obstacles that block the view. Speed is chosen so that you can stop before the crossing.

q-13006.text: In this situation, are you allowed to continue driving without stopping before the pedestrian crossing?
q-13006.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A pedestrian on the crossing or stepping onto it has priority, so the driver must stop the vehicle and let them cross. Driving through without stopping would, in this situation, be forcing priority.

q-13034.text: In the visible situation, is it only permissible to turn left from this lane?
q-13034.explanation: Correct answer: NO. From the lane intended for turning left you may also turn around, unless a sign prohibits it. The directions permitted from a given lane are always read from the signs and the arrows on the roadway before the intersection.

q-13035.text: When driving a motor vehicle with a trailer in a residential area, are you entitled to drive at 30 km/h?
q-13035.explanation: Correct answer: C. In a residential zone the permitted speed is 20 km/h, so driving at 30 km/h is not allowed at any time of day. In such a zone a pedestrian may use the whole width of the road and has priority over vehicles.

q-13037.text: At what speed should the driver of a passenger car drive behind this vehicle if the tunnel is outside a built-up area and its length is 600 m?

options.A: Such speed as to maintain a distance of at least 50 m.
options.B: Such speed as to maintain a distance of at least 80 m.
options.C: Such speed as to maintain a distance of at least 5 m.

q-13037.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a tunnel longer than 500 m outside a built-up area, the driver of a car keeps a distance of at least 50 m from the vehicle ahead. Speed is chosen so that this distance is maintained for the whole of the passage.

q-13038.text: What is the minimum distance you must maintain from the vehicle in front of you if you are travelling on this road with your passenger car at the maximum permitted speed?
q-13038.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a road of this type the minimum distance in metres equals half the numerical value of the speed in km/h. Driving a car at the maximum permitted speed, that gives 70 m.

q-13040.text: Should the design of the moped limit its speed?
q-13040.explanation: Correct answer: C. A moped is a vehicle whose design limits its speed to 45 km/h. If a vehicle can go faster, it is no longer a moped, and different requirements and different driving entitlements apply to it.

q-13041.text: What is the maximum speed allowed beyond these signs when you are carrying a six-year-old child in the sidecar of a motorbike?
q-13041.explanation: Correct answer: B. When carrying a child under seven in a motorcycle's sidecar, you may not ride faster than 40 km/h. This restriction applies regardless of the higher value the signs on the stretch permit.

q-13042.text: What distance from the preceding vehicle should you maintain when driving a passenger car on this road?

options.A: At least 30 m if I am travelling at 60 km/h.
options.B: A distance necessary to avoid a collision should the preceding vehicle brake or stop.
options.C: Any distance, if the preceding vehicle in the same lane is travelling at a constant speed.

q-13042.explanation: Correct answer: B. The general rule says the distance must be such as to avoid a collision if the vehicle ahead brakes or stops. Specific values in metres apply only on selected roads and in longer tunnels.

q-13044.text: What is the minimum distance you must maintain from the vehicle in front of you when driving a 6-tonne lorry at the maximum permitted speed on this road?
q-13044.explanation: Correct answer: B. On this road the minimum distance in metres is half the numerical value of the speed in km/h. A lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 80 km/h, which gives 40 m.

q-13046.text: What is the minimum distance you must maintain from the vehicle in front?

options.B: Such that other overtaking vehicles can safely enter the gap maintained between these vehicles.
options.C: 40 m if you are travelling at 80 km/h.

q-13046.explanation: Correct answer: C. On this road the minimum distance in metres is half the numerical value of the speed in km/h, so at 80 km/h it is 40 m. The rules set no single fixed value applying in every situation.

q-13047.text: At what speed is a motorbike not allowed to travel on this road?

options.A: 20 km/h, regardless of the prevailing road conditions.
options.C: 80 km/h if you are carrying a 6 year old child.

q-13047.explanation: Correct answer: C. When carrying a child under seven on a motorcycle, you may not exceed 40 km/h, so riding at 80 km/h is prohibited in this situation. The other values listed do not in themselves breach the ban.

q-13048.text: Which of the speed limit signs does not apply to the driver of a moped?
q-13048.explanation: Correct answer: C. The limit has no practical significance for a moped rider when the value on the sign is higher than the speed to which the vehicle's design limits them, that is, 45 km/h. Values below that threshold a moped rider must respect.

q-13049.text: Who does the speed limit expressed by these signs apply to?

options.C: The driver of a motor vehicle with the exception of a motorbike.

q-13049.explanation: Correct answer: B. A speed-limit sign binds every driver of a motor vehicle, and in practice restricts the one who can go faster than the value given — that is, the motorcyclist. A moped will not reach such a speed anyway because of its design.

q-13050.text: What is the maximum speed permitted in a built-up area when you are carrying a five-year-old child on a light quadricycle?
q-13050.explanation: Correct answer: B. When carrying a child under seven in a light quadricycle, you may not drive faster than 40 km/h. The general limit of 50 km/h in a built-up area does not apply here, because the lower value is binding.

q-13051.text: At what speed may one drive on a single carriageway road marked as such?
q-13051.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a road of this type with a single carriageway a car may travel at no more than 100 km/h. Higher values apply to dual carriageways and motorways, and speed must be adapted to the traffic conditions anyway.

q-13052.text: On which road does the driver have to keep a strict minimum distance from the preceding vehicle?

options.B: On a dual carriageway road with at least two lanes dedicated to each direction of traffic.
options.C: On a single carriageway road outside a built-up area.

q-13052.explanation: Correct answer: A. The numerically defined distance — half the value of the speed, in metres — applies on a motorway and on an expressway. On other roads the general rule applies: the distance must allow a collision to be avoided.

q-13053.text: What driver assistance devices help to maintain a proper distance from the preceding vehicle?
q-13053.explanation: Correct answer: A. Adaptive cruise control measures the distance to the vehicle ahead and regulates speed itself, keeping the set gap. Lane assist watches the lateral position, and stability control reacts only to a loss of grip.

q-13054.text: What is the permissible speed limit for a vehicle with a device projecting forward more than 1.5 m from the driver's seat?

options.C: 30 km/h regardless of the area in which it is travelling.

q-13054.explanation: Correct answer: B. A vehicle with equipment protruding more than 1.5 m forward of the driver's seat may travel at no more than 60 km/h outside a built-up area. A large overhang limits visibility and worsens manoeuvrability, so the limit is lower than usual.

q-13056.text: What is the permissible speed limit for a passenger car with a trailer on a road signposted as such?
q-13056.explanation: Correct answer: B. On a stretch marked with this sign a car with a trailer may travel at no more than 50 km/h. Towing a trailer never entitles you to exceed the limit in force on a stretch of road.

q-13057.text: What is the required minimum distance between organised columns of motorbikes travelling on a motorway?

options.B: A distance equal to half the speed in km/h expressed in metres of the first motorcyclist at the head of the second column.

q-13057.explanation: Correct answer: C. Organised columns of motorcycles travelling on a motorway must be at least 500 m apart. Such a gap lets other drivers overtake safely and change lane between the groups.

q-13058.text: At what speed is a passenger car permitted to travel on a motorway?

options.A: At a speed of not more than 140 km/h, while maintaining control of the vehicle and taking into account the prevailing traffic conditions.
options.B: At a speed of not less than 40 km/h, taking into account the prevailing weather conditions (blizzard, downpour, etc.).
options.C: At any speed that ensures control of the vehicle.

q-13058.explanation: Correct answer: A. On a motorway the upper limit for a car is 140 km/h, but speed is always chosen so that you keep control of the vehicle in the conditions that exist. The rules set no lower limit such as 40 km/h.

q-13059.text: What is the maximum speed permitted for a bus on a motorway?

options.A: 100 km/h if it meets the additional technical conditions stipulated by the legislation.

q-13059.explanation: Correct answer: A. A bus meeting the additional technical conditions laid down in the rules may travel on a motorway at up to 100 km/h. A bus that does not meet those conditions is bound by a lower speed limit.

q-13060.text: What is the maximum speed the driver of a passenger car with a trailer is permitted to travel on this road outside built-up areas?
q-13060.explanation: Correct answer: A. A car with a trailer may travel at no more than 80 km/h on a road of this kind outside a built-up area. A trailer lengthens the braking distance and worsens the stability of the combination, so the limit is lower than for a vehicle without one.

q-13061.text: At what speed is the bus driver allowed to continue driving past this prohibition sign?

options.A: 70 km/h if the GVM (gross vehicle mass) of the bus does not exceed 3.5 tonnes.
options.C: 50 km/h when towing a trailer regardless of the GVM of the combination.

q-13061.explanation: Correct answer: C. A bus towing a trailer may not go faster than 50 km/h, regardless of the maximum permissible mass of the combination. The value on the sign sets only the upper bound, and the stricter limit from the rules remains in force.

q-13062.text: What is the minimum lateral distance you must maintain when overtaking a cyclist, with a motorbike?

options.C: 1.5 m, if it is a motorbike with a sidecar.

q-13062.explanation: Correct answer: A. When overtaking a cyclist, a distance that is safe and no less than 1 m must be kept. A motorcycle's sidecar does not change that value, but it increases the vehicle's width, so the manoeuvre needs more room on the carriageway.

q-13063.text: At what speed is a passenger car allowed to continue driving beyond these signs?

options.A: 30 km/h to the nearest intersection and then 50 km/h.
options.B: 30 km/h to the signpost with information indicating the beginning of a city, and then 90 km/h.
options.C: 30 km/h on the entire stretch of road running through a built-up area.

q-13063.explanation: Correct answer: C. A speed limit introduced together with the start of a built-up area applies along the whole stretch of road in that area and does not end at the nearest junction. Only a cancelling sign or the end of the built-up area can lift it.

q-13064.text: What is the permissible speed limit for a quadricycle in a built-up area?

options.A: 50 km/h regardless of its gross vehicle weight rating.
options.B: 40 km/h if its gross vehicle weight exceeds 3.5 t.

q-13064.explanation: Correct answer: A. In a built-up area the basic limit is 50 km/h, and it also covers a quadricycle, regardless of its maximum permissible mass. A lower value can follow only from a sign or from the vehicle's design capabilities.

q-13067.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to the pedestrian?
q-13067.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In the situation shown the pedestrian has priority, so the driver must refrain from driving and not force them to change direction or pace. This requires slowing down early and being ready to stop the vehicle.

q-13069.text: In this situation, is it enough if you only exercise extreme caution?
q-13069.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Particular caution alone is not enough, because the situation imposes an additional specific duty: to give way, reduce speed or stop the vehicle. Caution is a necessary condition, but it does not replace performing that duty.

q-13070.text: Are you obliged in this situation to reduce your speed?
q-13070.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The situation does not introduce a duty to reduce speed: there is no obstacle and no road user to whom you must give way, and a speed adapted to the conditions remains safe. The duty to watch the road and readiness to react still continue, however.

q-13071.text: In this situation, are you only obliged to be cautious?
q-13071.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Ordinary caution is not enough here, because the situation requires particular caution — heightened attention and behaviour adapted to the conditions to a degree that allows a sufficiently quick reaction. This applies especially to places where vulnerable road users may appear.

q-13072.text: Are you obliged in this situation to reduce your speed when approaching a pedestrian crossing?
q-13072.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Approaching the crossing, the driver must take special care and travel at a speed that allows stopping before a pedestrian. If the speed is already suited to that and nobody intends to step onto the crossing, reducing it further is not required.

q-13074.text: In this situation, if you do not see other road users, are you absolved of the obligation to exercise extra caution?
q-13074.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty of particular caution follows from the place and the driving conditions, not from whether the driver happens to see someone. Another road user may be hidden or appear suddenly, so the level of attention must not be lowered.

q-13076.text: In this situation, is it permissible to drive through the intersection without reducing the vehicle speed?
q-13076.explanation: Correct answer: YES. If the driver is on a road with priority or has a permitting signal, and the passage through the intersection is clear, the rules do not require slowing down. Speed must, however, remain safe and allow you to stop should the situation change.

q-13080.text: Does the "give way" sign placed before the intersection apply in this situation?
q-13080.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A give-way sign does not apply when priority at the intersection is decided by traffic lights or by the instruction of a person directing traffic. The signals then take precedence over the signs, and it is to them that the driver must submit.

q-13082.text: In this situation, when driving straight through an intersection, can you refrain from taking extra care?
q-13082.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Approaching an intersection and passing through it always require particular caution, also when going straight ahead and when you have priority. Another driver may fail to give way, so you must watch all the approaches to the intersection.

q-13085.text: In this situation, are you permitted to make a U-turn if you are sure it will not obstruct other traffic users?
q-13085.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place turning around is prohibited, and the prohibition applies regardless of whether the manoeuvre would obstruct other road users. The absence of obstruction does not lift a prohibition arising from a sign or from the nature of this section of road.

q-13088.text: At what maximum permissible speed can you tow another vehicle?

options.C: 80 km/h on a dual carriageway road with at least two lanes in each direction.

q-13088.explanation: Correct answer: B. When towing, a limit of 60 km/h applies outside a built-up area and 30 km/h in a built-up area. The type of road does not raise these limits, but signs may introduce an even lower value.

q-13101.text: In this situation, are you approaching an intersection with a track that has the right of way?
q-13101.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing at this place indicates that traffic on the tramway has priority, so the approaching driver must give way to it. Approach the crossing at a speed that allows stopping before the tracks.

q-13102.text: In this situation, are you obliged to yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the transverse road?
q-13102.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signing of the approach you are on gives priority to the side road, so you must give way to the vehicles travelling along it. Giving way means not forcing them to change direction or speed and, if necessary, stopping the vehicle.

q-13105.text: Are you obliged to switch off your rear fog lights if visibility is more than 50 m?
q-13105.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Rear fog lights may be used only when visibility is reduced below 50 m, so once it improves they must be switched off. Left on without need, they dazzle drivers behind and make it harder for them to judge distance.

q-13106.text: Are you obliged to yield the right of way to a pedestrian approaching a pedestrian crossing?
q-13106.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Priority belongs to a pedestrian on the crossing or stepping onto it; a pedestrian only just approaching the crossing does not yet have it. The driver must, however, take special care and be ready to give way when the pedestrian begins to step on.

q-13107.text: In this situation, are you obliged to heighten your attention to the extent that permits you to react quickly enough?
q-13107.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Special care applies on this stretch, and its essence is precisely increasing attention and adapting behaviour to the conditions so that the reaction is fast enough. Trust in other road users must be limited at the same time.

q-13108.text: Are you obliged in this situation to stop the vehicle?
q-13108.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to stop the vehicle follows from the sign, signal or instruction shown in the material — the driver must comply with it regardless of whether the road appears clear. The stop is made before the line or the place it refers to.

q-13109.text: Can you continue driving in this situation?
q-13109.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the circumstances shown, driving on is not permitted — the duty to stop follows from the sign, signal or situation shown in the material. You may move off only when the reason for the stop is gone and the way is clear.

q-13112.text: Should you mitigate your trust in the pedestrian in this situation?
q-13112.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The principle of limited trust applies towards people whose behaviour may be unpredictable: children, the elderly, disabled people and those behaving contrary to the rules. The driver must then expect the pedestrian to step onto the carriageway and be ready to stop.

q-13113.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop moving to yield the right of way to a pedestrian entering the crossing?
q-13113.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A pedestrian stepping onto the crossing has priority, so the driver must refrain from driving and, if necessary, stop the vehicle before the crossing. Driving onto the crossing would force the pedestrian to change direction or pace.

q-13114.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop your vehicle to yield the right of way to a pedestrian?
q-13114.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Giving way to the pedestrian here means the vehicle must be stopped, because only that way are they not forced to change direction or pace. The stop is made before the crossing, not on it.

q-13116.text: Beyond this "residential area" sign, can you expect to see devices enforcing slow driving without warning signs?
q-13116.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a residential zone speed humps and other traffic-calming devices need not be preceded by warning signs. The driver must choose a speed that allows the vehicle to be stopped safely at any moment.

q-13117.text: Does this road sign warn of the beginning of the stretch of road where the average speed is controlled and recorded by a stationary recording device?
q-13117.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of the beginning of a section on which a fixed device measures and records the average speed between two measuring points. Slowing down momentarily at the device itself achieves nothing, because what counts is the time taken over the whole section.

q-13118.text: In this situation, should you heighten your attention to such an extent as to enable you to react quickly enough?
q-13118.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Conditions on this stretch call for special care, that is, raising the level of attention and driving so that the reaction to a change in the situation comes quickly enough. A lower speed and a greater distance from the vehicle ahead help.

q-13119.text: Does this sign indicate entry into a green transport zone?
q-13119.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign marks the beginning of a clean transport zone, which may be entered only by vehicles meeting the established requirements concerning emissions or type of drive. Other vehicles may not enter it, unless they are covered by a provided exception.

q-13120.text: Does this sign permit only electric vehicles to enter the green transport zone?
q-13120.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A clean transport zone may be entered not only by electric vehicles, but also by those powered by hydrogen or natural gas and others meeting the established requirements. The range of permitted vehicles is defined by the resolution introducing the given zone.

q-13121.text: Are you obliged to yield the right of way to a pedestrian entering a pedestrian crossing?
q-13121.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A pedestrian stepping onto the crossing has priority over a vehicle, but not over a tram; over a tram they gain priority only once they are already on the crossing. Even so, special care and readiness to brake apply.

q-13122.text: Does this sign allow hydrogen-powered vehicles to enter the green transport zone?
q-13122.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A clean transport zone may be entered by vehicles that emit no harmful exhaust gases, so besides electric ones also those powered by hydrogen. The detailed list of eligible vehicles and exceptions follows from the resolution establishing the zone.

q-13123.text: Does this sign permit a vehicle that runs on natural gas to enter the green transport zone?
q-13123.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Besides electric and hydrogen vehicles, vehicles powered by natural gas are also admitted to a clean transport zone. Further restrictions or exceptions may be introduced by the resolution establishing the given zone.

q-13127.text: Can a driver expect to see pedestrians using the full width of the road beyond this "residential area" sign?
q-13127.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a residential zone a pedestrian may use the full width of the road and has priority over vehicles. The driver must travel at a speed that allows an immediate reaction, including to children playing on the roadway.

q-13128.text: Does this sign indicate that you are passing in front of a driver approaching from the opposite direction?
q-13128.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign gives priority to drivers travelling in your direction on a section where two vehicles cannot pass side by side, so the oncoming driver must give way. Despite having priority, check that they really do stop.

q-13132.text: In this situation, are you obliged to give way to a pedestrian?
q-13132.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the situation shown, the pedestrian is neither on the crossing nor stepping onto it, so they are not entitled to priority over your vehicle. Care and readiness to give way still apply should they begin to cross.

q-13134.text: In this situation, can you drive past the pedestrian?
q-13134.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The pedestrian has priority here, and driving in front of them would force them to stop or change direction, which the rules prohibit. Slow down and, if necessary, stop the vehicle until the pedestrian has finished crossing.

q-13137.text: In the situation presented, are you obliged to give way to the pedestrian?
q-13137.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A pedestrian who is stepping onto the crossing or already walking across must be given way; this duty also applies to a driver turning into a side road. Giving way means stopping before the crossing and waiting until the pedestrian has crossed.

q-13139.text: In this situation, are you obliged to stop your vehicle to allow a pedestrian to cross the road?
q-13139.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The pedestrian has priority at this place, and the only way to give way to them is to stop the vehicle before the crossing. You may move off only once the pedestrian has left the carriageway and the manoeuvre endangers nobody.

q-13142.text: Can you overtake a vehicle from the right in the illustrated situation?
q-13142.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You may overtake on the right a vehicle whose driver is signalling an intention to turn left and is moving towards the centre of the roadway. The manoeuvre may be undertaken after making sure there is enough room and that no one is stepping or driving out on the right.

q-13143.text: Can you perform an overtaking manoeuvre in this situation?
q-13143.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place overtaking is prohibited — this follows from a sign, from road markings or from the lack of sufficient visibility and room to complete the manoeuvre safely. You may overtake only after the reason for the prohibition ceases.

q-13144.text: Can you overtake a vehicle from the right at this intersection?
q-13144.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At this intersection you may overtake on the right a vehicle whose driver is signalling an intention to turn left and has taken the appropriate position on the roadway. The manoeuvre requires making sure there is enough room on the right and no one is travelling there.

q-13145.text: In the situation presented, can you overtake the vehicle in front of you from the left or right?
q-13145.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking on both sides is permitted on a one-way roadway, where there is no oncoming traffic, provided there is enough room and the manoeuvre endangers no one. Before changing lanes you must signal your intention and check the blind spot.

q-13146.text: When overtaking an electric scooter, are you obliged to keep a distance of no less than one metre?
q-13146.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When overtaking an electric scooter, the driver must keep a safe distance of no less than 1 m. The same minimum distance applies when overtaking a bicycle, a moped, a personal transporter and a pedestrian.

q-13147.text: Do you have to refrain from overtaking in this situation?
q-13147.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You must abandon overtaking when a sign or road markings prohibit it, or when visibility and free space do not allow the manoeuvre to be completed safely. Overtaking in such conditions would force others to brake harshly.

q-13149.text: Are you allowed to overtake the cyclist in this situation?
q-13149.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is prohibited at this place, so the manoeuvre may not be started regardless of how slowly the cyclist is riding. When overtaking a bicycle, a distance of no less than 1 m applies as well.

q-13150.text: Can you overtake a vehicle on the right in the situation illustrated?
q-13150.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You may overtake on the right a vehicle whose driver is signalling an intention to turn left and is moving towards the centre of the roadway. The manoeuvre may be undertaken after making sure there is enough room and that no one is stepping or driving out on the right.

q-13152.text: Can you continue driving in this situation?
q-13152.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the circumstances shown, driving on is not permitted — the duty to stop follows from the sign, signal or situation shown in the material. You may move off only when the reason for the stop is gone and the way is clear.

q-13153.text: Are you obliged to stop driving in this situation?
q-13153.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signal, sign or situation on the road requires you to refrain from driving until the way is clear or permission to proceed appears. Entering against this duty would force the entitled road users to brake.

q-13154.text: Can you continue driving in this situation?
q-13154.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Nothing here prevents you from driving on: the signal or signing permits movement, and the road ahead of the vehicle is clear. Continue at a speed suited to the conditions, watching your surroundings.

q-13155.text: In this situation, do you have to wait for the red signal to turn green to continue driving?
q-13155.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At a red signal, travel in the direction indicated by the green arrow is possible after stopping before the line and giving way to all other road users. Waiting for the green signal is then not necessary.

q-13156.text: Are you permitted to overtake a vehicle in the right lane on a pedestrian crossing?
q-13156.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking on a pedestrian crossing and directly before it is prohibited, because the vehicle being overtaken hides the pedestrians from view. The ban applies regardless of which lane the vehicle being overtaken is using.

q-13157.text: Are you permitted to perform an overtaking manoeuvre in this situation?
q-13157.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The manoeuvre must not be started, because at this place overtaking is prohibited or the conditions for completing it safely without obstructing oncoming traffic are lacking. What counts is the state of the road when the manoeuvre begins, not the driver's intention.

q-13158.text: Is overtaking from the right prohibited on this roadway?
q-13158.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On this roadway overtaking on the right is permitted, because traffic moves in one direction in marked lanes. A lane change requires, however, signalling the intention and making sure the adjacent lane is clear.

q-13159.text: In this situation, are you permitted to overtake the vehicle in front of you from the right?
q-13159.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking on the right is, as a rule, prohibited, and the exception concerns above all a vehicle whose driver is signalling an intention to turn left. No such exception applies here, so overtaking is permitted only on the left.

q-13161.text: In this situation, do you have to wait for children and the person directing traffic to leave the pedestrian crossing?
q-13161.explanation: Correct answer: YES. As long as children and the person supervising their crossing are on the crossing, the vehicle must remain stationary, because pedestrians on a crossing have priority. You may move off only after everyone, including the person directing them, has left the roadway.

q-13164.text: Are you obliged to reduce your speed in this situation so as not to endanger the pedestrian?
q-13164.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Approaching a pedestrian crossing, the driver must take special care and slow down so as not to expose the pedestrian to danger. This also applies to the driver of a rail vehicle, which has a longer braking distance.

q-13165.text: When overtaking a cyclist, are you obliged to observe a distance of no less than one metre?
q-13165.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When overtaking a cyclist, the driver must keep a safe distance of no less than 1 m. If the width of the carriageway does not allow it, the manoeuvre must be abandoned or you wait for a suitable place.

q-13166.text: Can you start overtaking in this situation?
q-13166.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking must not be started when the visibility and the free space needed to overtake and return to your lane are lacking, or when the manoeuvre is prohibited at this place. The driver makes this assessment before starting the manoeuvre.

q-13168.text: Will you refrain from overtaking in this situation?
q-13168.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You should abandon overtaking when a prohibition applies at this place or when the manoeuvre would require using the part of the roadway intended for the opposite direction without certainty of a safe return. Safe overtaking requires free space, good visibility and a speed difference.

q-13170.text: When overtaking an electric scooter, are you obliged to observe a distance of no less than 1 m?
q-13170.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When overtaking an electric scooter, a safe distance of no less than 1 m applies, kept for the whole duration of the manoeuvre. When the carriageway is too narrow, overtaking must be postponed to a more suitable place.

q-13171.text: Are you obliged to give way to a pedestrian entering a crossing?
q-13171.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A driver must give way to a pedestrian stepping onto the crossing and to one who is already on it. The exception is a tram, over which the pedestrian gains priority only once they have stepped onto the crossing.

q-13175.text: Is it permissible to stop a vehicle directly behind a visible indicator post?
q-13175.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Marker posts only warn of the approach to a railway crossing and do not themselves introduce a no-parking prohibition. The prohibition covers the crossing itself and its immediate vicinity, not the spot by a post standing before it.

q-13198.text: Can you expect to see a level crossing without traffic lights beyond this sign?
q-13198.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of a railway crossing that need not be equipped with light signals or barriers. Before such a crossing you must exercise particular caution, slow down and make sure yourself that the tracks are clear.

q-13200.text: If a vehicle becomes immobilised at a level crossing, should you remove it from the crossing immediately?
q-13200.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An immobilised vehicle must be removed from the crossing immediately, and when that is impossible — others must be warned and the railway services or the police notified. Delay risks a collision with a train that will not be able to stop.

q-13204.text: Do you have to be extra careful when approaching a junction from a priority road?
q-13204.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Particular caution when approaching an intersection applies to every driver, regardless of whether they are on the road with priority. Priority does not guarantee that the driver from the subordinate road will actually give way.

q-13207.text: Does this sign indicate the start or continuation of a road with priority?
q-13207.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign informs of the beginning of a road with priority, and repeated after the intersection it confirms its continuation. Priority does not, however, release you from caution or from the duty to give way to an emergency vehicle.

q-13212.text: Are you obliged to switch on your hazard lights beyond this sign to indicate that the damaged vehicle is stationary?
q-13212.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The stopping of a broken-down vehicle on the road must be signalled with the hazard lights switched on, and when the vehicle has none or they do not work — with the position lights. In addition, a warning triangle is placed at the spot required for the given road.

q-13213.text: Is it permitted to stop a vehicle in a residential zone?
q-13213.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a residential zone you may stop a vehicle, whereas parking is permitted only in places designated for it. Stopping must not obstruct pedestrians, who use the full width of the road here.

q-13219.text: In the presented situation, are you allowed to continue driving through the pedestrian crossing without stopping?
q-13219.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Since there is no pedestrian on the crossing and nobody is stepping onto it, no duty to stop the vehicle arises. Special care and a speed that allows stopping before the crossing still apply.

q-13222.text: Are you approaching a bicycle crossing in the presented situation?
q-13222.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The signing here indicates a place other than a cycle crossing, which is marked with its own sign and its own road markings. A cyclist crosses the carriageway at such a place under the general rules, without priority.

q-13226.text: Are you entitled to drive with your daytime running lights on in these weather conditions?
q-13226.explanation: Correct answer: YES. During the day, when the air is normally clear, you may drive with daytime running lights instead of dipped headlights. When conditions worsen — fog, precipitation, dusk — dipped headlights must be switched on.

q-13234.text: Is it prohibited to stop a vehicle on a flyover to drop off a passenger?
q-13234.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Stopping a vehicle on a bridge, a viaduct and in a tunnel is prohibited, even when it lasts a moment and serves to drop off a passenger. The reasons are the lack of room to get around the vehicle and the limited possibility for a pedestrian to leave the roadway.

q-13237.text: Does this sign indicate an exit from a town?
q-13237.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign informs of the end of a locality, i.e. that you are leaving it. If the locality was at the same time a built-up area, from this point the speed limits provided for outside built-up areas apply.

q-13242.text: Does this sign indicate entry to a town?
q-13242.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign announces the beginning of a locality, i.e. that you are entering it. When the locality is at the same time a built-up area, from this point the lower speed limit applies and you must expect pedestrians and denser traffic.

q-13243.text: Are you entering a built-up area in the presented situation?
q-13243.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs at this place introduce a built-up area, so from this moment the permitted speed set for such an area applies. The rules on using the horn also change, and you must expect pedestrians.

q-13267.text: Are you allowed to stop at this point on the carriageway?
q-13267.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place stopping is prohibited, because the vehicle would obscure visibility or obstruct other road users. The short duration of the activity justifies neither stopping nor parking.

q-13277.text: Does this sign warn of an intersection with a road on the right without the right of way?
q-13277.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The sign warns of an intersection where the cross road joining from the right is subordinate. A driver on the road with priority should nevertheless watch that approach, because priority is sometimes violated.

q-13294.text: Are you permitted to stop on the left-hand edge of the carriageway at this point?
q-13294.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a two-way road the vehicle stops by the right edge of the roadway; by the left edge this is allowed only on a one-way roadway. Stopping on the left would require driving against the flow and would surprise other drivers.

q-13299.text: Are you entitled to stop a passenger car on the road at this point to drop off a passenger?
q-13299.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At this place a no-stopping prohibition applies, and dropping off a passenger is no exception to it. The passenger may get out only where stopping is permitted and does not endanger safety.

q-13305.text: Should the condition and load of the vehicle be factors to be considered when selecting a driving speed?

options.B: Yes, but only if you are driving a lorry.
options.C: Yes, but only if the road surface is icy.

q-13305.explanation: Correct answer: A. Speed is chosen according to traffic conditions, including the vehicle's technical state and the load carried, regardless of the type of vehicle and surface. A loaded or faulty vehicle has a longer braking distance and responds worse to the steering.

q-13306.text: Is the weather condition a factor to consider when choosing a driving speed?

options.B: Yes, but only when there is heavy traffic on the road.

q-13306.explanation: Correct answer: C. Weather conditions always affect grip and visibility, so speed is adapted to rain, fog or a slippery surface regardless of how heavy the traffic is. It must allow the vehicle to be stopped before an obstacle the driver is able to see.

q-13321.text: What distance should you maintain from the vehicle in front in the presented situation?

options.A: A distance necessary to avoid a collision in the event the preceding vehicle brakes or stops.

q-13321.explanation: Correct answer: A. The rules give no fixed number of metres here — the distance must be such as to avoid a collision if the vehicle ahead brakes or stops. It therefore depends on speed, the state of the surface and visibility, and in bad conditions it must be clearly increased.

q-13324.text: In this situation, are you obliged to exercise extreme caution when driving past a vehicle from the opposite direction?
q-13324.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing an oncoming vehicle, the driver is obliged to exercise particular caution and keep a safe lateral distance from it. When the roadway is narrow or the path is constricted, you should reduce speed and, if necessary, give room.

q-13382.text: Which of the following conditions besides a safety seat or other restraint system must be met for a child less than 150 cm tall to be transported in a passenger car?

options.A: The vehicle shall not exceed a speed of 40 km/h.
options.B: The child has a medical certificate stating that it should not be transported in a safety seat or other device.
options.C: The vehicle has an additional marking which indicates that a child is on board.

q-13382.explanation: Correct answer: B. A child shorter than 150 cm is carried in a child seat or another restraint, and the only permitted exception is a medical certificate stating a contraindication. Low speed alone, or extra marking of the vehicle, does not release you from this duty.

q-13383.text: Does this sign warn you of approaching an intersection with a road on the left without right of way?
q-13383.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The drawing on the sign shows from which side the subordinate road joins; here it is the left side. You are on the road with priority, but your attention must be directed precisely at the left mouth of the side road.

q-13384.text: You intend to continue driving to the left at the nearest intersection. In this situation, are you obliged to yield priority to vehicles approaching from the opposite direction?
q-13384.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to give way to oncoming vehicles arises when their paths cross the path of the turning driver. From the traffic arrangement visible in the material it follows that this is not the case here, but observation and caution remain necessary.

q-13385.text: Does the "Mandatory drive straight" sign apply at the nearest intersection or at the point where a change of direction is possible?
q-13385.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The straight-ahead-only sign applies at the nearest intersection or at the place where a change of direction is possible at all. Up to that place the driver may not turn or make a U-turn, even if the cross road seems clear.

q-13391.text: In this situation, are you permitted to stop your vehicle on the pavement within 3 metres of the visible bus shelter?
q-13391.explanation: Correct answer: NO. In the area of a stop a no-stopping prohibition applies, and a distance of three metres from the shelter falls within that zone. In addition, stopping a vehicle on the pavement is permitted only where the rules expressly allow it.

q-13392.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution when passing a vehicle marked at the front and rear with a visible blue plate and activated hazard lights when a disabled person is boarding or alighting?
q-13392.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When passing a vehicle with a blue plate and its hazard lights on, from which a disabled person is getting in or out, the driver must take special care. You must slow down and expect a person moving slowly or stepping suddenly onto the carriageway.

q-13393.text: When passing a vehicle marked with the visible blue plate at the front and rear and with the hazard warning lights on, are you always obliged to stop whenever a disabled person is getting in or out of the vehicle?
q-13393.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Special care is required, and stopping only when it is necessary for the safety of the person getting in or out. If the vehicle can be passed slowly and at a safe distance, no duty to stop arises.

q-13394.text: Can you stop the vehicle in such a designated space if you are transporting a disabled person with a parking permit?
q-13394.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a space marked as designated for disabled people, you may park a vehicle carrying a person who holds a parking card. The card is placed behind the windscreen so that it is legible from outside.

q-13401.text: When passing a vehicle with such a placard, hazard warning lights on, and a disabled person exiting, should you exercise extra caution and stop if necessary?
q-13401.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Such a plate together with the hazard lights on signals that a disabled person is getting in or out, so the driver passing must take special care and, when needed, stop the vehicle. That person's safety decides, not the smoothness of your own drive.

q-13402.text: Upon seeing a person with a white cane crossing the road, you should:

options.A: stop the vehicle to allow them to pass
options.B: use the audible signal if they are crossing outside a designated pedestrian crossing
options.C: in all cases, shift to a higher gear

q-13402.explanation: Correct answer: A. A white cane marks a blind or visually impaired person, who may not notice an approaching vehicle. The driver stops the vehicle and lets them cross, even away from a marked crossing; a horn could only confuse them.

q-13404.text: When a disabled person or someone with visibly reduced mobility enters a pedestrian crossing with a special sign, should you anticipate having to stop your vehicle?
q-13404.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Approaching a crossing onto which a disabled person or a person with reduced mobility is stepping, you must anticipate slower crossing and the need to stop the vehicle. Speed is chosen so that you can stop before the crossing without harsh braking.

q-13406.text: When driving a passenger vehicle and transporting a disabled person with a parking permit, you should:

options.B: exercise extreme caution at all times,
options.C: carefully observe the road and its surroundings, ensuring to check the vehicle's mirrors as well.

q-13406.explanation: Correct answer: C. Watching the road and its surroundings, in the mirrors too, is the driver's constant duty, and carrying a person with a parking card does not change that. Special care is taken in the situations specified in the rules, and daytime running lights may be used instead of dipped headlights.

q-13411.text: In this situation, are you entitled to continue driving without paying attention to the behaviour of pedestrians?
q-13411.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver must watch pedestrians and anticipate their behaviour, especially near a crossing. Driving without paying attention to them is unacceptable — you must be ready to slow down and stop the vehicle.

q-13426.text: Are you obliged to stop your vehicle before the STOP sign when approaching a level crossing in the presented situation?
q-13426.explanation: Correct answer: NO. An absolute stop before a railway crossing is required only when a "Stop" sign stands there, when a red signal is displayed, or when the barriers are being lowered or are lowered. Here there is no such requirement, but you must exercise particular caution.

q-13427.text: Are you obliged to exercise extreme caution at all times when driving in a residential zone?
q-13427.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Ordinary caution applies at all times, and particular caution only in the situations specified by the regulations. This does not change the fact that in a residential zone a pedestrian may use the full width of the road and has priority, and the speed there is clearly limited.

q-13429.text: Is it permissible to overtake a motor vehicle from the right on this road outside a built-up area?
q-13429.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is done on the left; on the right only a vehicle that is signalling a left turn and has moved towards the centre of the roadway. Outside a built-up area, on such a road, overtaking on the right is prohibited.

q-13430.text: Does this sign warn that you are approaching a crossroads with a one-way road entrance on the left-hand side?
q-13430.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The visible sign does not convey what the question asks about. Warning signs before an intersection show the road layout and the side from which the subordinate road joins, but do not say that it is one-way.

q-13432.text: In this scenario, could the behaviour of the scooterist approaching the intersection constitute a hazard?
q-13432.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A scooter is narrow, quiet and easily lost against the background, and it travels faster than it appears to a driver. Approaching a junction, you must expect it to pull out in front of the vehicle and slow down early enough.

q-13433.text: In this situation, might the pedestrian running on the pavement present a hazard?
q-13433.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A running pedestrian covers the distance to the carriageway much faster than a walking one and may run onto it without stopping at the kerb. The driver should watch the pavement, slow down and be ready to brake.

q-13434.text: In this scenario, does the loader excavator entering the intersection pose a hazard?
q-13434.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A construction machine is slow and wide, occupies the space of the intersection for a long time, and its operator has a limited field of view. You must reduce speed, keep your distance and let it leave the intersection.

q-13435.text: Does the sudden emergence of a scooterist from the internal road constitute a hazard in this situation?
q-13435.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An exit from an internal road is often obscured, and a scooter appears suddenly and silently, often without slowing down. The driver should watch such exits and choose a speed that allows braking before its path.

q-13436.text: In this situation, does the vehicle parked on the pavement pose a hazard?
q-13436.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A vehicle standing motionless outside your path does not in itself create a danger for the driver passing by. It does, however, require attention, because it limits the field of view and a pedestrian may step out or a cyclist ride out from behind it.

q-13437.text: In this situation, does the strong lateral wind pose a danger to the motorcyclist and other road users in the vicinity?
q-13437.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A strong crosswind pushes a two-wheeler off its line, and gusts when emerging from behind shelter can be violent. A motorcyclist may suddenly change course, so other drivers should increase their distance and slow down.

q-13438.text: In this scenario, does the lorry in front of you in the same lane pose a hazard?
q-13438.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A lorry travelling in the same lane at a matched speed does not create a danger in itself. You must, however, keep a distance that allows you to stop after it brakes suddenly, and remember that it blocks the view of the road ahead of it.

q-13439.text: In this situation, does the articulated vehicle emerging from the minor road and travelling to the left present a hazard?
q-13439.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An articulated vehicle turning left needs a lot of time and space, and its rear part describes a different arc from the front. It occupies the intersection for a long time, so you must reduce speed and be ready to stop the vehicle.

q-13440.text: In this scenario, could the vehicle travelling by the roadside pose a hazard?
q-13440.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The shoulder is not intended for motor vehicles, so such a vehicle is behaving unusually and may return to the roadway at any moment. You must reduce speed, increase the distance and watch its path.

q-13441.text: In this situation, does the vehicle travelling in the left lane pose a hazard?
q-13441.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A vehicle travelling in its lane in a predictable way creates no danger as long as it keeps its path and distance. It should, however, be monitored in the mirrors, because the situation will change when it begins to change lanes.

q-13442.text: In this situation, does the loader excavator pose a hazard?
q-13442.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A machine that does not enter or cross your path does not in itself create a hazard. Even so, keep your distance and watch it, because it is slow and its work may change at any moment.

q-13443.text: In this scenario, does the pedestrian in the pedestrian crossing pose a hazard?
q-13443.explanation: Correct answer: NO. A pedestrian using the crossing is behaving in accordance with the rules, and the driver must give way to them, so no hazard arises. The condition is slowing down early enough and being ready to stop the vehicle.

q-13444.text: When can you use rear anti-fog lights while driving?

options.A: When visibility in heavy rain is limited to 60 m.
options.B: When visibility in thick fog is limited to 100 m.
options.C: When visibility during snowfall is less than 50 m.

q-13444.explanation: Correct answer: C. Rear fog lights may be used when fog, rain or snow reduce visibility below 50 m. In better visibility they dazzle drivers behind, so they must be switched off as soon as conditions improve.

q-13446.text: Does a traffic light at a pedestrian crossing absolve you of your responsibility to exercise extra caution?
q-13446.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Traffic lights organise traffic, but they do not release the driver from the duty of particular caution at a pedestrian crossing. A pedestrian may step onto the roadway despite the red light, and a child or an elderly person may not manage to get off before the signal changes.

q-13447.text: Are you warned in this situation of a possible encounter with farm animals on the road?
q-13447.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The warning sign shown in the material announces a stretch where farm animals may appear on the carriageway. Slow down and expect the animal to move unpredictably, with a person leading it possibly walking alongside.

q-13448.text: In the presented situation, are you approaching the intersection from a road without right of way?
q-13448.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material indicate that you are approaching the intersection on a subordinate road, so you are obliged to give way to vehicles travelling on the road with priority. Speed must be chosen so that you can stop before the intersection.

q-13449.text: In the presented situation, are you approaching the intersection from a road without right of way?
q-13449.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The signs visible in the material indicate that you are approaching the intersection on a subordinate road, so you are obliged to give way to vehicles travelling on the road with priority. Speed must be chosen so that you can stop before the intersection.

q-13450.text: In this situation, is the driver of vehicle 1 obliged to drive as close as possible to the left edge of the lane?
q-13450.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before turning left, the driver takes a position as close as possible to the left edge of the part of the roadway intended for their direction of traffic. This way they do not block those going straight and shorten the path of the manoeuvre, and beforehand they must signal the intention with the indicator.

q-13451.text: May the devices forcing slow driving beyond this sign not be marked with warning signs?
q-13451.explanation: Correct answer: YES. In a zone marked with such a sign, speed humps and other traffic-calming devices need not be separately marked with warning signs. The driver must expect them and drive at a reduced speed throughout the zone.

q-13452.text: Is it allowed to increase speed to 90 km/h beyond the visible signs?

options.A: Yes, because you are entering an expressway.
options.B: Yes, because you are exiting a built-up area.
options.C: No, because the sign indicates that you will be entering the expressway in just 450 metres.

q-13452.explanation: Correct answer: B. Beyond the sign marking the end of the built-up area, the limit proper to built-up areas stops applying and a car may travel at 90 km/h. The plate announcing an expressway in 450 metres does not yet change the permitted speed.

q-13453.text: In the presented situation, are the drivers obliged to allow vehicles on the vanishing lane to change lanes?
q-13453.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The duty to let in under the zipper rule arises only when speed before the narrowing is significantly reduced and a jam forms. In free-flowing traffic it is the driver in the disappearing lane who must give way to those in the continuing lane.

q-13454.text: When you approach a crossing marked in this manner, should you expect limited visibility?
q-13454.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Such signing announces a crossing where the driver judges the situation for themselves, and the view along the tracks is often obscured by buildings, vegetation or the lie of the land. Approach slowly and, in case of doubt, stop and make sure the tracks are clear.

q-13455.text: When approaching a level crossing with overhead lines, should you be mindful of the extra risks involved?
q-13455.explanation: Correct answer: YES. High-voltage wires run above the tracks, so a height limit applies to the vehicle with its load, and getting close to the overhead line risks electric shock. In addition, an electric train travels fast and very quietly, which shortens the time to react.

q-13457.text: Could you put the lives or health of several people at risk by ignoring a stop while driving over the railway tracks at this point?
q-13457.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A collision with a rail vehicle endangers not only the driver and passengers of the car but also the people on the train, because it may derail. That is why you may enter the crossing only after making sure the tracks are clear and there is room on the other side.

q-13458.text: When approaching a level crossing, are you required to adjust your speed according to changing conditions?
q-13458.explanation: Correct answer: YES. You approach a level crossing with special care and at a speed that allows stopping before the tracks. You must allow for an uneven surface, slippery rails, lowering barriers and changing signals.

q-13459.text: Is it permissible to drive at a speed that could make it difficult to stop the vehicle when the red signal starts flashing?
q-13459.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Speed is chosen so that, after the signal changes, the vehicle can be stopped before the line or the traffic light without harsh braking. Driving too fast ends in entering on red or in braking that risks a rear-end collision.

q-13460.text: If you cannot remove the damaged vehicle from the tracks, are you required to alert the train driver about the potential danger?
q-13460.explanation: Correct answer: YES. When the vehicle cannot be removed from the tracks, the driver must immediately warn the train driver of the danger by giving a clearly visible signal from a sufficiently large distance on both sides of the tracks. A train has a very long braking distance, so every second counts.

q-13461.text: If your vehicle gets stuck on a level crossing, are you required to first alert the train driver to the potential danger?
q-13461.explanation: Correct answer: NO. First of all you must remove the vehicle from the crossing, and if that is impossible — see that the passengers leave it. Only when the vehicle cannot be removed do you warn the train driver and notify the services.

q-13463.text: Does the design of the barriers enable a vehicle to break through if it gets stuck on a level crossing between closed barriers?
q-13463.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Barriers and half-barriers are built so that a vehicle trapped between them can break through. In such a situation you must not wait — you must drive off the tracks immediately, even at the cost of damaging the barrier.

q-13464.text: When you exercise caution, are you allowed to enter a railway crossing if the barrier has just started to lower?
q-13464.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The start of the barriers lowering means entering the crossing is prohibited, no matter how carefully the driver is watching the tracks. The vehicle may get trapped between the barriers, and by then the train is already close to the crossing.

q-13465.text: Once traffic resumes at the multi-track crossing, should you check for approaching trains on other tracks before entering the track?
q-13465.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At a multi-track crossing, after one train has passed another may be approaching on the second track, often hidden by the first. Before entering, look both ways along all the tracks and move off only after making sure they are clear.

q-13466.text: In this scenario, once you’ve confirmed that no train is approaching, are you permitted to drive around the lowered half-barrier and cross the railway tracks?
q-13466.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Lowered half-barriers absolutely prohibit entry, and driving around them is forbidden even when the tracks appear empty. A train may come from the other side or on the second track, and its speed is easy to misjudge.

q-13467.text: In this scenario, are you obliged to bring your vehicle to a stop before the visible prohibition sign?
q-13467.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The visible sign orders an unconditional stop of the vehicle every time, even when nothing is approaching. You stop before the line, and where there is none — at a point from which the whole track or the cross road can be seen.

q-13468.text: In this situation, after halting and making sure that no train is approaching, do you have the right to proceed without waiting for permission from an authorised individual?
q-13468.explanation: Correct answer: NO. When traffic at the crossing is directed by an authorised person, their instructions take precedence over your own assessment of the situation and the signs. You may move off only after receiving a clear signal permitting you to cross.

q-13469.text: In this situation, do you have the right to overtake the vehicle in front of you to get across the railway crossing as swiftly as possible?
q-13469.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is prohibited on a level crossing and directly before it, and wanting to get across the tracks faster does not change that. The vehicle in front may brake suddenly before the tracks, so you must follow it and keep your distance.

q-13470.text: In this situation, do you have the right to overtake the vehicle in front of you by driving onto the part of the road designated for oncoming traffic, if you can stop before the railway crossing?
q-13470.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Before a level crossing you may not pass a vehicle waiting to cross if that would require entering the part of the carriageway intended for the opposite direction. It makes no difference that the driver would manage to stop before the tracks.

q-13471.text: When approaching a level crossing with infrequent train traffic, are you always required to check for any approaching trains?
q-13471.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The duty to make sure the tracks are clear applies at every crossing, regardless of how rarely trains run there. Besides scheduled trains there are extra trains and service vehicles, and getting used to empty tracks is a cause of the most serious accidents.

q-13472.text: In this scenario, do you have the right to cross the railway tracks without being sure that there’s enough space to continue driving on the other side of the level crossing?
q-13472.explanation: Correct answer: NO. You may enter the crossing only when there is room beyond the tracks that allows you to leave it without stopping. Otherwise the vehicle gets trapped between the barriers, and the train will not manage to brake.

q-13473.text: When approaching a level crossing with barriers, should you take into account that, for various reasons, the safety devices might not close the crossing in time?
q-13473.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Safety equipment can fail, be damaged or act with a delay, so raised barriers do not excuse you from vigilance. You approach every crossing slowly and check for yourself that the tracks are clear.

q-13478.text: When you see this road sign, are you required to stop your vehicle for an approaching cyclist at the crossing?
q-13478.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The sign announces a cycle crossing and requires special care, but it creates no unconditional duty to stop. You give way to a cyclist on the crossing; usually slowing down is enough, and you stop when safety requires it.

q-13485.text: At the spot marked by the visible sign, are you required to yield to someone using a mobility aid who is crossing at a cycling crossing?
q-13485.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A person moving with the aid of a mobility device enjoys priority at a cycle crossing in the same way as a cyclist. The driver must take special care, slow down and, if necessary, stop the vehicle.

q-13490.text: Are you allowed to overtake a cyclist at a pedestrian crossing if you exercise extreme caution?
q-13490.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking on a pedestrian crossing and directly before it is prohibited, and special care does not lift that ban. The overtaking driver blocks the view for the pedestrians and for themselves, so a person approaching the carriageway is noticed too late.

q-13491.text: In the scenario presented, are you required to refrain from overtaking the cyclist?
q-13491.explanation: Correct answer: YES. An overtaking ban applies at the place indicated in the material, and it also covers a cyclist. The manoeuvre must be postponed to a stretch where it is allowed, and a safe distance from the cyclist must be kept.

q-13492.text: In the presented situation, despite exercising utmost caution, are you restricted from overtaking the vehicle in front of you?
q-13492.explanation: Correct answer: YES. A ban on overtaking arising from a sign or from the place on the road applies absolutely, and not even the most attentive driving lifts it. The manoeuvre may be performed only where the prohibition ends and visibility is sufficient.

q-13493.text: In the presented scenario, is it permissible to overtake the vehicle in front of you, provided that due caution is exercised?
q-13493.explanation: Correct answer: NO. At the place shown in the material overtaking is prohibited, and declared caution does not replace meeting the conditions of the manoeuvre. You may overtake only when the rules allow it and a sufficiently long, clear section of road can be seen.

q-13494.text: In the situation presented, is it permissible to overtake the vehicle in front from the right side while exercising utmost caution?
q-13494.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking is done on the left; on the right only when the vehicle in front is signalling a left turn and has moved towards the centre of the roadway, or when the type of road allows it. In the situation shown no such exception applies.

q-13495.text: In the situation depicted, despite exercising utmost caution, are you prohibited from overtaking?
q-13495.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Overtaking is prohibited at this place, and exercising particular caution gives no right to perform a prohibited manoeuvre. The driver must stay behind the vehicle in front until a section where overtaking is permitted.

q-13497.text: In this scenario, as you approach the crest of the hill on a two-way road, are you permitted to overtake the motorbike?
q-13497.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a hill with limited visibility, when approaching its crest, overtaking on a two-way roadway is prohibited. A vehicle may come from beyond the crest, and the combined closing speed leaves no time to return to your lane.

q-13498.text: Before you attempt to overtake, are you required to ensure that the driver behind you hasn't already begun the overtaking manoeuvre?
q-13498.explanation: Correct answer: YES. Before starting to overtake, you must check in the mirrors and the blind spot that the driver behind is not already moving into the left lane. Only then do you signal the intention with the indicator and smoothly change your path.

q-13499.text: In this situation, are you prohibited from overtaking the vehicle in front of you on the right-hand side when driving on a one-way road outside a built-up area?
q-13499.explanation: Correct answer: NO. On a one-way roadway there is no oncoming traffic, so overtaking on the right is permitted. You must, however, exercise particular caution, signal the manoeuvre and check the blind spot, because the vehicle being overtaken may change lanes.

q-13500.text: In this scenario, are you allowed to begin the overtaking manoeuvre of the preceding vehicle while exercising extreme caution?
q-13500.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The manoeuvre must not be started where an overtaking ban applies or where the visible section of road is too short to overtake safely and return to your lane. Particular caution does not release you from these conditions.

q-13501.text: In this situation, outside a built-up area, are you prohibited from overtaking the vehicle in front of you on the right?
q-13501.explanation: Correct answer: NO. From the situation shown in the material it follows that an exception permitting this manoeuvre applies — you may overtake on the right a vehicle signalling a left turn that has moved towards the centre of the roadway, and also on a one-way roadway. Particular caution still applies.

q-13502.text: When driving a vehicle that's being overtaken, are you permitted to slightly increase your speed during or right after the overtaking manoeuvre?
q-13502.explanation: Correct answer: NO. The driver of the vehicle being overtaken is obliged not to increase speed and, if necessary, to move further to the right to make the manoeuvre easier. Even a slight acceleration prolongs the time the overtaking driver spends on the opposite lane.

q-13503.text: In this scenario, while it's not against the rules to overtake cyclists at intersections, should you avoid doing so, as it might create a safety hazard due to limited visibility?
q-13503.explanation: Correct answer: YES. The absence of a formal ban does not mean the manoeuvre is safe — the assessment of conditions decides. With limited visibility, overtaking a cyclist at a junction forces you close to them and takes away time to react, so it should be abandoned.

q-13504.text: Despite exercising extreme caution, are you obliged to refrain from overtaking the motor vehicle at the nearest junction?
q-13504.explanation: Correct answer: YES. At an intersection overtaking a motor vehicle is prohibited, unless you are on a road with priority or at a roundabout. Particular caution does not replace the prohibition, because at an intersection the paths of other road users may suddenly cross.

q-13505.text: Are you allowed to overtake the vehicle in front of you at the nearest intersection, while exercising utmost caution?
q-13505.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking at an intersection is prohibited except when on a road with priority or at a roundabout, and the material does not indicate that such an exception applies. You must therefore wait with the manoeuvre until the section beyond the intersection.

q-13506.text: Is it permissible to start overtaking without first ensuring that the driver behind you has not already begun their overtaking manoeuvre?
q-13506.explanation: Correct answer: NO. Overtaking begins only after checking the situation behind, including the blind spot of the mirrors. If the driver behind has already pulled out into the left lane, moving left will lead to a collision or push them off the road.

q-13507.text: Are you prohibited from overtaking a motor vehicle travelling on the carriageway at an intersection?
